The reason this review gets 4 stars vs 5 is because of the pool construction currently going on. The noise was not an issue as the had a live DJ. But I was told the reason the pools were so cold is because the heater was not working well due to the renovation. It really made the pools quite cold. It the grand scheme of things not a huge deal and once the renovations are over it won’t be an issue.

We will be back.

reviews.author: Canadian in the sun
reviews.title: Phoenician needs alot of work and attention
reviews.text: Sprawling resort.  Beautiful cactus garden with path along Camelback Mountain. 3 of out 5 pools were closed for renovation, and only one was heated well enough to enjoy, and only on one day. Food was ok, but not great for a resort of this supposed calibre. Restaurant servers were very friendly but service was super slow, particularly at breakfast.  It was off-putting to be told there is a wait list for a table in a mostly-empty restaurant, at every visit. Very friendly staff but thoughtless. The golf cart driver refused to wait even for one minute for us to gather our things when we were moved out of our completely dark room to a better one.  I had to carry a heavy bag a long way to the new room.  Not cool. The resort needs alot of repair.  Every exterior door in our building had paint missing on the bottom quarter. A hinge on our door was hanging by one screw.  A lamp flickered from a bad connection. The shower head faced the shower door making it impossible not to be sprayed with cold water when turning it on, not to mention flooding the bathroom floor. The sink drains were shut with no way of opening them.  Room carpet was quite unclean. Our room was made up each day around 5 pm which was annoying and the beds were half-heartedly tidied at best. One evening we found chocolates on our pillows, but not the next. In general, everything seemed uneven. My daughter and I joined my husband during a conference. We do love Arizona and have had fabulous visits at other hotels in Phoenix and Scottsale in the past.  We won't be returning to the Phoenician given the expense, the uneven service, mediocre food and the poorly kept property.  If you do end up there,  second floor casita rooms are bright with lovely spacious balconies.

reviews.author: Tour825773
reviews.title: Good bones. Needs some service upgrades at $1k+ a night.
reviews.text: Nice rooms except the blinking security lights all over the room. Very rude service at check in on Monday night.  Expect better service at over $1k a night. Conference facilities are nice and modern with excellent staff. A bit sprawling and long walks but good in winter when it’s not too hot   Room service takes over an hour and a half ant 7pm on a Monday and you don’t get any estimated arrival time. Really?  A $72 salad (yup with fees and BEFORE the tip the request) takes that long. Cannot imagine how long cooked meat takes.

reviews.author: Virna Z
reviews.title: 3 stars - some good some bad - not sure I would stay again
reviews.text:
We stayed in the casitas 
Building m overlooking the golf club
Second floor 
If I knew upon check in the location and that our room was on the second floor I would have asked to switch 
Second floor is very hard with strollers and luggage. . . So ask before . . . I didn’t know - the casitas that are located on ground level have a fire pit outdoors so that looked nice - so be sure to ask for that. . .  
There was no bell man to bring or take out luggage upon arrival or check out. . . And having to bring 4 luggages up a flight a stairs is not what I’m paying for in a 5 star resort! I was truly disappointed 
Second the view was horrible - I felt i was in a city - parking lots and the building of the golf club - I was paying quite a lot of money only to have a horrible view and a horrible room that was dirty and wasn’t cleaned until 4 pm every day 
The toiletries like cotton and q-tips were never refilled and that’s the bare minimum. . . 
 The positive 
If you like golf- this is a great place. The golf course and driving range are great! 
They had plenty of events and things for kids to do! 
Plenty of pools and space for kids to run around 
If you have a pet - they let dogs around which I didn’t like - a minus for me - but a plus for others cause soooo many guests had dogs here . . : 
Pickleball tennis 🎾 courts were great! 
We had our kids take a tennis lesson the pro was energetic and very knowledgeable . . We played both tennis and pickleball and the courts are well kept and taken care of

reviews.author: Rosina O
reviews.title: Not Worth The Money
reviews.text:
This was one of the most disappointing resorts we have ever visited.  My husband had planned a big surprise for my 60th b-day going to a warm sunny place in November to enjoy the beautiful pools this hotel offered.  
Upon arrival we encountered very persistent valet attendants.  Without checking in they insisted on taking our suitcases from our car and holding them until we checked in.  After standing in a very long line to check in because there was only one attendant available and the line was out the door, I took a walk only find that the entire main pool was under major construction.  Something that was not mentioned prior to reservation made or at check in. After check-in we were told about the two pools available, however, the lower pool was off limits due to a convention.  So, we really only had use to the smallest pool on the grounds.   We then had to wait for our car to load it back up to head to the other end where the casitas are located.
We reserved a casita, a little more exclusive and private.  Once we got settled in, we realized right outside our door they were setting up for the convention dinner, no privacy at all.  The casitas are very outdated, not very clean, mattress needs to be replaced and the tiny shower was covered in mold (see photos).  We headed to the hot tubs that we were told would be available.  Currently it is a maze of construction to get through only to find one of the hot-tub is off limits and the other had warm water with no jets.  The next morning, we requested a room change, we were moved to the main building. The rooms are much more spacious and updated and all though it has a large bathroom the shower is still very small.  We had a very nice balcony that would normally oversee the main pool.  If you like quiet, this is not the spot.  They have their private events there every night.  At the time we were there you either could hear the party and music or the construction noise. 
We asked what options they could offer us as the front desk was also not aware about their hot tubs off limits.  We were offered a one- day pass to the spa for the next day.  We decided to give the spa a try.  Apparently, something they don’t normally offer.  Upon arrival, the spa manager was already aware we were coming and was very gracious as he proceeds to let us know there was an electrical problem on the men’s side and the steam room was not working.  The spaces are separated for men and women so we would not be able to spend our time together.  We skipped the spa.
On this second day when returned from being out all day to a room that had not been serviced all day.  We called to get it cleaned and were told they would send someone. 
 The evening housekeeper that does the turndown showed up, was very apologetic for the morning staff but could only get trash and send someone else.  After waiting for 45 minutes a lady showed up with towels and a lack of desire to clean anything.

If you are a golfer, the course is beautiful and the gym was very nice surrounded by glass with views of the grounds.  
Overall, this hotel was very disappointing and for the cost I would choose something newer and with better service.

reviews.author: Jamie S
reviews.title: Luxury long weekend
reviews.text: Luxury experience, down to earth unobtrusive staff, extremely clean, comfortable rooms and exemplary adults only pool with best poolside food I’ve ever tasted.  Ample walking and jogging trails and  0.5 mile to Cholla trailhead on Camelback Mtn.

reviews.author: Sue H
reviews.title: Salon experience with Cynthia
reviews.text: I live in Scottsdale so didn't stay at the hotel BUT I booked a pedicure, expecting a lovely experience. I have never had a better pedicure in my life! Cynthia (ask for her!) was amazing. My toes are gorgeous, my legs are relaxed and most of all, Cynthia was a delight. She focused on my comfort and pretty much read my mind regarding an appropriate level of conversation! I cannot recommend this experience, the beautiful result and Cynthia enough. Truly first class!

reviews.author: Stephanie H
reviews.title: Spa Massage
reviews.text: Leaving a review for the spa- Gary was my massage therapist and I can’t rave enough about him! Hands down the best massage I’ve had at a hotel spa. My treatment was specialized to my needs and I left the table feeling extremely relaxed. 10/10 ask for Gary!

reviews.author: Dr Jeff
reviews.title: Excellent stay
reviews.text: Excellent hotel. Great pool area...one for adults also. Right at the base of Camelback Mt. if you want hike it. Food was amazing and the 24 hour gym was most excellent for someone on East coast morning time. There are lots of golf locations nearby

reviews.author: Montana16
reviews.title: Not that special any more.
reviews.text: We have visited The Phoenician many times over the last 25+ years. It is still a great place to stay but seems to have regressed since the Mariott takeover. Under the Starwood banner it was always top notch with lots of nice little touches which enhanced your stay. Now it's more run of the mill luxury hotel with nothing in particular to reccomend it, considering the rates they charge. Certainly not worth the money they demand any longer. We will probably return as it has been our home in Scottdsale for so many years, just not as good as it was.

reviews.author: Mark S
reviews.title: Great service
reviews.text:
Excellent service 
Highly recommended - overall experience. 
Pool great - kudos for Genaro, Hannah, and Gretchen
J&G - Jeff and Becky.  Thank you Frank 
Mowry & Cotton - Hector, Jordan, and Melissa are awesome. 

Service from these and others makes our stays memorable and keeps us coming back.

reviews.author: Jackie S
reviews.title: Don’t stay here save your money
reviews.text:
After staying here many many times I can say when things are good here it is a pleasure to stay here, however when there is a problem their solution is to ignore you.    After a stay here I flew home and realized I had a trash all over my body. They person I went with also got a rash.  After going to the dermatologist they told me it was from a bacteria in a hot tub.   After notifying the property they had Someone from security call me then ignore me.   I didn’t ask for my money back, my points back, or any kind of compensation, I simply wanted to make sure no one else got this rash.  After the call with security and made to feel like a criminal I emailed him pictures of my naked body with a dr note only to hear nothing from them! I hope they enjoyed the naked pics they requested of “proof of my rash” 

Save you money and stay someplace where you won’t get a rash from the hot tub

reviews.author: Holly K
reviews.title: Still great!
reviews.text:
We just returned from a weekend stay at the Phoenician and had a wonderful time. 

**Room:**  
We stayed in room 2016, which had a lovely view of the pool. The room was nicely appointed with a vanity area, comfortable beds, and a beautiful bathroom. The tub was a bit shallow, but the bath products and light robes were a nice touch.

**Service:**  
While the service overall was solid, I agree with other reviews that some areas could use improvement and polishing for a 5 star resort. However, the concierge was extremely helpful, especially when arranging a cabana for us, which turned out to be a great decision given the 110-degree heat. The cabana at the Mother of Pearl pool was relaxing, equipped with a fan, and offered great service. 

**Dining:**  
We had breakfast at Mowry and Cotton, which was excellent, and visited the tavern twice, skipping the steakhouse due to being too full from poolside dining. Everything we ate was delicious, and the service was wonderful. I didn’t realize the tavern accepts reservations, so next time I’ll book ahead—the only available table ended up being outside, and it was a bit too hot for comfort.

**Spa:**  
The spa was fantastic, with beautiful facilities, especially the quiet room. The service was wonderful. 

**Amenities:**  
The shopping on property was one of the best I’ve seen at a hotel, with a great selection in both the main shops and the spa store. The pool, especially when lit up at night, was stunning and perfect for an evening swim. The valet and bell services were friendly and efficient.

**Overall:**  
The property itself is beautiful, and although some service areas could be more polished, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Highly recommend the cabanas and the spa, and we’ll definitely be back!

reviews.author: sonofredhand
reviews.title: High-class eats, low-class sleeps
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed here in room 6054 (a "1 King Bed, Superior Guest Room") for two nights in September 2024.

Rating: 8/10

Positives:
• Spectacular Dining: The dining options here were truly outstanding. From steaks under the city lights at J & G Steakhouse, to chimichurri breakfast potatoes at Mowry & Cotton, afternoon tea at Thirsty Camel, and pub grub at The Phoenician Tavern, this hotel boasts an impressive array of culinary experiences. I rated each of these restaurants a solid five stars.
• Inviting Pool Areas: The resort offers several inviting pools and outdoor lounge areas, all complemented by excellent poolside service and equally impressive cocktails.
• Reasonable Room Rates: Although room rates at this resort can sometimes be steep, we enjoyed very reasonable prices for a hotel of this caliber during our September stay. Of course, this did come with triple-digit heat at the pool, but it was a fair trade-off!
• On-Site Convenience: The variety of on-site stores for treats, coffee, and sundries meant that we had everything we needed without ever having to leave the resort. This added to the sense of luxury and convenience throughout our stay.

Negatives:

• Uncomfortable Sleep: Unfortunately, we didn’t sleep well. The bed was worn, uneven, and quite uncomfortable. To make matters worse, the front desk confirmed that the hotel uses motion sensors to throttle the air conditioning when it detects no movement in the room. The real-world implication is that the air conditioning shuts off at night while guests are asleep—precisely when it’s most needed. It’s baffling that a 5-star resort would use such a flawed system that disrupts guest sleep. For me, no amount of dazzling amenities can make up for a bad night’s rest.
• Chromecast Issues: On our first night, we struggled for half an hour to get the TV’s advertised Chromecast feature to work, only to give up and resort to streaming on our own iPad propped up on the bed. The next day, the front desk informed us that Chromecast was currently non-operational across the entire resort and offered a $100 credit for the inconvenience. While the gesture was appreciated, this level of technical oversight was frustrating.
• Inconvenient Late Checkout Process: As a Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite member, I was granted a much-appreciated 2pm late checkout. However, I was told that our existing keys would stop working at 11am, requiring me to visit the front desk for new keys. When I went to do so, I had to wait in line for 20 minutes with people checking in, just to get access to my own room. This inefficient process overshadowed the benefit of the late checkout and left a negative impression.
• Bland Room Décor: The room’s gray decor felt bland and uninviting, lacking the warmth and luxury you would expect from a 5-star resort. A design refresh would go a long way in making the rooms feel more comfortable and welcoming.

reviews.author: RamblingJimbo
reviews.title: Great Service = great stay!
reviews.text:
My wife and I had a very satisfactory stay at this hotel for 5 nights in late August. The number one best thing about the hotel is the excellent staff, in every department. All employees were friendly, hard-working, capable and professional. The restaurants, bars and facilities were clean, modern and very comfortable. We used the spa, G & J Steak House, Lowry & Cotton, Phoenician Tavern, Thirsty Camel and Marketplace. Great service is continuous throughout every venue.

The rooms were clean and comfortable but could use a little refreshment as we noticed patio furniture was worn and outdated. Electrical outlets and USB charging stations were numerous and convenient. The beds were very comfortable.  The showers were not that great and could use some work. 

Public areas were clean, modern and tastefully decorated. The garden areas were well well kept and fun to explore. It was too hot to use the pool area while we were there but we explored it and noticed separate adult-only and family areas.

All staff were great but kudos to everyone below:
In G & J Steak House great service by Austin and his team. At breakfast each morning we were given great service by Rachel, Earnesto and Christine in Mowery & Cotton. One night we ate dinner in Mowery and credit Cristian with a great experience. Bryce at the front desk did an outstanding job at checkin and when we needed to make a couple of changes to our reservation. Celia in housekeeping was wonderful and went out of her way to say hello even after say had moved from our building to look after other hotel property.

reviews.author: Addison M
reviews.title: Off-Season Experience
reviews.text:
The grounds at the Phoenician are stunning with a view of Camelback mountain. The location is terrific, within minutes of restaurants and shops.  The amenities are plenty.  Unfortunately, I would not rate this resort as a 5-star based on the service and upkeep of the property.  Many parts of the property look tired and need an upgrade.  In particular, the pools are all cracking, the water is dirty and often only attended to once a day.  The cleanest we saw the pool was after a monsoon rainstorm.  The chairs are all stained as well.

In addition, we were surprised to find 1-2 people working the front desk which meant a lineup was generally the case when we walked by the front lobby.  We had two issues that required the help of the front desk and no one ever answered the phone, so we had to go in person to the front desk and be stuck in a line.

Also our room was not cleaned on one of the days, and the other days housekeeping came after 3:30.  This is too late for guests that are staying over in the hotel, especially when it is only 30% full during the off-season.

For a resort of this size, more staff need to be present, especially if it is being advertised as a 5-star.

reviews.author: vacationcruisin
reviews.title: The best of the best
reviews.text: We ended our action-packed family vacation with a very relaxing two nights at the Phoenician and enjoyed every minute of it.  Love the onsite amenities like the pool, waterslide (which was amazing) and the cactus gardens.  Upon checking in, they gave us a complementary upgrade to a very large queen room with a massive patio which we used in the morning to observe nature's activity on Camelback Mountain.  Onsite dining was also delicious.  This is the place to stay when in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: Vy H.
reviews.title: Resort in Scottsdale, AZ
reviews.text:
LOVED our stay here!  It really did feel like a 5-star hotel—from service to amenities.

Pros:
- Resort is huge, with lots of activities and several dining options, enough for you to spend your stay here and don’t really need to leave the resort
- Decor was nice and clean, and has a fancy vibe
- Service was EXCELLENT—majority of the staff were so friendly and helpful
- Our Spacious 2 Queens Bedroom was nice with comfy beds, huge bathroom and a balcony overlooking the pool.  Also received some complimentary welcome snacks after we checked in.  Had a fully stocked fridge (for purchase), and room safe 

Cons:
- Not enough security measures—I didn’t see security throughout most of the complex—also, just about anyone can walk around the resort, there’s no restricted card access to get to the rooms hallway area either
- There are 3 pools, but the Adults-Only pool had children and staff did nothing to request they go to the kid friendly pool—this was annoying when you expect a peaceful pool time and kids are shouting and splashing water all around
- Pool bar closes early, even around 6pm Saturday the bar was closed—resort should offer drink service because many of us would have ordered cocktails

reviews.author: J&M
reviews.title: Best Luxury Collection Hotel
reviews.text: The staff & personnel are professional, friendly and very helpful.  Accommodating Javier check- in our upgraded  Casitas suite, which is very neat and clean. Arrived early and had breakfast at M&C restaurant, Tom welcomed us and truly enjoyed the delicious food, the menu depends on the freshest ingredients available. Compliment to the CHEF. The hotel is perfectly located in Camelback mountain, the facility has a well maintained Cactus Garden, 3 layers of swimming pool Marissa did a good job serving us drinks. The gym is well equipped and lobby is pristine. Shannon the concierge, guide us where to go and we waste no time going around the Old Town. Excellent and relaxing stay.We will come back again!

reviews.author: Sheryl M
reviews.title: The best in Scottsdale!
reviews.text: The Phoenician is a wonderful resort in Scottsdale. It is in the perfect location - close to shopping and great restaurants. The property is beautiful. The pools are great. They are perfect for adults and children. The staff is warm and friendly. Housekeeping is great too. Mowry and Cotton a nice place for breakfast.  My first choice to stay when visiting Scottsdale!

reviews.author: MEHRDAD M
reviews.title: Worst Luxury Collection Resort
reviews.text:
First room was assigned to us had an extremely heavy odor of weed to a point that you couldn’t enter the room. Second room had mold on the shower floor, old and deteriorating furniture, slippers by the bed was used before and had blood stains inside of it. To top it off we woke up to the loud sound of a pounding noise coming from construction upfront. We checked out of the hotel early morning. Employees were polite and curtsy. 
Would not recommend this hotel at all.

reviews.author: Kelly M
reviews.title: Wow-disappointing!!
reviews.text:
Poor service.
Dated.
3 stars at best!!!
Came here after hearing about the Phoenician for years.
Booked a spa treatment prior to a business trip. 
Over priced for a hot tub/Sauna and steam room.  Hotel and spa are disappointing. All of it is dated and underwhelming.

reviews.author: Angie
reviews.title: No restaurants
reviews.text: I stayed at the Phonecian Canyon Suites. The rooms are beautiful but they neglected to tell me there are no restaurants on premises. You have to take a shuttle to a different property for all restaurants and spa treatments except breakfast or room service. The booking did not indicate that it is deceiving

reviews.author: B.Gretch
reviews.title: Beautiful Property, Service definitely not 5 stars, and leave asking yourself if the hotel really wanted you to stay.
reviews.text: I've stayed at the Phoenician dozens of times, my dad was one of the builders and so it has always felt like home and I know the property well. When ever in the Phoenix area, didn't matter price or time of year booking the Phoenician was a no brainer. For the longest time, the Phoenician wasn't the most up to date property but the service was spectacular and made you feel welcome and special and left you wanting to come back. However the past couple times we've stayed here, the renovation is gorgeous but the staff is definitely something that leaves you to be desired. Checking in with Max at the front desk left us feeling like we were at a used car dealership with the nickel and diming he was trying to do to upsell us instead of giving an elite upgrade, saying he would have to move someone so he'll have to charge us $100 extra per night, then it came down to $50 and when I declined tried assigning us a lower room category than booked. Being familiar with the property I questioned him about the assigned room being a lower category room and said oh let me take a look, and then was able to assign us an upgraded room magically. Max was not engaging or even that friendly and after telling him we came for my birthday he responded wit , oh. The concierge sent an email prior to our arrival asking what brought us to the phoenix area and I filled out their questionnaire that we were coming to celebrate my birthday and gave the arrival date and flight number. I received and email the day after I arrived asking if I wanted transportation to the hotel and told me to tell my partner Happy Birthday. I responded with we already arrived and are leaving tomorrow. When you call the guest services from the room they used to answer with your last name and how they could help, Not any more. Not one person the entire stay greeted us by name from the front desk, to the concierge, to the phone lines, and pool staff. Not what you expect from a 5 star resort or hotel for that matter. Another thing noticed when ever walking through the resort no-one smiled, or said hi. It was just a very cold feeling all around and not what you expect from a 5 star hotel. It was more inline with a Fairfield or franchised Marriott. We gave the hotel a lot of information about our stay and a lot of opportunity to make it special and that doesn't mean upgrades that are not available or champagne waiting in the room. A simple card from the hotel for my birthday would have been nice since they were aware, or lightSpeed tells the agent how many times you've visited a property so even a simple welcome back would have gone a long way, but at the end of the day just friendly staff that seem interested, professional and welcoming and can deliver just a sliver of 5 star service would have been really nice. We are returning to Phoenix in a few weeks and for the first time I'm considering another property as Scottsdale is flooded with beautiful 5 Star resorts and want a property that can make you feel welcomed and just smile.

reviews.author: DIEDRE S
reviews.title: Stay at the Andaz
reviews.text:
We chose this because we had stayed at the Andaz in Hawaii which was lovely.
This is not that. 
Upon arrival at lunchtime we were told the restaurant is only open for breakfast and dinner which leaves only one option-outside at the loud pool bar in 108 degree heat!
Our room overlooks the pool with very loud music all day.
We headed to the adult pool and ordered food which took a long time. The margarita was not fresh lime juice but sickly sweet mix of some sort. Not drinkable.
The pool was warm and looked sorta green.
Ordered breakfast from the room which was awkward-you must order through the front desk. The woman did not know the menu and kept saying she didn’t think they had things and putting me on hold.
All in all a bit weird and def not 5 stars!

reviews.author: JessChiro3
reviews.title: Phoenician was amazing! Canyon Suites has the best customer service.
reviews.text:
What a wonderful place to stay. We opted for the Canyon Suites because it has larger rooms and a private pool. Looking back now, I may have stayed at the larger part of the resort because it’s closer to the larger pools. 

The food at dinner was great in the hotel lobby and the free breakfast was amazing and plentiful. Definitely not your typical “continental”. This is one of the perk of being at the Canyon Suites portion of the resort. 

The pools were great and got busy!  The pool bar tenders weee fabulous and attentive. 

We utilized the Blow Dry Bar at the resort and had a great blowout. The small shops at the main Phoenician building were quite lovely.  

We would definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: Jeffrey D
reviews.title: Awful, just plain awful!
reviews.text: I’m a Marriott lifetime Titanium, and had high expectations of this resort given its past reputation.  However, let me tell you, that past reputation has, indeed, passed into something FAR less positive.  When I started running into issues, I thought “ok, every resort has its hiccups”; but service failure after failure occurred day-after-day during my 4 night stay.  On the positive side, I can say the grounds are really nice; not as nice as the neighboring Camelback Inn, but nice nevertheless.  Additionally, I found the food and service at the resort’s Tavern restaurant to be excellent.  The views from both the lobby and my room were outstanding.  That’s where the positives end, however.  The rooms, while large, are holdovers from the 1980’s with some refresh of paint and lighting.  The A/C was poor (the hallways in the hotel were at least 90 degrees), and the room never cooled sufficiently.  Bedding was mediocre; shower pressure incredibly poor; and the balcony furniture was stained and filthy.  Cart shuttles around the resort typically took 45 minutes to arrive.  It took 45 minutes to receive ice, each of the 5 times we ordered it (there are no ice machines on the guest floors).  One of my business colleagues summed up the experience at this resort nicely…”it’s like a supposed 5-star resort that is being run by really poor Springhill Suites management.”

reviews.author: ECTraveler
reviews.title: A fantastic experience at the Phoenician!
reviews.text:
While we stayed over in the Canyon Suites, we used the pools and restaurants while staying here. Mowry & Cotton had fantastic breakfast choices, J&G Steakhouse was wonderful for a quieter, more luxurious dinner. Their master wine list had some amazing choices on it! We also watched the fireworks from the balcony, which was the perfect view. Afternoon Tea was wonderful and had a plethora of food to fill you up, along with teas and champagne. The Phoenician Tavern was a good place to grab a quick lunch when we first arrived. 

We also used the adult pool and relaxed with drinks just to take it easy. All of the staff was very helpful, engaging, and nice. It was fun to just walk around and explore the area, cactus garden, pools, etc. My one critique would be I wish the main hotel gift shop had more in the way of souvenirs like other varieties of cactus candies, magnets, Phoenician themed items. I was able to get one or two things there, but ended up getting more items in local giftshops for our trip home.

reviews.author: Maddy
reviews.title: The Phoenician is my favorite hotel in all of Arizona. Incredible service and relaxing experience.
reviews.text: I have visited a few times now. Not only is the Phoenician a beautiful property, amazing spa and restaurants….. for me it’s the people that work there. Best service in a hotel that I’ve experienced in years. Derrick and Max, at the front desk, in the Canyon Suites section, were so helpful, attentive and amazing to me. They are so accommodating, friendly and their follow through is perfection. They literally go above and beyond for you. Many lovely hotels in Phoenix, but I always come back here and tell my friends and family to stay there. The bell men are very friendly and courteous as well. Just an overall fantastic visit each time.

reviews.author: Scott H
reviews.title: Great location, top notch service
reviews.text:
Had a conference in AZ (different resort) and decided to have my wife fly out and go ot the Phoenician for a couple of nights. A few friends had recommended it and I am so glad they did. We really enjoyed our stay and the entire property. The property, while architecturally a little dated, has been updated so well. On top of that everyone on the staff we interacted with was so fantastic and helpful and really seemed to want to make our stay something memorable. 

Room: We did not stay in the main building, but booked one of the casitas, which are out buildings below the pool area neat the spa and golf course. inside they are standard hotel rooms but from the outside they have the feel that maybe they were originally intended to be apartments/ condos. We wanted to go for this set up since we had plans at the golf course, spa, and ‘Mother of Pearl’ pool which is closest to the casitas. We were very happy with this decision as we were very close to those things and felt like we had more privacy. Point of clarification: There are two types of casitas. The regular casitas are along the back row of casitas and face towards either a parking lot, the golf club house, or a parking deck. We booked the Deluxe Casita which is guaranteed to face toward the pools and Camelback Mountain. We had a regular king room, but I believe they have some large casitas with fire pits outside and even fireplaces inside if you are there in winter months.

Food: While it si resort food so not cheap, there wasn’t a single thing we ordered and ate that we regretted. It was all delicious and you could tell it was prepared with care. We ended up having food from basically every restaurant option at the resort and you can’t go wrong with any. The pool side restaurant and service is perfect for eating outside pool side. Cotton and Mowry is great variety , and J&G has some incredible views. MY wife’s favorite was actually the Tavern which is above the golf pro shop. Each place had fantastic service,so props to the place for the training of the staff.

Pool: We were there in June which is not the busiest, but it didn’t bother us. The pools at The PHoenician are great. I surprised my wife with a cabana rental at the Mother of Pearl pool for our full day there and it really elevated the experience. The cabanas have ceiling fans and TVs in them and we really didn’t need to go anywhere all day. There are plenty of chairs and umbrellas even without the caban rental of course and we noticed the staff always being very attentive to all guests in moving umbrellas to t keep their things in the shade. Rich was the assigned staff for our cabana and he was the best. There are several other pools as well at the resort, including a kids splash zone and a water slide. 

Golf: The golf course at The Phoenician is run and managed by Troon Golf, so you can expect great conditions and good service. It delivered on that for sure. As for the course itself, I will say that if you are looking for classic desert golf, this won’t be your course. Conditions are great, but the front nine feels like playing a residential muni or country club. Lots of houses all around and you even ahve to drive through as construction site at one point. The back nine is where it is at on this course. The front  and back are far from one another, but once yo get to th back, it’s a different course. You are on the slopes of Camelback Mountain and the views are outstanding on each and every hole. 

Spa: While I was golfing my wife was at the spa. She loved everything inside. She spent some time on the rooftop pool and said it was enjoyable, but to know there are no views at that pool like there are at the regular resort pools.

Fitness Center: I have to call this out. The gym at The Phoenician is without a doubt the best hotel/ resort gym I have ever used and it is not even close. It is a little bit of a walk from the buildings and over by the tennis courts, but once your are up there you see why they put it where they did. 

Tennis/ Pickleball: Several courts dedicated for both. We didn’t play tennis, but saw others using the courts. We did play some pickleball using paddles and balls provided by the resort which was super easy. The courts did seem like they were not being used much or needed a good cleaning, but were in perfectly good shape.

Shops: There are retail shops everywhere. The golf shop, below the gym near the tennis courts is the tennis shop, then there are a set up shops attached to the main building. They all have variations of things depending onto e activity they pertain to. They are all well appointed and serviced well. My wife found a hat she liked at the tennis shop and I found one I liked at the golf shop. The other shops were great for buying things for our kids. We do wish they had more T shirt options specifically featuring the phoenician logo.

Other Activities: We did not do any of the organized activities, but there were plenty offered. We did walk through the cactus garden on the back side of the property and enjoyed that being from a very different part of the country.

Overall I would recommend a stay at the Phoenician to anyone. Could work for couples but also families. Beautiful setting and fantastic service all around.

reviews.author: WDWDolphinFan
reviews.title: Pleasant Stay
reviews.text: I had a stay here in early June, in a deluxe pool view room.  The room was large and spacious.   It was on a high floor, so a nice view of Phoenix in the distance, with mountain views to the side, and nice views at sunset.   Although I was there on a weekend, there was no problem finding lounge chairs at the pool, even in the shade.   The desert garden was interesting, with little signs identifying many of the different types of cactus.  Breakfast outside at Mowry and Cotton was pleasant, and it was interest to watch the gentleman with the trained hawk scare birds away from the dining area.  My facial at the spa was good.   All very nice, and I am glad I had the chance to stay here, but it nevertheless did not make my list of favorite resorts in the area.

reviews.author: blue720
reviews.title: Business trip at an awesome hotel
reviews.text: I stayed here fir a work conference. I was impressed by the rooms. They were large with our own patio. The bathroom had a tub and separate shower with plenty of room for two people to get ready. There is even a separate vanity with makeup mirror outside of the bathroom to get ready. The room has several full sized mirrors. We went to the pool and ordered drinks the service was top notch! Our room was nice and clean and service in room was wonderful too! Thank you for an amazing stay!

reviews.author: Farrah K
reviews.title: Wonderful hotel with five star service, pools were disappointing.
reviews.text: Incredible customer service. Five star all the way. Rooms super comfortable and very quiet. Best sleep I have had at a hotel in years. Awesome lobby bar with fun vibes and great food and cocktails. Great coffee shop for morning coffee run that also had great on the go breakfast menu. This hotel seriously had almost everything perfect. The only negative is the pools. They were very dirty, very dated and just kind of meh and ugly. As our group was here to spend two days at the pools, this was a bummer part of an otherwise awesome hotel. If your main priority is the pool, I would go somewhere else.

reviews.author: rodney n
reviews.title: WARNING!
reviews.text:
I recently had another disappointing experience with the Phoenician Hotel Resort. On my second attempt to stay at the hotel, I was once again let down and had to cancel my reservations while standing at their counter due to the hotel's inability to provide me with the rooms I had reserved. -Despite a low 45% occupancy rate in mid-June, I was told that my "connected" rooms were unavailable, which seemed like a poor excuse from the management.

Frustrated with the their poor customer service, I Celtic best to move to the neighboring Sanctuary Resort, where I was pleasantly surprised by the excellent service and a much nicer room that truly reflected a five-star standard. It's apparent that the Phoenician Hotel Resort lacks proper management and falls short in delivering on their promises to guests.

While I appreciated the Sanctuary Resort's ability to accommodate me in a time of need, I would caution others about the Phoenician Hotel Resort's lack of accountability and extremely lazy approach to customer satisfaction.

reviews.author: Katie S
reviews.title: Amazing resort experience!
reviews.text: This was my second time staying here and it was a 20/10. The service was absolutely top notch and the food was some of the best I’ve had. Every cocktail was perfection. My husband has celiac and they were extremely accommodating. I cannot say enough about this resort and I’m a pretty picky guest. I would come here a million times! We had the most amazing time. 5 star experience.

reviews.author: Irene4re
reviews.title: Phenomenal Phoenician!
reviews.text:
Phenomenal Phoenician! I had Dreamed of staying here and yes, my Dream came True!
Douglas, the Front Desk Manager was instrumental in making this Dream of mine so extraordinary! He went above and beyond to make sure that my stay was phenomenal! I highly recommend The Phoenician! The setting is Awe Inspiring! The Pools are lovely. Kevin will take good care of poolgoers! The Breakfast Buffet was Delicious with many yummy choices and excellent service by Felix and Raphael! The Dining is superb. Be sure to go to J&G Steakhouse. The manager, Kyle will make sure that your Dining experience is Magical!

reviews.author: Michael F
reviews.title: Don’t miss out on the cactus garden!
reviews.text:
Wow this place is stunning and we can’t wait to return. 

Stayed mid-week and the place felt empty but even if it were quite busier, I think we would have enjoyed just as much. 

Highly recommend the spa, the facility is just so relaxing including the sauna, hot tub, rooftop pool, and quiet relaxation room. 

We stayed in a Casita which allowed quick access to the pools from our walk-out fireplace balcony.

Breakfast at Mowry and Cotton and lunch by the pool (Kalio Kabobery) were just so good, we didn’t want to leave. 

Read all the negative reviews with a grain of salt, this place will WOW you. 

Thank you so much to the staff who made our trip so special.

reviews.author: lizzie68
reviews.title: Wonderful Weekend Getaway!
reviews.text: My husband and I just returned from a wonderful Memorial Day weekend at this resort, and I have nothing but positive things to say about our experience. Check in was easy and efficient. The bellhops outside were friendly and helpful. Every server we encountered when dining/having drinks at the Tavern, Mowry & Cotton, The Thirsty Camel bar and J & G Steakhouse restaurants was fabulous! The food was great every place we ate on site! There was also  live music at numerous places at this resort in the evenings. We were most impressed with how hard working all of the employees at each of the pool areas were. They were constantly helping guests by finding chairs and umbrellas, picking up trash left at pool seats, constantly refilling everyone’s pitchers with ice water and they were all very friendly! Ubers and Lyfts were readily available so no need to rent a car for our stay.  We did not check out the Spa or Athletic Center or play golf on this visit, but all looked great. This is our second stay at this resort. We would return in the future and highly recommend the Phoenician to others.

reviews.author: grspinelli
reviews.title: Staff yelling at guests at the pool and roaches for dinner
reviews.text:
My wife and stayed three nights and found the resort nice but a little tired. We had dinner at Mowry and Cotton one night were sitting on the patio when we started noticing roaches running around. We moved tables two times and finally moved inside. At this point the mood was quite different but we made the best of it. The employees didn’t seem too concerned about our experience and I even spoke with the F&B manager the next morning. He assured me that he would this was not normal and would have the area cleaned. 
We also had a situation at the pool the day before and spoke to the deck manager. Neither incident was followed up on and customer dissatisfaction seems to fall into a black hole. We will not be returning, there are better resorts in the area.

reviews.author: Bethany
reviews.title: Ready to go back!
reviews.text: What a gorgeous hotel. The grounds are  stunning, with colorful flowers and blooms everywhere we turned. The pools and villas were incredible with the most beautiful backdrop. Rooms were spacious and extremely cozy with immaculate attention to detail. Hotel restaurants and room service was delightful and delicious! We especially loved our morning breakfasts on the balcony. Customer service was top-notch; Whether it was Rich taking care of us at the pool, the friendly room service staff, the concierge or valet attendants…everyone was incredible!

reviews.author: Oakleaf1950
reviews.title: Disappointing Check-in
reviews.text: We are part of a meeting for a company. Most of us are in our 60’s-80’s so have traveled. We checked in and were assigned a room on the outer reaches of the main building where we walked about a block or more just to get to the room only to discover that the room had an adjoining door with a noisy family on the other side. At that point I called the front desk. No one answered for 25 minutes while I listened to a tape recording. For a hotel that calls itself a luxury hotel, this was inexcusable. No one ever did answer so I hiked back to the main level only to find several front desk employees available. Took another 1.5 hours to secure a new room, which is very nice. The moral of this annoying story is to go look at the room first before accepting it and before carting luggage. Very disappointing.

reviews.author: Dineriffic
reviews.title: Just another pretty face!
reviews.text: The resort is very pretty, but I found the place disappointing. Although I am at the highest level in the Bonvoy loyalty program, not one person ever recognized me as such. The hotel had been advised prior to my arrival that I would be celebrating my birthday. Again, not one employee of the hotel ever acknowledged this. Our room was a Grand Deluxe Casita, and it was quite comfortable.  However, it could benefit from a face-lift. There is a lot of building going on developing condos and houses. Although I have been to this hotel many times in the past, this time was the least memorable. The hotel is very nice but not spectacular. I would still recommend it, but I  do not necessarily think it is worth the price.

reviews.author: BethD614
reviews.title: Phoenix/Scottsdale gem
reviews.text: The staff and food were excellent. I was there for a work trip but it felt like a vacation. Excellent! the grounds were well cared for and rooms spacious and comfortable. The location was close to Fashion Mall and the pool area was 3 levels so offered plenty of seating and there is a golf course onsite.

reviews.author: Susan A
reviews.title: Too many nicer properties to choose from-sad to see such an iconic property go downhill
reviews.text:
We planned a midweek getaway and stayed in a Casasita # 7136. The light switches were dirty near the kitchen and two cigars were stuck in the outside screen on the patio. The shower curtain had orange shampoo stuck on the liner. I realize this was 2 days after the Final Four Basketball tournament took over the city but the cleanliness should be a standard for the room prices they are charging. 
We had spa treatments the first day and Julie at the front spa desk was incredibly rude and curt. We asked for the bellman to take our luggage to our room and when she called her response was ' Yeah, they don't want to roll their suitcases" her response is certainly not 4 or 5 star service. If she was able to locate our room on the map and explain the location maybe we could have taken the bags ourselves. I asked her where we meet for our massages and her response" Didn't you listen on the tour'? Wow-I didn't know how to respond to her rudeness. 
Bernardo the masseuse gave an incredible Fire & Ice massage and I wanted to leave an extra tip on top of the automatic gratuity and Julie said" We have already closed out our registers" It was 5:35pm and we were the last guests in the Spa-they should have waited for us to check out before closing up so quickly. 
We had dinner at Mow& Cowry the 1st night-Hector our server was rushed and indifferent until it came time at the end for the bill and we asked for a picture. 
Cameron in Turndown service is an AMAZING young man with manners and a service heart. 
Sherill at the Front Desk is polite and engaging. 
We had dinner at J&G Steakhouse-our server Becky was wonderful and informative. I made the mistake of ordering Salmon at a Steakhouse-it came out and was WHITE and had NO TASTE. The menu states 'Hand cut Steak Fries" but we were served thin McDonald's looking french fries. 
We bought a Thank you gift for our hostess on the final day:
The T-shirt was $42.00??? Seems a bit excessive for a standard tshirt

Overall, it was a nice trip but we will not be staying at the Phoenician again. I see too many significant downgrades since Marriott has taken over management and the property has lost it charm and 5 star level of service. Especially the Spa Front Desk, not a great start of our trip to be spoken to so rudely and condescending.

reviews.author: Lisa Statner
reviews.title: The Phoenician is the most beautiful Resort in Scottsdale
reviews.text:
We had the absolute best time at this resort!  So beautiful and our room was immaculate! The grounds were amazing and we enjoyed the Athletic club. 

Everyone we encountered was extremely nice. The pool was great and plenty of seating to choose from. 

We ate at the pool bar, the Tavern, had drinks at Thirsty Camel and had a mixology class at Monery and Cotton with Jordan! He was wonderful!  

Perfect stay for a girls weekend getaway!

reviews.author: Debbie F
reviews.title: Dont Stay Here
reviews.text:
This review is being posted while I am still here.   My one word review is that this hotel is DATED. Upon Arrival, we were offered an upgrade to a Casita.  $400. more on top of our original room at $1223 per night,  We accepted that upgrade gladly.  We are Marriott Elite members and were happy with that offer.   UNTIL we checked into the room.  BUGS in the master bathroom.  Took me several calls to even get anyone to deal with it,  They sent housekeeping but all they did was wipe away the bugs....which did nothing.  They were back the next day.   GROSS.  We asked for and spoke to manager (Ben) and he offered nothing until I asked for that $400 to be removed.   What a waste.  Like he was not concerned at all.   On top of the bugs, the room is old, walls scaped up, kitchen dated, Blow dryers didn't work, showers leaked all over the floor (which they did fix).

I WOULD NOT STAY HERE AGAIN.   BE WARNED.   Also, food at pool is Greek menu so if you're looking for chicken fingers or Grilled Chicken sandwiches you will not love that.

The spa has a deceptive practice as well.  Massage prices increase as they get busier.  So a $225 massage will cost you $285 if it is the last one available.   They slide that thru to you and it is an ABSOLUTE disgrace.   The price of a massage should be the dang price.   Price Gouging is not acceptable anywhere.........but the spa at the Phoenician

There are nicer hotels around and I would NOT stay here again.  Its concerning that we NEVER received a callback from anyone concerning the above bug issue.  Which is still a problem and we are still in this room.

reviews.author: Familyof4
reviews.title: Great family resort - fun for parents and kids!
reviews.text:
Our family of four had a great Spring Break stay at the Phoenician. We were upgraded to a poolside room upon arrival, the room was very large (huge bathroom), with great linens and comfortable beds. We had a ground-floor room with a patio/balcony that overlooked the cactus garden, so it felt very private and our views were great.

The pool area is large, with consistent waiter service and several pools to choose from, including a huge adults-only pool and a kids area with waterslide and treehouse. Our kids ran around for hours while we lounged and sipped cocktails. The boys’ favorite was the activity center/game room, with pool, ping pong, and multiple arcade games. They spent hours there while we walked around the resort, people-watched, and had a few drinks at the bar. 

One of my favorite things about the Phoenician is its close proximity to Uptown Scottsdale. It’s super easy to slip away for a day of shopping and eating at fabulous restaurants. It was also very easy to get to the airport for our morning flight.

While the spring break prices were insane (but comparable/less than comparable Scottsdale resorts during high season), I would gladly return during off-season for a mini-vacay.

reviews.author: Kristen M
reviews.title: A family favorite
reviews.text: We love this resort and have been twice with our kids (middle school ages). We stay in a casita suite w a fire table (first floor), and we get two roll away beds,  which are just twin beds basically. Suite is huge with 2 full bathrooms, so it’s great. Pools are fun and are heated, restaurants are great, especially the breakfast buffet. The gym is amazing, and I love walking in the cactus garden. Poolside service is good, and food is reasonable there. Great location that is close to old town Scottsdale, camelback mountain hikes, the mall, etc. wonderful resort for all ages!

reviews.author: M30001
reviews.title: Four out of five stars
reviews.text:
Stayed here for 5 nights with family (including kids 10 and 6 yrs) in 2 rooms.  Overall a 4 out of 5 – many highs about this resort but not currently operating at 5 star resort level.

Cons:
•	Housekeeping was inconsistent.  Sometimes beds straightened, sometimes not.  Sometimes chocolates, sometimes not.  They seem to always clean the rooms while leaving the door open, which for our rooms (where the door opened to outside hallway) allowed bugs in every day.  This should be a change to their standard practices. 
•	Service in some areas is good; other areas not.  The concierge team was fantastic.  Servers at Mowry & Cotton seemed overwhelmed and service was objectively bad (at dinner, I went to get water refills for the table and in search of additional menus). Pool wait staff was also overwhelmed at times, and service was mixed (over 1 hour to get a sandwich on one of the more busy days).
•	Limited view rooms are really limited/no view.  Our rooms overlooked the roof of the convention center.  There are a large number of rooms similarly situated.  I have not seen a ‘luxury’ hotel with so many rooms that have objectively bad views. This is especially odd given on the other side of the rooms is the beautiful cactus garden/camelback.  No clue why the hotel did not build the rooms facing something you’d actually want to look at.  At least the hotel could spruce up the roof with planter boxes of plants.  I was prepared for limited/no view but still surprised at how bad it was.  
•	Kids club activities were mixed.  Some of them were good, others were cheap and a waste of time and money.
•	Annoying fees.  A $75 per night connecting room charge so my kids and I could be in rooms next to one another?

Pros:
•	Great location at the base of Camelback.  We hiked it on multiple days.  You can just walk from the hotel to the Cholla trail entrance.
•	Overall resort build is very high quality and nice.  The hotel lobby bar is great.  Attention to detail in the hotel in various areas e.g. fresh flowers, falconer, is high and shows.  The grounds are beautiful and well kept.  The cactus garden was great. 
•	Pool deck areas are expansive and very nice.  On some days we found seating to not be an issue but on other days all chairs were claimed by early morning.  Our kids loved playing in the various pools and all ages thoroughly enjoyed the water slide. 
•	Variety of restaurant options that kept everyone happy with food options. 
•	Amenities very good (golf, fitness club)

Overall I’d be very upset paying rack rate prices with the cons above.  If you can get a deal and go in eyes open to some potential flaws, it’s very good.  Hopefully some of the issues above can be fixed with better training or additional staff hiring.

reviews.author: Conny Wylie
reviews.title: It's  All About Pampering,
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is an eye-catching & imaginative luxury destination resort at the base of the Camelback Mountains. I idolized my King Casita Deluxe done in tan desert hues. The spacious enclave was outfitted with desk, chairs and sofa, patio, floor-to-ceiling windows and high-tech room appliances. The opulent marbleized bathroom had a separate bath and shower. The resort has a wide array of dining and drinking establishments. For something higher-end I headed up to the fifth floor J & G Steakhouse where the menu is focused around classic steak fare with decadent dishes like Wagyu Tomahawk ribeye while I feasted on their equally decadent seafood,  sauteed Dover Sole. Mowry & Cotton offers modern American fare while the Thirsty Camel (in the lobby) offers a full bar, Sonoran-inspired snacks with live entertainment each evening. The Phoenician pools are a major highlight unfolding over 3 expansive tiers as is the Kids Zone. The Phoenician Spa is the pinnacle amenity of the property and is dedicated to pampering and wellness with an extensive menu.
So, if you desire an oasis of grand scale luxury with a majestic mountain backdrop.......
...........then try the ..............Phoenician.................it's all about pampering.

reviews.author: Karim C
reviews.title: Lovely resort with nice amenities! Close to everything.
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel, setting and service. I was traveling with my elderly mother and young daughter. The staff were very kind and accommodating. We were upgraded to a casita and the valets were all terrific and very helpful moving our closer for ease with my mother. The lobby is wonderful and has a great vibe and nice bar. Try the “Fire Side Chat” awesome cocktail. The grounds are lovely and have great amenities. Very convenient for visiting Fashion Square, Old Town, etc. We didn’t get to golf this time, but course looks in nice condition.

reviews.author: jeanbm
reviews.title: Phenomenal time at the Phoenician!
reviews.text:
We had the absolute best time at this resort and were sad to leave!  Javier at reception was very helpful and friendly and got us into a great room right away.  We reserved a Deluxe King and had a wonderful view of Camelback, the room was clean and comfortable, the turndown service was a nice touch.  

The grounds were amazing and we enjoyed the bikes at the Athletic club. Everyone we encountered were extremely nice.  The pool was great and plenty of seating to choose from.  We ate at the pool bar, the Tavern, and had drinks at Thirsty Camel; everything we ate/drank was great!  Special shoutout to Kelsey at the Thirsty Camel, she is fantastic!

10/10 would recommend the Phoenician!

reviews.author: kay
reviews.title: Expensive but wonderful for a Special Occasion!
reviews.text: Check in was wonderful.  Zane was accommodating and pleasant.  We were celebrating my birthday so he sent up a surprise amenity-so sweet and appreciated, made me feel truly special.  The rooms are large and we had a view of Camelback Mountain.  Yes it is expensive and we didn’t have time to use all the “resort fee” includes.  We had cocktails at Thirsty Camel and apps and drinks at The Tavern at the Golf Club.  The restaurants seemed expensive so didn’t eat there.  The location is great so it is not necessary to eat at The Phoenician.  Overall a nice experience.  Lovely!

reviews.author: V1979
reviews.title: Not a luxury hotel it once was, poor front office service, but great location and good golf club
reviews.text:
We normally stay at a different resort for our annual business trip to Scottsdale, but thought we'd give the Phoenician a try given its reputation. Unfortunately, this hotel no longer seeks to uphold that reputation and certainly does not merit "luxury," given our experience. 

ROOMS NOT READY BY CHECKIN TIME. We checked in online using the Marriott Bonvoy app two days before our arrival, specifying our arrival at 2pm (normal checkin is 4pm). Our travel agent made a reservation for us, and confirmed the day before that the hotel "was ready for us."  We arrived to the hotel later than planned - at 4:35pm - about 35 minutes after the guaranteed check in time of 4pm. We were told our room (Grand Deluxe Casita, which we reserved) was not ready despite being past checkin time, and notably that they DID NOT KNOW when it would be ready - could be 5 minutes, 30 minutes, or more, they said (it's one thing if it's a few minutes, but no clear defined time despite being past checkin time?). We had a dinner reservation across town, so the hotel's inability to pinpoint the readiness of the room well after the checkin time was concerning. I requested a different room, but they said they only had a lower level/class room than the one I reserved and all other Grand Deluxe Casitas were taken.  They did offer a "temporary room" to change/shower while ours was being prepped, to which we agreed because we had no other choice. 

SUSPECT SALES STAFF. Our agent asked how things were going and I told her the truth. She followed up with the hotel. This is where things went a bit off the rails... 

To our shock, the hotel sales director wrote our agent: "We will follow-up with Mr xxx on Sunday and inquire about how we may enhance their stay with us.  We provided a Casita guest room Grand Deluxe view upon check-in at 3:49 but they expressed that they preferred a different casita location and there was a brief wait for the next room to become available." 

This was patently FALSE. 
1) We arrived at 4:35pm, NOT at 3:49. As proof, I have a time stamped receipt from my car rental agency showing I picked up the car at the airport, nearly 30 mins away, at 3:57pm. So this was clearly untrue. 
2) The GRAND DELUXE room is what I initially reserved, and they specifically told me that nothing was available at that level. Now they are saying the opposite; and 
3) NO ONE reached out on Sunday because... well, they don't care.

It is one thing to fail in providing a service, it's another for a sales director to blatantly make up false stories about the Platinum Level guest's experience to their travel agent. Really in poor taste.**

**Update** - Sales staff reached out after being called out and backpedaled, offering to waive resort fees and provide a small credit. I appreciate the acknowledgement and the credit, but it does not change the experience or relieve the incompetence. 

Other issues we encountered: 

- The valet simply gives you the keys, doesn't drive the car around, even if the car is on the other side of the carport. This is fine for most resorts, but not at this level. Perhaps I'd be treated differently if my rental was a Lambo.

- The entire front desk was in a back room during check in, with only one person serving customers even though there was a long line. Occasionally, another person would appear from the back to relieve the line, but it seemed as though they were holding a meeting during the busy check in time. Odd, but again, seems like they a third rate hotel when it comes to service.

- Rooms are very dated, even the coveted casitas. Ours was much smaller than expected with a very loud HVAC and odd shower setup. The pillows are horrible (flat as a pancake as soon as you put your head down). Sadly, this is not unique to this hotel, but it certainly doesn't help. 

- Calling for service took an average of 5 minutes of hold time before anyone answered on Monday morning and Sunday morning (around 9am). Keep this in mind if you are in hurry - apparently, they are understaffed at all levels: housekeeping to front desk.

However, the views of the Camelback mountain are amazing during sunrise and sunset.

The hotel location is also superb : very close to old town (10 minutes) with restaurants and night life, the large shopping center is only about 7 minutes away, and the airport is relatively close as well. 

If you are into hiking, the Cholla Trail entrance to climb the Camelback mountain is an easy walk directly from the hotel. This is a fantastic albeit advanced level hike. 

The Golf Club and the attached pub "The Tavern" had good service from hosts to the bartenders to the waiters and bussing staff. They had a good food selection, included beer tastings at 11am (part of the resort fee), and well-placed TVs to watch the game.  Service at the lobby bar is also good; not the friendliest bar tenders, but the wait staff was very professional and courteous. 

It's too bad. As a Platinum Bonvoy member I really hoped for a better experience. I think the management and staff are just too preoccupied with satisfying the myriad of conventions/large groups that stay here to care about a small family/couple of business travelers.

reviews.author: MPudists
reviews.title: The weather may have been lousy but The Phoenician was great
reviews.text:
First let me say everybody at this property is incredibly gracious. Second, the physical beauty of the grounds are hard to beat. The public spaces are gorgeous. 

I came with my 92 year old mom who has mobility issues. I wanted her to have a week in the sun. Sadly the weather was dreadful. Which is why I upgraded us for a charge from our deluxe guest room to a suite. Both rooms have nice beds and linens with oversized bathrooms. I loved the soaking tub. Our suite was the better option because it was brighter and had lovely balconies so she could relax and read. 

Things I liked about this property: first and foremost the staff (Cheyanne at reception was a star). We enjoyed lunch at Cotton and Mowery. The self-park is a nice option. I got us a car after it became clear hanging out by the pool was not an option. The pool complex is great! I think this would be a terrific option for families. The kids have a water slide and there are dedicated adult areas. Their spa is beautiful. We didn’t have treatments but we did have blowouts at Drybar. We enjoyed cocktails at the Thirsty Camel.  The gym is well equipped. 

Things that need some work: room service (truly the food quality was dreadful) and housekeeping. I don’t know what the deal was but just dumb things like not refilling the in room Keurig coffee pods and creamers. Making only one of the beds in our suite. Weirdest of all, a drenching wet carpet in the master bedroom corner. It must be a busted pipe or hvac thing but it spread to a 4 ft radius and nobody did a thing. There’s no way housekeeping missed it your shoes would squish on the carpet. This property has been here a long time and the upkeep is a 24 hour job. Just a little more attention to detail in the housekeeping department would be appreciated.

reviews.author: Gary H
reviews.title: Taking away more and more from loyal customers
reviews.text:
I had just seen U2 in Vegas and wanted to extend my vaca someplace a little warmer, so my friends and I decided to spend 5 days in Phoenix.

The Phoenician is a beautiful property in Scottsdale and it's also pretty close to a lot of great shopping and restaurants.

I'm a Platinum Elite member of Bonvoy so I get special perks from Marriott properties. I've been to tons of Marriott properties and when you check they offer either 1,000 points or breakfast for 2 for the stay. It always seemed like an odd choice, I mean unless you don't eat breakfast? We took the breakfast. Another perk is being offered an upgrade (if available). No upgrade was available.

We checked into our room. We got in after midnight, so bedtime was fairly immediate. Breakfast is served at a nice restaurant at the main hotel, Mowry & Cotton. The menu has a nice selection of choices. The first day I had their French Toast. It was exceptional. When we got back to the room, I finally opened the curtains and there was a huge surprise. There was a wall very close to the balcony. Maybe a couple feet and it was as high to block pretty much everything. I really couldn't believe my eyes. I really had no idea what was going on? How could a hotel be built like this? 

Excepting this wall was for real and not some kind of prank I thought this is the kind of room you would give to your worst customer. And yet here I was, a Plat Elite staring at a wall?

A made a call and low and behold another room was available and we eventually moved over to the new room and the vaca could continue. Unfortunately for myself the next day I got some kind of sinus infection which would slow me down for the rest of the trip, but my 2 friends enjoyed their time at the pools. The pools are very nice. 3 big pools, 2 Jacuzzis, hundreds of lounge chairs, although Marriott has started a new policy where the best chairs are roped off and you have to pay more money to sit there. Status means nothing for these chairs.

On the day we were checking out I received an email with the final bill. When checking it I noticed the breakfast charges were a bit high, considering we were supposed to get credit for 2 breakfasts each day. Btw, this restaurant includes the tip. I thought that was odd. I missed it on the first day, so they got a nice big tip that day. I called about and the front desk couldn't explain it. A manager from the restaurant called me a told me the free breakfast was only 1 choice on the menu. Mostly everything on the breakfast menu was over $22, but the last breakfast on the menu, the Continental was around $15. I think it was yogurt and a croissant. He asked if anyone, the front desk, any waiter or waitress, had explained this and I told him no, no one has said anything about it. He told me he would make some adjustments, and I said fine.

The bill I received was $399. btw, valet parking was $38 and self was $28. We went with the valet.

So nobody got back to me so I stopped by the front desk to ask for a final bill. The woman printed it out, but something still didn't add up. She said she would review it and call me. She called later after we left the hotel and said she was going to take off $120 and I said that was great.

Later I received a new email and the grand total now was over $600. That's right, the bill actually went up. Once again, beyond belief. I called and asked if a manager could contact me.

Not feeling well the last 4 days I was at the hotel made this exiting experience even worse.

$399 (old bill) - $120 = $279

$612 (new bill) - $279 = $333, so since I contacted the front desk about charges for breakfast I am now paying $213 more than that bill. I know that was hard to follow, but it's because there are more than 1 moving parts.

I'm home now, and no one has contacted me.

A very nice resort, but as you can see, the hotel has some issues, and it all rubs the wrong was for Marriott and its guests.  

I really hate writing negative reviews, but I gave this hotel several chances to explain themselves, but I feel I'm being ignored.

A wall.

reviews.author: Kay G
reviews.title: Consistently a lovely experience.
reviews.text: This is still one of my favorite hotels after 25 years and many stays.  The quality of the experience has remained consistently high. Bar, restaurant, spa, tennis, pool service, golf and room comfort are all excellent.  And service staff is excellent throughout.

reviews.author: Brad C
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort with Top Notch Staff!
reviews.text:
I spent five days here for a work meeting and was very impressed. The hotel is beautiful, clean and well-maintained. But what stood out to me was the staff. Every single staff member I encountered was friendly. Whether it's front desk staff, food service or cleaning crews, everyone was personable. I spent significant time in meeting rooms with small groups well into the evening hours and any staff member that would see us was willing to get whatever we needed. 

The tavern was great and as a Celiac I appreciated them carrying a gluten-free beer. That isn't something you see everywhere. All of our catered meals also had gluten-free options. But if I had to give the hotel one negative check, it would be the catering food. It was good but not excellent like the rest of the resort. But I wouldn't hold that against them - feeding hundreds of people at the same time can't be easy.

reviews.author: Alex T
reviews.title: Gold and nice but weird
reviews.text: This is a weird hotel. The rooms are a good size, and the bathrooms are of a style that I think really date the place - I can't put my finger on it.  We saw some really weird behaviour from guests during our stay... which I hope was not normal, VS part of the clientele.  The staff however were fantastic.  We had a fantastic night initially at the firepit and our wait staff were so wonderful - explained the drinks and helped with recommendations. Later that evening the weather turned and we moved to the bar and the staff there were also wonderful. There was live music there one evening, which I am not sure is every night... however this one guy was doing sort of nu metal rock songs solo... occasionally covers, including one of that song Pumped Up Kicks about school shootings, so that was.... weird and odd,in this lavish gold setting surrounded by people dressed fairly nicely eating chicken wings. Was not expecting that experience. The valet and check-in staff were very helpful and friendly.  Our room was in the main building.  The balcony faced out over the lawn but we were not high enough to take in the views - but I enjoyed those from the fire pits near the bar!

reviews.author: Samdyredm1
reviews.title: Very disappointing
reviews.text:
Very disappointed.   The Phoenician shouldn’t be part of the luxury collection.  It is not nearly in the same league as other luxury hotels we have stayed at.     We are ambassador elite and have stayed at a lot of great hotels - Bonvoy and other brands.  We were disappointed from the moment we arrived.  Probably the worst check in experience ever.  The front desk manager was rude and ineffective. Our room was not ready at the time requested.  Waited  several hours.  We had to ask for assistance with our bags.    We wanted to sit by a quiet luxurious pool and enjoy a steam or sauna since we were paying to stay at a luxury resort and just wanted to relax.  We were told that we could not use the spa without both of us having a treatment .  Cheapest treatment starts at about $220.    We did not want a treatment or have time for one. And no appointments were available any way. . We were told there was no way we could use the spa and that they did not even offer paid access for hotel guests.  Basically the spa is a stand alone entity  and hotel guests are not allowed to use it .   After a prolonged discussion the spa manager did allow us to sit by the pool .  The place was empty except for a loud group of girls .  The sauna was not hot. The spa pool had no view. Not at all what you would expect for a luxury spa. 
The Propery is large and dated and soulless.  Really more like a Marriott not a luxury collection.  We booked a suite which was large but dated. Not well appointed at all. The main lobby has a patio with a nice view but the rest of the property does not have a view. The pool area is crowded with chairs.  All the good spots are “reserved” for extra charge. Not at all a luxury experience.  The jw marriott camel back is far nicer and far more upscale and sophisticated.   The Phoenician exudes a false sense of grandeur.   The room service breakfast was incredibly expensive. $180 for 2 people. We only ordered bacon and eggs and berries.   Ridiculously over priced.  The room was also very expensive.   Really a terrible “luxury “ experience.  Terrible service.  Bad ambiance.  Way better places to stay in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: CX
reviews.title: 這間飯店真的非常的大
reviews.text: 這間飯店真的非常的大，包括進來可能都需要導航，而且有很大的高爾夫球場，如果想要爬山的話，也是從這裡上去。總之這是一家非常高級的飯店健身房游泳池餐廳，會議廳，各樣設施應有盡有。

reviews.author: TAJ1231
reviews.title: Exceeded my expectations
reviews.text: I was quite impressed with the luxury hotel.  I was here for a business conference and wow! The grounds are expansive.  On a leisure occasion I would've gotten a golf cart to tour the grounds. My room view was not overlooking the pool but the mountain and city backdrop was nice.    Check in was swift and the staff were kind.  I had a drink at the Thristy Camel and the bartender recreated a drink I saw advertised on the room television.  The outside seating was comfortable with a beautiful fire pit.  Majority of the food served was enjoyable. My only regret was not making time for their spa.  I did enjoy the bathroom in my suite. It had a large step down tub that I certainly enjoyed after a long  day of networking.  Room service was also pretty good, which I enjoyed on my balcony because the weather was amazing.  Delivery was quicker than planned.  This hotel is definitely pricey, but hotel quality was top tier.

reviews.author: Rose M
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds, outdated dusty rooms
reviews.text: Booked stay for a few days. The grounds are stunning. I was underwhelmed by the room. It was dusty and old with weird staining on the walls. Unfortunately the staff was unable to find alternate better accommodation. Would carefully select room before staying.

reviews.author: Daniel C
reviews.title: Thankful for the corporate rate
reviews.text:
My wife and stayed at the Phoenician as the host hotel of the conference I was attending. We were graciously upgraded to a casita meaning that it had a large outdoor patio including a fire pit as well as a nice view of the pool area and Camelback Mountain.

Overall, my wife and I had an enjoyable stay however there were many issues (some minor and some more significant) that distracted from the enjoyment of our stay as a whole. 

These issues include the following:

All hot food at the conference breakfasts and lunches were lukewarm at best. The steaks we were served during our conference dinner were all cooked medium well. When our table asked them to be cooked medium they came back medium rare.

A tray of leftover room service food was left outside our room from a nearby guest for over a day and was only removed when I alerted housekeeping.

Although we were told the pool was heated neither I nor my wife nor other people I spoke to thought that was the case and was probably the reason why very few guest went into the pool even though the outside temperature during our stay was in the mid 80s

All the gates to the pool area were always unlocked and therefore anyone not staying at the hotel could have easily entered the pool area. This is probably the reason why some past reviews have mentioned that they had valuables stolen while at the pool.

The issues mentioned in this review might seem trivial to some howver the hotel advertises that they are the premier resort in Arizona. In order to justify this designation, it is my view that the issues that I encountered during my stay should not have occurred. I was also fortunate enough to pay the corporate rate as part of the meeting I was attending at the time. If however I would have paid the full price for my room which was listed on their website at more than $1,000 per night I would have been sorely disappointed.

reviews.author: Amy H
reviews.title: Disappointing not what would we would expect
reviews.text:
