Long story short we were celebrating our parents 50th anniv staff never delivered champagne to the room as they agreed to, our casita was on the main road you could hear all the street noise, requested to move waited an hour for the key to find out the room was upstairs which was not mentioned previously we are not putting our parents upstairs with luggage, ok so now we are late to dinner, walking back saw 15+ sewer roaches, no light on the patio at our room so we couldn’t see each other so went to bed we were wanting to visit with my sister and brother , water leaked all over food in fridge had to toss. Filled out Marriott survey received an email from Rooms Ops Manger Benjamin Fredericks; no response.sent another email to him  no response, We will back in Scottsdale next month so plan on popping in and discussing with management. Cancelling Marriott card which is fine the are other options so that’s no problem. Had just arrived from Canada staff at Fairmont Banff were incredible!
Truly a disappointing experience had been looking forward to this night for a long time, even more disappointing that a a manger doesn’t have the decency to reply to an email.

reviews.author: KN
reviews.title: Beautiful, friendly staff
reviews.text: We spent a night at the Phoenician over the Summer and it did not disappoint!  The resort itself is beautiful and we loved going on walks and even a bike ride (borrowed at the Athletic Club).  Everyone was friendly and our issues/ requests were always taken seriously and promptly addressed.  A special thank you to Virginia Hatfield.

reviews.author: Gio R
reviews.title: A real disappointment
reviews.text:
We arrived with the prospect of an unforgettable vacation, after purchasing an upgrade for the "casita." This prospect was immediately disappointed as soon as we went to bed, as we had to sleep for 6 nights with the air conditioning turned off due to the unbearable noise of the compressor. Once we made a complaint, the only solution was finding a note in the room that said "noise is normal." Perhaps normal for a Motel 6, certainly not for a hotel we paid about $800 a night for. For the first 3 days, the room was only cleaned in the late afternoon, forcing us to wait to re-enter. We even had to ask the maid to bring us sugar packets and a spoon to be able to have a cup of coffee. On two occasions, we found dirty coffee cups from the morning. At the time of checkout, after paying over $6,000, I received a message from my bank showing an additional second charge of over $700. I asked for an explanation at the Front Desk, and I was told that it's a standard practice, and he had no control over this operation. I never authorized this transaction and don't understand why I should be charged for this second one without even presenting the credit card (or a guarantee that I don't know for what), even though this amount was reversed late on the same day.
In fact, the vacation was unforgettable in the sense that I wouldn't return even if they paid me. We spent the 6 nights waiting for the day to come so we could leave the hotel. Furthermore, a good portion of the "casitas" had a view of the street or the parking lot. Unfortunately, many will be misled by the beautiful photo of the casita on their website, which shows a nice view of the lawn...
I am wondering how the hotel would be if they removed the “Luxury Collection” from their brand. As said a Motel 6 would very likely be more comfortable and less expensive, and as someone already wrote there are many better options at a much better price

reviews.author: Chad
reviews.title: Zero Security and the Staff could Care Less
reviews.text:
Online reviews are a tricky beast. With all the AI out there it is quite difficult to discern if you are reading a real experience from a real human. This I can assure you is genuine and mainly intended as a word of caution so no one else has to suffer the experience my wife and I endured at the Phoenician in September of 2023. 

This review has nothing to do with the room quality or amenities or facilities, those are all quite nice and frankly should be for the nightly rate you are paying. This review ties directly to the staff and their lack of care for their guests. 

We were there for a weekend with family and friends attending a wedding. On the day of the wedding my wife went to the pool for one hour by herself. She got her towels and set her things down on a chair. She then received a phone call that she took and spoke for 15 minutes next to the pool with her back turned to the chair. At this time someone grabbed all of her things including her purse and sandals. When she turned back around and realized her things were gone she immediately alerted the staff including waitresses and the towel clerk who had been working the area. This pool probably had 20 guests at the pool at this time, not a lot of activity. All the staff had the same lethargic response, “I am sorry mam, there is nothing we can do.” 

Now let me be crystal clear, we are not ascribing blame directly to the hotel. They certainly cannot be responsible for all guests' belongings at all times and my wife made a costly error in judgment, although an unconscious one, she never should have turned her back to her items. 

We immediately shut down credit cards but saw that the culprit already tried to charge $1,500 at Neiman Marcus just down the street so now we had validation that this was no accident or misplaced items. There was one gentleman that worked the hotel security, I believe his name was Thomas, he was the only one that took any ownership of the issue and seemed to show an ounce of empathy towards our predicament. The extent of effort from the rest of management at the Phoenician was to blink, stand still and continue to say “I am sorry, there is nothing we can do.” One gentleman who worked at the front desk (I wish I had his name) even had the nerve to tell us, “Things get stolen from the pool all the time” as if they had as much control over this as the weather. Further, if that statement is true, maybe an examination of security protocols might be a priority. 

Rather than attend our wedding we spent the reception filling out a police report. We knew the chances of recovery were slim and the financial loss was significant (>$500) but not catastrophic. I can hear the critics whispering, “first world problems.” The point is there is an absolute dearth of security at this resort. I can’t list all the shortcomings but here are a few: There are no cameras anywhere on the three pool decks (at least that is what we were told), All gates to the pools remain wide open at all times. I have stayed at resorts who charge half as much as the phonecian and they still require a room key to access the pools. The parking lot entry attendant showed no enforcement as far as which cars were allowed on property. We were waived through, never asked for a name or room number. If I was a thief I couldn’t ask for a more vulnerable environment. 

Here is the kicker. 7 hours after the purse was first stolen another charge was attempted on our canceled credit card BACK ON THE PHOENICIAN property. We thought this was our chance, how many establishments are even open at 10 PM to accept payment on the property? Less than five we thought. We alerted hotel management immediately and again the blank stares, the nonchalance, complete and utter deflection, “I am sorry, we can’t track that.” How easy would it have been upon our initial claim to tell their staff “If you run a credit card that is denied then alert security immediately.” With today’s tech and ubiquitous communication that is such an easy catch. You would think at $700/night there might be a modicum of effort or assistance for their guests. 

We were routed to some off-sight Marriott risk assessor that did not respond to us for three weeks only to tell us “our investigation results in no compensation to the guest.” I can only imagine the depths they went into such an investigation. 

Moral of the Story: Don’t take anything valuable to the pool 

Second Moral of the Story: Don’t rely on the staff. Their customer service extends as far as reading a script, over and over again. They are sorry, but there is nothing they can do, ahem, willing to do.

reviews.author: Diana L
reviews.title: One Disappointment after Another
reviews.text:
The views are amazing and the bedding is super comfortable. Those are the two highlights.

We did a little staycation last weekend and were disappointed at almost every turn.  Our room was tired and worn with ripped carpeting and mildew in the shower.  Housekeeping requests were not fulfilled until our second night and they removed the room robes after the first night for some inexplicable and inconvenient reason.

The resort itself needs an update.  The pool has tiles falling out along the water line and in general the area looks like it hasn't been updated in 20 years.  The public restrooms on the ground level sorely need an update as well, but really the tired, dated feel permeates the entire resort.

Service in the Thirsty Camel was subpar with guacamole smears on the table when we sat down that we ultimately wiped up ourselves with napkins we had to request at that bar.  We had to ask for water three times and we never received the snack bowls given to other tables.  

Dinner at the steakhouse was also disappointing on several levels.  They placed us at a brightly-lit table where were forced to sit side by side, prohibiting conversation (I know some people like to snuggle at dinner but we prefer discussion so perhaps ask before forcing people into that seating arrangement).  After a long wait for them to arrive, both of our steaks were not cooked properly; one was sent back and returned with the center still raw.  The wine pairings with the tasting menu were mediocre, the worst was the champagne, which resembled Martinelli's.  A bright note at the restaurant, however, was the friendly wait staff service.

As a final insult, the bill included those lovely little junk fees, including the expected resort charge but also $5 a day for housekeeping (really? that's not included in an $800 room charge?) and a porterage charge ($14), we assume for the valet and/or baggage service, which we did not utilize.  Upon questioning the porterage charge, we were told it was a mandatory fee.  

All in all, there are many, many better places to stay in the Valley and I recommend you try them all before checking into the Phoenician. We will not be returning.

reviews.author: pickytraveler58
reviews.title: Exceptional and Friendly
reviews.text: This was our second time to stay at The Phoenician.  The service and the accommodations were wonderful!  I look forward to staying again.  Our room was perfect in every way.  The bathroom was a great size and the walk in shower was very nice.  The staff from the desk clerk to the Valet personnel were very friendly and helpful.  Cleanliness was exceptional.  The Phoenician is my first choice when we visit Scottsdale!

reviews.author: Mike S
reviews.title: Disappointed stay after 30yrs as a frequent guest!
reviews.text: We are an Arizona family that frequently does stay-cations almost every summer at various resorts.  The Phoenician has been the most visited over the past 30 years---until now!!  We were so disappointed with the accounting services from the time we booked, until the minute we drove out of the parking garage.  Our quoted room rates at booking were not honored at the time of check-in.  Our cabana rates were increased as well with no notification or explanation. After no help from staff on duty, we contacted upper management and only received false promises! We have yet to receive the refund that was agreed upon. It is the principle of this issue, not the money.  Please be aware that keeping a file of all your confirmations with booking prices and fees noted is still no guarantee this 5-Star Resort will honor anything that was originally quoted at booking.

reviews.author: juergen l
reviews.title: Luxus Resort
reviews.text:
Imposantes Haus aus den 80igern, das seinend Special Touch noch nicht verloren hat. Das Hotel ist eine Destinationen für sich.

Anreise: In Scottsdale gelegen ist es circa 30 Minuten vom Flughafen. Circa 10 Minuten mit dem Auto zur Fashion Square Mall und zu Old Town Scottsdale Imposante (nicht kontrollierte) Einfahrt, die entlang der Ferienwohnungen und am Golfplatz und am Fitnesskomplex vorbei dann letztendlich im eigentlichen Hotel mündet.

Auf dem Weg zum Hotel passiert man die Canyon Suites. Eigenes Gebäude mit eigenen Empfang und eigenem Pool, etwas teurer. Wir hatten uns dort die Räumlichkeiten zeigen lassen, hatten aber nicht den Eindruck, dass sich der Aufpreis tatsächlich in der Qualität der Räumlichkeiten widerspiegelt, da man im eigentlichen Hotel ohnehin schon auf extrem hohen Niveau ist.
Allerdings ist bei den Canyon Suites (es gibt dort auch „normale“ Zimmer) das Frühstück bereits inbegriffen. Die Poollandschaft des Haupthauses kann man natürlich mit benutzen.

Check In: imposante Vorfahrt mit regionaler Kunst, gespickt. Freundliche Begrüßung durch die Valets, die sofort das Gepäck Aufnahmen und es Richtung Lobby brachten. Check In verlief freundlich und reibungslos. Leider keine kleine Aufmerksamkeit für Kinder. Karte als Überblick wurde ausgehändigt. Guter Concierge Desk.

Die Lobby selbst wird von großen Panoramafenstern und mittiger Bar bestimmt. Lebhafte Lobby zum verweilen.

Zimmer: Zimmer über vier Etagen. Lobby selbst ist im 3. OG. Erst ab Deluxe Pool View hat man einen wirklich schönen Blick. Ansonsten gehen die Zimmer Richtung Hotel - Vorfahrt oder Richtung Berge.

Sehr große Zimmer, mit Sitzecke und großem bestuhlten Balkon. Nicht mehr ganz taufrisch, gut funktionierende Klimaanlage, Kaffeemaschine mit Pads, großes Bad, mit separater Dusche und Badewanne. Viele Ablagemöglichkeiten gut beleuchtet.

Pools/Spa/Fitness: wirklich schöne Pool Landschaft über drei Stufen. Davon ein Pool, nur für Erwachsene; sehr angenehme Wasser Temperaturen. Ausreichend Liegen mit Sonnenschirmen. Weiche Auflagen. Schnelle Wasserrutsche für die Kids + Splash Pad. Sehr großzügig gestaltet. Hinter den Pool befindet sich dann das  separates Spa Gebäude und dahinter der Golfclub.
Fitnessclub für ein Hotel auf Weltklasse Niveau. 24 Stunden. Alles neu!

Für Kids: wie gesagt, große Poollandschaft und Wasserrutsche ist ein Highlight für alle Kids. Zudem gibt es einen großen, mit zahlreichen Videospielen ausgestatteten Game Room unterhalb des Fitness Centers.

Auch wird ein KidsClub angeboten. Allerdings wirkt dieser wenig ansprechen und die Aktivitäten kosten zusätzlich und sind limitiert. Das ginge bei solch ein Luxusadresse sicherlich besser .

Essen: tolles Fleisch im Steakhouse J&G im Obergeschoss. Ansonsten gibt es noch einen Coffee Shop mit gutem Frühstück und frischen Lunch. Lobby mit Snacks. Das Restaurant im Golfclub haben wir nicht besucht. Das Gartenrestaurant war leider geschlossen Mowry&Cotton.

Personal: besonders gut bei Valet und Concierge. Front Desk, mal so mal so. Housekeeping top! Restaurants: das geht besser - J&G unorganisiert.

Fazit: beeindruckendes Luxus-Haus mit toller Poollandschaft und exzellentem Fitness Club. Zimmer könnten einen Refresh vertragen. Personal mal so mal so. Bei Kindern könnte man sich etwas mehr Mühe geben.

Empfehlung

reviews.author: Susan S
reviews.title: Luxurious pet friendly hotel
reviews.text: Chef Renaldo asked if we had our dog with us as we finished our meal. 15 minutes later we were presented with a frozen yogurt with blueberries and carrots treat and a special meal of meat and vegetables for our dog, Honey. Dining at the Phoenician Tavern is a casual affair although there us nothing casual about the menu from burgers to hangar steak. Save room for the cobbler or cookies dessert (or both to share). Less than a 5 minute walk from our comfortable Casita, the outdoor balcony is pet friendly when weather permits. Our Casita is nearly 600 square feet with patio leading to lawn area, a soaking tub  two separate sink areas and a large walk in closet. My husband wants to ask the brand of mattress,  they are that comfortable. Beautiful walking paths made that much more special when spotting cotton tail bunnies scampering about. 4 paws up from Honey!

reviews.author: Cyndee W
reviews.title: Moving our son back to school.
reviews.text: To begin I had called the resort prior to arrival to see if we could have some bulky items delivered there to aid in moving my son into his new apartment for his junior year at ASU.  I was advised we could and upon check in worked with the concierge to find the item.  Our first room had a door lock problem.  No worries-after a fix attempt we were moved to another beautiful room where our package was waiting. Our request for extra pillows and towels were filled and kept every day in our amazingly large, clean, cool and comfortable room overlooking the pools and mountains.  Everyone to whom we spoke was kind, respectful and accommodating.  The pools, yes, pools, were each beautiful and clean.  My son thoroughly enjoyed his massage.  The valets always had our car ready to roll, helped us pack and unpack it- all while offering and wiping condensation from chilled bottles of water. The location of the resort is spectacular too- literal moments from downtown Scottsdale.  After we moved our son in my husband and I were still able to find quiet pockets of adult space even with the families in attendance. My only “complaint” is that mowry and cotton closed for maintenance after out first enjoyable experience.  I guess maintenance has to be done sometime.  Overall we had an amazing experience with beautiful accommodations and wonderful people at a great location.  Many thanks.

reviews.author: Ryan B
reviews.title: Thank you Phoenician staff!
reviews.text:
Absolutely incredible in all aspects. Hands down the best service. Not inexpensive, but you get what you pay for. Registration staff were amazing. Pool staff amazing (hunted down an umbrella for us!). Housekeeping staff - amazing and helpful. Beautiful property. Wonderful room. Beautiful views. Good food. Good drinks. Good times. 

Heaven on earth. Thank you, Phoenician staff. Great job!

reviews.author: Johnny P
reviews.title: Unforgettable experience…we felt like part of the Phoenician family
reviews.text:
I’ve written many reviews, but this one will be my favorite one to write. 

We just completed a bucket list stay with a group of friends to celebrate my husband and to enjoy time with dear friends prior to him entering hospice for cancer. From the moment we arrived, our stay was magical. 

Jeff at the bell desk was so kind, welcoming and personable. He took care of us and got us settled and made sure we knew how special the hotel wanted this trip to be.  

Lisa, the Resort Manager, met us and welcomed us to the hotel and made us feel so special. To have someone in such an important role take the time to meet us meant the world to us.

Regarding Daniel, the Senior Sales Manager, I truly have no words.  Daniel went so far above and beyond in all ways to ensure we felt like family, to make every moment exceptional and to experience a vacation like no other. He is not just incredible at his job, he is one of the kindest people we’ve ever met. 

Our suite….beyond anything we’ve ever stayed in, and we’ve stayed in some of the finest hotels in the world. Five star design, the ultimate in luxury, exceptional care and cleanliness and one of those “we will never top this” experiences.

Dino at the lobby bar….he’s fantastic and so personable. Truly enjoyed our evenings at the bar because of him!

Melissa, our server at J&G, she’s phenomenal. So fun, so sincere and so good at her job, we had a ball with her!

Christine, our cabana server, she is fantastic! We had the best day with her and she took amazing care of our group! She is so fun and made it the perfect day.

Lexi, bartender at Mowry & Cotton, she is fabulous! She is so engaging and kind, we went back daily to see her and always had amazing service and so much fun!

Thank you Phoenician team, this was a life changing vacation and you gave us memories we will cherish the rest of our lives. You all are truly incredible and truly a family.

reviews.author: Gabriella D
reviews.title: All in one spot!
reviews.text: The room was comfortable, bed and pillows were perfect! Very clean hotel. They offer everything- multiple pools, spa, golf course, game room, tennis courts, pickle ball courts, bikes to ride into Scottsdale. Happy hour was nice for half the price and live music. They also have small shops. I did order room service unfortunately steak was not cooked to order it came well done when ordered medium however the burger was on point! Dessert do even bother for the price.

reviews.author: AroundTheWorld
reviews.title: Disappointing first impression
reviews.text:
First, the good: Beautiful grounds/pool and excellent pool side service team. Lovely gym and spa, and fantastic service every morning at Mowry and Cotton. The team at the activities group was also super friendly. 

Now, why the 2 rating? Cleanliness of the room was not up to typical Marriott standards. Multiple issues lead me to believe other housekeeping items could have been overlooked. First, a questionable towel with rust and black ash like stains under the sofa cushion (def did not end up using the sofa bed) a hole in the sheet on one of the beds, and water left in the coffee maker from the previous guest. If these small things were overlooked, what else might have been? Ant infestation in the game room (crawling on the gaming machine). $45 resort fee when barely any included amenities listed in the resort fee can be used this time of the year. Internet was spotty/kept dropping out, so I used my hotspot instead, and even though they told us we would not hear construction noise, on our last morning while working from our room, it was disruptive. Our door also did not shut without a firm close. 

The quality of the front desk service and concierge was also lacking, especially for a resort of this caliber and cost. When I asked about where I might find a corkscrew, the front desk staff didn’t know, so I asked if they might be able to find one from room service or elsewhere. He called someone and they said they didn’t know. Turns out there is one in the mini snack bar. 

My husband is also titanium for life and has proven very loyal to Marriott over the years. We were supposed to take a trip to Vancouver to celebrate his 40th but a family emergency prevented it so we planned a staycation here instead. The concierge at the JW went out of his way prior to tell me he’d arrange a little something to celebrate his birthday, but we unfortunately never made it. When I called the concierge at the Phoenician to see if they would make a note that  we were celebrating his birthday trip on the reservation they said yes and they’d acknowledge it and at least say happy birthday. Come check in, nothing, not even a verbal happy birthday. We had to remind them about our breakfast benefits at check in or else they wouldn’t have said anything, and then when we asked about terms and conditions on something, we had to show her the terms and conditions, and then, only then did her colleague rectify it. The onus should not be on the customer to show a property its terms and conditions. 

We’ve had much better experiences at the JW Marriott and Kierland locally and many others across the globe. Was curious about this resort, but based on experience and cost, I’d gladly pick one of those properties over this one if I had to do it again, due to service alone. It’s a beautiful property, but you can find many other nice properties around for this price or less with much, much better service.

reviews.author: CN
reviews.title: Arrival experience turned around!  Thank you!!
reviews.text:
Thank you, thank you, thank you Carmella.  You exceeded our expectations and set us up for the family vacation we were hoping for.

Honestly, thank you is not enough. We are grateful for you.  You "heard" me when I explained our arrival experience.  I didn't have to go into a lot of detail.  You are incredible and we are very thankful for all you did turn our experience around .

Cherie

reviews.author: Cheri T
reviews.title: The weekend at The Phoenician
reviews.text:
The Phoenician was a wonderful weekend get away.  The property is high end, the pools are clean, and the rooms are lovely.  The beds are luxurious and very comfortable.  The did a 15 minute fireworks show in the lawn at the Spa.

Since it is high end, look to spend money with every move you make.  We got room service one night and it was over $100 for 2 salads.  There is no complementary shuttle service, so you have to Uber even 1 mile away to the Scottsdale mall.

Down sides:  The check-in took at least 30 minutes, only 1 Representative at the desk at 7pm.  We called the concierge, no answer.  We rented a car onsite, and the door was closed the majority of the time (3rd party vendor).  You have to go down to the pool early to secure an umbrella, because people fight over them.  The pool staff is very efficient and gave great service.  We waited too long to book services in the spa, they were full for the weekend.

I will definitely return, but may try the Biltmore, or Princess next time through Marriott.  We got recommendations from a lady at the pool that those are definitely places to check out as well.

reviews.author: Dougie D
reviews.title: Fouth of July weekend NIGHMARE
reviews.text:
Fourth of July NIGHTMARE.  As Scottsdale locals and Marriott Bonvoy members, we have frequented the Phoenician and many other Resorts in the area.  The Phoenician was always top notch, which is why we flew my 78 year old father out for a visit with his Grandchildren for the fourth of July weekend.

My Father arrived and spent time with my children in the pool and then went up to his room for a nap.  My husband and I ordered drinks and food for our family (using our credit card)  What happened next was nothing less than harassment. 

Even though we provided and validated my Father's room information, we were aggressively accused of being "resort crashers".  Unreal. My Father just lost his wife and came out to be with family and that's what he gets.  Phoenician, get your act together.

reviews.author: shopworksgal
reviews.title: The Phoenician is NOT what it use to be!
reviews.text: I lived in the valley & hosted events, & dinners at the resort over the years but I haven’t been there in probably 7 years. I was shocked and saddened by my experience as I attended a recent conference. My room was a disaster & I had to be moved. The room had dirty sheets, someone’s leftover dry cleaning plastic/hangers on the closet floor, dirty ceiling and walls. The staff were equally mortified and I was moved to another room. The new room was much improved even though there was a strange stain on the ceiling above the bed and the first towel I opened to use had black streaks on the towel. The restaurant experience was poor, the 27 dollar hamburger came out warm, cooked the wrong temperature and there was a very small container of warm fries, nothing came out hot. We ordered the Brussel sprouts but they were undercooked, hard and difficult to chew, we sent them back. The front desk staff were lovely, understanding and apologetic, and quite frankly the only positive thing i can say about my stay, but the entire experience was so disappointing that I walked away saying I would never stay there again! The room rate for the conference was $268. And normally over $600. It wasn’t even worth the $268, to be honest. Yes the views are lovely but in the end it was NOT a luxury experience.

reviews.author: Global Trekking
reviews.title: Luxury Hotel
reviews.text: Attended a convention at this resort. Great experience overall the food quality was good and plenty of dining options are available onsite. Great views of Camelback Mountain with a trail providing  acess for a  day hike. The staff was friendly and the service was great.

reviews.author: Ateamtravels1018
reviews.title: Amazing stay with a bonus!
reviews.text: I had an amazing stay at The Phoenician Scottsdale. This is the only Forbes Five Star and AAA Five Diamond hotel in the Phoenix area⁹, and it truly lives up to its reputation. The resort is located on the picturesque Phoenician grounds, with stunning views of Camelback Mountain and the Sonoran Desert. The rooms and suites are spacious, elegant, and comfortable, with beautiful furnishings and outdoor patios/terraces with large, round daybeds. My kids loved it, the Atalanta Braves had a game in Phoenix and they were staying at the resort, my boys got to pose with one of the players!  The resort also offers a variety of amenities, such as an exclusive infinity pool with private cabanas, a golf course, a spa, and several dining options. This is the perfect place to relax, unwind, and enjoy the best of Scottsdale. I highly recommend this resort to anyone looking for a luxurious and memorable experience.

reviews.author: handhos
reviews.title: Not off to a good start at all
reviews.text: I use to really love visiting this property over the years.  Hadn’t been here in quite some time.  So, I was excited to return, but unfortunately, very surprised to try to check in at 4:15 and no room in sight.  Even with our lifetime titanium ambassador status, there was just very low care level and nonchalance  to the fact there were no rooms, but they did offer us a bottle of water and a map.  Lots of bags in the lobby bar and watching others go up to check on rooms with no luck.  Would definitely make a different decision next time if you are coming from east coast, need to get ready for a dinner, etc…not even a manager saying sorry or offering a drink.  Sad for such a lovely property.

reviews.author: ncinaz
reviews.title: Definitely not a luxury experience
reviews.text: The Phoenician may be part of the Luxury Collection, but it is decidedly not a luxury experience, at least on this most recent visit. The hotel was packed for Memorial Day weekend and we were given an "upgraded" room in the casita areas. The casita rooms themselves are decent but the building's stairway and exterior might as well be from a run-down apartment building. I used points but rooms were running about $700 a night and I would be none too pleased to pay that to be in a building like this. We had dinner at Mowry and Cotton and I received a comically small piece of salmon for an entree. It looked more like a single piece of sushi. Breakfast the next morning was an absolute cattle call. We had to wait 30 minutes for a table. That said, the front desk and pool staff were all friendly and helpful. The reception desk at Mowry and Cotton was thoroughly overwhelmed and never sent a text message that our table was ready. Don't expect a luxury experience at the pools either, as all of them were packed and there were not attendants to help with getting seats.

reviews.author: Brett S
reviews.title: Major Need Of Repairs and Renovations
reviews.text: This hotel is in major need of maintenance and customer service. The first issue I had was the toilet seat was broken. It took them 3 hours to come and fix it as the front desk stated they had numerous maintenance calls. I didn't get that resolved until almost 2am. The next issue is their shower was broken. Water barely came out, which is not the worst part of it. The worst part is the fact that they had a loose handle and the screw was so loose that it came out. I almost stepped on a screw while I was showering at a 5 diamond hotel. This place should be no more than a 2 diamond. Lastly, I visited their pool in the evening to notice that everyone had maintenance issues. There was tile missing everywhere and the areas it was missing, the objects were sharp. I came close to cutting myself several times against the wall so I left the pool area. AAA and Forbes, you need to revisit this place and downgrade them.

reviews.author: Avi Baron
reviews.title: Rip off , not nice as it seems.
reviews.text:
Terrible experience. 
False advertisement- they offer a $200 spa credit , when we came to claim it they said “spa if fully booked) and they weren’t willing to accommodate in anything else using this credit. 
On top of that manager was rude and unprofessional. 
We also ask for a crib for our baby when we checked in and the front desk said she’s taking care of that . than we went out and came back at night - hotel failed to deliver crib to the room. 
So baby woke up and kind of ruin the moment till the crib arrived. 

On top of all of that - I saw $550 extra charges on my credit card , we call them - they lied and said that chase failed to pay them with the points , spoke with chase the agent said that’s not true , than called the hotel again and they said finally that they made an error and they will refund us the money.
They refund only portion but I seriously don’t have the energy chasing them for $100. 

I paid over $600 per night for an hotel that considering itself as high end- there was nothing high end in this hotel. Terrible experience. 
Definitely not recommended.

reviews.author: ClaudeWormwood
reviews.title: Great Time at the Phoenician
reviews.text: Loved the Phoenician. The staff was attentive and friendly and made sure the little things were done correctly (pool, front desk, concierge, valet) which to me is a sign of a quality resort. Grounds were beautiful and well maintained. There was a conference that overlapped our stay, which initially concerned me but the conference folks occupied their little areas and left plenty of (empty) hotel for the regular guests. Room was big and comfortable and housekeeping seemed to know our schedule and pop in to make up the room while we were out. If I were forced to find a negative, it would be the pool temperature… a little warm but assuming hard to keep the pool cool when it’s 100 degrees every day. Family and I had a great experience and would definitely come back again.

reviews.author: John M
reviews.title: Please avoid this dreadful Property
reviews.text: Please do yourself a favor and avoid this property at all costs. I used to stay here years ago before Marriott bought them and it was lovely. Now, I’m sad to say it is a low grade Sheraton! We checked into the lobby and the noise was so loud from conferences that we could hardly here the agent at registration. The room was very tired and quite dirty. The lobby and outside was littered from drinks the the conference people had and  they looked understaffed. Thankfully I was able to book at the Fairmont Princess and evacuate this dreadful property. I will say the girl at the registration desk was very helpful, she apologized for the appearance of the property. The Fairmont is stunning and I’m so happy I’ll stay here the next 4 days. I highly recommend the Fairmont, rooms are beautiful and the staff is amazing!

reviews.author: Coconut1178
reviews.title: Beautiful Area Beautiful Pools
reviews.text:
The hotel is close to the airport, old Scottsdale, the Amazing mall and so many fantastic places to dine. A wonderful location. The pools are beautiful and the service was wonderful at the pools. Everyone was working very hard. 

We did have a cabana one day, very nice. A little overpriced --- but it was a nice experience. 

Double check your room before unpacking. They gave us the wrong room and it was a little hectic getting moved into the RIGHT room category. It took 24 hours. 

The team could do a better job at communication. I felt I was always calling to double check and triple check questions we had during our stay and/or requests. It's became very frustrating. 

The spa is amazing! I really wish I would have booked two treatments instead of one. Classy, relaxing, nice and a beautiful setting. This is not to be missed! 

Finally the GYM! WoW....a hotel who really built an amazing gym. The equipment and space were five stars. Tennis and so much to do. Biking, hiking too. But the gym is really so beautiful. The views, the sunlight and the wonderful scented towels (that are so refreshing). 

Enjoy!! 

Dining recommendations: Burbon and Bones and Toca Madera off property. 

On property all the places were lovely in their own way. It was very nice sitting outside in the Lobby Bar. Relaxing.

reviews.author: Margaret V
reviews.title: Expensive for crowded and slightly dated resort
reviews.text: Resort was crowded and a bit dated/tired.  Service was off including our keyless entry pad ran out of batteries and it took 30 minutes for security to arrive to let us back in our room.  I’d stay elsewhere for the price.

reviews.author: K B
reviews.title: Beautful grounds
reviews.text:
Beautiful resort with friendly & professional staff. 

Stayed for a business conference. Food was delicious for all meals. 

The view from the pool is breathtaking. 

Gym is a bit of a walk since it has its own building but the walk isn’t too bad and has a nice view. 

Easy to get Uber yo and from airport. Downtown area is not too far

reviews.author: MN1445
reviews.title: Customers allowed to eat in the pools.
reviews.text:
We loved this hotel, with the exception of the fact that they allowed a large group of VIP customers to stand and eat food in the middle of the adult only pool. This was unsanitary as they were dropping crumbs and sauces into the pool water. Food trays lined the edge of the pool. When we complained to the pool attendant, we were told that it was allowed despite a large sign beside the pool saying no food is allowed to be consumed while swimming. We ended up having to go to a family pool, which was unfortunate because our group was 18+. When we tried to reach the manager by phone (several times) about this issue, no one returned our calls. 
I have never seen this allowed at any other hotel of this stature. Nightly rates plus additional resort fees should mean that all facilities are maintained to the highest standard. Felt as though those who paid additional VIP fees to sit at the restricted VIP side of the adult pool received preferential treatment to the other patrons. 
Disappointed to have had this happen and that no manager returned our calls.

reviews.author: cheri_0505
reviews.title: Solid large hotel, ok food
reviews.text: I wish I could say it was amazing but the rooms in the main building are really dated, the staff was overwhelmed with the volume of guests, and I was really looking forward to the bkft buffet daily but unfortunately their restaurants are catered to the general public not just hotel guests to it’s all a la carte. It’s a nice hotel if you have kids since they have a family and an adults only pool. I would instead recommend the sanctuary camelback if you are without kids.

reviews.author: Roam67559120010
reviews.title: Swimming in Luxury, Drowning in Fees: Our Stay at The Phoenician in Scottsdale
reviews.text:
As a husband who just spent five days at The Phoenician in Scottsdale with my pregnant wife, I have mixed feelings about this resort. On one hand, the location is perfect, with easy access to the airport, shopping, and great restaurants. On the other hand, the prices are extortionate and the additional fees and charges are downright annoying.

Let's start with the good stuff. 

On arrival day, surprisingly they delivered a bottle of non alcoholic sparkling cider and some sweets as my wife and I were celebrating recent pregnancy news. It was a nice touch. 

The staff at The Phoenician are exceptional, from check-in to the pool to the spa. Our Grand Room with a pool view was large with a sofa and very comfortable w/ AC, the king bed was soft and luscious, the bathroom setup was great with full tub and enclosed toilet, although the view itself was a bit disappointing. Instead of the promised amazing poolside view, we saw a slab of concrete and a lawn of fake turf, with a sliver of pool. But hey, we made the best of it.

Speaking of the pool, the service was quick and fast. We loved that they immediately gave us a jug of ice water as soon as we sat down, with service immediately after to take your nibbles & drink orders, pretty much checking in on us every 20 min. And the pools themselves were great - we had a blast swimming and lounging around.

The grounds at The Phoenician are beautiful, and although we didn't play golf, the course looked impeccable. It's definitely worth taking a stroll around the property to admire the landscaping.

Now, onto the not-so-good stuff. The prices at The Phoenician are steep, to say the least. Our room rate of $700 per night was expensive compared to other global resort hotels my wife and I have stayed at, but we were willing to pay for a great experience. What we didn't anticipate were the additional fees and charges that added up every time we turned a corner. Also, that nightly rate includes nothing but the room. No half board. No breakfast. Just the room. 

Some charges to be aware of:

There's a daily required resort fee of $45 per day for amenities such as the tennis court and 24/7 gym - neither of which we used once, but still had to pay for. Add another $85 daily rate for what’s accounted as a “Occupancy/Tourism” fee, although this is essentially taxes. To their credit, these 2 fees were in our original booking total, so not a surprise. 

Daily parking fees are here too and they have an entire underground parking garage, which is essentially empty due to the steep prices. I’m already paying steep prices for everything else, so why am I surprised they want to charge me a daily parking rate? Because of this, we didn’t get a rental car on purpose, rather just used Ubers, which has its pros and cons. 

One night we ordered room service as my wife wasn’t feeling well and we were shocked to see a $117 bill for a cheeseburger, chicken club sandwich, side of broccoli, and two sodas. Oh, you thought fries would come with a burger & chicken club? Nope, that’ll be an additional charge. So, how did it get to $117, you ask? Well, there's a room delivery fee, a 22% surcharge, and when they hand you the bill, the tip line is there, empty, waiting to be filled in - so do you tip or not? We felt bad for the guy who delivered it and set it all up, so we added another $5 tip. I’m not sure where that tip goes, to him? Does he get the 22% surcharge? Not sure. What should have been $60-$70 dinner bill, doubled quickly. These little annoyances of how they nickel and dime you the whole stay can add up quickly.

And don't even get me started on the spa prices. They aren't told to you (unless you explicitly ask, which was our fault, we didn't), but a 80-minute facial was $400. My wife's jaw hit the floor when we she saw the bill (mine did as well when the text came through), as we were expecting it to be around $200-250. We were wrong. Then, the final bill came upon checkout and that $400 spa treatment somehow turned into $480, but how? You guessed it - an additional $80 charge for breathing in that luxury spa oxygen. In reality my wife had read the bill wrong, it was $400 with a $80 surcharge. Was it the best Spa experience my wife has ever had? Yes. Was $480 good value for money? She didn’t think so.

So, is it worth it? 

While The Phoenician is an amazing resort and provides a great experience, the value for money just isn't justified in our eyes for the nightly rate and all the additional extras that get added on top. We’re in the incredibly lucky position that we can afford an experience like this, but we won't be returning, unless we ever see a nightly rate of $400-450. That would be good value for money.

But if you're swimming in piles of cash and additional fees, 22% surcharges, and ambiguous tip lines don't faze you, I'd highly recommend it. Just be prepared to swipe that credit card.

reviews.author: TravelingDave
reviews.title: Great Stay with the kids!
reviews.text:
I will say even though the Phoenician needed to upgrade a few things I LOVED my stay here with my family and would go back anytime. I couldn't tell from the reviews whether or not to stay here or the JW Camelback so I tried both. I read two reviews that said they are equal in accommodation and that is incorrect! I will say that this is a lot more expensive so I can see if you aren't traveling with kids and the FOUR pools and waterslide arent a big deal then you may be just as comfortable at the JW where you will spend about 40% less for a room there but this is a better property. To be fair to the JW, the food was better and the bonvoy elite status meant alot more over there in terms of benefits.  From the moment you pull up to The Phoenician it screams "opulence" where as the JW is very rustic and "earthy-crunchy" but still very beautiful.

Breakfast at the restaurant was a 40 minute wait to sit and the food was awful, overcooked and not tasty. If you have the time I'd drive 8 minutes to Hash Kitchen for breakfast where you will spend half the money and get the breakfast of a lifetime.

The staff on the property is very accommodating and pleasant to deal with. The four swimming pools each offer something different. 1 is close to the restaurant, 1 is close to the kids slide, one is adult only and another is off to the bottom of the resort  near the suites and casitas so you dont have to walk all the way up if you dont need to go to the main building.

 The Athletic CLUB is the BEST hotel fitness experience I've ever had. The gym is state of the art and there is even a game room on the bottom floor with pool table, table tennis and shuffleboard and a few arcade games.

All in all I still gave them 5 stars even though the food was no good here because the resort still gave me what I was looking for.

reviews.author: 524stephaniew
reviews.title: A wonderful trip
reviews.text: We spent the long weekend of Easter vacation at the Phoenician. I was very impressed with the staff and the grounds. It was a packed house and this resort rose to the occasion. The pool staff was attentive with towels, water, and service. The concierge desk was helpful with dinner suggestions and airport rides. Everyone was friendly and accessible. My family thoroughly enjoyed our time at The Phoenician Resort.

reviews.author: Angela S
reviews.title: Great Luxury Hotel
reviews.text:
Wonderful hotel - offering every comfort to travelers. 
The grounds are some of the most beautiful, staff is accommodating, rooms are spacious and comfortable. It’s like it’s own village. Everything you could want is there.
Very active hotel. We literally got the last room in the place. 
My only complaint was with the steakhouse. I asked for my steak in a particular way, and the waiter was very quick to tell me “no”. That the chef only cooks meat in medium or medium rare and nothing in between, which I found odd for an expensive restaurant in a luxury hotel. A little off -putting, but not the end of the world. 
Other than that issue, everything else was wonderful.

reviews.author: jamss22
reviews.title: Not worth the money
reviews.text:
The hotel was lovely if it cost half the price. For the cost, I expected much more. 

Pools were great - undoubtedly the best part of the stay.

Food was pretty good at the steakhouse (they relied too much on salt) and at Mowry & Cotton (portions are a bit small). The pool menu was limited. 

Rooms were large and clean. But the bathrooms are horribly designed. The tub is huge and the shower is very tiny. I was in an accessible room, so with the seat and bars in the shower, I didn’t have room to shave my legs (don’t know how someone who had limited mobility would do this). My friends non-accessible room had the same sized shower, just less cluttered. 

Service was ok, but not what I’d expect for the price point. Particularly the checkin desk was not very helpful.

reviews.author: JLRJRGJLGJRG
reviews.title: Excellent service, beautiful property, tired rooms
reviews.text: Absolutely everyone we interacted with at this property was exceptionally well trained. Everyone was so nice, wanted to help us, wanted to make us feel special. From the people who brought us water at the pool to the front desk staff to the guys who drove us around on the golf carts, to the kind employees who helped us navigate this sprawling property when we were lost - it was service with a smile every time. The grounds are beautiful and the spa was wonderful and relaxing. The bed was really comfortable and our bedroom on the top floor of one of the casitas was roomy. My only complaint is something the other reviewers have noticed: the interiors of the rooms are tired. It's surprising that the rooms aren't maintained the way they should be at a property like this one. My guess is perhaps they are waiting to do a major renovation soon. If that happens, it will make the interior match everything else we liked about the property. One other thing - our room was made up on the first day of our stay but not the second one. Perhaps they were just short staffed that day.

reviews.author: Gena
reviews.title: Spring Break 2023
reviews.text:
We are Marriot elite members and booked this stay for four nights on points. We stayed in the main building on 3rd floor, room 3136. It's down the hall from the main lobby but far enough down for a quiet nights sleep. The view from that room overlooks the pool and courtyard. We stayed here last year during spring break as well but stayed in a casita. I prefer the Casitas and next year hopefully it will be available on points.

When we arrived at 4 PM our room was not ready we had the same issue last year during spring break. They seem very overwhelmed and busy during spring break. When we got to our room a little after 5 PM it was very clean and we had no issues. I wish they had a refrigerator for drinks and snacks they do have a refrigerator for mini bar but not for private use.

 We used the pool two days of our stay and had no issues finding a chair, service was great food was good drinks were good too. The adult pool was full but the other two pools had plenty of chairs.

Main hotel guests park under the main building and it costs $23 per day. Make sure you have your hotel key out to get in and out of the garage. 

We will likely stay here again next year. It's a great spring break hotel for families, albeit crowded. The landscape is gorgeous, be sure to checkout the desert garden on property.

reviews.author: Jane2004
reviews.title: Luxury prices with budget mattresses
reviews.text: The Phoenician uses "EverNU" mattresses that have replaceable tops.  Unfortunately if you end up in a room where the lower part of mattress is old and tired, the new top doesn't make it better.  After a miserable night's sleep, I pulled back the sheets and noticed that we did not have a normal mattress.  I asked the front desk if our room had removable mattress tops (because only an accessible room (#4006) was available when we arrived at 8:30 pm), but I was informed that the entire hotel has these awful mattresses.    According a hotel industry article I found, the “EverNU” mattresses used by the Phoenician “allows hotels to keep the main part of their mattresses for twice as long”.  Zipping a new top on a tired old mattress is something Motel 6 would do, not something a luxury hotel should do when you are paying $1200 per night.  We will pass on the Phoenician.

reviews.author: Marissa B
reviews.title: Relaxed family spot
reviews.text: We are loving our stay here for a long weekend.  The grounds are beautiful and food is great.  Enjoying the relaxed atmosphere and pretty scenery.  Rooms could use some updating but overall a terrific experience!  We would come back again this time of year.  I recommend going in to town to shop and see the local art galleries.  Service has been good!  Kids activities are a plus too!

reviews.author: jay s
reviews.title: Total Ripoff
reviews.text:
This might be the most overpriced hotel in the United States (and definitely in Phoenix) and certainly not a good option for elite Marriott (e.g. Ambassador or Titanium) guests. They do not acknowledge status at check-in, the breakfast options are deliberately designed to be as cheap as possible and they don't provide upgrades when they are supposed to.

The rooms are tired, cheap and basic. The service is slow. The valet workers pressure you for big tips. The house-lined golf course is terrible and a complete rip-off. This is a just convention hotel with a nice pool area. 

It's clear that hospitality plays second-fiddle to extracting as much money as possible from customers. Therefore, on that basis alone, it is not luxury. 

But a pool does not make-up for all the shortcomings. If you are a seasoned traveler, avoid.

reviews.author: owemik
reviews.title: Beautiful property, overpriced with so so service
reviews.text: Great location with tons of amenities and things to do. Easy access to Camelback mountain trails. Rooms are ok but not much of an upgrade from a more moderately priced hotel. Spa and athletic center offer nice activity options but the prices for these are quite high. Onsite restaurants are ok. Good was average and prices were sky high. Service was good at JG and Mowry, but service at Tavern was rude and arrogant. Biggest issue with the hotel is the price. You could stay 3 nights at a more moderate hotel for just one night here. And be sure to check your bill as the hotel tends to add charges. We got charged for the free coffee at the breakfast and the hotel tried to charge $60 for Wi-Fi. Recommend only at a discounted rate.

reviews.author: Tal_Hameed
reviews.title: A nice stay but very pricey
reviews.text: I stayed at The Phoenician for a work conference and then another day for vacation. It's a very luxurious place to stay with beautiful scenery, nice pools, nice restaurants and plenty of amenities but very pricey. If it wasn't covered by work then I wouldn't pay out of pocket for here.

reviews.author: Holly K
reviews.title: Too much hype, room presentation an afterthought
reviews.text: This resort is definitely beautiful but over the top expensive.  Upon checking we were upgraded to the highest floor in a quiet area.  Room we actually got was more than likely used by guests with dogs.  Dog hair in hallway by exit and upon entering our room.  Hallway was never vacuumed during our 4 night stay.  Room had not been remodeled because the pictures on the website for bathroom were not the same.  Missing patio furniture compared to other rooms.  Rust stains on shower and worn door in bathroom.  The good was definitely the beds .  Extremely comfortable and very restful sleep.  Staff in fitness center were wonderful.  Marketplace cafe was good but extremely expensive for food selection.  If your looking for a more affordable place and actually more beautiful visit the Omni which we booked the past two years before trying the Phoenician.

reviews.author: Sherry W
reviews.title: Luxury gone bad!  Way overpriced, understaffed and needs updating!
reviews.text:
Was at the resort the week of 2/20/23.  We arrived at 11:00am and was told our room wasn't ready....never heard back from front desk (although we checked) until 4:30pm and then was not given a room that we booked.    Room walls had dirt smudges and furniture shows wear.  Nicks and dings throughout.   One one morning I asked housekeeping to come back in a hour since I was getting ready to leave....they never did.   
Came back to resort after a day out and there was no one at front desk nor anyone around at all on first floor.  NO STAFF around??
Rented cabana with friends but barely saw any staff on one day to order food or drinks.   Used spa for massage and nail treatment.  Massage was close to $400.  Way too expensive.  Manicure was $150.  Not gel or acrylic, just a shaping and some polish.   Again, just too darn pricey.
Very disappointed for a room that was $1200 per night.

reviews.author: 927donaldv
reviews.title: What a beautiful Experience
reviews.text:
The Hotel and Staff were excellent. With their help, we had a wonderful stay in the hotel. The property is beautiful, and the mountains as a background make it even more extraordinary. We enjoyed all the restaurants and had exceptional servers and food. The Spa is gorgeous, and the therapists were excellent.
I would be remiss not to mention the people that made our visit fantastic. I am sure I have missed someone as everyone was so helpful.
Suvanah, Mark Lyons, and Dakota
Ernesto, Vadim, and Lexi in Mowry & Cotton
Valets – Anthony, Matt, Lou, Doug
Encore AV - Gabriella and Sal
Front Desk – Brandon, Ireland
Julie at Tavern
Saharr Room coordinator
The Housekeepers on Floor 2
Max at the Golf Course
Lisa Mercer - Rock Star Resort Manager
Jo Anna in Leisure Sales
Massage Therapist - Debbie
Banquet Managers Brie and Sadie at Jokake
Thank you all for making our stay a success.
Yvonne and Don Varney
Herff Travel

reviews.author: vedettefille
reviews.title: High Energy, Quiet Nights
reviews.text: We booked this amazing resort through Whatahotel and had a great stay.  The hotel was busy and hopping which made for a fun night with live music at the bar.  We had a great meal at Mowry and Cotton.  We enjoyed breakfast through In Room Dining for free thanks to Whatahotel.  The In Room Dining delivery guys were brilliant.  And it was the quietest night sleep we'd had in a hotel room in ages.  Great stay all the way around.  We would definitely stay here again.  If a hotel runs this well at full capacity, then they do a great job.

reviews.author: mimiandb
reviews.title: Great vacation!
reviews.text: We just spent 12 glorious days in January here. Everything was wonderful. The food was delicious, the resort is beautiful, and all of the staff were extremely kind and helpful. We had a ground level casita with a fire pit. The entire room was perfect ( no kitchenette though) but our casita’s patio furniture cushions were quite stained. Time for new cushions! Our other family members had upper level casitas which also had kitchenettes. The pools are kept at a wonderfully warm temp so the grandkids never wanted to get out of the pool as it was warmer than the outside air! We would definitely stay at The Phoenician again!

reviews.author: Katey
reviews.title: wonderful stay in a beautiful place!
reviews.text: We had a great friends getaway weekend here.  We did the beer tasting with Matt and the cocktail tasting with Zack during our stay and thoroughly enjoyed both of them!  We learned so much about beer and mixology!  Our room was super clean and the beds were very comfy!  Everyone we came across was so friendly and helpful!! can't wait to go back!

reviews.author: dcb48
reviews.title: Schöne schon etwas ins Alter geratene Anlage
reviews.text: Leider ist die Küche sehr schlecht. Das Frühstück völlig fantasielos und tiefgefroren abgestanden. Lunch auf der Terrasse schrecklich die Sandwiches ungeniessbar die Chip’s eine Frechheit. Schlechter als Cafeteria Level zu erstklass Hotel Preisen.

reviews.author: OneReviewer
reviews.title: Highly recommend the firepit casita rooms
reviews.text:
I was attending an event in mid-November 2022 at the nearby Doubletree Paradise Valley, and we decided to stay here instead because we could take advantage of an almost reasonable corporate rate and get the remaining few nights needed to requalify for Marriott Titanium status for 2023.

As an added bonus, we decided to apply our remaining suite night upgrade certificates for 2022 to get a firepit casita room, and the upgrades cleared shortly before our arrival. The casitas are two story apartments located a short walk away from the main hotel building on the other side of the huge swimming pool complex. The casitas have their own parking area, allowing you to avoid the absurd parking garage fee that you likely would incur if you were parking a car while staying in the main hotel.

The casita that we had was very quiet and plenty large. As is often the case at top-of-the-line luxury properties, the bathroom had two sinks, a walk-in tub, a separate shower closet, and a room with a toilet and a bidet.

The Marriott Platinum/Titanium breakfast benefit consists of an $18 to $19 credit, per person per day (for two guests, maximum) at the hotel's casual restaurant. We found the breakfast offerings quite enjoyable, even though the credits only covered a portion of each day's bill for two adults if you ordered hot food.

The grounds of this hotel are immaculate, and we even strolled through the cactus garden, which was worth a look. The hotel has a building with exercise equipment and a game room for kids (but adults can play too). And, of course, there is a beautiful golf course and tennis too.

We have stayed at Ritz Carlton and St. Regis properties, but this was our first stay at a Luxury Collection property. I had heard that they can be of uneven quality from location to location, but everything we saw here was top quality. The main hotel building is very large, and we have not experienced what it would be like to stay there. But thanks to our firepit casita upgrade, we had a wonderful visit.

reviews.author: Mgitsme
reviews.title:
F YOU ARE VEGAN… you will starve!
If you are vegetarian u will be very hungry.
reviews.text:
I
For some reason,  this state full of wonderful Mexican cuisine, is NOT represent at his resort.  Unless you count chips and guacamole a meal.  The food is convoluted even for meat eaters. At 6:30 on a Sunday night the only restaurant in the hotel was closed.
Beautiful to look at.  The employees are WONDERFUL!  VERY clean.  The spa is amazing!  The rooms are very quite  HOUSEKEEPING  FABULOUS.
There ARE issues.  And they are a big deal when you are road weary.
-Lights in the room.  Easy where you don’t care about them. More challenging where u want them.  
- The layout of the hotel is not typical.  Be prepared to get lost often. the staff are amazing and will hand deliver u to where u are trying to go.
-You need to order your ice.  
-The pools are well lit and heated. the stairs are not so much and tripping is to be avoided.
-The toilet flusher is backwards.  Flush up not down. It take’s getting used to.
-There is a scent in some parts of he hotel that for me wasn’t pleasant.  It’s not awful.  
- The coffee is hidden at knee level behind a door that ,by design, sticks out at the foot of the bed.  No one is getting by when open.
-  I frond myself wondering if the decision maker have ever tried staying here on. A practice level to understand the experience.  Sorry.  The STAFF MAKES it all bearable. 
-
-

reviews.author: GTechMom
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds Amazing service
reviews.text: I have traveled throughout the world and can say without hesitation this is the best service I have ever received in a hotel. If you want to treat yourself to absolute luxury stay in the Canyon suites hotel. Every employee goes above and beyond to make your stay enjoyable. The cactus garden alone and the rest of the grounds of the hotel are enough reason to stay here. I hope to be back.

reviews.author: MMCT62
reviews.title: Best Thanksgiving Ever!
reviews.text:
Had an amazing time at the Phoenician during thanksgiving week! There was so much to do on-site that we barely left the property.

* tons of kids club activities- had so much fun at the circus school and family fall festival evening events. Crafts offered daily at 230 and also enjoyed Rice Krispie decorating 
* lots of outdoor fun included in resort fee such as bicycling and pickle ball 
* rented a cabana for thanksgiving day. It was a real treat!
* golf course was in great condition and had fabulous views of camelback mountain 
* walking distance to cholla trailhead - didn’t make it to the too but it was a great workout 
* delicious meals at all the restaurants- highlights included turkey dinner at J&G and dueling pianos at the Phoenician Tavern

reviews.author: Roxanne B
reviews.title: Holiday tea
reviews.text: This was the best holiday tea we have ever been to anywhere. Wonderful food and service. I highly recommend to anyone   It is the perfect way to start the holiday season. Get the champagne upgrade as it is well worth it

reviews.author: HollyCSM
reviews.title: Great experience-A few staff highlights
reviews.text: We stayed her for a family reunion and had a great experience.  I would like to highlight a few staff members that were extra memorable.   Perla at the front desk has the most welcoming smile and greeting.   Will at the Omlette station was extra helpful and kind.  Raul the breakfast waiter had amazing timing providing service.  When he noticed the Grandma in our group had sun in her eyes, he set up two umbrellas to make sure she was comfortable!    The last highlight was Chef Richard Boyer who called me personally when I had questions on how to navigate several food allergies for a child.  He was over the top helpful and accomodating.

reviews.author: CK2000
reviews.title: Expansive Resort
reviews.text:
We had the pleasure of being here for a few days.  This resort is beautiful and well maintained.  There is ample room pool side so it does not feel crowded.  The lobby was wonderful.

Our room looked at the mountain and it was very nice and spacious.  Everything was in order and well appointed.   We had a nice time at this resort and would return.

reviews.author: Kara U
reviews.title: Dont order Grimaldies for delivery; Phoneician wants you to eat there for $$$$$
reviews.text: Why do they only allow Uber Eats to deliver food there?  They recommended Grimaldi Pizza. Only Uber Eats can deliver  there. Pizza was cold, slimy/limp and disgusting by the time it arrived. Driver called 3x in 2min for us to come to lobby (when room was our option). Neither Phonician or Uber Eats cared A single bit. Eat at Phoenician for exorbinant $$$$ or just drive out for pick up. Terrible customer service by all

reviews.author: Daniel L
reviews.title: Drawling overpriced resort. Not all activities advertised offered.
reviews.text: Huge sprawling resort with golf, tennis, spa and multitude of activities. The resort is nice but super expensive. Rooms where fine and well appointed. They have 8 tennis courts but no programming- unless you want to pay $120 for a pro to hit. No classes, no drills , no clinics.  The golf course staff is great but the course is mediocre at least compared to other in the area. It seemed like an after thought rather than great design. For the price, I will stay elsewhere next visit.

reviews.author: christinesavoiea2022
reviews.title: Terrible Experience
reviews.text:
Our experience was terrible.  We checked in and we were given a Casita Room with 20 steps going to the room.  Why would they assign this type of accommodation to an 86 year old man who can barely walk?  They did.
We got to our room, put our fresh fruit in the
refrigerator, went down to the car and when we returned, they had removed all of our fresh fruit/veg - diabetic food to eat in the room.  It
took them a full day to reconcile their mistake
after housekeeping lied and told management it was ok to take our food.  Not true.  A fruit bowl they sent as a replacement was under ripe and tasteless, even though we said we’re diabetic.  The replacement was inedible.  The Casita they put us in was across from a construction site, with loud tractors, backup sounds starting at 8am every morning.  Most unpleasant.  The next day, we went for breakfast in the Cotton restaurant.  They were 10% full.  The coffee we ordered arrived cold.  The Eggs Benedict arrived mostly raw and was not able to consume.  Service was very slow, food very bad and dangerously undercooked.   We decided to eat at reputable restaurants instead of The Phoenician.  At checkout, we were never asked how our trip was.  When I sent a communication to the GM, I got a standard
letter saying they would use this as a “teaching moment,” which doesn’t have a ring
of truth to it, nor was it sincere.  They will use the “housekeeper’s lies” as a teaching moment?  Doubtful at best.  This is not how
five star hotels behave.  The lying starts with
management and trickles down to housekeeping.  Unsafe food is unforgivable.
Terrible management, terrible experience.

reviews.author: Lori C
reviews.title: Amazing Phoenician Get-Away!
reviews.text: Excellent team of hospitality staff, especially Alejondra, who took care of our room during our stay.  The staff at Mowry and Cotton went the extra mile each morning to make our breakfast experience special.  Pool staff were never far with towels, water and menus to order food or beverages!  The gym made working out a pleasure.  It’s clean, extremely well equipped and spacious!

reviews.author: ChicagoHiker11
reviews.title: Flying High at the Phoenician.
reviews.text: First up, the staff.  Incredible!  Just everyone in the hotel was a pleasure to work with.  Other than the staff, how does this compare with the Biltmore?  Well it depends on what you are looking for.  Both hotels are a pain in the neck to get into their on-site restaurants because they cater to corporate events.  I don’t think either pay enough attention to vacationers.   The rooms are very comparable.  I liked the Biltmore’s grounds better - less crowded in general because there is more space.   The pool cabanas were much better at the Biltmore.  Phoenicians need a major upgrade, major!   However, the food at the Phoenician was superior by far.   On site parking is very convenient.  All in all, it was a pleasurable stay.

reviews.author: jpsatnight
reviews.title: Beeindruckend
reviews.text:
Die Hotelanlage ist sehr beeindruckend. Die Einbettung in die Landschaft ist sehr gelungen. Es gibt ausreichend Platz an den Pools. Die Zimmer sind großzügig geschnitten. 
Der Service sowohl am Frontdesk als auch Concierge ist hervorragend. Immer zuvorkommend und keine Frage bleibt offen.
Empfehlung: Genießen Sie den Abend auf der Terrasse am offenen Feuer mit Blick über das Valley.

reviews.author: Passenger34658302065
reviews.title: Outdated and poorly serviced hotel with tiny rooms
reviews.text:
Compared to other hotels in the area, there is no comparison.  Here you are going to spend $1000 per night on a room comparable to the Best Western at the airport, only smaller.  The outdoor space I had in back was shared with others and not cleaned.  There was beer in a glass with cigarettes in it from the last guest when I arrived.  The valet parking scene felt like a casino.  The room was disinfected with industrial cleaners that smelled like a Motel 6 in the 1980s.  The entire property felt like a loud apartment complex or a Disney hotel with screaming children everywhere.  There was even some kind of rock concert going on until late evening next to my room.  Before my arrival I asked for a couple packages to be delivered and there was no notification and no indication of where those went until I finally found out there was a Fedex on site in the middle of a conference I wasn't attending.  The room service was slow, service overall was poor (the Valet lost my car for a minute upon check in and then realized I didn't need the valet anyway since I could drive to my room, laundry is outsourced and takes days to return).

Anyway, I came here to relax for 4 days and I left after the first night.  Went over the the Sanctuary instead, which is a dozen times better for the price, as are the Four Seasons and Royal Palms (Sanctuary is best IMO).  Will not come back.

reviews.author: Danest07
reviews.title: WAY too overpriced
reviews.text:
We stay almost exclusively at Marriott hotels and love the brand (Ritz is our favorite).  Will start with the good - the location at the bottom of Camelback Mountain is excellent.  And the property is really cool.  The service staff at Mowery & Cotton (restaurant), room service and bell services was really good as well.  The golf course staff were extremely nice/helpful (but the course is closed for a couple of months to redo the greens/fairways)  Finally, the gentlemen who guarded the kid slide were all helpful and nice.  

Unfortunately the bad far outweighs the good:  (i) you have to pay to have access to a chair at the pool.  We went with a poolside daybed - was $200 AND each person had to order $50 in food/drink.  The service was terrible - the server did not appear for 2 hours, had to go to the bar to order food/drinks that were mandatory.  And they asked us with 30 minutes left if they wanted any of the amenities that they never told us about, including a bottle of champagne.  Oh, and there is not complimentary sunscreen - it is a $20 menu item.   (ii) The property needs a serious refresh - someone told us that there was a $5M update a few years ago, did not see it.  There is a lagoon that is disgusting, dirty water and fake swans that are not even assembled (missing heads).  (iii) We decided to hike up Camelback Mt and were told the bellhop would take us close and that it is a 1/2 mile walk from there.  Unfortunately, the bellhop took us to the front entrance on Camelback Road, which is a 1.5 mile walk, instead of the entrance that is close to the trail entrance - no idea what happened.  Guess we got more exercise.   (iv) The Spa is a complete ripoff - materially higher than the spa at any Ritz we have used.  (v) There is a $45 day resort fee that you incur, even though you need to pay extra to have a seat at the pool (and order $50 per person per day if you decide to pay for a seat at the pool).  (vi)  The pictures of the Marketplace (to get snacks, quick meals, coffee, incidentals)s is completely misleading - don't expect a selection of anything worthwhile to eat, other than a muffin.   (vii) No information provided re things that teh resort has to offer.  (viii) the gates to and from the pool areas look like entrances/exits to a trash area, and slam super-loud (except for 1 by the bar near the upper pool).   In short, the place is WAY overpriced, needs to be significantly refreshed, some of the staff don't know what they are doing and are not helpful, and the resort surcharges you on-top surcharges.   We will never stay here again.

reviews.author: Jonathan B
reviews.title: They put the best interest of Marriott & Host over the health, safety & well being of the guest.
reviews.text:
We checked out early. It’s a beautiful property. However, it’s VERY old. The hotel is extremely cheap. The liquor license is under review. We entered the suite after having a lovely dinner at Mowry & Cotton Monday. We immediately noticed an unpleasant odor coming from the half bathroom. We inspected the bathroom & noticed a large area of the ceiling covered in mold. (See attached pics) They had to cut away part of the ceiling to remove the mold. The two gentleman who removed the mold made a terrible situation better; considering what was going on. I can’t say the same for the executives/management team. I’ve noticed that several salary employees at this hotel (dealing with my issues & other guests) has the best interest of Marriott & Host; not the guest.

Marriott corporate tried to work with the GM of the hotel (Mark Vinciguerra) & he had absolutely no interest in doing the right thing. 

The department of health found MOLD in the pantry, kitchen areas & air vents. If you got sick you have the right to know why.

reviews.author: Chip144
reviews.title: Top notch resort
reviews.text: Came here for a conference and had a great time.  This extensive property has so many amenities.  I had all meals coordinated with the conference and it was remarkable how good the food was when they had to feed so many.  Room was large as well as a fully appointed bathroom.  Bed was very comfortable.  Everything felt first class.

reviews.author: IrishFan-80
reviews.title: Our first stay
reviews.text:
We stayed two nights here on points and had a mixed opinion.  An early check-in was available but as Ambassador elite thought either an upgrade or nice view would be offered. The base king room itself was fine as was the ease of self parking. Given the reputation of the resort we were surprised at the limited breakfast too.
Pool service was very good but the jacuzzi/hot tub was cold and was not fixed despite multiple requests. We find that the best resorts keep everything in top condition.
Sadly this fell below our wonderful stays at the other nearby Marriott resorts.

reviews.author: larry b
reviews.title: Not 5 star service
reviews.text: We redeemed a certificate and were disappointed in what you used to be a deluxe 5 star resort.    gave us a nice casita but turns out 2nd day we found out they were kicking us out and gave us 30 minutes.   Said it was being renovated and we had no choice and no one told us.   moved us and said they would give an amenity.    took hours to get it.     did waive parking but hardly worth a move at 3 pm day before we left.   looking out window towels had been left on lawn for 2 days.     should have taken off resort fee which is stupid to charge when using a cert.   Waldorf does not charge resort fees.     food was good and it is nice resort but not super deluxe like it used to be.    No nightly turn down service either.

reviews.author: BusterJ
reviews.title: Loved this hotel!
reviews.text:
We checked into this beautiful hotel after a long flight from UK and immediately greeted by wonderful hospitality from start to finish.  We had a king room with adjoining queen queen for my 5 children. Exceptionally large (even by American standards) , beautifully furnished and bathrooms top level. stunning view over the pool area. 
Kids loved the slides and pool. Jetlag had us up super early first couple of mornings ans the welcome at the gorgeous athletic club was another level. The views from the treadmill are insane.
All in all a fabulous 4 nights and I will definitely return and recommend.

reviews.author: Joe H
reviews.title: Simply perfect...
reviews.text:
I can’t remember how many times we have stayed here over the years but its wonderful.  We really enjoyed high tea and dinner at J and G steakhouse.  Raul at Mowry and Cotton remembered us and welcomed us back to the resort.  Impressive…Sarah at the mother of pool was excellent and so efficient and great service with a smile.  Very consistent every day I was there.  

A gorgeous resort with great service…beautiful evenings.

reviews.author: B She
reviews.title: Great Resort
reviews.text: Very nice resort . Golf as good as anywhere else we played. Very good condition. Massive swimming pool areas. Kids water play area . Nice employees . Easy check in. Self parking under hotel with elevator.

reviews.author: Sheryl M
reviews.title: A Terrific Resort!
reviews.text: The Phoenician is a terrific resort in Scottsdale. It is in the perfect location - close to shopping and great restaurants.  Everything on the property is beautiful. The pools are great. They are perfect for adults and children. The staff is warm and friendly.  Housekeeping is great too. Mowry and Cotton a nice place for breakfast.  This was my eighth stay there and I am looking forward to my ninth visit!

reviews.author: Christine S
reviews.title: August 2022 Summer to Remember - Thanks Phoenician Staff!
reviews.text:
I really hope the GM is able to get this review.  Unlike neighboring luxury resort our check in experience was OUTSTANDING, thanks to Ireland.  What a gem she is.  We had a long car ride before arriving, kids were ready to jump out of car as soon as we arrived.  Ireland was so pleasant and welcoming!  Every hotel should have an Ireland!  We asked for a room with a pull out sofa and two queens.  She delivered.  She also wanted to make sure the pull out was made with sheets and blankets.
