Ireland is so attentive, kind and very professional.  She sent us sweets to our room, which the kids were thrilled to receive.  We had to also engage with other front desk staff, and they just could not beat the energy Ireland has.   
Our room was huge, plenty of space and large balcony which was so enjoyable in the evening.  The room was very clean, slightly dated, but very clean.  The A/C worked well, which is super important to me, because the first thing i check is how low the a/c can go and if I hear the compressor go on, which it did.  The cleaning ladies asked if we need anything multiple times, extra waters, towels, etc.  They were also very attentive. 
On to the pool.  Our first night we stayed at the upper pool because it was just easier.  No service after 5 or 6, which is a bummer, but August is not very crowded for this resort obviously, there was about 10 people in the upper pool and that included the 4 of us.  The next day we had a full day to enjoy the pools.  We arrived early and explored the pools.  We decided to plant ourselves on the lower pool, kids had access to the slide, which they used 100's of times.  My husband and I thought we had the ideal spot until a couple decided to yell into their cell phones for an hour.  This prompted us to explore a cabana.  Rich who assisted us made it happen.  This guy, similar to Ireland, Rich is amazing!  Above and beyond to deliver the best service.  Rich does not disappear nor disappoint.  He manages all guests, keeps all areas clean, makes sure ice water is refreshed, and keeps the cabana guests very happy.   Rich is top notch server!  We had handful of special requests, he was "no problem" to all!     Again, if the GM reads this, please make sure these two get all the bonus points they can get.  We are NYC picky people, Ireland and Rich ROCK.    For dinner we ate at the Mowry and Cotton and J&G. Had the filet at both, which the filet at Mowry and Cotton was actually a tiny bit better than the filet at J&G steakhouse, same size. Try all the sauces at J&G for the steak they are all good.  Service at both restaurants were outstanding.   Food was pricy at J&G, but we were prepared.  
Overall, our experience for what we paid was exceptional.   Given this place is probably a different experience during March/April, we would only come back during off season, we enjoyed all the amenities because it was not overly crowded.  We leave the NYC to escape the crowds.    
I also used the Spa, which was nice, pricy but service was good.  
We will back for sure.     Thank you to all the staff, if i could write a personal "THANK YOU" to all of them I would.

reviews.author: GastroEclectico
reviews.title: Best Resort in the Valley of the Sun!
reviews.text: I thought it apropos to review of an establishment visited very, very often for both day visits and staycations, special events, and culminating in some incredible memories – our absolute fave combined resort, spa and restos in the Valley.  Having the opportunity to regularly stay over many accommodations across and occasionally outside the country, not a professional hotel reviewer by any means, and not a regular business traveler - but as a primarily pleasure and needs wanderer, I have developed as what I believe is my concise method for scoring the worthiness of each hotel visited.  A little exception for this establishment is necessary though, since my wife and I enjoy staycating here very often and find the amenities, eateries and then some, very satisfying and enjoyable. The Phoenician spa lives up to its hoopla from massages to aromatherapy. For swimming and lounging in the sun the Phoenician has its main pools, lazy river or the Spa Pools. For contemplating a valley view while imbibing some of the best The Valley can offer The Thirsty Camel Bar has its cool, modern and relaxing inside, or the outside patio with live music and firepits. Or you can select being more recluse in the Phoenician Tavern! If you want an upscale yet casual dinner there’s Mowry & Cotton, which has been our only disenchantment to date at the Phoenician. They have gift shops with above average quality items, for adults and children alike. The poolside Kalio Kabobery Mediterranean offers an above average menu. Get your morning coffee and then some at the Marketplace Coffee House. If you your into Hi-Tea or Afternoon Tea you can’t go wrong with our fave Valley Tea,  Afternoon Tea & Champagne offering in the English tradition, with tasty selections of Finger Sandwiches, Fresh Baked Scones, not to mention the pastries, along with some incredible tea selections. Love it! Combining the aforementioned with my criteria are as follows and the results are: 1) ease of access to and from public or private ground transportation [Score:4.5]; 2) convenient and safe parking [Score:5.0]; 3) access, accuracy and convenience of check in and check out [Score:5.0]; 4) atmosphere, ambience, public facilities, lounging areas and access to an office center and Wi-Fi access [Score:5.0]; 5) overall customer service - including but not limited to Hospitality, Support Services, Concierge knowledge, communication, attitude and demeanor of staff [Score:5.0]; 6) quality, cleanliness, value, convenience, amenities (i.e., ironing board, iron, TV, charging access, phone, et.al.) and comfort of rooms, beds, room safe and/or valet services [Score:5.0]; Taking all the aforementioned categories in a scale of 1 star to 5 stars with 1 being the worst and 5 being the best a hotel can be!  This hotel rates a: 4.9. If you have an opportunity to experience the Grifin Club you will most definitely appreciate the upcharge, and being a Member of Marriott’s Bonvoy goes a long, long way! Great work staff and management, kudos and congrats for work well done. We’ll just keep coming back!

reviews.author: PCam321
reviews.title: Big, impersonal hotel but good rooms etc
reviews.text: Stayed here at the start of our Arizona / Utah trip.  It is a huge hotel and feels very impersonal.  The hotel was hosting a big  conference while there so hotel felt very full.   Rooms are great - good gym etc. but for some reason only one restaurant was open and the food was mediocre.  Some details are great, for instance the coffee shop near the foyer that serves coffee and pastries from 6 AM.  Overall the hotel was fine.

reviews.author: lrkell01
reviews.title: High Price without Amenities
reviews.text: Stayed in July 2022. No food or drink service at the pool after 6PM . They started trimming branches outside my room at 6 AM. Charged me for mini bar services that I didn't use. Terrible customer service from front desk. You can find a lot better options in Phoenix for the price.

reviews.author: revproj
reviews.title: Beware of Double Charging
reviews.text: I recently had my third stay on a recent long weekend at the Phoenician and I'll say that I have always enjoyed the resort. The staff, pools and location are fantastic for a nice getaway. However, this time around I was double charged for items at the pool area on the last day of my stay, which has been over a month and still is not settled. At the pool area, you are asked to sign a card to authorize charges to the room which will automatically tag on additional 20% gratuity if leaving the pool area. I made sure to close out the checks before departing the pool area and resort that day. To my surprise, I later received a hotel invoice where I was double charged that day for items even though I had closed out the checks. I'm not sure if it was an honest mistake (happened on more than one charge) or intended. I called the hotel the next day and spoke to an associate manager and he said he would take care of it. Unfortunately, nothing happened after a month and i've recently been back and forth with calling the hotel and accounting. The fact that I am still going back and forth with the hotel after a month to dispute the charges is absurd. No one should have this inconvenience when they were not in the wrong.

reviews.author: Philip J
reviews.title: Great besides cockroach
reviews.text: The stay was amazing until 430am when I went to use the bathroom and there was a cockroach the size of my damn thumb running around the toilet. I killed it and called the front desk who sent someone to dispose of it. I couldn’t sleep the rest of the night. Staff seemed pretty indifferent to it and explained that the resort butts up to the mountain. This might be true and this may be normal for Arizona in July, but I’ve never heard or experienced it before and will not return. Besides this issue the stay was great.

reviews.author: Felicia G
reviews.title: First time visit
reviews.text: Everything from the check in process, getting additional amenities, and ordering food from the hotel restaurants was easy and convenient. I want to especially thank Vanessa at the front desk, Cameron from the Kalio poolside restaurant, and Dwi at the marketplace. They truly know how to provide excellent guest service!

reviews.author: vichy
reviews.title: Great stay, but not perfect
reviews.text: Expected just a bit more for how the rate and billing as a luxe hotel. Service was great, pool options (ESPECIALLY the adult only pools) were great, spa facilities were great. Wish the spa offered a wider variety of services, restaurants had later hours and more consistently great food, more shopping options on the complex.

reviews.author: Harold
reviews.title: Service  & Thoughtfulness
reviews.text: I’d like to thank the Phoenician staff for a wonderful experience  during my recent visit. The property is well appointed and the staff strives to provide excellence in service and a most relaxing ambience. Most specifically Devin Magouirk for his dedication to detail and making every effort to ensure the best possible experience for the property's guests. His ability to remedy any issue w/ great care and thoughtfulness is what makes the Phoenician a wonderful 5 star resort to visit for any personal or business traveler. Thanks so much and I look forward to my next visit.

reviews.author: Christine A
reviews.title: Disappointment
reviews.text: Poor service at the spa.  Went with a group of girlfriends.  The massages were fine but the pool service was awful.  More than 2 hours for a glass of water and 2.5 hours for food.  I realize this is not the fault of our poor servers. They should not  let so many people in the spa if they don’t have enough staff to give them the service associated with this brand. Very disappointing.

reviews.author: Seng100
reviews.title: Nice, grand but oldish establishment
reviews.text: I stayed for 3 nights to attend a conference in the hotel. Rate for the room was reasonable for the offerings. Arrival was promptly met by the front office, check-in was efficient, friendly and professional. First impressions were that this was once a grand hotel but clearly beginning to show its age. Assigned room had "mountain view" but that was essentially blocked by a hill that was ~50 meters from the balcony. Room was of a good size, adequately furnished but uninspiring. There were ample outlets adjacent to the bed (nice feature) and working desk; there was also a stocked fridge and the bathroom came with tub and walk-in shower (but that did not drain well). I tried food at the steakhouse and Mowry (breakfast, lunch and dinner) - they were visually interesting but largely flavorless. This was particularly disappointing given the small selection of food offered for each meal. Redeeming feature was the staff - who were attentive, and polite. I also tried the spa, which was very nice and the service rendered was good. Overall, I think this is a nice establishment (for the rate) but I would limit my meals at the establishment.

reviews.author: ashleyelizabeth6
reviews.title: Birthday Staycation
reviews.text:
I was looking for something low-key, relaxing, and fun for my family and I to do for my birthday. We live in Queen Creek so we were looking for a good spot for a staycation. I never liked the idea of staycation, why spend your money where you live? It’s not really a wise investment considering you’re not having a new adventure? However, the way things have been going for me recently, that’s all I wanted. I wanted to pack up the family, but not have to worry about the anxiety of going to an airport, flight delays, “flightmares,” etc. We decided upon the Phoenician as I am a Marriott ambassador and it is part of the luxury collection of Marriott. I used my points for a two night stay with my husband and one year old. They upgraded us to a beautiful room on the ground floor called the Casita. It had a beautiful garden and fire pit outside but the room itself was very small. Typically we have much larger rooms. As an ambassador I get a certain amount of suite nights where I can put in a request to get upgraded to a suite. Anytime I’ve ever used that it’s always been accepted, but this time around it wasn’t. Too bad because I’ve had a horrible year and I really wanted that for my stay here. It’s also difficult with my one-year-old because he sleeps much better with his own space and when we have a suite he will have his own room. What was cool is that we didn’t have to park in any parking lot. We had our own parks parking spot right there outside of our room. It also only cost about $14 a night which isn’t bad for a resort. You do have to pay resort fees which I believe are $49 a night and include the regular resort fee type things like activities, etc. We took advantage of one of the activities because they had a play time out on the splash pad for kids. They had some toys for my son to play with. The concierge was absolutely lovely. They have a whole team of people and we checked in with them often to make reservations, ask questions, etc.
We ate at Cotton & Mowry the first night we were there and that was delicious. I will do a separate review on the restaurants. I actually enjoyed that restaurant more for breakfast than anything. I thought they would have a buffet breakfast, but they only had a sit down. It was delicious. The service there is great as well. They were very accommodating to my one year-old. The second night we dined at J&G Steakhouse. That’s not open on Mondays and Tuesdays. It was very fancy and very fun to celebrate my birthday dinner there. A separate review on that as well, great food, great service. I took advantage of the spa which I will try to do a separate review on as well. I made myself a massage appointment for the first day we got there. I was so happy I did that. It was one of the best spa experiences I’ve ever had and I already cannot wait to go back. The massage itself was amazing, my massage therapist is named Zach. He was great. What I really loved about this experience was the amenities. I felt so relaxed. It was the first time in a long time I’ve gone to the spa with a really amazing amenities. They had a steam room, a sauna, a large hot tub. A gigantic and beautiful quiet room, a locker room, showers, everything you would want and more. They serve tea, snacks, different flavored waters, it was so relaxing and so fun. My only regret is that I didn’t have more time there. They also have a rooftop pool. You can chill there, order off the menu, they have a bar and they also have fun nonalcoholic drinks. You can also rent a cabana while you’re there. I only had about an hour to enjoy all the amenities before my service, and I was able to enjoy everything within that hour, but if you wanted to spend more time relaxing, maybe fall asleep in a quiet room or at the pool, you definitely want to maybe make a day of it. You do not need to be a hotel guest in order to use the spa. Although, you do need to book a service in order to use the amenities, meaning they don’t let you pay just to use the amenities. I kind of like that, actually because it made the spa not busy at all. At one point, I swear I was the only person there. They also have a great gift shop on your way out if you’re looking to spend some extra money as everything is very expensive. Skin care, hair products, workout clothes, yoga wear, candles, & aromatherapy, etc. On the day of my birthday we rented a cabana for $325. We were at a very quiet pool and there were only a few people who rented a cabana and they all had families as well so it was very kid friendly. It was great to have a private spot to keep us out of the sun, however it was still very hot there. They don’t have any kind of cooling system or misters in there. Just the shade. They have a TV, they give you a choice of a complimentary champagne or a food item as well as a fully stocked refrigerator with water, Gatorade, etc. You get your own personal server who comes in and wait on you. I thought the price of the cabana was pretty high in comparison to what we actually got, but it definitely made the day more fun and more private. There are three pools there on site. There’s a big splash pad for the kids, there is a pool restaurant, and of course the opportunity to rent cabanas. The food was really good at the pool. We ordered fish tacos, and as our complimentary item we got chips and salsa with guacamole, we also ordered the hummus tray. The drinks were just OK. Honestly, my son‘s banana smoothie was probably the most delicious thing. I ordered a beer and a vodka drink and my husband ordered a beer and a margarita but the liquor drinks were very weak. The same person who waits on you also makes the drinks. It was a nice day. Honestly, I was a little bit disappointed about the room, although it was nice to sit outside after we put the baby to bed and enjoy our wine by the fire pit and watch the sun go down. Being from Queen Creek it definitely felt cooler with the mountains blocking some of that sun, and I think the big take away was the pool day and the spa experience. The restaurants were great as well. I thought the service was good. Normally at Marriotts  when they know you are celebrating a birthday, they send something, a letter, card, food tray, or wine to the room, they really didn’t do anything like that. I thought in terms of hospitality, that was lacking. Otherwise, I definitely recommend staying here. It’s a beautiful resort. They also have an athletic club and a golf course that I did not take advantage of but that looked beautiful.

reviews.author: Sarah P
reviews.title: Porterage Fees
reviews.text: Marriott platinum member of many years here. There is absolutely no disclosure of the porterage fees they will charge you when they drive you to a room far off from the main resort area. So, I was tipping the golf cart drivers $10 a trip on top of the secret porterage fee which came to $56 for four trips. So incredibly unethical.

reviews.author: yvonne eevee gonzalez
reviews.title: Luxury service
reviews.text: Amazing property, always something to do or explore. Every employee is genuine about caring for you and very helpful. Special moments from Front Desk Agent Hayley who was delightful & knowledgable at my late checkin, Concierge Evie who gave the perfect recommendations to elevate our Scottsdale experience, and Mowry restaurant manager Morgan who went above & beyond with her personalized service. Can’t wait to return!

reviews.author: Pamela2222
reviews.title: Excellent customer service and wonderful staff
reviews.text: We just returned from a four night stay at the Phoenician and had a wonderful time.  The service was five star in every respect.  We encountered a long line at checkin due to a conference group arriving at the same time we did, and the check in staff upgraded us to make up for the inconvenience.  There are three very large pools so it’s always possible to find a great spot.  Towel and umbrella service and food and drink service at the pools was outstanding.  We really enjoyed the bar area in the evening that overlooks the city lights. Our room was spacious and quiet with a small outdoor patio.  We were very pleased with everything at this resort.

reviews.author: Joe B
reviews.title: Big $$ over loyal customers
reviews.text:
After making a reservation in October 2021, and having a confirmed reservation and a loyal Bonvoy member, they emailed that the would not be honouring the reservation. 

The bewildering excuse “a computer glitch”. 

No it wasn’t, they sold out to a conference. 
Didn’t care that we were travelling from Australia. 

So we decided to make the effort to at least go and have a discussion with the General Manager. 
Nowhere to be seen or bothered to personally call to apologize. 

Don’t expect that they will honor your reservation. Have a back up..

reviews.author: travel_monkey426
reviews.title: not worth the price for a family trip
reviews.text:
Traveled with my husband and 2 small children to Scottsdale to go somewhere warm for a week.  Paid wayyyyy too much for the casita--the amount of space was nice, as was having 2 full bathrooms, but the room was not up to par for the price.  Tubs were too deep to bathe a baby in--had to use a bathroom sink instead.  "Kitchen" had a great microwave, small stove/oven combo, 3/4 size fridge/freezer combo, decent storage, 3 pans (saucepan, skillet, and a square griddle), and 4 cooking utensils.  And some wine glasses.  No plates/silverware/bowls/cups.  Not sure what the point of a kitchen is without these items as well as usuable cooking vessels/utensils.  Main door to the room was a pain to get in and out of while carrying children--it's a double door but opening only one side gives you less than a normal door width to get out of (fun with an infant carrier).  Secondary door to our room was in the vestibule of the main bathroom and needs new weather stripping (could see sunlight all the way around it).  Bed was fine (daily sheet changes which I appreciate), towels were plentiful, bathroom was clean.  
Dirty champagne bucket sat across from our room for 3 days before being picked up.  Splash pad was acceptable but could use more shade and a good hose down every evening.  Closest pool to the splash pad (up a set of stairs) has one small staircase in otherwise just ladders.  Might want to consider a zero entry pool with a future renovation to make it more family friendly.  Pool service was acceptable but nothing like a 5 diamond resort should be--no one putting out towels on your chairs for you, refilling waters, etc.  By 4pm, the pool area has a decent amount of empty cups and straws that haven't been picked up (and there are no trash cans).  
We ate breakfast daily at Mowry and Cotton.  Good food, acceptable prices.  Rachel was a fantastic server.  Coffee was plentiful.  
Afternoon tea--need to get a reservation weeks-months early or check back daily for openings.  Too involved for my 3 year old, but my mom and I enjoyed it and the food was good and multiple servings of each course were offered.  The tea, however, was not strong despite brewing for more than the suggested time--my Indian grandparents would have absolutely sent it back. 
Spa--I got a facial--bit weird to have 30+ people (men and women) sitting around in the dark while the estheticians go around looking for their client for the hour.  Facial was good and she didn't try to upsell me on a ton of things, which I appreciate.

Perhaps if you were staying in the main hotel part and did not have children, then the rooms and service would be 5 diamond quality, but I just don't think this resort was worth what we paid.  Will not be visiting again.  Would go back to the JW Marriott instead.

reviews.author: Steve F
reviews.title: Dissatisfied
reviews.text:
Booked a Casitas suite a month ago. I thought casitas meant something more than Marriott Hotel room with a small patio. Very disappointed. Not a five star experience. 
I tried to move to another resort near by but they refused to refund my deposit. Terrible customer experience.

reviews.author: TrayDC
reviews.title: Service not on par with the price
reviews.text: The resort doesn't seem to be fully staffed and service suffers. The rooms are large and well appointed but very expensive. Our room was $1200 per night (Friday to Sunday reservation) for a double queen bed room that had a view of the driveway (and the related driveway noise). We had no maid service on Saturday despite being out of the room nearly all day. When we called the front desk to inquire they said housekeeping probably hadn't gotten to our room because they are short staffed. Some features at the hotel, such as the fitness center, are new and lovely while other areas, such as the bathrooms near the pools, desperately need an update. There was a large corporate event on the property while we were there, which may explain some of the service challenges, but I recently stayed at the Biltmore on a weekend when it was also at full occupancy and didn't experience the same issues. Another disappointment was that there was no access to the Camelback Mountain hiking trails because of construction. If you want to go hiking you have to get an Uber to take you to an access point about 10 minutes away (no hotel shuttle or ride via a resort vehicle). The food on the property was very good and the drinks at the lobby bar were exceptional.

reviews.author: S D
reviews.title: Beware of extra charges on checkout folio
reviews.text: Nice resort but overcharged at checkout and refused to fix. Added mini bar items to bill and refused to refund shame on you otherwise it was nice experience there with friendly staff at the pool and slow but cool bartenders at the lobby lounge

reviews.author: Donewithatlantis
reviews.title: Average at Best
reviews.text: While a beautiful location, The service was disappointing.  If you are there as a paying guest and not part of a convention, prepare to be treated as you don’t matter as much.  We called weeks in advance for reservations to restaurants and the spa to be told the restaurants were closed for “private events” and the spa was booked because the convention gave each participant 4 treatments.  So much for regular guests.  One day we returned to our room and housekeeping never came - we called front desk at 5:30 and they said there would be no more housekeeping that day???  No explanation.  We asked for clean towels which came an hour later.  We emptied the trash but no one offered to take it or the used linens.  Each morning as we walked to breakfast, the pool waste baskets were overflowing with trash from the evening before and unconsumed cocktails were on tables….. we spent over $5000 to stay there and will choose better next time.  They go all out for big business but the average guest is pretty meaningless to this hotel.  They should just make it a convention center.

reviews.author: Weezy718
reviews.title: Spring break stay
reviews.text:
On the pros: our family loved this resort. Customer Service was fabulous, the room was nice and big with a comfortable bed and a great view overlooking the pool on the 4th floor. The gym had great equipment plus a Peloton which kept me very happy.

On the one con: the mismanaged pool situation. Kevin who worked at the pool was obnoxious, going up to guests and telling them they could only leave their chairs for 30 minutes or else their personal items and towels would be removed. He was doing this even when there were plenty of chairs available. Bothering people to tell them that piece of news which did not make guests very happy. I found that very unprofessional and felt like bullying. They need to figure out a better way to manage that like maybe remove some of the food tables and add more chairs b/c we were there during April spring break and it did get very crowded. Having to first find a chair and then guard it for the entire day really put a damper on a relaxing vacation. 

Aside from that, we really did enjoy our stay here.

reviews.author: bhojan_chacha
reviews.title: Luxury at its best , food so-so
reviews.text: Went to Phoenician with family. Great morning walk , perfect ambiance , pools weren’t too crowded as they had 2-3 different pools with slides ,  nice bar at pool - great cocktails  didn’t get time to play golf but the desert garden is pretty too .. food wise mowary and cotton is expensive but food is so-so . Again it overlooks the pool so it’s definitely pretty..  In fact fact was salty for our liking.

reviews.author: jksilva7
reviews.title: Service at its absolute worst!
reviews.text:
When you book months in advance, confirm your connecting rooms multiple times, take down the names of the people you confirmed with,  then arrive so excited only to find out they ignored you, ridiculous! What could be worse? Danny, the manager told us that there is nothing he can do and suggests our kids (11 and 8) stay in their own room “near” us, outright dangerous in my opinion, how can anyone suggest that with a straight face? 

Well, we have a whole week left, 4 of us crammed into one room since Danny and the Marriott Ambassador Elite team just point fingers at each other instead of making this right!

reviews.author: Julie M
reviews.title: Lovely resort, fabulous staff!
reviews.text: We visited over spring break / Easter weekend with our family. The resort is lovely - great grounds, lots of fun activities, good food. The staff made the trip though! Felicia at registration was WONDERFUL (thoughtful, considerate, and funny - especially with our kids) as were Cullen, Savannah, and Jeanne with the kids activities (they remembered our names, were energetic and attentive, and just overall fantastic!). Jaime at the concierge desk was an absolute pro - it’s clear how much she cares and knows about the place, and she won over my very upset son who had face planted on the cement. The people made the trip - thank you to all!

reviews.author: DKSF7777
reviews.title: Wonderful visit
reviews.text: My husband and I had 3 wonderful nights at the Phoenician.  Our casita room was in perfect condition . Plenty of staff and excellent service.  We had dinner at the steakhouse and it was wonderful.  Plenty of pool chairs. Was nervous given recent reviews but everything was perfect.

reviews.author: L55386
reviews.title: Not luxury, not with the price at all
reviews.text: This hotel is far from luxury… do yourself a favor and book anywhere else! From the rudeness of the staff, to the horrible room view of a roof, this place is the worst value I’ve experienced. Food was terrible, the drinks at the bar were overpriced and not good at all. The hot tub in the women’s spa had so much used (dirty) chlorine, it made my eyes and nose sting just being near.

reviews.author: Sean W
reviews.title: Not the same experience as 15 years ago
reviews.text:
So let’s start with the positives. Staff was friendly (very young). Exterior Gardens and exterior maintenance was exquisite. Common Areas were very nice. Pool staff was attentive and worked very hard. Pool service was the best service in the entire resort. Due to this being a large family trip I was able to see 4 different room types. Main Hotel Rooms were shabby, Casitas were very shabby,  I am not handicapped and we ended up in a handicapped room(booked this trip in October).  Restaurants were meh. J&G was forgettable. All steaks were ordered medium rare temp, all steaks came out medium and it was very expensive. 
Room was not serviced daily were there for 8 nights and they missed at least two services.  This was an expensive experience for mediocrity at best. Probably a sign of the times but won’t return for a while.

reviews.author: Greg R
reviews.title: Poorly run
reviews.text: The property is great. The management is lacking. Coffee in the lobby? Or water? Or charging station for a tesla? Or a restaurant that doesn’t make you wait every time you dine? Or a lobby bar that is open all day? Or a concierge that makes reservations for you instead of giving you phone numbers to call on your own? None of the above. Uninspired leadership on display. Definitely not coming back to spend $1000 a night and $50 a day for a poolside chair.

reviews.author: HLM
reviews.title: Urine soaked sheets
reviews.text: My family and I checked into the hotel yesterday. The trip started off on a bad foot when our rooms were not ready by 4 pm. That was annoying. We wish that was our only problem. I got into bed at night and realized the sheets felt cold- I kept thinking why is this cold?? I then realized I think it is wet. I asked my husband to feel and he realized it was. We pulled the covers back and realized the sheets were wet. I just assumed they were not dry from the washing machine. We pulled the sheets back and the mattress pad was SOAKED with urine. The smell was horrible. We called downstairs and asked for a manager and housekeeping. The manager on duty showed up and basically told us to get over it. He had no room to move us to and he said I don’t think that’s urine. I said touch it and smell it. I already had to shower because I touched it. He refused to get close to it and asked us when we would be leaving. We had the connecting room as well for our kids- so we were spending close to $2k a night at the property and he dismissed the fact that the bed was stained w urine. The other family friendly resorts in Scottsdale are booked. We were forced to go to an airport hotel for the night and had to switch our flight to return home three days early. Sorry kids. Spring break is cut short because the bed is soaked with pee. The customer service was terrible. can’t believe the manager would dismiss urine on a bed. Housekeeping never even came to the room to address the situation. If you stay here-  check the sheets and mattress pad. They may be soaked with urine.

reviews.author: Dustin B
reviews.title: Family fun
reviews.text: We spent 6 days at the Phoenician over President’s day weekend this year and had a great time. We traveled with our 4 and 6 year olds and they loved every minute of the pools and splash pad. This is a great family resort with a ton of amenities and activities. Everyone was super nice and accommodating to our requests and the restaurants were delicious - We didn’t have one bad meal the whole trip, even out super picky kids were happy!  If your traveling with young kids, definitely check out the kids club schedule as they had some cool activities when we were there.  This was our first time to Arizona for a family trip and we couldn’t have been happier!

reviews.author: Glenn F
reviews.title: Worse Conference Hotel ... Luxury should not be in the Name!
reviews.text: The hotel staff does not care about the conference attendees.  Do not expect a nice room if you are a conference hotel rate.  My room was on the driveway entrance to the hotel; Luxury street level room.

reviews.author: Mfroning56
reviews.title: Superb Service!
reviews.text: We had an awesome time and the service was amazing. We had an incredible service level in our breakfast at Mowry and Cotton from Christine Lam. She was so attentive, professional and upbeat. Sure made our morning…She didn’t miss a beat and kept the coffee coming on a cool and windy morning!

reviews.author: J W
reviews.title: Mother daughter get away
reviews.text:
OMG, I didn’t think a resort with all the amenities still existed! So many places even pre-COVID have scaled back any luxury items requiring you to ask for even a bar of soap. 
They have staff working in all areas of the resort, even someone to greet us with a 2am arrival. Daily housekeeping and a desire to help you fully relax and enjoy a retreat. There is an on-site spa, fitness center, pools, restaurants, golf, and of course a beautiful view. I would highly recommend.

reviews.author: Serge v
reviews.title: Poor service - disappointing
reviews.text: Despite more than half of the hotel/rooms were empty the staff didn’t accept to use any of the upgrade certificates. We stayed two nights and booked 3 rooms spend all days at the resort despite it was a Monday hardly anyone was still there a late check out was offered until noon.. official check out is 11am  - we only asked for one room Being a long-term member very disappointing experience - a little arrogant not very customer friendly. Pool area is great incl. staff food is expensive. Disappointing experience

reviews.author: Dad2Twins1969
reviews.title: Beautiful property great spa pool and food. Highly recommend.
reviews.text: This is my third time here. Love to come here in the winter time. What a wonderful property. Great spa. Great pool. The food is top notch too. Great experience. Highly recommend.  Golf is great too. Love to get up with the sunrise in the AM great views and have a glass of wine at Thirsty Camel bar around fire table.

reviews.author: jaizee
reviews.title: Exceeded Expectations
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is a large resort - my expectations were not high and I have to say we really enjoyed our time here. The rooms are not “new” or stylish, but I had nothing to complain about in terms of cleanliness or “worn out” furniture. We did have a very large room (Executive Suite) and I did not feel like there was enough furniture to fill the room up adequately but the bed was comfortable and there was so much space for my family (2 adults, 2 kids). Our room did not have a great view - looked out onto a concrete structure - we were trying to decide if we wanted to ask for a better view but looking at the layout of the hotel, it seems like many of the rooms do NOT have a view.  I can see how this could be very disappointing to some people and while it would have been really nice, ultimately it didn’t affect our overall enjoyment. One additional quirk was there was a cricket stuck between the walls (we spied an antenna) who was pretty loud at night. We did not get the staff to do anything about it because we didn’t want them to spray chemicals near where our kids were sleeping. 

We were there at a busy time of year - the biggest issue with that was that every morning when we tried to get breakfast at the main restaurant, Mowry and Cotton, there was a very long wait. And the restaurant staff definitely seemed a bit overwhelmed. 

One of the best things about the resort was the pool scene. Plenty of chairs such that I didn’t feel the need to ever fight for a spot.  More importantly, the staff at the pool was the best. Our favorite was Gennaro (I am so sorry but I probably have his name wrong - it starts with a G though. He was really great and memorable but it’s been over a month since we stayed and I am not good with names!). Literally as soon as you sit down they bring you a pitcher of ice water and replenish throughout the day. Additionally I think the pool menu is much better and more inventive than the usual pool menu at other resorts. I read some people complain about the music by the pool but I liked it. I would be the first to complain if it was too loud but I never found that to be the case and I liked the soundtrack. 

We also loved utilizing the pickleball/basketball/tennis courts. Easy to get court reservations even at this busy time of year and easy to borrow equipment. It’s a great amenity. 

Finally, we had dinner one night at J&G and enjoyed it immensely - the views are spectacular and the food was so good. (We hadn’t planned ahead and didn’t know anything about the restaurant beforehand - the concierge booked the table for us on our first day of our stay). 

Overall, we had a really nice experience here - I am surprised to say that we want to go back already!

reviews.author: Anish S
reviews.title: For the price, Good but not Great.
reviews.text:
As you can read from the other reviews and blogs, this is an incredible resort with an amazing backdrop of the camelback mountain.  From the lobby to the hotel grounds to the golf course, the property is beautiful.  Not to mention the gym, which looks amazing.  
Rather than concentrating on all those positives, I'll highlight the few negatives we came across during our 4 night stay at the resort.  

1.  The biggest frustration for us was the self-park garage.  The garage is attached to the hotel so getting from the room to the car wasn't an issue (though you do have to take a different elevator).  The issue was getting in and out of the garage itself.  You have to swipe your room key card to open the gate.  However, 95% of the time the gate did not open.  Coming in, this was rectified by pulling a ticket.  On the way out though, you had to call for help so they could remotely open the gate.  It's really weird to have such broken technology for a resort of its class, not to mention the fact that each room is $500+ per night.  Either fix it so guests are not troubled with this nuisance, or just leave the gate permanently open.  

2.  You could see some wear and tear in the room hallways and the bedrooms themselves.  They should spend a bit of time making the hallways and the bedrooms look just as nice as the lobby and the grounds.  The rooms have a marriott look and feel and smell to them.  Which I would not have expected. 

3.  Resort offers free beer tasting every day at 11 AM.  This was a very weird experience for us.  The first day the bartender offered all 3 beers but only to those that showed up at 11 AM, not any later.  The next day, the bartender/manager stated that the beer tasting is only for one beer, not all beers.  What kind of beer tasting is this.  My family and I assumed this was a normal beer tasting where you get to try multiple beers on tap, hence we sat down at the bar looking to enjoy the experience.  However, after we were served the beer, the bartender/manager were whispering to each other and it was obvious they were talking about us (based on how they kept using their eyes to point at us).  

4.  The pools have 2 hot tubs.  One upstairs by the main pool and the 2nd on the lower level.  The hot tub up top was always full given it's the most convenient.  Unfortunately the hot tub downstairs had the heater broken so the water would be luke warm at best.  It's unfortunately that a hot tub cannot be heated during the winter months - hopefully they fixed that quickly.  

5.  While certainly not something a hotel is required to provide but we wished there were more vegetarian options for the pool menu.  The online menu shows more veg options but apparently that's outdated as the menu we were given in person has limited veg options (which was confirmed when we questioned the lack of options with the bar manager). 

Everything else was amazing at the hotel.  The service (except for what i mentioned was great as well).  A special shoutout to concierge, especially Rebecca who responded to every email of mine and always provided the right suggestion/recommendation for dinner and for hikes.  She was def. integral in ensuring a successful and enjoyable vacation.  

For families, this is a wonderful resort and a very comfortable stay with spacious rooms and large pools.

reviews.author: Morris C
reviews.title: Amazing proerty and staff!
reviews.text: We spent two nights here after a conference at the Westin to unwind and just relax. Amamazing property and staff. Highly recommend. Awesome pool area, great dining options, and a friendly, hard working staff. Will return.

reviews.author: MsHellfire
reviews.title: Not as good as last time
reviews.text:
Booked this trip based on a superb experience staying in February and decided it would be a perfect one stop shop experience for Christmas. Unfortunately the flawless stay last time was not replicated this time but I still enjoyed this property more than JW Marriott Camelback. 

Found it very difficult to book in for afternoon tea even trying well in advance. Managed to get the Bonvoy ambassador team to help me. Struggled even more to get a reservation at J&G steakhouse which was a frustrating and lengthy endeavor and I eventually found out that the restaurant was not only closed the night I wanted to dine there but the ONLY place I could have dinner was Mowry & Cotton. So much for my one stop shop resort full of options. With less than a month to go before my stay the hair salon rang me to advise they were cancelling my hair appointment because they were closing for an indefinite period of time. 

Check in: very easy experience. For Ambassador status I was afforded a small upgrade. Unfortunately sun didn’t seem to hit the balcony at any period of the day which was in stark contrast to my previous stay. $37 breakfast credit which could be used towards a la carte and buffet options. Room was ready early - was great to be able to drop my things in the room before the spa treatment. 

Room: well sized basic room. I liked that there was a bathtub but it wasn’t a large one and due to the shape and size was not really conducive to soaking. Toiletries were Byredo. Bottles of water were supplied and re-stocked throughout stay. Housekeeping came daily and for turndown also. 

Spa: last time was flawless but not so this time though treatments and therapists were very good. One of the reception staff was antagonizing and impatient when I was asking questions of her. The spa attendant during my first visit could not have been more unfriendly and unhelpful. Attendants were nowhere to be found when I needed them during the first visit and restroom by the relaxation area was out of paper towels for the four hours of treatments. Second visit no one was rude or unhelpful but at the salon the nail file sliced into several layers of my skin and cut me which was uncomfortable. Third visit during my stay was very good with different spa attendants on duty than the first visit. 

Afternoon tea: a bit expensive for the holiday experience. They were offering photos which was a lovely gesture but if I may suggest - that type of information would be good to have with the holiday afternoon tea information because had I known about it, I would have put make up on and as it was my hair wasn’t done nicely due to the cancelled appointment I had booked in for before the afternoon tea. 

Mowry & Cotton: delicious a la carte breakfast and gracious servers each time. Dinner food was also good despite not being what I was hoping for in terms of variety of restaurants. 

Really nice service from the front desk - asked for a late check out but it couldn’t be afforded for my room. They managed to find me a another room instead for my last few hours and it was so appreciated. 

I hate resort fees and was able to take advantage of none of the inclusions because I had no interest in them. I hope a hotel significantly more wealthy than I am enjoys the forced donation from me. While I think resort fees are unethical, if you must charge them, please think about a dining or spa credit. 

Overall it’s still a great property with polished and professional staff but I no longer think of it as the best Marriott in the US which was my impression after my first stay.

reviews.author: starfish7
reviews.title: Not the same
reviews.text: We stayed here  5 times before covid and loved it.  Now its not the same.  No guard at the entrance asking you if you are staying there and your name ... this is a big negative, its a safety ting ... plus the Falcon guy is gone so bird poop every where ... and yes, the music is too loud.   I was  expecting the coffee/tea in the morning to be gone  ... negative is when we checked in and asked, he said oh, only on some days.  I will not be coming back for a bit.

reviews.author: Johnny P
reviews.title: The most magical weekend ever!!
reviews.text: We are staying here to celebrate my husband’s retirement after 25 years in law enforcement and public service.  The hotel team at The Phoenician has made our stay absolutely perfect in all ways.  Our room has an incredible terrace and view, the food and bar experiences have been perfect and all of the staff is top notch.  From the front desk to housekeeping, all amazing.  Thank you for helping us have the most special weekend possible, Merry Christmas Phoenician team!!

reviews.author: wine4et99
reviews.title: Worst hotel experience in 20 years
reviews.text:
No value to being a Marriott member.   Our 1 st room was just off the lobby.  Drunk guests coming in late and cars arriving at the front area    After three nights we asked for our room to be changed.  Our options were a room with two queens or a king handicap accessible.   We asked about the differences, the person at the desk gave a minimal explanation.  We chose the handicap room for the king bed.  

The new room had 1 sink vs two, lousy views, low bed and a queen bed, not a king.   We called and complained but we’re tired of moving.   Also the hotel has the worst pillows we asked for foam but never got them.  The beds were very soft.

We have never slept this bad over 5 nights.  I could have slept in a courtyard and had better rest.  Called and spoke to management and front desk staff.  One manager unexpectedly bought us dinner one night but it did not make up for the overall lousy service and experience 

I have no desire to ever go back.   We left Scottsdale for the Ritz Carlton in Tucson.  They should train the Phoenician staff.  What a night and day difference.  

Bottom line the property is beautiful but the hotel is grossly overpriced and overrated.

reviews.author: Bruce A
reviews.title: OVER RATED! Over Priced! Terrible Service!
reviews.text:
The Phoenician clearly is living on its legacy and lack of any luxury competition in the area!! 

The property is beautiful. However, the service and experience are absurdly poor! Housekeeping staff gathers in the hall at 8:00 AM and it sounds like a construction site in NYC! Loud banging, rowdy conversation no consideration for guests. This rude loudness continues pretty much throughout the day as they frequently convene in the hallways and carry on and constantly yell to each other down the hallways!

Most everywhere in the hotel is understaffed or they need some serious training! Long waits in restaurants, at the front desk and calling the concierge despite not many guests being present.

As an Envoy Ambassador member, you'll get absolutely no consideration. It's clear that either Marriott or the hotel (or both) want the affiliation for booking purposes but as a guest, you're no different than the average traveler!

Counting the days until the new Ritz opens up the road!!!

reviews.author: Cami
reviews.title: Stunning resort
reviews.text: We are already planning our next Thanksgiving stay. We absolutely loved the resort and the spa, it could not have been more perfect. The room was so spacious and the grounds were beautiful. Can’t wait to come back next year!

reviews.author: tysonandsasha
reviews.title: Bring Earplugs!
reviews.text: I don't get it. The service is satisfactory, the amenities are adequate, and it's clean. But a "luxury" hotel, this is not. DEAFENING music at the pool from 9:30 - 5 pm every single day. I booked a casita with a balcony, and it's completely unusable. We cannot hear ourselves think in our room, even with the balcony doors and curtains closed. It's loud in the main building, loud in the casitas, loud everywhere. When we asked for a quiet room, we were offered one in the building next door. No different. We are here currently, but I'm so desperate for quiet that I'm considering leaving early and returning to a more tranquil Marriott property.

reviews.author: Naples Nomad
reviews.title: Nice but not a 5 Star Property
reviews.text:
I am a Titanium Marriott member and Spire Ambassador IHG member (lots of hotel nights).  The outside main areas of the resort were very beautiful and well maintained, worthy of the 5 star status.  The difficulty I have is with the rooms and service at the hotel, which fell below expectations.  First, when we arrived, while it was busy, there were no bell hops available and we ended up pulling our own luggage into the lobby until one came by and grabbed it.  We showed up about 2 p.m. so I expected a slight delay before check in.  We had dinner set for 6 p.m. and figured we would have enough time.  At 4:45 I went to the front desk and was told they were still cleaning a room for us.  About 15 minutes later, we were carted to a room with two double beds (requested a King). I asked to have it changed and was told there was nothing else available.  At check in, they failed to recognize status with their Marriott program (I know, petty), and no welcome gift in the room.  The front desk folks were not very friendly or helpful.  I also feel bad for the cart drivers as it was clear that they were overworked and understaffed.

Room felt very dated and in definite need of a face lift.  I also am not a fan of the multiple separate buildings where the rooms are.  Think apartment buildings and one big hotel building.  The biggest turn off was that thee were multiple insects/moths dead on the floor along the double doors and carpeting.  If they were cleaning the room, I would think they would have found these. The other issue was, we had a lovely view of the 18th hole, so we had to keep our curtains shut absent making lots and lots of friends at all hours of the day.  

Food prices at the restaurant were reasonable and in line with most resorts. Drinks were also in line with what I would expect.

Given the price to stay here, I think they could do a lot better and make it an absolutely stunning location.  As it is, I probably wouldn't stay here again unless the room was significantly discounted.  I much prefer some of the other properties over this one.

reviews.author: jcveit
reviews.title: Resting on its laurels, but has the potential to become fantastic again
reviews.text:
I arrived at 11:30AM for an annual golf weekend, room wasn’t ready and that’s completely understandable as I was before checkin. I gave the front desk my phone number and went to grab lunch (side note one of the best Salmon BLTs I’ve ever had) and do some work, a few hours later nothing and I was told a few more minutes for a housekeeping supervisor to inspect the room. Finally a phone call came around 2:30. 

A valet took me by golf cart to my upgraded casita. It was a bit removed from the hustle and bustle but still close enough to all the action. The room was well appointed with a fantastic soaking tub. Honestly, while as a Titanium Bonvoy member I appreciate the upgrade, but the room overlooked the main road to the hotel. 

The casitas interior looked to be much more updated than my friends room in the main house (in my view). If you look at the hotel from the Spa or the pro shop, you see a hotel that is very stuck in the 80s.

The next day a friend and I also had a spa appointment, checkin was seamless and the facilities were just as I had remembered them from a few years ago. My massage was excellent and Chris did a phenomenal job. We sat by the spa pool afterwards and the facilities while lovely were frankly understaffed. There were 1.5 servers (let’s call it 1.5 since there were technically two servers, but one server said yes to every request but never delivered). After an hour of slow service and a limited food menu we called it quits.

Overall the food was quite good at the hotel, but the overall service at the hotel makes you feel as if you’re non-existent. I had originally booked the Canyon Suites and rearranged my reservations since my friends were staying at the main house of the Phoenician. Perhaps in hindsight that was a mistake, I felt like a number at the main part of the hotel.

While the aesthetics of this report are beautiful, the service just lacks all around. Lines to speak with anyone at the front desk were always long, even for simple requests such as to get keys recoded. The upper bar by the front desk was a joke to a get a drink, for three nights straight we were just looked over. I get they host various events on weekends, but it leaves guests feeling like second class citizens. 

We’ve come to the Spa at the Phoenician so many times before with fantastic service, and we expected the hotel experience to be the same and unfortunately that was not the case. 

The Phoenician has a great reputation, but you just can’t call it a luxury property with the current standard. I’m sure it will do fine with the pent up demand to travel, but I just don’t feel as if it lived up to the luxury collection brand.

I want to love the Phoenician, and perhaps it’s Covid or issues finding staff but there’s nothing leaving me to rush back. The golf is great, so is the spa and pools. But don’t expect to quickly grab a bite, because there’s no one to serve you and the restaurant is at half occupancy. 

Yes, the grounds are beautiful and the spa and golf are a draw. But for the money and my experience after my last stay has me looking for another options in the area.

reviews.author: rabbibjk2018
reviews.title: Check Your Room in Advance
reviews.text:
We had a truly lovely weekend getaway at The Phoenician.

Great room, excellent service, good food, nice spa.

Here is the concern:  We reserved a room at a "casita," imagining privacy and space.  We discovered that said casita was on the second floor, with no elevator.  This was going to be impossible, as one of our party recently had knee surgery and could not manage the steps.

Why was this critical information not shared when the reservation was made?

So, the staff were accommodating enough about finding us another room, with elevator, which was lovely.  However, they neglected to share the fact that the room would be $800 per night MORE than the original, not inexpensive, room.

We enjoyed our two night getaway, yet, with modest meals, we wondered if 4K$ might not have been excessive and better spent elsewhere?

reviews.author: Robert N
reviews.title: A bit dated and so-so…
reviews.text: I hadn’t stayed here in a few years but definitely not up to five stars of the past.  In desperate need of a refresh.  Rooms dated, things falling apart, paint peeling off of exterior doors.  Clearly understaffed with reduced hours and some food venues closed.  I would say the service was just ok…again not up to 5 star billing.  It just felt tired and worn down.  Even the sign outside of the Marketplace was rusting down the side of the wall.  The Four Seasons, while quite farther out is an infinitely better experience.  Not sure whether Marriott is just milking this great old resort for cash flow or what.  One investment they made was a standalone gym building which was modern and nice.I hope they will refresh this once grand place back to its previous glory.

reviews.author: Stephanie P
reviews.title: Disappointed, Birthday Trip
reviews.text:
I checked in for a four night stay last Thursday 11/15, after flying in from San Antonio, Texas. I booked a stay two months in advance for a one bedroom, executive suite, with a balcony with a resort view. What was supposed to be a nice luxurious stay in an amazing room, to enjoy room service and champagne for my birthday turned in to a total disappointment! The room we were given had zero view. It was a horrible room that faced on all sides the adjacent buildings. No trees, no grass, no garden, no camelback mountain, no saguaro, no pool…concrete buildings! I didn’t book this stay to be in a concrete jungle. The room wasn’t cleaned to my standards, dirty fridge, etc. Lack of decor, very underwhelming. I am not totally convinced they don’t ever use this room for guests due to its condition.
Management repeatedly told me that all rooms were booked solid and they could offer me a measly $400 resort credit for food and beverage. After two nights they put us in the room I assume should have been ours to begin with. After spending $4k for a four night stay at a so called five star hotel, we were taken advantage of and screwed over by management and this hotel. Not a pleasant or positive experience.

reviews.author: B C
reviews.title: Poor experience, no hospitality, terrible value
reviews.text:
With ~400 Bonvoy nights and stays at over a half dozen properties in the luxury collection portfolio, this by far the worst property and experience. I would avoid and suggest elsewhere should you stay in Scottsdale (you can get much better for far less). Specifically,
- Am lifetime gold elite
- Checked in on the app as early as available - apprx 24 hrs before arrival 
- Had booked and reconfirmed King room
- Requested early check in

When I arrived not only was there no early check-in (which understand it’s only if available) but then they also put us in a room with two queens, see attached photo for our “view”. This hotel’s avg. rate is somewhere around $800 I believe. There was tremendous turnover the day we checked in so I am certain they could’ve found us a king sized room or even a better view (not to mention try for an upgrade, again, part of gold status, but of course also only if available). They didn’t even try. Hospitality is dead 

Went to the restaurant while waiting for the room to be ready. Couldn’t even get any server to grab a second beer. I get that everyone is short staffed and trying, but again, you’re paying for “luxury” and this ain’t it.

reviews.author: suesv
reviews.title: Almost Perfect
reviews.text: We stayed here four nights for vacation last week.  The resort is beautiful and expansive and the rooms are large and well appointed.  All employees and services that we encountered at the front desk, housekeeping, pool service & restaurants were excellent.   They really do a great job with customer service all around and the staff seem happy to be working there.  We ate exclusively at the resort restaurants and were very happy with them all.  The only negative that takes away a star was our room location.  We booked a King Mountain View but it wasn't ready when we arrived and they offered us a City View that was and we took it.  Unfortunately, the room overlooked a massive concrete roof and the housekeeping walkway between the buildings which at times was loud moving the cleaning carts.  After 2 nights we asked if a Mountain View was available and they moved us.  Again unfortunately, the room was on the bottom floor with our patio steps away from the cactus garden path that people walked on all day into the evening, so no privacy at all and was awkward even using it.   So, a warning, know specifically what your view will be when you book.   If we had had a better one it would have added much more enjoyment to our stay.  That being said, this is a great resort and we would return.

reviews.author: Naomi
reviews.title: Beautiful Desert Resort
reviews.text: My husband and I visited The Phoenician in January and had a wonderful visit - beautiful location, beautiful room, amazing bydero bath products, and awesome pelotons in the gym. Thanks to Marriott Titanium Elite status we were upgraded to a firetable casita guest room with a mountain view (and two full baths!) which was very luxurious. We also had complimentary breakfast at Mowry + Cotton each day, and were treated to incredible service by Christine, who not only ensured we had a wonderful dining experience, but also gave us great local tips. We hope to visit the property again soon!

reviews.author: Ned B
reviews.title: Great staff great resort
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed there for a week and was able to get a room
Upgrade to a suite via ambassador status.  

The staff are incredible…Christine and Ernesto at the main restaurant near the pool were just tremendous.  The operator I think her name is Latizia or something like that equally impressive.  Pool staff were on point.  

Just had a great relaxing time at this beautiful facility.  Uber’s to old Scottsdale for meals and cocktails were five minute rides.  

Breakfasts are great and their coffee blend is really good. Avocado toast with poached eggs so damn good. 

Anyway…great time at a beautiful spot.

reviews.author: AZ-LGE
reviews.title: Perfect Anniversary Choice
reviews.text: Fantastic 5* resort at the base of Camelback Mountain.  We were upgraded to a Firepit Casita that had a great mountain view in addition to the main building.  There was a nice patio with chairs, a table with chairs and an additional outdoor couch.  We had a mini fridge which worked great as we brought our own wine, beer, snacks, and makings for Irish Coffee.  Service was outstanding, especially the guys by the pool who kept us supplied with ice water, set up our umbrella, and took care of towels.  Since I'm Marriott Titanium, we had vouchers for breakfast which applied $38.95 towards what we ordered.  Even with that, breakfast was about $25 including the 18% added tip.  Drinks by the pool were equally expensive – averaging about $20 each with the included 20% tip.  However it was really no different that being in Hawaii and to be expected.  I had an Corporate rate for a basic room which was $437 + $86 in resort fees and taxes.  Our upgraded room was significantly better and would have been several hundred more if we had booked it.  We had a excellent 2 night stay.   I'd definitely like to stay there again.

reviews.author: FSFan
reviews.title: Complete Chaos
reviews.text:
Short version: even though it’s touted as a Luxury property, there is zero luxury here, mostly because it is overcrowded and understaffed. It is basically your run of the mill basic Marriott resort experience, for twice the price.

Long version: We knew we were in trouble when we pulled up and saw the massive crowds waiting around. We hoped for the best, but check in took forever (long lines) — even though I am Bonvoy Gold there was no dedicated line. We also got exactly zero Gold amenities — the status was completely ignored.

Our luggage took over one hour to be brought to the room. I had to call 3 times for them to finally bring it — the first 2 times nobody picked up the phone.

Fortunately we self parked so we didn’t have to deal with long valet wait times.

The pool area was super overcrowded with all the loungers crammed together like canned sardines.

We got a (very expensive) cabana the day after, but our attendant also showed up only 45 minutes after we checked in to the cabana.

There was a constant smell of gas in the air in the Adult Pool area, probably from the hot tub heater.

The kicker though was when we asked another attendant for locker rooms where we could shower and change — he swore there were none on the property. Nobody would pick up the phone either. Fortunately the chat feature on the app was the redeeming factor and they told us to go to the gym building… which did have locker rooms but they clearly hadn’t been attended all day since there were no towels in the men’s one and there was a cockroach in the women’s.

Finally: make sure you don’t leave anything in the room accidentaly past check out because housekeeping will throw everything you leave behind away immediately. Again: fairly typical on your typical Marriott but just another proof point the only luxurious thing about this place is the price.

reviews.author: C B
reviews.title: 100% Lackluster
reviews.text:
The 10 times during my stay that I called the front desk, eight of those times I was immediately placed on hold and nobody picked up and answered my call for at least 5 minutes, and a couple of those times it was closer to eight minutes.  That is unacceptable.  Also, the same with the few times I called the concierge the same.  Also, the sofa in my room was filthy dirty!  So gross I wouldn't even sit on it for two seconds.  The room was not updated as in the pictures on the website.  Instead of a luxury feel which I was expecting, I got more of a regular Westin Hotel vibe.  

The 10 times during my stay that I called the front desk, eight of those times I was immediately placed on hold and nobody picked up and answered my call for at least 5 minutes, and a couple of those times it was closer to eight minutes.  That is unacceptable.  Also, the same with the few times I called the concierge the same.  Also, the sofa in my room was filthy dirty!  So gross I wouldn't even sit on it for two seconds.  The room was not updated as in the pictures on the website.  Instead of a luxury feel which I was expecting, I got more of a regular Westin Hotel vibe.

In-room dining is way overpriced.  I was charged $62.00 for my breakfast which consisted of avocado toast, two eggs and a side of bread.

reviews.author: Lstuehmer
reviews.title: Amazing!!!
reviews.text:
We had a perfect stay for the last 5 days! We travel often and enjoy high end accommodations and experiences and I cannot say enough great things about this resort. It is beautiful and well maintained. We stayed in a king room on the 4th floor and we had an amazing view of the property. The room was huge, with two closets, an enormous bathroom with a big tub (wish there were bath salts to use in the tub!), step in glass shower, separate toilet, a long counter and full wall of mirrors. The bed was very comfortable. The room and entire resort were immaculate and very well cleaned.
The front desk staff was professional and attentive and always available (in person at the desk, calling them from the room isn’t helpful as the phone just rings and rings). The valet team…amazing! Always there to assist, offer bottled waters, etc.
The pools were wonderful. Plenty of chairs because there are so many pools! The pool attendants are constantly refreshing pitchers of ice water for you and the pool servers are always around offering drinks and food if you’d like. The pool service is fast!
The spa is the best we have ever been too…and I am a spa person. The epitome of relaxation, the spa, the staff, music, services, amenities and treatment cannot be beat! We had our treatments first thing in the morning and then got to spend the day at the spa enjoying the sauna, steam room, relaxation areas, whirlpool and our favorite…the rooftop pool. It’s quiet and wonderful. 
The Thirsty Camel is a great bar in the lobby that has a beautiful outdoor area with fire pits at night and a good menu for small bites. 
We loved the restaurant Cotton and Mowry for two of our breakfasts. Good selection and ambiance. Excellent service and the food came quickly…and tasted amazing. We also dined there for dinner one night. Although the food was good, our server wasn’t. He seemed more interested in watching the game on the TV in the bar than being a server so that was a bummer. 
Overall, we loved our experience here and we will definitely we back!!!

reviews.author: Dan O
reviews.title: Good but could be better
reviews.text:
First of all, I'm a little jaded and a bit of a hotel snob.  I'm a lifetime platinum marriott rewards traveler and have a good bit of history for comparison.  
This site did nothing to make a rewards member feel valued.  I tried to use my suite nights to upgrade my stay, but it was declined.  we were told the resort was fully booked.  I found this a little difficult to believe given the easy of finding a seat at the pool or a table at a restaurant.  
What I did notice was several large groups that came during our stay.  My guess is that this hotel caters to large groups and gives them preference for suites and choice rooms.  
The regular king pool view room is nothing special.  For the rate that we paid, it was a disappointment.  The doors leading to the bathroom and the closets make it impossible to walk through the hall way when opened at the same time.  
The resort itself is nice.  The pools were outstanding.
The staff were very nice and all should be complimented.  
All in all, I would not go back.  Probably would look for a resort that caters more to the individual than the large group.

reviews.author: Diane T
reviews.title: Luxury Hotel
reviews.text: We spent 7 nights at The Phoenician in Sept/Oct. with our 10 year old granddaughter. It is a beautiful resort with lovely views. The pool staff are extremely friendly and attentive. The elevators are awesome and quick, state of the art! The restaurant Mowry and Cotton was good but very very pricey, especially the cocktails!! Front desk staff somewhat dismissive! The housekeeping staff was the BEST! Not sure if it was the time of year but weren't a lot of children, and even though we used one of the family pools it was filled with 30-40ish somewhat arrogant people seemingly annoyed that our granddaughter was using the pool. Valet or self park very pricey too! Very conveniently located to airport and many excellent restaurants.

reviews.author: pscuderi
reviews.title: Pricey But Worth It
reviews.text:
My wife and I spent 5 nights at the Phonecian in early October. We were looking to relax and this desert oasis fit the bill.

The hotel was sold out while we were there, so we were expecting the pools to be crowded. But that was not the case. It was always easy to find a place to sit by any of the pools and get food/beverages served to you. Most days there is a Falconer walking around the pool area chasing the birds away.

The restaurants are top notch. J&G Steakhouse served maybe the best fillet I’ve ever had. I tried a different breakfast at Mowry & Cotton each morning; and they were all very good.

The spa is beautiful. There’s an exclusive pool on the roof that you can use any day you pay for spa services.

Despite the price being fairly high, we’re already planning another trip!

reviews.author: Jojo Y
reviews.title: Best luxury hotel
reviews.text: Best luxury hotel in Scottdale. Their elevator is different than normal elevator. Very high tech hotel. The spa is the best. When you stay here as soon as you drive through the entrance, you will forget that you are in the city of Scottdale. It felt like you are somewhere else. Best customer service. Looking for a place to getaway, this is the place. You won't regret it. Make sure you visit the spa.

reviews.author: RoseAnn G
reviews.title: Beautiful..great location..great service (mostly) .
reviews.text:
Pros: beautiful hotel, great location, lovely pools - plenty of lounges. Great pool staff..nice touch pitcher of ice water placed for you as soon as you grab your lounge. Food was very tasty and wait staff terrific. 

Cons: tried each day to call front desk...was put on hold for well over 10 minutes when I finally gave up. Then tried housekeeping and concierge..same. no one answered. 

Finally walked (was at Casita) to front desk to ask our questions. Woman at front desk was very dismissive when I asked about answering phones.  ( plus her mask kept falling down) .Titanium bonvoy..no one explained about bfast coupons etc. 

Re restaurant (Mowry)  food very good plus good service. Did have to wait each day 30 plus for a table. Seemed like waitstaff shortage. ..but nice seating outside.

reviews.author: MermanSF
reviews.title: Could have been a nice stay but!
reviews.text:
Great amenities and nice staff but lost two stars due to:

- I asked for one hour late check out since my flight was delayed and they said no. I’m a Marriott elite member and this is the first time a Marriott hotel rejected my request. Starting 10:30, staff kept banging on the door while I said I’d leave at 11 to the first round! 
- Accent shop: staff are very rude and have an attitude- I don’t know why! None of the staff at this store wears a mask while others do! 
- Mask wearing by guests is almost zero. I understand the hotel can’t do much but they don’t even encourage it like other spas in town do. There are some signs with CDC guidelines that are outdated.

reviews.author: Tj B
reviews.title: Some good, some not so good
reviews.text: My wife and I visited to celebrate our anniversary.  When we booked it, the reservationists at the hotel (we called direct) told us that he was putting us in for a room upgrade.  When we arrived, we checked in with a guy that really seemed bothered when we told him what the reservationists said.  He put us in a garden suite first floor that looked out over a beautiful concrete slab.  The good news is that we went back to the desk to a different guy and he did the right thing, what we expect from Marriott.  We got a much better view.  There was a wireless company that basically took over the property for 3 days.   Just disappointing.  But I want to call out Ashling who did an amazing job running around the pool and taking food and drink orders.  I’d recommend this property for a business event but not a personal visit.  There are too many places that are better for the price.

reviews.author: Rohit T
reviews.title: Horrible Management
reviews.text: We have our booking to stay two nights and afternoon tea at Phoenician. We called to inform them that we are feeling sick and would like to cancel our reservation and get credit for future dates! The horrible hotel management decline our request! We were just trying to be polite and not spread the germs! They are not good people abd care only about their bottom line! I would not recommend anyone for this incentive and horrible management.

reviews.author: Carolina
reviews.title: Birthday Weekend!
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here for my birthday weekend! Service was amazing and the food throughout the whole resort is delisioso! We had breakfast and lunch at mowry cotton. Awesome views in their outdoor seating and a great menu. They even have a trainer with a hawk to keep the pesky birds away so you can enjoy your food . It was cute and fun to watch the hawk hard at work flying around patrolling. Market place has yummy ice cream and quick and go breakfast foods and snacks. We stopped there early in the morning before heading out to sight see. Good coffee selections. Poolside was fun and quick service. Great options for pool food and servers come to your lounge chair.  We got upgraded to a king suite that was spacious and clean! Bathroom was a great size and there was a vanity in the room too for extra space for my makeup and hair tools. I didn’t feel crowded with mine and my husbands stuff. Definitely request pool view as the view of camel back mountain isn’t that amazing. Overall very happy with my stay here!

reviews.author: PVFamilyBMGN
reviews.title: So Happy We Stayed at The Phoenician
reviews.text: We stayed at The Phoenician over the Labor Day weekend.  Our children (7&10) enjoyed the Luau event consisting of the cup stacking game, the limbo party, and the bottle flip competition!  Such a wonderful recreation team!  We usually stay at quieter boutique hotels, but so glad we chose The Phoenician.  We loved walking around the beautiful Cactus Garden.  We also loved sitting by the pool while kids enjoyed the water slides.  I think The Phoenician is overall a top luxury hotel.  The room was VERY spacious and hotel grounds include multiple swimming pools, a spa, a gym, lawns for events and recreations, and a shopping mall (~5 stores). We also enjoyed our dinner at the J&G Steakhouse.  The restaurant had a beautiful view on the 5th floor.  We will definitely go back when/if we visit Phoenix/Scottsdale in the future.

reviews.author: Kristina L
reviews.title: Holiday Weekend Staycation!
reviews.text: The hotel is absolutely beautiful and our stay was great! The staff was extremely helpful and nice. The room was really clean and housekeeping was very attentive and responsive! Our family and friends had a great time.

reviews.author: Kelley G
reviews.title: Crazy fun getaway
reviews.text: Just got back from an amazing weekend!  We had a room facing Camelback - and the mountain is so close you can almost touch it.  Even tough they were crazy busy - we felt like rockstars at the pool bars.  Special mention to  Genarro at the main pool and Brandon at the rooftop bar.  We had 2 glorious relaxing days enjoying their service.  Highly recommend you visit and get to know them!!

reviews.author: Howard L
reviews.title: Scottsdale - getaway
reviews.text:
Had an awesome time in Scottsdale at the Phoenician Resort. The service and accommodations were outstanding.
