reviews.author: AnyaKap
reviews.title: Blasting music everywhere, all day long.
reviews.text: The hotel has beautiful grounds, three swimming pools and nowhere to sit without being bombarded by the speakers with annoying music. In the bathrooms it’s even louder. Fine Restaurants no exceptions. I cannot believe that not a single chase and table is quiet friendly. I couldn’t enjoy the pools or the restaurants. And even avoided bathrooms. In the fitness center two gigantic TVs where playing loud noise. Horrible. Does this hotel cater to kids? Or pretentious to be luxury? Should at least have options for people who cannot tolerate noise.

reviews.author: Ryan S
reviews.title: One of the rare hotels that is truly 5 stars!
reviews.text:
Just returned from a long weekend at the Phoenician. I can't recommend the hotel highly enough, it was truly 5 stars. The service from the concierge, to the front desk was all top notch. The housing keeping staff was also fantastic, cleaning the room more than once a day, refreshing water, toiletries, etc.

The grounds are all perfectly manicured, with new tennis courts and an athletic facility that has to be 5K sq feet. The machines/weights are all brand new, and the views are beautiful. The downstairs facility has a gaming area for kids/families to play around in as well.

Golf course is fairly priced for such a high end resort. Course was in great shape, carts are new and rental clubs are fresh. They have a 19th hole area, and are opening a new "tavern" shortly that will allow for even more dining/drinking post rounds. It's a great course, and Troon does a good job managing it.

Food was very good, and not abnormally expensive for what you got. The breakfast was continental (if you are Marriott elite w/bfast), and you could up charge for $10/day basically. Very reasonable, buffett was OK. Probably the most underwhelming food on property. J&G Steakhouse is a really good option, in line with high end steakhouses price wise. The pool food was fantastic, just wish it had been warmer!

Pools are great, adult pools, family pools, tons of options. Hot tub could be a little bigger, but fits 10+ people already.

Staff is truly fantastic. Very customer focused, always attentive to one's requests. 

WiFi is very high speed and complimentary (included in resort fee). 40mbps+, easy to stream content as needed. TVs are large and tons of channels in room. 

Rooms themselves are quite sizeable, seemed very new (fresh paint, etc). Lots of outlets, and lighting. 

Highly recommend the Phoenician, you won't be disappointed!

reviews.author: JohnJSmallwood
reviews.title: Afternoon tea here is a great experience
reviews.text:
My wife and I are spending the week in Phoenix on business, and we went to the Phoenician for afternoon tea.  When we saw all of the tables occupied, we realized that we had arrived about 15 minutes after seating ended.  As we turned to leave, the charming and lovely Lilliana approached us and offered to set a nearby table in the bar area. She didn't even mention that we were late - she just made us feel welcome. Thank you Lilliana!

The tea service itself was superb and must be enjoyed - in fact, my English wife gave it her seal of approval!  We will be back every time we visit Phoenix - this is a great way to spend an afternoon.

reviews.author: Areyoureallybringinghim
reviews.title: Beautiful Desert Oaisis
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel grounds, make sure you visit the cactus garden on the mountain side of the property! It is extremely quiet over there and beautiful. Also a very nice lobby and pool area. Drinks on the patio are a must

reviews.author: Seth G
reviews.title: Great stay!
reviews.text: Just came back from a great stay at the Phoenician for a conference /staycation.  5 star service all around. Highlight:  Daniel, the server at the spa, was a consummate Pro.  My wife loved the Margarita. Made our afternoon special!

reviews.author: Dan S
reviews.title: Built into Camelback -- good across Biz, adult, kid.
reviews.text: With only one notable exception, the service was extraordinary, the property is beautiful and food options are excellent.  The property is built into Camelback mountain and within walking distance of a popular local rigorous hike (Chola trail) and golf.  There is a relatively recently built spa on site and exercise facilities with an assortment of classes.  The hotel hasn't caught up to the "rigorous is better" crowd yet, so most classes are either yoga or relatively tame circuits.  Pools!!  Many pools including some adult only, a few hot tubs and there's an entire kid area with cool tree houses and a mini-water park.  In general, the service was exceptional, responsive, accurate, and quick.  The steak-house on the 5th floor was especially amazing and we were fortunate to have a junior chef look after us (Nicolas).  Mowry, the downstairs restaurant was excellent too -- with innovative menu items and plentiful and varied seating in and outside.  We had one meal where we were completely forgotten, mid meal, by a server but I suspect that's unusual and not emblematic.  The rooms are excellent and we happened to have an extra large balcony we enjoyed.

reviews.author: bsammy11
reviews.title: Really fantastic service
reviews.text: From the spa to the valet to the pool. Just an amazing service experience. Everyone was genuinely happy to help me and went above and beyond as the norm. Daniel at the spa pool is the best!! And the spa service were all very well done (a lot of times these big name places lack in the quality of spa services but no complaints here!)

reviews.author: twjones100
reviews.title: some good but mostly bad with this new Marriott ownership and renovation
reviews.text:
As I believe I mentioned in my previous review of The Phoenician, I have been coming to this hotel since 1980. It has always been a delight and though it was aging, I still liked it.  This new renovation has some good and points.  While the good points are great, the bad points will have me thinking twice about ever returning.  Sad but true.

Good points:  The new Spa is amazing. I loved everything about it from the facilities to the treatments.  Nice work!    I also really like the new revised lobby area which I was hesitant about.... I like the option to have more table space and seating for more than 2 people.  I also really appreciated the boutique area.  FINALLY!  For the first time since 1980, we actually bought some things.  I hear these are now 3rd party run and it has made a huge difference.

Bad points;  The Food!  every single menu In the entire hotel ( except JG Steakhouse) has 90% of the same items.... and they were TERRIBLE.  The new restaurant downstairs ( Mallory & Cotton ?) was a HUGE disappointment.  it looks like a Marriott and not a luxury resort restaurant.  The menu was random, food was awful, and the staff inattentive. And why oh why did you take the cozy little bar out from downstairs???? 

 The menu at the pool has also been changed with a bent on middle eastern flavors ( why??) and served in plastic bento boxes.  Not one thing - other than the chicken fingers from the kids menu - was good.  Room service was the same.  Limited horrible food ( except for the chicken fingers!).  And speaking of room service, they were very slow.  The gave us time to expect it when we ordered and were another 20 mins past that.  And what have you done to the little coffee shop??  Again, the menu is limited, the pastry selection is terrible, and it closes at 6pm so getting ice cream after dinner is not even an option.  In addition to the lack of variety, they now only serve Diet Pepsi.  BIG MISTAKE.  If you are a Coke product person, this is not ok.  Sometimes the wait staff ask if Pepsi was ok ( no!) and sometimes they would repeat that you wanted a Diet Coke and just bring you the Pepsi instead.  Not ok either.  If someone at the bar goes to order a vodka tonic and the bartender says sorry we only have tequila, that would not be acceptable.  Pepsi only should not be acceptable either.

Wait Staff.  What a joke.  At the pool they were more interested in talking to each other than servicing the guests.  Most of the staff at the Thirsty Camel bar or the downstairs restaurant did not look like they belonged at a Five Star resort.  Many of them were sloppily dressed and again inattentive. 

New Decor:  The darker paint in the bathrooms does not go with anything else in the room and really makes the bathroom too dark for my liking.  I have no doubt it will start to look dated and worn very quickly. The cheap bathtub remodel (whit plastic tub insert on brown marble decking) looks cheap and again takes away from the luxury feel.  "glitzy" hallway wallpaper and scones do not tie into anything else in the hotel. Very Random choice in my opinion.

Still to be determined... the pool seating situation. While they have added seating and a now a "reserved" section, the pool was not crowded on this last visit so I cannot properly address that now.

So - To sum up this review,  the horrible food is enough to keep me from returning to my once favorite desert gem.  Seriously. I come to The Phoenician because I can stay on property and relax and it used to be seamless.  If I now have to think about where every meal now has to come from, then I will choose someplace else to go.

reviews.author: J B
reviews.title: Not Good for Fine Hotels and Resorts Travelers
reviews.text: The online pricing included 2 rates for our selected room, one was standard and one included an amenity.  I made the reservation for standard rates.  I usually travel using the American Express Fine Hotels and Resorts benefits so I went to the AmEx FHR website and it said to call AmEx to get rates.  When I called the AmEx agent, she was quoted a rate $100 per night higher than the published rates.  When she objected and asked to have the FHR benefits added to my reservation, her request was told the nightly rate had to be higher in order to cover the FHR benefits, especially the guaranteed late check out.  What?  So why go through FHR if you have to pay for the benefits?  Bad Faith!  I canceled the reservation and booked The Royal Palms which turned out to also be an AmEx FHR participant.  Had a wonderful experience at the Royal Palms.

reviews.author: Halie E
reviews.title: Upgraded upon arrival
reviews.text: Writing my review early because of such a satisfying welcome and arrival. Staying here on business and I’m very impressed with the staff and check in process. I was upgraded immediately and greeted with a smile - from the valet to reception. The rooms are spacious and have big comfy beds. Plenty of amenities and can’t wait to explore more of the property.

reviews.author: Traveling_M_from_CA
reviews.title: Nice stay in a dramatic backdrop
reviews.text: This hotel, with the Camelback mountain in the background, is an oasis of calm and sophistication. The service is impeccable however, I found the bedroom decor to be a tad bland.  Note:   it’s also a rather expensive resort (luckily, I was on a business trip).

reviews.author: 830titat
reviews.title: High Tea with my Favorite gal pals was so nice with Pianist playing tunes from Musicals I knew.
reviews.text: I surely did not expect so many little sandwiches to choose from right from the beginning and in any amount of several or just your favorite. The second course of the Scones was so good with all the sweet butter and the last course was PERFECT small bites of cakes, eclairs and chocolate covered strawberries.

reviews.author: alyssamartell14
reviews.title: sad to see this place to turn just another hotel
reviews.text: I have come to this hotel for over 28 years, needless to say i used to love this place with every ounce of me, but as any place does after a while they started to make cut backs. , their phenominal easter brunch  turned into a casino brunch, over salted and no class. just because you serve crab and have chef hats does not mean it is "classy" . maybe if you had never been to this place in its prime or if you are used to eating poorly this place would look nice. but for the price you pay it is not worth it any more( believe me i would have paid $500 a person to have what it use to be ), the decor is poor taste and their excellent their staff turned into snobs who could give a crap about any of the guests.and went from a upscale resort to what feels like a family resort/ best western this hotel has made a turn for the worst.

reviews.author: bukagirl
reviews.title: What a property
reviews.text:
Beautifully maintained grounds, make sure you see the cactus garden and the other smaller pool with a beautiful waterfall near it.
The gym is unbelievable all new state of the art equipment. 
The rooms are very luxurious a huge soaking tub, heaps of towels a tad rough however was surprised.
Lovely views, entertainment in the lounge, several bars.
Would highly recommend and return.

reviews.author: DesertDan77
reviews.title: Fun to see a world-famous resort
reviews.text: You know this is different because there's a staff guy manning the gate watching every incoming car. I can't afford to stay here, so I walked around and grabbed coffee at one of the shoppes. No golf course view? Nah, just a view of the driveway! That was disappointing, but the property overall is very impressive. If you're invited to a meeting or party here; or someone else is paying for your room, the Phoenician is top-notch and deserves its reputation.

reviews.author: Ryla_M
reviews.title: Very Luxurious
reviews.text: We are staying in a casita with a outdoor gas firepit.  Our view of Camelback Mountain and pool area is very beautiful.  The room is luxurious and spacious.  King bed - comforatable with many pillows.  Rain Shower and soaking bathtub.  We have 2 closets, refrigerator, large flat screen tv on wall.  Sliding doors with screens can be opened at night to let in fresh air.  The grounds are beautiful with tennis, golf, spa, walking trails, pickleball and much more.  Very beautiful at night with lighting and fountains.  Highly recommended to stay here.

reviews.author: 788katherineg
reviews.title: At the top of the list
reviews.text:
My husband and I had never been to Arizona before so we decided to spend our 5 year anniversary there this past November. Growing up in the midwest, our vacations almost always centered around Florida or South Carolina. I was a bit nervous venturing to the desert for fear it would be boring and not tropical feeling. Scottsdale surely did not disappoint and neither did The Phoenician. The dry desert heat is phenomenal compared to the humid south, and we loved the amazing restaurants in Scottsdale, hiking Camelback Mountain and the service at this beautiful resort.

Apparently we came at an opportune time because it was the very start of peak season (first week of November) so the resort was not crowded and the temperature was at a perfect 80 degrees. The grounds of the Phoenician are massive and expertly groomed, and while we were staying there there were at least 2 large conventions going on but luckily the place is so big that those large groups never "took over" any of the pools/restaurants/bars, etc. Our room was also gorgeous with a view of Camelback mountain and the cactus garden. The one drawback was that the room was a bit of a hike from the lobby, pools, etc. but we were never really in a hurry so it didn't matter. 

We loved getting lattes every morning from The Marketplace, and having a delicious breakfast at Mowry and Cotton. The service and ambiance at Mowry and Cotton was great and the breakfast was delicious. The highlight in terms of service and experience was at the spa and spa pool. We booked spa treatments one day and spent the rest of the day relaxing at the private spa pool. The service at the spa pool there from our waiter, Gennaro, was literally the best service we've experienced at any spa or resort. Gennaro was friendly, fun to talk to, and went out of his way to make sure our experience was relaxing and memorable. The following day we decided to pay the premium to get the spa privileges despite not having treatments so that we could relax by that pool again before our flight back home. 

Needless to say, we cannot wait to plan another trip back to Scottsdale and when we do we will definitely be staying at The Phoenician.

reviews.author: bestfamilyadventures
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text:
My family enjoyed an extended stay at The Phoenician. Our casita fire table room was separate from the main hotel and easily walkable. The newly renovated common areas including the: pools, athletic centre and Spa all beautiful. Only a short Uber ride to old town for shopping and restaurants.

A few notable mentions: Joanna P, Camelback Mountain Hike (Hunter), Afternoon Tea (entire team), Mowry and Cotton for breakfast (Jorje), Trey (Front Desk), Spa and Mother of Pearl Pool (Daniel) and finally Alain (who left personalized notes at turndown). Thank you for a great stay!

reviews.author: Travel
reviews.title: A Few Days over Thanksgiving
reviews.text:
Decent place, feels very corporate.  They have a small kids pool area, but if your traveling with a teenager not much to do on site.  Cactus Garden behind hotel was nice - about 10 minutes back there.  

What I don't like about where these resort hotels are going is that they charge to many fees for things that should be included.  A lot of the pool chairs were full but they wanted to charge us to sit in a area that had about 100 chairs open and maybe 3 folks in 3 chairs.  Charge more for the room and stop the nickel and diming for everything.

Waited about an hour for breakfast, they seemed to be understaffed.

reviews.author: Clarayalejo
reviews.title: Luxury and Location
reviews.text:
Our stay was wonderful. The resort is upscale with nice amenities.The staff is always helpful and willing to help, especially the concierge team.We got worked in at the restaurant without reservations in 2 occasions.Needless to say, we wished they had at least one more family friendly restaurant in the resort.The have one of the most complete gyms you can ask for and plenty of tennis courts.The resort is very close to Old town Scottsdale and only 15 min from the airport.We did several outdoor activities which required some driving.Initially we tried to Uber everywhere but quickly decided to rent a car which is highy recommended if you want to explore beyond Scottsdale.For example, one activity required a 40 min drive to the location ( 100 dollar trip with uber one way ).
The resort has very nice golfing facilities including a driving range.Behind the resort and within walking distance is Camelback Mountain wich provides a great hike and beautiful views of the city.
Overall we had a great stay and consider renting a car if you plan for outdoor activities outside the resort such as horseback riding, atvs or hot air ballooning.

reviews.author: RThomas2015
reviews.title: Wonderful Experience
reviews.text: We needed to be in Phoenix for the Cheez-It Bowl, so I looked long and hard where to stay in Scottsdale/Phoenix. Ultimately, I ignored the mixed reviews and booked at the Phoenician and we are glad we did. The resort is majestic, the people are friendly and, overall, the service was excellent. Our rooms were a nice size, well appointed and clean; what we would expect for this price range. Registration was friendly and welcoming. The concierge staff, who we consulted daily, was receptive and helpful. We thoroughly enjoyed a magnificent sunset dinner at J&G Steakhouse. My family loves to dine and our standards are very high. The dinner exceeded our expectations in every way. The ambiance is superb, the service was attentive and the food was delicious. Appropriate live music was the cherry on top. This restaurant feels so much more than a hotel restaurant. The golf course was in tip top shape (and hostess on the beverage cart was charming and timely!), the Spa lived up to its billing, and the Athletic Center is the best we’ve seen at a hotel. Our only disappointment was at Mowry & Cotton, where we ate breakfast two mornings. The place is very nice, the breakfast buffet was more than ample and the food was good, but the service left much to be desired. Both times, we were greeted, escorted to our table and presented with a waiter/waitress who would attend to us. But, after the initial introduction, they were AWOL. We were pretty much on our own or had to get up and hunt down a wait staff for attention. The cost of breakfast was very high, and we’ve had better service at Denny’s. Fortunately, we stayed here on the American Express Platinum program, and the benefits include a daily credit of $80 for breakfast, so the pain of poor service was somewhat mitigated. Overall, however, our family was very pleased with our stay here. We recommend it highly to others and intend to return as often as we can.

reviews.author: Janae L
reviews.title: Another stay at the Phoenician - I LOVE this HOTEL.
reviews.text: For reasons which don't bear the long story, my husband and I are again staying at the Phoenician this weekend, a mere few miles from home.  We're having a GREAT staycation.  I LOVE this hotel.  The property is well-appointed.  Our room is terrific (inside and out - we have a great view looking down toward Old Town).  And the service is just outstanding.  Everyone just seems determined to make us 100% happy, including the Falconer, who bore my dumb questions this morning with great grace.   Dinner last night (at J&G steakhouse) was terrific.  Breakfast this morning (at Mowry and Cotton) was even better - great, inventive food and a wonderful waiter.  Sorry to sound like an ad, but they deserve every one of their 5 stars.

reviews.author: Anthropologie
reviews.title: Opulent Hotel in a Stunning Location
reviews.text:
The lovely setting at the base of Camelback Mtn and  numerous, beautiful pools and gardens are  what attracted us to this very plushly decorated large hotel.  Stayed here the week after Christmas and it was very crowded and busy in the lobby area.  

Upon arrival we were given a room on the 2nd Floor.  The room was fine with a large deck BUT the deck was walled in by a 12 foot wall---with a view of absolutely nothing but the wall.  

When we called and asked for a higher floor, the lady who answered immediately realized the problem (clearly this had happened before!).  She was apologetic and found us a very nice room on the 5th floor with a view of the fountain out front and the mountains.  Not sure why the Phoenician feels like they can try to get away with the kind of room they offered us at first. 

Gym and  pools were clean, well laid out and equipped  with great views.   We ate at Mowry and Cotton---excellent service and food. Breakfast and desserts at the Marketplace are very good and service is polite and quick. 

Overall the staff was polite and helpful although they did seem understaffed during the busy holiday season.

reviews.author: AnotherHoustonian
reviews.title: Mixed bag
reviews.text:
Grrr.....I was “upgraded” to a room in a casita.  Don’t fall for it.  This means you will get a room super far from everything.  Morning coffee will be a hike.  If you need ice, it will be a forty five minute wait because there are no ice machines and it’s room service only.  My “upgrade” irritated me every time I thought about it.  The tub is oversized but the showers in the “casitas” are shower boxes and if you a girl, good luck shaving your legs because of the water angle which is not adjustable.  I laughed because they give you a stool for the vanity which is normally awesome, but if you sit it in, because the vanity is so high you can’t actually see the mirror.  (I bet the non upgraded rooms didn’t have this problem....).  The stopper of the oversized tub was weirdly sitting in the middle of the floor on arrival, so using it didn’t seem advisable.

Anyway, even with the casita incident, there is still much to love about this property. The grounds are amazing.  The pools looked fabulous.  The workout room is incredible.  I’m absolutely positively not knocking the place.  We had a great time.  It’s a luxurious yet relaxed vibe.  I hope to return again and will decline the upgrade :)

reviews.author: Sarah R
reviews.title: Canyon Suites stay
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Canyon Suites section of the hotel. Hands down one of the best hotels I've stayed at (and we have stayed at multiple 5* resorts). The service was fantastic. Room was spacious (we had the one bedroom suite). We were traveling with our one year old child and were concerned about the hotel being family friendly; however, the hotel was very accommodating to children/babies. They provided us with a crib, high chair, and a stuffed animal. They also provided us fresh whole milk from the kitchen each day so we didn't have to run out and buy it ourselves. Sharon, who worked the breakfast, was amazing and made my child fruit animals every morning (she even made extra for her days off so he would still get one each day). 
Visited in December so did not have a chance to use the pool facilities due to weather but can imagine how nice it would be in warmer weather. Lots of Christmas decorations and activities at the hotel. The guided cactus tour was good. General area of hotel is nice. We rented a car since we wanted to do some sightseeing. Old town, fashion mall, and Starbucks are all close by. 
Overall fantastic hotel. Would definitely stay here again if I am back in Phoenix area.

reviews.author: HavePillowWillTravel
reviews.title: Gorgeous hotel
reviews.text: I didn't stayed at the Phoenician prior to their remodel so I can't compare pre/post but it is gorgeous. I understand it was a massive renovation. The lobby is beautiful and the bar offers excellent service and tasty drinks. The guest rooms are nicely appointed and very spacious. I love the views of the mountains. The pools are stunning and the spa is incredible. I loved my massage and felt so relaxed afterwards. I can't wait to return to the Phoenician.

reviews.author: temasteele
reviews.title: One of my absolute favorite places to stay in AZ!
reviews.text: This hotel is amazing. They have so many pools to swim in and the place is just gorgeous. The service is amazing from everyone that works there. The breakfast we had was really good and healthy. The lobby is beautiful and we loved the cactus garden- it is a must see!

reviews.author: RecruiterMom11
reviews.title: Really nice!
reviews.text: My adult son and I stayed here for hiking and training for an upcoming marathon, we were upgraded to a huge room with a huge walk out balcony for a party of 10. Very nice hotel. Very spread out and it took us a couple of hours to walk around but def a classy resort, tried the Athletic Club, pool and Blow dry bar. Only negative is the folio. They charged 200.00 more for one of the nights including a room charge tax for the incorrect nightly rate. I’ve called to send my confirmation showing the correct rate but no calls back and charge is on my Amex. Hope they address this shortly, so check your folio before you leave the property.

reviews.author: blanquita79
reviews.title: Great Hotel!!!
reviews.text: We were here for a conference and I have to say that this is probably my favorite hotel yet in the Phoenix and Scottsdale area!  The rooms were like new with really nice decor and amenities.  The beds comfy.  There is a restaurant that opens up to the outdoor area that was superb.  We actually had the pleasure of seeing a storm roll in while we were there in August.

reviews.author: HeathersS
reviews.title: Huge disappointment! Hidden fees!
reviews.text:
Overly priced for what you get.
($350/nite) plus ($40/day resort free) plus ($35/day valet or $18 day self park) They don’t tell you this info when you book! 
Extra fee if you want to use the spa facilities, for the day($40) unless you book a treatment ($200+) 
Front desk and valet were robots. No one took the time to meet and greet me  I am a number at the Phoenician that’s it! J&Gs was booked by the “public” ? At a resort I expect there be a seat for me at the onsite restaurant. Instead I hear that they have been advertising for weeks now about there ($10 steaks) My bill came to ?($200+) Too much catering to the public. I don’t stay at a resort too pay top dollar to compete with the public. A resort should be exactly what it is A RESORT. This is not a resort!
Our room was okay kinda reminded me of a nice Holiday Inn.... our Tv on the wall was hung crooked... huge burn mark on bench at bottom of bed? Contemporary furniture. Bathroom shower was a drip. The Tub was ridiculous...on the floor.. ?come on... Dated! Millions in renovations.. where.. not our tub..
I picked this hotel because it was a 5 star diamond resort. Forbes gave it 5. My only thought is that they have become money hungry with there new renovations and frankly don’t give a ($&@ about there Resort guests. 
Tea time anyone? A new perk at the Phoenician ($75) Be prepared to see rich youth (12yrs) not resort guests... drives me nuts. What the point of staying at the Phoenician? They cater more to them then you..
No turndown service-? I had to call the front desk then wait on hold to get a human being to request turn down. It’s suppose to be included. Drives me mad! I feel like I’m reminding them to do there job! Same with Mowry and Cotton went there for a Birthday dinner they forgot to add a candle to the cake. I had to totally embarrass the entire table and tell them to put the candle in the cake . When I booked the reservation I had them make a note of this. Oh well they forgot!(shakes head) sheesh!
We had some cocktails at the Thirsty Camel before our dinner and found Alex to be one of the brightest ,nicest, professional staff members in the entire resort 
We will not be returning. Too much catering to the public not enough for the ppl paying ($350) a nite at your resort

reviews.author: EliteTravellers
reviews.title: There is a new Number One Resort  in the area . You rock GM Vinciguerra
reviews.text:
This is my sixth visit in the Scottsdale area, all staying at resorts and hands down this property (incredibly a Starwood/Marriott property) beats all hands down!

It’s an easy drive from the airport and as you drive in, greats security. Aa a Lifetime Platinum I had requested, at short notice, a particular room and I was really pleasantly surprised not only to hear back from Executive Assistant LEANNE BIRD-BOUEY but the GM himself...always the mark of an exceptional Leader when a GM takes the time to write back.

I received a great upgrade in the Canyon Suites and a special welcome. It’s a short walk to the main building  and the gym (which is spectacular). These suites have their own pool as well as staff on hand to check you in or out. If you don't want to walk back and forth, then there is always someone to drive you over.

The Suites have morning breakfast (which I did not know was complementary) and evening a la carte snacks. 

In the main Hotel, there is a Happy Hour with great appetizers passed around.  Very attentive and friendly service.

The grounds are spectacular and well maintained. I don't golf but my colleagues told me the greens were in immaculate condition.

I hope you are there for leisure but if not, the Conference facilities are awesome, well laid out with spacious rooms, exits to sunlight and washroom facilities all over. Lots of staff to guide you.

There are a nuber of nice boutiques that aren't outrageous and have very nice merchandise.

Its also a short ride to town and to restaurants and more shopping.

I was not aware that Marriott had properties of this high caliber in the USA and it was a delightful stay.

GM Vinciguerra and his staff should be commended for the high standard of service provided throughout the hotel, from check-in, to Housekeeping.

PS Even though service charges are included, I provided gratuities over and above for great service.

reviews.author: Chris_Schmo
reviews.title: Terrible service and not acceptable communication
reviews.text: It never happened to me in 9 years Business Travel, that a booked and confirmed (with confirmation number) room was not available for me. Even worse the amount for the total stay was already blocked on my credit card and was blocked for 4 more weeks. I will never ever consider to go back and recommend to stay in another hotel. We were simply send away and had to find spontaneous a hotel by ourself. Terrible! And the reception management was not helpful at all...

reviews.author: rollinon-9
reviews.title: Wedding event -  Great stay
reviews.text:
Great stay at this resort. We didn’t get to take advantage of the all of amenities since it was a short stay for a wedding. I did play golf and utilize the spa. Both were solid. The golf course is new and recently got seeded so it was cart path only, but the course is in good shape with pretty views. 

The spa is phenomenal. We’ll come back here with family and stAy a while.

reviews.author: Rob R
reviews.title: Wedding Anniversary
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed at the Phoenician hotel for our wedding anniversary. The shower water pressure was not worth taking a shower there. Very noisy outside of the room. They charge you $18.00 to park your car there, and then on top of that a $35.00 resort fee for sleeping over night. I am very dissapointed, in the fact that the room cost should have covered all of that. Then all of a sudden extra fees included on the bill? That is way out of bounds. I can assure you that we will not ever return there again. It is way over priced and not worth it. There are thousands of hotels in the area not even as close to $300.00 per night and you do not have to pay to park there. Such a real dissapointment.

reviews.author: vkcgordon
reviews.title: Holiday High Tea was delightful
reviews.text:
A friend and I enjoyed a lovely afternoon high tea that was truly festive.  We started with sparkling wine, then ordered our speciality teas.  I ordered the Sweet Berry tea, and I loved it.  Can’t remember the flavor of my friend’s tea, but she loves her’s as well.

We started with the traditional finger sandwiches, and they were all very tasty.  My favorite was the fresh asparagus spears and ham - so yummy.  The sandwiches included salmom, chicken salad, cucumber, and others.

Second course was a berry scone and a buttermilk scone.. both were good, but I preferred the berry scone.  There was ample clotted cream, lemon curd, and fruit jam for the two of us to indulge freely.

The final course was the sweets course.  Several of the sweets were decorated with Christmas trimmings, and they were all good.   Shorthread, chocolate dipped strawberry, apple cinnamon tart, and a mixed berry tart with custard were all delicious.  I couldn’t finish my sweets course because there was just a lot of food.

reviews.author: JoseNunezFamily
reviews.title: Excelente Hotel, con todo y para todos
reviews.text:
Diseño exquisito, múltiples áreas sociales, habitaciones de primera, excelentes dos restaurantes y lo que mas me gusta el Gimnasio es de lo mejor.
Las canchas de tenis y golf también son un lujo. La cercania con la montaña Camelback otro diferencial.

reviews.author: P L
reviews.title: Lost track of the wows
reviews.text: From the moment we drove up the expansive, winding path to the hotel, we were wowed. The Phoenician is truly a wow experience, from the warm professional service to the impeccable modern rooms to the perfectly executed food. The desert views may be worth the price of admission alone - grab a drink from the Thirsty Camel as the sun sets and enjoy the stunning vista. We also has a delightful brunch at Mowry & Cotton, definitely try a fro-mosa (sorbet + sparkling wine) along with crispy potato appetizer. You could spend a week here what with all the available amenities. We want to commend the Front Office Manager Daniel whose hospitality really shined through.

reviews.author: karen r
reviews.title: Girls weekend gone “meh”
reviews.text:
The service at the Phoenician often starts with “no”, when instead it should start with “yes, and...”

Spa weekend where all hot tubs were set to tepid and two days of asking them to turn up the heat resulted in nothing and no follow up from the staff even when we requested answers from a manager.

Very overpriced for the bland conventioneer atmosphere and only the housekeeping reminded you this was a “fancy” hotel. I will for sure look elsewhere on return visits.

reviews.author: kent r
reviews.title: beautiful property, great restaurant, room service lacking
reviews.text: We just returned from a 3 day conference at this beautiful property. The conference was run superbly and was a very nice space. Our room 5058 was spacious,well appointed with comfotable bed and beautiful bathroom. The hotel restaurants were superb and although pricey, they did not disappoint. Unfortunately the hall outside room 5058 is tile and it was like sleeping in an airport, the click/clack of rolling luggage all night. Also for a highly rated property we did not receive room cleaning for 2 of the 3 days we stayed. The turn down service person cleaned the room the last night. We were shocked by this since we were out of the room 90% of the day. Overall its a great place for a conference with beautiful grounds and restaurants. Not 5 stars due to noise and service isssues.

reviews.author: Mike G
reviews.title: Perfect and Personalized Post Wedding Stay
reviews.text:
We checked into the Phoenician coming off of our Mini Moon at the Edition in Miami. We were in the area for Thanksgiving as a lot of me and my husband's family live in the area.

Several weeks before our arrival date, their Personalization Coordinator, Taylor, reached out to ensure I was going to get the best out of my stay. This act alone is above and beyond what I expect from a hotel and was truly impressed to have this level of personal touch. I assume this is due to my Marriott status.

When Taylor learned that we would recently be married, this is all she needed to go above and beyond for us. She was able to work with Julian the Operations Manager of the Canyon Suites, the more exclusive part of the resort to have us in a room there. Upon arrival, Taylor personally greeted us and showed us to our room where we received a welcome letter from Julian, champagne, a personalized cake and a framed photo from our wedding. it was absolutely perfect! 

Almost any staff we interacted with knew we were celebrating our wedding. Even the lady at the security tower knew who we were, and when my parents drove to the resort for dinner, congratulated them on my wedding! 

The Spa is pure heaven and Gennaro on the pool deck was the most kind and attentive pool service I have every experienced. 

Speaking of pools - the main pool area (3 large pools) also had incredible service throughout. The only disappointment was how understaffed the private pool area at Canyon Suites was. We had to set up our own chairs and wait an extraordinary amount of time for the server to come to us.

Otherwise we experienced personalization and anticipatory service at its finest. I was blown away. I have stayed at many luxury properties in the Marriott and SPG brands and I have NEVER seen a hotel reach a level of personalization.  We were truly impressed and truly touched. After coming off a less than stellar experience at the Miami Beach Edition, this was a welcome change of attitude and customer experience.

reviews.author: Joanne M
reviews.title: A nice getaway
reviews.text:
We were anxious to return to this hotel as they just underwent a huge renovation. It is a lovely hotel, with very friendly staff. There is a lot to do....beautiful pools, several restaurants, nice golf course, hiking close by. The grounds are lovely 
However when we arrived at 4pm we were told that our room had been given away by mistake.  We waited a very long time for them to find us another and I was disappointed. Room 2140 is large, very clean with a big balcony but there is NO view so why sit on the balcony?

reviews.author: andrewsY2166PE
reviews.title: Thank you Phoenician, amazing service!
reviews.text:
We had an amazing time at the Phoenician on a recent couples trip. Rebecca was an incredible server in the thirsty camel who made our weekend very special and memorable by sending a congratulatory note for us expecting our first child. Thank you!

The entire staff was always catering to the guests and the grounds were immaculate.
I have never stayed at a hotel that had a gym as big, new and clean as the one at the hotel!

We will be back tot be hotel, thank you Again for an awesome weekend.

reviews.author: Victoria Z
reviews.title: Royal Treatment
reviews.text:
Absolutely superior stay at this desert Oasis nestles in the shadow of Camelback Mountain.  From our first warm greeting at reception to our final, personal goodbye, we felt like royalty.  It was our 30th wedding anniversary and every person we met greeted us by name and wished us Happy Anniversary. There was champagne and a card in our room; we were treated to free dessert and more champagne at Mowry and Cotton restaurant, and a card and more delights at J&G Steakhouse.  Inventive food at both restaurants, top-notch service and ambiance.
The Spa is unrivaled in its offerings and its serenity. It has a private rooftop pool and lunch service.  The pools overall are massive - yet offer private cabanas and little meandering paths and cozy corners. The loungers are comfortable and there are plenty of umbrellas for shade. (There are handicapped lifts at every pool which is a courteous, embracing gesture.)  The tennis center is new and crisp and has a stadium court. We didn't golf, but the links were green and glorious.
The lobby bar - both in and out - has a view of the resort and beyond, with creative cocktails and excellent service. The general feel and flow is desert chic, yet relaxed everywhere you go.  
AND THE GUESTROOMS!!! Our room was huge, with a deck so large that we had an outdoor sitting area, a dining area AND two lounge chairs. We could have had a party of 75 people - all with a sunrise view.  The marble bathrooms are loaded with thick, fluffy high-quality towels and beautiful smelling amenities. Separate shower, bathtub and personal commode. Clean, clean, clean and I am fussy.
Concierge services included mailing postcards at no charge. I don't know why, but this simple offering made a difference to me. Sure, we were paying 5star prices, but most places charge you, and The Phoenician doesn't nickel and dime you there. Very nice.
Service was the best we have had nearly anywhere. Wonderful people and a well-run resort on every level. HIGHLY recommend. People of note: Ryan Sudden, Daniel Uhlry, in the front of the house. Rebecca at the bar and TWO Davids in the restaurants. Cher, Amanda and Jennifer in the Spa. Ivan in Tennis. All of you made a difference to us in person. Michelle in chef service and Patrick at J&G sent us cards.
THANK YOU ONE AND ALL!!!!!!   We are in LOVE.

reviews.author: Pat L
reviews.title: Housekeeping...above and beyond
reviews.text: We are here again at this fabulous hotel.  It is always so welcoming and we always have a great experience.  We arrived very late on Thursday night so slept in a little Friday morning.  When we left for a late breakfast the housekeeping staff was in the hall way.  Being from NH, my husband had on a New England Patriots shirt. We chatted for a minute and went on our way.  When we returned to our room it was immaculate so that didn't surprise us.  But what did, was a nice hand written note from Gloria and Candy saying "Mr & Mrs L...., We hope the Patriots get plenty of rest on their bye week.  Best of luck this season and on the 25th of November against the Jets!"  Who does this kind of thing?  Obviously, housekeeping at the Phoenician.   How nice to take the time to wish our team well.

reviews.author: Andrew D
reviews.title: Amazing location.  Very reasonable prices.
reviews.text: We dined at the J and G Steakhouse as Jean George’s is a favourite chef of ours.  The meal was fantastic, we even opted for the Kobe beef special to share.  For 4 people it came in around 500$.  We thought this was very fair.  The highlight of our night however was Rebekah (Rebecca with a K) a warm, friendly and truly genuine girl who served us drinks in the lobby bar - The Thirsty Camel.  She turned the fire on for us, brought us blankets, was enthusiastic about bringing us drinks and ensuring we enjoyed them.  As a restuarant owner - I know what to look for - and this girl has it.  Keep an eye on her - she’s going places!

reviews.author: Jahniece
reviews.title: Not what I expected
reviews.text:
This hotel gets great ratings and I was underwhelmed. Yes the room was large and I had a balcony, however the service could have been more memorable. The vents in my bathroom were dusty. 
The cactus garden den was enjoyable. Fortunately I did not run into any snales

reviews.author: rleary13
reviews.title: Service could really use some work....
reviews.text:
First, The Phoenician is a beautiful property.  High end.  Good food.  Amazing views against Camelback Mtn.  I gave the resort 2 stars because of the aforementioned.  Now on to that negative.....

I was extremely disappointed in the food service at 2 out of 3 meals at the property.  Pool service — we had to beg to get service to begin with.  After waiting 20+ minutes to order a drink, it took another 20+ minutes to get that drink.  The waiter was a complete “dumb dumb.”  The food we ordered was fantastic but again the wait time was unbelievable.  And to get our check?  I’ll let you guess on that one?!?!  Breakfast the following morning was even worse.  Like the pool, we had to beg to get water and coffee.  Our “server” was a ghost and the food was not good — runny eggs out of a big vat.  The worst part was certainly the “server.”  He was basically non-existent.  We had to ask numerous other employees for coffee, water, et al.  It was a joke.

For such a nice and luxurious property, the Phoenician really needs to work on their service.  People spend way too much money to be treated 2nd class.

reviews.author: Danielle L
reviews.title: Just ok
reviews.text: My daughter lives in the area. My husband and I traveled to Scottsdale for a visit. I have stayed at the Phoenician before however I stayed at The canyons suites. Extreme differences between the two parts of the resort. We had a great room here, overlooking the cactus garden.  The resort was very busy however the service was still very good. The breakfast was SO expensive..there was no reason a simple  breakfast for two cost $100 with tip. The coffee shop was out of food very quickly.  The pool situation was AWFUL.  There was no place to sit by 10 am.  They were a lot of people that had guests meeting them at the pool not guest of the resort. Eight chairs next to us were reserved for friendsfriends of a bride that weren’t staying at the resort but they have the chairs at 8 o’clock in the morning and didn’t show up till about noon. The only available seating cost money. There was no availability to the spa or hair salon.  The parking garage wasn’t working with their key pass and we had to have that fixed three times, not a big deal except each wait was about 20 minutes. They charged us for items out of the refrigerator which we never used as we brought our own. We took the stuff out of the fridge and put it on the counter and let the hotel know we were doing so, yet they charged us for the items anyways. They did credit us but again after we had to dispute that. Very loud in lobbies, pool and grounds....would not stay here again. The bed was very comfortable.

reviews.author: Highlandlass38
reviews.title: Relaxing in luxury
reviews.text:
We landed at the airport and were picked up by a driver and taken to the Phoenician where we were accommodated in the Elite Floor.  So comfortable.  The next day we went to the newly renovated and ultra-luxurious spa for a wonderfully refreshing massage!  We had breakfast at Mowry and Cotton, tea one afternoon in the Camel Room and dinner in the J and G Steak House.  All top notch!!!
One thing of interest ... at breakfast outside, birds that were around were kept at bay by a hawk and its handler!  One of the nights there I used my SPG points which made the trip even more of a pleasure! 
Service and food were outstanding.  Well done Marriott for making the transition so beautifully.

reviews.author: ericadpr
reviews.title: One of the best. Excelente!!
reviews.text: One of the best hotels I have been. Quarto espaçoso, limpo, excelente atendimento (serviço) na piscina e lobby, 3 piscinas e ótima área para crianças, varias opções de restaurantes e próximo (5 min de carro) da “Old Town”

reviews.author: davidfromop
reviews.title: World class experience, even after a rough start
reviews.text:
We checked in to our Casista's one-bedroom suite which turned out to be a disaster (all of the Casistas feel like an afterthought).  We moved into 2 adjoining rooms in the main building and never looked back.

The outdoors facilities are immaculate.  The pools cascade across three levels with adjacent hot tubs and children's play areas (adults will enjoy the water slide too).  The tennis courts feel like you are on tour with the pros.  Try to get some time on court 1!

The staff was extremely warm and helpful across the entire property.  We concluded most nights in the main bar area to live music.  In spite of the rough start, we rated this 5-stars and will be back.

BONUS TIP:  The resort has a separate Gluten Free kitchen that the restaurants share to avoid cross contamination.  We've never seen a better solution in a resort.

reviews.author: Ann M
reviews.title: Modern and luxury, just not my taste
reviews.text:
Attended a conference here and while there was nothing wrong with the experience, couldn't say much about except that it was high end.  Very large rooms & nice location up against Camelback mountain.  The conference facilities were convenient.  

The decor was very modern and angular, but I didn't find it attractive (personal taste).  Beds were comfortable and they did turn downs with a bit of chocolate, can't beat that.  

I enjoyed the cactus garden  -- it was a nice walk and I learned to recognize some of the plants there.  And the newly renovated spa was beautiful will review separately.

reviews.author: Coconut62
reviews.title: Luxurious!
reviews.text: We would definitely return. Great service. Helpful and attentive staff throughout. Rooms are spacious. I would say my only small beef would be to check the beds and make sure they are all highly comfortable. Ours was somewhat soft but not enough to ruin our experience. Quiet grounds. Nice pools. Awesome gym.

reviews.author: Fernando F
reviews.title: Amplio y muy confirtable
reviews.text: Estuve aquí para una reunión de Google.  The Phoenician es un Resort de convenciones muy bien ubicado junto a Camelback.  Amplios cuartos con terraza, algunos restaurantes un muy buen gimnasio y un campo de Golf.  Lo único que mejoraría es la amabilidad y agilidad en el Frant Desk.

reviews.author: Chip144
reviews.title: Complete resort, great setting.
reviews.text:
Let me say it is more like 4.5 out of 5 but that is not an option in Tripadvisor.  I was here for a business conference and all lodging and meals were prearranged.  I had t initially change rooms because the room I was assigned first was on the 2nd floor of the east wing and the balcony faced a cement wall about 6 feet away.  I was fortunately moved to 4th floor room facing north. The rooms are quite large and recently remodeled.  Bed is very comfortable.  The bathroom is big with a large tub and a separate shower.  The only two criticisms of the room were: the towels, though very nice and large, could have been more soft, and the shower is a smallish stall shower and should be bigger.  All the conference meals, served buffet style, were all very good and was a good indication that the other restaurants should be good. 
The facility has a kids pool and play area, 3 swimming pools, one of which is adult only, tennis, golf, gym, and other activities to choose from.  If you get a chance take a few minutes and explore the cactus garden near the back of the hotel.

reviews.author: EyeDrMom
reviews.title: Top Shelf Luxury Resort
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here for a business conference and can’t wait to schedule a return visit for leisure. We were blown away by the service, amenities, food, and rooms. We had many opportunities to interact with various resort staff and had professional, courteous experiences with every single individual the entire weekend. There are so many different unique activities on site for both adults & kids, it would make a great family destination. Food & wine choices and quality were beyond exceptional.  We truly felt like royalty!  HIGHLY RECOMMEND if traveling around the Phoenix/Scottsdale Arizona region. You won’t be disappointed!

reviews.author: suetmon
reviews.title: Average - not worth what you are paying
reviews.text:
I’ve stayed at a bunch of nice resorts and hotels and so in going to based my rating in comparison to other 5 star hotels. With that said, simply the service, hospitality, and price to value ratio is just not here. You’re much better off at some of the other Scottsdale resorts where it feels like they know your name, really care, and want to deliver on the cost that you are paying. 

The pool was crowded and they don’t setup towels for you, don’t provide sunscreen, and just didn’t feel like they were cleaning at a good pace. However it was large, there is a cool water slide, and adult pool. The bar at night was probably some of the worst service I’ve ever experienced. The room is super nice - no issues. Breakfast was good. Dinner was good but nothing special. Cactus garden was cool. Grounds didn’t feel super well maintained. Self parking is a nightmare given how close the spots are in the garage and requires two different elevators to get to your room.

reviews.author: mojoFCH2020
reviews.title: Back to 5 Stars
reviews.text: I last stayed here several years ago prior to the extensive renovation. This renovation has clearly restored this luxurious resort hotel to its days of glory. Huge rooms, attentive service, fabulous 24/7 gym, sophisticated cuisine all contribute to the positive impression. As I was there as part of a sell-out business event the price was remarkably affordable for this level of hospitality. Two little nits that need to be addressed to sustain the high rating: bottled water in the spectacular gym, some discoloring of the grout in the shower is starting to appear.

reviews.author: Ceguttilla
reviews.title: Excelente conjunto da obra
reviews.text: Embora grande (resort), mantem qualidade de serviços impecáveis. Quartos super espaçosos. Fiquei em um Grand Deluxe Room, que conta com o benefício de uma varanda bem ampla. Excelente academia, restaurante, bar animado, piscinas, etc. Nota 10 para o atendimento.

reviews.author: Sharibd
reviews.title: Wonderful hotel and 1st class service
reviews.text: We stayed for 2 nights at the Phoenician after 5 days at a horse ranch in Tuscon. This was a perfect ending to our trip. We are SPG Gold members and were treated like royalty. We have traveled all over the world and this was one of the best service experiences. Every person working at this hotel is professional and operates at a high service level which you do not typically find. The hotel is beautiful and the spa is one of the nicest I have been in. I had a massage which was 1st class all the way and you have access to the entire spa for the day, including steam room, hot pool, rooftop pool etc. There are many pools and plenty of seating and again the service at the pool was wonderful. The only negative was we were given a mountain view room which was over the loading dock so hard to sit outside withouth hearing the trucks beeping and backing up and noise from the staff unloading the trucks. Other than that, would highly recommend and will definitely return.

reviews.author: Camellia167
reviews.title: Great Hotel with kids
reviews.text:
We stayed at this hotel at the end of August.  It was hot (100 and over) but when in the pool you don't feel the heat. At nights it's perfect to eat outside. The restaurant has mist blowers at the restaurant so that really helps. My only criticism is that there was only one restaurant to eat breakfast, lunch and dinner (called Mowry & Cotton).  The cafe by the pool closes at 5 pm right when you are ready for a nice drink by the pool. Lowry & Cotton food is good but a bit too experimental for our taste to eat there 5 days (breakfast, lunch and dinner.  Pool cafe is good for lunch. J&G steakhouse was closed for renovation however we couldn't eat there all the time since it's fine dining. Not appropriate with young kids and also can get pricey. The burger restaurant was closed by the golf club which you would walk to. Thirsty Camel Bar is in the lobby and the terrace and beautiful. But it is not a restaurant.  It's a lounge, you can't have breakfast, lunch and dinner with kids. The hotel needs another restaurant or need to expand Mowry& Cotton meal options. Very limited food options for a hotel this size and quality and remote location. You can go to the city but need a car.Can't just walk out and find other dining options.
Great place for kids. Kids club,water play area, movie night at the pool and golf cart safari.
Hotel staff were amazing. Super helpful and super nice!

reviews.author: marc7704
reviews.title: Großartige Anlage!
reviews.text: Sehr schönes, gut gepflegtes Hotel mit Golfplatz, Tennisplätzen, großem Fitness-Komplex und schöner Poolanlage. Die Zimmer sind groß und geschmackvoll eingerichtet. Eine der besten Adressen in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: KennJP
reviews.title: Luxury and Service beyond compare!
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is truly an amazing property!  The canyon suites are nestled right up against Camel Back mountain and are surrounded by the manicured grounds and the natural beauty of the Arizona landscape.  
The lobby, lounge and bar are bright and inviting with a fountain and wall of windows looking out onto Camel Back mountain. 
The rooms are large, comfortable and fashionably decorated. Nice bathroom with tiled shower, separate large tub and television. Also an Additional half bath. The rooms Very peaceful and the beds so comfortable including the roll out couch.
The gym is very large and newly built and filled with the newest equipment available.  there are several pools on the grounds.  Pools have food and beverage service and the staff is making sure your water pitcher is always fresh and full of ice. There is a kids pool and a separate adults only pool
for a more relaxing time.
Above all the service was fantastic!  The entire staff from the reception, concierge, room service, pool staff and management was above and beyond any in my previous experience.  We needed to use the sofa couch for our stay and when we called for sheets, within minutes a gentleman arrived with sheets, blankets and pillows and made up the bed for us.  The room service was remarkable. Such attention to detail. They even rolled up my cell phone cord and had a special little clip to hold the cord together.
There is a Morning complementary breakfast that is not to be missed.  A delicious array of fruit, salmon, nuts and cheese, cereal and pastries as well as an espresso machine and a specialty breakfast dish. 
So much more to this experience that I could go on and on writing. I cannot say enough to express how wonderful our stay was at the Phoenician Resort.
Thank you!

reviews.author: Caitlin M
reviews.title: Platinum Premier Elite Approved
reviews.text:
My husband and I travel 48/52 weeks a year and are thus The Hotel Snobs of Snobs.

I am in town for business, and my family came to enjoy a long weekend with me. We reserved 2 rooms and were upgraded to the Elite Floor with views overlooking the pools and mountains (it was beautiful!)

The service at this hotel is IMPECCABLE. Need Ice? Call downstairs and within minutes a cold bucket will be delivered. Want your shoes shined? Leave them outside the door in the provided bag, and receive them back the next day. Thirsty? Water will be placed in your car after the valet brings it to the front for you. 

There were so many more small details that go farther than a occasional vacationer could appreciate, so THANK YOU to the staff at this property for getting it right!

In addition to the fabulous service, the rooms are beautifully decorated and very comfortable. The pool furniture is in great shape and there is plenty of seating for everyone, along with plenty of pool options for everyone. 

The spa is gorgeous, and the service is equally as impeccable. 

I am honestly not sure where any negative, justified, reviews come from about this property because I assure you that I and my husband are probably known as “those people” to hotel staff and I promise you, this place is knows what they’re doing and not one detail was missed during our stay.

I will be back in a couple of weeks, and plan to continue my business travel to Scottsdale specifically to stay at this property.

Thank you again Phoenician Staff, and SPG for getting it right! 

(Bonus points for catering to women business travelers too, by adding Bravo to your cable line up!)

reviews.author: MelandGary823
reviews.title: Top Notch Service
reviews.text:
We stayed here for a combination of business and personal for 4 nights. The resort is quite large and in excellent condition. Even though there were a number of conferences underway, it was quiet for sleeping. 

They rise to the commitment of superior service. EVERYONE was friendly and acknowledge each guest. We requested a complimentary upgrade and received the King Deluxe room. There are a few enhancements from the regular King room:  a love seat vs a chair, a larger table, higher end water to purchase, and a couple of additional bath amenities. Otherwise, the rooms are the same so if deciding to pay for the upgrade, perhaps save your money. We had both rooms during our stay and enjoyed the privacy of the regular King that looked out into Camelback Mountain vs the driveway. 

The rooms are large and well appointed with very comfortable beds. The balconies have tables and chairs. 

Room service was great, offering help with anything else we needed. Everyone was so very helpful. 

There are a number of food options and a few shops, though they are quite expensive. The best good value is the gelato - double scoop for $5 at the cafe, yum. They have grab and go food items as well. 

The food at the conference was excellent as was the table service. There was no waiting - they were VERY efficient. At the end of the conference there was a buffet lunch before travelling and they offered take-away boxes if you could t stay - awesome. 

There is a Happy Hour each day at The Thirsty Camel with $5 beers and $2 off local wine. 

The pools are lovely and there are adult-only sections. The loungers are high quality and there are lots of umbrellas. 

We enjoyed a stroll through the Cactus Garden, but passed on the lawn bowling due to the heat. There is an air conditioned games room for teens or young at heart. 

Overall, this resort was fabulous and does live up to being part of “a luxury collection” especially because of the service.  So pleased to have had the opportunity to stay here.

reviews.author: MooshLA
reviews.title: Sprawling resort set against Camelback Mtn
reviews.text:
Had a nice stay overall at this property in Phoenix. First the goods...

The grounds seem to be well maintained as crews were out and about all day long and it shows. The gym is brand new and well equipped with the proper amount of workout equipment and machines. Finally! The staff seem to want to ensure a comfortable stay. The rooms are really large and complete with large terraces. Bathroom had a large soaking tub. Loves that they had Netflix available in the rooms as I don’t watch movie channels. They provided some nice amenities including a chapstick. Although the resort may seem sprawling, there are actually multiple pathways (utilizing stairs) that can route you around quickly. The multiple pools are gorgeous and inviting and the immediate access to be able to hike Camelback is super cool. The trailhead is literally right there at the resort. 

The not so goods include the following... 
I kinda wish the tub had bath salts to take advantage of a luxurious experience. I had a handicap accessible room so the bathroom lacked any hooks for anything which was so odd. The shower was kind of gross and uninviting. The resort overall - especially the guest room had some strange smells. Almost as if someone had previously partied hard or smoked there or something. Hard to describe but I would get whiffs if it throughout the property. The room was quite noisy from housekeeping or others accessing keypad doorways that you can hear well until 2A whenever they needed to enter those closets or doorways - the sounds would travel the hallways. Then by 5A the birds starting very loudly singling and chirping and making a fuss which echoed throughout. The beds were super low and seemed old and worn in. Lastly the front desk staff seemed to be fairly new or leaned on the inexperienced side as it took forever to check people in. 

The property is located in a prime area that requires a drive to downtown or Old Town however it’s close. The airport was pretty close as well ~18 min away. Plenty of gold and tennis available for those that want. Enjoy!

reviews.author: JSMD19
reviews.title: Stunning property
reviews.text: This hotel has it all!  Family friendly, restaurants on site, modern and clean, and so much more!  The athletic club is awesome, has a game room for kids!  The spa is beautiful and the pools are amazing!  Our room was I think a casita, it was very spacious!  A great place to stay would highly recommend it!

reviews.author: MrEcosse
reviews.title: Nothing like as good as it thinks it is - and we had problems too.
reviews.text:
We had serious problems with our stay here, but my rating is based on how I would have felt regardless of these issues which I will describe later.

We stayed in one of the Grand Casitas on the property.  These are supposedly luxury 'oversized' rooms.  We didn't think they were anything special.  There was nothing of wow value about the room at all.  Given how the hotel promotes itself I really was expecting something more.  I think the refurbishment must have been lead by an accountant, not a hospitality specialist.  In particular, the cracked tiles on the steps leading up to the Casita that had been poorly repaired suggested a hotel of much lower quality.

The Casitas are a bit odd.  Yes, you can park outside but by doing so you never enter the hotel via the main lobby.  In a way this makes them feel like a cheap motel rather than the luxury end of their offerings.  Of course, you can choose to stay in one of the main rooms.  On a practical note for those with limited mobility, the Casitas are some distance and many steps from the main hotel.

Then there were the issues with construction.  On our second morning, we were woken at 8 am to say we had to move our car from outside the Casita as they were starting construction work.  Shortly after concrete cutters and jackhammers started.  This was totally unacceptable.  When we complained the front desk told us that they did not know about this work.  There must be some serious management issues if the Rooms Manager does not know about construction on their own site!

We were moved further away from the work but the next morning it was still too loud to sit out on our terrace.  We complained again and after a shaky start, we were offered to move to the Canyon Suites (which is effectively a different hotel).

Without the resolution, I would have rated the property 1 Star (Awful).  That aside there is obviously a management communication problem here.  Complaints are not unusual it would seem.  If you look at the reviews you will see pretty much anything negative receives a 'cut and paste' reply from the management about hopefully giving them a second chance.

reviews.author: MamaKLB
reviews.title: Met expectations
reviews.text: We spent a long weekend at Phoenician for a girls getaway. The accommodations were nice. The rooms were a good size and clean with nice bathrooms. The grounds and dining options were top notch. We enjoyed the pool and spent two days at the spa. The spa was renovated this year and they did a fantastic job with amenities and decor. The spa menu is very expensive when comparing to other spas in the area or high end spas I’ve visited elsewhere. That being said, we spa hopped and of the four we visited The Phoenician was by far the best in aesthetics and quality.

reviews.author: Bob M
reviews.title: Great facility
reviews.text: Went for a corporate conference and the room was excellent. The personnel were extremely nice and the hotel did an outstanding job with the conference, from the breakfast spread to the break items and the different dinners we had. Fitness Center was excellent also. Didn't have time for much else, so I did not experience the restaurants on my own.

reviews.author: Alexgran63
reviews.title: EXcellent refurbished to a high standard
reviews.text: Difficult to find any fault and when we did it was only minor and the management couldn.t have been more helpful. Staff are well drilled and unobtrusive. Constant EDM music in the pool area, though to be fair there are 3 pools to choose from makes it more of a party vibe but that's a small criticism. Can understand why they charge for cabanas/poolside seating at weekends but during a sluggish weekday not so sure its a sensible policy for hotel guests. The fitness suite is fab and the new spa is simply breathtakingly luxurious and the $50 day charge fine in my view. Only 2 restaurants at present; Mowry is very nice and relaxed. J&G just opened but food was super and wine list top drawer. For a family holiday it was first rate though they do host a lot of conferences so the bar can get v busy in the evenings...if it was just me and the wife I would probably opt for the desert quiet of the Four Seasons but its a close call.

reviews.author: Abe
reviews.title: Great service and room
reviews.text:
I had a small conference at the Phoenician. It was a great experience. The staff was very friendly and helpful - from registration to housekeeping to the bartender - I was ver well taken care of.

The room was great. Roomy with a sitting area and a place to work. There was a separate tub and shower in a large bathroom.

And the food presneted for the meeting was excellent and plentiful. 

All in a gorgeous setting.

reviews.author: Murray L
reviews.title: Relaxing holiday in lovely surroundings but v hot
reviews.text:
We were recommended to The P by many parties for a relaxing holiday and golf

We got good advice

We have just returned from a 2 week stay and really enjoyed our time. 

Having done my research I plumped for an upgrade to a deluxe room with city view and it was the right choice! Room 3006 on the ground floor was perfectly located and had fab views of the pools and grounds too. Worth the extra 

We were probably a little early in the season as overall the hotel was pretty empty during the week, save lots of conventions but you never felt they imposed on the hotel. There are huge double lower floors which accommodate this “out of the way “

Also the weather hit 109dgs during quite a few days and boy is that hot 🔥🌞🌞🌞
Perhaps we came a bit early in the season!

The staff are charming. A great touch is the way they remember your name and they always greet you with a smile. Special thanks to Jordan on reception who had dealt with my constant emails pressing for the right room and her colleague Erik who sorted out a few issues with room cleaning times but that’s picky.

Sara and Hannah around the pool gave great service and Sara certainly went the extra mile to make sure we had all we needed 

We only ate at Mowry and Cotton which was ok but not really our sort of menu. Would have preferred a few more option both for breakfast and dinner 

JWs only reopened while we were there and we decided to give it a miss as we had been recommended to so many other great restaurants (see my other reviews)

We would certainly recommend the hotel and when it gets the course re-opened in November it will be excellent 

If I have one issue it’s the cost of parking 
$18 to self park or $33 for valet !!!! (Plus tip!)

I can understand that for day visitors but not for long term staying guests . Should be included as it is at Turnberry Isle Miami (also a Marriott) if a 2 week stay. Some consistency please Marriott’s!!

Otherwise ideal

Thanks to The P

reviews.author: ddmullis
reviews.title: Not for the Average Middle American Family
reviews.text:
Upon arrival and being rudely greeted by the valet staff I knew this was not the place for me. He said if I wasn’t paying for valet I must immediately return to self park and find my way to the lobby for checking.   I then proceeded to go find self parking and wind the maze to find the lobby.  

As I was about to check in I made various inquiries including having my local family visit. It was then I was read the rules of the property including only so many can go to pool and wrist band must be worn at all times etc. I was then told they have a $35 per day resort charge and additional fee for self or valet parking   As a platinum guest you only get a continental breakfast and they do not have a concierge lounge 

Thankfully I requested to cancel my room with no penalty and he graciously did that.  I feel this is very much a place that caters to the rich and famous vs everyday  folks. 

The front desk staff was great everyone else rude and not friendly.

reviews.author: Scott A
reviews.title: Home of what was the largest pool in the world when built.
reviews.text: The remake of the golf course is the last step in a total renovation of the entire property. The grounds are beautiful and well maintained. The fitness are an spa are amazing.  Several really good restaurants on site, you can easily spend three or four nights without leaving the grounds.

reviews.author: ed_conway
reviews.title: A Terrific Get-a-way
reviews.text: A great place to stay! My first visit here and I had a wonderful but too short experience. The staff here is amazing. The resort landscaping grounds are beautiful and easy to walk around. The suite/ room was spotless and luxurious.  Highly recommend the Canyon Suites which has a it's own check-in and lobby.  Dined in the Steakhouse that offer a great view from the 5th floor.  I'll be back with plans to check out the spa and I highly recommend.

reviews.author: cralm
reviews.title: Not the same as it used to be
reviews.text: The hotel recently underwent a major renovation the goal of which must have been to spend as little as possible.  In fact, you could be forgiven if you misheard and thought the place was about to undergo a major renovation.  Everything from the fake grass, to the Moen plumbing fixtures, to the quality of the towels and robes seems distinctly middle rate...especially for a five star property.  Perhaps Marriot has decided to make Ritz/St Regis its top brands and make everything else more accessible; who can say?  In any case, for those who remember the Phoenician as an elegant luxury hotel, the current incarnation will leave you disappointed.  Put another way, whereas the Phoenician was once on par with brands like Four Seasons/Ritz Carlton/Peninsula, it now feels like a Hyatt.  On the plus side, the rooms are large and while it was sometimes difficult to find staff, everyone we came in contact with was first rate.

reviews.author: photoameteur
reviews.title: Excellent - and it could have been different!
reviews.text: I’ve got to say that I have been moved to post a review of this beautiful hotel. I have stayed in five-star resorts across the country so to post a review for the first time in a long time means there’s something worth saying. I am staying at this resort as part of a conference being held here.  I have been nothing but impressed with the service and attention shown to me as a guest. I normally am not a needy gas so I don’t always get a good feeling for the customer service at hotels. However, During this day I did need to call on the front desk for assistance and they were very quick to address any concerns I had above and beyond the call of duty. The attention to detail has been phenomenal. I’ve visited the spa, Which has a rooftop pool private to the spa gas and I was very impressed as it ranks amount one of the top spas that I’ve been to.  The food has been amazing I honestly have nothing bad to say. The accommodations are perfect.

reviews.author: KiloTango
reviews.title: Nice hotel with great views
reviews.text:
Stayed here 3 nights for a company meeting. Had a nice room on the froubd floor up against the hill to the north overlooking the cactus garden.

Huge room and spotless bathroom. Meals we had (catered to about 500) were excellent. The margaritas in the lobby bar were spectacular, if somewhat pricey.

There are several tiers of pools for both familys and adults. We hung there for most of our free time as it was 110 degrees. No golf for me! Nice poolside service and shaded lounges as well as cabanas should you wish to par for some privacy.

Only about a $6-8 uber to old scottsdale although you can also get a shuttle from the hotel for somewhat more.

My only regret was not having the time in the morning while it was cool to hike up the trail to the top of the mountain behind the hotel. Maybe next time.

reviews.author: Matthew W
reviews.title: Great getaway hotel! 7 pools, great service!
reviews.text:
Stayed here for a work conference. Drop off at door, staff takes car. Entrance gets crowded. Huge complex. 7 pools, multiple hot tubs. Pools are open 24/7. Swam for hours alone. 

A/C was not cool enough in room. Actually had to buy a fan. But we were here to relax and pools made up for for it.

Also underground parking is tight. Way too many big trucks. would stay here again.

reviews.author: Stella P
reviews.title: High tea
reviews.text:
Before I wrote this review I did write a letter to the Marriott Hotel and did not get a reply  back of the concerns that should be addressed
 My daughter and I went for high tea 
We have been to other places and countries for High Tea   We do enjoy our tea 
The service  was very good.  
The food was the same type of that I gave to my daughter when she was 5. (She is now 16) Egg salad and tuna sandwiches with the crust cut off 
I had to continually swat flies off of my daughters head and food.   When I complained about it I was told it is nature and that since the hotel has doors that there is nothing they can do. They even said other people have been complaining. Nothing they can do to prevent disease infested flies from coming in and being in our food 
When we were leaving it was brought to my attention that the food (egg and tuna sandwiches)we were eating was being continually wrapped in a damp towel cross contaminating with the same towel over and over again. This I did see.  I also saw dessert trays that we ate from being left all over tables   I did not appreciate eating from the same plate as the rest of the restaurant was eating from.
