Next we were served five different types of finger sandwiches (loved the chicken salad and egg salad) and that was followed by scones - buttermilk and cranberry along with lemon curd and Devonshire cream (excellent) and then a selection of sweets - my favorites were the shortbread cookies and chocolate strawberry. The whole experience was pleasant and relaxing and we will definitely go back.  If in doubt, I say that you should treat yourself.  Note:  we saw a couple men there so it is not just for the ladies.

reviews.author: innovit
reviews.title: Very Nice but not Great
reviews.text:
Just spent 5 days at The Phoenician.  Very nice stay. Positives.... great location, courteous and helpful staff, nice rooms. Negatives... CONSTRUCTION! , no gym to speak of, overpriced because of the above.
   Booked through AMEX Platinum Fine Resorts and Hotels.  When you pay this price for a resort it is not the room and views alone but the price reflects service and amenities at the resort. With all the construction and lack of some amenities the price at this resort should be reduced until all is completed.  Also I find that on the AMEX plan a room upgrade is possible. I find this varies from property to property. It seems like Ritz Carlton and Four Seasons Resorts really look hard for a possible upgrade... not so much with Starwood luxury collection resorts.  A possible upgrade was not even mentioned at check in whether it was available or not... I will review this with AMEX.
    The big question is ... would I return? I am likely to give this resort another shot AFTER the construction is done and I would advise you to do the same.

reviews.author: Cassandra D
reviews.title: Wow! Impressive accommodations - even while under construction
reviews.text:
We are thoroughly enjoying our stay at the Phoenician! Our room is huge, with comfortable beds & a luxe bathroom & patio. The kids enjoy the pool everyday & we have no trouble securing pool chairs & beverage service. There’s an array of family activities to enjoy every day. The breakfast buffet is 100% amazing! 
We booked so that my husband could golf. Unfortunately, the course is under construction; but he was able to find other courses in the area to play at. 
While in Arizona we got tickets to Coyotes hockey game, baseball spring training & took a day trip to the Grand Canyon. 

If I could suggest 1 improvement to the resort it would be to put in automatic doors from the self parking to the hotel. It’s difficult to carry in your shopping & get stuck at the pull without a free hand.

reviews.author: sgrim1
reviews.title: Great stay!
reviews.text:
First visit to the Phoenician since the pool and interior updates.  Overall a great experience and I thoroughly enjoyed our visit which was for a combination of work and pleasure (cactus league).  Staff in the lobby and restaurants were attentive and friendly to all needs.  Pool staff was on top of everything and quick with towels, drinks and regular check ins.  

The experience at the Phoenician was fantastic in all aspects.

reviews.author: kmlkm246
reviews.title: Old classic hotel with updates
reviews.text:
Newly renovated lobby is pretty and bright. Lots of construction happening around the property, but they do a nice job keeping it clean and not impacting your stay.
Rooms are very spacious and elegant.
Don’t try to get breakfast/brunch on the weekends in their restaurant. They could not keep up with their guests, and there was over an hour wait. We opted for room service and it came in 30 minutes and was perfect.

reviews.author: Ranjiv H
reviews.title: Luxury and Relaxation at its finest!
reviews.text: The Phoenician has always been one of my favorite getaways.  The pool is perfect and the service is always attentive and warm.  Now with the recent remodel this iconic property is back on top in the valley of the sun.

reviews.author: perlygirly
reviews.title: Desert Paradise
reviews.text:
I Enjoyed a wonderful, warm respite from my Midwest winter before spring breakers. I was welcomed by A+ personnel.  

I am especially grateful for; Taylor Mercer, you are a shining star at customer service, you and Alex B. magically produced 2 bikes within 10 min when another associate (Belinda in the tennis shop) dropped the ball on us. 
('so shines a good deed in a weary world' Willy Wonka)

 Brandellin Nickles you are officially dubbed the 'Snow White' of the Desert (Credit to T.M. for this most accurate moniker)  Brandi summoned 2 species of hummingbirds, quail, gnatcatchers and other beautiful birds to our 'Golf Cart tour' and she added a breadth of knowledge by identifying local birds, their habitat and calls and descriptions of desert foliage. Most importantly, Brandi's personality sparkles with a kind heart and love and passion for nature. 

Thank you to each of these Phoenician stars whom I had the joy to share a chat with Shanielle,(I would love to see a Native American tour/info session for guests, you have so much to offer) Thankyou to  Cristine, Jordan, Chelsea, Charlotte, Anthony, Alex, Randy O. in the tennis shop who ultimately solved our bike issue for the remainder of our stay on something that should not have been difficult day one. (Randy I will be returning for a golf lesson when the course is finished) Thank you to Sara, Tre, Kate at Canyon Suites (great tour, thank you Kate), Kevin, Isreal thanks for the quick response on the keys.  

In-room dining, you are ALL stars, fast, courteous service you never missed a beat.  
The Kabobs by the pool...WOW, delicious however the pickled veggies a bit too pickly for our taste but the fruit was a nice sub.  

Mother of Pearl Pool...Randy, thank you for the recommendations and great service, I agree The Mojito is my favorite too but truthfully you cant go wrong with ANY of the cocktails.  (Phoenician...The poolside Music is a bit of a fail.  Love the speakers but you need a better loop of popular, rock music versus the spa/elevator loop)  

Matthew, Landscaping, thank you for the informative chat, so nice.  

Veronica, Room Service, thank you for the beautifully made bed!  

Cotton and Mowry...Great breakfast, love your huevos rancheros fresh and delicious. Thank you, Maddy and Ivan, for your excellent service.  

 ( Phoenician...the piped in music is a big Fail though, weird)   

The New Spa is nearly finished and its remodel and the many events did NOT interfere with our vacation or enjoyment of the property.  Mike and Phil, thank you for the friendly chat poolside you were so patient with our love to meet new friends.  PS The Spa looks amazing!  
I Love the remodel and the fresher, modern look of The Phoenician.  The earth tone Colors make the blue sky and natural surroundings pop.  A beautiful update of Cotton and Mowry.  

Only Wish...that you allow small pets EVERYWHERE.  The Setai in Miami allows pets everywhere,  so it can be done.  (My little white dog is better behaved and trained than some guests ;) 

Thanks, Phoenician !!

reviews.author: David M
reviews.title: great meeting place
reviews.text: The hotel has been recently remodeled in the main building. The bar has been also redone it turned out very nice and a great place to gather after meetings. The Spa is in the process of being remodeled along with the golf course. This was the second week of February when I was at the Phoenix. The restaurant Relish has one of the best burgers

reviews.author: geldab2018
reviews.title: Splendid!
reviews.text: We did a staycation here with friends. Even thoiugh we have visited this resort, we had never stayed here. I can honestly say we will be back again, We loved it. The rooms and grounds were impeccable! Highly recommend!

reviews.author: ChrisTocino
reviews.title: A bit dated but still very nice
reviews.text: When it was built, this was a one of a kind resort.  Today, there are many similar resorts and the property feels somewhat dated. Nevertheless, it is a nice hotel. The employees are very friendly and obviously well-trained, the rooms are nice, the amenities nice. The restaurants offer very good food and the public areas are well-appointed.

reviews.author: Lacey J
reviews.title: Girls Weekend-40th birthday
reviews.text: When you go to a luxury hotel you expect certain things, liked your  room to be cleaned without request, reservations for the time requested and promised, ability to get a drink at a bar.  Unfortunately, we didn’t experience this here.  When we arrived we were told they could accommodate our adjoining room request but once we got in the room that wasn’t the case. They did move us the next evening in the late afternoon.  I requested to have the rooms cleaned since it was noon and it wasn’t done yet and they came and cleaned one instead of doing both.  The adjoining doors were open so you would think they might notice that it also needed to be clean.  We had a reservation for 8am that the hotel made.  When we got there they said it was at 1pm even though our itinerary from  the hotel said 8.  They were able to get someone by 9am.  We tried to get a drink at the bar one night but could never find a server and left after 15 mins.  None of these things are a big deal but if your going to charge luxury rates then you should provide luxury service.   It seemed a little like they didn’t have enough employees to provide the necessary services.

reviews.author: Jami W
reviews.title: Excellent!
reviews.text: This resort is beautiful and luxurious, but the number one thing that stood out for me was their excellent customer service. Every employee -- from gate security, front desk, concierge, housekeeping, and restaurant staff were all just wonderful. Very warm, friendly, professional and helpful. The rooms were large and clean. I loved the huge bathroom with a sparkling clean soaking tub. There was construction going on so parts of the resort were blocked off but that didn't bother us at all. This resort sets the standard for how luxury resorts should be.

reviews.author: Secsanfran
reviews.title: Frustration with Spa and Renovation
reviews.text:
I was so disappointed with the spa as it was highly recommended to me. I just couldn't wait to get there. I made an appointment for Friday, February 23 for the Crowning Touch and Desert Serenity Scrub Wrap massage. I was referred to the spa by my friend who said it was amazing - excellent salt baths, etc. I knew the spa was going through some renovations, however I had no idea that the Spa on 4th was just another hotel hallway. The website lists that there are limited amenities. 

The truth is that there are no amenities- the waiting area is a regular hotel room with a few chairs and lemon water. I had my service in another hotel room which was quite awkward. There were kids running around the hall during my treatment and the lady told me the other side of the hall is actually occupied with guests. My spa gal, Dawn, was amazing and was trying to do the best she could with what she was given, but this is not a "spa experience" as described on the website.

I've been to many spas-some full and some during upgrades. I was very disappointed and tried to talk to someone at the spa. I couldn't reach someone directly and they kept butchering my name even after I pronounced and spelled it. After several phone calls back and forth, I was told that the price reflected the renovation of the spa. That is simply not true - I paid $358 for almost 2 hours of service and nothing else. Now if I had never been to another spa, then maybe I would have understood. However, I've been very lucky to go to many spas and the price I paid at the The Phoenician was actually more than other spas where you can spend all day in the sauna, spa, pool, baths, etc. There was no option at this time. I have paid less than $200 at other spas and have received much more and also spent the entire day at the spa which is worth the money.

I was very disappointed with the lack of regard for my concerns and the high price of a "spa experience" that happened in a hotel room. I do understand the idea of the renovation but it is not communicated clearly about what services they actually offer during the renovation. This was not a spa - it was a service in a room. I paid way too much money for that and do not recommend it.

This is not a great place to be during construction. The loud construction started very early in the morning by 7:00am and it is not resort-like. The price is just too high to deal with those issues.

We did have a great time during the Trapeze activity!!!

reviews.author: scottandmaryg
reviews.title: Construction, Construction, Construction
reviews.text: We booked a Casita at The Phoenician for a week.  I had stayed here before on golf trips, and remembered it to be a great resort with a good restaurant.  Boy were we disappointed!  Our Casita looked right at construction.  This had not been clearly marked on the United Airlines booking website.  We called the front desk and asked for a room that did not look at construction and the picked us up in a golf cart and took us to a Casita with even more construction.  Two hours later we finally had a room on the back of the hotel looking at the base of Camelback a few feet from a popular hiking trail..  They reluctantly agreed to credit us the difference between what we payed for a Casita (their nicest room) and our hotel room, but they wanted us to spend it at their hotel.  We were hugely disappointed with our visit, with the management (or lack thereof) and with their flimsy resolution of our issue.

reviews.author: KristenNix
reviews.title: Excellent Family Resort
reviews.text: We stayed here through New Years Day, and we really enjoyed everything about this fantastic resort.  Great location directly below Camelback Mountain, close to restaurants, shopping, and very convenient to PHX airport.  Pools are beautiful and the water slide is a lot of fun.  We played 2 rounds of golf just before it was closed for the renovation... really looking forward to playing the new course when it opens at the end of this year.  We were in a Grand Deluxe Queen Queen room and it was amazing.  Very spacious and modern, beautifully decorated, awesome large bathroom with double sinks, soaking tub, and separate shower.  Large Balcony with great view over the pools.  Breakfast at Mowry & Cotton was very good, and Relish at the Golf Course was excellent.  We are gluten free and the food was safe and delicious.  We definitely want to return to the Phoenician Scottsdale.

reviews.author: LADarya
reviews.title: Great hotel and great care
reviews.text: Our beautiful time at the Hotel, which is surprisingly kid friendly with water slide and play area, was interrupted by a visit by the paramedics as our son got bitten by a bee and went into a major allergic reaction. As he was rushed to Phoenix Children’s, we were impressed by the quick response, help and attention we received in particulate by Hotel Security Mr Salazar. We hope to be back for first week of spring g training next year and hopefully get warmer weather and no ER visit in 2019. The hotel is super clean and comfortable, and the restaurants are terrific with healthy food on the Terrace and a Steak house up top.

reviews.author: Larry T
reviews.title: Chistmas and New Year at the Phoenician
reviews.text: Two and a half weeks at the Phoenician was not long enough to sample all that Phoenix and the Phoenician has to offer. Our room {4468} was luxurious and provided us with a feeling of our home away from home. The coffee shop was perfect for our early risings and provided a perfect and very healthy breakfast for the start of each day. Parking underground was easy . The outside patio at night by the firepits is an excellent place to socialize with friends and enjoy exotic drinks. The live entertainment was top notch. The grounds are simply spectacular. The flowers and desert plants  are truly beautiful. The walking trails are beautiful and easy to negotiate. The fitness center is small but it is my understanding that a new one is being built.

reviews.author: Lebotraveler
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text:
I will begin by saying we travel quite extensively and that I usually am quite happy when we book luxury accommodations. However, I have to say that our experience this weekend with this resort was ho hum. We have been to Scottsdale many times and always stayed at the JW. But this time we hoped to step it up a notch and pamper ourselves for my birthday weekend. 

From the checkin to checkout, we never felt welcomed or pampered. Our room was the furthest from the lobby and on the ground floor facing the mountain. The outdoor garden is beautiful but we felt like we were in a cave. When I booked, I requested a balcony and a fire pit. We received neither. The porch only had one chair to sit on and it was far to chilly to sit outside without a warm fire or a propane heater. 

At the pool, we were not welcomed or given towels for over 1/2 hour. The only reason why we were even addressed was to tell us that we were sitting in an area reserved for those paying for cabanas, even though we were in front if it with no signage stating this. Due to weather, that was the only day we even tried the pool area. 

We parked our rental car in the garage. Each time we tried to enter or leave, our card didn’t work. We would have to press the button and wait for someone to answer. No one ever picked up! Not one time. 

We decided to give the Burger restaurant a try. Asking the concierge where it was, we were told to hike down to the golf club. This was a significant distance down through the pool complex and steps. It was windy and chilly. Upon arriving, there was a sign stating that the restaurant was closed today. No explanation! Why didn’t the concierge tell us? Hiked back up and got in the car and drove over to our familiar JW which was warm, welcoming and friendly. 

Checkout gave me a near heart attack when I tried to check out via my room tv. It had doubled my bill! I was late leaving for the airport because I had to go to the front desk to check out to resolve the problem. I was told...oh we have a problem with that! Really? When you pay this much for a hotel, you expect the correct bill and online checkout.

I believe this resort is great if you are looking for a nice conference center but I would call it cold, plastic and not welcoming. I am an SPG member but I am not coming back any time soon. Too bad because we love resorts like this!

reviews.author: compgal
reviews.title: IFly at Phoenician
reviews.text: We LOVED attending the FREE iFly event at the Phoenician.  The Mad Hatter was this month's theme.  The trapeze artists were amazing.   The Phoenician provided free lemonade and popcorn which was a lovely touch.   We will be back!

reviews.author: JMG672014
reviews.title: Family vacation
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is a beautiful resort and the staff are all so nice and accommodating !
We have been there several times and never been disappointed.
They are remodeling and adding a new spa and fitness center which should also be spectacular!

reviews.author: Kitchengardener
reviews.title: Truly part of the Luxury Collection
reviews.text:
Our first visit to the Phoenician came at a Hectic time in the Valley-golf tournament, rodeos, auctions to name a few things going on.
The hotel recently underwent an extensive makeover-the spa is still under construction as are some athletic facilities. I imagine it will be just perfect when all the work is complete. Meanwhile there is a spa on the fourth floor with a number of signature treatments. The hotel has a modern vibe with very personal service.
Another attractive feature is a beautiful cactus trail behind the hotel. Even our entry level room was incredibly spacious, and it was cleaned meticulously. 
I have never seen such thoughtful turndown service. Other hotels should send their housekeeping managers to the Phoenician to learn how to do it right! We enjoyed the market cafe as a quick option for coffee and grab n go meals, their staff was friendly and helpful. We preferred the delicious poolside lunches at Kalios Kabobery over the more formal Mowry and Cotton. The restaurant had an outstanding pheasant dish, interesting Oregon wines, and cocktails,but the sharing menu still needs some tweaking. We also had a great Super Bowl dinner at the Relish Burger Bar, with, as you might expect, excellent burgers! There are three pools, the most beautiful
Being the Mother of Pearl pool on the lowest level, staffed by Rich and his helpful crew. We hope to return again when the resort is totally renovated!

reviews.author: rick c c
reviews.title: Amazing resort property
reviews.text: The Phoenician in Scottsdale AZ. is an amazing property close to great hiking. My wife and I stayed over there during the X-mas holiday for a romantic getaway and had a very nice time. The staff caters to your every need and the rooms are clean and comfy. Loved the pool and spas. Very good dining too! 5 stars!!

reviews.author: 1HighStandard
reviews.title: Best Resort Location in Phoenix, Really Nice Renovation, Some Lingering Dated Colors
reviews.text:
Really Nice Main Entry 
Very Cordial Valets / Bells / Registration
Very Large Scale, Not Intimate
Stepped Monolithic Architecture could use tone variation
Very Accommodating Pool area and Services

My room was at the west end of the westerly hillside building and quite a long walk to the restaurant and ridiculously long to the pools, having to walk through the more "dressed" areas.
The room was very nice, large and appointed.  Great television system. Nice bathroom.
BUT..... I was in a middle floor and could hear steps above and everything in the hallway (knocking, doors closing, voices).  i've been in quieter W hotels.
J&G Steakhouse had nice views, typical dark wood / mood lighting. Service was average, so was the food....really average, but prices were not too bad either

reviews.author: MSG60763
reviews.title: Average experience
reviews.text: If you want an average experience with average food and average service this is the place for you. You have to beg for service and for food and even to clean the room. I was so disappointed by so much. The pool is three feet deep and poorly maintained. They say it is heated but it is freeing and only fit for 8 year olds. The renovations are all over the place and the gym is not in use and everything seems in flux. I am told that the main restaurant used to be good when it was Italian. It was pricey and awful. The concierge couldn't help me and she complained that they were fully booked so they couldn't accommodate any of the things that they advertised. Sorry I went.

reviews.author: Jen B
reviews.title: Great Long Weekend
reviews.text:
We stayed here for a long weekend with another couple after finding a great rate due to the construction. The location was perfect - it was about a $6-7 uber ride to downtown Scottsdale and only $15 to TopGolf/casino. We were able to do Camelback two of the three days we were there. Not having to drive to the mountain and deal with parking was a huge plus for us. Don't let the concierge scare you about the dangers of the mountain :)  We also were able to go for nice runs nearby the hotel.

The pools were large and we enjoyed the adults only one every day after our hikes and runs. The pool lunch menu was decent and the prices were surprisingly reasonable. In the early evening, it was nice to enjoy a cocktail on the terrace and watch the sunset - it's really a fantastic way to start the evening.

The rooms have just been redone and they're beautiful. They're very spacious and we had a great view of the mountain with chairs and a table on the patio. The bed was very comfortable. We didn't seem to notice noise from the construction that others have mentioned.

The only negatives to mention were:
1. There was a LOT of chairs/cabanas at the pool reserved for people willing to pay more. The hotel seemed to be about half full so it seemed unnecessary to block off such a large area that no one was using.
2. The gym is really really small. They're building a huge new one so I'm excited to see what that looks like the but the current one is a joke
3. The walls seem to be pretty thin - we heard a lot of noise from people coming and going throughout the night. Our friends had a room facing the lobby of the hotel and mentioned it was very noisy with people getting dropped off all night long.

Overall, I'd recommend this hotel to anyone visiting the Scottsdale area. I can't wait to come back and visit again once the gym and spa are complete.

reviews.author: JewelsL76
reviews.title: Great Weekend!
reviews.text:
I meant to write this over the summer. Rooms were amazing! Three people that stood out with exceptional service Kris,Allen and Nicole! 
Water slide is fun for kids, lots of activities available! Can't wait to return with my family!

reviews.author: J_and_A_1
reviews.title: Big and Splashy
reviews.text:
We decided to stay here primarily to check out this newly renovated legendary property. Overall we were impressed with what we saw.

Of course the room is an important part of a stay and we really liked the new room look.  It is easy to say it is straight out of a Restoration Hardware catalog and for us that is a good thing.  The room was very spacious and included a large couch with a lounger section.  There was also a nice desk area and plenty of drawer space and good lighting.  The color palette was soft grays and blues.  The bathroom was very stylish with double sinks, separate shower, tub, and water closet.  The shower was nice but a little tight.  The only thing we did not like about the room was that the entry area was a little busy with two closet doors, and the bathroom door all converging on top of each other along with the entry door. The spaciousness of the room flows out through a wide sliding door to a private terrace with a small cushioned couch and a table and two chairs.  A great indoor outdoor setup can be enjoyed as long as you have a good view.  

A big deal at this hotel is the three level pool area.  While big and fun, it is a little too much and I did not like that two of the pools were strange shapes that created a clunky arrangement around them.  The bottom level is where you will find the famed mother of pearl pool which has a more traditional and refined look to it with cabanas around it on one side. As noted in reviews, the spa is not open yet and seems to have a ways to go.  It is going to be near the pools so construction noise can be a factor at times.  The hotel is also operating with a temporary gym located in the tennis center.  About half of the gym space is in a covered open air patio.  If you workout in the morning or evening this space can be very cool. Regardless, there is enough equipment to pretty much obtain a full workout.               

The rest of the hotel carries out the RH look to a stylish and somewhat glamourous effect. The exception is Mowry & Cotton which has a more relaxed modern country feel.  We wanted to have breakfast here but the menu was limited with no basic fair such as pancakes or waffles. Relish Burger Bistro has a classic golf club look but that might be changing.   

One of the best advantages of this hotel is its location close to downtown Scottsdale making it easy for off-site adventures. While we enjoyed our stay at this hotel it is not one we would most likely return to primarily because of its size.  It is just a little too big, at over 600 rooms plus large event space areas.  And as attractive as the interior renovation is and the grounds pretty, the hulking exterior is very hard looking and dated in appearance.  But if size is not an issue, the posh space, convenient location, and ample on site activities will make you a happy guest.

reviews.author: Saphire10
reviews.title: Idyllic
reviews.text:
Recent renovations show a beautifully polished and designed resort.  

The pool area with its multi levels and comfortable seating, numerous umbrellas with attentive staff is a relaxing way to spend some time in the sun. 

Even The basic rooms are spacious and well appointed.  Our room was a long way to walk to due to the design of the hotel. Which did help me work off the delicious food!!!!

The hotel has a falconer that patrols with a hawk called Flex.  The hawk is a natural predator to the black birds that can be a nuisance, especially around outdoor restaurant.  A natural way of pest control that is a new and innovative green way of handling the problem of pest birds🦅

My one disappointment with my stay was the construction noise all day.  I know the necessity of it but the reality of it was still annoying.  

The views of Camelback Mountain make this resort so lovely.  I even managed to hike up to a t box on the golf course (closed for renovations) to catch a gorgeous sunset.  

A good choice for our 3 day stay.

reviews.author: luchito09
reviews.title: Excelente hotel
reviews.text:
Me encanto! Estuve hospedado en una suite y la vista es espectacular
La atención tanto en el lobby como en bares y restaurantes es inmejorable. Cuenta con albercas muy bonitas pero no busques ambiente de fiesta
Para los que juegan golf el campo que tiene el
Hotel fantástico

reviews.author: brhendri
reviews.title: High Tea
reviews.text:
With all the changes at the resort, some very good, other still underway, it was great to see Wanda and Natalie still managing High Tea. High Tea is a wonderful experiences and the Phoenician’s Tea is at the top!  Thanks go to Wanda and Natalie who have managed this event for years. They remember us, know our favorite tea and that we enjoy champagne. They also know where we like to sit. Although with the renovations we have had to deal with changes. 

Management, while you have changed many familiar faces and good friends, thank you for realizing these two ladies are as closer to irreplaceable as it comes.

reviews.author: arielmac
reviews.title: Great amenities
reviews.text: This resort has amazing features and seems to have a lot of options for families. The bar was very welcoming (we ate their twice just because we liked the vibe) and they played live music one night; really nice. They have a lot of pools that were very clean and had adorable shops. Definitely a resort to choose when going to Arizona. They also left truffles for our belated anniversary celebration- nice touch.

reviews.author: Jason K
reviews.title: OUTSTANDING
reviews.text: I would have to say that I have been well traveled in my career and this was by the very best service I have ever had.  The rooms were clean, the view was amazing.  The food was top notch.  There wasn't one thing that I would change about my stay.  We decided to do a couples massage, even with the spa under construction, it didn't matter.  The best massage of my life happened there.  I will be returning for future visits maybe annual visits.  This place is at the very top of my list.  It is pricey however, you get what you pay for as with anything and everything.  What you are paying for is worth it.  If price tags bother you go somewhere else this isn't a place you go looking for a deal it is a place you go to for great customer service and a vacation without any sort of worries.  I cannot say enough about our trip. If I could give it 8 stars out of 5 I would do that.

reviews.author: EGRap
reviews.title: Great location, comfortable room, great time @ I.FLY but hotel service was really lacking..
reviews.text:
Like others who noted the service at the end of December to New's Day was lacking for my family too at this hotel.  Check in process was slow, I found the layout of the finding my room less than intuitive and we asked for help from the front desk and bellman a couple times but after waiting 17 minutes and asking twice, I just went on my own, which is not a very warm welcome..

I also made the mistake of paying for parking as I exited the hotel and then learned this was not required, so don't waste your money like I did..

As noted in the headline, this hotel is at a great location and it was easy to get to other places in Scottsdale & Phoenix and the room was very comfortable but it is not in the same league as other hotels as we ended up staying at the Four Seasons for the last four days of our trip and found a noticeable difference from the moment we arrived where we felt welcomed to all the details in our room (ie shampoo & toiletries, towels, etc).

Our 9-year old daughter loved the I.FLY trapeze experience so much she said it was the best part of our vacation.  I.Fly is by the tennis courts at the Phoenician and the I.FLY team is first rate. Our entire family had fun here!

The biggest disappointment for this hotel was the wait/hostess staff at Mowry & Cotton, who I will give the benefit of the doubt and say they were just too busy but they were really rude, which turned out to be a positive for our family because we probably would have eaten there more but found some wonderful and better places within minutes of the hotel.  My advise to others would be to do the same.  Scottsdale has some wonderful restaurants and excellent food & service!!

Again, good location, comfortable room but service is not very good for the price point they charge.

reviews.author: TracyJane76
reviews.title: Babymoon getaway over the New Year.
reviews.text:
My husband and I usually leave the country for the New Year holiday but because i'm pregnant this year, we decided to stay in the US and try out a nicer resort for some relaxation pre-baby. We were not disappointed in the Phoenician. The grounds were gorgeous as we drove up past the golf course and the tennis courts. The flowers were bright and vibrant and you could tell a lot of work had gone into making things look perfect. We did notice the different areas that were under construction and I had been slightly worried that it would interfere with our relaxation, but we never heard any construction noises or were put out by anything not being open. Luckily over the 6 days we were there, they only worked a couple of those days, so that probably helped. 
The service at the hotel was amazing, with one exception. The front desk people were less than helpful when we arrived around 2pm to check in. We understood that there was a chance our room would not be ready as check in time at the hotel is 4pm. It was not ready, but we were assured that they would call us if the room became available before 4pm. We walked around the resort, grabbed lunch and then some cocktails as we hung out by the pool. Never once did my husband's phone ring and we stayed on the property. Finally at 4pm, he went to check on the room and he was told that they'd been trying to call us for an hour and leaving messages saying the room was ready. Again, there was no phone call, no message on his phone and we were on property so there were no service issues. We were ok with the room not being ready, but the blatant lie by the front desk was uncalled for. It set a bad tone for the beginning of our vacation. Also, while at the front desk, we asked about the restaurants and were given some incorrect information about them which we found out the next day when we actually went to the restaurant and asked the server. Also, we were told we'd get a little packet of amenities and information with our keys. We didn't receive that either and had to go back to the front desk for our amenities. I feel like the front desk staff needs a little more instruction on how to make people feel welcome and also how to give out information to guests. 
Other than that slip up, I will say that the rest of the service we received at the hotel was top notch. We attended the pool on a few different days and the pool attendant always remembered us and our room number for when we ordered beverages or food. One detail we loved is that they brought us a pitcher of ice water and glasses as soon as we sat down and then they continued to refill it throughout the day. It was nice to stay hydrated and not have to ask. 
 We had breakfast at the restaurant every morning and we were called by our name and seated within 5-10 minutes each time. Very attentive staff with little details covered to make us feel special. Food was delicious!! 
We stayed in a casita and it was great to have the extra space and patio that overlooked a waterfall and some good landscaping. We relaxed out there after dinner most nights. All in all I'd say it was a great stay at this resort and I'd come back again!

reviews.author: westendave
reviews.title: NEW YEARSWEEKEND
reviews.text:
Spent 6 nights over New Years 2018 Weekend with family in 2 rooms.
The staff was uniformity helpful and friendly always smiling and trying to please. Breakfast was excellent with delicious fresh fruit and very attentive wait staff, 
The gym is a bit crowded due to renovation but I would expect the new facility will be fabulous. The grounds are impeccably kept. Tennis courts perfect and helpful tennis staff.
Rooms well maintained and clean 
The hotel small takeout  store and clothing store are a bit pricey.

reviews.author: Klur56
reviews.title: Disappointed with this visit
reviews.text: We have been visiting the Phoenician over the last 20 Years. This visit, 12/28-1/2/18 was a large disappointment. Customer service was not attentive. They had no control over the large # of guests with very young children. Our room was not ready, while everyone else was checked in, and when we did go to our room, it was not what we originally reserved. The updates they did are mixed, some nice, others, do not like. We will try again in late Spring, but if not pleased, will look for another property. For $ you pay, don’t see results.

reviews.author: TravelAgentLyns
reviews.title: UNDER RENNOVATION - Don't DO IT.
reviews.text: Unless these are the views you're looking for....Don't Do It. Grounds are under Renovation. Spa is under Renovation. Golf Course is even under Renovation. (Which i'm sure you didn't know when you first log on to their website! (Gotta love a resort just trying to make a buck!).

reviews.author: Char H
reviews.title: The trick here is to avoid your room
reviews.text:
It would be tempting to just sit in a bathtub and lounge in the bed and admire the mountain view’s from your balcony. No one would blame you if you ordered steaks from room service and binged “Fixer Upper” (especially if you’re a cord-cutter). But NO - go wander the little path running behind the hotel along the mountain and see a gecko or two. 

Wend your way across the property toward the golf course and at least watch putting practice. When you drive up to the lobby, resist the tempatation to turn left toward the elevators. Instead, amble down into the bar and hang out. People on vacation in Arizona are exceedingly laid back and chatty. When they’re watching birds eat patio-dining guests’ food RIGHT OFF THEIR PLATES, their conversation is downright exciting. It’s a superb location - right where Arcadia abuts Scottsdale and within a short drive to Chandler and Tempe. Use The Phoenician for beauty and abatement - not just lodging. I’ve stayed there 5 times over 7 years. The place isn’t brand new, but it is classic and the people who work for Starwood take pride in it and in caring for guests’ experiences at a high level. I like it better than the North Scottsdale Westin.

reviews.author: TJ P
reviews.title: Beautifully renovated with excellent service
reviews.text: My wife and I experienced this newly renovated property during a professional conference in December 2018.  Though there were additional renovation & addition components being completed - we never felt as though we were on a jobsite.  The new fitness center was yet to be completed so the existing facility was a bit lacking - but available during our stay.  If the final version of this added piece matches what has been completed so far - it too will be fantastic.  Rooms well renovated & housekeeping staff was timely and attentive.  Our dedicated conference staff was friendly and other staff unrelated to our conference were equally welcoming and attentive.

reviews.author: John F
reviews.title: A little too spread out
reviews.text: When a hotel does not provide coffee in your room its a tough half mile slog to reception in the morning! To be fair during this stay it was under renovation, including the main pool so wasn't a great experience compared to others.

reviews.author: janecR8033VM
reviews.title: Flying trapeze and a great stay
reviews.text: My family had a fun-filled stay at The Phoenician over holiday week 2017.  We have two children age 8 who did the iFly trapeze activity three times and loved it.  We all loved dinner at the steak house restaurant which has excellent food, live music and great service. We also liked Lowry + Cotton- avocado toast was the best I've ever had. The cactus garden is beautiful.  The hotel helped arrange a guided hike of Camelback Mountain with the Wild Bunch Desert Guides which was fun and exciting - a little scary but fun.  Also went to Phoenix and did the Arizona Science Museum, loved it.  Thought our room rate of $419/night for what we got was a great deal.

reviews.author: Ansel C
reviews.title: A Fantastically Renovated Phoenician
reviews.text: My wife and I recently made a site visit for my trade association's 2018 annual conference. Our first visit was in August when the renovation of the rooms and meeting facilities had been completed as part of a multi-year $200,000,000 renovation and expansion project. The lobby, restaurants, lounges and try-level pool area have now been completed. The 40,000 square foot Spa and adjacent Fitness Facility will be completed in March. We stayed in a Casita one bedroom suite that was quite comfortable. The setting is beautiful. The staff is clearly highly trained, professional, friendly and helpful. We enjoyed eating at two of the restaurants.

reviews.author: Peggy Woon
reviews.title: Nice property but lacking in service
reviews.text:
My family and I stayed here last week and felt the hotel was nothing special.  We stayed in 3 standard rooms and it was beautifully renovated and spacious.  However there were many reasons why I felt this did not live up to a 5 star hotel:

1) Lying front-desk attendant:  when we checked in the attendant said he would like  to upgrade us to a room with a better view but they were full occupancy.  When our bell service came up to deliver our bags, he said the property was only half full. Hmm?

2) Horribly rude waitress at Mowry & Cotton:  we had tickets to a timed museum exhibit and and when ordering asked if they can rush our food. Christine our waitress says flatly “No. The restaurant is full and your order will be after everyone else”.  No apologies or anything! She then said if we wanted a fast option we should “get the buffet”. 

3) Selling EXPIRED MILK at Marketplace:  after our bad breakfast experience at Mowry we decided to grab a quick bite at Marketplace, their grab and go dining option. The pastries here are really good. But halfway through our meal we realized my toddler son was drinking bottled milk that expired 4 days prior. When we alerted the register staff they went through the rest of the fridge and pulled out a bunch of expired beverages - not just milk. I was then offered an explanation that they contract a 3rd party company to stock the beverages and they’ll need to let them know this happened. As a hotel guest I don’t really care how they stock the milk I just want them to take accountability and apologize for serving my young child expired milk. 

4) Slow housekeeping: on our last night my parents we were out intermittently throughout the day. Our room got serviced, but my parents, who were right next door to us and had requested service, did not get a knock until 8:30pm. Seriously? 

All in all, the hotel itself is a great property but with so many 5 star options in the Scottsdale and Phoenix area I don’t think we will return.

reviews.author: Leona M
reviews.title: Amazing stay!
reviews.text: By far my favorite hotel! I have been here a dozen times and always enjoy the service, rooms, grounds and overall experience!! And when I was able to stay at the canyon suites it was even more amazing!!I will be back! Truly love this place ♥️.

reviews.author: TXflyfisher
reviews.title: Fantastic Service
reviews.text: The room was great (very quiet), the food fantastic, I loved the view from the mountain (and trails), and wow, the pools are beautiful (especially the mother of pearl) but it was the great service that makes this a true five star resort.  From the very start, the concierge, Taylor Mercer, who set up the perfect trip to Alan from room service.  Everyone, even the valet parking attendants and lady at the registration desk, were just great.  It was really nice to experience true service again.  As a very frequent traveler, with world wide experience, this was just about the best service I have ever seen.  It made the high cost of the room worth the price.

reviews.author: popishpartyoftwo
reviews.title: Poor Experience at Golf Course
reviews.text:
My wife and I were visitors to The Phoenician golf course on Wednesday, December 27th. We booked a tee time online on Monday and we were aware that the course was beginning its renovation process on January 8th, 2018; however, the entire experience was one that has left us disappointed and quite frankly very upset. 

We typically play on city courses as they are more affordable for us to visit on a more frequent basis, but today was a special occasion. I purchased the round of golf for my wife and I as a first wedding anniversary gift thinking that it would be a nice treat for us to play a luxury course and enjoy the amenities that come with that type of course. Unfortunately, I was sorely mistaken and I wish that I had chosen to visit the Biltmore Golf Course, which would have been $20 cheaper and of a much higher caliber. 

To begin with, we were not greeted in any fashion upon walking up to the bag drop. A gentleman did take our bags from us but only after we stood there for a minute or so looking around for assistance. We were told to visit the pro shop, where the gentleman behind the counter was very nice. We decided to spend our time waiting for our tee time on the practice putting green, which was expertly maintained with luscious green grass. If only I could have played my entire round on that single practice green as that was the only real grass that I was to see for the rest of the day. 

As our tee time approached we got into our cart and headed to the first tee. As we were about to get ready to tee off, from hole 1, an employee approached us and said that we were actually going off of 10 and that another employee had gone to collect our playing partners for the day. This was the first interaction we had with one of your employees in regards to our round of golf for the day and it was all very disorganized. Our playing partners were very nice and their company was appreciated; however, they only had one full set of clubs between the two of them. The female of the group only had two clubs with her, an iron and a putter, for the entire course. While they were both very nice, this would never be allowed on any course we've played before and it did slow down our pace of play as she proceeded to tee off of almost every hole, including the par 5's, with an iron. 

Mentioning pace of play, I was astounded to be approached before we had even finished the second hole about our pace of play. The "course assistant" rolled up as we were making our way down the fairway and proceeded to tell us that we needed to catch up with the group in front as the course was very busy today. My wife and I had yet to adjust to the poor course conditions, and as mentioned above in regard to our partner's club situation, we were still able to catch up with the group ahead of us by the 4th hole, finishing the entire round only 4 minutes over Time Par. It would have been nice to have some more time to acclimate to the course before being hounded about our pace of play. 

Speaking of poor course conditions, I was astonished to see that major construction had already started and that the upkeep of the entire course was far from what we saw advertised on their website. As I mentioned at the beginning, we were aware of the upcoming construction, which the website stated was set to begin on January 8th. That being said, we did not expect to come across drained, brown, and smelly lakes, and dying greens and fairways that had clearly been painted green in an attempt to hide their true condition. In addition to the fairways and greens being painted, the general upkeep of the grass was poor - there were many divots that had not been repaired on a majority of the greens, and some of the greens were lacking in general repair as there were piles of dirt on them and very uneven edges. Overal, the entire course lacked a clean and manicured appearance, making us wish we had saved our money and supported one of our local, city courses. 

In the end, we just wanted the round of golf to be over and done with so that we could go home. I am upset that I wasted my money on this course to celebrate our first wedding anniversary and would not recommend it to anyone looking for a luxury round of golf.

reviews.author: FatBaxter
reviews.title: A sight to see
reviews.text: Beautiful large rooms. Stayed for free using SPG points. Helpful staff. Restaurants and bars are VERY expensive. Great pool.  An electrician walked into my room while I was trying to take a nap. Manager was mildly apologetic. Not a great customer service experience. Worth a stop on your way to/from Sedona. A sight to behold.

reviews.author: Caseyvtb
reviews.title: less for more
reviews.text: Had for several years gone to the Terrace restaurant holiday buffet spreads, lavish and excellent, pricey but worth it.  With the renovation and the general downgrades overall, they now do the holiday buffet in the steakhouse.  Same price, half the food, much of it served cold.  A Phoenician manager explained to me that they could no longer make money on the old buffet because they needed 700 customers to break even.  Perhaps, but offering so much less, in a less pleasant space [noisy, no table cloths, cluttered, with blaring Muzak], FOR THE SAME HIGH PRICE is just an insult to your customers.  (Oh, and $120 for the buffet is a lot:  but there's also a mandatory 20% service charge, so it's really $144 per person.)  Just not worth it, but it's all part of the hollowing out of a venerable institution to make it into an ordinary golf club.

reviews.author: BobbyD6363
reviews.title: Started Great then Ended Badly
reviews.text:
This was my first time staying at the Phoenician.  I was in Phoenix for a conference and decided to split my stay over two resorts.  I spent two days at the Arizona Biltmore before moving over to the Phoenician.  I thought it would give me a good perspective before our return in May 2018.  I always book through American Express Platinum travel for the great benefits during my stays.

Driving into the resort you are greeted by a gate guard who asked my name and told me how to get to the Valet.  The Valet is right next to a beautiful fountain and my luggage and car were whisked away and I was escorted to the check in desk.  Dustin greeted me and gave me all the particulars regarding the resort and actually looked up my Marriott Rewards number for my stay.  As a Marriott Gold level guest I could receive a free drink or 250 points … of course I chose the beverage!  Dustin informed me I had been upgraded to a Deluxe Casita King with a fire pit.  I instantly had visions of a bottle of wine and a fire pit evening reading my book.  Dustin went over the American Express Platinum benefits: $100 resort food and beverage credit, reduced resort fee, free premium internet and $80 breakfast credit per day.  Lastly, Dustin informed me the casitas have their own parking and he would have the valet bring my car to my casita and park it.  

With directions from Dustin, I wound my way downhill to Casita L room 7161.  Unless you drive your car to the casitas, I feel mobility restricted guests will have a problem navigating down through the orchid garden and several sets of stairs.  Note the Phoenician is undergoing massive renovations and around the casitas it shows.  First off the trail leading down the hill to the casitas is lined with some rather cheap looking café lights and surprisingly fake grass.  Casita L is right next to the fence where the new Spa construction area is located.  Note: I checked in at 5PM and all was quiet on the construction side (more on that later).

Casita L Room 7161 was nice and clean with a large bathroom, mini bar, and a mini-fridge in the bureau, two closets, king bed and very large TV.  I went outside and checked out the sitting area which has the aforementioned fire pit, two chairs.  The lanai also has a small table and chairs as well as a cushioned bench.  The entire outdoor area was filthy.  The cushions on all the chairs were COVERED in bird droppings and dust.  There were several pieces of paper and Splenda packets in and among the shrubs.  Room 7161 has an adjoining room but I didn’t hear noise through the adjoining door.  Then it was time to explore the property.

The main lobby is GORGEOUS!  The money being spent on the renovations is obvious!  In the lobby I spoke to the Concierge regarding spa treatments to find out there was no spa.  Basically there are only massage rooms set up in former guest rooms until the renovation is complete.  The lobby bar has a great view of the sunset as I enjoyed my free adult beverage.  I made my way to the J&G Steakhouse and spent the bulk of my food and beverage credit on an amazing dinner!  J&G service was outstanding.  I bought a bottle of wine from the lobby bar and headed to enjoy my fire pit evening.  I had to call engineering to get the fire pit lit!  LOL! It is a challenging set of steps which I can now recite.  After a bottle of red wine it was time for bed.

Promptly at 645AM I was awoken by several trucks and loaders beep, beep, beeping along with several construction workers yelling back and forth.  Mind you it was 645AM Saturday morning!  I called the front desk and was informed that construction begins at sunrise. ON SATURDAY!??? I was literally the last Casita room adjacent to this construction area.  Additionally, Casita L and M are the staging area for all the construction equipment (see the resort map I added to this review).  The front desk lady said yes we are doing construction from sunrise to sunset daily until the renovations are complete.  She offered to send me some earplugs.  EARPLUGS??!!!!! I am quite aware the Phoenician website clearly states ongoing renovations but NOT SUNRISE TO SUNSET!  While on the phone with the front desk she said she could actually hear the construction noises through the phone! At this point I was offered another room.  I find it strange that I was UPGRADED to this room!  Apparently my room was upgraded but not the location. I had to get away from the noise so I went to Mowry & Cotton for breakfast.  The Mowry & Cotton service was outstanding.  After a very leisurely breakfast and watching birds attack leftovers on other tables, I went back to shower before the airport.   While brushing my teeth I noticed BLOOD on the bathroom wall next to the sink!  SERIOUSLY! BLOOD!  I grabbed my bags and went to check out.  At the front desk I spoke to the same poor lady I had been talking to all morning.  She was very apologetic over and over about the problems.  They eventually gave me a $125 off my room.

Bottom line: It is NOT an upgrade when you are moved directly adjacent to construction!  DO NOT BOOK Casita L or M!  Probably shouldn’t book Casitas N, O and P as well.  The Phoenician is a beautiful property which will be even more amazing when it is all done.  The staff are wonderful!  However, I may just return to the Arizona Biltmore until the Phoenician is construction free.

reviews.author: Buckeyebigdog
reviews.title: Premier luxury resort
reviews.text:
What an amazing place!  Went for 2 day weekend to unwind from work and that's exactly what i did! Make you eat at the J & G steak house ! The food and the service was 5 star! 
Also the pool area and Spa area is also a great way to unwind and Recharge!!

reviews.author: plumgirl20
reviews.title: Afternoon Tea Delight
reviews.text: What a fabulous destination for afternoon tea!  Lovely pianist playing great songs, gorgeous view, superb service and food.  We left stuffed!  Tea was out of this world.  We have lived-in China so we know our tea! Plentiful and gracious edibles were top shelf, both quality and offerings. Afternoon tea is one of those special occasions when we  remember we are civilized when we so often encounter an uncivilized world right outside our door.  Just Go - for the holidays, to celebrate the New Year or just to celebrate our good fortune to have so many lovely warm days here in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: FunTravels1
reviews.title: Stayed during renovation
reviews.text: We stayed at the resort in September 2017.  This was a mistake as the property was under renovation.  We checked into a temporary lobby that generally is reserved for large groups.  Although this was fine, the walk to the hotel room was unbelievably long and inconvenient.  While we do not mind a little walk, this was really pretty crazy.  When we got to our room we noticed it was located in the area of the temporary make-shift spa (massages only).  So, the rooms around us were being utilized for spa treatments.  It was strange to walk through the temporary spa lobby area each and every time we went to our room.  The one pool that was open consisted of a very basic temporary pool near the tennis courts and workout area.  It was again a pretty good walk.  The workout area (I believe was only a temporary setup pending completion of renovation) was very small.  While the bar/restaurant was nice (large windows overlooking pool area which was under renovation), we found it to be a little stuffy and too formal - especially considering it was nearly vacant every time we visited.  We have no doubt when the renovations are complete this will be a great place to stay.  However, we soon regretted our decision to stay there during the renovation.  While the price was certainly competitive due to the renovations, it was nothing spectacular and in hindsight we should have chosen one of the many other nice resorts in the area.  However, this entire review is all prefaced on our stay during renovations (felt the hotel could have been more informative and upfront as to the drastic changes and limitations during renovation).  We do intend to return to the Phoenician when the renovations are all complete (maybe they are by now?).

reviews.author: Tiffany J
reviews.title: Beautifully Renovated and the improvements keep coming
reviews.text: Visited the hotel in early December. Absolutely beautiful indoor renovation. Modern and large standard rooms with a wonderful view of Camelback Mountain. Multi layer pool and outdoor area is beautiful and ALL of staff were extremely helpful and accommodating. I like that they pay attention to details here. First night I left my sunglasses out and reading glasses and they left me cleaning cloths by both of them. Also a makeup remover towel next to my makeup bag nightly. Its the little things that wow me. Located very close to the mountain, the mall, Old Town Scottsdale and more. Just a note that there is a $5 housekeeping charge per day, resort fee, and 14% gratuity for bell services even if you don't use them. Nice to know what to expect ahead of time.

reviews.author: Mnree7
reviews.title: Not my best visit to The Phoenician
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is beautiful, classy, and a hands down 5 star resort. This was my third stay there and I have to say it was my least favorite. One of the greatest features of this resort is their elaborate pool area... 3 levels of pools set to the backdrop of Camelback mountain. The huge amount of construction however, completely took away from the entire experience. The top pool had a restaurant being built all day... loud non stop drills and circular saws right next to where people are sitting in lounge chairs. Not at all relaxing. Then I moved all our things to the bottom pool for some peace and it turns out an entire building is being constructed next to it as well so you have the luxury of listening and watching cement mixers driving by, and beep beep beep as they are backing up, etc. I'm amazed they kept the place open during such a renovation. The middle pool is for adults only and probably the best bet, but I had my 3 year old daughter with me. It was very disappointing because the pool was the reason we came. Also, after receiving a sour mix filled $12 margarita, I asked the woman if she could have the bartender make it more like the one from the lobby bar instead of full of mixer. She came back and said the skinny margarita is what I was looking for and charged me the extra $ for that without even asking. Bad form for a hotel of this caliber.
     Relish is a nice hang out and good bet for food. It's right on the golf course and more laid back. Mowry & Cotton had great service but that's about it. Expensive mediocre food and Il Terazzo, the restaurant that was previously in this spot, was much better. 
     The outdoor patio on the main level of the hotel is amazing...excellent  service and a very relaxing environment to enjoy some drinks. The renovations are actually done in that part of the hotel and the results are stunning.
     If you are traveling with children, there are a few options for you especially if they are a little older. The splash pads could be for younger kids but that was closed for renovations. The water slide would probably be for 5 and above. I'm not sure how the kids club works but I believe it's extra. Kids under 5 need to be accompanied by an adult and when we stopped in to check it out the woman behind the couldn't have been less interested so my daughter and I looked around quietly and left. I think it's a good space though. There is also a nice sized playground near the tennis courts that is shaded. 
     While I was disappointed in this recent trip to Phoenician, it doesn't take away from how beautiful and amazing it is and I look forward to going back when the renovations are finished

reviews.author: Jamie D
reviews.title: Family thanksgiving gathering
reviews.text:
So the resort itself has a lot going for it. 
We stayed in the main building.  The rooms were nice and the service staff was great!  Well kept, turndown service provided, and just very friendly.

The views, some seemed to be great, mine overlooked the roof of the lower building so nothing spectacular.  Some had views of camelback and in the distance we overlooked Scottsdale so it was still decent

They were doing some renovations but nothing that bothered me or made it obstructive.

Pool, awesome!  Water slide, wish they had two for racing but the single slide, beat hotel slide that we’ve been to!  Warm water and fast!  The pool had four separate pools, hot tub and a bunch of seats.  Water was a good temp and very clean.  Bonus, pools open I believe 24 hours but staff is done around 6 pm

Night swims were fun for the kids

Why I dropped it a Star was the food. 

Room service, I ordered burger cooked medium well and it came rare, yuck and I really didn’t feel like waiting so we just left it, waste of food and it was also overly salty.

We had thanksgiving dinner at Mowry and Cotton and honestly, if I would have rated the resort based on this one event I would have given it a one.  Breakfast service, great, thanksgiving, we had a larger group, they put us off the side on our own and literally that’s how they treated us.  I pretty much cleared my own table...to say the least, but to be fair, the hotel and resort is better than the restaurant 

Anyhow, relish was solid, but probably more due to the service.  Michelle was awesome, overall burgers were good and she deserved the extra tip we gave her since she went out of her way.  She made relish great

Main bar and outdoor patio are nice.  We did not hit j&G but I’m sure that was good

Resort is overall great.  

Golf, the Rental clubs are nice, we hit the range which was nice.  Clothes were ridiculously priced, but it’s an upscale resort so I guess I get it.  Even at 40 percent off, under armor polo was 65 bucks?

Basketball courts could use some checking.  Two basketballs were low on air, but still playable.  Little kids park next to it.  Kids draw on the court so if your playing one on one or pickup game, chalk makes court kinda slick.  But it’s not a main feature so  no issues here in my opinion 

Trapeze looked cool and tennis seemed to be huge here.  Locals all taking lessons or playing along with guests.  They even have a tournament court.

Quick 15/20 money walk to start of camelback hike.  

Mall is fifteen minutes away

Lots of great restaurants nearby

Garage is tight so please pull all the way forward when parking.  We had large suburban, which easily fit but when two pickup trucks are parked and not fully pulled in and parked across from each other, it gets tight.

Also, know that there are two entrances to garage.  I wasn’t paying attention and I went out the other side and ended up at camelback/golf entrance.  No easy way to get back to main lobby so just drive back through garage otherwise your driving all the way around.  No charge for in and immediate out.

Anyhow Scottsdale rocks 

Resort was great and when fully renovated I’m sure it’ll be even better

reviews.author: PalmerBob
reviews.title: Dismal renovation:  end of an era
reviews.text: The Phoenician was a luxury resort of the first rank, the absolute top of high-end properties in the Valley.  Now it will be a golf club with several sports bars scattered around it.  First Mary Elaine's became a steakhouse, then Windows on the Green became a burger bar, then the ice cream shop was given a thorough quality-reduction (now it's a grab and go convenience store), now afternoon tea is being shoved into a corner while the Terrace restaurant becomes a fast casual cafe and the beautiful brunches and buffets there will be sharply cut back (Thanksgiving buffet was served in the gloomy steakhouse space to a much, much smaller audience than before), and the beautiful lobby has been ripped up to plop down a large bar with big screen TVs all tuned to sports.  And their building a bar and grill outside by the pool, while the classic mother of pearl pool is being surrounded by dozens more pool chairs to make sure it's as noisy and overcrowded as possible.  Charles Keating must be turning over in his grave.

reviews.author: gablegirl
reviews.title: Huge resort hotel which is just not for us.
reviews.text:
We stayed for a wedding and had never been to Scottsdale before. 
The hotel has undergone a massive renovation.
For me, to walk through the front doors and see 2 huge screens showing sport in the bar that you see immediately on entry suggested this was not going to be my type of hotel.
Look at the website photo (even though it is a CGI) and you can see the left one immediately - but it's black in the photo whereas when you walk in the hotel there are 2 and they are both on!!
Way too big for me - levels and levels of pools and all lovely but busy! 
The rooms are very nicely appointed and bathrooms well appointed but what is it that there is no hand shower in the bath????????? Not only can't you wash or rinse your hair but you can't rinse the bath either!!
The little market shop was great for coffee and a snack. 
The pool restaurant was shut. The spa was shut. Both being renovated - sure will be beautiful when re opened.
The food at Mowry and Cotton was good.
The food at J and G Steakhouse was good also and the view beautiful from the terrace.
The wedding was beautiful. 
Would we stay in Scottsdale again - no. But then I prefer a beach or scenery.
Hotel very nice - not for me.

reviews.author: PaddingtonLeigh
reviews.title: Great service and beautiful resort
reviews.text: The service at The Phoenician is amazing - from the car and luggage valets to the waiters and everyone in between.  They seem to genuinely want to help and are friendly - not fake or pretentious.  Our room was beautiful - very luxurious bathroom, comfortable bed and a great view from our balcony.  The current workout room is small, but they are building a huge new facility that will house a new workout room.  Breakfast at Cotton and Rye was tasty and we had prompt friendly service which was much appreciated before having to catch a flight.  They even have a resident hawk and handler as a natural means to scare away the annoying black birds that would otherwise be all over the place.  We will definitely return to this resort and will hopefully have more time to spend on our next trip.

reviews.author: Caesar15
reviews.title: Excellent Stay
reviews.text:
This was my second time staying at the Phoenecian. After previously visiting a few years ago and having a great stay with my husband, we returned over Thanksgiving weekend, 2017 with our 5 year old daughter. The resort is gorgeous. We stayed in a deluxe king room, which was very spacious and tastefully decorated with a nice private patio. 

There was so much for us to do with our daughter at the Phoenician--swimming, splash pad, basketball, trapeze lessons, playground, princess tea party, cookie decorating, arts and crafts, and it is a short walk to hiking at camelback mountain.  This is a luxurious resort with plenty to offer whether you are looking for an adult get away or a family vacation.  

The staff is really top notch--very friendly and helpful and responded super quickly to every request.

reviews.author: bobobull56
reviews.title: Great New Restaurant - Mowry & Cotton
reviews.text: Yummy new restaurant in Phoenician!  We went early and stayed quite long. (By the way, I do not think the pictures on internet do the restaurant justice.)  The gorgeous wood ceilings and rustic touches blend nicely with modern furniture.  There is indoor and outdoor dining - all near the pool area.  We dined indoors.  Luis was our server and he presented the new style menu explaining every detail.  Rest of staff was most accommodating.  The food is meant to be shared.  We got the chopped salad, country sourdough bread, crispy potatoes, roasted squash, wild mushroom flatbread, and the smoked spare ribs.  Food was outstanding and beyond.  Every dish was superior.  We were most impressed with the cocktails, too.  The desserts were lemon pie and smores.  While I must admit I didn't indulge in the sweets - those that ate the desserts loved the desserts.  Will return again for sure.

reviews.author: Anniecramm
reviews.title: Luxurious Massage Experience
reviews.text: The Phoenician is a beautiful resort with friendly staff in every department. I especially enjoy the spa treatments which are always first class. A lavender scrub and massage by Sara is one of the highlights of my visits. Treat yourself....often!!

reviews.author: Exploration735341
reviews.title: High tea a must
reviews.text:
If you are in Scottsdale do not miss this experience. Upgrade to the champagne high tea and the best 2 hours you will ever have
Great staff(ask for Wanda). The assortment of teas was interesting and sandwiches scones and pastries were delicious.

reviews.author: stunt101
reviews.title: Perfect, Personal and Top Notch Service
reviews.text:
We stayed at The Phoenician for 5 nights in October. We got in really late due to a delayed flight. We arrived at the hotel, after midnight - greeted with a smile and a level of professionalism, not sure you would expect at 1 in the morning.

Check in was very smooth. Our room was on the 4th floor, in the main building. The room had a great view overlooking the pool area and the rest of the resort. It's beautiful at night with all the lights. The room it self is large and spacious - which is expected for a high quality resort. Comfortable bed - every night was a deep sleep. Large bathroom, and nice sitting room. Room was always kept clean and loved the turn down service at the end of the night. Room has a well stocked mini bar, snacks and drinks for purchase.

During our stay at the hotel, we received quality service across the hotel - we got recommendations from Josh (the pool manager?) on places to eat and things to see in the city - awesome recommendations, including the mission. Lots of advice and direction from Paige at the concierge. Paige helped book a hot air balloon ride for us, provide recommendations for our day trip to Sedona, and made reservations at J&G Stakehouse. Every member of the staff we met was polite, professional and provided great service.

The resort is huge, don't think we walked the entire resort, there was just so much of it. The resort is beautiful, just went through a huge renovation. The place is quite peaceful, we enjoyed a couple of days just relaxing by the pool, reading books and enjoying pool side drinks. I believe there are 3 pools, one was for adults only, and the other 2 were for all ages. The pool was never crowded, unlike some of the other resorts we read about, we didn't have to get up first thing in the morning to hold chairs, like some of these other resorts which pack them in... In terms of dinning we ate at J&G, Mowry & Cotton, Relish Burger, Kalio Kabobery and the Marketplace - all of the meals at these restaurants were amazing. My wife has a dairy allergy and every place was able to accommodate or make adjustments. 

We enjoyed room service, twice during our stay - once for dinner and once for an early morning breakfast on the balcony. Recommend enjoying your breakfast on the balcony.

This was a very relaxing, and enjoyable stay. The resort met all our expectations, we enjoyed our selves, and wish we had more time. We didn't get a chance to try the spa, afternoon tea or go to the cactus garden or climb the camel back mountain - all which were on our list.

The resort fee gives you access to wifi, fitness room, bikes and a tennis court, and morning yoga class. Great coverage on the wifi, and I enjoyed the chrome cast feature on the tv.

Special shout out to Denise, for assisting us with our reservation. This resort is top notch and we recommend it.

reviews.author: barnsandnobility
reviews.title: 5 star all the way
reviews.text: Wonderful afternoon tea.  Wanda made it outstanding.  And thank you James, what an awesome attitude. Food was wonderful and the views WOW, what an amazing property and staff. Will go again and again...LOVE

reviews.author: Guy L
reviews.title: Forget relaxing by the pools and they charge for Wi-Fi
reviews.text:
We arrived in the evening having flown in from the UK. When we checked in it was dark but first impressions were good. Prestigious and well appointed lobby with an inviting bar area. The guy who checked us in said we had been upgraded. I should have trusted my instincts and made specific enquiries about our booked room and it’s location and the “upgraded” casita. The casita was away from the main hotel below the pool complex.

The room itself was fine and again well appointed. Ridiculously in 2017 this hotel still clearly thinks it makes commercial sense to charge guests for Wi-Fi. It cost $12.50 to use the slower of the two options. This is the US of A for crying out loud, it’s supposed to be a leading developed economy and this hotel still thinks it’s right to charge for Wi-Fi. Go to Hoi-An in Vietnam and there is free high speed wi-Fi in the hotels and in the taxis!

We were woken up at 7am by an angle grinder /drill right outside our balcony. Two workmen had started working on a water feature alongside our casita block. It got worse because across the lawn there was a full blown construction site with workmen, saws, grinders, plant etc. Working on the construction of a new gym complex.  At that point we thought we’d ring reception and look to change our room (3 hours later and they had still not returned our enquiry and yet the website was showing vacancies for that night). 

Whilst waiting (as it turned out in vain) to hear about the room change we went up for breakfast just above the pool area. We were then met by yet more builders and workmen who were working on a children’s play area and a new pool bar restaurant. The time was now 7:45am. At breakfast at times you couldn’t even hear the background music because the sound of drills and circular saws drowned it out.

So far that was 4 construction areas near our room: the gym, the water feature, the children’s play area and the new pool bar/restaurant. Things weren’t looking good for a relaxing day by the pool but there was a lower pool area that we had yet to look at.

After the breakfast shared with 20 workmen and their tools, we took a walk to look over the rest of the hotel. Lo and behold there was yet another huge construction project complete with an operating JCB digger 30 yards from the adults only lower pool. 

We went backed to the room and checked straight out. No one from the front desk or management was in the slightest bit apologetic for our experience. Their website fails to disclose that there are significant construction works with attendant noise in progress. The gym construction has only just started and the building by the lower pool has at least another two to three months to go.

Awful experience and inexcusable failure by the hotel to disclose the ongoing construction.

reviews.author: PinkShoesandPearls
reviews.title: Beautiful Hotel, Excellent Service
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful with a wonderful lobby bar and outdoor area that was most enjoyable during our October visit. We enjoyed the indoor and outdoor area in the afternoon and evening and the service in both places was exceptional. The restaurant was also very good with equally good service. The accomodations were nicely appointed and had nice balconies. The sun does come up early on the balcony so if that is important to you - make a note of it. There are three pool areas and an adult pool with more than adequate space, pool staff and wait staff. The weather was perfect. The Spa is under construction so if that is an issue it will not be complete until February. It does have a small facility in the main hotel, but the fitness center is not as easily accessible. That was the only inconvenience we experienced.

reviews.author: John H
reviews.title: Lovely Grounds, Spacious Pools
reviews.text: The hotel grounds are lovely, with sprawling lawns and extensive pathways. In fact, the hotel backs up to Camelback Mountain, making it an ideal place to stay if hiking the famed peak is your goal. To be fair, it's an older property, and the furniture is a dated, but it's well maintained, and the staff is very friendly. If you have kids, they'll love the pools and waterslide, and if you're traveling as a couple, there's plenty of serenity to be found as well.

reviews.author: Misty S
reviews.title: Afternoon tea changed, and not for the better
reviews.text: We are regulars at the Afternoon Tea, and we are not impressed with the changes that have now taken place. There is no longer the glorious chandelier or water fountain when you first walk into the hotel, but that's a different story. Just recently we went in for tea after the renovation and everything was different. Before the renovation, the afternoon tea was ideal.
