reviews.text: our timeshare is just down the road, "scottsdale camelback resort". my friend and i walked here for dinner as the fellows were at a hockey game. love this resort, we walk through it the 2 weeks we're in town on holidays. i buy coffee and treats for my family at the 19th hole, during the week. my friend and i shared a veggie pizza and a creme brûlée dessert. the wine was delicious as was the food. we had a seat looking out towards the rising moon. busy deck, fireplace on next to us, fun chattering of families all around us. music drifted out from inside. the previous week my husband and i had been here for drinks, and a lemon torta to die for. would have had a second drink but our server never returned! the second time the service was excellent. a terrific spot for an eve pastime.

reviews.author: A K
reviews.title: Everything was Awesome!
reviews.text: This place is spectacular.  Stayed 6 days for business incentive trip.  Everything from service to good to our room was too notch.  We spent most of our time by the pool, specifically the bar calls Surge.  Chris and Car took fantastic care of all of our good and beverage needs.  Banquet facilities were first rate.  I have stayed at many resorts all over the US and this is one of the best.

reviews.author: Monadsk
reviews.title: Still the one☀️
reviews.text:
I first came to the Phoenician in 1991 and it was heaven on earth. We've been back a few times over the years and have stayed at other Scottsdale resorts. The Phoenician was, is and always will be one of my favorite resorts anywhere!
For my birthday, my husband planned a surprise stay there and surprised me even more when my bi-coastal sons, daughter-in-law and girlfriend came!
Room was a little dated and being spring break/training you had to be at pool(s) 6:30 am to get lounge chairs and even then, VERY few were available. But the resort and property are still the one!! The grounds are gorgeous! We ate at Il Terazzo and it was lovely. So many beautiful memories!!!

reviews.author: Jeremy W
reviews.title: Fun Easter and great facility
reviews.text:
We enjoyed our stay and the resort offers tons of activities.  The food was good, not great, but the staff was very attentive and responsive with requests.  We had a casita room with patio and fire pit which was awesome.  My only complaint was the lack of pool chairs.  They have a no reserve rule but it appeared many people would come early and then disappear for hours.  The facility does not have enough chairs or space around the pools for the amount of guests in the hotel. 

Overall had a great stay and the location is perfect.

reviews.author: crazypinklizard
reviews.title: Pick a Casita!
reviews.text: The casita's are quite a walk from the main hotel, but you can call concierge and they will pick you up in a golf cart.  I loved our casita.  big rooms, huge balcony with table and chairs, comfy beds.  enormous resort pool with water basketball and water volleyball.  Plenty of pool side chairs.  Staff will take your food or drink order at the pool.  Be sure to visit the cactus garden.

reviews.author: travelsaurus
reviews.title: Smoking Paradise
reviews.text:
We stayed in a wonderful Casita room looking at Camelback mountain, Necklace Lake, and the pool.  We looked forward to spending plenty of time on our spacious balcony during our down time from Spring Training games.  Too bad we couldn’t use it.  Too bad we had to keep the sliding glass door to the balcony closed, so we were unable to enjoy the beautiful weather, and were captive in our room.  Next door to us, with an adjoining balcony, was a chain smoker we called Count Smokula.  

Beginning at 6:00 a.m., and continuing late into the night, dude and his wife smoked (and coughed).  Nothing like waking up at 6:00 in the morning because your room has filled with your neighbor’s cigarette smoke.  From then on we had to keep to sliding glass door to the balcony closed, and could not enjoy fresh air. It’s hard to enjoy a cup of coffee and the paper on a beautiful sunny morning on your balcony when you are subjected to billows of cigarette smoke.  Good lord, this isn’t the 60’s.  

We complained to management, but the resort allows smoking on patios and balconies, so we had the pleasure of spending $600+ each night for a room that had an unusable balcony and for which we had to keep the door to the balcony closed.

If you are a smoker, this is your place.  For the rest of us—AVOID.  This policy is so out of whack with every other USA resort we have been to.  It was shocking to hear the room service waiter and front desk apologize, and blame the problem on the resort ownership.

I could cite chapter and verse about the health risk of second hand smoke.  I would happily have accepted that risk, if I just could have enjoyed my $600+ per day room and balcony, but all that smoke was just disgusting.  Pretty much ruined our experience there.

Resorts we visit from Hawaii, to California, and throughout the USA have nonsmoking policies under which there are designated smoking areas away from rooms.  But not the Phoenician.  

There are lots of great resorts in Scottsdale.  This one won’t be one we visit again.  Shame on the Phoenician ownership for having such a ridiculous policy.  At the very least, they should make this policy more prominent so that nonsmokers can know what they are getting into before making a reservation.

reviews.author: Erin G
reviews.title: Wonderful Gorgeous Resort
reviews.text: I went here with my family for spring break and, even though it was spring break, we did not feel super crowded or anything. It was a very peaceful resort with plenty of room and gorgeous views, not to mention great service and food. I would come back here every year. Best place to stay in Phoenix.

reviews.author: Sara F
reviews.title: A disappointing stay.
reviews.text:
My husband and I just returned from a 4-night stay at The Phoenician. We planned this short trip as a "babymoon" of sorts (with Zika killing our initial dreams of Caribbean/Mexico) and were hoping for a luxurious, relaxing little vacation at a resort with excellent service. We knew we were traveling during spring break (an unavoidable reality given our own schedules), but since the hotel's website boasted an "adults only" swimming pool, we thought we could still have a relaxing environment despite a busy family travel season. 

First, the good things -- the service at the pool and in the restaurants was excellent. A really amazing pool attendant named Brian helped us find a chair each day. Had it not been for Brian and the other attendants, our trip would have been abysmal. All we wanted was to lay by a pool with drinks in our hands (mine virgin, of course) and in that sense -- once we were able to get a chair -- The Phoenician did not disappoint. (Excellent virgin cocktails by the way!) The servers at the restaurants were also very friendly, and the grounds are well maintained.  It is a beautiful place to stay. 

The bad -- we arrived at the hotel Wednesday night around 8 (10pm our time). We were extremely disappointed that our Casita room -- what we thought would be a nice upgrade from a standard room -- was located offsite from the main building and overlooked a parking lot. It did not justify the inflated price. We spoke to the front desk about a different room, and they were able to move us to a more private room overlooking the cactus garden (very lovely). They told us they would move our bags to the new room, but when we arrived at the new room after dinner, our bags were not there.  

Mistakes happen -- we understand that. But this introduction to The Phoenician troubled us for several reasons: (1) it took over an hour for the staff to admit to us the bags were even lost -- until then, they were blatantly lying to us by repeating that the bags were "in transit"; (2) the staff didn't listen to us the first time when we said we believed the bags were in another room (when my husband called to move the bags, not knowing our new room number, guest services told him they were going to another room) -- it was not until we had been calling at regular intervals for over an hour that they bothered to look at the most natural location; (3) had we not called repeatedly, suggested where to look for the bags, and asked if they were lost, I am quite confident we would not have received our bags that night at all; and (4) we essentially had to ask the staff for an apology over this incident -- no one contacted us the next day to apologize or see how they could make our stay any better. I am happy we eventually received our bags that night (at 12:15am local time), but for a facility that prides itself on being a luxury resort, we were incredibly disappointed with how this situation was handled. Maybe if this happened in the middle of the day, or maybe if I wasn't 6 months pregnant and had been traveling all day, we would feel differently... but it was an extremely stressful, frustrating start to what was supposed to be a relaxing vacation.

We tried to make the best of the rest our stay.  Ultimately, the place was not for us.  To get a chair by one of the three pool areas, you needed to be there by 8am, or earlier. We learned this the hard way the first day. Since relaxing by the pool was our main goal, we felt like we had to compromise on other things, like not setting an alarm or doing a morning activity like hiking or other exercise.  And the pool areas itself were disappointing because the promise of an "adults only" pool area -- a main reason I justified this hotel selection -- did not exist. It did, in theory, but it was not enforced at all. So every pool area was full of children (it was spring break after all), and there was nothing relaxing about the pool environment. 

In the end, while The Phoenician certainly has beautiful grounds and many nice amenities, it did not provide us with the luxurious, relaxing vacation we have enjoyed in other locations and were hoping to have for this vacation. Given the way our experience from our first night was handled, the "blood sport" competition to get a pool chair each day, and the failed promise of an adults-only pool area, we would not return. They clearly put a lot of effort into making this a family-oriented place, and I respect that. But I certainly do not feel like they catered at all to couples. Even when we do vacation with our children in the years to come, I can't see myself coming to a place that has little semblance of relaxation.

reviews.author: Lynn Z
reviews.title: No room available?
reviews.text: I arrived here at 6:00 pm after a long day of travel from the east coast for them to tell us our room is not available and they don't know when it will be. They offered me a free appetizer. Really?  This is a room that I booked and paid for 6 months ago. Truly spring break gone bad.

reviews.author: Andrea T
reviews.title: True Luxury
reviews.text: This first class hotel has old world charm. Outstanding service and beautiful facilities. There is a fee for the bellman that is charged to each room along with a maid service fee. There is turn down service and nice room amenities including slippers, and lip balm. It is very dry here so that comes in handy, There is a wonderful spa and a beautiful pool.

reviews.author: Phoenix051
reviews.title: Aging a bit, but still great for families.
reviews.text: We reserved 2 Casitas which appeared to have last been renovated in the 1980's. They actually had acoustic tile ceiling in the entryway! Regardless, the resort is beautiful and there are many activities for kids. I golfed on the Desert Course and had a great time. The staff are courteous and attentive. Prices for everything are sky high, so be prepared for sticker shock. Good, but not great...

reviews.author: MorgRansom
reviews.title: Excellent service!!
reviews.text: We loved the resort. It was incredibly comfortable and the staff was great. The spa is wonderful. We each had a facial and hot stone massage and they were both top notch. The pools are fantastic and you can't beat the view of Camelback!! We will definitely be back!!

reviews.author: Alicia
reviews.title: First class hotel, amenities and staff!
reviews.text: This hotel is top notch. My room was amazing! While it was not recently refreshed, the room was immaculate and the furnishing and bedding were top notch!  Bathroom was large with separate soaking tub and shower with great water pressure.  Every member of staff I came into contact with was genuine, friendly, but not too over the top.  This is a first class establishment!

reviews.author: Vickie J
reviews.title: We love the Phoenician
reviews.text: We got married at the Phoenician 22 years ago. It is just as beautiful now as it was then. We go there for dinner anytime we get a chance. The grounds are so well manicured and it is just a beautiful, restful place. We also had a family reunion there with our family. The kids had a blast in the extremely large pools and the waterfall area. I give it a thumbs up all day long. One of the best in the City. We have also used it for conferences for our business, very accommodating, never have had one problem. EXCELLENT!

reviews.author: Diane P
reviews.title: Fantastic Property in Scottsdale
reviews.text: We had been to the Phoenician many times several years ago and really enjoyed it but hadn't been back to Arizona in a while.  A last minute spring break trip with our son prompted our decision to go back to this property.  It was just as fantastic as we remembered it.  The resort is set at the base of Camelback Mountain which makes for a very serene and beautiful setting, featuring the natural landscape with beautiful flowers, plantings, and cactus.  Everything is top notch at this property. There are lovely pools, a superior tennis facility, a beautiful golf course featuring 3, 9 holes courses, several restaurants all serving high quality food, a great spa, and gym.  The rooms are nice sized and attractively furnished.  It must be noted that with new ownership in place, the hotel plans on renovating all the rooms starting May 2016.  While they are certainly in very nice condition now I can only imagine how beautiful they will be when completed.  I think there are also plans to close the resort in the summer for some other renovations in some of the public areas so you should check this out before going.  I can't wait to go back!!!

reviews.author: Sandyteachabc
reviews.title: Spa
reviews.text: Phenomenal, professional, and a wonderful experience. My esthetician was very knowledgable. Loved the entire experience and would return in a heartbeat. I'd choose this location before returning to any other. I made a full day of the experience by using the gym, steam room, and enjoying a meditation class.

reviews.author: Doug L
reviews.title: 1st Day
reviews.text:
When we got to our room "most" of our bags had been delivered.  All had been loaded on the cart when we arrived but one wasn't in the room.  They found it but that and difficulty connecting to wifi has not started the stay as expected.  

The rooms and the view are wonderful.  I'll update the review at the end of my stay.

reviews.author: Charles B
reviews.title: Delightful vsit
reviews.text: A great place to redeem Starwood points.  We used them for a delightful long weekend.  It was nicer than we remembered.  We ate and golfed on the premises and fund all amenities to be outstanding.  The golf course was impeccable. The flyng trapeze brought back memories of Club Med.  This would be a great place for a family vacation or couples.  The location is very convenient to old town Scottsdale.

reviews.author: JT
reviews.title: Not a five star resort
reviews.text: This was our second time here in 3 years ,,the property is looking dated the rooms were clean but the couch in the room was dirty and very worn out ,the grounds were well kept but this is a very large property and it has numerous pools ,we enjoyed the pool with the mother of pearl tiles ,it was a bit quieter,,the one big negative for us was the food on property,,it's totally overpriced and was overall horrible,,16 dollars for a tuna sandwich ,oops I forgot you get a bag of chips to go with that,,lol,, we don't mind paying for a nice meal but this resort is over the top with pricing ,and the quality of the food was frankly a joke ,love coming to Scottsdale but ,will not return to this resort,

reviews.author: Susanloveshotels
reviews.title: There's a pool for everyone, the rooms and food are great.
reviews.text:
We came here for an overnight staycation with 2 teenaged boys. I found reasons to walk back and forth to the room (the hallway is partially outside) just to take in the views. The room was very spacious, well appointed, and quiet. The carpet needed repair, to be fair to readers here. I had read other reviews stating their rooms needed updating and repairs, and to be honest, our room seemed to have been updated but the carpet forgotten.

As a family, we tend to stay away from louder pool scenes, so we went to the bottom pool. (There are 3 or 4 to choose from.)  

Poolside food and drinks are adequate but I would say not to waste your money on a poolside cocktail since the alcohol content is negligent.

When it comes to food at The Phoenician, brunch really shines. Everything was just fantastic.

There are some great summer rates, and the self parking is convenient.

reviews.author: Mi
reviews.title: Another glorious week of relaxation at a fabulous Hotel in a fabulous City!
reviews.text: I have visited The Phoenician on many occasions on my holiday trips from the UK. It is a simply outstanding Hotel, with outstanding rooms, restaurants and facilities with second to none Customer Service!

reviews.author: Sarah F
reviews.title: Afternoon Tea is the Best!
reviews.text: We have not stayed here as hotel guests, but every year we go to Scottsdale for spring training, we absolutely make sure to make a stop at The Phoenician for afternoon tea. A lovely experience in a gorgeous setting with armchairs, couches and a beautiful view. The food and drink are outstanding, but the real gem here is their staff. Every single person who has served us has been so polite and hospitable. In particular, we love Wanda. She is an angel! So friendly, knowledgeable and she remembers us even if we haven't been there for a year at a time. She's such an asset and deserves great praise. We will be back next year and every year!

reviews.author: activenretired
reviews.title: Not worth the money for us
reviews.text: Don't get me wrong, the resort is beautiful, with a lot of different kinds of accommodations.  The staff is very friendly and helpful.  But you pay a lot of money for a "deluxe" King room, which is just average in size with just a mini bar and a big bathroom.  Plus the resort fee, plus tax, plus TWELVE DOLLARS a day to park your car (valet parking is $29, I believe).  Then on the night of a special event, half the garage is roped off for extra valet parking so good luck finding yourself a space.  This is a ridiculous add-on for hotel guests.  In addition, the exit gate didn't work right half the time.  There are so many other beautiful places close by that I could not recommend this place unless someone else is paying for you.

reviews.author: Alice M
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Surge Sign Has To Go
reviews.text: The Phoenician is such a beautiful resort with unbelievable service; however, the Surge sign needs to be taken down. My family and I have been staying at the Phoenician for over 20 years, and we were mortified to see that a tacky, light-up sign was placed above one of the pool bars, taking away from the most stunning view in all of Scottsdale. The sign continues to stay lit during sunset and through the evening, making it difficult to enjoy the scenery. While I was contemplating throwing a party at the J&G Sunset Room, I will be taking my party elsewhere, purely because of the sign. It is truly distasteful.

reviews.author: horsetastic
reviews.title: Stunning and timeless
reviews.text: This is the most amazing hotel in Phoenix and it was my first introduction to a TRUE luxury hotel as a child. I love to come back. I will never forget my little brother thinking the bidet was a water fountain OR the fun grand piano shaped pool. I love this hotel! Truly a cut above!!

reviews.author: Duanegwizdala
reviews.title: great resort
reviews.text: this is an absolutely beautiful resort with all the amenities you would want. Beautiful pool great restaurants wonderful staff impeccable service. if looking for a resort this is the one I would recommend. The rooms are clean and immaculate.

reviews.author: ExecutiveTraveler33
reviews.title: No Longer a Five Star Property
reviews.text:
1.  The Phoenician eliminated the weekend falcon program at sunset with NO NOTIFICATION to past guests with current reservations.  As late as yesterday, March 10, 2016, there was information on The Phoenician's website about the sunset falcon program on Friday and Saturday nights.  Our son looks forward to the falcon program every visit and we were shocked to learn that it had been discontinued when we inquired upon arrival about the start time for this evening.  Anyone who has stayed at the Phoenician understands that this is an essential part of the experience and that part of the charm is lost without the birds.

2.  While the guest policies clearly state "All guest rooms and public spaces are 100%  non-smoking," what the policy doesn't make clear is that the hotel defines public spaces as interior spaces only, which means that chain smoking of cigarettes on the patio lounge area is actively encouraged through the provision of ash trays.

3.  Lifetime Platinum SPG members, and other SPG members booking with points (regardless of the thousands of dollars in food, beverage and incidentals spent on property) are treated like second rate citizens.  Year after year, we are given the worst rooms and face multiple issues with the rooms we have booked.  My suggestion to SPG members is to spend your points elsewhere - for example, the Parker Palm Springs is a comparable property that welcomes SPG members using points and always pre-blocks repeat guests into upgraded rooms.

4.  While Starwood's Luxury Collection tries to compete with properties such as the Four Seasons, the Phoenician falls short in the area of service expectations.  I don't think it's too much to ask for the check-in agent to provide accurate information about the assigned room or for housekeeping to promptly provide a rollaway bed upon request, but these are common issues at The Phoenician that require multiple follow-up visits to the front desk and via phone to correct.

reviews.author: NYC2085
reviews.title: amazing desert oasis
reviews.text: greeted upon arrival, staff very attentive, beautiful pools great views of valley and camelback mtn. truly one of a kind resort. must eat at relish delicious burgers and great views of golf club and if you don't feel like walking you can be shuttled around buy little stretch golf carts. very fun resort

reviews.author: TennisgalGreenBay_WI
reviews.title: World Class Elegance
reviews.text: The some friends and I decided to have drinks at the Phoenician.  We parked our car in the underground parking and went up to 3rd floor.  We toured the place and found a seat outside on the patio.  Beautiful views and cozy couch with fire pit.  The waitress was informative and helpful with the drink menu.  There was a guy at the piano and a women singing, all gave a warm ambiance to the entire evening.  We will be back.

reviews.author: Bob T
reviews.title: Nice Hotel
reviews.text: Nice hotel. Beautiful grounds and surrounding area. Close to airport and local activities.  Very large grounds and feels a little like an event hotel with large ballrooms and eating areas. Felt crowded at the pool with the chairs right on top of each other but love the fact they don't let guests reserve seats.  I also feel they "nickel and dime" you too much on services.  Service staff was also very attentive and experienced.   Food good.

reviews.author: KatieGJD
reviews.title: Beautiful property but pricey food
reviews.text: In fairness, I stayed here less than 24 hours. The grounds were beautiful (it was so cool to sit at the pool and look at the mountain in the background).  The hotel did a great job with my husband's conference and the social events for the conference (food and service were great). That being said, while my husband's food could be expensed, mine could not and I didn't love paying $18 dollars for a very small breakfast and $18 dollars for poolside tacos. As much as I would love to bring our entire family here, those prices would definitely make me reconsider. I also was disappointed because we were given a room with two "oversized full-size beds". I didn't even know hotels offered less than queen-sized beds these days. Being accustomed to king size beds, the full sized bed seemed very small and out of place in a luxurious hotel. Despite the beds and expensive food, I would still come back to this property (but not with my always hungry twin boys given the cost of food) and would definitely recommend it.

reviews.author: IrishColleen2010
reviews.title: Second Stay Doesn't Disappoint (Much)
reviews.text: I had been to The Phoenician previously on business several years ago and thought it was excellent.  On that trip, I stayed in a casita that was truly lovely.  I was excited to return for another week on business. This time my room in the main building was not as nice; it overlooked the carport, and noise from the fountain was overwhelming when I opened the balcony door.  There was also a fair amount of noise throughout the night of foot traffic/ carts outside my door on the tile floors.  That said, the room itself was clean (if a little dated), nicely sized, with comfortable beds, a nice balcony and large functional bathroom. The hairdryer was sub-par for a hotel of this caliber. The grounds are absolutely gorgeous, and the staff was all incredibly friendly and customer-service oriented.  The pools are large and uncrowded, and the outdoor bar area off of the lobby offers a beautiful view (if only it stayed open a bit later). I'd still definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: antony359
reviews.title: Nice Property
reviews.text:
Nice property with efficient and well trained staff.

Good sized rooms approximately 600sf but expensive

Liked the JW Marriott a little better.

Both are great and you won't be disappointed in either

I found the JW Marriott just a step above

reviews.author: Heatherbelle73
reviews.title: Tea Time
reviews.text: The Phoenician offers a lovely tea package. Reservations are required, the servings are pretty unlimited.  The views are spectacular from anywhere in the seating area. I recommend it if you're looking for something fun to do in Scottsdale. There's a lot to do there, but this was well worth the price.

reviews.author: LoriBkyln
reviews.title: Luxury and excellent customer service
reviews.text:
This review is long overdue but I wanted to share how much my mom and I thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the Phoenician in Scottsdale Arizona over Labor Day weekend. We were impressed by the beauty of the resort. You would never know it was 27 years old since it maintained so well and we were even more impressed with the service. Everywhere we went, we were offered water and a smile.
 
The grounds are beautiful. There are plenty of pools and plenty of seating. The cushions are so thick they are like little mattresses. As soon as you pick a spot, attendants cover your chair, provide extra towels and a pitcher of ice water that is continually replenished as long as you remain by the pool. There is a cactus garden on site that you can get a tour of. It was amazing to see how many different types of cactus there are.
 
The beds in the room are super comfortable. The bathroom is luxurious with a double sink, tub and rain shower.
 
What stood out most was the excellent staff. The best example of the staff at its finest was in the Bellman Joe. He went above and beyond typical customer service to assist us and make our stay a wonderful one. 

The dining in the resort was excellent as well. The burgers at Relish are delicious as we discovered on the first day. The manager at the Thirsty Camel was incredibly accommodating. Relish closed early one another evening and we felt like turkey burgers. He made the effort to go get burgers from Relish for us, cook them up and his kitchen and have I served at the lounge.
 
The breakfast at Il Terrazzo was delicious. J&G steakhouse is as fantastic as you would expect a restaurant of the renowned Jean George to be.
 
If you are visiting Arizona and want to be pampered, this is the place to be.

reviews.author: michael_in_irvine
reviews.title: Here's what you need to know...
reviews.text:
* The hotel is located about 20 minutes from the airport so an easy, convenient taxi ride.
* The hotel is your classic Phoenix area country club property.  It has been around for a while, so the architecture looks somewhat dated.
* The property is very large and in addition to the golf course (I am not a golfer so cannot comment on how good the course is), it has many pools and play areas. 
* The lobby is large and comfortable to hang out in. In addition to the bar, there is plenty of space, inside and out, to just hang out and enjoy the beautiful desert views.
* There are a number of restaurants on the property so you can really do all of your meals onsite.
* The room was of average size.  While a little dated, it was very clean, and comfortable.
* The fitness center is about a 10 minute walk from the main hotel building, but it is well equipped and if you use the treadmills, they have a nice view of the mountain adjacent to the property.
* If you are looking for a vacation property in the Phoenix area, this hotel is a very good choice, although on the expensive end of the spectrum.

reviews.author: ChantalHickman
reviews.title: The pool is stunning.
reviews.text: Beautiful rooms and decor. The oyster shell pool is not to be missed. Grab a cabana if you can. Also make sure to get afternoon-tea. The food in every restaurant was wonderful. A quiet respite in a beautiful oasis.

reviews.author: Aag411
reviews.title: One of my favorites
reviews.text: I have stayed in quiet a few hotels and this has to be one of my favorites. We stayed in one of the house type rooms down below by the pools and it was such a great spot because you can go golfing on an amazing course the pools are great with the cabanas. also the restaurant on the top floor is very good. It creates a very good feeling while on the resort very comfortable and relaxing. it is a very luxurious place to stay and I go back as much as I possibly can!

reviews.author: Donna A
reviews.title: Beautiful property
reviews.text: I attended a conference at this resort.  The facilities and grounds are beautiful; the rooms were comfortable and quiet; the staff was very pleasant and attentive.  The shops that I visited were great, too -- interesting things to shop for.  The concierge was also very helpful, even after I left when I requested them to look for something.

reviews.author: MaggieGosia
reviews.title: All in one resort!
reviews.text: This resort definitely qualifies as luxurious. I managed a 3 day retreat for my company and everyone was raving about the property, food and the very dedicated and professional staff. The grounds are immaculate, hotel is beautiful and well maintained. The resort offers so much that you never need to leave the grounds, feels almost like a Caribbean resort minus the all inclusive price. I would recommend the property if you want to treat yourself, definitely not for someone on a budget.

reviews.author: Lili L
reviews.title: Beautiful luxurious hotel
reviews.text:
Spectacular!
I wish I could spend more time here. Very nice and big hotel. Beautiful decor. Very comfortable large bed. The design is a bit outdated but I like it a lot. There's a cactus garden, big swimming pool, beautiful golf course, and spa.

reviews.author: Steven K
reviews.title: The Canyon Suites provides unmatched service and luxury
reviews.text:
Our trip nearly didn't happen, as our booking was done thru Expedia, and the night before our departure, we learned that the resort did not have our reservation. But Justin, the managing director, worked magic and all was worked out.(NOTE - confirm all expedia bookings with the hotel itself)
The resort is phenomenal, the service at the Canyon suites was remarkable, special shout out to Amanda for making our entire stay special.
The resort is set back next to Camel Back mountain, but very close to every area of interest you may wish to visit. While I'm sure you can find less expensive accommodations, you will be unable to find a higher quality stay

reviews.author: abkovacs
reviews.title: Valets need training
reviews.text: We arrived at the front of the hotel to inquire about about the restaurant as we did not have reservations.  My husband left the car running and went inside to check with the desk.  I was sitting in the car and a valet got into the car and commenced to pull the vehicle ahead to park it as our car was apparently blocking the traffic flow.  He did not introduce himself or say anything to me.  I was in total shock and asked him who he was and where he came from.  He just looked at me with a smirk on his face.  After parking the car, he got out without ever saying anything to me.  My husband had no idea what had transpired when he came out and told me they could accommodate us without reservations.  When I explained to him what had happened in his absence, he spoke with the valets when we came back from dinner.  One valet stated they were sorry but our car was blocking the flow of traffic.  They did not seem to recognize that an introduction and explanation should have been given before getting into our car with me in it.  We did enjoy a nice dinner despite the shocking beginning.  The evening was warm so we chose to eat outside where the view was spectacular.  We began our meal with a bottle of red wine and watched the aircraft landing in the distance.  The food was very good and service was excellent.  We felt the prices were a little high as most entrees were a la carte.  My husband and I shared a salad, which was a mixture of greens, apples, walnuts and blue cheese with a light dressing.  We thought it was excellent.  We both had the mahi mahi which was served with one piece of bok choy and no grain or potato.  There were items that could be ordered a la carte.  The warm rolls we had with our salad were enough of a starch for us both.  We shared the warm chocolate cake with a scoop of ice cream and coffee for dessert.

reviews.author: Anonymous A
reviews.title: Deceptive pricing and unannounced charges
reviews.text:
The Phoenician hotel is fine and provides a good service.  But our stay was marred by repeated disputes about deceptive charges.  Disputes used up a good chunk of our time that was supposed to be dedicated to long-deferred leisure.  Hotel customers should watch the following:
- "Green option" means no room cleaning.  We always agree to have linens changed less frequently, but the hotel should take out the trash and make the beds.  Not at the Phoenician!  You do your housecleaning.  If you ask for this service, they charge you.  We were told that we would get points for using the 'green option', but at checkout, we found that the points cost $5 per day!
- Free phonecalls??!  As platinum members, we were told that calls in the US would be free.  Hilton does this too, so it seemed reasonable.  We sometimes used the room phone rather than the cell phone.  But we got $700 worth of charges at 8.5 cents per minute!  It took hours of back and forth to get them removed.
- $28 porterage fee for carrying suitcases to your room.  We have not seen this in other hotels, and it was not announced in the rate they sent us.  More hours spent disputing.
- Being part of a group, we were allowed to stay until 8 pm to catch a flight.  After it was all agreed and settled, someone called our room and said that if we stayed one minute after 4 pm we would be changed $300! no half-day rates, either.  

This is a sought-after hotel, where there are many conferences. Predictably perhaps, the management will charge whatever they can.  If someone disputes fake charges, they may be eventually removed, after hours of hassle and repeated phone calls.  If not, it's their profit.  
Consider these issues before going, and get in writing what you will be charged for, ahead of time.

reviews.author: TONY614
reviews.title: Buffet from Heaven
reviews.text: Was in Phoenix for a family get together. We went to the Phoenician for brunch. The quality, abundance , and presentation were perfect. I recommend this to everyone   The grounds are a sight to behold. The entire day exuded class and a subtle elegance.

reviews.author: Billghorton
reviews.title: Luxury oasis nestled in the desert
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed here Valentine's Day weekend. The grounds are stunning! Spa is amazing, golf course is PGA quality and the tennis facility was beautiful. 

We took complimentary bikes for a ride and hiked camelback mountain before coming back to the spa for a good sweat in the sauna. 

The rooms were well appointed and the service was over the top! 

It's expensive but you get what you pay for.

reviews.author: siegeljm
reviews.title: Birthday weekend
reviews.text: I think I am pretty picky and critical when I travel, but from the moment we arrived at the Phoenician I was extremely impressed. The staff was friendly and helpful, going over and above what was expected. Our room was unexpectedly large. The bathroom was expansive and we used our balcony often. Pool staff was always helpful providing towels and finding chairs! The location of the hotel allowed us to walk to and hike the cholla trail up camelback mountain and dine out easily at some great restaurants. We also drove to ursery park and did some hiking there. We were not able to play golf or use the spa services because we didn't book ahead. That didn't diminish our weekend at all. We would return again and highly recommend the hotel as worth the price tag.

reviews.author: Michael M
reviews.title: Very Nice Resort
reviews.text: We stayed here in January for the WVU/ASU Bowl game.  The staff was friendly and helpful.  The grounds were very well kept.  The Christmas decorations were still up, which was a nice touch.  The only real downside was that drink and restaurant options were overly pricey, even for resort pricing.

reviews.author: Cara P
reviews.title: Small details let this hotel down
reviews.text:
When arriving The Phoenician looks like a great resort, with everything you need for an amazing stay - pools, bars, restaurants, golf courses, stunning views and even a cactus garden! However there are a number of small (but cumulative) issues with attention to detail that let it down. 

I'll start with the good:
1. Beautiful grounds, diverse restaurant options, huge pool area, cactus garden is lovely
2. Location - within walking distance to Scottsdale Fashion Mall (has Macy's, Barney's, Marcus & Neiman and Dillard's plus all the usual major clothing brands). Great view of Camelback Mountain and easy access to hiking.
3. Rooms are large, good for sharing with friends/colleagues as there are two basins, large room, two wardrobes etc. Nice balcony with lounge and chairs to relax in sunshine. The rooms aren't amazing/new but nice enough with great natural lighting
4. Wifi is good - strong and does not have a cap (I believe this is normally paid but was included in my business rate). There is free wifi in the lobby, also very strong.
5. The bathroom is huge, luxurious and had a separate bath and shower

It would have been a great stay if not for some minor issues that cumulatively let this hotel down:

1. Housekeeping are friendly however my room was across the hall from a housekeeping depot, where between 7:30am and 8am they would all congregate, sing, laugh and talk before a procession of no less than 5000 (Ok maybe a slight exaggeration) trolleys would be trundled past making it absolutely IMPOSSIBLE to sleep. This is particularly irksome when it's a Sunday morning and you have flown in from Australia the previous day, trying to get over jetlag prior to a conference. Not impressed.
2. My shower gel was never replenished until I called housekeeping to specifically ask for it.
3. I am a gold member but you would never have known it outside the obligatory welcome 'gift'. Given a terrible room (outside housekeeping) and when I requested late checkout I was told this was not available, yet found out later that some colleagues (who asked after me) were given an additional 2 hours despite having no status
4. The shower was really terrible, no pressure at all and it was also annoying that you had to be blasted by cold water when you turned it on. Perhaps that was specific to my room (the water pressure) but it was particularly annoying when trying to wash shampoo out of your hair. 
5. The concierge, while friendly enough told me it was not safe to walk to the mall, which was just very strange when it was completely safe! I find it odd that they try to discourage people from walking there and wonder if it is a ploy to get $ from hotel car service (that is what he tried to get me to do). 
6. One night stood at the bar for over 10 minutes and wasn't served. It was like the barman was deliberately ignoring our group (I promise we were not being rude/drunk!). They clearly needed more staff working and a lesson in customer service.
7. Lamps in the room are old and very difficult to switch on/off. I couldn't even get the bedside lamp to turn off so had to unplug it from the wall! 

Tips:

1. Walk to the mall! It's a lovely 15 minute walk and you can go via Chaparell and 68th street (residential) to avoid busy Camelback Way. 
2. In 'N' Out burger is 15 minutes away (car) and 5 Guys is at the Mall (5 minutes) if you like a good burger. Personally I preferred 5 Guys :)
3. Bring your hiking shoes and go for a hike up the mountain! 
4. At dusk the cactus garden has rabbits and hummingbirds - very tranquil. 

I would stay there again because of the location and because it is overall a nice hotel, but I do hope management places more focus on improving the finer details, which are letting them down currently.

reviews.author: joancodown2015
reviews.title: Golf Saturday 13th February
reviews.text: Beautiful scenery and well manicured course. However we were put off short tees and with 5 par threes course played very short. Also we were behind a 4ball group with 2 absolute beginners showing little regard for any semblance of golf etiquette.  Gentleman at the entrance was less than welcoming, so all in all while the rest of staff were very pleasant we felt we had poor value for money and not a great golfing experience.

reviews.author: J H
reviews.title: Outstanding customer service
reviews.text: Wonderful get away for a ladies golf group.  We played three days, pro shop was welcoming and accommodating to allow us to play different back to back 9 holes.  Desert course our favorite.  Good golf lessons before day two, pros very helpful and tips and tricks.  Spa was fabulous!!  Allow time to relax before and after your treatments.  Great selection of teas.  Room service good, asked for tray pick up time.  Steak House on 5th floor was a delight.  Outstanding culinary food, worth the $$$$ price.

reviews.author: Lucrecia11
reviews.title: Appalling customer service
reviews.text:
The concierge refused to call another SPG hotel that I had a reservation for the following day  to notify them that I would be checking in earlier.

The staff at the bar did not advise of "last call" and shrugged when we asked where we could get a drink

Front desk categorically refused a late check out (1pm instead of 12) out even when I said I would do my bets to leave on time. 

Room is old and AC dated and noisy. For all the hype about the Phoenician this was a very underwhelming customer service experience.

reviews.author: Mvmess
reviews.title: Phoenician Golf Great Experience!
reviews.text: We played all 27 holes of the Phoenician on a recent buddies golf trip. What a great experience! The nine hole layouts are very different and a test while being fair. The back-to-back Par threes on the Canyon course are spectacular. of all the course we played this was the most fun and a bargain as well!

reviews.author: Joanne M
reviews.title: A Spectacular and Unforgettable Vacation
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is by far the nicest hotel in Scottsdale.  The rooms were spacious and the views were spectacular.  The staff couldn't be friendlier and the food was delicious from the finest restaurants to the take out deli.  
Having lunch on the manicured golf course is a must and if you are lucky enough to play golf on the course, you will enjoy every hole.
Hope to return in the near future.

reviews.author: brhendri
reviews.title: High tea
reviews.text: On Thursday February 3rd my wife and I enjoyed high tea. We routinely enjoy this wonderful experience and our time with Wanda. She has made tea one of our favorite events at this fabulous resort.  She has an amazing memory and provides unbelievable service. She is a real asset to the hotel.

reviews.author: TECLWR
reviews.title: Quiet resort, Golf course is very well maintained
reviews.text: the location is quiet, a taxi ride away from everything which is fine.  Dining is good, golf course is fantastic. No nightlife to speak of, that requires grabbing a taxi but the choices in Scottsdale are good and nothing is too far

reviews.author: 606KennyG
reviews.title: Great resort
reviews.text: A great hotel with great staff. Clean rooms with nice beds and linens. Restaurants and bars are wonderful.  The grounds are immaculate and vast. Excellent tennis facilities and challenging golf courses. A true luxury property. Close to downtown Scottsdale and Camelback hiking.

reviews.author: S L
reviews.title: Canyon Suites Service Unparalleled
reviews.text:
We are speechless! No adjective to describe the unprecedented unparalleled service we received at the canyon suites! Their attention to details are so on point that it is almost scary! Huge thanks to their ambassadors, especially Alex and Jordan. They never missed a beat. Here are some examples. 1) We asked for a turn down therapeutic salt bath at 8 pm and our doorbell rang at 8 pm Exactly On The Dot! 2) Every time we asked for our car, Patrick , ( valet service) would Sprint to get it, our wait time is less than 5 mins.3) We mentioned a specific champagne that we really liked that we had tried the day before at the Hour of Joy, and the sommelier immediately went back to get another sample similar but different for us to taste. 4) We asked for additional toiletries that weren't in the room and Maria our housekeeper immediately brought them to us along with extra chocolate ! Now this is a first at any hotel...They even coiled our charger cords with plastic . I can go on and on but you get the point. 

The only thing we can think of to top this would be to offer a bit more variety for their refreshments.  If you read their website about The Hour of Joy, they list a whole bunch of variety of food.. Fruits, cheese, etc but in reality it did not meet up to their advertisement/slightly below expectations.  How about OJ or some juice in the morning? Their French Press coffee are to die for!

reviews.author: Cynthia F
reviews.title: High Tea is special
reviews.text: We went to High Tea while attending Spring Training in Scottsdale.  The setting is beautiful and the tea service is delicious.  Some of the patrons are a bit on the stuffy side, but the staff makes you feel right at home.  If you like High Tea, you definitely need to put this on your list while visiting Scottsdale!

reviews.author: Jett
reviews.title: Wonderful experience
reviews.text: Everything at this hotel was great. The customer service is excellent . The food is excellent . The rooms are spacious , comfortable and clean. Oh and the lip balm is so nice ! The views are nice with the mountains in the back ground. The pool is amazing. I will definitely be back.

reviews.author: JoC
reviews.title: Great Place
reviews.text: The hotel was fabulous. Went with my son and step son. We golfed every day, the staff were fantastic and accommodating at the golf course and the hotel. We had breakfast at the 19th hole, not in the main dining room. Our room was enormous, great for three guys over 6'2. The only very minor complaint was that they don't let you tee off on the third nine until after lunch so we golfed for four days and had to play the same two nines every day. There is a third nine. One bonus was that my 17 year old was free for golf. While this is not a cheap place, it was beautiful and felt it was good value for money spent. Lots of families there if you're looking for a family trip. Weather was cold but we made the most of it. We would definitely head back.

reviews.author: SuzKats
reviews.title: Always first rate!
reviews.text:
I have stayed here many times and it has yet to disappoint. It's pricey, but all worth it. The service is top rate. We had high tea this time and is was very fun and one of the best I've had.
Restaurants and pool are great too. Make sure if you are with someone that has limited mobility you tell them because it's a big property .

reviews.author: clarhilary
reviews.title: Most AMAZING Work-vacation!
reviews.text:
If you want a little slice of paradise while being treated like royalty, visit the Phoenician. I stayed in the Presidential Suite for a 3 day work function and it was absolutely FANTASTIC! The food was terrific (visited the steakhouse - best fish I've ever had) and the ambiance was perfect. I kept looking around in awe - the wine, the view - everything was just flawless. The pools were PERFECT (along with the giant hot tub you can swim around in)! I took a hike up Camelback mountain one morning and I recommend this to anyone and everyone. When you get to the top, you feel rejuvenated & the view is just to die for. 

I promise you, when you return from a vacation from The Phoenician, you will feel refreshed & rejuvenated. I can't WAIT to go back!

reviews.author: ActiveLuxury
reviews.title: Tennis and golf resort with great facilities and food
reviews.text: We stayed at the Phoenician for 4 days with 2 other couples and no kids. It was delightful and relaxing. Just what we hoped for. No real issues of any kind, but the rooms are a little dated, though large and very comfortable.

reviews.author: Terri F
reviews.title: Fabulous getaway
reviews.text: This was a lovely getaway in a beautiful setting with Camelback Mountain in the background.  The hotel is well-appointed and you really do not need to leave the resort.  Excellent dining choices, beautiful rooms,gorgeous mountain views.  There is a fabulous pool and world class golf with stunning mountain holes.  Staff are all top notch.  You can not go wrong with a stay at this resort.

reviews.author: JFu15
reviews.title: Sunday Brunch
reviews.text: It's always a treat to go to the Phoenician. The property is terrific and the Sunday brunch is delicious. I noticed the amount of items available was somewhat less than previously, quality and flavors are great.

reviews.author: Ron P
reviews.title: Exceeded our expectations
reviews.text: We hadn't been back to The Phoenician for about 10 years and were hoping it was as good of an experience as the first trip. The first trip we stayed in a suite, and the second trip we stayed in a deluxe king room. The grounds of the hotel are absolutely beautiful and the staff is very cordial and accommodating. We found Mora at the front desk to be excellent, helpful and warm. Mora became one of the better parts of our experience. We absolutely loved our time in the beautiful pools. We had dinner in Relish Burger one night and that was an excellent meal and experience. The hotel was spotless and the rooms although a little dated were more than fine. We are very much looking to go back.

reviews.author: Valerie O
reviews.title: A normal family resort
reviews.text:
This is not a luxurious resort though one might think it is based on the photos.

The grounds are well manicured but that's pretty much about it.

Location : great
Service: great in main building, extremely slow in the casitas
Food: good
Pools: too cold in the winter and no lap pools
Gym: ok
Spa: needs updating
Gold: good

reviews.author: Anna P
reviews.title: In a class of its own
reviews.text:
Our recent three-night stay at the Phoenician was wonderful.  We stayed in a casita.

The grounds and property itself are beautifully maintained.  Though it an older resort, you can tell that significant energy and resources have been devoted to keeping up the grounds and in updating the decor.  Those looking for a sleek, minimalist modern hotel will not find it here, but it is clear that it has been redecorated and maintained with care.

The resort offers multiple swimming pools, dining options, bars, a cactus garden, tennis, golf, a spa, and biking and running trails.  Though it was too cold to swim and we didn't have enough time to golf or play tennis, we enjoyed the remainder of the amenities.

The service is excellent, with friendly ad knowledgeable staff to help you at every turn.

Our casita was large, tastefully decorated, very clean, and had a huge and comfortable bed.  It was quiet and we slept well.  Parking was available right in front of our room.

Overall, our stay was fantastic and we would definitely return.

reviews.author: NickDC33
reviews.title: A terrific property -- treated us well
reviews.text:
Setting:
The Phoenician is one of (if not the) largest resorts I've ever stayed at.  You can easily spend 25 minutes navigating from one end of the property to the other.  It's located in a beautiful spot right under the mountains.  However, you are also only 5-10 minutes from a number of great restaurants in Scottsdale as well as shopping if that's your thing.

Service:
Everyone was terrifically nice in all interactions.  The hotel even went out of its way to make things feel special -- e.g., we were there on Halloween and they had a woman dressed as a witch giving out candy to children.  Really liked these little touches.

Amenities:
Multiple huge pools, nice hiking trails, great golf course, awesome gym.  They also have a cool show with a "Phoenix" (i.e., South American vulture) and other birds of prey that you can watch at sunset.  You can park for free in a convenient garage which is also a nice touch (there is valet if you are so inclined, to be clear).

Status Recognition:
I used one of my SPG Platinum suite nights on our stay and the room we were upgraded to was the nicest I've ever stayed in.  It had two balconies, which combined to be larger than some apartments I've lived in.  Huge living room and separate bedroom.  Really appreciated the value there and generally making me feel welcome.

Summary:
Loved staying here and would try to come back soon.

reviews.author: SimoneSmithson
reviews.title: the other were right, sadly outdated.....
reviews.text: My husband and i stayed here in December of 2015 for the Christmas Holidays and i can honestly say for the money spent (about 400.00 a night) this resort is truly in need of much updating and refresh.  I was a bit worried prior to booking because i had read so many reviews about how "out dated" this place would be but we decided to give it a try.  The views ..... Yes are absolutely stunning , Camelback mountain is right there in front of you , beautiful pools, beautiful landscaping..... but that is just the outside.  Inside (even the lobby) seemed to be very outdated......  I'm usually the picky one as i expect certain things when paying that much per night..... but after walking into the lobby even my husband looked over at me and said ,  wow this is a bit old looking..... lots of worn outdated chairs / fabrics,  carpet that looked like it was from the 80's, shiny marble floors that gave the place a dingy feel.  If we hadn't pre-payed i would have left and gone to another hotel.....    Again just a bit let down....  the room was the same way.   I just could not get my head wrapped around how dated everything was.....   Needless to say we spent most of our time outdoors to enjoy the beautiful scenery.  They gym which we frequently went to was not bad at all, a bit small but ok.  The hotel is just a short ride from old town so that definitely was a plus.   Overall not a great experience, much better places to choose in Scottsdale.  Next time i think we will try the Omni which looked very nice. Or perhaps the 4 Seasons.....

reviews.author: Ruth B
reviews.title: Classy & elegant
reviews.text: Recently stayed at the newly remodeled Canyon Suites at the Phoenician Resort.  This is a high-end property with a top-notch service level.  The Ambassadors at the Canyon Suites can take care of any request...they're just a phone call away.  And don't miss the on-site restaurants!  Wow, I was impressed with the Steakhouse, Il Terrazo, and Relish Burger bistro.  Every meal exceeded my expectations.

reviews.author: azwee1
reviews.title: High Tea
reviews.text: Having high tea at the Phoenician is a delightful afternoon in the beautiful city of Scottsdale Arizona.   You are greeted to a beautiful setting on the terrace of the gorgeous  Phoenician  Hotel. Wanda and Natalie make you feel comfortable immediately. The setting is beautiful the tables are elegant the three courses are delicious and the entire afternoon was spent so comfortably. The finger sandwiches start the delectable  service followed by scones that just melt in your mouth and finished with the most scrumptious desserts. I have been coming here with my family for over 20 years and I hope to continue for many more years to come.  It is a yearly trip that we just love and sometimes it's even more than once a year. Both Wanda and Natalie make you feel special. I will give this activity five stars it is something you should not miss if you are an afternoon tea person.

reviews.author: mifyanks
reviews.title: Outdated and Underwhelming
reviews.text:
I had a room in the main building so maybe other locations are better or updated but I was completely underwhelmed. My room felt like it was fresh out of the 80's. 

The large desk was attached to the wall by cords that were screwed in place, giving no freedom to move it. So if you wanted to watch TV while working, you were out of luck. The TV, was in an extremely large entertainment center that gave little flexibility on that end as well. Additionally, wallpaper was bubbling and peeling off the walls. Yes, these might be minor details but I would expect more from someplace billing itself as a "Luxury Collection" resort. The only thing that made the hotel feel like a luxury resort was the attentiveness of the staff, who made you feel welcomed and appreciated.

I was at the Phoenician for business so didn't get much of a chance to enjoy the resort aspect, so I can't offer a review of those facilities.

reviews.author: PamWestchester
reviews.title: Very disappointing
reviews.text: I was really surprised that this is considered a five star resort.  The rooms are nothing special. The beds are comfortable, but they don't make the beds well and the fitted sheets don't stay well on the bed. The service at breakfast was very slow and they got at least one order wrong every day of our six day stay. The rooms were very dusty. When comparing this to a Four Seasons or Ritz Carlton resort, it really doesn't compare at all.  The grounds are quite pretty, but the entire place needs a facelift.

reviews.author: briannareviews702
reviews.title: Mediocre & lacking the experience I used to get here
reviews.text:
Long time client to the Phoenician, over 12 years now actually. 

Check in was seamless, was told I was given an upgrade but in fact was downgraded to a suite overlooking a very noisy parking garage. I didn't complain as I didn't wish to be one of those people. 

The room was ok, in need of updating and more frequent maintenance. Light bulbs out, had to call & have them bring fridge key, shower leaked and had mold (ew). I again didn't complain as I had my puppy with me & didn't want to freak her out with people she didn't know. 
Bed was ok comfort wise, no complaints there. 
Maid service came to spruce up & didn't change the sheets when I specifically asked for them to be changed. Was a short trip, so again, I dealt with it. 

The gym  was well appointed and had what I needed for working out while traveling. Good they don't charge for it anymore as the resort fee should cover that. 

Upon checking out, we were told that the food/bev credit of 100 wouldn't be honored when that was the deal I booked through them directly. I asked to speak to a manager after pulling up proof on my phone & they fixed it but that shouldn't have happened. 

I stay at both Phoenician and canyon suites, I won't be back to Phoenician...might be time to test out another resort when in Scottsdale-sad to say it.

reviews.author: Brindsie
reviews.title: Wonderful Concierge Experience- Robert
reviews.text:
We have hosted our annual sales meeting at the Phoenician for years.  Always a great experience.  This year, Robert at the concierge desk went above and beyond.  He helped me out tremendously and provided exceptional customer service!

Thank you again, Robert!

reviews.author: Nabil C
reviews.title: stay of 9 days
reviews.text:
great hotel and resort, top class,  with 3 9 holes golf courses inside the resort, plenty of activities and swimming pools. Suggest you get a rate inclusive of breakfast if you can, although, if its over 100 US$ per person, its not worth it.
The resort is against the Camelback mountain and therefore has an amazing trail behind it for those enjoying that. i Highly advise it. Its also a great place to explore other areas.
highly recommend it.

reviews.author: mosthecat
reviews.title: Large resort right at Camelback
reviews.text: If you like small and intimate, look elsewhere.  This is a very large resort and grounds, with different levels of rooms and several pools (though we only we only found one hot tub on our recent cool weather stay).  We like both small and large hotels.  the benefits of these large places is a choice of restaurants, a gym, many swimming pools, and so on.  The gym is free (if you're paying the resort fee), and squeezes a lot into a smaller space.  Self-parking is free, and there are stacks of free newspapers in the morning by the concierge.  There are a few restaurants on-site, though there a lot of good restaurants in the area, and you should definitely check them out.  We tried Il Terrazo, the upscale Italian spot, on our first night.  It is a bit quiet and aims to be a fine dining establishment.  The food was OK, but that's all - and not cheap.  A small menu in the bar and lobby offers some good snacks.  The coffee and ice cream shop closes at 6pm, which is a shame, though each room comes with a K-cup coffee machine (we had to have ours replaced with one that worked).  You pay for views, and we had the lowest level, which, as the front desk person told us, "faces the integrity of the building".  In English, that means it faces the roof.  But, we also faced (very closely!) Camelback Mountain, which was great.  There's a short walk through a cactus garden on property, and grassy areas fro kids to play, as well as a spot popular with kids for feeding ducks.  Unless you plan on every meal on-site (don't), you'll need a car.

reviews.author: Dj112
reviews.title: Amazing Scottsdale Gem!
reviews.text: The Phoenician is an amazing experience in itself! From the great on property restaurant choices to the staff who make it feel that you're the only person at the resort!  The front desk staff are exceptionally nice and are there to satisfy your every need! The bell men are always there to call you a chauffeur, or in some cases drive you to where you need to go in one of the resort's beautiful luxurious Infiniti SUVs! The rooms are very luxurious! You can tell the rooms are a bit old but they are beautiful and extremely clean! The resort is built into Camelback Mountain which adds to the Phoenician's beauty! The Phoenician is with in 10 minutes to many shopping destinations like Fashion Square, and Old Town Scottsdale with about a 15 minute drive to Sky Harbor Airport! Overall I would highly recommend The Phoenician   I guarantee you won't regret it!

reviews.author: CoventGarden1
reviews.title: Tea?
reviews.text:
Finished lunch, did some shopping then will go to dinner later. I know - let's drop into the Phoenician for a cup of tea. 

Unfortunately my heart sank when, even in this establishment - expecting a pot of afternoon tea is asking the impossible. Whilst they serve a more formal afternoon tea, we didn't have room for it and to be honest the cost is irrelevant. 

On ordering one earl grey, we were told that Assam was only for the people who had a full English tea. On clarification, English Breakfast tea was available. I asked for a plate of biscuits - you guessed it, they were only for the people who were having afternoon tea and they 'only just had the right amount'. 

Unbelievable. They (or perhaps only the waitress? Hardly) seem oblivious to the real content of an English afternoon tea. Someone having a cup of tea with biscuits is an entirely different thing. The waitress did offer us a dish of nuts. Hardly. 

Tea arrives. Two mugs with hot water (on a saucer also containing hot water) with a piece of lemon and a whole pot of honey. Cold milk for English Breakfast? Sugar for English Breakfast? 

God, they're hard work. If any management read this, please get your F&B team in your international hotel to be able to serve a very basic requirement. Seems as though we can't give money away to hotels nowadays. 

If you come to London, we can serve you coffee in any way shape or form in any five star hotel.

reviews.author: tivmamtv
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Beautiful resort with an attentive staff.  Grounds are gorgeous. Nice patio bar and poolside bar. Great views looking south toward Phoenix.  The spa is very nice.  Nicely decorated for Christmas.  Rooms were spacious with standard amenities. Bathroom was huge.

reviews.author: Kelly O
reviews.title: Beautiful resort with excellent front desk, housekeeping, and pool staff
reviews.text:
The overall property is beautiful and well maintained.  Our stay began with a friendly and personable check in and a room on the 4th floor with a gorgeous pool view.  The room was immaculate for our arrival and cleaned in the same manner each day.  The Phoenician lip balm was a welcome treat.  Sarah, Gabe, and Daniel made the pool our favorite place to be. Their service was unobtrusive, prompt, and seamless.  We always had chair, umbrella, towel, and food service with a smile.  The Oasis food quality was excellent.  During our vacation we tried a CA wrap, salad, fish tacos, guacamole and chips, chicken fingers, fries, and a variety of mixed drinks.  All were delicious.  They were also willing to do a special fruit order for my daughter who only eats berries.

Relish Burger and J and G Steakhouse had excellent food but the service needs improvement.  At Relish, we had 3 different servers and the last one was good but we only had him for dessert and the check.  Our drinks were not refilled, no one asked how our meals were or checked on us at all until it was time for dessert.  J and G steakhouse we were checked on more often but our server was hard to find and appeared to have too many tables to manage.  

The breakfast restaurant (floor 1) had excellent variety, especially if you eat GF.  The omelette station was my favorite and there was an excellent assortment of fresh fruit.  The waiter substituted berries for my daughter due to her melon allergy.  

The holiday tea was wonderful although the tea sandwiches were a bit dried out.  

The ice cream shop offered some great breakfast options, including hard boiled eggs, if you request.

The pull out sofa in the room was unacceptable for sleeping.  The mattress was approximately 2 inches thick and you could feel all of the springs.

All of the staff throughout the hotel were very friendly and desired to make our stay excellent.  (Except for restaurant exceptions noted previously.)

reviews.author: RJtraveler64
reviews.title: First visit, looking forward to the next
reviews.text:
We spent three nights and enjoyed each aspect of the resort.  Our Casita grand room had a relaxing location and comfortable accommodations.    Next time, we will look to book a Casita Suite.

Great experiences at the Spa, Il Terrazzo, Relish and the J&G  Steakhouse.   Services, food & beverage, and staff were solid all around and excellent in most cases. 

I understand that room updates are planned for 2016, and this would add to enjoyment.   

We would return on our next visit to the area.

reviews.author: Lots_of_Baggage
reviews.title: Comfortable room, cheerful staff
reviews.text: Wish there was a way to give 4.5 stars. We really enjoyed our trip and were very comfortable during our stay. The lobby, especially the view from the lobby, is stunning. Slightly relaxing in and of itself simply due to how hot it can be outside and yet you are in a darker, air conditioned room with huge windows looking out over sand and palm trees. I'll say our room could have probably used a touch of a facelift, but it was nothing to be concerned about. We enjoyed great room service for breakfast. Parking was in a downstairs garage, which can be slightly intimidating but was actually very convenient. Plenty of spaces available regardless of time of day. Our room faced some of the hills that surround the property, and it was quite serene looking out our window each morning and seeing the vibrant colors. When we come back to the Phoenix area we will be staying here again.

reviews.author: Livesoutofasuitcase9
reviews.title: Desert Charm
reviews.text: The Phoenician in Scottsdale is one of the nicest resorts I have stayed at. I was there for business and wish I would have taken the time to stay longer and enjoy the facilities. The food was great and there are ample facilities for meetings, weddings, pool time, golf, hiking and the spa. Old Town Scottsdale is charming and worth the trip. The staff here was truly what set this place apart from others. One word of warning, if you hike Camelback mountain behind the resort, be prepared. I hike and run just about every day and was surprised at the difficulty. That being said it was one of my favorite parts, but I wouldn't bring a child or someone out of shape all the way to the top.

reviews.author: Danielle N
reviews.title: Great Location, Amazing Staff, Lovely Stay
reviews.text:
We arrived Dec 17th, 2015. My luggage was lost at the airport but Mora at the front desk was amazing and tried to do everything she could do to help. Lonni the concierge was great and helped with all our questions. The room was large and very comfortable. Double sinks in the bathroom was great for my husband and I as we could spread out. Alex at Il Terrazo restaurant was so pleasant and always provided great service. Overall the staff bent over backwards for us. They provide turn down service at night where they give you chocolates and water. On Xmas Eve they delivered a plate of cookies. We couldn't complain about a thing! If I were to nit pick the cost of the meals were pricey but I guess you get what you pay for.
The location is great. It takes about 20 mins to get to the airport. 15 mins to Desert Botanical garden. 10 mins to Scottsdale Fashion Mall/ downtown or 30 mins to walk. Highly recommend this hotel. We will be staying here again!

reviews.author: cjmsmco
reviews.title: Great Experience for a Christmas Getaway
reviews.text:
We checked into the Phoenician late on the night of the 23rd and were promptly greeted at the front desk by a lovely bubbly girl.  We were given directions to our room, which was 4167 on the back of the hotel facing the cactus garden.  After winding through the large wings of the building we arrived at our room, which was large, clean, a little worn, and certainly dated. The 1980's decor is certainly obvious, but when the place is clean and service is as good as it was, a little bit of separating wall coverings and cracked marble in the bathrooms can be overlooked.  The one spot that was a little on the "eww" factor was the tiled walk-in shower had black mold around the drain which could have been better addressed. 

The resort is easy walking distance to the Cholla Trail to the top of Camelback, which was a great way to start the trip.  We had excellent coffees and two pastries in the shops before heading out.  The two coffees and pastries were $26, so about a 35% push over what we would spend at Starbucks, but the coffees were good and the pastries were very good, and unless I am mistaken, were baked locally so they were worth the spend.  We hiked the mountain and then spent some time hanging around the property.  The grounds are outstanding.  We went back to the shops and had an awesome turkey and havarti sandwich which we easily split, and was on great bread.   The sandwich with the chips and bottle of Diet Coke was $14, and again, well worth it. We then returned to the room, had a nice hot shower and went for Christmas drinks at the Thirsty Camel ahead of our dinner at the J&G Steakhouse.  Holy smokes!  Anthony the bartender was absolutely fantastic. Great personality, talked with us about our plans, kept us filled on bar snacks and we had some awesome drinks.  The hubs loved they had blue cheese stuffed olives for his martini. Dinner at J&G was phenomenal.  The GM was there, we recognized him from commercials on the hotel channel on the floor, and was helping the servers keep up with the crush of guests. How many restaurant GMs can actually participate in all aspects of the  business AND step out to check on all the guests?? Again, phenomenal service, great management, great food with a great view of the sunset. Christmas dinner was at Il Terrazo, which was a set menu, very industrial- think cruise line food.  At $300 for two people with wine, it was disappointing, and I would advise that restaurant be skipped.  Again, great service, just industrial cruiseship type food. On the third day, after another long day of hiking, we hit up the Thirsty Camel and the amazing Anthony again.  That night we ate at Relish Burger Bistro.  Wow. Just WOW.  We had a beer at Happy Hour, which was 3:00-6:00, then sat down for some shared onion rings, chicken wings and a burger while we watched football and hockey on a multitude of screens.  The onion rings and wings were fantastic as was the burger.  Total bill- $56!!!  And the food was awesome as was the service. 

So all in all, yes, the lady is showing her age a bit, but with the cleanliness and the service, that is quickly overlooked.  I highly recommend this resort.

reviews.author: FoodQD
reviews.title: Great Location, Great Facility, Great Staffs
reviews.text: This resort has always provided us with great time every time we visit Scottsdale.  The location is less than 30 minutes away from Phoenix airport.  The facility is always well kept with wonderful view of Camel Back Mt.  There are three 9 hole golf course that wraps around the beautiful resort.  You can count on the staffs to be very helpful and genuinely nice.  Some rooms have great view of the golf course and mountain, but all are roomy and comfy.Breakfast in the lower level is always good.  It's too bad that the old restaurant Madeleine was replaced by JG Steak house and Window on the Green has been changed.

reviews.author: HalleyB88
reviews.title: Not worth the $$  Outdated!!
reviews.text: First off, the hotel and rooms are outdated.  The lobby and grounds are beautiful but other than that it's outdated.  The main pool is even outdated.  The food and service at the pool is terrible as well as room service!  For $400+ night, I would think they could toast your toast for you instead of sending cold bread and a toaster.  Really??  This is not Holiday Inn!   The service at the pool was awful and nobody even helped us, we had to go up to the bar to get service.  Did not enjoy this hotel at all.  Definitely better places to stay in Scottsdale.  Not worth the $!

reviews.author: richlester
reviews.title: Perfection! in every component of our stay!
reviews.text: Occasionally a restaurant can pull off a perfect meal,however The Phoenician managed to pull off a perfect 5 night stay! I mean everything.The check-in experience set the tone for excellence,but it was the extraordinary attention to detail and followup by the "customer experience team(lead by Ruby and executed ,in our case ,primarily by a Carolina) that really distinguished our visit.Personal details,exemplary,ontime room service,specific requests honored...The "casita" was spacious and the hotel grounds beautiful.Roomservice,with formal tablecloths,discreet,efficient, staff and Michelin star worthy food was as much fun as going out.The stay,the staff the room,the grounds,the experience were flawless.I can't recommend it highly enough!Great location too halfway between Fashion Square and the Biltmore Plaza!

reviews.author: Colorado_hi
reviews.title: Relaxing stay @ The Phoenician, Scottsdale
reviews.text: From the moment I called reservations til the time we checked out, we received outstanding service.  Cheryl in reservations could not have been any kinder and good at her job!  Our room was beautiful and had a balcony with chaise lounger and bistro set that overlooked the pool area.  The rooms are large and comfortable; however, a bit dated.  Bathroom was large with a bathtub and frameless shower.  Toiletries are top of the line; there's even a bathroom scale should you want to weigh yourself after enjoying any of the fine restaurants The Phoenician has to offer.  My daughter and I enjoyed an afternoon at the Centre for Well Being, being pampered with massages, body scrubs, and facials.  The Centre itself has every amenity you can think of as far as a spa is concerned.  My massage was the best I've ever had (Regina I believe?), and I was able to relax afterwards in the sauna, steam room, and whirlpool.  This place is the epitome of the word "tranquility", from the hotel to the pools to the spa.  Thoroughly enjoyed our stay here and will make it a point to return on my next vacation to Scottsdale.

reviews.author: Andreass B
reviews.title: Anniversary
reviews.text: The resort was amazing! Front desk was very friendly! The relish restaurant was fantastic! Food tasted incredible and our servers Drew and Tanner gave us the best anniversary experience we could ask for both were very knowledgeable of the menu, welcomed us with warm smiles and overall made our stay perfect!

reviews.author: MarshalltownMan
reviews.title: First rate, but one dining glitch...
reviews.text:
We had a great experience overall.  The facility is beautiful and service was mostly excellent.  I loved the pools, and appreciated being within walking distance of the Camelback trailhead.  

However...we made the big mistake of going to their coffee shop the day after Thanksgiving.  The coffee was OK, but there were other problems.
