The rooms were merely OK.  The decor was a bit outdated and there wasn't anything particularly impressive about them.

The pool areas were nice and the view was spectacular.  The pool service was decent.  The workers were friendly but you tended to have to flag someone down to get service started.

The final straw was when they overcharged me for my stay.  I called them back and had to argue with the person for over 10 minutes.  She insisted I wasn't overcharged but when I presented her with the math she admitted it but still tried to insist no mistakes were made!  Hmmm, how is that possible.

There are countless nice resorts in the Scottsdale/Phoenix area.  I will not be staying at the Phoenician again after my experiences.

reviews.author: Lisa G
reviews.title: The Phoenician Resort lives up to all the hype!
reviews.text:
Just returned from a four day conference at the Phoenician and I was quite impressed. The service was impeccable; everyone from the bellmen, housekeeping, waitstaff and concierge were welcoming and friendly. 

Our room was in the main building with a view of the pool. It was very spacious, well kept with a great amount of closet space and an enormous bath with separate toilet. 

During down time, we were able to enjoy the pool and lawn games. Drink service however was a little slow. 

Location was convenient, only about 15 minutes from that airport and a quick cab ride into Old Town.

reviews.author: David H
reviews.title: My experience of The Phoenician
reviews.text:
Wow.  What an experience.  First class service from the time I checked in until the time I left.  Everything I desired for a quick getaway was at my finger tips.  Rooms were clean and welcoming.  Food was prompt and first class.  Maid service was excellent.

Atmosphere at the pool was great.  The golf was fantastic.  Service at the pool and the clubhouse were once again spectacular.

I was there on a business conference but feel it would be a nice high end family getaway.

My only small complaint is that there were not enough options for "quick and easy" on the go meals.

reviews.author: barbiflys
reviews.title: most perfect
reviews.text: We loved this place.  It was so quiet.  We both slept great--the bed was great and the pillows were perfect.  I love how this property is situated at the base of Camelback Mtn so it made climbing the mountain very easy and convenient--I was able to do the Cholla trail 3 times during my stay.  All staff members were extrememly accomadating and really friendly--we especially remember Brette at the front desk who got us the perfect room.  Would love to stay here again!!!!

reviews.author: slbe
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, attentive staff
reviews.text: Very large resort...well maintained grounds and pool. Staff were all very attentive. We had no issues with check in and got the room we booked. Hotel is well located to shopping, restaurants but you will need transportation. Having stayed at the fairmont last time, I would say location is the biggest advantage. Couple of small quibbles: coffee shop didn't open til 7 and there was always a line up waiting. Given all the early risers maybe open a bit early. Restaurants were ok...nothing terrible, nothing great. Fairmont has the advantage there.

reviews.author: AmyLa992
reviews.title: Overall amazing hotel, fun hotel bar
reviews.text: Highly recommend this hotel, gorgeous setting.  Love the hotel bar, Thirsty Camel, so much fun.  The pool area is great too, basketball and volleyball pool options.  Wonderful golf in the area.  Love all Luxury Collection Hotels and this one also meets the standards.

reviews.author: Nancy D
reviews.title: Great service, attention to detail!  Wow!
reviews.text: This was our first trip to Scottsdale and to the Phoenician.  It was incredible!  As soon as we pulled  up to the valet, the service started!  We had an early flight, but was able to get right in our room at 11:00am!  Very friendly front desk.  Very large room, with comfortable bed and sofa bed.  Large separate bathroom also.  The room, pool area, and property was very clean. Loved the turn down service at night and our 15 year old loved the slippers!  Anytime we needed anything, they were quick.  My only small issue is not being able to get your own ice, but we've been to other hotels that do that too. The pool area and grounds are beautiful!  The service at the pool is fabulous, very attentive.  Great variety of food and cocktails.  Activities for kids and adults of all ages.  The fitness center had plenty of machines, weights, etc.  The Concierge's Desk was so helpful to us.  We were only there for 5 days, but Gary, Robert and Michelle all helped us with great restaurant suggestions, tours,(The Pink Jeep tour in Sedona was awesome, thanks Gary!) and directions.  They were patient, friendly, and knew their stuff!  I read some reviews were folks said the property was outdated, and we didn't see it.  The 3 of us had a wonderful time, loved the area, the Diamondbacks Game, golf, the pool, and the service at this outstanding hotel.  Can't wait to return!!!

reviews.author: Stephanie T
reviews.title: Amazing stay, questionable billing
reviews.text: Stayed at the Phoenician for three nights at the end of April for a conference. Our room was located on the first floor of the main building - great location, spacious room (even with four grown women staying in one room), lovely balcony. We had wonderful service as hotel guests, however, many of our fellow attendees experienced copious amounts of issues with billing ... duplicate charges, fees added and not disclosed, etc. I would make sure to check your bill very closely at check out.

reviews.author: skinnermj
reviews.title: More bad than good
reviews.text:
We've been making an annual week-long trip to the Phoenician for the past 12 years.  With each year, our experience gets progressively worse.  Here are my comments about the good and the bad from this most recent visit:

Good- grounds are beautiful, pools and pool waitstaff are great (especially Rich at the cabanas), wonderful massage and nice manicure at the spa.  I wanted to spend money on tennis, but they made sure that I didn't.  

Bad- rooms are in need of a renovation (see every other review), spa facility is terribly outdated and tennis staff were incredibly unresponsive.  The pro, Jason Purcell, took 3 days to follow up to my request for any clinic availability.  3 days? Belinda in the pro shop basically told me to go find people to play with on my own...like I knew anyone there. Players usually talk with the pro shop about pairing up for a clinic or a semi-private.  

What was most concerning is that we had the same experience as so many other reviewers with being 'downgraded' to a lesser room than what we purchased.  We reserved 6 nights in a casita 4+ months in advance and were given an awful mountainview room upon arrival.  The manager on duty checked us in and he didn't even acknowledge the mishap until I pointed it out.  He was still charging us for the casita!!  I eventually called the Platinum desk and they helped to get us moved a few days later.  We called Bowen, another manager, and he never returned our call.  When we got home, we wrote to SPG.  In response, we received a letter from Guy Bittner's administrative assistant (he's the GM) saying "sorry for not giving you the room you reserved, here are 8,000 points to add to the 5,000 points that you received from the Platinum desk." We now have enough points to spend 1/2 a day there, after spending 70 nights there over the years.  There was no reply to our mention of the poor service and lack of response from Bowen.  Well, at least they are consistent...consistently bad.

Now that Starwood is for sale, you can bet that the service and attention will be lacking.  Let's hope the buyer teaches service recovery and values loyalty.

reviews.author: PJsooner
reviews.title: IT'S Phoentastic!
reviews.text:
The hotel was just great. Everyone was helpful the room was large with comfortable bed. But let's be honest it's all about the POOLs.

I recommend  the mother of pearl pool a bit smaller area but has bathrooms on either side of the pool. The pond &  fountain are good to relax near. 

The Spa was fantastic had a great massage by Amy highly recommend her. 

Golf was perfect! Easy to get tee times and course is in excellent condition. OK my best ever round might make me a bit bias! 

Steak House food was rediculouse. Filet and Salmon were the best we had this week. Glad we saved best for last. 

The Longe outside the lobby was great also. Enjoyed the fire pit at night. 

I have no complaints after a 7 night stay!!

reviews.author: KENNETH S
reviews.title: The Fantastic Phoenician! Perfection!
reviews.text:
Luxury is an understatement when referring to this resort!  I was in Phoenix for 3 days on business and I cannot sing enough praise for the level of service this establishment provides!  I felt like royalty with the efficiency of room servicing, turn down service, in room dining and just overall hospitality of the staff.  

It's a truly magnificent compound with Camelback Mountain set in the backdrop.  The grounds are sprawling and truly well manicured.  The gym was an added jewel, the pools offering multiple spots to lay out and take a dip. The multitude of dining selections was spectacular as well as the many stores available for whatever you need.  

You don't hear the word NO at this resort, in fact you find yourself having to tell the staff no at times lol.  It's located in Scottsdale but is only a few minutes from the very upscale fashion mall which is easily accessible.  It's a gated resort with 24 hour security so you're perfectly safe.  The rooms are extremely spacious and comfortable!  The bathrooms very elegant offering both shower and bath options. 

I was immediately impressed upon my arrival and I left this resort vowing to come back in a leisurely capacity bringing along family members to enjoy this plush establishment!  I highly recommend this resort for any occasion!  I will be back!

reviews.author: Dictaitor
reviews.title: Disfunctional and Defrauded
reviews.text: My wife and I recently attended a work function at this resort and attempted to check in at 5:30 pm. Our room was not ready and we were offered double beds, which we declined, by a young lady with a LARGE chip on her shoulder. As a result, we ended up waiting for an hour for our room, making us late for our reception event.  The room we received was not the Casita we reserved, but rather a King on the top floor(6164), with a disfunctional television, disfunctional handicap door buttons down the hallway, and a great view of the parking area. Today, 9 days later, to add insult to injury, I noticed they charged my card for an additional $295 above the final bill that they emailed me. They made a simple Holiday Inn Express experience seem inviting.

reviews.author: Maddie T
reviews.title: Here for my birthday
reviews.text: I have stayed at many luxury hotels throughout the years. I have to say this is my biggest disappointment to date.  If you are spending 400 dollars a night 500 including resort fee and taxes you expect great rooms.  Complete shock with the old outdated vintage 70's rooms.  They announced they are planning a re do...should have been done 10 years ago. Stay away!

reviews.author: Ken M
reviews.title: Golfing in Scottsdale
reviews.text:
This hotel was selected by our travel agent during a golfing trip to Arizona.
The hotel is very grand and a little impersonal. The room was top notch and overlooked the pools and lawn area.
Restaurant prices were high especially if you just wanted a light breakfast but the cafe provided a cheaper alternative. We found the reception staff to be very helpful and the waiting staff on the balcony were delightful. Our chief criticism is that the hotel tends to favour corporate guests over individuals. There were numerous business groups using the hotel during our stay. The pool areas are spectacular as is the setting beneath Camelback mountain. The golf within the resort was of high quality with excellent practice facilities.

reviews.author: brithbigguy
reviews.title: Wonderful Family Resort
reviews.text: Stayed here for Spring Break and were pleasantly surprised by the family atmosphere. Tons of water, including a water slide. Spent several hours at the bar by the pool, catching up with old friends and enjoying cocktails (Dark and Stormy and Moscow Mule's). Staff were all friendly and accommodating. Several food choices a different locations on the property.

reviews.author: Carrie H
reviews.title: Beautiful resort
reviews.text: This is probably the most beautiful place you can stay in Scottsdale. I accompanied my partner to a conference here in late April. The scenery is spectacular -- the mountain, the three golf courses, the cactus and flower gardens, the pools, the waterfall and the koi fish pond. The resort is only a 5-minute cab ride to Fashion Square mall, fun restaurants (Salty Senorita, Morning Squeeze) and a vibrant club district. The hotel itself is pretty spectacular as well. The staff are great. Our room had everything we could want and the bathrooms are very spacious. We didn't have a view so that's the one thing I would change next time, but we weren't in the room much anyway. On the last night, our group had dinner and a live band outside at sunset at the Jokake Inn and it was unforgettable. I would definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: iamfullofbliss
reviews.title: Luxury hotel and best staff
reviews.text: I attended a blogging convention. The staff were amazing and very accommodating. The beds and pillows were awesome. No noise, beautiful balcony, spacious rooms and luxury bathrooms. The staff really care

reviews.author: Beverly R
reviews.title: Screaming for a redo
reviews.text:
My husband & I went to the Phoenician for a long weekend. After flying for almost 5 1/2 hrs we tried to check in but we're told that our rm was not ready. So we waited in the lobby for over 3 hrs then it took another 45 min to receive our luggage. Much yo my dismay, since this was my first trip to AZ I opened the drapes to a view of the ballroom roof!  I called & was told they were 100% occupied but they would move us the next day. First day completely wasted & to add insult to injury they still charged us a resort fee for that day even thought it was too late to use the resort 
Would never recommend this resort go to the Ritz if u want a fabulous resort & exceptional service.

reviews.author: Laura D
reviews.title: Great hotel - wish we could have stayed longer
reviews.text:
We stayed a single night at the Phoenician and it was great for our quick stay. We booked two connecting rooms (2 adults + 2 kids), and although initially they had lost our connection booking, they were able to find us two adjoining rooms with a limited delay. The kids thoroughly enjoyed the hotel pools, especially the water slide (although I wished the slide were located in an area where you could easily see it from the deck chairs). Their only complaint was that ducks repeatedly landed in one of the pools they were swimming in, which scared my 5-year-old (although other kids seemed to think it was an added bonus). My daughter rated the chicken fingers served poolside as "the best ever." The pool area was packed and it was hard to get chairs together, so would advise going earlier than we did.

Our rooms had no view to speak of (booked on points, so not surprising), but they were very spacious. We ate at the Italian restaurant above the pool area, dining outside in near perfect weather. The kids enjoyed running around on the lawn, chasing real bunnies which appeared. They were also showing a movie on an inflatable screen in the pool area, which was great. We got the sense that there were a number of activities at the hotel (we just missed some sort of birding show), which if we had stayed longer I'm sure we would have been able to take more advantage of.

The cactus garden located behind the hotel was a nice little area to explore. All in all, a very nice resort, very family-friendly, and we would happily stay there again.

reviews.author: Andrew R
reviews.title: Massive property that is in need of some TLC
reviews.text: This flagship Westin Property has definitely seen better days.  It is in dire need of updating, from the bland carpeting to the drab colors in the lobby.  In April, we were quoted $450/night for a basic room, definitely over priced for the room, service and overall experience.  The service at the pool was terrible, usually taking 30-40 mins from ordering a drink to having that drink delivered.  The bell captains definitely hate if your using UBER since they don't get tipped for waving in a car for you, you can tell by their disdain the second you say you've gotten a ride.  The patio bar was also comically slow during prime time, happy hour.  Took 25 mins before a server got to us.  I'll give the hotel credit for 2 things: 1. the rooms are nice sized and the one's that overlook the pool have a great view.  2.  The gym and spa were great.  The gym was well stocked and your room gives you free access to use the spas facilities such as steam room, sauna, and whirlpool.  But it's definitely not worth $500/night after the "Resort Fee".

reviews.author: SuzanneMWH
reviews.title: My wedding was amazing, the journey there was not!
reviews.text: This review is for people thinking of holding events here.  I'm originally from Scottsdale, and grew up dreaming of getting married here.  My first job was at this hotel, my mom took me here as a little girl for high tea, I always knew I would get married at The Phoenician.  Well, I did.  What a horrific experience, from start to almost finish.  I say that because my wedding was perfect, mostly thanks to ur amazing wedding planners, Trista and Alex at BTS Event Management.  I can't even imagine what I would have done had I not been smart enough to hire them, they were life savers.  I picked The Phoenician based on my own experiences there, which had always been top notch.  I expected for a day as special as my wedding that things along the way in the months leading up to it would be seamless, or at least not crisis after crisis.  Nope.  From the start, nothing I was told was what actually happened.  Where do I start?  Because my wedding was small (38 people) I was never made aware that we wouldn't be getting a food tasting, since we weren't spending enough in food and beverage, apparently you have to spend 15 grand to taste the food. In fact, in our original meeting with catering, we were told we would get a tasting, and how the chef would be willing to work with us, blah blah blah.  The area where we planned to get married in a gazebo had the gazebo torn down, so it looked nothing like what we signed on for, and no one told us there were plans to tear down or alter the appearance of the area.  Because our wedding was small, and we didn't want to rent a ballroom, we asked to reserve a small section of the lobby bar after dinner for guests to have drinks, we were told absolutely not, its a public area, and there is no reserving seats.  We planned to have a five course dinner at J and G, a very expensive steak house on the property.  To say the managers there were unhelpful is an understatement.  They also refused to provide a tasting, and when one manager was talking to my father about it she actually said "our steak tastes like steak, and our potatoes taste like potatoes, why do you need a tasting?"  We did get one, after I called the GM, that cost us close to 400 dollars.  They comped one entree, thanks.  The one manager that made the steak and potato comment was rude to my dad so many times I stopped counting. About thirty days before my wedding, I was told that the rehearsal we had planned and already told people about (remember, people were traveling from out of town for this wedding, and especially the wedding party were making travel arrangements around what we were telling them), could not be held in the location my wedding would be in because they had booked an event there for that evening.  Their solution was to let us rehearse "in a different location."  Call me crazy (which they acted like I was), but what is the point of a rehearsal if it isn't where the actual wedding is?  How do you know where to walk, etc if you aren't rehearsing in the correct location?  The response to my anger was a resolute "Sorry, your rehearsal is not happening on the Orchid Lawn, deal with it."  (Well they said this in much nicer words.)  It actually took me reaching out to the General Manager of the hotel to get any movement, and we still didn't get the rehearsal as planned.  He let us rehearse at 3 pm (many in our party had to pay to change their flights) and moved us into the presidential suite, for the rate of a regular room, and comped one night.  Very generous, and we appreciated it, but again, it was another example of me literally having to scream and yell to get things somewhat fixed.   What I found most challenging is all of their "corporate rules" and a real unwillingness to make us feel special and taken care of on such an important day.  No upgraded room for your wedding night, no suite to get ready in, you get ready in a conference room.  We ended up saying forget the conference rooms, since we had the big suite comped after I complained, but really, who wants to get ready in a conference room with a table and five uncomfortable chairs and a water station.  No place comfortable to sit, no bathroom, no TV.  I thought that was really silly.  With all the rooms they have available, if you don't have a huge suite, they should at least let you get ready in a real hotel room.  I don't fault the employees for this, they have to follow the rules, which are set by corporate and upper management.  And the service here is outstanding, that's why we chose it.  But tell me, because I'm sure a PR person will respond to this, are all these rules really serving your guests?  Do I really have to almost throw a tantrum (which is not my personality at all) to get a tasting for food that's being served to my guests because J and G just arbitrarily doesn't do them or because I'm not spending enough?   They have a saying that a happy guest will tell one person, and an unhappy guest will tell a hundred.  I hope I've reached at least that many here.  Get married at The Royal Palms up the street, its a much better bet, especially for a smaller ceremony.  I have the distinct feeling that at The Phoenician, unless its a wedding that costs over 100 grand or is for over 200 people, you just aren't that high of a priority, or at least pleasing you isn't.  Now, that being said, my wedding was magical, and was pulled off flawlessly.  however, I think this is much more to the credit of my excellent wedding planners than The Phoenician.  Trista and Alex of BTS could throw a wedding in a closet and it would be beautiful.  It did end up being the best day of my life, but when i think of The Phoenician, I'm not sure it was worth all the anguish it took along the way.  By all means, if you have all the money in the world, get married here.  And sure, stay here as a guest whenever you want, the hotel is amazing and service is flawless.  But if you are having an event where you have a budget (and ours was high, at the end of it all we spent over a grand a head), and you want to feel taken are of, this isn't the place.  Hire BTS and get married someplace else.

reviews.author: Jimking2
reviews.title: A very well run and delightful place to stay.
reviews.text: A very well run and delightful place to stay (but pricey). Hotel is very close to old Scottsdale. J&G Steakhouse was very good! However, you can skip the flight of the Phoenix show. The bird would not fly down from the roof and had to be brought down in the elevator (quite comical actually).

reviews.author: BethTO
reviews.title: 5 Star Stay thanks to Tripadvisor reviewers!
reviews.text:
After reading reviews we asked to be in an upper floor in the main building and facing the pool. Even though we used SPG points for all 5 nights (and were not charged for self parking - yippee!) we were upgraded to a pool room as requested. The front desk associate did say that housekeeping does not like to put rollaways in the rooms, but we convinced them to do so. Plenty of room!  Our room was beautiful, toiletries were wonderful (love the lip balm!) and view was amazing. Only suggestion (and its a minor one!) is that a towel hook is needed by the shower.
I agree that finding pool chairs was a challenge. Many chairs were "saved" and no one showed up all day.  Staff did not want to clear them (or release empty cabanas) but did bring chairs over to the end of and isle so that our family could sit together. Only other issue was cigarette smoke drifting from the pool bar.  Special shout out to Jennah (Sp?) for outstanding pool service and to to the sweet lady with the Russian accent who gave me a nice pedi!

reviews.author: Longballer
reviews.title: Nice but pricey
reviews.text: For starters this is a very large and well appointed property.  Beautiful views.  Great amenities.  The pools are fabulous.  The golf course and staff there are superb.  But we had some sort of intermittent clicking coming from the AC system in our room.  Maintenance came and repaired it but the issue recurred the following evening.  So essentially we lost two nights sleep.  This is difficult to accept given the price.

reviews.author: ChandlerMomma
reviews.title: One of the best places in the world to stay. Ever.
reviews.text: I live in Arizona and I've traveled to many places - but we keep coming back to the Phoenician Hotel in Scottsdale, AZ. We go here to get away from the kids some weekends and other weekends we bring the entire family because there is so much to do here. It is an immaculate property - with golf, views, hiking. Rooms are beautiful, bright, modern, and clean. Service is five star. I would highly recommend the Afternoon High Tea (which my sisters take our mothers to every single year for Mother's Day but it's offered daily) and their Relish Burger bistro (which my husband and I visit often). If you're looking for a very nice, fun hotel in Arizona to stay in, this is the hotel.

reviews.author: Simon A
reviews.title: Agréablement surpris
reviews.text:
Je suis resté une semaine dans l’hôtel et j'ai vraiment apprécié la chambre, la qualité du service offert, les gens accueillent avec le sourire et ont su répondre à nos demandes.

Il y a plusieurs restaurants sur le site, tous assez cher mais la nourriture y est très bonne.

Je n'ai pas "essayé" les terrains de golf mais j'ai pris la peine de prendre quelques marches pour les voir et ils semblent très bien.

reviews.author: Dineriffic
reviews.title: Phoenician still flying at its peak.
reviews.text: I have been lucky to have been a guest at this hotel many times over the past 10 years. I have never been disappointed and this time it was better than ever. The grounds and the hotel itself are absolutely beautiful. Behind the hotel is a gorgeous and extensive cactus garden.  The staff is first class. The pool area is beautiful and relaxing. This is a five star hotel in every way and I look forward to making it back in the future.

reviews.author: Rjs1951
reviews.title: Impeccable Service
reviews.text: Just spent three days here for my wife's birthday.  It has been about 5 years since we were at the Phoenician and this trip was just wonderful.  Every staff member, from the front desk to the chambermaids to the bartenders knock themselves out for you.  The rooms were beautiful, and the halls etc seem to have been recently renovated.  The atmosphere is quiet elegance and the pools are fantastic.  I mentioned we were celebrating my wife's birthday and champagne and chocolates were delivered to our room gratis.  We plan on returning as often as we can--we also stay at the Biltmore for it's architecture but it isn't as convenient or restful a the Phonecian.

reviews.author: MeqonTraveler
reviews.title: Good and Predictable
reviews.text:
I have stayed at the Phoenician a number of times, and each one is pretty much the same (which is good).  Each time it is very good.  Which is good.  I use this as my "go to" when I want to meet friends for a couple of days of golf.  Easy trip from that airport.  Easy to checkin.  

The rooms are fine (it is a conference style hotel), if a bit bland, but in good shape.  I am usually in the main building, but this time in the back building which has no interesting view and is quite a hike from everything.  The breakfast buffet is pretty good, but the outside seating always fills up right away, and the wait in general can be long.  The pool area is vast, but pool side service can be spotty (sometimes attentive other times you have to chase someone down).  The patio bar area off the main lobby has a great view, but almost impossible to get service.  The times I have had to make changes to my room, I have had varying degrees of success, but the front desk has always worked hard to find a solution.   

The golf is run by Troon, so expensive but pretty well organized and with three nines, you can easily come in for two days of golf and have variety.

reviews.author: Oliver S
reviews.title: This is a five-star hotel?
reviews.text:
PROS: large comfortable rooms, tastefully furnished and decorated, fine bed & bath linen, great cacti garden.
	CONS: 25 minute wait to check in, late check in, messy, (see photos taken at 7:30PM, cleaning cards and dirty linen littering the floors), poor room service, poor restaurant service (see separate review of Il Terrazzo)
This is unacceptable for a five-star hotel. My last visit there.

reviews.author: LoveBeach515
reviews.title: Great Guest Service!
reviews.text: Beautiful property, great food, great guest service & great for families with kids, including location.  Rooms are dated and need refreshing to meet 5 star expectations such as stained carpet and couches.

reviews.author: steveboces1
reviews.title: Beautiful Property, but the staff needs training in people skills and other things
reviews.text:
I recently stayed, at the resort with my wife.  We were there for the wedding of one of my closest friends daughter.  The ceremony and every thing that accompanied it was fabulous.  However, and it's a big however, I found the front desk help to be rude and less than gracious.  On top of that my friends room was not ready until after 4pm despite the fact that he began calling them in the morning to say that he was at the hotel.  I went to the desk to see if my room was ready and asked about his room. I was told that he hadn't checked in.  I told the young lady that he was in fact at the hotel and had been for at least three hours.  The room still wasn't ready.  Finally, at a quarter after four the bride called down and five minutes later the room was ready.  This is really inexcusable.

This all was on top of a saga I watched for almost a year regarding the management of the hotel and my friend.  Every week there was another surprise, mostly monetary and much at the last moment.  Can you imagine having a very expensive wedding and not tasting any of the food?  Well, that's what the hotel wanted.  There were charges on top of charges that were never mentioned.  The only thing that makes sense about all of this is that the Phonecian is so well known and so expensive, that people who hold events there never ask about the prices because they don't have to.

reviews.author: Reed J
reviews.title: A Fading Desert Icon
reviews.text:
Some good news: Lots to do and fantastic amenities to include golf and tennis. Outstanding central location. I also love the history behind the hotel. 

Here are the issues: I give this place a 4 star rating. I have no doubt this place was once at the top of its game and probably the leader in the premium hotel category. Unfortunately there is no way this is still a 5 star hotel. The rooms and property are "tired". Although the rooms are large and spacious both my family's rooms had stained carpet, peeling wallpaper, chipped baseboards and fraying carpet. Even the common areas, hallways and elevators were not in great shape.

I am sure the Phoenician marketing department reads these posts and will respond with a polite explanation. The truth is this place is about to undergo a major renovation of the guest rooms sometime later this summer. I applaud the effort. It is needed especially if you are charging $600+/room - which is what we paid per night for the holiday week.

I would hesitate to visit this property again until the renovations are completed. I definitely would not recommend this place to others that are seeking a 5 star resort.

reviews.author: Ben B
reviews.title: It's not in Scottsdale!  Very 80's... beige everywhere...
reviews.text:
Finally got a chance to stay at The Phoenician.... after visiting many dozens of times since the 1980s.  A few things:  

1) It's in Phoenix not in Scottsdale, not at all... it's close, but how they have a Scottsdale address is pretty interesting to me, since the western-most border with Scottsdale is at least 6 blocks away... check out google maps, just type "Phoenix", and zoom out - you'll see that the resort is not in Scottsdale at all, it's in Phoenix.... besides if it were in Scottsdale shouldn't it be called "The Scottsdalian"?

2) Really, really, really expensive for solo travelers who aren't part of a meeting/convention/group.  I think that they advertise at really high prices to make it look more attractive for meeting planners... when comparing our rate to rates that groups were paying, the difference was jaw-dropping.  I think other major resorts follow this same model - price high for individual travel, then get the groups in, and focus on the branding in the meantime.

3) Depending on the rooms we saw, the furnishings are still very 'stuck in the 80s', don't really reflect much regional flavor, etc... this could be a Ritz in Osaka for all you know, and that's usually my biggest complaint with Ritz Carlton - you're always staying in something like your Grandma's house, no matter if you're in Japan, India, St Thomas, etc.  If I were a traveler from Europe or New York or San Francisco or London, I just don't think I'd want to feel like I never left home, I want to feel like I'm in Arizona.

4) Service is good, food is good... but definitely leave the resort to eat... Phoenix and Scottsdale are known as some of the best foodie cities in the world, so go support a locally owned and operated restaurant instead of something owned and operated by a foreign company.... after all, you travel to experience the world, not shelter yourself from it, right?

5) All in all, you're going to get great quality, service, amenities, etc., but there are options out there for 1/4 the price that leave more money in your pocket each day for shopping, spa services, tours, events, etc., etc.

reviews.author: Journeyman644
reviews.title: Frank Loyd Wright architecture and tributes to his achievements.
reviews.text:
Beautiful  natural sandstone, milkglass lighting fixtures, stained glass and glass block materials are gathered together,  Frank Loyd Wright ball room and other various named tributes to  the famed architect.
Beautiful gardens and wedding sites placed with white chairs etc. and wedding planners and brides to be shooting up all over in bloom and colorful as the flowers.
We enjoyed our visit.

reviews.author: TravelnDr
reviews.title: Gem in the Sun
reviews.text: Nice property.  Lots of pools.  Oasis pool side food is commissary...stay away unless you have a tight budget.  J & G Steak House is the way to go. Great food,excellent view, and nice waitstaff.  Get a Casita room.  They are unique. Nice, not hotel feeling, pvt patio/deck, quiet, easy access to all.  Dont do the main hotel.  Spa services are outstanding!  Mani/pedi/massage for everyone! Overall very comfortable.  We were there spring break week so a bit crowded and kids very noisy at pool. evenings very pleasant.  Seen the 20 min Phoenix rising bird show.  Interesting diversion.  Lasts about 20min. Have fun cocktails while you watch.  We'll be back next year.

reviews.author: John L
reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text:
The Phoenician in Scottsdale has service down to an art. Many hotels claim to be 5 stars. This place truly deserves that rating.
The staff was amazing at every turn, they make this experience.
The hotel is older with a "Rat Pack" feel to it, however everything is kept up wonderfully. No bathrooms kept together with caulking here. The rooms are large with extraordinary 5 piece bathrooms - at least ours was. I recommend requesting an upper level room looking out over the pools and grounds. 
There are several restaurants on site - all very good. The golf course is great and not dramatically overpriced as you might expect. There are several pools in the main hotel area and several more throughout the grounds. The one recommendation I would make to management here would be to expand the amount of seating by the pools. During our stay, each morning was a game of 'who can wake up the earliest to reserve pool chairs?'. Ever been on a cruise ship? Kind of like that. We tried to rent a pool-side cabana but were told that those were all rented months in advance - OK that might have been nice to know ahead of time.
The Phoenician also offers condo-style accommodations in addition to the standard hotel room.
We will definitely be back again.

reviews.author: L l
reviews.title: Busy place, but well managed
reviews.text: I just got back from a three night stay at the Phoenician for an industry conference. The hotel was packed full, and that created some navigational challenges in getting from point to point as well as a lot of congestion in the restaurants and bars. But the hotel service staff were uniformly courteous and seemed to handle the crowd pressure well. And the hotel is in a very beautiful setting with very well kept grounds. Productive and enjoyable visit.

reviews.author: Lisa F
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: Recently stayed at the Phoencian to visit our daughter for Easter weekend.  We always stay at this resort.  The service is excellent, the food at all of the restaurants is delicious.  The rooms are very comfortable and quiet.   The location is great, 20 minutes from the airport and close to Scottsdale Mall.  You can walk to Cholla trail from the hotel.

reviews.author: Cayuga22776
reviews.title: This is simply not a luxury hotel in any way, except for the price
reviews.text:
I am here for a conference for the second year in a row - and things have gotten worse.  I only stay because the conference is here.

The issues:
-Totally insufficient staff - they simply don't have enough people working to manage anything - restaurants have long waits, slow service - lines out the door for any food of any kind, filthy tables and trash on the ground for hours, birds invading the rotting food left by the pool, one hour room service waits, endless ringing and nobody answers the phone.  They need more people in order to provide service.
-Poorly trained staff - the staff are generally unable to provide directions or answer simple questions.  They knock on doors despite privacy signs.  They are clearly overworked and harried and the lack of training is clear.
-Shabby rooms - this comment has been made over and over again in other reviews.
-Non-responsive - as I raised issues to management, they simply apologized but there was not even an indication of any solutions - they have none.

The AAA Five Diamond designation means nothing now if this resort is able to maintain it.  Good news is that there were so many complaints that the conference will be moved next year.

reviews.author: ketml
reviews.title: Beautiful, but pricey!
reviews.text: Beautiful resort, gorgeous grounds, and nice rooms.  Some others have posted about the rooms being dated.  I didn't find that to be true.  Nice, comfortable bed with great linens.  We were on the mountain facing side, and the only downside to the room would be that it was on the end, so we could here delivery trucks early in the morning, and our trash never seemed to get emptied.  Good service, good, but extremely pricey food and beverages.  We couldn't have a meal at less than $75.  $7 for beer and $12 for a margarita is extreme, in my opinion.  I tried not to focus on that though.  We spent most time at the pool.  The cactus garden is gorgeous!  I loved walking through it.  Hiked up Camelback mountain - a must do, but I wouldn't take smaller children.  Not far from the Fashion Square mall, which I loved!  I was really disappointed upon checkout to get an additional $600 bill - after the huge nightly rate, to find that there was a daily resort fee was a shock.  Overall, I very much enjoyed our stay.  Would I recommend it?  Yes.  Will we return - not sure because of how expensive ALL of the extras are.  I felt it was more expensive than Las Vegas.  If money is no object though, I don't see anyone not loving this resort.

reviews.author: travelislifegal
reviews.title: Nice Property, But Not Relaxing
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed here for three nights for a work related trip.  We arrived and were greeted by a massive check-in line.  After 25 minutes of waiting in line, we had our room key.  The room itself was very spacious and clean.  We had a view of the cactus garden and when people weren't running though it, talking loud on their cell phones or kids screaming - it was peaceful.

I know it was spring break for many, but you have to be able to still provide good service.  All the staff were very friendly and helpful - despite looking completely stressed out with all the guests and the countless complaints.  They really did try their best, in my opinion.  

The one area, which is mentioned by others on here over and over, was the pool.  Picture college spring break in Panama City, FL and Disney World rolled into one.  You couldn't move an inch in any of the pools without touching someone.  And the chair situation was a nightmare.  It took us close to an hour to gain two chairs...then another 25 minutes to gain two towels....and 3 hours to get drink/food service (we kept walking up to the bar those hours until someone came by).   

The stress continued all the way up to our check-out, when we tried the TV check-out.  It then said our request couldn't be made and to call the front desk.  We dialed the front desk and got an "all representatives are busy, please hold."  We hung up after 20 minutes and walked the 8 minutes to the front desk to check out.  

I'll give them the benefit of the doubt, with it being a busy time.  However, I felt a lot more relaxed when we left not being surrounded by screaming kids and many drunk adults.

reviews.author: Kaimada
reviews.title: A bit outdated but very very nice property
reviews.text:
A friend and I decided last minute to enjoy our Easter weekend at the Phoenician.  The property is quite large and nice.  Despite having a ton of guests, I always felt like it was low season (except at the pool) as everyone is spread out doing a variety of things.  We found the rooms quite nice, enjoyed the variety of eating options and certainly appreciated the fact that we didn't have to leave the property.

I will say that the best part was the service.  We found everyone to be very helpful, always offering water, etc.  A special thanks to the concierge who was always willing to help, share a laugh and smiled the whole time.  The only exception was a couple of waitresses serving on the patio outside of the main bar - they weren't very excited to be working, let alone serving anyone.  Regardless of that hiccup, we felt that everyone working there was intent on making the stay very nice.

I'm a platinum Starwood member so I was lucky to use points/cash for the room (although I think this did put us in a nice room but without any view but the backside of a retaining wall) but I do think it would have been worth it to pay the full price (with a better view) for a special weekend.

reviews.author: 865Anne
reviews.title: Wonderful staff, they could not have been better, especially the concierges!
reviews.text:
We have just come back from the most wonderful week at the Phoenician.  Despite the hotel being 100% full the staff were amazing.  They seemed to keep everything running smoothly without making it obvious.  We found the concierges and bar staff particularly helpful and charming and the beautiful terrace is a perfect place to relax with a few cocktails.
The fitness center was well equipped and there was always plenty of clean towels and water and my daughter and I did the Yoga classes as well as having several treatments at the gorgeous Spa.
So! A big negative was the lack of sun beds by the pool caused by the ridiculous behavior of some of the guests who set their alarms for 5.30am in order to bag sun loungers. Despite these blocked sun loungers remaining unoccupied most of the time whilst the 'owners' played tennis, golf etc.. no one else could use them.  It is difficult to see what the hotel can do about this level of selfishness! 
We are planning to go back to the Phoenician next year as this was the only annoying thing, but I will probably bring my own sun lounger! Unless anyone can suggest a remedy....

reviews.author: Mike F
reviews.title: Great service, location, facilities
reviews.text: This was our first visit to the area, during Spring Break.  Most noteworthy was the friendly service among every hotel employee we encountered.  While the facilities look a little old, built in the 1980s, they are well maintained.  The pool area is spectacular.  And there's plenty to do on and off the property - tennis, golf, hiking, taking in a spring training baseball game.  We didn't use the dining options too much but the breakfast at Il Terrazzo was supurb - both the food and the relaxed outside seating.

reviews.author: Sandra D
reviews.title: Not up to par for price
reviews.text: I'm shocked they could have a 5D rating.  No way with the condition of the rooms interior should this property be rated that high.     Old old furniture carpet and bed.  Bathroom nice and renovated.  Outdoor areas and course were very pretty.  Staff was extremely nice and all service of our 5 day spring break stay was impeccable.  Pool chairs situation created constant arguments and scuffles between guests. Totally unacceptable scenario while on vacation to listen to and to personally deal with.   Food was very good for every meal even with our special requests for picky eater.  Too dated and WAY overpriced for quality of room.

reviews.author: twjones100
reviews.title: An aging gem but I still love it.
reviews.text:
I have been coming to The Phoenician off and on since the late 1980's and have just returned from my 11th visit.  There have been good visits and not so good visits but at the end of the day, despite things that have gone wrong, i love to come to this place. I must say that I agree with some of the current reviews from other travelers.... The place could use some updating and deep cleaning.  What once was definitely a 5-diamond property could use a little cash infusion from the Starwood Ownership.

Here is my current assessment:

PROS: - When housekeeping forgot to clean our room unit 9pm, the hotel did a nice thing and comped our dinner without asking.  A nice gesture indeed.

CONS: - 
(1)  even though we have been there many, many times... there is no note in our file that we are repeat guests and therefore no regonition of our loyalty. Quite disappointing.

(2) allowing guests who are not present to reserve prime pool seats at a ridiculous hour of the morning (5:oo am) and then not return until late morning or after lunch to claim those seats... and sometimes not at all.  There is a sign posted that all items not claimed by 9:00 am will be removed but that was never enforced.  Everyone at the pool was discussing their frustration.  It is not a good practice for the hotel to continue to allow.  In addition, you do not pay these room rates to sit on plastic apartment pool furniture that filled the overflow.  

(3) Adding an additional night to our reservation almost 2 weeks prior to check in resulted in the first night being spent in a casita and the need to change rooms for the balance of the reservation.  Not cool on any account.

(4) Billing - despite changing the billing method at check-in, the first days charges did not change when the room changed.  When we attempted to sort it at check out, we were told that could not be taken care of at the front desk but instead would result in us having to contact "central accounting" and would take a multiple days for an adjustment to happen AFTER the charges were sorted.  SERIOUSLY?? When you are traveling, who has time to do that? It seems to me they should be responsible for their mistake.... making it as easy on the guest as possible. 

General observations:

ROOM:  A room in the main building... great, comfortable size but needed a deep cleaning.
 (my curtains and carpet in the room had stains and spills on them). Patio furniture is nasty and not up to par for this type of property.

POOL:  Bathrooms also need a deep cleaning and some better lighting at a minimum... but really need an update.  Walls in stalls were dirty and by early afternoon, there needed to be more servicing.  There was also not enough wait staff at the pool to properly service the guests.  I must add that i DESPISE the new "surge" kids area. While I appreciate the need for such space, it should not scream at you with the bright flashing lights, etc. It seems like there could have been a more refined way to excute... or perhaps another location on the property to place it.

DINING: I really like all of the options currently available on property... particularly J&G steakhouse upstairs and the breakfast buffet in the mornings.  i think all the drinks are about 25% too expensive at every venue.  It is nice to also have the option of the 

SPA:  again, a little dated but the spa staff is always well trained.

CONCIERGE:  current staff was very helpful and friendly this time... has not always been the case during previous stays.

GROUNDS:  always gorgeous.  they do an amazing job of keeping everything looking beautiful.  

All in all... really just minor issues but small improvements would go a long way in making this resort worth the dollars you spend.

reviews.author: Daniel U
reviews.title: Great Stay!
reviews.text:
I just returned to work from a fantastic weekend at The Phoenician and let's just say I'm having withdrawals! 

We arrived to the property very late (after 2am) and were greeted by a friendly gate attendant who directed us up the long drive. Once inside the Front Desk agent was ready with our keys (she knew we would be a late arrival) and gave very clear directions to our Casita. 

We were greeted by a lovely and large room that was exactly as expected. Clean, comfortable and ready for us to hit the bed! 

The resort was clearly very busy for the spring break period but every staff member encountered truly went above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable. 

My partner and I really enjoyed the spa facilities, the services were top notch and the relaxation areas were nicely appointed - I only wish they had a plunge pool! 

Thank you Phoenician for a fantastic celebration weekend - I can't wait to return!

reviews.author: Meghan C
reviews.title: Beautiful Spring Break Spot
reviews.text:
My family stayed here four nights during spring break.  After reading some of the recent reviews I was worried about the crowds. The resort and our room were beautiful but the staff at the Phoenician made our stay memorable. Everybody was so nice!  There are lots of cool things to do--teen lounge, the cactus garden and The Flight of the Phoenix were our favorites.

Yes, the pool was crowded but we always found a place to sit. If you have older kids the lawn is a better place to be.

reviews.author: Kent K
reviews.title: Old, worn, needs remodel
reviews.text: We went for baseball Spring Training.  The wallpaper in our room was curling up along the seams.  Visible wear patterns in the dirty carpet.  Old, dark hallways with worn carpet.  Not what we expected from a resort which represents itself as a five diamond property.  We would rate it two stars, tops.

reviews.author: Skych8ser
reviews.title: WAY overpriced for this once fabulous hotel
reviews.text:
They have let it go. It's old and tired and has lost it's charm. The Phoenician used to be the go-to resort, I wouldn't recommend it now. I must give huge kudos to the staff as they are all amazing and go out of their way to make your stay the best it can be. 

Rooms (in the main building). Very old and tired. I promise that you have not seen color schemes like this since the 70's. Furniture, carpet and drapes need replacement. Truly an embarrassment  considering the status this place once held. On a good note, the bed is comfortable as are the pillows and linens. The bathroom has clearly been renovated and was huge. The room was very spacious, large enough to make into a suite. Equally as spacious was the balcony (back side of the building with no view). The lounge chair cushions were old and dirty however. We could easily hear noise coming from the room beside us...this could have been due to the adjoining door. 

If lounging poolside is part of your plan, get there EARLY! Hard to say how early that would be, as we were there at 7:00 and every chair was taken. This is absurd. Get it together Phoenician. Every guest around me was complaining about it.

reviews.author: sissy2048
reviews.title: Don't bother, not worth the money.
reviews.text: Our stay was ok, but certainly not a 5 star, luxury resort. We stayed in a grand deluxe room which was dated. Carpet was old and patio furniture pillows were old and worn-out. I didn't even want to sit on them. If you want to lay-out by the pool, you better get there as early as 5:30 a.m. to hold a lounge chair as they do not have enough lounge chairs to accommodate guests. Service was slow at the pool area. This resort needs some major renovations. Not worth the money. Find somewhere else to stay.

reviews.author: ludwig d
reviews.title: Nice but not my style/dated
reviews.text:
We stayed there around NYE last year and although the place is clean and well kept, the overall look was dated. Our bathroom looked like it was designed in the 60's.

The outdoor space is nice. Great pools, although it was so cold when we went that we didn't get to sue them.

Avoid the SPA though. Treatments were OK but the Jacuzzi/steam area is more than dated, it needs to be redone.

reviews.author: Nscreative
reviews.title: Like a cruise ship on the ground
reviews.text: This resort has much to offer, especially its three tiers of pools so adults get serenity and kids enjoy a waterslide.  The breakfast buffet is fabulous at the main building and lunch near the golf club satisfying.  The views of Camelback Mountain and the cactus walk are delightful.  If you golf, you will love it all.  The gym and spa are a hike from main building unless you stay in a casita.  The buildings are a bit dated-very 1980s concrete or neo-adobe, but rooms are spacious.  Prices are high for everything.  The front desk gave us a room which was occupied and we had to wait an hour for another room.  Not fun.  The maid service was efficient.  All told, a big resort that isn't for everyone but quite luxurious.

reviews.author: KublaC
reviews.title: Don't do it...
reviews.text:
Let me just go through my week so far.
1) arrived 10:30am on Saturday
2) told room was not ready which was expected, no specific time frame given for availability so we went and had a great brunch
3) at noon one of the managers offers to call and check on the room.  We are told that they are finishing up cleaning
4) go up stairs to lobby to wait for the room. At 2pm we are told that "...we have until 4 so..."
5) check at 4 - still no room
6) get a call at 4:30 that the room is ready.  When we go to the desk the bell man says he had already removed our luggage from the room because he was told we didn't like the room.  So we were given a room that no one else wanted.  What happened to the suite I paid 192,000 points for.  (Yes points Starwood gold member for years)
7) we saw the room. It is basically the party room at the end of a hall of about 12 conference rooms and it looks it.  Huge patio with no view - awful room for a wife and kid - it's like being in a cave for work.  1/4 mile walk away from anything.
8) we turn down room. At this point it's 6pm on Friday. We've been there 7 and a half hours now for those keeping track.  No suites available. We are stuck in it for one night 
9) a bright side - we are given a Casita Suite for Sunday - Wednesday.  Great room
10) Wednesday we go on a morning excursion great Tomcar tour in the dessert.  We get back about noon with no word of where we are going next.  So, thankful for an opportunity to shower we do.  I walk to he front desk to inquire no am told again to wait for a call.  While I am at the front desk a cleaning woman that speaks no English sees that we are still in the room.
11). About an hour after the cleaning lady stops I get a call from the manager of he vapid group at check in ready for a fight.  I tell her we were told to wait for a call and had no idea what to do. (All true)
12) we are moved to a king deluxe room and I am not sure how a rollaway is going to fit without throwing furniture on the porch.  

So about 12 hours lost to waiting for the front desk to figure out reservations and moves, 192,000 points burned on a suite that I don't have.  But I can say that the bellman, valets, and service staff are great.  He front desk couldn't seat a 20 table restaurant.

reviews.author: LorraineChance
reviews.title: A Brunch to Remember!
reviews.text:
I've brunched at The Terraces at the great Phoenician resort for 27 years - guests used to dance to a band back in 1987!

The food buffet has always been very good and substantial, but nowadays it has reached haute cuisine levels, with healthy alternatives and exquisite small dishes like tuna carpaccio, shrimp in marie rose sauce, italian meats and live cooked omelets and carved meats.

The desserts are 'to die for'. I counted 14 different dishes with something for every palate, including sensational chef baked bombolones (light donuts with vanilla sauce)

Above all else, the service is as good as ever; superbly trained staff and a brilliant manager in Manuela Gonzalez.

reviews.author: Ceri M
reviews.title: Super relaxing resort in a beautiful location
reviews.text:
We stayed at The Phoenician for 4 nights and loved every minute of it. The resort is beautiful and the backdrop of Camelback Mountain is amazing. We stayed in a West-facing Grand Deluxe room and enjoyed a beautiful sunset each evening.

We had lunch at the Relish Burger Bistro and the Oasis Pool Bar & Grill and enjoyed each of them immensely. We also had tea one afternoon in the Lobby Tea Court which was well worth it. We didn't try any of the restaurants for breakfast or dinner.

We played tennis each day, one hour on a hard court and another hour on the grass court (the whole reason for our trip). This was our first experience playing on a grass court and it was fun. We learned fairly early that we couldn't really play competitive tennis that was fun as the points ended too quickly, but just hitting on the courts was a lot of fun.

We definitely plan on returning for another stay at The Phoenician.

reviews.author: jjder8
reviews.title: Great location, facilities and staff, but guestrooms in need of renovation.
reviews.text: We've been staying here for almost 20 years due to the location, staff, and facilities.  But they are charging a premium price for rooms that are sorely in need of renovation.  A few years ago, for example, we checked into a room with a clogged toliet and a non-functioning AC system.  We had to wait almost 3 hours while they fixed it.  Apparently the suites were recently renovated but I was told by a staff member that they usually would do renovations in the summer (slow season) but they have high occupancy then due to large price reductions offered to the locals so the hotels is not in a rush to renovate.

reviews.author: CB328
reviews.title: So, that was a disaster
reviews.text: It's hard to write this review, since The Phoenician holds such sentimental value for us. We got married on the property, and have returned on special occasions through the years, including a family Easter Week stay two years ago. What a disaster today's attempted check in was! First of all, the (high) room category that we had booked months ago was oversold. Shockingly, we were asked to downgrade to another room!?! Then we literally couldn't find a single lounge chair at the vast pool area - at 10:30 am! Finally, my 6-year old daughter was not allowed admittance to the kids club because they were overbooked. Enough was enough. We left the property immediately, and checked into the Four Seasons, where we experienced attentive service. We appreciate that it's a very, very busy week in Arizona; but we would have appreciated if the Phoenician took better care of us, with nightly room rates topping $600! We hope to return to the hotel someday. It's an awe-inspiring property. We just hope the service returns, as well.

reviews.author: Charles808
reviews.title: Nice but just ok
reviews.text: We had high hopes but left saying we would stay elsewhere the next time we were in the area. Our room was clean and comfortable and about a 10 minute walk to the lobby and pool area. The prices were high and the property felt chaotic. Granted, it was a busy spring break week but a 5-star hotel should promise great service no matter what time of the year it is. There weren't enough chairs at the pool and the pool staff was running around and hard to flag down. The servers in the lounge were friendly and efficient. Overall, it is a big property that did not feel personal or warm. If you prefer this and are willing to pay high prices, this could be a good choice for you.

reviews.author: CaliforniaFussbudget
reviews.title: I just want to sit down.
reviews.text:
Finding a lounge chair is the height of first world problems, I know, but all I want to do at a resort pretty much is pool time. First day we sat in restaurant area for an hour waiting for a chair to open up. The pool guy was supposed to call us when he found one. I went to see how we were doing and he was chatting with someone so I pounced when someone left. You have to get up early and put a magazine on a chair and then most of the day those people don't show up. Anyway, the Phonecian is very crowded and big - rooms on long hallways and not super. 
Lots of kids and a big meeting when we were there. I agree not a 5 star for $600. 
I can fight for a chair for half that. The staff were good for the most part and food decent. I wouldn't go back because I don't have kids and look for quiet and the hotel is aging. Resorts need to build pools enough for everyone - I've seen this before. I think must add on rooms or something. There were extra plastic loungers galore on the AstroTurf! Near the pool - pretty sure that's not what the architect had in mind. Easily 250 people in the pool area. It's large but not large enough. So, if you're looking for quiet and a sense of luxury and exclusivity this is not it. More like a Marriott.

reviews.author: MikeCamel
reviews.title: Another conference, another excellent stay
reviews.text: I find it difficult to fault this hotel.  I've visited twice, now, and been impressed on both occasions.  Both times, it's been for a conference, and I had less time to enjoy the hotel this time than the last, sadly.  it's a great place for a business conference, golfing (by all accounts), and even seems to handle family visits rather well.  Recommended, again.

reviews.author: Ryan B
reviews.title: Best place i have ever been to!
reviews.text: Very fun place to go with a family! Cactus garden was awesome and beautiful nice trails! Pools were huge and awesome so much fun! The slide was the best I went really fast and the landing pool is thankfully warm! Basketball in the pool is really fun! There is a kids splash pad in case you want to cool off. Tennis courts were awesome

reviews.author: ttgrant
reviews.title: Mediocre at best
reviews.text: Unfortunately, this resort did not meet the expectation for a 5 star SPG luxury collection property. The grounds are beautiful, however the rooms are dated, the service is below average and the pool area is fool of heavily drinking young people. So unless you are a group of college kids looking for a fun spring break experience - I recommend finding a different resort.

reviews.author: mccown53
reviews.title: 5 Star?
reviews.text: The rooms and flooring are in need of replacing.  The staff at times appeared to be bothered by questions. The grounds are beautiful as is the main lobby, but that's about it.  We asked for a ground floor and were placed right by a busy street where the linen trucks, etc., drove by constantly.  I will say that the housekeeping staff were very friendly and helpful.  In need of help to remain a 5 star.

reviews.author: terryw678
reviews.title: Wow in every aspect
reviews.text: The location, grounds, rooms, staff, spa, golf lessons and restaurants were all super. Our room was very large and had sliders out to a quiet nook with flowing water nearby. The staff was all friendly, helpful and knowledgable. We enjoyed 2 breakfasts and 2 dinners on property in 3 of their restaurants, all were expensive but worth it. Nice housekeeping touches like slippers by the bed. We never used the pool or exercise, but they looked nice. My husband took a golf lesson that included playing a round with the pro, he really enjoyed it and learned lots. While he did that I enjoyed a full day at the spa, had 5 treatments including an unusual cupping massage as I like to try the unusual when I travel. Extremely helpful concierge staff.

reviews.author: ninaortiz
reviews.title: Really bad experience BE AWARE of how they use your credit card
reviews.text: This is definitely the worst hotel I have ever stayed at. I went to that hotel for a business conference, since I  did my check in it was a nightmare! They have been charging my credit card for different reasons that not even the hotel can explain. This has been going on as far as three weeks after I checked out. It is ridiculously pricey for what they offer in my option IS NOT 5 STAR RESORT at all. The hotel has a nice garden and a beautiful pool but that is it. My advise stay away from this hotel spend your money in a better place where they are not going to use your credit card as they please.

reviews.author: plh66
reviews.title: Best tennis facility anywhere
reviews.text:
After several decades of annual trips to the Phoenician, the tennis facility remains one of the best parts of the resort.  It is beautifully designed and maintained and the staff, especially Belinda, the tennis shop manager, is so welcoming and accommodating. 

Overall, the property is amazing.  The guest rooms, however, are in great need of updating.  They smell musty on entry and the furnishings feel and look very dated.  For a property of this stature, attention needs to be paid to bringing the guest rooms up to a higher standard.

it remains a wonderful family vacation destination.

reviews.author: HopeM1
reviews.title: Swoon worthy! Oasis!
reviews.text: I Love this place,,,,no really really love it. I am not a golfer ( if I was I might be more in love). But I am an artist and I painted in the amazing cactus garden full of fabulous specimens. If you like to sketch of paint stay here!!!!! in luxury And beauty.

reviews.author: MandDplus2
reviews.title: Disappointing.  5 star resort; 2 star room.
reviews.text: Our family stayed at the Phoenician's Canyon Suites last June and my review was entitled "Wow!".  It was deservedly the best review I'd ever written. For March break we decided to stay at the Phoenician.The 2 properties share the resort; but that is about all they share. First, some pros: The resort property is beautiful. The lawns and gardens are amongst the best we've seen. The main lobby is large and grand. The burger bistro Relish was our favourite on site restaurant with delicious food, excellent service and casual but classy ambiance.  There are numerous pools that are kept at a nice temperature. Some general cons: pool was woefully understaffed for March break time. Towels were piled up and often not available. The bathrooms ran out of paper towels with garbage cans overflowing and filthy floors. Food service was slow and spotty. Newspaper delivery didn't happen, and when I'd go to lobby to get one (before 9 am) they were usually "all gone". As for our specific experience: We stayed in a casita room in order to have our car handy and be close to the pools. It was very clear there are different classes of rooms here, regardless of the room category. The casitas that are closer to the pool are bright and open up onto the lawn and a fountain looking at the resort and camelback mountain. The casitas south of these border the entrance ways (and roads) and golf course. Our first room was on the first floor in the "O" building and without a doubt had a notation: "do not rent out ... unless it is March break"!  Worst room we have ever stayed in, 5 star or otherwise.  Dark, dingy, stained carpets, bubbling and peeling wall paper, unusable walk-out deck. The safe wasn't working (low battery signal) and wooden hangers in closet had an inch of dust (clearly the room hadn't been rented in a long time ...).  How does Starwood reconcile a 5 star resort with advertised AAA and 5 diamond service and quality and let out rooms in this condition? "Fully booked" is how. After 2 nights I went to desk at 9 am to at least voice my displeasure assuming nothing could happen as the hotel was fully occupied.  Kaitlin was the supervisor and apologized profusely. No argument from her on state of room. She said we could move that day and it would be ready in the early afternoon but without question by 4 pm. I was very grateful. Phew. We packed after lunch and room wasn't ready until 4:30. We were moved to building H which was still a casita in the "second tier" of buildings on the roadway. But it is on the second floor with a view of golf course so at least brighter and the drive-by car noise not as loud. Arrived after dinner at 8:30 pm and the room was really warm despite the AC set to 68 so we called the front desk. Tony the engineer (great guy) came to check it out. He was up on the roof for 20 minutes and advised that the compressor was shot so no air conditioning for the night ... My husband went to the front desk and had a tete a tete with the on duty manager. The foregoing issues were explained along with our frustration. She said they would do something for us and move us again if air didn't work the next day. We left the room at 8 am to let Tony and crew fix the AC; it just started working when we arrived back at 2 pm. Ultimately, after a feeble offer of a meal (no drinks) at Relish as an apology to us, the hotel comped us 2 nights of our 6. This was the right thing to do and was appreciated, but it doesn't take away from the incredibly negative experience we had. If you have the $ to stay at Canyon Suites, by all means, jump at the chance. But unless there are some major renovations to the rooms at the Phoenician (we were told by more than 1 staff member that major renovations for the casistas are planned for the Fall!), and given the array of luxury 5 star resorts in Scottsdale (Four Seasons, Biltmore, Fairmont, JW Marriott etc), the risk of a bad room (less than 5 stars!) given the cost of the stay is not worth it. We will return to Scottsdale but doubtfully stay again at the Phoenecian.

reviews.author: jimcor317
reviews.title: Great relaxation
reviews.text:
Hotel, service, ambiance, golf course, & spa under the control of the Phoenician were top notch. Only negative was that I booked via Southwest Vacations who used Expedia as their hotel packager.  I thought the package route for Air & hotel would be more convenient.  Unfortunately, I believe the % of the room fee paid by SWA/ Expedia reduced the hotel's yield that the available room was very distant from the lobby and the pools, etc.  The room quality was very nice - just a long walk away.   Prior to booking via SWA vacations,  I checked the hotel web site and verified that the per day room cost was comparable.   

My conclusion is that there are two extra commissions when using SWA vacations so that the hotel's yield is much lower - they fill distant comparable rooms with SWA/Expedia bookers.

I will stay at the Phoenician again. I just will take the extra step and book directly online.

reviews.author: Debbie M
reviews.title: Service is excellent, property is beautiful, beds not so good..
reviews.text: The property is beautiful, the service is excellent and the rooms are very clean and good size. This said, the beds are uncomfortable as are the chairs in the rooms.  Room décor is simple and furniture is in good shape, the style is outdated in my opinion.  The pools are very nice, but it’s hard to find a chair on a crowded day.  You may end up on a less comfortable lounge set off in the grass away from the pool.  Not great if you are watching kids.  The restaurants on property are just OK and definitely overpriced. Another issue, due to security, cabs can’t get on property, so unless you happen to catch one that is dropping off a guest or willing to wait 30 to 40 minutes for the hotel to call one for you, you are stuck using the onsite car service.  While very nice, they are expensive and you can find yourself paying $25 + tip for a 12 minute drive..   When you add on round trip car transportation costs to dinner it suddenly makes the on property restaurants less expensive.. though still not as tasty.  This issue makes the location bad, unless you have a car.

reviews.author: Robin T
reviews.title: Luxurious....
reviews.text: Recently held a business conference at this resort and it did not disappoint! This resort is rated 5 stars / 5 diamonds because it is just that!  The customer service and attentiveness to their guests is unsurpassed.  We were given early check in (before noon!) on all of our requests (10 rooms), the valet staff went above and beyond to ensure transportation for our attendees and the banquet staff were knowledgeable and always available.  The rooms were nicely appointed and the beds were like sleeping at home.  The resort is geared towards golfing and the course is in excellent shape!  Would definitely book here again.

reviews.author: kawhitcomb1
reviews.title: Falling thru the cracks on the service this time.
reviews.text: We have stayed hear many times before, but this was the first time it was a disappointment.  Our suite was not ready when we arrived, they called us at 6:15pm to say we could get in a room.  This ment we had to go to dinner without a shower or changing cloths after a long day of flying.  The room we were given was more of a overflow room (I heard from a room attendant).  The room was fine and the terrace would have been great, if it hadn't been totally surrounded by roof tops and an exhaust fan from a kitchen area.  The room has an odor due to the exhaust plus a bit musty.  All this on a Platinum membership with Starwood!

reviews.author: Jbet44
reviews.title: Excellent Business Conference Destination
reviews.text: Stayed at The Phoenician for a business conference in February.  Excellent service all-around, what you would expect from a highly rated destination hotel.  Knowledgeable and helpful staff were available even opening up a store after hours to get some advil.  The hotel was comfortable with inviting restaurant and bar areas.  I was pleasantly surprised by the high quality meals served at lunch and dinner.  The rooms were spacious and comfortable. I did not get a chance to explore the grounds to the fullest (no golf either) but I am planning to come back very soon!

reviews.author: terminal454
reviews.title: Phoenician does well -
reviews.text:
the grounds were very nice but I thought too skewed to the golfers, more walk areas should be open to the rest of the guests.
to be a real five diamond resort  this hotel needs another restaurant for lunch and dinner.
the burger sandwich spot for the golf course was ok and the italian style was good for breakfast, so so for lunch.   The steak house upstairs was nice - but only open for dinner.
A guest shouldn't have to leave the premises for a decent lunch.

the pool areas were well kept - I think a games room might be an idea.
the workout room was well appointed but could use a bit more free weights for those who can handle more than 20-40 lbs.

the cactus walk in the back was nicely done.

Our casita had this annoying whistle every 15 minutes or so - must've been mechanical - I would advise staff to look into it - Casita A, ground floor near the pool

reviews.author: Sean J
reviews.title: Stunning resort and excellent service
reviews.text: I stayed at the Phoenician on February 18th and I was initially impressed from the moment I was drove on to the grounds. Well kept property with a gorgeous mountain in the backround. When I say the staff there gets it, they get when it comes to service!!! One of the best experiences I've had in regards to the staff genuinely making sure my stay was comfortable and pleasant. There are plenty of pool and outdoor activities to satisfy whatever you are looking to do, or if you simply want to relax, they have everything you want right on the premises. The Fitness center is awesome as well. I recommend this Resort absolutely. I cannot wait to go back!!!

reviews.author: tina p
reviews.title: Amazing Service!!
reviews.text: During my spa day visit, I had the best hospitality and received the best invigorating spa treatment.  The pool service was over the top!  The pool was safe, CLEAN, and fun along with some fun music. My kids enjoyed the slide and the big gold fish.  Of course the red white and blue drinks were a hit too.  The facility is large but sooo charming.  We cannot wait to return.  Thank you for a "staycation" we cannot wait to come for the weekend!

reviews.author: Kevin B
reviews.title: Comfortable and enjoyable stay.
reviews.text: Excellent spot to spend a Phoenix / Scottsdale vacation at.  First class accommodations, service and surroundings.  Enjoyed time there with our adult sons recently, having stayed there with them years ago to close out a Grand Canyon trip.  Happy with both experiences.  Golf courses are scenic, fun, in great condition and very playable for mid to high handicaps as well. Pools are excellent, though I wish the "Adult Pool" rules were enforced, as our quiet afternoon of lounging included several 5-7 year olds playing Marco/Polo in the adult only area.  A little frustrated that there was no parental or staff supervision the one day we chose to relax by the pool.  But small issue compared to our wonderful time in general.  Will stay there again next time to the area.  Lastly...I see other comments regarding service...our room was always immaculate and our wait staff attentive.  Even remembering our names at certain tables and at the lobby piano lounge after a couple of days.  Very professional.

reviews.author: RAK350
