reviews.title: If you have the means, I highly recommend
reviews.text:
It is been a number years since I have stayed at the Phoenician, but in the words of Ferris Bueller, "If you have the means I would highly recommend".  This resort is by far one of my all-time favorite's.  Rooms are comfortable, grounds are spectacular & what sets this place apart is the exceptional service.  Really, I probably sleep in hotels @75 nights a year and you forget that places like this actually exist.

I was here on business but, I need to return with my family.

reviews.author: LiviaLinda
reviews.title: Not worthy the money
reviews.text:
I was in the pool for 2 hours and I never got a service, I asked 4 servers to help me, and they just ignored me and never came to my table.
 The pool service is not a 4 stars, worst pool service I ever had

reviews.author: MBMalm
reviews.title: Thank you, Charlie Blonkenfeld!
reviews.text:
During my stay here at the Phoenician I have found myself sick with shingles during a national sales meeting. I was not able to participate in the dinner that took place tonight, and am stuck in my room.  I requested a plate of food be sent to my room, and Charlie delivered a lovely meal and kind smile. He was empathetic, as well as accommodating. 
I will certainly return to the Phoenician the next time I am in Arizona.

reviews.author: sherrynongratis
reviews.title: Not so outstanding the second time...
reviews.text:
We stayed here in April 2013 and I wrote an awesome review.  We had loved this place.  Could not wait to return...

We came back in Feb. and the service was poor....over & over again.  

After check-in, we went to our Casita & had a nice patio overlooking the water fountain.  There were smashed tortilla chips all over one of the chairs and on the patio floor.  Obviously the housekeepers did not clean the patio area when the old guests left.  It made me wonder what else was not cleaned prior to arrival.  Missing hairdryer in the room as well.

I ordered dinner from the steakhouse on property to go.  I walked all the way over to the main building to pick it up & when I got back I noticed they had forgotten my cheesecake.  No biggie, but the place was empty.  I called and they delivered it to my room.

Ordered room service one morning before a hike up Camelback Mountain.  The order form is to be filled out & left on outside doorknob before 11 pm.  I left it out before 9:00 pm.  I was in a hurry that morning and wondered why room service had not shown up?  I checked the door and my order was never even picked up.  The order form was not picked up.

Pool service out by the adults only pool was poor.  We had warm pitchers of water with melted ice and no one coming by to refresh it.  Had to flag down servers.  This was not a busy season, mind you.  They were out of their advertised frozen Milky Way bars the entire stay.  Every day we asked, every day they told us they were sold out.

Service by the coffee shop was slow.  The servers couldn't handle the orders at breakfast time.  One day, I went for lunch and it was slow.  I ordered & paid for a few desserts and after waiting a while for them to bag them, I realized they had totally forgotten about me and the desserts.

Not sure what the deal was with the service this time, but it definitely changed my mind about staying here again.  Like I said, it was not a busy time of the year and occupancy was low.  It's a shame...it really is a lovely property in a spectacular setting.   However, there are many beautiful resorts in the Phoenix/Scottsdale to choose from and that is exactly what we will do the next time we stay in this area....choose another resort.  

Sorry, Phoenician, you fell short this time.

This is not the type of service one would expect staying at a luxury property.

reviews.author: bretdb
reviews.title: Excellent Stay in Scottsdale
reviews.text:
The Phoenician has to be one of the best hotels in the entire world! We were there right before Thanksgiving 2014 for a convention. The weather was spectacular but the hotel and it's staff were even better! From the manager of the steak restaurant to the front desk people (who found my wife's earring somewhere in the hotel) to the parking attendants - all superb and over the top. 

The dinners and breakfasts were unbelievable and we can't wait to go back!

reviews.author: CBROOM64
reviews.title: junior staff results in less than perfect service
reviews.text:
Stayed at The Phoenician with two kids and two adults.  When we checked in, I asked if the cribs we requested (and I had called many times to confirm) were in the room, because in my experience with ALL hotels, they usually are not.  The woman who checked us in assured that the crib was in the room and if they were not, then housekeeping would take care of the matter quickly.  Well, that was not true. We arrived and realized the cribs were not in the room and told the gentleman who helped us with our bags and called housekeeping.  45 minutes passed.  At this point, it was way past our 7 month old and 2 year old's bedtime, they were screaming and tired, and we were afraid we were going to miss the rehearsal dinner for the wedding we were in town for.  We called and the front desk assured us that the cribs were "on their way".  "On their way" is code speak for "i have no earthly idea where they are".  Long story short, it was not until TWO HOURS after check in that someone came with cribs.  we of course, missed our dinner, was furious, and then the manager had the gall to call us to apologize and to see if there was something he (she? i didn't answer the phone, it was my husband who answered the phone) could do.  in my experience, when a hotel messed up this badly, the manager calls WITH a solution, not a weak apology.  How about "i'm so sorry this happened to you, we would like to offer you free internet.  Or comp you a meal.  Or give you a voucher."  not "how can i help?"  such an open ended question infuriated me and i told my husband that there was nothing that could be done.  our evening was ruined and i wasn't going to waste energy in trying to figure out a solution.  that was not my job.  

the issue seems to be that the staff is very junior and under-trained.  for example, we were wandering the halls for a nice family breakfast.  we stopped a young lady to see if there was "a place for our family to eat, perhaps at a buffet?"  she looked at us as if we had 7 heads.  she asked us, "buffet?"  we were so put off by the incident the night before that we quickly thanked her and found a restaurant packed with families, serving, surprise! a breakfast buffet.  

it is frustrating when i travel to a hotel and it seems like the majority of the staff who work there have never even stayed at a 4 star resort themselves.

reviews.author: kazootripper
reviews.title: Great place and great people.
reviews.text: From start to finish the hotel and the staff were great. The hotel was price at the upper end for hotels in the are and after our stay I would say it was priced fairly. The only negative I would bring up is the layout of the hotel. Try to get a room on the lobby and pool side, a lot less walking. We had 4 couples in our group, nice golfing for the guys and the wife's enjoyed the pools, spa and the shopping.

reviews.author: ttj1028
reviews.title: Fabulous hotel - excellent for family, business or fun with friends!
reviews.text:
My family loves the hotel.  There is always so much to do.  I would request a room close to the pool area when the kids are with you.  The property has great pools and I do think it is worth it to rent a cabanna at the adult pool (older kids fine)  You don't have to fight for chairs etc.  
The location of the hotel is perfect with great golf, hiking and fabulous shopping all of which you can walk to!  There is even a movie theater at the mall that the teens can do to keep busy at night!
Restaurants in the area are wonderful too!  The Henry, North, Chelseas Kitchen and LGO to name a few.

reviews.author: JMG672014
reviews.title: Phoenician in Feb. 2015
reviews.text:
We stayed here for a week in Feb. 2015 and had a great time!
we have an 8 year old so wanted a kid friendly resort with a great pool area, the Phoenician fits the bill! Plenty of activity's for children going on everyday to keep them busy while the parents relax.
The grounds are very well kept, the staff great, very friendly, helpful and always nearby. The location is perfect, close to great shopping, restaurants and the traffic moves quickly down Camel back road with no congestion!

This is definitely our new favorite resort in the Scottsdale area and we will return there often!

reviews.author: Mark D
reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text: An impeccable resort at the foot of Camelback Mountain!  Everything about this resort is absolutely top shelf, but the service is absolutely amazing!   Rooms are nicely appointed and very comfortable.  The pool area is gorgeous and the lounges are wonderful - the prickly pear margarita is NOT to be missed!  I highly recommend this resort!

reviews.author: Alaskanabroad
reviews.title: Great place for superbowl weekend
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is a spendy but fairly simple hotel located in the center of the Phoenix metro area. Access to the freeways is not the best but neither are the hotels that are close to the freeways.

Be prepared to spend a little extra. The grounds and service were what you would expect for a hotel of this quality. Nice lounge in the lobby.

I was there for the weekend of superbowl and TPA. The place was packed. However, it is spread out enough that you really didn't know it. Service was really quick with maybe an extra 5 minutes for valet.

Everything about this facility makes it a very relaxing, full service hotel for business or pleasure travel.

reviews.author: xygb7dklt
reviews.title: Camelback wrap-around
reviews.text: Was here for a business meeting and, although our room 5084 was large with a king bed, desk, lounge chairs, double closets, fridge/coffee maker and big bathroom, it had a stunning view of the roof of the conference center and the room balconies opposite. Their golf course wraps around Camelback Mountain and consists of 27 holes (three integrated 9-hole courses) with desert and lake features. At the rear of the hotel is a cactus garden with over 200 varieties displayed along a pathway which is illuminated in the evening. Rental bicycles are available or you can hike to the top of Camelback if your heart can take it. Sculptures and paintings by local artists are on display in the lobbies. There are a number of swimming pools and a water slide Did not use the spa. Saw many families with children and there is the “Funicians” activities club for kids. There is a concierge desk where you can arrange day tours to Sedona, Tombstone, Navajo Nation or Grand Canyon. Had a relaxing dinner outside on the Terrazzo restaurant. Menu was soups, salads, salmon, chicken and beef on an Italian theme. Service was attentive but not cloying. Picked up breakfast sandwiches and coffee at the Café and Ice Cream Parlor near the shopping arcade and main lobby which is brown and beige and has a fountain in the middle. Hotel staff were pleasant and efficient. The hotel taxi service took us to the Camelback entrance of Fashion Square Mall for $15; got a Scottsdale cab back for $10. But you do need a car if you stay here and we will rent one the next time.

reviews.author: Jeffrey L
reviews.title: You won't find better and more accommodating service
reviews.text:
Stay here for a few days annually before going on to our unit at the Westin Kierland Villas.  Golf course with 27 holes well maintained and a good layout. Rooms are clean and comfortable.  Marble and art throughout the property.  Check out the history of the resort's development--most interesting. Relish is a great lunch/co tail experience and J & G Steakhouse on property rivals any top notch steakhouse.
If you like to hike, Camelback Mountain Cholla trail is great exercise with outstanding views at no cost but Youe expended energy.
You can relax in luxury or take part in outdoor activity.  The resort is one mile away from Old Town Scottsdale  and interesting dining and shopping

reviews.author: ANOUL
reviews.title: We saw no flaws
reviews.text: We spent three nights there last week and we loved every minute of it. The service was invisible but excellent across the board. We didn't need to ask for anything basic, it was just done.......no muss no fuss. Breakfast, lunch dinner, no matter, service and food excellent each and ever time. Our room (Cottage) was very large, very clean and staff managed their schedule in accordance with ours. We had a plumbing issue that needed attention and the service  fellow was at our door almost before I hung up the phone. Here's a little thing; there's a lot of glass at the hotel, doors, walls, panels, etc.(used very effectively I might add). We never saw a smudge or fingerprint anywhere! This is a hotel that understands those kinds of touches.We see lots of high-end hotels now that we're older and able to travel. This is one of the ones we'll go back to.

reviews.author: boja69
reviews.title: KEEPS ON GETTING BETTER
reviews.text: I was there for five days and could not find a thing to complain about. Excellent food accompanied by outstanding service for buffet breakfast and for lunch in Il Terrazzo. Christina and Bernadine made the experience memorable. I rarely eat consecutively in any restaurant but we had four lunches here. (We ate dinner out each evening). The lobby bar brought personalized service to a new level. Sean remembered not only my drink but my name and room number after day one. I didn't think the Phoenician could improve but clearly they have and deserve high accolades.

reviews.author: AGC314
reviews.title: Poor customer service not becoming of a "5 star" establishment
reviews.text:
This review is in reference to my parents’ stay at the Phoenician Dec 26-30.  I booked the stay as part of a birthday gift for my father’s 70th birthday celebrations. I spent many hours researching hotels in Scottsdale, and given the numerous favorable reviews posted, I decided to choose the Phoenician. I booked the stay by phone with reservations agent Cheryl Byerle, who I have to say was the most helpful person throughout the entire ordeal. At the time of booking, I completed necessary paperwork to ensure that the entire stay and incidentals would be charged to my credit card, as the vacation was a gift to my parents. The paperwork was confirmed to be received, and in fact, 4 days before their arrival, Cheryl emailed me to reconfirm that they had my credit card info on file for the entire stay. I should add that I booked a rate that was to include breakfast.
So far, so good…. I thought. Upon my parents’ arrival, they were asked to provide their credit card for incidentals. Not knowing what I had actually contracted with the hotel, they went ahead and gave them their credit card. Apparently, the front desk did not notice that MY credit card was on file. Mistake number 1. The events that followed are not a testament to the “five star” quality that the Phoenician advertises.
The day of checkout, my parents received a folio detailing every charge with the entire stay charged to their credit card. What a great birthday present. Not only did they give them the bill, but they charged them as well?! In addition, apparently my parents were never told at check-in that breakfast was included in their stay. This was only realized by my parents upon seeing the bill and noting it was a “bed and breakfast rate”. On the bill were additional charges for room service (since my parents were not aware their rate included breakfast). Upon noticing his credit card was charged for the entire bill, my father went to the front desk to inquire about the situation. He told them that his daughter had paid for the stay… at which time they went back and looked at the notes and realized their error. Very little apology was offered. When he mentioned that no one ever told them about breakfast, and that they had used room service and were charged, he was offered a $10 credit (barely enough to cover a glass of juice). After more haggling (which at this point was purely ridiculous since there were multiple errors), the front desk removed the resort fee and some other charges, again offering very little in the way of an apology.
The story gets worse. Days after their stay was completed, I still had not received a copy of the folio, which I was told would be emailed to me upon checkout. When I emailed, then called to inquire, what I received was a very undetailed folio that showed my credit card was only charged for the room, not for incidentals. My parents had spa treatments, dined at the restaurant, etc. All that was charged to my father’s credit card. 
I proceeded to contact Cheryl, who put me in touch with Nathan Davidson, reservations supervisor. He apologized for the error and told me all charges had been corrected after my correspondence and my father’s credit card had been refunded. He was very nice via email and phone, but this was NOT ENOUGH OF AN APOLOGY! I subsequently asked for a detailed folio and to speak to the manager. I was referred to Bowen Kilker, front desk manager.
On January 9, I spoke to Mr. Kilker by phone. While the exchange was cordial, I reiterated my disappointment in the entire situation, and how upset I was that once the errors had been recognized, that I hadn’t been notified. The only reason I became aware of the errors was when I inquired about the bill. My father was so upset and kind of embarrassed (for us) by the whole situation that he never told me about it. At that time, Mr. Kilker told me who would send out a personal letter of apology to my parents, as well as a voucher towards a future stay at the hotel. This was little comfort to me given my parents’ celebration vacation had been ruined, but better than nothing. 
That brings me to today. As of yet, we have not received said letter of apology. On February 12, I emailed Mr Kilker to inquire about the status of said letter, and have received no response. I cannot express how disappointing and upset I am by this entire situation. I feel that the initial error was egregious enough, only to be snowballed by the ridiculous number of errors to follow. We, as well as our friends and family, are frequent visitors of the Phoenix area and its high end resorts, and this pretty much guarantees we will never again set foot in this hotel.

reviews.author: Michael T
reviews.title: Pool was very crowded
reviews.text:
Scottsdale is a very nice place to visit, much to do. The Phenician is quite a nice resort; the grounds are great and service excellent - but at this price point that is expected so I dont think you get extra stars for that. What detracted from our stay was the pool which was very crowded. Our family would typically go do something in the morning and head to the pool in the afternoon and we would have trouble finding open lounge chairs let alone three together. We inquired about renting a cabana but they were sold out the entire time we were there so I would suggest if you are interersted in that option book it at the time of room booking - and expect to pay - they are $300 a day during the week and go up to $325 or $350 I believe on the weekend. 
We had a one bedroom suite which had a strange C-shaped layout resulting in the sitting area to be quite narrow; in fairness the room had three balconies one of which was huge and when we were hanging out in the room we were outside. 
We had a good trip but it could have been, and at this price point I would say should have been, better.

reviews.author: 2Texas_Travellers
reviews.title: Nice, but not AAA five diamonds
reviews.text:
We spent a weekend at this property in February 2015. While we had a lovely time, it didn't meet my expectations of a AAA 5 diamond property.
We loved the personalized greeting at the guard gate and check in.
We had a casita overlooking the main pools. It was well appointed , but has several maintenance issues. Within one hour of checking in, we had to call security to fix the door lock ( after 3 rounds of keys) and maintenance to fix the broken faucet in the kitchen, non working phone, and two lights  that didn't work. 
We had dinner at the Italian concept restaurant . The setting was lovely and the food was wonderful. Unfortunately, our waiter took a very casual approach to addressing us, didn't know how to pace the meal and didn't have a decent knowledge of the wine list. We had to stop our meal and wait for the sommelier to come by and help,is to select a wine.
Breakfast the next mornng was another variation of the same. Great food, but an odd service experience. The hostess didn't have a sunny/ morning disposition. Requests for refills on tea and coffee weren't honored. When the meal was delivered, our check was also deposited. I felt like I was at Waffle House. The same check process happened on the next day. 
The gym was good but the equipment needed tuning and a good cleaning. The spa was good and had wonderful facials. Dinner at the steak concept was fun and we had a terrific server.
All in all, we had a nice weekend, but if recommend to the GM to take a critical,look at the maintenance (paint, concrete) at service at the property.

reviews.author: DillonJames
reviews.title: Beige and dated
reviews.text: The grounds of this property are incredible and very well maintained.  The lobby area and rooms are very beige and dated.  It feels a bit like a very nice funeral home in some ways.  The staff is excellent and very helpful.  The beds and sheets were awesome.  We stayed in one of the casitas which had a nice view of a lush green lawn area however, it is quite a maze to get back and forth to the hotel lobby and conference center. We had dinner one of the nights at the J&G Steakhouse on the property and because we were with a larger group, it felt like they were just there to "get us fed and out of there."  Poor service.  The exterior of the main hotel complex feels a bit like a concrete building out of the early 80's.  There are newer parts of the complex including sections of the conference center that were excellent.  The conference center food and snacks were great. We had great weather during our stay which made our stay that much better.

reviews.author: Traveling Traveler22
reviews.title: Beautiful property, service needs some work
reviews.text:
I stayed here for 3 nights with my wife and 21-month old son.  We loved the property, the pools, the food, etc. We thought the room was spectacular and made good use of the patio overlooking the pool. The grounds are beautiful and there is so much to do. For us it was a perfect resort and I would certainly stay here again based on the amenities and location.

We had some issues with the service and housekeeping, which was unexpected given a resort of this caliber.

All in all if you are looking for a beautiful, well-maintained property in Scottsdale and don't need exceptional service, I would highly recommend the Phoenician.

reviews.author: Clovernookwilly
reviews.title: Phoenician Exceeds Expectations
reviews.text:
I stayed 4 nights recently as part of a non-profit conference group.  We had three group meals there.....two in small group settings at two of the restaurants and one 1000 person banquet.  The two restaurants were very good and the banquet was well executed also.  All food was excellent and service good.  

The grounds of the hotel are beautiful,, especially the cactus garden in the back of the property.....don't miss it!

reviews.author: georgianna w o
reviews.title: Finer things...a well maintained property.
reviews.text: This hotel is meant for a somewhat mature crowd that cares about quality, service, and all the finer things in life. It is not ideal for kids, but that is what makes it nice too. I love that they have afternoon tea, fine dining choices, a some of the best views in Phoenix area. Such a pleasant stay. Kudos to great management. My room faced the entry area, but I didn't care. I think some views are not great, but what can you do other than plan ahead.  Highly recommend for a few days of relaxation or meeting up with friends or business associates. Cannot go wrong!

reviews.author: Michele L
reviews.title: LUXURIOUS DESERT RETREAT
reviews.text: We went to the resort for a business meeting. The resort is luxurious and the guests are catered to quite well. We look forward to going back. Wonderful amenities everywhere. Pool staff, especially Kye, was super. They were readily available to bring a pitcher of ice water, food drinks, towels, etc. Bernadine was a wonderful waitress for our buffet breakfast. The breakfast assortment was fresh, local, delicious.

reviews.author: K3Kim
reviews.title: Really great - in every way
reviews.text: We have just returned from a 6 night stay at one of the best hotels I have ever had the privilege of visiting.  Admittedly it is quite expensive, but the service is impeccable, the rooms and lobby areas were spacious and well appointed, and all the restaurants were a delight.  It was the service from all the staff members across the board that really sets this place apart from many others.

reviews.author: jncoop
reviews.title: Needs a major facelift.
reviews.text: We were told we had a view room. Sure, if you consider screaming kids coming down the waterslide a view. The room was an average size, but the décor was outdated, worn and stained. We took photos of the dirty carpet, stained curtains, threadbare upholstery, and chipped furniture. The worst was the lanai where birds had perched. There was bird poop all over the walls. The "relaxation pool", previously the adult pool, was filled with kids and pool toys. We left within an hour and went to the Biltmore, a gem designed by Frank Lloyd Wright. Cheaper and fabulous!

reviews.author: IWriteforFooddotcom
reviews.title: Consistent Excellence
reviews.text: The Phoenician never seems to change.  I've had the pleasure of visiting eight times in the past decade, and the quality never wavers.  The service is unfailingly friendly, the rooms spotless, and the facilities top-notch.  I'm not sure what else to say - it's a world-class resort, with great service and great facilities.  If that's what you're looking for, this is the place.

reviews.author: katie c
reviews.title: Beautiful spot but...
reviews.text: We stayed at the Phoenician for just a few days. I tagged along with my husband on a business trip. We stayed in a casita.  The decor was very dark & dated.  The lighting also--dark and not enough of it. I found that strange.   However, It was very spacious with lovely views of the property.  Nice enough staff, however, upon my arrival a bellman seemed "put out" that he had to take me in a golf cart to get to my room (my husband had already checked us in, as he arrived earlier).  The bellman did offer the ride, but did not seem happy about it.  Other than that, the staff was helpful and pleasant.  Food was good.  Service was good.  Maid service good.  All good, just not great.  I guess I expected more.  Pools and property are lovely.  Nice spa.  Nice gym.  Great hiking.

reviews.author: Vegas
reviews.title: Showing its age, not updated, not a 4 star room...
reviews.text:
Service may be AAA 5 Star, which is a wonderful thing here, the rooms are not. Worn, old furniture, dated carpets, colors, flooring and average casita's rooms are not what was expected. Stained carpet from leaking shower in one room, that of friends, mine had just plain old dated furnishings. No ice machines, honor bar from 1987, phones which did not work. The nights we were there, were $499 a night. I wouldn't pay $199. Consider other true style 4/5 star resort in the area. 

Service at all levels, (except via telephone, as calling for ice, housekeeping, or front desk rang and rang, and rang without answers and was forced to call again a few minutes later), where fantastic. Polite, professional and above average.

reviews.author: Andrew C
reviews.title: Old and dingy, left in 2 hours.
reviews.text:
Phoenician was a disaster. My wife and I checked in on Valentine's day and we left after 2 hours. Room wasn’t ready so we went to breakfast and were ignored for 15 mins. Generously, they took 50% off our breakfast. Then we got to room and it was old and dingy. They said we had a mountain view.  The only view we had was of the kids sliding down the water slide into a little pool screaming their heads off. We could also see the "quiet pool". Tons of kids screaming there, too. And the room was disgusting. Old beat up furniture, stained curtains, carpet way beyond it's lifespan. Bird crap all over the balcony. I talked to the front desk and they said there was nowhere to move us.  They offered to take $200 off per night. Seemed to be a trend - bad service and room, get 1/2 off. Amex travel was able to move us to the Biltmore where they completely took care of us and we had a terrific time other than that first morning. Highly recommend Biltmore over Phoenician; how could Amex have Phoenician on their fine hotels and resorts? 
Even better: Phoenician sent me a survey on how our stay was. Can't wait to fill that out.
I have photos but couldn't add to this note.

reviews.author: BlessingsWisconsin
reviews.title: 5 stars complete hotel and resort
reviews.text: Where to begin-from check in to service, activities, relaxation, to check out. Absolutely everything was wonderful. Staff was always friendly and greeting. Multiple restaurants to have your meals in the resort. Beautiful scenery and the weather was a plus. There is travel service from the resort to just about anywhere you want to go outside the resort. We climbed Camelback mountain and it was absolutely exhilarating. The spa salon was Great! Atmosphere and the layout was so zen! The massage therapist was petite but worked out all the kinks out of my back! Very relaxing! Would definitely recommend and go back!

reviews.author: Aimee N
reviews.title: Expected more
reviews.text: This is a beautiful hotel in a lovely location in Scottsdale. We've stayed there several times, but unfortunately on our last visit, the hotel did not live up to our expectations. We had reserved two separate rooms for 5 days each, and convinced our business partners to also stay there (occupying 3 other rooms), plus we hosted a company dinner at the hotel (50 people at the restaurant). So considering the fact we spent quite a bit of money there in one week, we expected to be treated a bit better. Unfortunately when we arrived, they showed us to our ground level room facing a brick wall (even though we had made a reservation about two months prior and requested the mountain view). And to make it worse, as soon as we walked into the room we saw 3 cockroaches run across the floor. They were able to move us to the only other room available which was directly next to the gym, so we were woken up by the sound of weights dropping every morning around 6am (I realize that is not the hotels fault since there is a sign in the gym asking guests to not drop the weights, but regardless, it didn't make our stay anymore pleasant). We had previously loved our stays there, but this last trip did not encourage us to stay loyal to the Phoenician.

reviews.author: Carrie C
reviews.title: Best place to stay in Phoenix
reviews.text: Attended a conference the weekend of the Pro Bowl in Phoenix. The Phoenician property is beautiful and well maintained. The staff is excellent. Especially loved the concierge specialists  and the wonderful gentlemen who work in bell services. Pool is lovely and food at the pool was excellent. We attend this conference every year and will stay only at the Phoenician even if the conference moves back to the Biltmore.

reviews.author: AlexCherie7233
reviews.title: Stunning in every regard
reviews.text:
I've had the chance to attend meetings at The Phoenician twice in the last several years, both for business meetings. 

My wife and I have had the good fortune to stay at some Tier One hotels - the Laguna Nigel Ritz Carleton, the Waldorf Hotel in NYC, the St. Regis in Park City Utah - and I would say this is the equal if not better than any of these.

Public areas are very grand, with stretching windows that look out over a wandering pool area and out to the golf course. Big soft couches and chairs are great to simply rest with a book.

Rooms are well appointed, quiet, with nice bathrooms and soft beds. Although the resort is large it didn't never seemed like the walks from one spot to the next were too far. The interior banquet facilities are fine enough as well.

One of the things that makes The Phoenician stand out was the capacity to hold meetings outdoors. On one occasion, our meeting backed up to a mountain stretching vertically away from the buffet line as the sun set behind it. You can imagine the beauty. 

And the food was excellent. All three hotels above serve a great banquet menu, but this Arizona place stood out to me. Naturally it depends on what the host orders for you but everything I ate was rather good - and I am not easy to please.

Service was subdued and prompt, friendly and affable without being familiar.

reviews.author: Gail042014
reviews.title: Beautiful resort
reviews.text: This is a beautiful resort. The grounds are immaculate and the pool and lobby are beautifully decorated. The level of service here is amazing. The rooms are large and comfortable. I found the decor in the rooms to be somewhat dated and was frustrated by the total lack of pressure in the shower. The rooms are a good size and housekeeping is very thorough and helpful.  The breakfast buffet is excellent.

reviews.author: CDonovan9
reviews.title: Excellent service, but pools crowded and only 1 hot tub
reviews.text: Stayed here for a work trip, looking for a little R&R when not working.  The service was EXCELLENT... from the bell hops to the lobby bar staff (Jenny at Thirsty Camel was GREAT) to the front desk.  But, for this level of hotel there are a few things needing improvement... they boast 10 pools, but there we had to SEARCH for 2 spots on a Saturday afternoon... barely able to find an open seat.  Also, there is only 1 hot tub for a hotel this size; at least 2-3 more needed.  Also, I've been to many hotel SPAs which have their own pools + hot tub area, but they didn't have any dedicated outdoor SPA space - seems a shame since this is such a large property, seems ample space to accommodate that.

reviews.author: Ron R
reviews.title: Impressive property with great service
reviews.text:
The property is self-described as iconic, and I would agree.  Every aspect is upscale and stunning.  The rooms are spacious, including a large bathroom with a separate shower and whirlpool tub.  J&G steakhouse was rather expensive, but the food and wine selection were excellent - they have a sommelier on staff.  The golf courses were plush, and the grass was in such great shape it almost looked fake.  The property is big enough that it can require walking, but you can ask for a ride in a golf cart for any destination.  
The hotel is backed by Camelback Mountain, which has a hiking trail called Cholla Trail.  While you can walk a mile or so down 64th St to get to the trailhead, you can also ask the golf staff for a ride across the course to a convenient drop point to save you time (especially convenient late in the day).  
Taxis are easily and quickly retrieved by the bell staff, including town cars and Escalades on site.  
The conference rooms were spacious, and the room temps remained consistent.  
There was staff all over the resort waiting to help, and I did not encounter anyone who was not smiling and service-oriented.  
I'd recommend hanging out at the fire pits and enjoy the valley view in the evening.

reviews.author: Imgoinonvacation
reviews.title: Wonderful Resort
reviews.text: We are headed back for our second stay at the Phoenician in March- it was that great!  The hotel is beautiful, the grounds are well manicured and the staff is excellent.  Don't hesitate to book  your stay- you will not be disappointed.  The pool area is wonderful- my daughter and husband loved the waterslide!  The rooms are quite large- ours overlooked the pool.  Bathrooms are large and well-appointed.

reviews.author: kaattie
reviews.title: in comparison to other Scottsdale resort hotels - excellent
reviews.text: After struggling to find a quiet, comfortable, upscale hotel for my frequent business trips to Scottsdale, I'm finally satisfied with The Phoenician.  I posted a review of the Omni Montelucia last month, and The Phoenician is everything the Omni isn't.  True customer service, from the "personalization" representative who emailed me before my stay to the check-in staff to the room service staff - top notch: friendly, efficient, genuine.  The room (I was upgraded to a superior, big, huge gorgeous balcony, wide open to a splendid view) is hush-quiet, not a stray sound.  Clean, pleasantly decorated, great bathroom.  The HD TV actually has a lot of HD channels, wow!  And the room service food actually matched what the menu said, and was delicious and best of all HOT on arrival.  I will be back!

reviews.author: MEGADAN
reviews.title: Breath taking resort.
reviews.text:
Was here on business. The resort is beautiful. Just gorgeous. The cactus garden was beautiful and peaceful. The service at the hotel outstanding. Everyone was helpful and friendly. The conference facilities were very good and the food at the organized events were wonderful. The bartenders were very professional and the drinks, with the exception of the pool ($20 for a watered down margarita) were very good.  One thing that I was disappointed with, being from the frigid east coast was that the pools lacked afternoon son and all services closed at 5pm. 
Also if you check in after 8 pm there is only room service and lounge apps available. The resort was very expensive. I was there on business and would return but no on vacation.

reviews.author: morrie K
reviews.title: Great facility, spacious rooms and great service
reviews.text:
Great experience from the minute that I checked in, until the minute that I left.
I stayed at this hotel as part of a convention, and entire stay was seamless. My bags were dropped off in my room, whilst I went to register for my convention. Room was very big, and extra large. Bathroom was also large, with separate toilet. Gym was also well-equipped , and located about a 5-minute walk from the main building. Food was excellent.

reviews.author: Beth F
reviews.title: personal service
reviews.text: While on a business trip, I was in the lobby and casually mentioned that I would like to perhaps take a little hike up camelback mountain. That afternoon, I was totally surprised to see the lead customer service representative and in his hand he had put together a backpack with a granola bar, water and sunscreen " just in case" I wanted to take that trip. I felt a smile from every employee. It is a beautiful place. Calm, serene and elegant. I hope to return soon!

reviews.author: TexasLina
reviews.title: Hard to Beat! Beautiful Landscaping, Large Rooms, Great Service
reviews.text: Once you arrive it is hard to set foot off of the property it is so beautiful. The million dollar pool is awesome.  Be sure to bring your credit card, you will need it especially for the steakhouse and room.

reviews.author: Vegas917
reviews.title: Camelback
reviews.text: A great time.  The rooms were very comfortable.  There for a golf tournament which was close by.  The restaurants and shopping were excellent as well.  I would go back any time.  The area has unlimited activities.  A great city!

reviews.author: Lkerby
reviews.title: Giants Spring Training
reviews.text: Stayed at the Phoenician for 4 nights for spring training - had a blast!  The hotel was exceptional.  The guys golfed on two of the courses at the resort.  The rooms were fantastic, larger than most hotel rooms and a great balcony.  Would definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: LochLake
reviews.title: Something for Everyone
reviews.text:
This is a great property for all types of travelers. If you are a couple, the Spa and restaurants are great, as well as the adult-only designated pool area with cabanas. If you have kids, the pool is a lot of fun, they have bocci ball on the grounds and there is hiking nearby. For business travelers, the meeting rooms look quite grand, the outdoor terrace is fun, the golf course looks great and the workout room is 24 hour access. I was there with a group and we utilized as much as possible when we weren't out and about. The restaurants on site are all good, but only open to 10:00 pm. There is a standard room service menu after that. We went out once to Old Scottsdale to have dinner where there are many good restaurants located. Workout room has a good collection of equipment. 
The rooms were very nice. Mine was huge and had a great bathroom, as well a a large balcony. 
In the evening, guests hang out in the lobby bar to have drinks and people-watch. 
An expensive splurge, but I would stay here again.

reviews.author: mckal
reviews.title: Beautiful place to visit
reviews.text: I have stayed here a few times and would definitely go back again.  This most recent time I had a basic room and it was large enough for my family of three.  A previous time I had a one bedroom suite in the Canyon Suites area of the hotel which was great as it was more than spacious and had it's own private pool.  At the main part of the resort they do have several pools to choose from.  The service at the pool was excellent.  The grounds are just beautiful, maintained very well and so pretty to walk around.  They have choices for restaurants, too. The Thirsty Camel lounge is a nice place to sit and admire the views.  This time I did not use the spa but I did during another stay and I would highly recommend it.  Everything here is top-notch.

reviews.author: AKEPIL
reviews.title: Phun for all
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is an older resort but it was made so well that it is still beautiful today.  The rooms are quiet and spacious; recommend getting one to overlook the pool area which is amazing.  The lower pool is made from mother of pearl - it shimmers so pretty!  We have stayed here many times over the last 5 years but this trip it was not quite warm enough to swim, but the pool bars are still nice and the cooler temps make it better for the golfing and nearby hiking!   There is an excellent steak house on the top level as well as many options for food and drinks throughout the resort.  We really enjoy outdoor dining, and the Phoenician offers several options for that.
Besides golf and pools, there are tennis courts, bicycles and hiking...lots to keep you busy!  There are also some nice shops on site, but I didn't get to those this trip.

reviews.author: TheBlithes
reviews.title: Beautiful stunning views!!
reviews.text: I used to work here a long time ago. Said to myself, "I would like to stay here, one day"! Years later, I did. My mother and I stayed for a week. My mother was in heaven! We ate at the excellent restaurants on-site. We made good use of the Spa, also!! We loved the spa. We had a late dinner one night at the restaurant on the top floor. The views were amazing and the meal was delicious. My mother is not well now and to be able to think back at these wonderful memories make me feel very blessed. Thank you!

reviews.author: Michael S
reviews.title: Consistently Great
reviews.text:
My wife and I have stayed here twice over the last three years and the place is spectacular.  The grounds are stunning with a golf course surrounding the hotel and Camelback Mtn. immediately behind.  Pool is several levels and equally gorgeous.

Rooms - we have only stayed in a room with a view of the mountain.  Room itself was great - spacious, nice bathroom and what you would expect from a resort of this caliber.  Certainly if you can get a room with a better view - facing the pool or one of the cabanas that would be ideal.  

Golf - resort course which is in great shape and has some memorable views of the surrounding area and a great way to see the entire property.  

Overall we love this place and highly recommend staying here.  Cant wait to go back.

reviews.author: JanD442
reviews.title: Wish I had been there on pleasure instead of business
reviews.text: This hotel is set right below Camelback mountain. This is convenient for hiking or just looking at the beauty of the surroundings. I was here on business so I did not get to use the amenities. What I will say is that the staff is excellent (I was lost one day coming in to my group breakfast and was escorted to the room, even though the staff member was clearly in the middle of something else). When a group of us sat down for 5 minutes at the pool we were immediately greeted by pool staff and brought a pitcher of cold water and cups. The pools are lovely, there is a water slide for the kids and a nice bar area. Lots of lounge chairs for relaxation. The food was very good for a work meeting.

reviews.author: mischka4
reviews.title: The Phoenician, Scottsdale...too pricey for business
reviews.text: I didn't get  much time to really explore the resort and all it's amenities as I was here on business, which for a business trip it's pretty pricey, for leisure or holiday, to take advantage of all there is to do might be a different story.  Upon my arrival I ate at an outside bistro,(I think it was called the Burger Bistro), overlooking the golf course which was very relaxing. The burger was big enough to split, and pretty tasty, my grilled chicken sandwich however was dry and tasteless, and it was a $60.00 bill....that's a lot for a burger and dry chicken sandwich. The rooms were quite large, clean and comfortable.  The staff was friendly and professional. They have a wine tasting in the evening which was a nice way to wind down the day and sample something new. In the evening you can sit outside by the fire....that was nice. Couple of shops to peruse but they closed at 5 so wasn't able to go in them.  Again, very pricey for a business trip when your in a conference room all day.  In the morning all that was available was a small cafe where a bagel cost 15.00!  I probably would not stay there again only because just for my room for 3 days was over 700.00, food was about 400.00...and it wasn't "fine dining" either, this was eating on the fly.

reviews.author: Adriano H
reviews.title: Inesquecivel
reviews.text: Excelente resort com campo de golfe em localização privilegiada aos pe de uma montanha. O serviço é perfeito bem como os chalés. As piscinas aquecidas na temperatura ideal proporcionam momentos únicos de relaxamento. Os vários restaurantes oferecem um cardápio variado e de alta qualidade. Recomendo!!

reviews.author: Tracey K
reviews.title: Worst overpriced overrated Hotel experience EVER
reviews.text:
So prior to booking our stay I of course read review after glowing review from my fellow TripAdvisor travelers who wax poetic upon the wonders of The Phoenician. .. On top of that, it was one of my American Express Corporate Platinum Fine Hotels and Resorts options so I enthusiastically booked the Resort for our first night in Arizona with complete confidence that we would have no less than an absolutely stellar experience.... Well let me tell you - NOTHING could be farther from the truth.  Before I bore those of you that are going to be brave enough to sit through the rest of this review with the countless details surrounding what made this such an absurdly dismal experience let me just start off by saying that this was no conventioneer budget priced visit... This was a pricey $700 one night investment that I mistakenly thought would be a memorable way to kick off our Super Bowl trip... Well it was memorable alright but certainly not in the way we had anticipated.  How anyone can rave about this chamber of horrors is just beyond my comprehension. So sit back and relax as it is going to be a long detailed ride...but if I save just one of you reading this from staying here and having an experience like ours it will be worth the time invested.  The one bright shining light was our bellman as he was sweet and enthusiastic as he escorted us to our "suite" (as AMEX Fine Hotels guests we were upgraded from the suite class we originally booked in to an even supposedly better suite classificaion but trust me when I say that I use the word suite loosely here to describe what we were installed in).. The traffic pattern is spread out so it is a crazy long haul to get from the lobby to the elevator that ultimately took us up to our 4th floor room and as we walked, my husband and I couldn't help but look at eachother and ask one another "What the heck is that smell??" ...  I genuinely thought it was along the lines of urine as if they were having sewer issues but my husband deemed it more in the mold/mildew category... I don't know what it was but it is pervasive throughout the entire place and you never stop smelling it or "get used to it" to the point that it goes away until you finally make your escape at checkout (and even then it took an hour to get that smell out of our noses completely) YUCK...  

Our suite was at the farthest point down a long dated sad looking hallway filled with old tired carpet, old beige boring wall covering, and the most god awful cheap $25 a print 1980s "artwork" you can imagine.  I am not exaggerating here.  I had read that the resort boasts some stupid crazy figure in art - well I can assure you that the art budget on our corridor was a whopping $150 collectively. As we finally approached the double doors to our suite I was amazed to see two cheap hollow core doors with big gaping places where the two doors connect and when the bellman opened the door they rattled like they were literally going to fall apart from the effort. Walking in, the only thing we can figure is that someone had the bright idea to simply take two rooms and attempt to merge them to make a "suite" (every time I type the word suite to refer to these rooms I just shake my head in amazement).. The first "room" was a dark depressing awkward space containing a little dinette table, a couch and a desk as well as a complete wall of ugly louver doors that we were told were closets (but they were nowhere near the bedroom so I have no clue what purpose they actually serve)... As you backtrack out to the front doors you have to go through yet another locking key card entry hotel door that takes you to the sleeping quarters and bathroom. (However it is important to note that if you happen to make the mistake of walking from the bedroom to the goofy couch room and don't remember to bring your key card you will wind up locked out of your bedroom even though you are still within your suite behind the first set of key card activated double doors!  It's just insane!) The entire space is dark, dank, dated and depressing with claustrophobically low ceilings and a just ridiculous amount of ugly louver doors everywhere.  I kid you not when I tell you that our room must have had no less than 30 louvered doors and cabinets... Whoever designed this place must have had a brother in law in the louver business because it was comical how many there were (see photos).  As I opened the curtains I was rewarded with a big expansive window that runs the entire width of the room and overlooks the oh so lovely view of the. ...  ROOF .  Yes, $700 later,  a golf course and some of the most beautiful surroundings in the country and what do we see from our "suite"? A massive expanse of hideous flat roof (again see photo to truly grasp just how awful it really was) ..  The whole room from top to bottom was ridiculous and so poorly conceived and designed on every level that it actually boggles the mind.  Even the lighting was totally annoying as before getting in bed you had to run all over the room switching off each light on the light fixture itself and then, when you finally made it to the bed and got in you realize that the wall lights mounted high up on the wall on either side of the bed aren't within reach and must be turned off by literally getting up out of bed and reaching up to the light to turn it off - individually on both sides - so my husband and I both clamored out of bed and switched them off - just stupid stupid stupid. How does that even pass the most basic logistical hotel quality controls? I challenge the manager of this decrepit place to stay in room 4092 and spend $700 for the privilege out of his own pocket and then tell me how fabulous it is.....  In any event, suffice it to say that I don't know what everyone is smoking that writes these slobbery effusive reviews on the virtues of this place but they all clearly have a far different idea of luxury than I do.  The best thing they can do here is stop throwing good money after bad trying to dump 100s of millions of dollars into conducting "soft" remodels on a place whos 1980s bone structure simply isn't able to be effectively changed.  You can't alter the smotheringly low ceiling heights, the functional obselescence of the sprawling crazy floor plan or the ugliness of the dated hideous external architecture so instead champion the site and setting and do yourselves a favor and just mow it down and start over again.

reviews.author: CherWest
reviews.title: Camelback Phoenician Resort
reviews.text:
Loved it! We live here in Scottsdale and just wanted a holiday weekend getaway!
This resort has everything you could ask for. And if they don't, they will get it for you. Lots of shopping right down the street at the 4 floor Fashion Square Mall, featuring all the top designers!
This place is a must!   Great golfing retreat too!

reviews.author: JamezDean
reviews.title: Great hotel in the heart of the city
reviews.text: The Phoenician is a beautiful property all over. The building is a resort setting but it is surrounding by complete excellence. The service is superb as well. We stayed here for 4 nights in January and it was amazing. As platinum members we enjoyed free wifi and breakfast each morning which was a gem. The resort charges a $29 resort fee p/n but waive it for platinum guests (THANKS!). It is amazing from top to bottom and you will feel like royalty staying here. Of course there is a price for this and the hotel isn't an inexpensive one. Expect rates around $400 a night. Amazing, though. The golf course is also incredible!

reviews.author: bobsT2615LH
reviews.title: The Phoenician is rising!
reviews.text: My experience staying at the Phoenician last weekend was memorable. From the warm greeting by the front desk manager Michael, to helping me with a complimentary upgrade and future reservations, I greatly appreciated his extraordinary service. I also had the opportunity to talk at length with Michael Lee at the Il Terrazzo restaurant. He is also a terrific person and he runs a great restaurant. Even Chef Richard came out to say hi with a surprise “breakfast desert” that was extraordinary. What more can any guest ever want in life? Service like this is the reason why I spend over 100 nights annually at Starwood Hotels. Since I live in Tucson, the Phoenician has truly become our home away from home on our frequent visits to Phoenix.   Bob

reviews.author: razzmatazz2
reviews.title: Wonderful resort
reviews.text: Lovely hotel with great golf on the property.  The multiple pools with the great vistas add to the experience.  We preferred our room 4127 since it was in the main building and easy to get to all the areas in the property.  Excellent service from all - bellman, front desk, concierge, restaurant, pool, etc.

reviews.author: Rob F
reviews.title: Family time at the Phoenician
reviews.text:
This is our second stay in the last 3 months at the property.  The grounds are amazing and so well maintained.  The pool is relaxing and refreshing and fun for the kids (including the slide).  Even thought he hotel was sold out, the pool and grounds did not seem crowded at all.  

Would highly recommend for family fun in the sun!  Lives up to the 'luxury collection' moniker.

reviews.author: 263zelmar
reviews.title: Beautiful resort with many amenities!
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is lovely with many elegant and lovely vistas!  The restaurants are delightful and the settings magnificent.  Strolling through the grounds is relaxation in itself.  Be sure and enjoy time a the spa and indulge yourself with plenty of time to spend.

Our only real complaint was housekeeping!

reviews.author: FollowingtheEquator
reviews.title: Mixed emotions
reviews.text:
Mixed emotions.    Run down:

Location:   Scottsdale – it is pretty much in the middle of it but you are going to need to take a cab anywhere if you leave the place.  

Property:   It’s very nice, very well kept.  It is also a labyrinth, very resortish – which is what it is – so you have access to every shop etc that you need.  I’ve golfed there a few times – it is a resort course but nice and entertaining. 
   
Service:   Very good.   I had no problems with the service at all - the people were great and very attentive - especially on a busy weekend.
   
Room:  Here is my issue – the room I had was tired.  It looked tired, it needed updating, and it cost $500 + a night.    I understand that Scottsdale is desirable, the market probably demanded it, but that caught me the wrong way simply because the value just was not there.    I do not know if I was in a wing that they eventually will renovate, but it would take a conference or no other open location in Scottsdale to get me to stay here again for that price.  If it were priced out at $250-$350 I would probably not care as much.

reviews.author: RealGypsy
reviews.title: First choice in Phoenix, AZ
reviews.text: Fabulous. World class! 5-star dining. Many activities on site & local, including shopping, swimming,hiking & golf. Very relaxing. Spectacular views. Huge suites. Excellent service beyond compare. Great for beautiful photos. World famous resort. Enjoy!!

reviews.author: soapdodger73
reviews.title: A luxury resort … indeed !!
reviews.text: THere are many words to describe this resort but I will start with one … Massive. Everything is on a gigantic scale from the swimming pools to the cacti to the restaurant to the food on your plate. The staff also went out of their way to be helpful, particularly with directions as you will get lost. We had a great time here. We used the bars and restaurants lot and enjoyed sitting in the Arizona evening having a cold beer in the warm air. We ate at the sports bar (Relish Burger Bistro) for the sunday football and it was just what you wanted in a sports bar. Now it is hard to find but if you are looking to watch the NFL it is the place to do it in the complex. The Steakhouse is expensive but very very good.

reviews.author: Josh B
reviews.title: The Place to Stay in Scottsdale, if you don't care about money...
reviews.text:
This is the place to be if you are in Scottsdale.  Conveniently located to everything.  The grounds are gorgeous, the golf course is great, and the staff is wonderful. 

If you have the money, stay here.  Everything is insanely expensive and its not a good value proposition at all.

We were upgraded with no status, which was awesome!  There were some problems with our room, but they made every accommodation possible and did everything they could to make it right.

reviews.author: sander9t
reviews.title: A grand resort with impressive ground, stunning view, and dated rooms
reviews.text: Stayed three nights in a Casita Guest Room.  The bedroom is spacious and comfortable.  The bathroom is also of good size and has separate bath and shower.   The resort ground is huge and gorgeous.  The Mother of Pearls pool is stunning, especially at night.  The lobby is grand and beautifully decorated.  The hotel is a museum by itself and is said to have a $25M art collection.  The Cactus Garden is worth a stroke as well.  The view, yes, the panoramic view is the highlight - the best view is from J&G Steakhouse and the view from the terrace outside the lobby is not bad either.  The food at J&G is superb.  We were surprised how fresh the seafood cocktail was and the steak was great too. The service is top notch.  The only reason I could not give it a five star rating is that the room was a little dated.  I heard that they were planning to renovate the rooms, and hopefully the renovation will fix the problems.  Before it is completed, check out the Canyon Suites next door, which is a resort within the Phoenician resort,  if you want a newer room.

reviews.author: CKiser_BC
reviews.title: Rolled out the red carpet.
reviews.text: We went here for our honeymoon and the staff made us feel like royalty. They were so attentive to our needs and really made our special trip even more special. The room was upgraded and so beautiful, with a great view of the mountains and pool. It was easy to get into town to enjoy dinner. The hotel helped with all of our reservations and even surprised us with treating us to an appetizer one night. If I have to be critical of anything, I would say the hotel food was a bit on the salty side but we can't wait to go back for future anniversaries! I hope we get the upgrade again!

reviews.author: Wolly_Woolacombe
reviews.title: Exceptional hotel for families, couples, or friends -- anyone would enjoy this!
reviews.text:
Went for four nights with four girlfriends.  We stayed in two, pool view rooms.  The service at the Phoenician is comparable to the service everywhere in Scottsdale which is to say it's phenomenally accommodating.  Everyone is tripping over themselves to be kind -- really sweet people.  Scottsdale may have the best service I've come across.  The rooms are large, the room service breakfast we had was complete with white table clothes on the balcony, and the hotel itself is extremely clean.  There are a number of pools including a beautiful kids area/water slide.  

The hotel is stunning but the staff is what makes this hotel worth staying at.

reviews.author: audrasena
reviews.title: Phenominal Phoenician
reviews.text:
This place is worth the money to stay here.  Our family had 5 rooms and were treated like royalty, no matter what our need was.  Amazing....!

Now, the food/customer service in the restaurants was lacking, very much so.  Waiting for 30 minutes for a table, for a buffet, where there were open tables in the lounge, etc.  Didn't make a lot of sense.  

Stay here - eat elsewhere!

reviews.author: ManyMilesStill2Go
reviews.title: Lows + Highes = Average
reviews.text: First impressions are very important and leave a lasting memory (or scar). In our case our room assignment staring outside at four walls and patio did not meet the description of a deluxe room.  We were upgraded by the rude front desk agent.  Another agent on a different shift agreed that was not where the deluxe rooms were located. (Helpful. In some ways but in other ways made me even more upset.) So much for booking directly with a Luxury Collection Agent.  And our New  Years Celebration at Relish also did not meet the description and hype (separate review of that disaster).  However with that being said there were also some wonderful things that I must note.  The other staff encountered were excellent -- wonderful concierge staff who provide very helpful local information and excellent housekeeping who do a great job in the morning and in the evening keeping the room neat and well stocked. The Spa staff are also very courteous and helpful   The resort amenities - our favorite being the cactus garden, to the pools, to the short hike to Camelback mountain, to the neat tour of the art collection all live up to the name of this being a Luxury collection resort.  We certainly left with mixed emotions.

reviews.author: ltl_elvis
reviews.title: We started our wedding / honeymoon here...
reviews.text: The Phoenician is an amazing experience…hands down.  We traveled into Scottsdale, before getting married in Sedona for relaxation and golfing before the big event.  Upon checking in we toured the facilities; I have the most incredible pictures of; different waterfalls 15+ (and it has far more), 10+ pictures of us playing 36 holes of golf, the 5 bunnies they gave us from the children's center for our kids, the inflatable movie screen and glow in the dark items given to children, the bar by the pool, the watersides, 5+ pools, and all of the amazing landscaping they had).  WE LOVE this place.  A previously divorced couple with a near-brady bunch 5 children we look forward to the day we return on our anniversary (yes April Fools Day, after all, it is the day we met) to let them enjoy as we did the many adventures of the hotel. They even have a program for the kids (don't fear they will have as much fun as you did) so you can golf or bike while they live it up for a day or two.  Well worth the trip…WE WILL BE BACK!

reviews.author: Steve D
reviews.title: Wonderful Visit
reviews.text: We stayed the week after Christmas and had a wonderful time. Since we brought our child, we spent a lot of time at Relish, the more casual restuarant- which is very kid friendly and the staff was great. We also had a guest personalization specialist- Andrea- who genuinely cared about our stay and was there for us every step of the way. I would agree with other reviews that the only negative thing I could say is that the front desk staff was cold and indifferent. They were all young- and seemed to be going through the motions. Everyone else was fantastic. And a big thanks for expanding the breakfast service this year to Relish as last year the main restaurant was overwhelmed- as it was again this year.

reviews.author: dbeniamino
reviews.title: wow
reviews.text: Luxury is the right word for this place. all is amazing, the place, the food, the golf course. everything is absolutely perfect. I'm an Italian traveler and my standards are very high but this place is just gorgeous. Be back soon!

reviews.author: Karan M
reviews.title: Phenomenal Property, Great Service & Excellent Golf Instructore
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Phoenician from 1st Jan through the 4th. We loved every aspect of our stay there. The staff was very friendly, the coordination across staff was seamless and it is right at the foot of Camelback mountain so the view is splendid. The weather was a bit cold while we were there but it was an amazing experience all the same. We stayed at the Canyon suites and as a Platinum at SPG, I am spoiled for good service. And the staff at the property totally nailed the experience. Very courteous, well informed and make you feel like royalty. We'll definitely be back!

Speaking of being back, I would definitely give a call out to our golf instructor, Michael Lamanna. One of the best instructors we have spent time with. Very well informed and very patient (we aren't exactly pro golfers). We've continued to stay in touch with him and he has been extremely helpful. In fact, I would be back just to spend more time on the course with him. Thanks again for all your help!!

Definitely recommend the stay and the spa (great service there too!!). And while you'll are there, definitely hit Michael L up if you're trying to learn golf or just improve your game.

Cheers,
Karan

reviews.author: WindyCityTravelBug
reviews.title: Beautiful Property; Staff Needs Improvement
reviews.text: Close to Camelback Mountain.Free self parking.Quiet & spacious room.Use an audio device from the concierge to explore art. Afternoon tea is delightful; great service at Il Terrazzo.I used a voucher purchased at ACS Discovery Ball & Joanna & Taylor treated me as if it was coupon from the pennysaver.

reviews.author: Amy
reviews.title: Absolutely Amazing...
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed at the Phoenician over the New Years holiday.  The resort is wonderful, clean and the staff was more than friendly and attentive.  So much attention to detail from the wait staff calling us by name to housekeeping accommodating our lazy schedule.

We took advantage of the guided tour up Camelback Mountain and enjoyed the hike.  Further, the spa was pure luxury...

We look forward to visiting again soon.

reviews.author: STLtraveller08
reviews.title: Great Location, Good Property, Okay Service
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed at The Phoenician over New Years. Overall it was a good stay, considering I used points. Check-in was slow (although there wasn't much of a line) and the front desk agent seemed indifferent towards us, not rude, but not friendly either. We didn't have much interaction with any other staff except our waitress at breakfast, who had the same attitude towards us. (Also, $46 for two parfaits and two orange juices and a slice of banana bread seemed ambitious, even for a property of this caliber) The room was clean and well appointed, however it was starting to look a bit dated. (i.e. peeling wall paper, cracking crown molding, worn towels etc. The beds were fantastic though. We choose to use the free self parking, which is a great option not usually found at a 5 star hotel. The overall property was very well maintained, although we didn't use a whole lot of the amenities. As mentioned, the location can't be beat. One complaint however is that it seemed like no heat was used in the public spaces. I know it's the desert and all, but it was only in the 30s-40s while we were there and the restaurant felt particularly cold inside. I would stay here again, but I think the next time we are in the area we might try out the Westin or W just to compare.

reviews.author: Funati
reviews.title: Spectacular Service!!!
reviews.text: Amazing property with spectacular level of service. The staff truly understand how to make each of their guests feel special. This hotel/resort makes you feel completely relaxed and you forget you are in the city. Great for families or couples looking to keep busy or simple relaxation.

reviews.author: Oliver S
reviews.title: Oasis in the Desert
reviews.text: We met the New 2015 in one of its restaurants, Il Terrazzo (separate review of that disaster) and stayed overnight to avoid driving in the wee hours after much Champagne and dancing. The hotel is expensive, but worth it. Our room was large, tall ceilings, tastefully decorated with paintings and prints of cacti in bloom. Bathroom excellent size, both tub and shower, separate toilet, all sparkling clean and beautiful. Large screen TV,  bar & safe in the room, gorgeous crispy white linen for bed & bathroom, peace and quiet, everything was just right! It helped alleviate the anger we felt after the New Year's Eve dinner in the restaurant. I would have rated them excellent, if it weren't for the cold and condescending service we got from reception at check in time. Her whole person was saying: "It's bad enough that I have to be here on New Year's Eve while you party, you don't expect me to work, too, do you!" Regardless of that, I will go back anytime.

reviews.author: Joe M
reviews.title: A++
reviews.text: Great resort, the grounds are perfect, the staff was awesome. This place is perfect. We were here from a conf. So glad we came. Visited many of the restaurants while there. Yum, yum. You really don't have to leave.

reviews.author: lkatz430
reviews.title: What A Lovely Property
reviews.text: Had the opportunity to stay in one of their villas. While the weather wasn't that great the accommodations and service are first class. At in their steak house which was very good as well as their burger bar, which has a huge tequila list. Top notch service and amenities. Contact Ellyn in reservations if you plan on going...she is great at setting things up!

reviews.author: Toria1212
reviews.title: First stay at Phoenician and many more to come!
reviews.text:
I was delighted with a stay at this sprawling and picturesque resort which I just returned from this evening.  

 From the moment we arrived, the customer service was top notch, very enthusiastic and everything was easily attainable-from spa appointments, to drivers, to a tootbrush replacement.  We enjoyed the pool, the spa, the tennis courts too.

 In a very convenient location, we were able to walk to the the trails of Camelback Mountain and enjoy a most spectacular view overlooking the Scottsdale area.

 We ate at the Relish Burger Bistro more than once, where the sweet potato fries and bbq nachos were tasty and filling.  We also dined for dinner at Il Terrazzo where the cuisine was remarkably gourmet and delicious, as well as a lovely ambience.

 We took advantage of room service as well, and were not disappointed by the flavor or the portions.

 I recommend a stay here to families, couples, girls' getaway weekend, etc.  I am looking forward to another stay soon(to escape this midwest COLD) and to enjoy all that the Scottsdale area has to offer.

reviews.author: 99_amber_999
reviews.title: Beautiful property, excellent service
reviews.text:
We were treated to a night at the Phoenician in December of 2014 during one of the busiest times at this resort.  The property is beautiful with 9 pools including a hot tub.  Our suite was incredible with gorgeous views and a very comfortable bed.

We were truly impressed with the service.  Lisa, our server at Il Terazo, was very helpful and kind, as was Andrew at Relish.  Highly recommend the Phoenician for a getaway - whether romantic or with family.

reviews.author: 129steph
reviews.title: Beautiful Old-School Resort
reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I spent last weekend at this lovely Starwood resort.  We chose the hotel based on other Trip Advisor reviews and were not disappointed.  The entire resort is beautifully maintained and offered wonderful amenities - three 9-hole golf courses (we are not golfers so we did not use), nine pools, a gym, spa, and numerous outdoor games such as croquet, bocce ball, etc.  

We are SPG members and were upgraded upon arrival to a room with a garden view.  It was quite large with a nice-size balcony.  While it is a bit old-school with beige everywhere and the flat-screen is inside a cabinet clearly designed for an older box-style tv and VCR, the room was immaculately clean, except for the shower.  The shower had some mildew around the edges and in spite of my request to have it cleaned and a woman spending 15 minutes using something in the bathroom, the mildew remained there.  I've noticed this problem tends to recur in Starwood hotels, even the St. Regis ones, as they seem to have an aversion to using bleach - perhaps it's the smell.  At any rate we were very pleased with our room.

My boyfriend enjoyed the pool daily, as well as the steam and sauna in the spa.  We had a great time and highly recommend the resort.

reviews.author: drmartine
reviews.title: Great 4 days to play tennis
reviews.text: First off all I must say I'm a Starwood Preferred guest and before our arrival we received  email by a guest personalization specialist wow! first time ever. She ask few questions about our next visit and plan a lot of surprises for us. I was celebrate something and we choose this resort  to play tennis. The room was large, very clean with balcony and a nice view, room service delicious and all the breakfast were really good. Tennis center is huge, the manager was really attentionate, water supply and towel. All was perfect. We were able to play on the grass court on our last day, can ask for more :). We will be back.

reviews.author: Cat23
reviews.title: Friendly service, fun golf and outstanding music
reviews.text: We visited in December of 2014 for a family gathering and to play golf.  The resort is beautiful with lovely gardens and fanciful artwork. The golf course is delightful and challenging.  What made the stay exceptional enjoyable was the super friendly people who helped with bags, food, golf, etc.  An unexpected highlight of our stay was hearing the inspired Anthony Mazzella  play his heavenly guitar at the Thirsty Camel on Friday night.

reviews.author: Sam P
reviews.title: Spg members mean nothing here
reviews.text: So my wife and are here on a much needed vacation. We are Gold level and also 3 star elite with their vacation ownership. We booked this a month out and were told we would get an upgrade upon arrival by our concierge 2 days prior to arrival. We checked in around noon and are told there were no upgrade rooms available. I enquired about the casitas and was immediately told by Joanna at the front desk that those rooms were smaller than the rooms attached to the hotel. Turns out she lied big time in an effort to say she was doing me a favor. She then tells me I am being somewhat upgraded to the 6th floor with a gorgeous mountain view. Oh boy was I upset when we get to the room. Average room in need of a serious upgrade. The view of the mountain was right in my face. Not much to look at. I have stayed at a luxury collection hotel and this is not anywhere near what I expected. The westin keirland is way better that this place.  Good luck with your status doing you any favors!

reviews.author: Justin F
reviews.title: Great place for families
reviews.text: I stayed here with my family of 4 and our friend's family of 4 over Thanksgiving break.  We had a few hiccups at check in (not able to get our room until 7pm), but the hotel went out of its way to make everything right.   It is really a fabulous place for families.  There are multiple pools, a great water slide, and an area called Splash for little kids to run around small water activities.  The Burger restaurant Relish is off the charts good.  We ended up eating Thanksgiving dinner there instead of the main dining area since the food is so good.  Kids club and sports courts are really fun.  The whole property is quite large with tons of things to do for kids and adults.  We stayed in a Casita Suite, which are really beautiful and large (like 1500 sq feet).  This was our 5th trip here and we will be coming back again really soon.  Highly recommend for families.

reviews.author: Dj112
reviews.title: Excelent Luxury Resort
reviews.text: The Phoenician is a hidden gem nestled on the base of Camelback Mountain. As soon as we arrived, the attentive bell staff were at our car opening the doors, and taking our luggage out of the trunk. The lobby is magnificent, the clean, shiny marble floors really adds the classic yet elegant lobby. The front desk staff were exceptionally nice, they gave us a "desert view" room overlooking the front of the hotel, which we were not happy about. So we went back down to the front desk and explained that we would like a different room. They were apologetic, and they quickly moved us to a new, beautiful "city view" room. Our room overlooked the pool, but in the morning and at night the sunrise/sunset was beautiful over the city's horizon. The room was extremely comfortable. The hotel provided 2 plush bathrobes and an array of toiletries. The room also had a porch, with a lounge chair and a table with chairs. Off of the lobby by the convention center escalators there is an area of shops, and a business center. The grounds of the resort were beautiful, the waterfall, cactus garden, and the amazing views of Camelback Mountain were definitely one of my favorite parts of my stay. The golf courses were amazing, also the restaurant above the golf shop "Relish Burger Bistro" is a must stop! The pools were very nice, and refreshing.
