Also the parking situation was the best I've ever had at a hotel.  We got to park 20 feet from our door and paid nothing for parking.  The rest of the property was just as well kept and up to date as the room.  The pools were completely clean and a great temperature. The staff was the most professional I've seen in some time.  The breakfast buffet was just average and way overpriced, but the most negative part of the stay was that the Jacuzzi was closed for renovations and there had been no indication of this when we booked the room.  The temperature was in the mid 60's and a Jacuzzi was really needed.

Overall an incredibly nice property.  Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Teresa J
reviews.title: Exceptional service!
reviews.text: The staff has been wonderful. Our trip started with some problems and everyone has bent over backward to make sure our stay is beyond expectations!  You will not find a more helpful and friendly staff anywhere!

reviews.author: BelieveMeOk
reviews.title: Complete garbage
reviews.text: For claiming to be a 5 star resort is embarrassing. The staff here need to have their heads examined. I have never before dealt with such rude and lazy staff in my life. The costs are atrocious 9$ for a hotdog.. Really... 17$ for a single rum and coke. It really is disgusting. And if and I say if who a big sigh the staff was at all helpful and polite it would be ok. But these guys are just gross. Do not waste your money. The golf side of things... The course is not bad but there are no sand traps they are rock pits. Again out of 5 maybe a 3 at best

reviews.author: SavvyTraveler738
reviews.title: They didn't miss a beat!
reviews.text: I was just there this weekend and was very surprised at how clean the hotel was both inside and outside and how cordial the staff were in all areas.  The fact that they recognize you from the morning after you have breakfast and you come back for either a drink or a lunch/dinner in a certain restaurant is appreciated.  The rooms are large and you get a view of wither the Camelback mountain which is right there...so close you can almost touch it or you get the view of the beautiful Gardens and the pool area.  I was in a deluxe room I understand and again, all the rooms are large with ample space. There were too many pools to count and each one of them looked inviting.  They also have a beautiful trained hawk that manages to keep the "pests" at bay and a large koi pond for the children to feed during feeding time.  The lobby and its bar area are very inviting and there are terraces with fireplaces/pits all around the hotel.  I had breakfast at the Terazzo which was well done and dinner at JG (Jean George Vongerichten), the famous steakhouse where I dined with a colleague on a tomahawk steak with mushroom and spinach as sides.  The wine list is very good as well and all the people seemed to know about wine and wine pairings.  Again a sign of a well trained and caring staff.  For starters we had the seafood platter with a bottle of Shramsberg Californian sparkling wine and for dessert we shared a delicious apple crumble.  From a service, food presentation and ambiance perspective, it was excellent and we will definitely go back if we were ever in AZ.

reviews.author: BBBB0708
reviews.title: Beautiful Peaceful Hotel
reviews.text:
Although I have been very fortunate to have traveled  all over the world, I have never been to Scottsdale,Arizona.Two weeks ago I had a business conference in Scottsdale and stayed at the Phoenician.The hotel is beautiful and immaculately clean.
The staff was fabulous,so accommodating and nice.It was a pleasure seeing these young,exuberant,sweet kids always there to help with a smile.
The bar and restaurant service were excellent .The food was better then I thought it would be.
The only complaint I have is our rooms were not in the main hotel and they were a long walk from the main building. All of the conference meetings were in the main building and so it was a hike .However ,we were able to get golf cart service back and forth from the out buildings to the main hotel so that was very helpful. It was also very cold that week ,and we didn't have coats with us so we appreciated the rides back and forth.
We had a corner room with a beautiful terrace and a wonderful view.My only complaint is that the rooms need more light,they were a little dark.
It's worth a visit to Scottsdale just to stay at the Phoenician.The scenery is beautiful and the Hotel is great!

reviews.author: michelle0404
reviews.title: Location great
reviews.text:
Having stayed in Phoenix a few times now we thought we'd try this hotel. It is big and can get a bit overrun with conferences. We were lucky re room 6195 whilst a very long walk the balcony and view of Phoenix, camelback, cactus garden and hole 9 made up for it. Some great sunsets seen as a result. 
Don't bother with valet it is 29 dollars per day and the self parking is really easy.  
Ate in J&G steakhouse one night lovely food definitely worth the money

Pool area good and attendants look after you well. 
Some good classes at spa and enjoyed a great massage too.
Location is excellent both for Phoenix and Scottsdale plus very easy journey too and from the airport
We did the cactus walk which was great the guide who has been working at hotel since it opened and cares for the garden was very knowledgeable and was great throughout definitely worth doing.

reviews.author: Sandra P
reviews.title: An idyllic 8 days, just bliss!!
reviews.text: The Phoenician is in the up market side of Scottsdale. Everything about the hotel is first class. The staff are very accommodating nothing is too much trouble. Our room was spotless we had a huge bathroom. The grounds and pool areas all very pleasing on the eye. The adult pool area also overlooks a lake with hundreds of koi carp, very relaxing watching them swimming around!! Brilliant golf facilities. The hotel also caters for businesses and had quite a few conferences going on, although they didn't intrude on us holiday makers. My only gripe would be $12 per day extra for Internet in your room, which considering you are already paying top dollar was insulting! Another tip would be to pack some slightly more smarter clothing for the Eve's in the hotel as most people are very well dressed! Not usual when eating out in the States. (Sat afternoon they had "afternoon" tea with lots of ladies dressed as if they were off to Ascot!!) quite a contrast with the rest of us off to the pool area. The end of our stay came too quickly. All I can say is we will look back with fond memories.

reviews.author: WILLIAM K
reviews.title: Nice stay...
reviews.text: Very family frendily, great service and staff, nice amenitities, beautiful landscape. Some items are in need up updating (air conditionaing controls and room lighting) but overall this was a nice place to stay and I'd like to visit again.

reviews.author: Cheryl D
reviews.title: Casitas need help!
reviews.text:
The resort is beautiful, staff very friendly, but the casitas are in desperate need of updating.  I booked a surprise 25th anniversary trip for my husband and I thinking the casitas were going to be lovely and romantic.  I have stayed in other resorts in Arizona that were perfect but this one fell short of my expectation. From the pictures the rooms look huge, advertised at 530 sq. ft. but I highly doubt that is true.  We constantly were running into each other.  The hall way barely fit one person through  it to get to the bathroom. The carpeting is worn down to the backing and had stains in several places.  I did request a different room on three different occasions but they could not accommodate us.  Also the decorative pillows had stains as well as the shears to the patio and the drapes were falling off in the corner.  For a five star resort these things should not be overlooked. I really think they spend so much time and money on the grounds they are overlooking the rooms.
This room was nothing more then an average room at a Holiday Inn at 7 times the cost. Save your money. Also, they say a short walk to the main building, no way, up stairs down stairs, and if there is a corporate party you have to detour around up elevators walk across to other elevators etc. because you can't get through to get to your restaurant. You can have a cart pick you up or drive there but that isn't what I planned on.  Also they say you can park outside of your casita but the spot that says "Casita Parking" is always full with cars from people visiting the restaurant or golfing so you had to go to the parking garage which is a bit of a distance. We're in our 70's so it was not convenient.  They should have the parking marked and have a sticker for your car and tow the cars that don't belong there.
There were four issues with the restaurants in eight days but they were addressed, a five star resort shouldn't be serving cold food so when they were correcting it one of us was eating alone. It should never happen in the first place.  
Save your money and don't get the buffet, it's not worth the price.  They do not have a big selection.
They also need someone who knows how to make omelets properly.
The other restaurants in there are just average, nothing to brag about.
All in all, just glad to get away from cold Chicago but never would choose Phoenician again.
There are other beautiful resorts out there. Choose wisely, I thought I was but got fooled.

reviews.author: Lordegbert
reviews.title: Private luxury, private location
reviews.text: Stupendous architecture and access to nature. Guests were obnoxious and snobbish but the staff handled them expertly. Loved our room and room service on a "Mister" basis. Beautiful art objects on display and a pool to for die for. Duck pond was comfortable, especially for the ducks. Popular for conferences although many of the conferees I observed were off the wagon. I have never seen so many examples  of desperate plastic surgery among the guests. There must be a big class difference among guests and I felt out of place as lower on the food chain. I saw My first Bentley parked at the front. Our cab driver was from Ghana and the front guard gave him a hard time. I would say that security was on its toes displaying many hard looks. It was like being at a museum.

reviews.author: BerkeleyJohn
reviews.title: First Rate Experience for Business and Leisure Traveler
reviews.text:
It's been awhile since I stayed at this hotel, but I recently attended a business conference here, and had a terrific experience, starting with the complimentary water bottles as we were checking in, a very nice touch.

The conference rooms (large and small) were very good, and the business center was efficient.  All the hotel staff (bartenders, waitresses, pool, front desk, bellmen, greeters, cleaners, etc.) were unfailingly courteous and helpful.

I am not a "pool" person, but the variety of pools, and the facilities for sunbathing, seemed ideal to my untrained eye.

I enjoyed sitting on the patio in front of my room, listening to the water fountain and relaxing.  Seems to me that this hotel has a lot to offer both the business and leisure traveler.

Recommended.

I managed to demagnetize my room "key" on consecutive days which required a long walk to and from the front desk, apparently a not uncommon problem.  I think the hotel could institute a system that avoids this problem.

We walked through the Cactus Garden, definitely not for everyone but worthwhile for those of us with an interest in this sort of thing.

reviews.author: David T
reviews.title: one of the best in scottsdale
reviews.text:
The town is full of high class hotels and this is one of the best. Everything is good including service, food and facilities such as golf swimming tennis etc. 
The rooms are beyond reproach and the location is great

David T

reviews.author: NYC_Southerner2013
reviews.title: Great experience at every turn
reviews.text: I love this hotel! They go out of their way to insure you are enjoying your luxury hotel experience (including with my 8 year old son). Concierge: I cannot say enough good things about the concierge. She was helpful with many things including, finding dinner reservations on a busy a Valentine’s Day and finding adventures for my son (and making him feel special the whole time).  Funicians (kid’s club): We had no plans use the kids club services but stopped by to check it out. My son had such a great discussion with her that he decided to stay and begged to go back the next day. Dining: I have a number of allergies -several are severe. The whole resort was great with accommodating these allergies but I wanted to call out the Chef at Relish. Not only was the food fantastic at Relish (yummy), but the Chef's care with talking into account food allergies was remarkable.  Spa: Great experience.  Pool: A big hit with my son.

reviews.author: dtgdallas
reviews.title: Much, Much Better
reviews.text:
Given that I posted a lukewarm review of The Phoenician a couple of years ago, I feel compelled to post on our thoroughly enjoyable recent experience there.  It was a business/pleasure trip for me, and a 100% pleasure trip for my wife.  Every service encounter we had was top notch.  From Violeta in the coffee/ice cream shop (good to see her there every year!) to Samuel around the pool to Lidia at Il Terrazzo to the front desk help to the guys/gals in the golf and tennis shops, everything was “my pleasure”, “no problem”, “yes, sir”, etc.  They couldn’t have been any nicer or more interested in pleasing the customer.  

The food at Il Terrazzo (several breakfasts, one lunch and one group business dinner) was superb. The mahi-mahi sandwich from the pool menu was one of the single best lunch choices that I’ve had in quite some time.  

The room was more than adequate, with the bedding being so good that I’ve already been on a website this morning trying to find the equivalent for our own home.   

The only hiccups of the entire trip actually represented opportunities to shine.  Lunch at Il Terrazzo on our day of arrival took forever to arrive and the server seemed kind of oblivious about how long it was taking.  They ended up knocking 50% off the bill for the long wait (which benefitted my company, not me!).  I had a light bulb out in the light above the bathroom vanity (one of four bulbs), and for three days running I had the bulb laying in the sink, thinking that would prompt the maid to call someone to have it replaced.  Three days running, the burnt out bulb was laying nicely next to my toothpaste, etc.  Finally one day I caught a housekeeper doing turn down service and asked about getting a new bulb.  She called maintenance who sent someone to replace it.  The supervisor called back 10 minutes later and asked if everything was now fine, and I said “uhhh, no, the bulb still hasn’t been replaced…”  Apparently there was a mix up and the technician thought it was the shower light that was out.  He popped in, saw that it was working and didn’t even notice the light above the sink out.  In any event, they came back, got it working and I received yet another follow up call.  Despite the three day wait for the light to be fully functional, it was a quasi-humorous, but ultimately good, service encounter.  

The Phoenician may not be the newest resort property in the area, but it rocks.

reviews.author: 3gJane
reviews.title: Time for an update
reviews.text:
In the last 3 months I have stayed at the The Canyon Suites and at the Casitas and the experiences were OK.  To pay the premium for the Canyon Suites simply didn't make any sense at all -- the service seemed fine in both places. The room at the Casita had a much nicer view, but needs a serious update - bad lighting, ceiling tiles worthy of a Motor Inn etc.
Two of my adult kids came here for a couple of nights in September without us and reported that they remembered the place from childhood as being the most luxurious hotel imaginable and were surprised at how unimpressive the rooms in the main building were. (which is why I booked the Canyon Suites for my subsequent visit).
The Phoenician is a charming old friend resting on its laurels. That said, the staff are friendly and the service is remarkably good considering I am writing this about President's Day Weekend. I also can see and appreciate the pleasure young children have simply being in the grounds.

reviews.author: rfink22
reviews.title: Less Than Expected
reviews.text:
This resort is beautiful.  The open layout is nice with rooms, restaurants, pools, etc. spread throughout the grounds.  There are 3 beautiful pools, with another family/children pool under construction.
The staff is friendly and helpful.

We stayed in a regular Casita room away from the main building which had a beautiful view of the resort and Camelback.

We both has 80 minute spa treatments and both therapists were wonderful as well as the check-in staff.  The locker-room is dated as well as the sauna and the steam room has a musty smell.  The whirlpool tub is poorly located within the locker-room and is too small and shallow.

The fitness center is large enough with updated equipment.  It has a large window with a nice view looking from the cardio towards Camelback Mountain and the resort pool.

We has a continuing problem with housekeeping.  A knock on the door at 8:30 one morning, then came after 2:00 the next day.  Service was spotty with coffee and supplies not always replenished.  towels were also not always replenished.  We generally do not complain, but when turn down was nor done and we needed towels for a morning departure, we complained about all of this.  The manager was gracious and offered to comp us for our last nights dinner, thank you.

All in all, nice, but "less than expected" for a high end luxury resort.  some updates to the spa area would help a lot.

reviews.author: Dan O
reviews.title: Great Resort and great service by staff
reviews.text: Great everything from the rooms to the food to the pools!  Great service by all staff.  Signed up for the iPhone picture taking class but no class that day so the Activities Director gave us a private tutorial!  Wow what service.  Learned a lot in the class too.  Great stay, we will be back next year!

reviews.author: Stephen J
reviews.title: Great Hotel
reviews.text: Loved my stay at this hotel.   Evevrything was top notch and the service was great.  The pools are very relaxing and it was a perfect weekend get away.  We enjoyed everything the hotel had to offer.  My only warning is do not eat at the J&G steak house.  The food was not good at all.

reviews.author: Acornart
reviews.title: Most Enjoyable
reviews.text: We stayed here for a corporate event and thoroughly enjoyed it. We stayed in one of the well-appointed "casitas" which overlooked the pond, fountain and one of the swimming pools. The restaurants were good, as were the bars and heated outdoor terraces, all with wonderful Arizona views. The hotel backdrop is Camelback Mountain and I can vouch that you will be tempted to hike it, so make sure you bring appropriate hiking shoes with good treads, because there are none for purchase and if you are tenacious enough to go to the top, you will end up on all fours at some points (hands-free backpack, lots of water and snacks, sunscreen highly recommended). Hanging by the pool is also recommended if you forget your hiking gear. There are boutiques on site for shoppers. There is also a lot of fabulous art throughout the property; if you are keen to learn more check with a concierge and they can equip you with an electronic audio guide which tours you around in 40 mins. I never made the spa, but my friends did and were quite pleased. There is a nice golf course on site, as well as a tennis club, which rents racquets and has a pro shop with very helpful staff.

reviews.author: RUSSELL GUAJARDO
reviews.title: best resort in scottsdale
reviews.text: Stayed here around thanksgiving 2013 .. The grounds are beautiful. One of the pools are under construction but not a problem. The rooms are luxurious and worth every penny. Drinks on the patio overlooking the pools around sunset are a perfect way to start your evening..

reviews.author: chewync
reviews.title: Large Hotel, Attentive Staff
reviews.text: Stayed 3 nights, hotel is undergoing some winter refurbishment, but still a very nice experience for a large and older hotel. Great workout room equipment, very attentive and responsive staff, every employee smiles and says "hello", they were well staffed to assist with directions to meeting rooms, etc., above average food for a large hotel, room was well appointed, great linens, and this room in the main building had a great shower. The hotel also has multiple great outdoor pools, and is adjacent to Camelback Mountain so plenty of recreational options.

reviews.author: Carolea G
reviews.title: Beautiful hotel that needs a little help
reviews.text: The room is lovely and the bathroom is great. The worst shower I have  encountered as it is the water saver mounted very high and almost no water reaches the body. Lovely amenities and service was excellent. Major problem was my room was never vacuumed the entire time of my six-day stay. Other than that I would rate the hotel four star. Great concierge help and wonderful desk registration service. Service at all restaurants was excellent. Pastry chef should be commended as desserts were the best I've had at almost any hotel or restaurant. Food presentation at all restaurants was excellent. I find it unaccceptable to have a charge on my bill for Bellman delivery and also for maid service daily as I feel this should be discretionary. It is just another way for the hotel to make extra money and not pay their employees properly on their own. Also, I find it difficult to understand why finer hotels charge for Internet when  least expensive moderate hotels do not. A this is just piggish as it is only a flip of a switch to give Internet to everyone in the hotel and actually Costs the Hotel zero. I would rather pay one charge and  have everything included than the extra add on fees that the  five-star hotels like to surprise guests with.

reviews.author: Jewlman
reviews.title: Paradise Lost
reviews.text:
With trade shows a "dime a dozen" the attraction of attending this one used to be for the venue.

However a poorly maintained casita soured my opinion.  After checking in we discovered issues and my request for a room change could not be accommodated.  Much later that same evening, we awoke to an unexplainable soaking wet floor. Oddly enough, the sold out hotel now had a Villa Suite available at 2:00 am for me. 

Upon my visit to the from desk the following morning, management was very apologetic and appeared accommodating. 

To their credit, our Villa was spacious and well maintained. My low rating is a reflection of the way this problem was handled and not the problem itself.

At check-out a token credit was issued to my account and quickly doubled when I expressed my displeasure for the inconvenience. 

I'm my opinion, 5 Diamond ratings also come with the same level of problem solving.  Management by crisis at 2:00 am is a failure to me.

reviews.author: Mike O
reviews.title: Great facility...middle management...not so great...
reviews.text: Our organization had the opportunity to spend time here during the Phoenix Open.  The younger up-and-coming management is truly in need of training when dealing with people.  We will likely never stay here again...which is a shame.  The facilities are wonderful and many of the staff were exceptional.  Poor judgement when treating my guest with disrespect will remove this facility from the ranks when coming to town.

reviews.author: stephen10023
reviews.title: Dont Go!!!
reviews.text: We just attended a conference there. They were moving a jewelry show in right over our group. It was difficult to walk down the hall. You could hardly get to a restroom for all of the trade people. They had pallats of cases, carpet and cords and lighting where you had to walk. The most inconsiderate move in I have ever seen. It is too bad as the people in the hotel are great. This is not a five star hotel when they would do something like this!

reviews.author: DebKel
reviews.title: Attentive staff, beautiful resort
reviews.text:
My husband and I have stayed at the Four Seasons Troon North and the Fairmont Scottsdale on our past trips and now The Phoenician. We used SPG points for this stay, it was well worth it. The attentiveness of the staff at The Phoenician was outstanding. We were well taken care of during our stay. We have not been dissatisfied with any of our stays in Scottsdale yet. 

The landscaping at the resort is very beautiful, the resort is maintained extremely well. Most mornings we ate breakfast at Il Terrazzo, we also had supper one night there, all were very good. We had supper one night at J & G Steakhouse, it was outstanding and had live entertainment. We also had drinks at the Thirsty Camel Lounge which also had live entertainment. We played 18 holes of golf at the resort. The golf course was beautiful and well maintained, but overpriced. I know they want to make as much money as possible but more time between tee offs would be much appreciated by players, as it was quite rushed. 

I would recommend The Phoenician to anyone looking for a luxury resort stay in Scottsdale. You will not be disappointed. We enjoyed our relaxing stay immensely.

reviews.author: barboellen
reviews.title: The Phoenician offers one warmth amidst a dazzling environment as their staff opens their welcoming arms to ensure you have a me
reviews.text:
My two sisters and I flew in from Boston and Detroit January 23 to celebrate our special birthday year. As we are five years apart, it was a big one for all three of us. Even before we arrived, Andrea W reached out to us asking if we were celebrating anything special and offered her assistance to me by recommending transportation alternatives from the airport. I let her know the day before that I would be arriving around noon as I got in-before my sisters . I was so pleased to find that our Casita rooms were ready for an early checkin so I could unpack and begin to enjoy the resort. 

When champagne and chocolate covered strawberries arrived at our door, I felt so special and couldn't wait to start celebrating with my sisters .

Our experiences with room service, pool service and dining at Relish, La Traviata for lunch and buffet breakfast and even at Golf club small outdoor snack bar all exceeded our expectations in the quality of the food as well as the friendliness of the staff. My sister and I agreed that the portobello sandwich was the tastiest we had ever had . The chef at the omelet station even had staff search the kitchen to locate feta cheese so my egg white omelet would be to my liking. Even a small thing like having a fresh, perfectly toasted sesame bagel with cream cheese at Golf Club put a smile on our faces.

We loved their heated pools, views of Camelback Mountain,beautiful cactus garden,orchid waterfall area,sculpture gallery, sunset views from Thirsty. Camel Lounge and the JG Steakhouse deck and the soothing sounds from the many fountains on the property, especially the one outside of our casita.

Everything about our stay was perfect including how Tyler , front desk manager handled a misunderstanding upon checkout and the wonderful service we received from concierges, bell men, waiters throughout our stay. The staff set the tone to ensure we were comfortable and that our stay was a memorable one.

reviews.author: Amease
reviews.title: Phoenician for Christmas
reviews.text: We stayed here for a few days over Christmas to celebrate my son’s college graduation.  It is a pricey resort so we used points to pay for the room.  I thought this was a good deal, but I don’t think I would want to pay retail for the room.  The grounds are very nice and fairly large.  Included on the grounds are the pools, a bocce ball court and a croquet court, a cactus garden and of course golf.  We enjoyed the pool, bocce court and cactus gardens which were decorated with lights for Christmas.  We did not make reservations for Christmas Eve or Christmas dinner in advance so there was not any availability.  If you plan to come over Christmas and want to dine in one of the main restaurants, make a reservation in advance.  The room was very large as was the bathroom which was great since we had our two adult boys with us.  The room also had a large balcony which enabled us to enjoy the view and our sons to talk in privacy on their cell phones.  Service at the hotel was very good as expected.  Check-in was fast and friendly and the lobby staff was happy to take photos of our family in the lobby in front  of the Christmas trees and ginger bread house.  One last touch which I enjoyed was the hand delivery of Christmas cookies to our room on Christmas Eve!

reviews.author: R T
reviews.title: Dirty carpet vs beautiful grounds. You make the call.
reviews.text:
The room we were given had big stains on the carpet and was worn. We called the front desk and they had another room we could move to. That room had the same dirty and stained carpet. We checked 3 more rooms and ended up choosing the room that had the carpet with the least amount of stains. One front desk clerk was very nice and another was rude. Keep in mind that each time we went to see a room - we then had to go back to the front desk and wait in a long line to talk to a front desk clerk again. This process took about an hour and a half and they lost our luggage in the meantime. 
On the positive side - the rooms were large and would have been lovely with new or cleaned carpet. The bathrooms are large and have a lot of counter space. 
The property grounds are beautiful and there is much to do. Swim, tennis and golf filled our days. We ate at J & G Steakhouse and it was outstanding - we would go back any chance we could!

reviews.author: Bob H
reviews.title: Staff and the View!!!
reviews.text: The Staff, especially Chris (Hotel Manager) and Hannah (Front Desk) were amazing.  They both ensured that we had the best experience.  We stayed at the main building (nicer than the other rooms), and had the mountain view.  The Hotel lobby, the view, the staff and the amenities are Five Star; the rooms are nice and clean, but not as great as the rest of the Hotel.  Overall, we truly enjoyed our stay, and we have Chris and Hannah to Thank for it.

reviews.author: tripstocker
reviews.title: I would like to live here.
reviews.text: My wife was on a business trip and I came along, Wow what a set up, as soon as you drive in this resort you notice how special it is. The grounds are spectacular, the service from check in on was the best we have ever received anywhere. My wife's company meeting at the hotel was top notch. Our room was perfect, bed comfortable, nice soaker tub, patio with view of golf and mountain. It truly was a desert resort, can't wait to return and would highly recommend this resort.

reviews.author: BillyReyn
reviews.title: Epitome of desert luxury
reviews.text:
This was my third or fourth stay, and it never disappoints. About a year ago I commented on the guest survey that coffee makers should be in each room, but upon my return there are Keurigs in each, with ample refill capacity.
All facilities are impeccably maintained and modernized and the staff is unfailingly gracious. I shall not need to look around for alternates in Phoenix or Scottsdale.

reviews.author: nmiler84
reviews.title: Truly 5 Star
reviews.text:
Wow, the Phoenician is truly a 5 star property.  Immaculate in nearly every sense of the word. Grounds perfectly kept, beautiful rooms, excellent staff, spectacular rooms.  

Tips:
-24 on site limo service with very reasonable rates.  
-Room service has a 22% service fee AND a delivery charge
 
Food is pricey, but we didn't have a single bad meal.

reviews.author: Dollyamas
reviews.title: Wonderful property
reviews.text: The resort is a beautiful property and exceptionally well maintained. The rooms are lovely and immaculately maintained. All of the services are excellent and the staff professional and courteous. A wonderful destination. I will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Brenton M
reviews.title: Platinum Member reveiw
reviews.text:
The platinum member benefits are okay. They waive the 29.00 resort fee. Yet in three separate trips to this property we have never had our room upgraded. This is the single hotel in the Starwood chain that has failed to up grade our room. Even up request, we did not receive an upgrade to our room. For that we will work with another Starwood property in the future. 

The staff is great, service is prefect 100% of the time. The property is as a whole is very nice.

reviews.author: BOLDMissionHills_KS
reviews.title: Your Best Starwood Option in Scottsdale – The Phoenician
reviews.text:
If you are trying to decide on whether to stay at The Canyon Suites or The Phoenician Hotel, I hope this review helps in your decision. Fortunately, we have had the opportunity to stay at both properties. I must first say they are BOTH excellent properties and truly some of the best that Starwood has to offer. Comparing platinum recognition, price, convenience, guest room, and service, The Phoenician is definitely the winner. Let me explain why.
 
Platinum Recognition –The upgrade and recognition we received at the Phoenician was much better than the Canyon Suites. The Phoenician provided us with a suite upgrade, local gift, and waived the resort fee. We did not receive any of these upgrades at the Canyon Suites. You changes of getting an upgrade are better at The Phoenician since they have many more suites.
 
Price/Hotel Category – The Phoenician was much more affordable and requires less Starwood Points. The Phoenician is a category 5 hotel and The Canyon Suites is a category 6. There is truly not that much different to spring for the higher prices or points. The Phoenician also offers cash and point more often.
 
Convenience – Most of what you will want to do at the resort will be located closer to the Phoenician’s property. This include tennis, gym, spa, & golf. We loved parking in front of our Casita at getting into our car quickly for short trips to the mall, store, or dinner. At the Canyon Suites, they offer free car valet service, but it takes a while to get your car. They also have a free car service; however, it is rarely available. You should note that staying at the Canyon Suites will have you feeling a bit “removed” from the center of all shared resort activities.
 
Guest Rooms – I actually preferred the rooms at the Phoenician. The Casita we stayed in was spectacular. The kitchen, fireplace, dining room table, and three balconies were new and picture perfect. The Canyon Suites rooms are a bit dated with 70’s décor.
 
Customer Service – Both locations have outstanding service. Everything from check-in to property maintenance was perfect. Everyone was friendly and helpful.
 
Helpful Hints –
Pay extra to stay in a one or two bedroom Casita. They are spectacular.
Make sure to take a hike up Camelback Mountain. Access to the trail is just a short walk from the tennis courts.
Try the Happy Hour at Relish. It is fun and there are great deals.
Have a drink and/or dinner at J&G on the property. Go before sunset to enjoy it. The views are beautiful.
Play a game of tennis, which is included in your resort fees. The hotel will provide complimentary rackets and balls. The grass court costs $35 per person and a great splurge if you are a tennis nut.
Breakfast at Il Terrazzo is very good. As Platinum members, you get an $18 credit for two ($36 total) towards your breakfast bill. If you prefer, your breakfast will be completely complimentary if you opt for the continental buffet breakfast.
 
If you are looking for the best Starwood value in Scottsdale and want to be close to that action, you will definitely want to stay at the Phoenician. It is one of the best Starwood Resorts in the country.

reviews.author: trvlmaven
reviews.title: Excellent and relaxing stay
reviews.text:
We stayed for 4 nights in December at the Phoenician. I had considered other hotels in Scottsdale, but we decided to stay here and treat ourselves. I don't regret that decision one bit. The Phoenician is very luxurious resort very centrally located- close to Old Scottsdale, Phoenix, etc. We stayed in a Grand Deluxe Room- very spacious with a balcony overlooking the lawn and pool area. Oversized bathroom, great amenities- Keurig coffee maker, large TV. 
We enjoyed the grounds and public spaces of the Phoenician- spent time in the lobby and the porch outside the lobby in the evening- very relaxing. The pool areas were fantastic- there were 8 pools, so we were able to relax at one pool that was for adults and it was very peaceful. A family with kids did come into that pool and I was surprised none of the attendants didn't direct them to one of the other pools. Service was a little slow but not terrible. There is a terrific gym, world-class tennis courts, the beautiful cactus gardens- so much to enjoy. I highly suggest a stay at the Phoenician for a relaxing stay- you will leave refreshed!

reviews.author: MHlush
reviews.title: Great for relaxation and golf
reviews.text:
My wife and I booked a 4 day stay on SPG points to get away from the cold Northeast, and play some golf just after Christmas, 2013.  The hotel itself is on beautiful grounds, well kept, and great scenery all around.  As I am a Gold SPG member, we received a base room but with a gorgeous view of Phoenix and the surrounding area.

The service was impeccable, and I cannot praise the staff for always looking to go 'above and beyond'  It is exactly what a Luxury Collection hotel should be, plus more.

Unfortunately, the only restaurant we ate within the resort grounds was Relish, a bistro burger bar.  I am a man who enjoys food, and even though the burgers were priced at $16.99, you did get a lot of burger.  In addition, we did spend some time at the hotel lounge/bar area, and the wait staff was on point.

If you enjoy golf, the resort has 3 9-hole golf courses onsite, and I was only able to experience Desert, and half of Canyon, due to Twilight play.  The course/fairways are well kept, the greens are gorgeous, and the course is challenging.  For a novice golfer such as myself, I was able to keep the ball in play for the most part, but some of the holes can be quite narrow, with sand traps and rocky areas, aplenty.  The golf staff was really courteous and professional.  The pro shop had plenty of clothes to purchase, however, I didn't see many ball sleeves.  I could have missed these altogether, but just in case, make sure you bring a few extra sleeves of balls if you have a tendency to lose them.  This will help you in the long run.

Overall, the resort was a bit pricey, BUT you do get what you pay for.  Professional service levels, well kept grounds, and a great experience all around.  Although this was my wife's and I first trip to the Scottsdale area, we will make sure to return someday and make The Phoenician our resort of preference.

reviews.author: bettybreck
reviews.title: Not as impressed as I wanted to be...
reviews.text:
I did not stay overnight at The Phonecian, instead I had a spa day and afternoon holiday tea party booked. 

My first disappointment was when we called to book our (3) spa massages. We told the spa representative that we had a 7 year old girl with us who was part of our Ladies Day Out and we wanted to include her. We were told that she would not be able to stay in the spa (even with an adult in our group the entire time) because the age limit at the spa was 15. We understood this and then suggested that maybe she could swim in the pool with one of us while we were staggered our massages. This time, the spa representative said this was absolutely not possible at all, and if we were "caught" in the pool area, we would be escorted out by security. 

We had approximately $600 in massages booked and they couldn't even let one child in the pool? And then to be escorted out? We were NOT looking for the spa or an employee to babysit this child. We were going to have one of us with her the entire time. 

That's not much of a "can-do" attitude if you ask me.

The second disappointment came after we received our bill for our tea. Each person who submitted a credit card had a section under the sub-total for "service charge" and then the next line was for "gratuity". We were confused so we asked our server what the "service charge" meant. She said it was the automatic gratuity. I asked if it was 20%? She said no - it was actually 22% percent and we thank you very much for this.

Where was the full disclosure on this? The servers did indeed deserve at least a 20% tip, but to hide it in a service charge in the hopes that people are not paying attention and then double the tip is deceitful. Clearly, the management has caved to the demands of the employees on this one. 

If I was answering a net-promoter survey from this resort, I would be a complete DETRACTOR.

reviews.author: Patti G
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text:
We vacationed here with our daughter, son-in-law and 18 month old granddaughter . The people here are gracious, helpful and knowledgeable about the facility and surrounding area. We had two rooms facing the lake and lower pool area and they were both clean and roomy. We requested Steve every morning for breakfast at the restaurant as he was great. It was lovely to sit out on the patio or the balcony and enjoy the scenery and balmy warm air. 

Would we go back?  In a heartbeat.

reviews.author: 780brianl
reviews.title: Campy but in a good way
reviews.text: Beautiful property that has a certain Southwestern campiness that I enjoy.  Service is pretty good.  Definitely worth walking around the grounds as there is a lot to see.  However, I found the food at the J&G Steakhouse to be fairly disappointing.

reviews.author: daverw6LosAngeles
reviews.title: Everything a resort should be
reviews.text:
After a recent 4-night stay, I have to say the Phoenician is everything a resort should be.

Spacious rooms overlooking beautiful grounds. Unique features such as their Cactus Garden. A number of dining options, including the first-rate J&G Steakhouse, which should be a destination whether or not you're at the resort. The Relish Burger Bistro (down at the golf club), is a great choice for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Get the Bloody Mary - a meal in itself.

And the Centre for Well-being. The hot stone massage as delivered by Kristen is not to be missed. A wide range of services means there is something for everybody.

One of Phoenix/Scottsdales prime attractions, Camelback Mountain, is literally out the resort's back door - walking distance.

Only negative I have is service at the poolside Oasis restaurant. Sat for 15 minutes with no service whatsoever, so moved on to Relish. Plenty of servers, just didn't seem organized.

reviews.author: amy e
reviews.title: Exceptional property but lacking attention to details
reviews.text:
This was our 10th visit to the Phoenician.  The property is beautiful but the attention to detail makes it not a luxury resort.

Pros:
- location perfect - close to PHX & Scottsdale 
- property is beautiful 
- lots of restaurant options 
- great spa & gym 
- people are very nice 
- turn down service lovely touch 
-large rooms 

Cons:
- attention to detail lacking
- we have had light bulbs out in our bathroom for the entire stay
- 2 nights in a row the wrong items were delivered from room service 
- we had to move rooms after our 1st night & waited 45 min for a bellman before giving up & moving ourselves 
-wifi slow - I turned off & went back to AT&T 

Overall a great place that needs some tightening up to bring it back to its former glory

reviews.author: RknRon
reviews.title: Great grounds and great room
reviews.text: We had afternoon tea (a must do if you are here in the area - it makes you appreciate the English), toured the facility and got our room upgraded to a suite.  The suite is as big as a house.  The reason for the 4 stars is there was no creamer in the room for coffee and we had to request a key to the minibar.

reviews.author: Kudzubuy
reviews.title: Great Hotel, wonderful Service
reviews.text: We enjoyed the Hotel and the area. This was a great stay, we enoyed the dining, the room, the view, the gym, the pool was under construction. enjoyed the local area, food and malls. Went their for physical and will be back this next year.

reviews.author: Refresh33
reviews.title: Perfect " Ladies Weekend Out"
reviews.text:
If you are looking for a great Spa Resort to meet your girlfriends at, you will love
the Phoenician!  The Spa was heavenly, the food was superb and the resort 
was beautiful !  It is close to shopping with Niemans and Saks, and 5 star
 restaurants in downtown Scottsdale, especially The Mission, if you venture off the awesome property.

reviews.author: eliz933
reviews.title: Another great stay!
reviews.text:
Just left The Phoenician and we are so sad. It was another beautiful stay. We loved all the holiday decorations. They've obviously started focusing more on families again with great  activities coming up for the holidays. It looks like they have a lot of options for kids of all ages. I wish we could have done the guided cactus garden tour and the beverage class in grape and grain, next time! Al was our server in Il Terrazzo and he's the best! Also spent time at Relish and Andrew took great care of us. 
This time we had our baby with us and the crib was nice to have. I would recommend bringing an extra lined garbage pail with a crib request!! It would be used. 

We can't wait to come back for the splash pad!

reviews.author: mymysmema
reviews.title: Absolute elegance
reviews.text: Probably the best hotel I have been to. The utmost in luxury in a glorious valley that is breathtakingly gorgeous. No need to leave the resort, as everything you might desire is on site! Wonderful meeting facilities and shops. The cactus tour should not be missed!

reviews.author: John R
reviews.title: Casita Rooms Are Convenient for Golf, Spa & Parking
reviews.text:
We had two rooms at The Phoenician for a two-night stay in December.  Both rooms were given SPG Platinum upgrades to Casita Rooms.  These rooms are roughly the same size as the rooms in the main building but are located in a separate area.  Staying in these rooms means you're closer to the golf course, spa and mother of pearl pool.  You'll also have a bit more privacy and you'll park your car for free right in front of your room.  The downside is that you'll have quite a walk to the main building for access to the free SPG Platinum continental breakfast (if you select that option) or other food & beverage offerings.  The golf club house does have a restaurant as well, but will not have as much to offer as the main building.  An alternative is to take your car up to the main building when you're dining.  The valets were very accommodating and would leave our car right out front without charging us any fees.

The room worked well for us since we had golf plans.  The main pools were closed during our stay for renovations so we didn't utilize them.  The SPG Platinum breakfast is a good option if you're eating on a weekend when they have the buffet, however it's not offered during the week so you'll order from a menu.

The service was good overall.  Standouts were the omelette chef and server at Il Terrazo.

I'd recommend trying drinks and small plates at the Thirsty Camel lobby lounge during sunset.

SPG members should note that golf charges do not accrue SPG points.

reviews.author: Lori H
reviews.title: Luxurious - Excellent Experience
reviews.text: My husband was on a business trip and conference held at the resort. The weather was very nice the first two days then we got rain and a bit cooler but the pool was still incredible. They were doing some construction work in the upper levels which affected the experience at the pool and we couldn't really use our patio due to the noise, but evenings were fine and I do understand the work has to be done some time; you just always wish it was at a different time than when you'll be staying there. Anyway, the room was plush, luxurious, very spacious with staff attending to small details. I thoroughly enjoyed my short walks through the cactus garden and if you are a photographer, you can get some great macro work done there. Several eating options and all can cater to my unusual food allergies with the Relish Burger Bistro going above and beyond with a menu that not only lists gluten but 7 other allergens under each menu item. That was a rare treat for me. I loved this resort and hope to stay again some day with more time (and less construction).

reviews.author: cimartin
reviews.title: Outstanding resort
reviews.text: I stayed at the Phoenician in Nov 2013 for a 5-day conference and was most pleased with the service, accommodations, location and food. All of the staff I encountered were friendly and helpful...valet, bellmen, desk clerks, restaurant, and conference/catering staff. My room was very spacious and nice, and I LOVED that my room had a coffee machine (not common in luxury hotels these days).

reviews.author: NYC3131
reviews.title: Stepping up their game
reviews.text: I have traveled to the Phoenician 4-5 times over the last 5 years, and my recent trip was my best. The resort is really stepping up its game in terms of service and care of the property. Really executing very well on all of the small things, which collectively made for a true luxury experience. Wonderful stay all around, and hope to come back soon!

reviews.author: RCM
reviews.title: Time Tested Luxury
reviews.text: Second visit and it still wows my wife. A classic style of luxury. Outstanding restaurants and amenities. Service is exceptional as are the spa and entertainment. The Phoenician is one heck of a place to relax as well as for business meetings.

reviews.author: dps_Sedona
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort - First Class all the way
reviews.text: We spent our anniversary here over the weekend.  Had never been to this resort.  It is so well maintained.  The grounds are beautiful.  Pools are beautiful.  The interior was decorated for the Holidays and beautiful.  The staff was very attentive and welcoming.  Just the experience we were looking for and hoping to get.  No disappointments.

reviews.author: MariliaClark
reviews.title: In the "lap of luxury"!
reviews.text:
We stayed for 5 days in a Guestroom Casita at the Phoenician, using our Starwood points, what a wonderful experience! Large, super comfy beds, extra large bathroom with separate sink areas, nice tub, big shower and even a walk-in closet! Nice, big flat screen TV (happy hubby!), sitting area outside facing Camelback Mtn and the pools.Even with extensive pool work being done at the time of our stay, that didn't take anything away from the atmosphere.
A bit on the cold side, but nice and sunny to enjoy the grounds and the beautiful gardens, including the Cactus Garden with pretty Christmas lights in the evening.
Staff and service were great! 
Great experience at the "Relish" restaurant at the Golf Club, we went there twice, great Happy Hour from 3:30 pm...
A wonderful way to feel very special in a classy resort!

reviews.author: jkozik
reviews.title: Luxury Resort.  Great Spa, great golf, fine dining and entertainment.  Loud jackhammers.
reviews.text:
For me back for the first time in over ten years, the Phoenician Resort has been a recurring  meeting place for my wife's business. But for this weekend, it a fun getaway weekend for the both of us.  My wife loves the health spa, I love the Scottsdale golf scene and we both were looking forward to hiking the desert trails.  

Overall, things turned out great, but we were initially very disappointed with the loud jack-hammering going on with the pool rehab project.  What I thought would be a show stopper is now a faded distant memory; so many other good things figuratively muffled-out the noise.  By the time we were leaving, we were already making plans to come back.

The Phoenician is located at the foothills of the Camelback Mountains in Scottsdale.  The resort is a very luxurious hotel, a main building with normal hotel rooms, conference meeting areas, luxury shopping, multiple tiers of swimming pools, and a perimeter of smaller 2 story cottage like building with semi-private rooms, called Casida Guestrooms -- we stayed at one right next to the golf course and Centre for Well-Being spa -- which my wife loved!!

Room. Our Casida Guestroom had a beautiful view of Camelback mountain and the swimming pool complex.  The room had a nice king sized bed, huge master bathroom with big shower, jacuzzi-style bathtub, two sinks, and walk-in closet. The room had a normal flatscreen TV, Internet (included with the room) with both wired and wireless connections, and for a nice touch the turn-down service set the clock radio to some really nice mood music.  We didn't use the room mini-bar.

Golf. Our room was across the access lane from the Phoenician golf course.  I played a couple of rounds there first day on the Desert, the second day on the Canyon course.  The courses were in excellent condition, even though the morning tee times were delayed by frost.  The course runs along the foothills of the mountain, making for some really nice low-to-high and high-to-low golf shots; overall, I consider the courses mid-difficulty, not that hard.  The course edges up to the desert and we saw beautiful desert plants, roadrunners, and quail.  The pro-shop and starter staff did a great job.  I was thrilled when they recognized my 10 year old bag tag from my prior Phoenician visit.

Poolside. While the weather was cool (low 50s) and we weren't planning on much swimming, we were disappointed that half of the pools were being rehabbed.  Loud jackhammers spoiled the poolside atmosphere.  But on Saturday, the workers took a break and we spent the late afternoon by the mother of pearl pool.  My wife even swam in it; (yes, it was a heated pool); I covered myself in beach towels. A separate time, we sat by the fire on the outdoor patio. While cool, the sky was clear with very little wind.  Very refreshing -- and much better conditions that the snow and ice falling over the rest of the country. Both times, the Phoenician staff did a great job taking care of us. 

Food and Drink. The lobby level has a piano bar -- a very nice place to relax and have drinks;  we heard 3 different live performances.  On Saturday night we had dinner at the J&G Steakhouse; there, we had a really fine dinner, a great view of the Phoenix sunset, and yet another excellent live band.  The J&G was packed; it was a lively hopping place!!

While we saw a couple of families, the resort seemed to cater more to business functions and conferences.  We were thrilled when the golf starter called out for the St Louis Rams group to tee off.  

If you are still reading this far down, you need to understand that this is a really nice luxury resort --  these are code words for: It's expensive!  We knew this coming here, and overall, it is competitive with other luxury places we've stayed over the last couple of years.

Hiking. New for me, we went hiking.  My wife's business meetings usually included some kind of activity in the desert.  She took us to the McDowell Sonoran Preserve. Here, the desert trails run along the foothills of the McDowell Mountain Range about 30 minutes North East from our hotel.  We hiked the Lost Dog Wash Trail, the Bajada Nature Trail, and the Gateway Loop Trail.  This was beautiful. We saw big beautiful Saguaro cactus as well as barrel and cholla cactus.  Much more lush than I ever thought a desert would be.

Basketball Game. We went to the Phoenix Suns vs Toronto Raptors basketball game at the US Airways Center in downtown Phoenix.  We went straight from the hiking trails to the game.  The game was fun, very good play from both teams; we sat near some visitors from Canada.  The courtside announcer was full of energy; the dance crew, the gorilla, and the contests between the basketball timeouts were fun.  The stadium was new and the facilities were really nice. We were able to park close and cheap.

reviews.author: smr1021
reviews.title: Beautiful hotel with beautiful gardens in very nice location
reviews.text:
We stayed here for birthday celebration for two nights and this was a very pleasant experience. Hotel features like Cactus Garden, spa, pools, and restaurants are exceptional. Everything here made with great taste and style. We walked on Cactus Garden and pool areas, have a tour inside hotel to see art collection, stay in lobby tea court, visited all restaurants and used spa. We also had chance to see how hotel prepared for dining accommodation in Ballroom. It was beautifully decorated in Japanese style. Interior is exceptional and because of holiday season decoration outside was great.
Ours rom was oversized (600 sq. feet), and bathroom as well. We had a private balcony with a lounge chair and table. Room also had writing table. 
Spa was great with an oxygen infusion. Atmosphere in the spa was very relaxing  Hotel staf was very friendly and eager to help you in anything.
Over all we had a great time in this outstanding resort. I wish that we have something like this in St Louis. This resort is very highly recommended.

reviews.author: Jim S
reviews.title: Nope
reviews.text:
Our stay was totally not worth the price we paid and we actually cut the time we spent at the Phoenician short by four days and ended up moving to another hotel/resort with a similar reputation that was actually cheaper and an overall better experience.    

I don't think our issues with our stay were minor in that the room had an exposed electrical box in our closet, a bathroom faucet that didn't work, carpeting that was stained, a mini refrigerator that woke us up throughout the night,grounds that were mostly not accessible with a stroller due to construction and two twin beds in an upgraded suite that were not up to par by any means.   

The grounds generally looked fantastic (what we were able to see), but we had a difficult time actually getting around because it was too much of a pain to carry a stroller up and down so many stairs.

The only real bright spot was the staff in the golf pro-shop who gave us suggestions on what we could do in the area.  They also were kind enough to let our five year old putt some balls on the practice green which he really enjoyed.  The golf course looked great, but we didn't stay long enough to enjoy it.  

I have been to a number of resorts/hotels in the area and I heard good things about the Phoenician so we thought we would give it a try, but I have to say we really came away rather upset with our experience.

I totally understand our stay may have been a case of bad timing on our part, but that doesn't explain the condition of our room and the lack of notice regarding the construction.  It's also not the cheapest place (near $400 per night) to stay and we found it to be not worth the expense.     

We were traveling on vacation with our five year old and nine month old and we were uncomfortable letting our baby crawl on the floor in our room due to the condition of the carpet if that tells you anything about our stay.

reviews.author: TD64
reviews.title: Awesome Place!
reviews.text: We transferred to the Phoenician from another hotel and could not have been happier.  The room was very clean and had a view of the pool and grounds.  The pool area is amazing!  We ate at J&G Steakhouse 2 nights and Miguel was our server both nights.  He was great and provided some excellent suggestions for wines throughout our evening.  The food was fantastic!  We also ate at the lobby bar and had sushi.  Again, service and staff were great.

reviews.author: JohnSV
reviews.title: Big sprawling resort without much charm
reviews.text:
Rooms are big but in need of a refresh and can be quite a long walk from the lobby. However, staff are friendly, professional and courteous which really does help.
Effectively the hotel is simply a bit of a non descript sprawl.

reviews.author: bobk1717
reviews.title: Outstanding!
reviews.text: They keep doing this right here and I'll keep on returning. Elegant, but not stuffy, prisitne property, and customer focused staff. Special kudos to Jarred at the Oasis and Austin? at front desk, both are great ambassadors for the Phoenician brand.

reviews.author: vacationer71
reviews.title: Fine resort
reviews.text:
My wife and I enjoyed three days at the Phoenician, and I stayed another couple of days for a conference.

It's a beautiful, sprawling property -- we were in the North Wing which is a bit of a hike from the lobby, but offers quieter and larger rooms, which is probably worth it.  Ask to face the mountain, it's a gorgeous view and especially quiet.  Our room and its bath was spacious and well appointed, with fast WiFi.  Service was consistently good at check in, valet, what have you.

We played two of the the Phoenician's three 9-hole golf courses.  Beautiful courses, great for middling golfers (generous fairways, forgiving greens, and only a couple of very serious challenges).  Staff was fabulous.

We played tennis at the tennis center twice, nice staff and good facilities, but a definite hike to get there.  A bit expensive to be honest, and the grass court (always fun) was closed for overseeding.

The pool complex is beautiful and is broken up into loads of smaller areas which creates a lot more quiet and more personalized service that you'd get in comparable pool complexes.  The adults-only area is a nice touch.  We had no trouble getting chaises without having to come down at an early hour or needing to rent a cabana.

Over the trip, we ate at pretty much every restaurant in the place as well as room service and poolside service, and every food service point was competent with friendly, professional service.  Nothing to blow you away, cooking wise, but nothing to complain about, either.

Did not use in-room television or fitness center.  Business center was fine.

reviews.author: Foxjax
reviews.title: Rooms tired & outdated service terrible!
reviews.text: Don't let the common areas fool you. This hotel is badly in need of an update. Service, food quality and cleanliness is not the greatest. We stay here repeatedly with conferences...our firm must get a good deal because in the past we have stayed at two other much better hotels in the Phoenix area yet for some reason we keep coming back:(

reviews.author: David355
reviews.title: Sprawling resort, excellent service
reviews.text:
If you like big, sprawling resort properties ( 9 swimming pools, 3 -9 hole golf courses ), this is for you. The property, while it shows some signs of age and need for refurbishment, is flawlessly maintained. The staff have obviously been well-trained, as the standard of service is not only high, it is very consistent. 

Reflecting its size, there is a wide range of accommodation types available, from conventional hotel rooms with no view, to golf course villas to casitas.
Food is pricy ( fish sandwich, salad and a beer poolside $ 48.00 ). Although there are 9 pools, one of which is described as " the relaxation " pool, with children banned, you cannot get away from the piped-in music. if you want a quiet time by the pool, you can't do it here.

The onsite J&G Steakhouse ( which turns out to be a Jean Georges restaurant ) is excellent.

Be advised that there is presently construction underway at the both the extreme east and west ends of the property, so that if you are located at either end, on weekdays you will hear heavy equipment, jackhammers, etc.

reviews.author: kab77
reviews.title: Excellent Conference Experience
reviews.text:
Let me start by saying that I've stayed in a lot of expensive hotels touted as luxury 4 or 5-star resorts and I would almost never agree.  I really enjoyed my stay here for a conference and would absolutely recommend it.

Staff:  Professional at every turn.  No messing around on the job, which I have come to appreciate.  Everyone called me Mrs. but it wasn't overly formal.  Everyone smiled and said good morning - housekeeping, random employees walking by.  They left me a plate of cookies for my birthday - I assume they noticed my birthday from my brunch reservation.

Rooms:  I was disappointed in my room at first because of the carpet.  They really should change stained or bunched up carpet.  But that was the only issue.  I could throw a stone to Camelback mountain from my balcony so the view was lovely.  The bed provided an excellent night's sleep.  The bathroom was very spacious with the nice big standalone shower and the counter space was fantastic.  Hair dryer not great.  

Property:  Gorgeous.  The conference held an outdoor Moroccan themed party at the Jokake Inn.  Wow.  Maybe it was the lighting on all of the vegetation but it was almost magical.  The permanent bar was huge so we could grab and drink and stand around it to chat.  I would definitely hold a party at this location.  I went for a short run around the property before heading to a nearby neighborhood for a longer course. If you want to walk, you can stay on the property and enjoy the views of Camelback mountain.  The walk to Camelback Mountain trailhead is short from the hotel.  In the winter you will appreciate this - I once had to park 1.5 miles from the trailhead so the location is rock star.

Conference Space:  I could go on and on.  Best I've ever seen.  Decor is lovely.  Meetings spaces cool, but not freezing.  We got to eat outside at every meal and there were umbrellas to help with the sun.  

Conference Food:  Outstanding except for breakfast.  Breakfast pancakes pretty tough but when we had eggs I liked them.  Lunch was delicious - lots of fresh vegetables to choose from in salad form, grilled form, and steamed form but all were flavorful.  Meat was well-prepared  - not overcooked. Desserts were small so I could indulge without eating a ton or have a selection of a few if I was ready to chow-down.

Il Terrazzo:  My parents took me to brunch.  I thought I wouldn't be full with the 3-course brunch but I was full in the first two and my food was delicious.  I had Juevos Rancheros and loved it.  The pork was tender so I could cut it with a fork, the egg yolk was perfectly runny, and I liked the texture of the crunch tortilla at the bottom.  Enjoyed the seared Ahi as my first course - very well prepared and the portion was much larger than expected.  Bottomless mimosas too!  We took the last seating and the coffee was pretty burned by then but that was fine.

One issue with the outdoor seating - they HAVE to do something about the birds. It almost ruined brunch for us.  Birds are all over any food that gets left out (after diners leave).  Bus the tables faster or find a bird mitigation technique (no need to poison them, there's plenty of ways to do this).

Location:  Easy to drive to Scottsdale for shopping and excellent dining.

reviews.author: Ari S
reviews.title: Close to perfect
reviews.text:
I stayed here for the first time in almost 20 years and while the resort is starting to show some age it was still truly wonderful. 

It all starts at the front door with the valets and bell men taking your bags and car swiftly, whisking you in and the warm faces of the front desk staff. Not quite St. Regis warm, but close. 

We stayed in a casita (building B - try to get a Casita on the inner circle) instead of the hotel proper, and with all of the pool construction taking place it was a bit of a circuitous walk to get to the hotel proper, but the staff graciously picked us up in golf carts as we needed. It was an easy walk to the gym and golf club though and to the pools, had they not been under construction. 

The restaurants were very good, we ate a lot of catered meals in the convention but ate in the steak house for dinner one night - steak was fabulous, only gripe was the wine list, a little limited and overpriced. 

If you are a golfer, as I am, you will be a little disappointed in the courses. They were very nice and well maintained (Canyons is the best of the 3) but they are short and designed to be resort courses - they are just not Estancia or Troon North. But, as a family resort they are perfect.

The gym was excellent, great selection of machines, free weights and plenty of cardio machines - never had a problem getting what I wanted. Large studio for classes/stretching that I did not use but others did.

Overall, the service was top notch and the facilities were excellent. Luxurious towels, quality items and service make this a perfect place for a romantic retreat, conference center and when the pools are done (they have like 5 of them so it's not like there wasn't plenty of pool available) frankly, I can't think of a better family spot in AZ.

reviews.author: Witter1
reviews.title: Very attentive staff
reviews.text:
I stayed here for 2 nights following a trip to the Grand Canyon.  I am Gold, and they upgraded me (I had booked a standard casita) at checkin to a 'lagoon view.'  However, this casita seemed like a stepcousin to the casitas facing the pool - it was remote, dark, and also overlooked construction.  I went back to the front desk, and the check-in agent was great in finding me a similar room in a better location.  I was very satisfied with the service in general, from the bartender (Sean) at the Camel Lounge to the servers at Relish Bistro.  I thought the room furnishings were a bit dated, and couldn't believe they still had the old-fashioned thermometers (round, with a dial) in the rooms.

One disappointment (first world problems, but hey I'm paying an astronomical resort fee) is that  I didn't get any turn-down service the first night, and the second night, someone came by at 10:00 p.m., which in my opinion is way too late.  Perhaps it was because I was in a casita and not in the main hotel, but they need to step that up.

One great thing, if you are a fitness buff, you can walk to Camelback and hike there and back while everyone else needs to find street parking.  Very convenient.

Was it the best hotel experience I've ever had? no.  It was perfectly servicable, which isn't the best for a Luxury Collection.  If I had gone in peak season, and paid a lot more, I would have been much more disappointed. But, the weather was good, I slept well, I ate and drank well, and I would recommend it to others.

reviews.author: Stephanie K
reviews.title: Expected Better
reviews.text: Was sorely dissapointed in this hotel.  This might be a good hotel for those that wish they were still living in the 90's.  I was shocked that a so called luxury hotel was so outdated in both amenities and decor.  First of all, they still actually charge for wi-fi, by the day, no less.  I have been to 5 star hotels in other cities that have not only provided free wi-fi, they also had an iMac in the room for my personal use. The gym was also very difficult to find and far away...I got a work out in before I even arrived.  Finally, and what may be my biggest pet peave in hotel rooms these days is the fact that they only have sweet and low stocked for the coffee.  Seriously?!?! I didn't know they still made that stuff.  Will not return.

reviews.author: 74pj
reviews.title: Excellent Property
reviews.text: Huge room, huge bathroom both well appointed. The resort was almost full but it didn't feel overcrowded.  Pool and tennis facilities were very good too. We ate and drank at various places within the resort and all were great.

reviews.author: lucus82
reviews.title: As good as I frist time
reviews.text: This was our second visit to “The Phoenician”. You always worry if it will be as good as the first time. It did not disappoint The attention to service is still excellent.  The grounds, golf course and hotel are first rate.  We dined off the resort but we did use the service to and from the local restaurants which was great. Our breakfasts and lunches onsite were very good.  The bar in the main dining room is a must for the view and service.  The only issue was the rebuild of the pool area (very noise) but to be fair it's not something that would be normally happening.

reviews.author: heatherswan
reviews.title: Not a 5 star experience
reviews.text: We are Starwood gold members and the 4 night experience has been less than 5 star to say the least. The checkin was not professional. Our bidet is rusted and un useable. There are jack hammers and construction poolside. Our privacy tag was hanging on our door until 12:30. From 12:30-3 when the tag was off, no one cleaned our room and at 2:30 a message was left that if we wanted the room cleaned, we should call housekeeping due to the privacy tag on the door.

reviews.author: aarjay
reviews.title: Service, service, service
reviews.text:
We recently spent 4 nights at The Phoenician while my husband was on a conference.

The stand out of our time spent there was the calibre of the service which we received. This was across the board and included the concierge (who were just so incredibly friendly, helpful and informative), the dining staff in both the restaurant and the conference dining area (who were so obliging in assisting with foods to accommodate my food allergies),the maintenance guy and others too. I needed to package some items which we bought and they were happy to give us packing tape and boxes which they had. No ask was too big. 

Whilst we were there we had delicious Mexican Wedding Cakes and when we got home I emailed the  hotel asking if it were possible to get the recipe and it arrived in my inbox within the hour!! So thumbs up for excellent service :)

The pool area is lovely with plenty of shade if required, which is a pleasure. The room was very nice and spacious but nothing ooh aah. I guess one could say it is a typical Sheraton room of it's time - not suggesting at all that it needs renovating. It was in very good nick and I enjoyed the balcony with lounger.

The food in the restaurant was very nice. We ordered 6 meals all up there and they were all great. The food served at the conference was a bit disappointing. Certainly nothing to rave about. It would have been nice to be able to get toast at breakfast. Perhaps this has to do with the choices of the conference organisers.Not sure.

All up a great stay at the Phoenician and I can recommend it

reviews.author: luv2truv3l
reviews.title: A little tired by 5 star standards, but for Phoenix a step up
reviews.text:
When we arrived, the occupancy was very low.  
The location of our casita was great. Close to the pools and quiet overlooking the Camelback Mouintain.  
When we arrived the terrace was in need of a clean and the room felt unused for awhile
We arrived on the last weekend of the local last family long weekend.  
We left the resort once in a cab ride to a lovely delicatessen-wine store that was worth the drive.
 Also on Camelback but with great selection of anything you cannot get at the resort.
The burger bistro -relish was great. we ate there a few times.  an ongoing flow of golfers go through the place...the food is OK...
The steakhouse is stuffy...
They claimed to have no seats (empty restaurant at the time)..and almost grudgingly agreed to serve us... really strange ...maybe we were NOT dressed appropriately
The food was adequate for the price -not amazing...
 We enjoyed the adults ONLY-pool that was NOT adults only....Anyway..
Would we return? Maybe ......Because service was excellent....Keep your staff to keep people coming back...

reviews.author: longtimetraveller16
reviews.title: Once again, it was great!
reviews.text: This is my third visit to The Phoenician and it has maintained its standards and continued with upgrades.  Service was great as it should be for a hotel of this standard.  The gym is loaded with all the best equipment and the room was lovely.  We stayed in a villa on the ground floor near the pool and found it to be spacious and private.  The food was wonderful and the meetings and events in the ballroom great!   I have no negative comments and that's how it should be!!!

reviews.author: Thomas D
reviews.title: Excellent resort
reviews.text: I stayed at The Phoenician for a business conference over 3 nights.  The hotel is great.  The hotel is in excellent condition with great views.  My guest room was spacious, clean, very updated, and comfortable.  The staff was very friendly from check-in to room service to pool staff.  They do an excellent job and would highly recommend.

reviews.author: wicketty
reviews.title: Renovated & Magnificent
reviews.text:
We had a glorious 7 nights in a Suite. Everything was exceptional, from the room itself with 2 full bathrooms, the room service, the conference facilities to all the swimming pools.
Highly recommend if you want a luxurious break.

reviews.author: rosecroft2007
reviews.title: accounting/billing nightmare.
reviews.text: First off, let me say I LOVE the phonecian. I am a regular guest, and stay here well over 30 nights a year. Overall the resort and it's staff do a great job. But the billing and/or accounting department  is not at a 5-star level. Now you may ask, how would this affect your actual stay? My last stay was a three night stay november 2013. I always book with points, and as a 100/night platinum starwood guest, I used my personal concierge to book this stay. Imagine my  shock/anxiety/anger after seeing an $8,166.20 charge on my amex card!! Now this would not be such a bad thing, If the error was caught on my folio, and could be corrected and dismissed as a "typo". BUT when I left my folio was zeroed out, and my actual charges were around $300.00. I only discovered this charge because I checked my amex account online saturday night, where I saw this. I FREAKED OUT. I was up all night with worry, could do nothing about it!. So to say the least the accounting/billing department pretty much added several "grey hairs", days of worry/anxiety to my life, and pretty much wiped out my 3 nights of "relaxation". I understand from reading other reviews, this is common with this resort. Imagine if your bank did this, or well just about any merchant!. Really screws up your credit, your ability to use your card,  well you get the idea.

reviews.author: Songer5
reviews.title: Amazing Property and Service
reviews.text:
We booked using SPG Points for 5 nights. My platinum status didn't get us a suite upgrade, but we did get a 6th floor room overlooking the mountain. While it was a long walk each morning to the breakfast/pool area, we didn't mind and enjoyed taking our time.

The service across the board was exceptional. Everyone took the time to make you feel like a VIP, from the valet parking, to the front desk to the servers at each of the restaurants. We LOVED Relish Burger Bar the best, but we didn't get to try all the restaurants on the property.

Continental Breakfast was complimentary for SPG Platinums as a welcome amenity. We were given cards for each morning to give to the server. Each server seemed to have a different way to upgrade your breakfast however. Instead of just the cereal/yogurt/pastries, you could use the coupon to upgrade. One server gave us a $14 credit ($16 including tax/tip) per person off our bill. Another server just allowed us to order any item per person we wanted even if it was over $14 as long as "we didn't go crazy with all the sides." I never look a gift horse in the mouth.
