The grounds are exceptionally well maintained and if you have kids, bring them to the lower pool with the cabanas at 9:30AM where the staff will let your kids feed the koi fish in the pond behind the pool. My 2 year old loved it.

reviews.author: imphillips
reviews.title: Relaxing Retreat
reviews.text:
We enjoyed our long weekend at the Phoenician.  The grounds are truly lovely and the pool is very inviting. Our room was very comfortable with nice amenities including a coffee maker and good quality toiletries. The hotel itself is grand with a beautiful lobby staffed by very friendly and helpful concierge (especially Jacquie). I did find the front desk evaded my questions about room pricing policies.  We had added an extra night at our own expense and were surprised that there was not a better offer than the rate we could have received through our AAA membership. 

The service at each meal was excellent and the food was tasty.  The hospitality suite was well stocked with treats and drinks.  I especially liked the presentation by a local bird rescuer that the hotel set up in the garden.

It was a very nice break - especially as it was snowing at home!

reviews.author: tworthyreviewer
reviews.title: Great Lobby and Grounds...
reviews.text:
Hotel appears to be recently renovated with ample parking / valet, spectacular grounds and nice rooms. Service was good, check-in quick, and lobby very nice. 

Only complaint, was the large party happening outside our window at the pool. Wasn't objectionable to us as it came with some good music to listen to off our balcony. That being said, my guess is that functions are the norm here and some might find it  more disruptive. A beautiful pool and great views from higher floor rooms. Would return and recommend.

reviews.author: David M
reviews.title: Superb Staff
reviews.text: The Phoenician is understated and it takes time to appreciate just how good it is. The hotel's hallmark is attention to detail - everything is done well. Small courtesies like bringing round fresh towels and iced water poolside are done with meticulous efficency. No request seems to be too much trouble for the friendly and helpful staff. The grounds are beautifully kept. Once you get hold of the 'Master' wine list you realise they keep some great Bordeaux. We had a brilliant time here.

reviews.author: klf94
reviews.title: Awesome!
reviews.text:
We just returned from spending 5 nights at the Phoenician and had an absolutely wonderful time.  The service from everyone we encountered was very professional and friendly.  We were fortunate enough to have dinner in the Praying Monk and the meal was fabulous and it is a spectacular room for a special event.  There was a bit of improvements going on but it did not interfere with our stay.  I enjoyed a yoga class and my friends enjoyed an aqua yoga class.  
I am looking forward to planning our next visit.

reviews.author: Kevin Bonnie S
reviews.title: Majestic Views around every corner- Respectful Staff- very Personal <3
reviews.text:
~The Phoenician has been an incredible experience from fine dining to a beautiful hike to the ultimate spa experience..  We stayed a week and took advantage of their little perks like the Hike; WOW what an adventure, my group pushed ourselves hard and then FELT it the next day :D  just in time for a glorious massage..  We did the aquatic YOGA as well, thats the easiest..  They have 4 levels of YOGA <3
~The staff was SO helpful, i heard MY PLEASURE so many times and of coarse each and every one of them remembered my name the FIRST TIME and addressed me directly the whole stay..  i am so grateful to Maher in housekeeping and Marli by the pool..  Down to earth and pleasant <3

reviews.author: Bree_zimUK
reviews.title: Old world style with some cool touches
reviews.text: The Phoenician has a very old-world style but even though I generally prefer a more modern look I enjoyed the pools, as well as the fire-pits outside the bar area at night.  Service was great - super-friendly and helpful staff!

reviews.author: mummycentric
reviews.title: Girls Getaway
reviews.text: Had a lovely Mommy-Getaway w/ my dear friend. Loved the resort - had been there before which is why I chose it! Be sure to take the short walk from the hotel to the Cholla Trail of Camelback Mountain for a 1.5-2 hour hike with amazing views of Scottsdale. A great morning work-out, not for the faint of heart! Then back to the hotel for their amazing buffet breakfast!! Omelets to order, smoked salmon, all the delicious treats of the morning! The pool serves lovely food and drinks which is where we spent our afternoons after shopping at Kierland (20 min drive) or the nearby Fashion Plaza. The Spa was lovely as well and I would highly recommend the Phoenician for any type of relaxing getaway!! BTW, the MOST COMFY beds - ever!!!

reviews.author: gdptraveler
reviews.title: Spectacular Resort and Spectacular Staff
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is a luxury resort, to say the least. From the luxurious rooms, awesome pools, or the spectacular staff. Everything at the resort has the "Phoenician" branding from the water bottles to the towels with the hotel's logo to the bags with a hotel's logo. I don't even know where to start! When you pull into the lobby, bellman open your doors, take your luggage, and even give you Phoenician branded water with the hotel's logo! We arrived at around 1:00 p.m. and they were able to rush the room and get it by around 2:30 to 3:00ish. In the meantime, we went to Relish Burger Bistro, which was fantastic by the way (our family of 4 only needed 2 burgers we realized afterwards), where we were waited on by the awesome and helpful Rachel. She helped us a lot to kind of get to know the area! It is helpful to know that the resort does provide golf carts to shuttle guests around the property since it is so huge-- we had one take us to Relish from the lobby.

We had a guest casita room, which was incredible. The spacious bathroom included a huge marble shower, a large soaking tub, double vanity, and a water closet with a toilet and bade. However, we were disappointed that our room wasn't conveniently facing the pool, rather, it was facing the golf course, which was ok too. The large outdoor patio included a chaise lounge as well as a set of table and chairs.

We all really enjoyed the pools! There is a huge, elaborate pool complex which is basically made up of 3 levels. The top level, which has 3 pools and a kiddie pool. The middle pool is one large pool that the resorts splits in half-- one side is family friendly and the other is adult only. Finally, you have the bottom level with the water slide pool and the fantastic Mother of Pearl Pool which is all tile with the Phoenician logo in the middle, which was our favorite. The kids loved the slide which was wild at the end and gave everyone a few injuries. We especially enjoyed George Alexander the slide attendant! Now the pool situation can be a bit frustrating. Half of the chairs are in the shade, which is a problem for people like us who want the sun. 

However, there is one catch to the pool situation which was annoying, and would bring the hotel's rating down. Large businesses rent out parts of the pool complex so the guests can't get near the lawn with their event. During our stay, they rented out 3 of the pools including the Mother of Pearl Pool! Now this really ticked me off. Why would a hotel let a business rent out a pool and block it off from their guests who rightfully paid for it!!!?? That is just wrong-- the guests should be the priority, not the businesses! But in the end, this is a management problem, and the staff can't do anything about it-- this is the manager and owner's fault. 

On the other hand, all the staff we encountered did put the guests first. EVERYONE was so kind and helpful! Everyone always asked how our stay was and what they could do to make it better! I should've told them that they should open up the pools that they closed for the businesses! 

Overall, the hotel and grounds are gorgeous and staff is very helpful as well. The view looking back towards Camelback Mountain is breathtaking! I'm sure I left plenty out but I tried to cover a lot. I do definitely recommend Scottsdale Fashion Square for shopping (it's a mile down the road). It was also worth the drive to the Kierland Commons up north. Additionally, we took a drive to Sedona and it was so worth it! It is a must do if you've never done it before!

reviews.author: Jacqui
reviews.title: Older facility meant for the golf crowd
reviews.text:
Without doubt the views from the property are amazing and amenities were most likely top notch 'in the day'.  This property looks and feels as if it was once an gem and has been holding onto a heyday long gone.  It truly has the makings of a gorgeous hotel however the cream marble and brass fixtures mixed with some of the newer pieces, accentuate even further what is out of date.  Handrails throughout the property were wet with paint during our visit, so obviously the 40th coat when replacing them would provide an aesthetic upgrade and tactile confirmation.  

Upon arriving our room was changed from the first floor (where there was loud construction) to the third floor.  After a walk down a very long hallway, that had no lights and still surrounded by machine noise, we arrived to a half update room. Request a room closer to the elevator. Apparently, the third floor had been used for a convention/meeting rooms recently and they were putting furniture back together and cleaning up wet carpets. Perhaps this is why things didn't match in our room - three different eras of lamps and incongruous art?

Car service and valet were stellar.  They were prompt and helpful with information about the area and able to give us an idea how long to get where we were going each time.  Bell service was confused with our room change and I ended up going back to get my luggage to bring to the room myself.

Housekeeping began knocking at 8 a.m. and came back every 20 minutes - even after asking that they come in the afternoon.  Several items in our mini bar were stale and out of date - a bummer when you are hungry for a snack and have acquiesced to mini bar rates for convenience.  

The golf courses looked pristine and the hotel guests seemed to be mostly older folks and families.  The children's pool was busy while the adult pool was moderately populated with Ricky Martin on the radio and men drinking cans of beer in the pool playing water basketball.

A trip to the spa was telltale that this is not the touted 5 diamond resort & spa that it once was even though the pricing (which is elevated on the weekends regardless of being a hotel guest).  Manicure pedicure services are in the hair salon while the 2nd floor of the spa is reached by an industrial "wood" formica elevator.   Not a recommendation.  We booked elsewhere after canceling our appointments. 

The gym was clean and the equipment looked new and well kept; floor to ceiling glass made the small space seem airy and inviting.

The food was excellent at JG Steakhouse and the bar and live entertainment excellent.  I would definitely recommend the restaurant, bar and the ability to sit outside next to the fire pits with a cocktail.  Service at JG was top notch - attentive and personable without being intrusive. 

Not a bad hotel - just not as fabulous as the website leads you to believe.

reviews.author: susalina56
reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.text:
This is my second time to Scottsdale and first time at The Phoenician. Overall my boyfriend and I really, really liked the property and our stay.

The space itself is beautiful and Camelback provides a great view. We received an upgraded room prior to checking in and also received some coupons for breakfasts and dinner upon check-in, which was great. (This may be through a Starwood frequent member type program, I'm not sure.) We had a corner room that was a two-room suite, which was really spacious and included two bathrooms. The only negative was that it was a bit far from the pool and restaurants. The bed and turn-down service was great though!

The pool area was great and included 8 pools with one adult relaxation pool. My only suggestion would be to have more adult pools and just a few reserved for kids. The adult pool was shaded most of the day so it was mostly families instead of some quiet that we were hoping for. There was no wait for chairs and the staff brought out a pitcher of water right away and kept it filled all day, which was great. The waitstaff was really friendly, but a few more servers probably would have been helpful as there was a bit of a wait for food/drinks. We ate lunch by the pool each day and the menu and food was good.

I wasn't as huge a fan of the dinner options at the restaurants on-premise, but I did enjoy the live music by the lounge/bar at night. We headed into Scottsdale for dinner two nights and had really blah meals at two places that had great reviews, which was surprising. The cabs seemed really pricey for the distance ($29 for a ride that was maybe three miles?!) and the places were really not worth it. (We went to Wildfish and Roka Akor.)

The spa treatments were overall really good, though not cheap. The spa itself was pretty nice, but lacked much outside of the treatments itself. There is a meditation room, which is basically an outdoor quiet area with nice chairs. There was also a steam room and jacuzzi, but it left a little to be desired. I had an excellent treatment with Sara and highly recommend her. 

Overall a great stay and just what I was looking for - R&R. We're already planning to come back next fall.

reviews.author: Calberkeley1997
reviews.title: Family Weekend
reviews.text: My sisters and I always stay at least 2 nights at the Phoenician when we go to the desert. The food is incredible, the service is ok but what makes this resort a gem are the views. Staring at Camelback mountain while swimming at the pool or resting in a private cabana is all we need to feel at home. This is definitely one of our top 2 favorite resorts in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: Terri B
reviews.title: Business meetings in style!
reviews.text: Loved the meeting space at The Phoenician! The chairs were extremely comfortable, the decor - lovely, the round table amazing! The food provided was very good and the staff very accommodating. Will definitely return for pleasure next time!

reviews.author: UkCallie
reviews.title: Very comfortable
reviews.text: A group of us stayed here for 3 nights.All staff were very helpful and pleasant.Great rooms and views.Hotel and grounds were quite spacious |I only wish we had seen more of it. We spent most days around the pools playing water volley ball etc.

reviews.author: RAHWilmette
reviews.title: Depends on room
reviews.text: Lovely hotel with friendly competent staff. It is a large conference hotel and we were there at quiet period so we don't know effect on service if full. Nice pool.. Rooms facing Camelback Mtn have first rate views. You can get stuck with views or arrival area and valet parking so be careful.  Housekeeping spotty. Vacuum cleaners and Swifters left in hall overnight, some cleaning requests not followed. Room location is everything. Request 6th floor facing Camelback.

reviews.author: lansingisland
reviews.title: Just great
reviews.text: We thoroughly enjoyed our 3 night stay at this fabulous resort.  The facility and grounds are stunning, the rooms were large and very quiet and comfortable, and all the people we encountered were wonderful and friendly.  One small quibble was the lack of available coffee for the folk from the east coast who were up at 4:30 Phoenix time.  There are coffee makers in the rooms but I did not want to disturb my husband.  The front desk might keep a pot handy as there were several of us looking for our morning joe that early...  I loved the small workout room (equipped with water and fruit), pools, bars and all of the restaurants that we tried.  The staff even took us in a golf cart to the trail head for Camelback Mountain hike (challenging!). Housekeeping even mailed me some clothing I had left in the closet.  Highly recommend this place.

reviews.author: weathergirl29
reviews.title: A lovely desert oasis...perfect for a long weekend
reviews.text:
We booked a 4-night stay for the two of us before my husband had to stay for the following week for a business meeting. The hotel is only 15-20min away from the airport, and is close enough to Old Town that you have plenty of restaurants and activities from which to choose.

Hotel Overview: The lobby is spacious and grand, with a beautiful fountain as the centerpiece. A grand piano serves as the focus of some light evening entertainment, with the Thirsty Camel bar overlooking the grounds. Check in was smooth and easy and we got into our room shortly. It is a large property overall, so be prepared for a lot of walking in between your room and the other areas of the property. Some stairs as well, so maybe not as convenient for those with mobility issues.

Room: The rooms are a nice size with a king bed and sitting area (sofa, chair, coffee table) plus a desk. The balcony was a comfortable size as well with two chairs and a padded chaise lounge. We overlooked the pool and cities of Phoenix/Tempe in the distance. There is ample space for clothes with TWO full size closets (very nice to be able to separate clothes) and a large bureau with several drawers. Bathroom is very large with a deep soaking tub, double sinks and a walk-in shower. ONLY complaint (and it is a small one) is that the shower head is low-flow (I'm sure for conservations reasons...being in the desert and all) and it took awhile for the water to get hot. Very small complaints, but it was something I noticed.

Pools: There are many different pools on different tiers of the property. There were always plenty of padded loungers available in the morning, but they would fill up pretty quickly in the afternoon. Attendants would bring extra towels and a pitcher of ice water with cups. This was a wonderful touch that I honestly have not experienced anywhere else, even at the top beach resorts we have visited. Hope they don't stop doing this! There are plenty of shade options, including umbrellas. Attendants stroll through if you want to order a drink or food. The lowest tier pool has a slide attached, so that is where most of the kids are...if you want a quieter experience, go to the "adult's only" pool by the cocktail bar.

Restaurants: We ate at J&G Steakhouse our first night and really enjoyed it. We ordered salads, filets and a side of potato gratin and it was all amazing. Nice ambiance and the servers are well trained. Would recommend, even if you are planning to eat some meals off property as well. We ate breakfast each morning at Il Terrazzo and it was always an enjoyable experience. Definitely get the "Il Terrazzo benedict" poached eggs with spinach and tomatoes on top of foccacia bread- delish! 

Spa: Had two treatments at their "Centre for Well-Being" and they were both nice. The spa itself is actually pretty small, so don't expect a large property. There is a small jacuzzi, a steam room and a sauna...plus a co-ed area with zero-gravity chairs to relax in before your treatments. I had an 80min massage and 80min facial, and they were both pretty average, but nonetheless relaxing and enjoyable.

reviews.author: ChaTha123
reviews.title: Beautiful and relaxing
reviews.text: Went off season (at the beginning of the summer) so it was less crowded and very hot (dry viheat not humid like we have in NYC). Got upgraded to a room with a view of the mountain behind the hotel. Most amazing thing about the hotel are the grounds. There are walking paths and the grounds are meticulous! The pools are also excellent with probably half a dozen to choose from.  Service was great, very friendly. Borrowed bikes and went biked around Scottsdale. This is more of a relaxed understated type hotel, not glam but still elegant which was great for a relaxing sit-by-the-pool vacation.

reviews.author: AMM5226
reviews.title: Fabulous
reviews.text:
This hotel is fabulous. The rooms are really large and spacious with gorgeous views and a lovely balcony. The staff is welcoming and helpful. Everyone couldn’t have been more helpful. There is a bar with an outdoor area and fireplaces! Such a great ambience. Hotel parking costs $29 per day, so not inexpensive but it is a city. The food in all of the restaurants was very good. There are numerous pools from which to choose where you can get drinks or light food. 
I have stayed here several times and always have a wonderful experience. Relaxing and rejuvenating atmosphere. I highly recommend staying here for any reason. You will love it!

reviews.author: sunnyskiesabove
reviews.title: Love this hotel!  Service with a smile!
reviews.text:
I can't believe that I haven't written a review sooner.  I've stayed here each of the past 3 years for a conference and had wonderful experiences each time.  The staff could not be friendlier.  They are prompt with requests and happy to help.  The food at the restaurants is good.  (I've eaten at the Italian restaurant, steak restaurant, sandwich shop, by the pool and had room service.  I have no complaints with any of them.)  The rooms are large and well appointed.  Oh, and the beds....  I want to take it home with me!!   They are so comfortable!  The bathrooms are huge and they have tons of plush, very nice towels.  A definite plus!  The pools are fantastic and the grounds are great!  I love walking through the paths in the cactus garden.  

Also, my favorite spot is on the balcony off of the bar from the main lobby at night.  This is a very relaxing place to have some drinks and enjoy some conversation.  I highly recommend checking it out.

In addition, to give you more details on the efficiency of the staff - - last year due to medical circumstances, I needed to make some special requests to ensure my room was close to my meetings and to arrange for a refrigerator in the room as well as a late check-out.  All of this was handled over the phone ahead of time and ready for me when I arrived at the hotel.  (You'd be surprised how few other hotels were able to handle such requests.)

As for which room you should choose:  Personally, I prefer to look out to the pool and think that my favorite spot would be in the main building on one of the upper floors, but for my conference, you pretty much have to take what you can get.  This year I didn't have a view really (instead looked out to the traffic circle in front of the lobby), but they did a good job of trying to shield this view with some foliage.  The casitas are very nice too, but can be a bit of a hike from the main building.  If you're there to play golf, these would probably be perfect!

reviews.author: Cheaky44
reviews.title: Exceptional Anniversary Trip!!
reviews.text:
This was our first trip to the Phoenician and we were extremely happy with everything!!  I surprised my husband with a trip here for our 20th wedding anniversary and couldn’t have picked a better place to stay!

After about a 20-25 minute ride from the Phoenix airport we arrived around 3:00 pm and were greeted by the very friendly and professional Kaitlin at the front desk.  She congratulated us on our anniversary, informed me that we were upgraded to a 1 bedroom casita and made sure she added my Starwood number to our reservation.  She went over everything with me, pulled out a map of the property and showed me exactly where our casita was and that we could park right in front of the room.  I took the keys and we were on the way!

We stayed in Building “F” and were able to park directly in front of our door.  The casitas are 2 stories and do not have an elevator so we were quite happy that we were on the ground floor.  Our room was one of the most luxurious rooms we’ve stayed in.  (It’s right up there with the Ritz, Peninsula or Four Seasons in Chicago and Boston).  We had 2 full bathrooms, a very large living room with a fireplace, dining room table with 6 chairs, work center (fax, printer, internet connections) desk and a very large bedroom.  The bedroom also had a large desk/chair, 2 side chairs and table, 2 nightstands and a foot-bench at the bottom of the king size bed.  The mini-bar/fridge was fully stocked with everything you could need and the master bathroom was almost the size of the living room!

The bed was incredibly comfortable, the towels were very soft and absorbent and the toiletries smelled fresh and exhilarating.  We had 3 sets of sliding glass doors that allowed you to walk out onto the 2 different patios.  There were more than enough chairs/lounges on the patios that you have several couples over for cocktails.  You could walk out the patio, across the lawn and a bridge and you were at the “lower” pool.  We spent all of our time at this pool and on our patios.  This was an excellent building to be in because in the afternoon the patio stays in the shade and when the sun is BLAZING out there you can sit on the patio, stay cool and enjoy the views.

Service at the pool was excellent.  Every lounge chair had its own towel already on it waiting for you to sit down.  As soon as you did, one of the servers came by with an ice cold pitcher of water and 2 cups.  With the heat index it was 100 degrees when we were there so the water was refreshing and welcome.  Rich was our server and it was incredibly helpful without being over-attentive.  Because it was so warm we ate lightly and had the tuna salad sandwiches.  They were delicious and had a very nice spinach salad as a side.    

We couldn’t have asked for a better trip.  The Phoenician was wonderful and made our anniversary even more special.  We will definitely go back for a visit and are already taking about spending our 25th anniversary there!!  Thank you so much to the entire staff who made us feel so special during our visit and we will continue to tell all of our friends about out tript!!!

reviews.author: LoveDosTravel
reviews.title: Have stayed twice in room 6195
reviews.text: We have decided to call this room our Time Share in Scottsdale. It has a great view, but is not as shaded from sun and is too hot in the afternoon to be out there. The beds are fantastic and service is very good except housekeeping sometimes fails to replenish coffee / tea supplies. I loved the food in the small cafe--the grilled cheese sandwich and the portabella sandwich are excellent and so much less than the restaurants on property. We ate breakfast on property and it was $50!  After that we went to The Breakfast Club (not far) for half the price and just as good food. Pool is huge and nice. Patio off main lobby at night is wonderful.

reviews.author: luxevacationlover
reviews.title: Fantastic resort with great golf, spa, and pool
reviews.text: This was my second stay at the Phoenician and I have to say I love this resort.  Spacious rooms, great service... but truly spectacular golf, spa, and pool area.  We played 18 of the 27 holes - a really fun, challenging resort course with fantastic scenery and views.  The pool and views were very nice and even had time to get a massage.  The staff was very competent and food was great.  Can't wait to come back!

reviews.author: TheRamblingRountrees
reviews.title: Outstanding service in a beautiful setting
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at the Phoenician last week as part of a large business group. When we arrived we were quickly checked in by a friendly staff and given directions to our beautiful room on the fourth floor overlooking the pools. In the hall way we were warmly welcomed and shown to our room by the general manager.Our room faced the pools and and and we could also see mountains is the distance as well. The grounds were impeccable, the staff attentive and went over and above to serve us at all times. The first night we arrived, we had a private dinner at the Jokake Inn right on the premises. The quality of the food was excellent and the beauty that surrounded us was breathtaking. The chefs preparing the meal and servers were all very friendly and provided us with wonderful service at this outside dinner. The service provided at the concierge desk was outstanding throughout our stay as well. In fact any staff member met during our stay provided some of the best service we have ever received!  I could right more, but I definitely give the Phoenician five stars and will surely visit again soon!

reviews.author: Pete_Gill_W
reviews.title: Very Happy
reviews.text:
Big room, very well appointed, quiet and overlooking the pool.  Staff were all friendly and helpful. Great pools and we had a fabulous meal in J&G steakhouse,   Whilst we didn't use any sport facility they all looked fabulous. If we visit Scottsdale again The Phoenician will definitely be our first choice place to stay.
We were staying over Labor Day weekend and the hotel planned many extra entertainment events, we really enjoyed the bird display. We also endeavoured to climb Camelback Mountain behind the resort, but stopped 2/3 way up as we ran short of water - it is worth the climb but needs to be taken seriously and start early.  If like us you don't make it all the way enjoy the hummings birds.  
Fashion mall is 2 miles but if like us you have no car you can catch the number 50 bus from the bottom of the drive, which was $2 compared with $15 car from hotel.  We also walked one way.

reviews.author: SNL_in_Tokyo
reviews.title: Satisfactory but not more than that
reviews.text: I stayed for 3 nights at a 1BR Casita.  The room was well appointed and gently worn.  Reminds me a bit of St Regis in Houston.  What struck me was the perfunctory service.  Of course, I am likely to be prejudiced and spoiled by the Asian service standard as I mostly travel there.  But I kind of stared at the face of the breakfast waiter while he recites the very polite words explaining the offerings without meeting my eyes nor with a hint of smile to his face.

reviews.author: Ángel A
reviews.title: An Extension of Canyon Suites
reviews.text:
This property is an extension of The Canyon Suites. What a beautiful property. 

We were in town for a week and utilized the hotel as an extension of services. They provided the utmost customer service. What a pleasant property to stay at.

reviews.author: Raphael D
reviews.title: A week in paradise at an amazing luxury resort
reviews.text:
My wife and I just returned from a fabulous 8 night stay at The Phoenician. Our stay at the resort was truly exceptional, which is what prompted me to join TA and write my first ever review. We were celebrating my wife's 50th b-day and wanted a week of complete rest, relaxation and to spoil ourselves - and that is exactly what we got. My wife and I can be very critical when it is justified, so we feel it is only fair to also be complimentary when it is well-deserved.

We stayed in a 1 BR Casita Suite which was very spacious, had luxurious furnishings, and was most comfortable.The mattress, duvet, sheets & pillows were perfect (wish we could take the set home with us). The room was immaculately clean upon arrival and kept as such throughout our stay, with turn down service each evening. We had complete quiet/privacy, while at the same time being at close proximity to the Spa, the Golf Clubhouse, and the 'Mother of Pearl' pool. Shortly after checking in, the hotel was kind enough to surprise us with a bottle of champagne in honor of my wife's 50th birthday - very thoughtful and appreciated. 

After our daily early morning walk, we had breakfast most mornings at Il Terrazzo, and I have to say that we were pleasantly surprised by the quality & selection of the breakfast menu and the world class service of the wait staff. After the first day, the hostesses greeted us by name upon our arrival, and we were seated at the same table (per our request). The manager (Marc) and our waiter most days (Paul) and the rest of the staff went out of their way to ensure we had a great start to the day. I highly recommend the Yogurt Parfait, the omelets, and the 'everything' bagel with smoked salmon. 

We spent time relaxing at all the pools, and were very pleased with the various amenities such as the plush new towels, the comfy cushions on the loungers, the many umbrellas available (as we mostly like to be in the shade). In addition, the pool attendants bring the guests a pitcher of ice water which is a nice touch, though there is also a great assortment of food & beverage offerings at a reasonable cost considering it is a 5 Diamond resort. We had lunch by the pools several times, with the Turkey Burger and  Chicken Wrap being our favorite choices. We wanted to highlight one pool attendant in particular - Benjamin B. - who provided outstanding service. 

For dinner on our last evening we were fortunate to receive the assistance of Eric at the concierge desk who was able to get us a reservation (a prime table at peak dinner hour on a Saturday night) at Mastro's City Hall Steakhouse (5 minutes from the resort) - without Eric's help we would not have been able to get a table as Mastro's was completely full all night.   

I played a few rounds of golf, and although there are three 9 hole courses, I suggest the Desert & Canyon courses which are the most picturesque and challenging. The staff in the pro shop and the starter were quite friendly and helpful.

We each had 2 treatments at the spa (Centre for Well Being) as well as using the steam room & meditation lounge on most days. The facilities are wonderful and the experienced therapists gave absolutely great massages. After every visit we felt refreshed & rejuvenated. After our first visit to the spa, we were also greeted by name on each subsequent visit by Phillip at the spa reception counter.

The grounds throughout the resort are nothing short of spectacular. From the time you turn off Camelback Road and drive up to the main building, the majestic palm trees and flora greet you to make a memorable first impression. We loved strolling through the cactus garden, watching & listening to the numerous fountains, discovering the native artwork throughout the property, and  watching the koi fish in the lagoon, etc.... The main lobby & bar is also quite impressive and a great place to have a cocktail and listen to the evening entertainment either inside or on the patio overlooking the resort.

We've stayed at other resorts in Scottsdale (Westin Kierland, Fairmont Princess, Hilton Tapatio), and we've traveled extensively across the USA, Europe and Asia; and I have no qualms in saying our stay at The Phoenician was the best overall experience we've had - by far. Any discerning traveler would undoubtedly appreciate the heightened level of customer service and attention to detail by the staff as well as the deluxe accommodations, dining options, activities, etc... We will absolutely return to this spectacular resort again next year.

reviews.author: FRTravellers
reviews.title: Overall good experience but far from flawless
reviews.text:
Large and clean room, nice pools, gardens, lobby.
As far as I can remember, the Wireless Internet connection was good. 
For the rest, the other reviews you can read here pretty much describe the resort.

So what went wrong for us? Actually we can be picky but booking a five diamonds resort means that you expect a five diamonds service. And actually, even if the resort looks nice, it is nowhere near 5 diamonds (or 5 stars).

First, when we checked in after and long and exhausting travel we asked the front desk a small easy information : 
Is it too late to have a glass in a bar or restaurant in the resort? 
We were told that we could have a glass àt the bar in the main lobby.
Then the woman gave us map and our room key. 
And that's it. No further indication about the path to our room or anything. Must be easy to find the romm then ? 
Well, keep in mind that the resort is pretty large. So, after, 15 minutes looking around for some information, asking other guests, we came back to the front desk and asked our way. The woman apologized and gave us the information. She apologized right, but it shouldn't have happened in a first place.
We then unpacked our bagages and went back to the lobby in order to have a glass. We sat there only to be told 10 mins later that the bar is closing.
Ok, the woman seemed to be enduring a training session since another woman (manager?) was standing next to her during the entire checkin process. 
1) They made us waste some time because of the lack of informations
2) We couldn't have the glass we were waiting for.
3) Her collegue apparently couldn't care less about the lack of information we had.

After a rather good night (quiet hotel, good mattress) we decided to have breakfast at the restaurant facing pools and Golf.
Well, during a 25 days trip through the southwest, the is the one and only time I've been sick. 
That is what happens when using industrial mixtures rather than fresh eggs... Eggs are killers and they don't lie.

I didn't expect much from the Phoenician : we only had a single night there. Still, I'd certainly think twice before I'd return and I would certainly avoid eating their eggs again ...

Oh and make sure to ask them how to get to your room.

reviews.author: LisaLaza
reviews.title: Grounds & view lived up to "Luxury Collection"  branding, rooms not so much
reviews.text:
Husband and I celebrated our anniversary here over Labor Day Weekend.   Stayed 1 night - the Saturday of Labor Day Weekend.  Consistent with other reviews, I'd say the rooms were my least favorite part of the hotel.  They were better than average and  spacious, but definitely felt more dated than luxurious.  At check-in, I believe the front desk confirmed I had a Platinum upgrade....Ground floor at the end of the wing.  We had no noise issues which was nice, but again, there was nothing special about our view.  

Service was ok.  Again, not spectacular.  Waited a while to check in on Saturday around 5:30pm.  Someone at the front desk finally gave me the "we'll be with you in a moment" when she must've seen my irritated face when when another guest approached and looked like he wanted to cut in front of me and not wait his turn.  

We made it in time for last call at the Relish bar for happy hour.  Initial service was nice as they put in our order at 5:58pm so we could get the specials before they ended at 6pm.  After that, it felt like decades before we were checked on again. 

The resort had a nice outdoor concert and 2 food trucks on the lawn by the pools Saturday night for Labor Day.  That was a nice surprise. 

Interesting that some reviews mentioned there being an "Adult Only"  pool at the resort.  I didn't see any note of that during our stay but would've definitely liked that if they had offered and enforced that.  

All in all, I'd say our stay was ok.  I wouldn't go out of my way to plan a trip to Scottsdale and stay here, but I would recommend this resort (with my words of caution above) to anyone who will be traveling to Scottsdale.  Don't expect uber-luxury and you should have a fine stay. 

We stayed at the Westin Kierland the next night and it had its pros and cons too.  If pool time/relaxation is what your looking for, you will probably have a better chance of achieving this at the Phoenician.

reviews.author: Veronica S
reviews.title: View is the best part, rest is okay
reviews.text: Having grown up near this resort but never having stayed here I was curious to stay here on a visit back to Scottsdale. I am a frequent guest at the other top resorts around Camelback so I wanted a change of pace. Phoenician was interesting-- kind of like a Las Vegas hotel in the middle of Phoenix, in that it is very big, and has kind of a glitzy 80s vibe. I really liked the big patio off the lobby with the gorgeous view, and the bar was cute. My room was a bit dated but okay-- clean enough. Nice balcony with view of the mountain behind the hotel. The one thing I was not a fan of was the stale air in the hallways and the confusing layout (needed more signage at least). All in all I'm not sure I'd go out of my way to come back, but there's nothing terrible about the Phoenician. Just a very large resort hotel, with all the good (large grounds and pools) and not so good that comes with a big, 80s-era luxury hotel like this.

reviews.author: Sarah J
reviews.title: World's best Babymoon!!
reviews.text:
After visiting the Phoenician last week for our "Babymoon", I am not surprised to learn the resort is the #1 rated Luxury Collection hotel in the Starwood chain!! Wow! What an experience! My husband and I both work stressful jobs and we desperately needed some R&R before our baby makes her debut. I read way too many hotel and resort reviews before finally settling on the Phoenician. I was initially concerned about staying at the resort during Scottsdale's "off" season and worried the weather would be too hot for a 7 month preggo to enjoy the pool and sun.  However, after spending four days there, I quickly realized that off season is OUR season. 

Because the resort wasn't at 100% capacity, we felt like we were given a lot of special attention (and maybe they make everyone feel that way all throughout the year). From the moment we checked in, every single person at the resort made sure our stay was exceptional. The ladies at the front desk were so kind and offered restaurant advice and appropriately commented on the nature of our trip. They even gave me a gift-- a Starwood Kate Spade golf bag! The bellman, the servers... Even housekeeping made our stay phenomenal. We all know you can stay in a beautiful building with the nicest amenities... But if your room isn't clean then your view of the hotel is diminished. The housekeeping staff at the Phoenician are some of the best in the country. We always had plenty of fresh towels, always replenished soaps and coffees, and the little extra touches like chocolate on our pillow and slippers by our bed at night was so appreciated. 

If you stay at the resort, I highly recommend participating in the resort events and activities. As a non-yoga person, yoga was surprisingly one of the highlights of my stay. Susanna, the yoga instructor is amazing and truly teaches on every level--including altering her class so that I could participate (full belly and all). My husband enjoyed the cocktail lesson and we loved the live music at the Thirsty Camel at night (see my separate review on Yelp). 

The bottom line of my review: Would we go back? Absolutely!!!

reviews.author: The_Traveling_Tom
reviews.title: Phoenicianal!
reviews.text:
Once again, we can't say enough about how phenomenal our anniversary stay at the Phoenician was! Virtually every member of the highly-professional and friendly staff wished us a wonderful anniversary, and the hotel offered numerous delightful surprises during our visit...all adding up to our best stay at one of our favorite resorts!
All this, needless to say, is on top of the sheer beauty of the hotel...the Phoenician is the real deal! We can't wait to come back!
PS: their restaurant, Il Terrazzo, is truly not to be missed. We enjoyed both breakfasts and dinners!8

reviews.author: Jim P
reviews.title: Very approachable getaway
reviews.text: This is my second time here for a conference. What I like about this property is that it blends conference center with resort perfectly. I will come back with my family, the pools and staff make it a very easy place to stay. The spa is great, the gym is 24 hours and the restaraunt a are very good.

reviews.author: shesthetravelingirl
reviews.title: I am saddened that she is not as I remember her.
reviews.text:
It is with sadness that I have to write a review like this, but I think it is necessary for other travelers who are coming here looking for a quiet and serene oasis. I have been coming to the Phoenician for over 20 years in which I have many wonderful memories. During the years it has changed hands many times. It was at one time the premiere resort in Arizona. After my last visit, I still believe it to be a gem in the desert, but until I feel I have a need or longing to come back, I will gladly choose the Four Seasons and here’s why.

The Phoenician is a massively large resort requiring a tremendous amount of upkeep and maintenance. While they have done an okay job considering it is a resort encompassing over 600 rooms and suites, she is wearing down, and fast. Nothing has been done to really overhaul any of the standard rooms (besides suites) in the past 25 years. Carpets are dingy, floorboards and bases are dirty with old dust in crevices…it just looks old. The resort as a whole needs repairs to really look clean again. I would have thought within the past few years they would have attempted to update/renovate some of the standard rooms, but they have not. I knew the resort was looking a bit dated , but I kept coming back because it was still a quiet oasis to me with great service and it was still an impressive property. It was like coming home whenever we would visit Arizona.

We were on a short vacation with my parents in which we were arriving later than them. My father informed me the front desk kept them waiting 3 hours to check into their room. The woman at the desk told them it wouldn’t be long, so they went down to the pool bar to grab something to eat. Over 2 hours later they were still waiting which resulted in a wasted day. If the front desk had just told them after many inquiries about the room that it might be a while, they could have changed into their swim suits and enjoyed a pool day. However by the time it had been 2 hours it was too late for that. Come to find out they kept them waiting while housekeeping shampooed the carpet. It was still damp when they finally entered the room.

It was around the time of my parents’ anniversary so I had decided to send them three different gifts purchased off of the amenities section of the Phoenician’s website. I was very clear that I wanted one item to be delivered each night at 6:30pm over the 3 consecutive nights that we would be there. I even designated which item should be delivered on what date. I was disappointed to find that this instruction was completely ignored when the first night TWO of the gifts I had ordered arrived 1.5 hours before the designated time. Because we were still outside enjoying the pool, the chocolate covered strawberries were left out in the room to sweat and become warm (and undesirable to eat) and one of the other surprises I had ordered was ruined due to its early delivery. I called the front desk to express my displeasure and they referred me to in room dining who only apologized for the mistake without replacing the undesirable strawberries. I knew they screwed up, but they only went so far as to say they had sent an EXTRA of the fondue, rather than admit they made a mistake altogether without intention of sending my third surprise on the correct night. I told them it was fine when they said it would still arrive on the third night, although it really wasn’t because the surprise had been ruined. It would have been nice had they owned up to their mistake and offered to make up for it with something else, not just send a second of something they already got. 

My parents finished the second dessert the next night and left the tray of dirty dishes on the bench at the end of the bed for housekeeping to take. They did not want to put it outside their door because they feel dirty dishes outside hotel room doors just isn’t nice to look at. They left it in a spot that was more than visible for housekeeping to take. However, whoever turned down the bed that night not only neglected to inform the correct party to remove the dirty dishes (or take them themselves), they proceeded to knock over the martini glass full of chocolate onto the fabric bench, leaving a huge stain. Whoever the offender was attempted to wipe it up, although making it worse and even getting it onto the white sheets. They then PROCEEDED TO LEAVE THE DIRTY DISHES and the offending stains! Seriously? My parents had to go down to the front desk to inform them of the mishap so as not to be charged for something they didn’t do. This blatant lack of attention is not what I would consider 5 star or 5 diamond service.

If you are looking for an escape from the craziness of daily life, DO NOT come here over a holiday weekend. It’s almost as if the Phoenician forgets their original vision…it was not at all quiet, serene, or an oasis. Loud obnoxious drunk people crowded the Mother of Pearl pool and restaurants, and after speaking with fellow guests, found there was some less than desirable activity of a sexual nature going on at the pool bar the Saturday night we were there. If the Phoenician has changed their vision, in which it appears they are marketing themselves as a family resort, is this something you’d want your children to witness? From what I have heard nothing was done to quell this disturbing display.

I know the Phoenician may respond and try to defend the resort by stating they can’t control the activity within the resort walls, but they absolutely can. Slashing rates to almost $100 a night will cause this type of behavior to come trickling in. Considering I have never experienced this here before, I was appalled and disappointed with what I saw, and we always traveled here in the low season so that had nothing to do with it. It was a combination of slashing rates and heavy promoting of the Labor Day activities that caused the activities we saw. I can’t fault the wait staff at the Mother of Pearl pool; Rich taking care of the cabanas was as great as he’s been in the past, but I did see some cabana guests bringing in their own alcohol which is unacceptable and according to hotel policies, not allowed. However nothing was done to remove the offending alcohol from the premises. I was also under the impression that the pool just before the steps leading down to the Mother of Pearl pool is supposed to be an adult pool, although every time I went by there were children in that pool. Once again, the Phoenician failed to enforce their own policies. (Note: I am aware the Mother of Pearl pool is NOT adult only, although some guests believed it was supposed to be. The Phoenician needs to do a better job of informing guests of this, although I agree with other guests that it should be adult only.) The Phoenician also needs to put a limit on the amount of people occupying one cabana. We counted 12 people in the one next to us which was just overwhelmingly too many and invaded into the space we rightfully paid for.

If I come back, I know not to come back over a holiday weekend. We stayed at the Four Seasons Labor Day Weekend in 2011 and it was nothing like what we saw at the Phoenician. Everywhere we went we could not get away from loud, obnoxious people. We visited in July 2012 and had a wonderful, quiet meal at J&G. This time we were accompanied by the same VERY LOUD drunk people that were by the pool every day. While the food was still good, the ambiance was less than pleasant and I had to shout just for my husband sitting next to me to hear what I was saying. We did not ask to be moved in fear they would stick us into some back room that wasn’t encompassing of the restaurant’s beautiful décor.

All in all I will visit again if I know I can get back the experience that the Phoenician was once known for. For now, I prefer to remember her as she was in her yesteryear as she is not what she used to be.

reviews.author: trvlsokmonkey
reviews.title: Classic Elegance
reviews.text: I was there for a conference, the service was superb. The property is very nice and well kept. The rooms are very spacious and well stocked. The fitness center and spa are well equipped.The staff is very well trained, the service was exceptional.

reviews.author: Mauibums
reviews.title: Great resort for a quick getaway
reviews.text: We recently stayed over the Labor Day holiday and really enjoyed our time at this resort. The one thing that stood out for us was the friendliness of the staff. EVERYONE was super helpful and nice. They even call your room to tell you if they were unable to "turn down your room" because they saw a Privacy sign on the door. The Concierge helped us with dinner reservations and another gave us great detail on hiking Camelback. Our room was clean and comfortable. No complaints. Loved the location as well. The one thing I would like to see is that the Mother of Pearl turns into the "adults only" pool. The Oasis pool is supposed to be it, but that pool is small and does not get a lot of all day sun. When you are going to a resort of this caliber it would be great to see one great pool that adults could really relax at comfortably. We did rent a car, which I would recommend. Nothing is within walking distance and there are some great places to eat and shop. We valeted the first evening because we weren't sure of the self serve parking, but after that one day of $29.00 for valet, we quickly figured out that the self serve parking garage was pretty simple and used it the other 2 nights for free.

reviews.author: Peter F
reviews.title: Stayed over Labor Day - LOVED it.
reviews.text: We stayed at the Phoenician in a Casita over Labor Day in 2103.  The grounds and pool are top notch.  Everything about this place says luxury.  We dined at Il Terrazo and Relish, both were great.  The staff went out of their way to assist in anything we needed, including recommendations for dinner off the grounds.  Only complaint might be that the Casita rooms need new carpets and some new fixtures?

reviews.author: concetta2
reviews.title: Dazzling dessert oasis
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Phoenician for a 3-day spa getaway before visiting a friend in California. 

Although I arrived early (10:30 a.m.), I was immediately given a room, which was great in and of itself. More on that later.

The property and all spa/salon facilities was pristine are excellently maintained. The dining services and food quality were very good; wait staff at both the pool bar, Il Terazzo, and the Thirsty Camel Bar were very attentive. 

My spa services were well-executed. I had a Papaya Quench wrap, Swedish massage, manicure, wash/blowout. Only the manicure was a disappointment, lasting as much as one from a much cheaper nails-only establishment (for triple the price!) 

A few small downsides: 
My room was definitely in need of some serious cleaning and updating/renovations. The rugs, patio furniture, and curtains were all stained. There were dead insects near the sofa and the bed that were NOT removed after the first night of my stay. I do suspect that NOT every room in the complex was in such sad shape as mine. I had made the booking through expedia.com. 

I requested The NY Times upon check-in but was given the other two other available newspapers instead each morning of my stay. 

Overall, I enjoyed my stay at the Phoneician. The grounds were beautiful and the staff were friendly and welcoming.

reviews.author: ylime1001
reviews.title: Great Experience! A+
reviews.text: My boyfriend and I drove from Sedona to Phoenix for the last stitch of our wonderful trip. We heard such great things about the Phoenician so we definitely wanted to give it a go. From the moment we drove into the complex, the service was outstanding. Plenty of space at the pool with friendly staff coming around every 10 minutes to see if you're ready for a refill. Every time you sit at the pool, a staff member brings a pitcher of ice cold water and cups, which I thought was such a nice yet simple touch. The breakfast we had at the Italian restaurant was unbelievable. Best fruit platter and Eggs Benedict I've ever had: and I've had a lot. Our dinner at J and G's steakhouse was also exceptional, and a gorgeous view of the hotel estates. I was very impressed and hope to visit again soon!

reviews.author: trvlr50
reviews.title: Great Rooms
reviews.text:
Stayed here in June for a work conference. We had canyon view rooms. The room size is very large and the bathroom is fabulous. Beds are quite comfortable and with the chair and ottoman, desk or balcony with chaise, you have some sitting/relaxing options.
The pools are lovely and the lunch at the restaurant at the pool was great. Staff is attentive with pitchers of water and ice and cocktails if you wish. The desk staff are very professional as are the concierges. 
I felt this property did a great job in handling our conference in meeting our demands for meeting space and dining. I liked the fact all the rooms were easy to locate and the overall feeling of the property felt very succinct. 
I had the opportunity to rise early each day and walk the grounds and truly enjoyed the desert beauty. We had a company dinner one evening at the Jokake Inn and the food and service were great.
I did take the opportunity to experience a spa service. If you chose a facial, try and book it with Ann. She is a lovely woman and her facial was wonderful. Her gentle and sweet personality blended with her expertise and background make for a unique spa moment.
On last item, I ordered room service various times. One evening, some ice cream I ordered was not to my taste. I was quickly brought another flavor and was charged for neither when I checked out. Attention to detail and customer satisfaction are high on their list.

reviews.author: K M
reviews.title: What a lovely experience!
reviews.text:
My husband and I are just wrapping up our six night stay at the Phoenician.  I have always wanted to stay at this lovely, expansive hotel and I was not disappointed.  This is our second trip to Scottsdale to play golf in the last three years and our trip did not disappoint.  

We checked in for six nights the day before Labor Day.  Things were a little crazy Sunday, but everyone cleared out on Monday, so we basically had the place to ourselves for the week.  The staff is lovely!  So kind and helpful.  The decor is nice and despite its age (the Phoenician is celebrating its 25th anniversary this year), it is extremely well maintained.  All in all. . .I loved the place and was not disappointed after wanting to come visit for so long.

The hotel is huge.  If you are looking for a private, boutique experience, this is not your place.  If you're looking instead for a property that offers everything you could possibly need. . . golf, spa, pool, restaurants, in an elegant atmosphere, this is it.  We took advantage of all of that and were not disappointed.

The room was large.  I believe we had a Grand Deluxe room, which i understand is "grand" because of the view over the pool.  It was lovely with a king size bed, a good size balcony, a sitting area inside the room with a desk, sofa, coffee table, armchair . . a huge bathroom with a large sunken tub, marble shower, separate water closet, two sinks.  The room did not disappoint.

The first night we dined at Il Terrazzo, a restaurant in the bottom level of the hotel which offers three meals a day.  We took advantage of a three course, prix fixe menu with wine pairings for an additional nominal charge.  I believe the charge for dinner was $29 each plus $10 or $15 for wine pairings with every course.  It was a good value. . . the food was fine. . . nothing to rave about, but very solid.  We enjoyed Il Terrazzo for breakfast almost every morning and was also not disappointed.  ITs a beautiful restaurant with a lovely outdoor area if you're willing to brave the elements.

The pool at the Phoenician is what I would call a Vegas-style pool in that it is huge and diverse with a bar and a restaurant in the middle, like an island.  There are fountains and water features. . .an impressive slide for the kids that will land them in a separate pool off to the side.  The place is huge with three or so different levels of pools. . . private cabanas are available for rent for $150/day.  We originally rented one only to realize that the hotel cleared out after Labor Day and we pretty much had the entire three-levels to ourselves.  We enjoyed the pool, the bar/restaurant. . . Steve was wonderful  in taking care of us several afternoons.  We enjoyed this part of our trip very much.

Another highlight was the spa.  Do not miss this!  I enjoyed a massage and a facial while my husband also had a massage.  What I thought was exceptional about this spa was Luanne, who provided a facial for me and shared her knowledge from 22 years at the spa at the Phoenician.  She herself has beautiful skin that I attribute to her practicing what she preaches.  I emerged myself with gorgeous skin that I have kept up with the help of some of the products I purchased at the spa and plan to continue using when I return home.  The spa will ship for no charge. . . 

Golf was another lovely offering at the hotel.  It was day 3 for us, so the heat had caught up.  We didn't play our best game, but we enjoyed the course.  We also played Troon North, Grayhawk and We Ko Pa on this trip, but the Phoenician maintains a beautiful 27 holes.  I am still learning the game after picking it up five years ago, but I enjoyed the course.

All in all, it was a lovely stay.  I was honestly worried when I booked a six night stay that my husband and I would be climbing the walls after day four or five, but everything the hotel had to offer really made for a lovely, entertaining yet extremely relaxing stay.

reviews.author: LizzieMoyano
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: I spent 4 amazing days here...just beautiful!!! This resort has everything and is close to everything.  The property is so big!! The food was yummy down by the pool.  The room was big the beds are big and I had a fab view of the pool from my room. I want to go Back!!

reviews.author: diann w
reviews.title: Pools fantastic
reviews.text:
I love this property. The one pool has a cener of  Mother of Pearl! 
Pure luxury are the rooms!
room service great as well as the terrace dining room!
the lounge bar is fun, especially after playing golf (love to golf here too.)
i can never get enough of this wonderful peoperty!

reviews.author: funmom10877
reviews.title: Fun time
reviews.text: I can not say enough good things about our 5 wonderful days at this hotel.  From the time we checked in to the time we left everyone from the bell hops to the front office to the restaurant and poolside workers could not have tried harder to please us.  It was extremely hot and they made sure that we all had water every time we entered and exited the hotel.  The hotel staff was eager to talk to us and always helpful with directions and also reservations for various activities and dinners.  They even upgraded us to a 6th floor room which had a magnificent view of the mountains.  I hope some day I can return for another wonderful stay at this beautiful resort.

reviews.author: TheMysteryTraveler
reviews.title: An Ordinary Stay
reviews.text:
The Phoenician, a Luxury Collection Hotel in the Starwood family, is somewhat oddly located in the Scottsdale area.  Fairly close to Old Town Scottsdale and the Scottsdale Fashion Square.

The Phoenician is away from many other resorts in Scottsdale, but does have a great location in that it hugs the south side of Camelback Mountain.

As you enter the property, you will encounter a guard gate.  You will merely be asked if you are checking into the hotel, there for dinner, to play golf, etc. and pointed towards the appropriate parking area.

The Phoenician offers valet parking, of course, or complimentary covered self-parking.  If entering through the self-parking garage, you will take the elevator or escalator to the third floor in order to check-in.

Check-in was smooth, and all SPG Gold amenities were explained.  Since there is a resort fee of $29 per day, which includes internet, I chose the extra 250 points as my amenity.

Although the hotel was probably not more than 30% occupied, I did not get an upgrade.  I was able to book my room by finding a Better Rate Guarantee, which netted me an extra 2,000 Starpoints so all was not lost.

Rooms at The Phoenician are fairly large by most standards, measuring approximately 600 square feet.  The Grand Deluxe King Room overlooks the pool areas.  There is a balcony with patio furniture, but when its nearly 110 degrees sitting outside doesn’t sound like an appealing proposition.

Upon entering the room, there is a small bar area with a Keurig coffee maker to the right.

The bathroom is located to the left, and is very spacious.  There is a large soaking tub, shower and separate toilet.  There are double sinks with ample counter space, however three large vases take up some valuable counter space, although it is located over the tub.

There are Laboratoire Remede branded bath amenities which have a menthol/minty scent.

The bedroom is very spacious with ample room to roam around without running into furniture.  The bed is very comfortable, with super soft pillows.  There is a bed bench at the foot of the bed.

There is a large sofa and lounge chair with coffee table in which to unwind, relax and watch TV or have a conversation.

The desk area although fairly large, was lacking in outlets that were convenient to plug in your computer or to charge your phone or gadgets.

The Phoenician boasts 9 swimming pools, 27 holes of golf and tennis courts, in addition to a somewhat small gym and full spa.

Although a Five Diamond AAA hotel, service was professional but somewhat impersonal.  All employees were polite but not overly friendly.

The hotel also boasts J&G Steakhouse, a Jean George Vongerichten restaurant.  Although I did not get a chance to eat here on this visit, it is definitely on my list.  If anything close to my past visit at Prime at the Bellagio this is a sure hit.

The property is also starting to show its age, and could use an update in the near future.

I would definitely stay here again if I can find a good rate, otherwise there are other properties in the Scottsdale area worth checking out.

reviews.author: Gerry R
reviews.title: Getaway
reviews.text: One of our favorite stay-cations. The resort is spectacular nestled at the base of Camelback mountain. Excellent outdoor spaces, multiple swimming pools and 27 holes of golf. The resort also offers choices in dining from casual poolside to upscale.

reviews.author: loveadventure4
reviews.title: Mixed Levels of Service
reviews.text: When we previously stayed at The Phoenician, we found the service to be uniformly excellent.  Unfortunately we can not say the same for our last visit.  Check-in was slow, although there were two working the front desk and  we were "next in line". When I had made our reservations directly with the hotel reservations I was specific as to our room's view (Camelback Mountain) and was assured we would have it.  After a long day and slow check-in, we arrived to our room to find a view of the convention center roof.  Our room assignment was corrected when we immediately returned to the front desk, where we were asked if we had used any of the amenities in our original room.  Really?  We did love the view from our room. Camelback is a desert-view room and is not considered by the resort to be one of the premium views.  If you enjoy quiet, privacy, and a wonderful view of the mountain, it's the absolute best choice.  As far as experiences with other staff during our stay:  We enjoyed breakfast each morning in the coffee shop, where the staff was extremely friendly and fast, despite a large convention in attendance.  We appreciated the friendliness and helpfulness of the woman running the tennis pro shop.   The maid service was excellent. And, our waitress in the bar was great.  On the negative was the pool staff.  Although the pool was not crowded, the service staff appeared to want to converse between themselves and stand in the shade rather than check on their guests.  We waited twenty minutes before searching someone out to get a pitcher of ice water.  Overall, we enjoyed our stay and would consider returning.  But, we hope that our next experience would provide us with more uniform excellent service.

reviews.author: Anne Marie Nanc... V
reviews.title: The Grand Dame is showing her age
reviews.text: I've stayed in this property many many times over the last 15 years. It used to be elegant and regal with its High Tea service and  the classic five star bar with the requisite background live piano. The hotel now seems to cater to children and thrive on high volume deeply discounted weekends. While I recognize the need to summer revenue, The Phoenician has lowered its standards of class and decorum. The service in the hotel is excellent and the staff is well trained, the rooms are very clean and amenities above average and the restaurants are fairly good but overpriced. The common areas of the hotel are still in gorgeous condition but the hotel hallways are dismal and the rooms are average and need  complete remodel.  Catering to the masses with deep discounts changes the complexion of this once stellar property. The  Phoenician is a lovely property but it isn't "special"anymore.

reviews.author: ayu312
reviews.title: Amazing customer service!
reviews.text:
My husband and I just stayed at the Phoenician for 5 nights during the labor day weekend.  We got the unlimited golf package which is a great deal!  We were really impressed with the hotel.  The lobby is grand and beautiful!  Their art collection being displayed all over the hotel is impressive!  The room is very spacious and comfortable!   But what impressed us the most is their customer service!  Everyone working there is really friendly and wants to make sure you have a good time there.  
 
We would definitely come back!

reviews.author: larryt456
reviews.title: very nice hotel
reviews.text: Great hotel with nice large rooms,baths and beds. Super patio and pools galore. Play golf, hike , bike and enjoy the sun. Hotel has underground parking (your car stays cooler) and is located at the base of camelback mountain.

reviews.author: Patrick C
reviews.title: Well-maintained but aging property
reviews.text:
I came here for a conference. Even with a conference discount, this Starwood property was definitely a high-priced resort. That being said, service was fantastic. We took a cab into the property, and the bellhop immediately took our luggage and delivered it to the room.  Check-in was smooth.  Our room was slightly dated (worn out sofa, carpet, wall studs), but still elegant.  Complementary shoe shine was offered, and turn-down service was standard.  The bathroom had high-end furnishings. 

The pools were well-maintained, and had attentive pool service.  I used the complementary bike rental to tour the property, and rode downtown. It was very convenient.  The property also was within walking distance to Camelback mountain trail head, so hiking was available if you wanted to do more than lounging.  There is also a cactus garden, and standard resort mallshops.  

The Spa was also fantastic. I didn't use any services, only the facilities. There was a hot tub, sauna, shower, and a lounging area with complementary teas, coffees, and fruits.

We also dined at Il Terrazzo--overall, service was a good, but slow. The tiramisu dessert was underwhelming (tasty, but not spectacular).

I am a Starwood Preferred Plus member (ie: no status, only the SPG credit card).

reviews.author: incumeg
reviews.title: It was not worth the money
reviews.text: I was disappointed in this hotel as I had quite high expectations after reading the reviews and seeing the ranking. The price exceeded the quality. I would highly recommend to anyone The Boulders, a Waldorf Astoria Resort in place of this hotel. It is not super near by, but it is so worth the 20 minute drive. I paid less for the Boulders and had an exceptional experience.

reviews.author: acwong
reviews.title: Excellent resort to stay at and we would return.
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed here over a discounted summer staycation.  Since it was August and blistering hot there were not many people here but that was ok with us because it made it more private.  I would have given this resort 5 stars it it weren't for a few things that made our stay not as comfortable.  

Check-in was fast and simple and we were celebrating our anniversary and was upgraded to a nicer room.  Kudos to them for that customer service act.  We also had a nice dinner at J & G steakhouse making it our number 2 steakhouse in Phoenix, just being edged out by Mastro's City Hall.  Having turndown service was also a nice touch, but is mandatory for a 5 star resort.  The room we got was a king that had a nice bathroom with both tub and shower.  The room was spacious and had a desk and couch as well as a balcony where you can sit out and look over the grounds.  The resort itself is beautiful and well kept.  

The few little things that dropped them half a star are as follows.  The hot tub was broken and not addressed during our two day stay.  The water was only at 90 degrees and the jets did not work in it.  The hot tub itself is large and the only one on the resort.  I would have expected a resort of this size to have two of them, but this was plenty large enough.  The only problem was that it did not work and repeated attempts to report this to the front desk brought about no one to address the problem.  

There was also construction that took place outside our bedroom that was loud an obnoxious and could have been avoided.  I'm assuming that the resort is aware of the construction going on seemed to take place on one side of the resort.  There are two wings to the resort and a simple placement of guests on the otherside would have avoided this problem.  It sure made our anniversary staycation a little annoying and sleeping in virtually impossible.  Since it was summer, and the lack of visual guests around the property, I'm sure there were many rooms available on the other side of the resort that could have been used.  
They also missed turndown service on our second night, which was more of a missed service than actual inconvenience.  

The resort is very romantic and would make a great getaway.  Despite the small short-comings, we would still return here and give it another try.  The only big things were the hot tub and construction.  They have a nice sunday brunch and afternoon tea that we were not able to take advantage during this stay and we'll just have to try them next time.

reviews.author: hawaiiboundstt
reviews.title: Fun at the Phonecian!
reviews.text:
Visited here in Late May for a conference with my family. Be sure to request a room close to the pool if you plan on spending time there. It could be a long walk otherwise. Rooms need updating but have been well kept and although boring were fairly well done back in the day. romantic they are not. The pools are large and quite nice. The mother of pearl pool is very nice and the cabanas are fabulous with great service. If children were not allowed by this pool I am not sure we would return. although the kids loved the other pools as they had a grouping of boards they ran across for hours and a slide the "family" area is while large and clean is rather drab an unimaginative with poor towel and food service. so call ahead to ensure children will be welcome at the m of pearl pool if you have kids in tow and prefer a nice pool with good service.

Food was good and fairly priced but nothing memorable. 
The kids club was good and the boys enjoyed it.
Tennis lessons were loved by the kids and my wife.
Service all around was good and prompt, concierge was excellent and hooked us up with the best tour guide ever! David from my arizona tour guide. Wow! The best.

The food and convention spaced was excellent. A fabulous place to hold a large meeting.

reviews.author: Charlotte S
reviews.title: Can't keep away
reviews.text: I love this hotel! I have stayed here with my family for years and no doubt will be returning again next year, even the manager calls it our second home! From where we live its about an 11 hour flight but when we arrive its worth it. All of the staff remember us which is a lovely, the truly do go the extra mile.  The pools are stunning, the restaurants are beautiful and the view of camelback mountain is spectacular.  Can't wait to go back!

reviews.author: Lindsay B
reviews.title: Phantastic
reviews.text:
Luxury 5 star with everything you'd expect. Rooms were excellent and the pool was huge and crystal clear. Staff at the pool were attentive and brought iced water without prompting. The grounds were beautifully maintained and i liked the complimentary starbucks in the reception area in the morning. Lovely hotel with not a hair out of place.

Location very convenient for local attractions - zoo, botanical gardens, fashion square.

reviews.author: Hannah G
reviews.title: The Phoenician saved our holiday
reviews.text: We were actually booked into another nearby hotel (supposedly 5*) but when we arrived and saw the tiny pool with no free sunloungers at 10am in the morning we called the Phoenician and luckily they had rooms free, so we hopped back in the taxi and fled! 30 minutes later we were happily perched at the Oasis pool bar with plenty of space and room to actually swim in the pool, rather than just stand at the edge squashed in with other guests. We had previously stayed at The Phoenician in 2012 for a week so we knew we'd be happy there and it didn't disappoint. We had a spacious room on the 4th floor overlooking the pools - the room was spotless every day and the turndown service was always appreciated, although times were very variable. The property is large, you can take a spin round it on the complimentary bikes. With the many pools, well equipped gym, cactus garden, trails up the mountain and 27-holes of golf there's plenty to do on site but we also made a couple of trips to the shops and hired a car for the day to go up to Sedona which is about a 2 hour drive. We ate in J&G Steakhouse twice - great meals with really good service on both occasions. Breakfast in the restaurant is quite expensive, but you can pick up pastries / croissants in the ice cream parlour which was more reasonable. I've only ever been during the hot summer months when the hotel (and indeed the whole area) is quite quiet - I couldn't comment on what it's like at peak times but given what I've seen I imagine the staff are more than capable of providing consistently good service. I can't find fault with The Phoenician, and I suspect it won't be long before we return.

reviews.author: Mary W
reviews.title: We had the best service at this wonderful resort!
reviews.text:
My family stayed at the Phonecian for three nights. We stayed in grand suite rooms. They were very spacious with large bathrooms. We also had a balcony facing the pool.

All staff members were very friendly. It was my birthday weekend and when I returned to the room there was champagne iced down and a half dozen chocolate covered strawberries!! Denise Heamin even wrote me a personal birthday wish!  
We ate at the J&G steakhouse there at the resort. The view was spectacular and the food was very good. Again, I was treated to a delightful dessert with a candle to blow out. Patrick and his team gave us impeccable service.
We lounged by several different pools, ate at the gold club and I had a wonderful massage at their spa, Center for Well Being.

We would all highly recommend this resort.

reviews.author: travel-king13
reviews.title: Two Faces of The Phoenician
reviews.text: First impressions are always very important, and the Phoenician doesn't disappoint here.
