I'm not a "high maintenance" person at all, but the rooms and common facilities are run-down (frayed upholstery, carpet stains, ripped lamp shades, etc) and the service is very lacking. I'm usually a Starwood fan, but, hate to say it, this is really lacking.  Room service trays and glasses siting in the hallway for TWO days???

reviews.author: ScottN
reviews.title: Seamless luxury in downtown Scottsdale
reviews.text:
We chose The Phoenician over the other top competing 5-star resorts (The Boulders and the Four Seasons) based on its convenient location (the others are north of Scottsdale on the border of Carefree).  If you want the natural ambience of the Sonoran desert and mountains and a less urbane resort atmosphere, then the others are probably a better choice, but for convenience and saving 30 minutes to downtown Scottsdale or Phoenix (each way!) the Phoenician is unbeatable.

Gratis self parking is convenient, and underground (important on hot days) located in the basement of the hotel building.  Lobby check-in was prompt and efficient.  No bell captain was available at check-in, but the head of housekeeping insisted on taking our luggage to the room and would not accept a tip.  During our stay, there were other special items we asked for, and they were promptly and unobtrusively provided.  We were offered the opportunity to waive daily housekeeping service "for reduced environmental impact" which we politely refused.

The lobby still reflects the 1980's/90's Charles Keating era of over-the-top decadence with giant chandeliers and marble floors; I'm not particularly a fan of this, but it did not distract from an excellent stay.  The $25 million artwork scattered around the grounds, primarily from the Native American sculptor Allan Houser is another story: that is absolutely stunning and spectacular.  Make sure to pay homage to the life-size bronze statue of the Chief offering the Peace Pipe near the front of the spa; it is the same piece that also fronts the United Nations building in New York City.

The hotel is laid out in two separate curved terraced buildings separated by a driveway. Our first room was in the upper terrace with a view of the city (and rooftop of the first building) that we were not happy with, but they moved us the following day to the lower terrace with a view of the gardens and golf course and we were much happier with that.  This was also more convenient each day as the parking lot is underneath the first building and uses the same elevator.

Rooms are laid out with calming beiges and botanical prints; are spacious and were absolutely and impeccably spotless.  Unlike many other 5-star resorts nowadays, the Phoenician still provides full nightly turn-down service automatically, tidying up the room and providing bottled water and chocolates.

I was charged $29/day "resort fee", and did not use any of it, except the internet service. I was not given an option to waive it, but did not ask if I could either.

The highlight for us was eating outdoors on the terrace of their main restaurant Il Terrazzo.  Each day, it included a simple but good quality breakfast buffet, and a huge staff that obviously enjoys their jobs and keeping the clientele happy.  Please note the aggressive wild birds that are on a constant look-out for an ignored plate of food or pitcher of cream, and KEEP DISHES COVERED if you visit the buffet...even if others are sitting at your table.

Definitely a place for stresses and worries to seem far away.  I will certainly be staying here again.

reviews.author: 931ek
reviews.title: Will be back again!
reviews.text: This is a beautiful resort with every amenity that you may need. The service was exceptional, room clean and food was amazing. The check-in was seamless and there are shops to browse on the way up to your room. I felt very comfortable in my large room with a great balcony to rest on. I ate at two restaurants on site, both were excellent and very reasonably priced. I plan to go back!

reviews.author: Townhaven
reviews.title: Lovely hotel
reviews.text: This hotel is really a 5 star property.  The regular rooms are huge,  600 square feet with a balcony.  The fitness classes are excellent, I took a Yoga class, and really enjoyed it.  The pools are nice and the beds really comfortable.  If you want some down time in luxury, this is it!

reviews.author: Cissy J W
reviews.title: The BEST Of Front Desk!
reviews.text:
Last weekend was undoubtedly one of the best vacations I've ever experienced at a resort over the course of my lifetime!
     When we arrived at the Phoenician, we were happily invited to the beautiful 200 plus acre property by a helpful greeter. By the time we parked and went up the elevator we were extremely anxious!
     Although the trip was divine and the food was overwhelmingly delicious, the element that stood out the most was a resourceful and courteous front desk associate named Jessica.
    Right away she pulled up our reservation, upgraded our room for the weekend, recommended several restaurants at the resort, as well as give us a complimentary drink offer for the Thirsty Camel lobby bar.
     She was extremely beneficial and appreciated during our first stay at the Phoenician! We definitely look forward to returning to the Phoenician due to her wonderful service. 
     Overall the two days and two nights we experienced at Scottsdale's Phoenician was above and beyond our own expectations. Everything was serviced to us as if we were presidential guests, the tennis session, bike rentals, pool and dining! Can't wait for our second stay and anticipate checking in with Jessica again.

reviews.author: John R
reviews.title: My favorite business conference hotel, period.
reviews.text: 2nd time we held large client event - rave reviews from clients and colleagues. Great service, great food choices, accommodating to last minute changes. Number of folks extended to enjoy some vacation time. First class with relaxed but hospitable staff who like their jobs and employer - it shows!

reviews.author: Beverly T
reviews.title: Pure Luxury
reviews.text: While on business in Scottsdale, I stayed over at the Phoenician hotel for the weekend. I highly recommend this hotel. The hotel is first class. The grounds are lush and the pools are just delightful.  Beds are really cozy and comfortable. Parking is easy, as you can self park and wireless is free and no extra charge!!  The Relish Burger cafe overlooking the golf course was fun and yummy!

reviews.author: OneCageyTraveler
reviews.title: Beautiful Property in Scottsdale
reviews.text: I recently stayed here for two nights while attending a business conference.  Although I did not have time to check out all of the facilities this property offers, I have to say the areas I did get to are beautiful and well maintained.  Expect to do plenty of walking if you stay here as the property is very spread out.  My room in the north wing seemed a little out of the way at first, but I found shortcuts to get from there to the main building and ballroom area where our conference activities were taking place.  Although huge, comfortable and clean with a private balcony, my room did not have a view, as the balcony was surrounded by tall, thick shrubs.  Great for privacy, but disappointing as I'd have loved to view the area and Camelback Mt.  My favorite spot was the cactus garden, to which I had easy access from the north wing.  All in all a nice property, but expensive - even with a convention rate discount.  Oh, and I have to agree with a previous reviewer - the coffee served at breakfast could have been much better!

reviews.author: Jason M
reviews.title: I tried really hard to like it
reviews.text: My wife had a conference here so I came along and we stayed a few extra days.  The positives include the burger joint Relish, the grounds were immaculate and beautiful, and although i didn't play golf, the course also looked incredible.  The pools were really nice too.  I wanted to really like this plus but there were too many negatives.  We were "upgraded" to a casita, which was essentially a regular room in a group of small buildings surrounding the lower pool.  We were so far away from the main building that we drove there for dinner one night instead of walking.  Worst of all about our room was the fact that it looked like it has never been updated.  The decor is straight out of 1988, with wallpaper pealing off the walls and chipped paint on the baseboards.  We had dinner one night at J&G Steakhouse on the property.  Dinner was good but overpriced, and you can get a better steak at Mastros a mile or so up the road.  Nice place to stay if your company is paying for it, but we've had better accommodations for less money at other places in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: Lisa K
reviews.title: Expensive resort, cheap experience...
reviews.text: Not a good place for adults to relax. Why even have an adults only pool if you're not going to enforce it?? There are multiple pools, ONE of which is dedicated to "adult relaxation." Except for the fact that there were children in it every day. Pool staff always served them, and never enforced the rule. Not my job to tell pool staff to do the right thing. Nowhere to relax, and cheapened my experience greatly. We won't come back.

reviews.author: wannabeprincess49
reviews.title: service wasn't as expected
reviews.text: was so excited to be staying here. love this property as a whole. i will definitely stay again but . . . saw a HUGE cockroach at the pool. kind of thought maybe we'd get a comp on something as this was unbelievably gross and unacceptable. pool service overall was lacking; not attentive at all and we spent the day there eating and drinking.  we had to track down our waiter. went to the little coffee shop/ice cream shop in the hotel for coffee and a little bite to eat the next morning and we waited in line for 10 minutes. i finally had to ask if we could be helped as no one was paying attention to us. room was wonderful, of course. we were upgraded because we were celebrating a 50th birthday for a friend. that was a nice surprise!

reviews.author: TreeHuggerTravels
reviews.title: Front Desk Fabulous Face of Phoenician
reviews.text: Endless thanks the front desk team who really started our trip off to a superb level. Amanda truly has what it takes to offer service excellence. Her knowledge of the property, humble confidence, professional presence and charming style made me want to see what was next. It is great when a classy hotel like Phoenician can be matched by its staff- after all- it is the people who make the brand. Suite upgrade was sweeeeeettttttt- decor is stunning as with the views. Take some time to walk the cactus garden- hidden gem. Thank you again Amanda- keep making people smile.

reviews.author: Rod_CFP
reviews.title: It's been around for years but you'd never know it.
reviews.text: This resort has been around for years but everything is in like new condition. Lots of marble and quality rooms and furnishings.  It makes a great hotel for business conference because of several large ballrooms.  There is plenty of attentive staff who are willing to go out of their way to serve.  Our conference elected to have all our breakfasts and one lunch on the lawn which was fine except for the birds. They are hovering ready to take any food that is dropped and if there is no one there they will swoop down on the serving tables.  I'd have preferred eating inside.

reviews.author: Jethrosdad
reviews.title: Love it, even the flaws.
reviews.text:
Fabulous setting just outside Phoenix,  with great staff - most of the time!

Good rooms, if a little lacking in facilities. The food at J&G restaurant was good but breakfast is not up to scratch, especially the buffet - cold bacon, solid scrambled eggs, and c'mon guys, get some decent coffee for breakfast.

reviews.author: Sandinmyhair
reviews.title: Amazing service and tranquil setting
reviews.text:
The Phoenician definitely deserves its 5 stars. The service is amazing, everyone is very friendly and eager to provide whatever you need. The rooms and pool are beautiful and overall great for singles, couples, or families. 

I stayed in a deluxe room facing the mountains and it was very tranquil. I would definitely return.

reviews.author: Rubesgirl
reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.text: We stayed here for just one night at the end of our week long Grand Canyon/Zion trip.  We all wished we could've stayed there longer. Everything was perfect. Our suite (in fairness, we were unexpectedly upgraded) was amazing, the pools were fabulous (we have 3 kids, ages 9, 13, and 15 who really enjoyed them), and the two meals we enjoyed there were incredible.  The staff was exactly what you'd expect from a resort of this caliber, and their attention definitely added to our experience.  We now talk about heading back to Scottsdale someday just to visit this hotel again.

reviews.author: ShelbyB15
reviews.title: Excellent staff, accommodations, and experience!
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at the Phoenician while working a business conference on the property. I cannot say enough great things about this place! My room was spectacular. The bathrooms are huge and the beds are by far the most comfortable I have ever slept in aside from those in my own home. On my down time I enjoyed sitting on my private patio or dining on the fabulous meals provided by room service (special thanks to Caleb and Logan for the prompt and friendly service). 
If you're looking for a place to host a business meeting, conference, etc, this is the place to do it! The entire staff was so accommodating and willing to help whenever they could. The banquet service staff treated me like a queen while I was working. One woman in particular, Rosa, went above and beyond to help us. On the first morning she went and got coffee for some of the staff (not just any cup of coffee - very specific latte orders). The next morning so arrived a little after 7am with the same coffee orders as the day before! Not only did she remember our orders and go get them for us, but she also did this while working another area of the building. Rosa, Leonardo, and many others made this experience great for us. I really cannot thank them enough for their hospitality.
Bottom line: stay at the Phoenician! Whether for business or pleasure, I highly recommend it!

reviews.author: breigle01
reviews.title: Incredible place and staff!
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed at the phoencian in May for a 4 day getaway.  It was absolutely incredible.  From the moment we checked in to the time we left the staff was some of the best we've seen.  Our room was in the Casitas (which I highly recommend) and our view was of the lagoon and waterfall...it was great.  The pools were fantastic and we enjoyed 3 days of pretty empty times.  Unfortunately it got pretty busy on Saturday, but every other day it  was wide open.  We had tremendous food at the il terraso Cafe overlooking the pools.  Ask for Paul the best server we've ever had and he will take care of you.  If you are platinum on starwood get the breakfast for your amenity as Paul hooked us up with a great breakfast that wasn't a buffet every day.  Really outstanding food, service and place.  Would highly recommend during the week to experience and just relax.

reviews.author: lyung
reviews.title: Paradise in Scottsdale
reviews.text: I have been staying at this hotel for the last four years every time I visited.  The services are exceptional, the rooms with great views (make sure to ask for a city and pool side view), and the restaurants are excellent and love the SPA treatments.  The golf course is great, too (but i didn't get a chance to play).  A great place for family with small children.  Location of this hotel is convenient to the airport, shops and ASU.  This is one of my favorite hotels.

reviews.author: Sara S
reviews.title: Beautifully wonderful!
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Phoenician for a business conference. The hotel grounds were spectacular. With the hotel being at the base of Camelback Mountain, all of the views were amazing! Our rooms were spacious and very clean. The bathroom was almost as big as the sleeping area in our room. All of the staff we encountered were very accommodating and provided us with the best service. Everything we ate at the resort was delicious, from the catered food at the conference, to the burgers at Relish (a burger joint on the property).
Though our stay was too short, and we were inside the hotel a lot of the time, we had an absolutely enjoyable stay at the Phoenician. We will definitely be returning for a relaxing vacation.

reviews.author: luvalu
reviews.title: A room with a view was expected
reviews.text: You would rightfully expect the best out of such a prestigious and expensive hotel.  The kind of place where you would not expect rooms overlooking another building separated by a roof top.  We had a very small balcony with no sunshine at all.  We would have appreciated to be able to enjoy some privacy on our balcony since the pools were over crowded with children, hard to find lounge chairs in April (probably a remainder of spring break).  We did not expect families, once again considering that this is a pricey hotel.   The spa services were again overpriced for the quality of treatments, the restaurants on site were also average. We travel a lot and we have to admit that we were disappointed.  According to our experience, this hotel is over rated.

reviews.author: Joseph S
reviews.title: Great experience during recent conference
reviews.text: Recently stayed at the Phoenician for a business conference and had a tremendous experience.  Beautifully crafted hotel, rich, opulent and luxurious.  Amenities are fantastic:  golf, cactus garden, tennis, fitness center, spa, 9 pools, art tour, restaurants, live lounge music and shops.  It is conveniently located not too far a drive from Phoenix main airport.  Valet of $29/night definitiely high, but can opt for self-parking your vehicle.  Hotel has a desert, beige, neutral tone throughout that fits the locale very well.  They have a $25 million dollar art collection on premise, including 7 million year old fossils, and fantanstic Native American statues throughout the grounds.  Room was great, with a generous patio with lounger, table and chairs, nice big TV, desk, sofa, great in-room bar and snacks.  Bathroom was superb, with rainshower shower, enclosed toilet area, soaking tub, huge mirror and dual sinks - marble everywhere.  Had one of the best burgers of my life at Il Terazzo restaurant on premise - Kobe beef, boston lettuce, avocado and aioli on a butter toasted bun - a must for lunch if you go.  Front desk and car service were a little robotic or workmanlike, but friendly.  Requests for ice were handled immediately.  Tiered pool area during the day and outdoor fireplace at night were spectacular.  Being a luxury property, this does not come cheap, but if willing or able to pay, it is a tremendous property.

reviews.author: Travel4c
reviews.title: Perfect getaway
reviews.text: We spent five days at The Phoenician, three for a meeting and extended two more.  We found the hotel very accommodating, service was excellent.  Pool is stellar with plenty of space for privacy. Pool attendants were quick to give you water and drinks.   Had two treatments at spa very relaxing and professiona staff.   We ate at steak place, best steak ever with spectacular views of the mountains.  We golfed two rounds one an dessert  and canyon  nice course.  We  rented golf clubs they were perfect,  grab a burger at club house after a round, yum.   We will definitely be back five days wasn't enough

reviews.author: LovemyKing
reviews.title: Relaxing
reviews.text: Stayed here for my husband's business conference. Very nice big resort. Close to Fashion Square. Everything we had to eat on property was delicious. At base of Camelback mountain. Beautiful. Amazing views if the valley.

reviews.author: gume1
reviews.title: Perfect Stay
reviews.text:
Wir, Ehepaar 43 J,  besuchten das Phoenician für 3 Nächte als entspannenden Abschluss einer Rundreise.
Lage: Optimal, in 5 Min mit dem Auto zur Mall z.B. zum Essen, trotzdem ruhig und in einer tollen Landschaft
Service: Alle freundlich und enorm hilfsbereit, auch am Pool wurde ständig kostenlos Eiswasser gereicht, es gab sehr gute Restaurantempfehlungen auch für ausserhalb des Resorts
Zimmer: Gross ( für europäische Verhältnisse ), sehr sauber, ruhig und edel mit Balkon
Essen: Haben nur morgens den kostenlosen Starbucks-Caffee genossen und  abends Cocktails am Pool und auf der Terrasse, preislich absolut OK ( Mojito 9€ ) für so eine schöne Umgebung. Gegessen haben wir immer in der Stadt
Parken: In der Tat kostenlos - Tip ist aber eigentlich selbstverstandlich
Sport: Modernes und top-sauberes Fitness-Center
Fazit: Wir überlegen, das nächste Mal statt der Rundreise lieber 2 Wochen hier zu verbringen :-) Es war das beste Hotel auf unserer Reise

reviews.author: djh5723
reviews.title: An excellent stay
reviews.text: Visited the Phoneician for a conference. What a great place. Rooms are very large, pools are great and the staff is extremely helpful and friendly. This was a great place. We will come back for a family visit.

reviews.author: tripswitht
reviews.title: amazing
reviews.text: Upon arrival to the day we checked out the staff in every area of this resort was outstanding.  Restaurants, pools, spa, front desk and housekeeping was great, we enjoyed our stay and didn't want to leave.  If you can splurge then this is the hotel to splurge on, you will not regret it.

reviews.author: Michael G
reviews.title: Great Experience
reviews.text:
My wife and I spend our wedding anniversary at The Phoenician, Scottsdale and had a wonderful time.  Our room was spacious with a lovely balcony overlooking the resort grounds.  We enjoyed a beautiful sunset with a glass of wine on our balcony our first evening there.

The only issue we had was our room availability upon our arrival and it took the staff over two hours to get us into our room which actually pushed us in getting ready for our anniversary dinner at the hotel restaurant, J&G Steakhouse.  Otherwise, it was a great experience and we would definitely stay at the Phoenician on our next visit to Scottsdale.

reviews.author: Renee L
reviews.title: Pure luxury  and comfort!
reviews.text: This was by far the best vacation I've had in a very long time. The room was absolutely luxurious. The bathroom was bigger than most hotel rooms. Wonderful large soaking tub and fluffy robes, The pool area was huge with refreshing water and waterfalls. Loved playing a little volleyball with friends and relaxing with drinks by the pool.

reviews.author: pbolland
reviews.title: Just short of Excellent
reviews.text: An elegant resort that just misses the mark. Staff was attentive, but not perfect. For example, at a recent convention, the bar was understaffed on the first night. Management or the bar staff should have adjusted by the second night, but they didn't. The pool staff were very helpful, but not so easy to find. That said the rooms were well maintained and the staff pleasant.

reviews.author: Travelforfun0818
reviews.title: Loved the Phoenician
reviews.text: Not quite sure what to expect, but very pleasantly surprised! My girlfriend and I spent 5 nights here, and we still didn't get to use all the amenities .  Great pools, although, even though we left our towels and clothes on our chaises, they were removed and our chaises taken. We had breakfast in their dining room, service was poor, never introduced to our server, eggs not cooked, toast burnt .. Definitely could have been better.  Our rooms weren't made up till after 4pm .. But all in all, an excellent place to stay, just room for improvement . Definitely recommend.

reviews.author: SappiNY
reviews.title: Nice place, lots of pool areas, nice grounds, restaurants OK, very isolated location
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed at this resort for a conference last month, we spent 4 nights here, it was our first time in Scottsdale.  Giving the Phoenician a 4 is pushing it, I was debating between a 3 or 4.  Although this is a 5* diamond rated place..... I did not get that vibe.  However, it was a very nice property with nice staff.  I had a few good experiences which I highlighted below.  

1)  Pools-  I think the staff in yellow did a great job replenishing our waters, clearing out towels, providing towels when needed.  What I did not like was that there was no great adult area.  I believe one pool was the Casbah pool which was only for above 18.  However, that pool was in between the two other large pools, not an ideal place for an adult only area as it gets loud with traffic.  Also, it felt a little congested in terms of the layout/tree coverage.
2)  Oasis pool bar/grill-  Blair and Gabe were great the two times I dined poolside, the Mediterranean wrap was excellent.  One thing I noticed not just at this restaurant, but all restuarants in Scottsdale is that the establishments are very understaffed.  I'm not sure why that is.  Although we had to had to wait quite a while before we placed our order, got our bill, etc. the waitstaff was superb and pleasant.
3)  Il Terazzo-  dined here twice for breakfast.  The first day I was NOT impressed with the hostess and our waitress.  I thought they were cold and a bit snooty.  The menu was very overpriced, typical for a resort I guess.  The  yogurt and granola parfait was excellent.  Jocelin our host the next day, and Jose our waiter, were both excellent and reflective of what the restaurant should be for a fine dining place.  Also the first day we dined on the patio which was great, however, there were crows EVERYWHERE.  They would fly in constantly and feast on the plates that were not yet taken away.  The staff should do a more speedy job of clearing out tables after guests leave to help prevent this.  It was a bit of an annoyance and also not sanitary to have birds all over chairs/tables
4)  Thirsty Camel-  loved the piano and live singing, I think her name was Tanya.  Added a nice feel to the evening if you want a relaxing evening outdoors, watching the sunset.  The food was not impressive, did not like the Tiramisu, it was 80% cream which made me nauseus
5)  Cactus Garden-  Beautiful and different!  I was so happy we were able to go on the cactus tour with Naoiti, who was a great guide.
6)  Camelback hike with Grayson-  great experience!  he was a great guide, he was a little too fast for my husband and I to keep up with comfortably though.  Can be done without the guide, hike costs $20 per person w/o resort fee.  However, I liked having the guide as he explained the sights and nature during our trek.
7)  Meditation course with Cindy-  atrium is beautiful and relaxting in the center for wellbeing.  The meditation course was a very interesting experience, happy I was able to try it.  Phillip in the Center was very helpful in making the appointment.
8)  Rooms/hotel-  spacious, clean, housekeeping did a great job, nice spacious bathroom, bit outdated colors.  The carpets are definitely in need of replacement, the large floral prints look very 80s-ish.  The lobby is spacious with ample seating
9) Front desk was very helpful and friendly throughout our stay, check-in and check-out

Overall I'm glad I tried this place, haven't stayed in a resort like this before.  One downside is it is a drive from Scottsdale downtown, old town, the mall, etc.  The cab ride is around $8-9 so not bad, we did that twice  because we were getting tired of the limited options for dining at the hotel as many of the restaurants and room service have similiar menu items.  There were a lot of families there, it wasn't overcrowded with kids, but definitely noisey at times.  Would have liked more areas for adults only.

reviews.author: tlefkovi
reviews.title: Heavenly Bliss
reviews.text:
We previously visited The Phoenician about a year ago and fell in love with entire resort. It has everything we look for in a resort. The pool areas are plentiful and as intimate or open as you like. The layout of the resort is welcoming and easy to get around. We tried most of the F&B outlets but truly enjoyed one called Relish. It had great burgers and assortment of other comfort foods. 

The only down side in service we experienced was during breakfast in their main restaurant. On two occasions we got the impression the servers were going through the motions. Orders were mixed up and there wasn't a sense of true hospitality. Beyond this, I can;t say enough good things about the employees we encountered.

It is truly a slice of heaven and we will be back.

reviews.author: farriesgc
reviews.title: Really good food
reviews.text:
We were here for a conference April 23-27.  I found the room comfortable and clean with fantastic sun exposure!  I had no need to leave my room to sun myself; we were in room 6158.  Relish, one of the restaurants on site had the best chicken caprese salad (caprese burger ordered bun-less) I have ever eaten!  The pro shop at the golf course had many unique items and was well priced, as it goes.  

As far as looking after us as a conference of around 300 or so, the staff was attentive and the banquet facilities were lovely.  

Sam at the pool bar was fantastic.

I hope to return to The Phoenician soon to enjoy without the obligation of a conference and recommend it to anyone looking for a relaxing and stress free vacay!

reviews.author: Susanna
reviews.title: Coming Back!
reviews.text: WOW!  This property has all the amenities you would expect from a 5 star resort. What was the most impressive (and it was all top quality) was the staff service. Every staff member made us feel welcome - greetings and smiles all the way 'round.  Ate at Il Terrazzo when we arrived and would recommend in terms of menu choices, quality of food and service. While on the property it is worth doing a tour of the Cactus Garden (you can walk through on your own and there is also a guided tour). It is as fine as any public botanical garden! A wander to look at the art collection is also worth the while. Some exquisite Native American pieces.

reviews.author: JAJDallas
reviews.title: A wonderful relaxing resort
reviews.text: Just spent 4 days at the Phoenician Resort.  Wonderful accommodations with excellent service.  A short walk and you're ready to hike up Camelback Mountain.  With 9 pools to choose from and an great fitness center.  I plan on returning.

reviews.author: John D
reviews.title: Lovely view and sounds of the loading dock--what a joke.
reviews.text: I'm here for a conference, known for holding meetings at luxury resorts.  They put me in a mountain view King that does have a balcony overlooking the mountain and partial view of the golf course and distant mountains.  But just below the balcony is the loading dock with diesel engines running and clanking metal from unloading trucks.  Some gold status Starwood Gold priority...

reviews.author: jesric
reviews.title: Excellent Customer Service, Beautiful Resort
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at this resort April 10-13. We did stay with a group for an event and it was absolutely wonderful. The service was amazing, every single staff member said hello and would ask if you needed anything. The views were beautiful, the food was excellent and they had many gluten free options. The room was spacious, the bed was very comfortable and the decor was beautiful. We did not get a chance to use the pools, but heard they were very nice, there is even a waterslide for the kids. The golf course and grounds were beautiful and we did get to hike up Camelback Mountain twice which was less than a mile walk from the resort. I would go back to this again and would recommend it to anyone looking for a nice vacation in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: promo_jake
reviews.title: wow, what a place!
reviews.text: I really like this luxury resort. It was wonderful to sit back and be pampered. Great food and golf. The pools are nice as is the spa. The children have fun and so do the adults. I cannot wait to go back!

reviews.author: sherrynongratis
reviews.title: Wonderful Stay with Kids @ The Phoenician
reviews.text:
We stayed at The Phoenician 4/17 for four nights with our two children, ages 12 & 10.  With a very early flight from the Midwest, we arrived at the hotel @ 8:00 a.m.  We were not expecting a room to be ready, but to our surprise, we were upgraded to a Casita room that was available at no extra charge.  There is free parking right outside of your casita which saved us the $29 valet charge per day.

Our casita was an end unit in the N Building and very convenient to the lobby & pool.  It was very cozy with plenty of room for the 4 of us.  Sliding glass door overlooking the lake and the kids could go out and play on the lawn.  Very large marble bathroom with large bathtub & separate room for toilet & a bidet.  Two sinks on opposite sides were a plus for my husband & I.  Large stone shower with seating area, rainfall shower head  & glass door.  The largest bathroom at any resort I've ever stayed.  The mattress & bedding was incredibly comfortable.  We all slept like rocks for 4 nights!

On the way to our casita, we walked over several footbridges over the lake at the resort & came upon the Kids Camp director feeding the koi & ducks with several other children.  She was kind enough to invite my children to feed them as well (even they they weren't enrolled in the camp)and gave them handfuls of fish food.  There were dozens of koi that literally swim right up to you for food, as well as a mother duck and her brood of babies.  My kids enjoyed that very much!  We also saw a turtle & there are tons of little bunnies roaming around the property.  If you have children, make sure to stop by the Kids Camp before 4 p.m. and they will get a free plush bunny as a souvenier.  Very cool.. as we've never stayed at a resort that ever gave such nice free gifts to the kids. 

The grounds are very expansive.  It took us about a day to get acclimated.  There are beautiful stone walkways winding around the resort with lush landscaping & flowers everywhere.  A private gazebo and patio in the shade with tables & chairs to read a book.  Waterfalls, flowering trees, cactus & a beautiful backdrop of Camelback Mt.  The resort is beautiful at night, too, with the resort lights glowing and the firepits and swimming pools lit up.

THE POOL:  There are 3 levels of pools.  The first pool is at ground level and overlooks both the pool & lake.  Saw mostly adults at this pool & we never stayed at this one.  Go up the stairs and you come to the Adults Only pool & bar.  Again, didn't stay at this one, but looked like fun.  Go up another level and you will come to the largest pool which is divided into three separate pools by walkways.  The one in the center is the largest & has a basketball net, as well as a volleyball net.  This is where we spent most of our time.  There is also a waterslide for the kids.  Plenty of padded chaise lounges with umbrellas.  Extra long towels provided so cover the entire chaise.  Excellent food & beverage service out by the pool.  They also bring you pitchers of ice water & refill as soon as you're low.  All the food we had was excellent, especially the homed guacamole & salsa.  If you want several chairs out by ANY of these pools, I suggest you get out there no later than 9:00 a.m to get your chairs.  I went out @ 10:00 a.m. the first morning & had a hard time finding 4 seats together.  Most of the chairs were taken by families or had the good ol' towel & personal item on them to be "saved".  The pool staff really needs to keep an eye on this sort of "chair saving" practice because it is very annoying to the other guests who are actually ready to sit out by the pool & cannot find a chair.  I had two chairs next to me "saved" and no one showed up for 4 hours.  Some people even took up a whole chair just to lay there bags & clothing on.

The pools are heated so the water is not freezing.  Large hot tub was very nice.  Ducks occasionally fly in & out of the pool.  Great view of Camelback Mt. from the pool.  Great gold course although my husband did not play during our stay.

Il Terrazzo was pricey and the food was good.  Nothing to write home about as far as Italian food, but it was good.  We had breakfast off property most days since The Phoenician did not have a breakfast buffet except on Sundays during our stay.  We drove over to Talking Stick Resort and enjoyed the breakfast buffet for $10.95 per adult.  Very good & very good value.  We also enjoyed breakfast at the 5 & Diner and Butterfield's (both off-site).  There is an ice-cream parlor/coffee shop on-site which was a nice treat.

The only THREE negatives we encountered were the following:

1.  There was a private function in one of the restaurants one evening during our stay.  We had to walk by the front entrance to the function to get to our restaurant we were eating at that evening.  There was a man "guarding" the entrance to the private function like he was the Gestapo and practically charged my kids saying "No, no" at them like they were trying to get in.  He told us we could not walk through since there was a private function, so we had to walk back to the elevators, go to the 2nd floor, go around & catch the escalator & go back down to the first floor and walk to the restaurant.  I did not like the feeling like we were outsiders when we were paying good money to stay at this resort.  If a guest is holding a private function, please consider having it in a private function room, not one of the main restaurants where paying guests have to be guarded off & re-routed to get to their own dining location. 

2.  My husband ate out on the lobby patio one evening with our kids and ordered them a side of fruit from the kids menu ($5 each).  When the bill came, I saw that the waitrees charged us a total of $26 for both fruit plates.  When I brought this to her attention, she had somewhat of an attitude and explained that they ordered the adult fruit plates @ $13.00 a piece.  Why would we do that?!  I reiterated that we asked for the children's fruit plate & she took the bill and checked it with her manager.  When she returned (again with a noticeable attitude & no apology) she explained that her manager took off one of the fruit plates off the bill.  So I was still overcharged, but just paid the bill and left.

3.  We stopped by the front desk & asked the gentleman if we could get 4 foam pillows.  He asked for our name & room number and let us know they would be delivered shortly.  After waiting for nearly an hour and it was getting late, I called the front desk and they said they had no request written up for the pillows??  She apologized and pillows were brought to our room shortly thereafter.

Those were our only problems.  Other than that, we loved this resort, had a great mini-vacation & would highly recommend staying here!

reviews.author: TravelVal
reviews.title: Nice Place for a Staycation
reviews.text:
We won our 2-night stay at The Phoenician at a charity auction, which included dinner and brunch at the resort's Il Terrazzo restaurant, and even though we live in Phoenix it seemed worlds away from home. We requested a pool view at check-in and the only room available had two beds.  Not a problem, we thought, until we saw that they are full-size and not queen. Oh well, our romantic weekend was just that much, um, closer. The room was large and the balcony relaxing. Nothing super special but well appointed and comfortable. They hadn't given us a key to the mini-bar so we had to call for one, then we couldn't find an ice machine so we had to call for ice. Both were delivered promptly and with a smile. Later we had great cocktails (try the $20 Manhattan - it's worth it) and smiley service at the Thirsty Camel, outside at sunset - very romantic. The live music in the lobby was awesome and we felt like we were truly on vacation. We had no problem finding a spot at the pool on Saturday, at about 10:30am.  We even snagged an umbrella but there were other people who had problems finding loungers and umbrellas later, when it started getting warmer. One couple, next to us, ordered lunch from the gluten-free menu and told us all about the resort's separate "allergy-free" kitchen. I had no idea that the restaurants could accommodate just about any food request or allergy. Nice touch.  In fact, they said it is why they prefer the Phoenician to other luxury resorts in the area. 

All in all it was just a nice, relaxing atmosphere. Everyone was super nice and I never detected an attitude among the staff, no matter where we were on the property, or what we asked for. Refreshing. They also didn't nickel and dime us to death like some other resorts. We may have felt this way because we self-parked and since we are Starwood Gold members they waived the resort fees and gave us a free drink.  

At checkout we told the front desk clerk that they needed to clean the bathroom door in our room - it was black with grimy fingerprints when we checked in). She was very apologetic and seemed genuinely interested in making sure it was noted.  That's all we ask for, what we expect and what we found at The Phoenician - an effort at sincere customer service.

reviews.author: JBCR_Travel
reviews.title: Perfect Combination of Activities and Relaxation
reviews.text: The physical infrastructure of the resort was what you would expect from such a highly rated facilitated.  The service set it apart for a North American hotel - every Phoenician employee I interacted with was professional, courteous, and trying to go above and beyond.  I was fortunate with the weather (70s and 40s) so outdoor activities (great trail within a mile walk from the hotel) were possible.   The fitness center, spa and pools were great.  Specifically regarding the fitness center - clean, good choice of equipment, etc.  It is a tad small for a resort this large.  I recommend, weather permitting, to do your cardio outside of the gym and use the gym strictly for resistance training.  Final comment - food and drink prices are Mandarin, Ritz, Four Seasons like.  I expected higher than average, but not that high.

reviews.author: John M
reviews.title: Wonderful Spring Break!
reviews.text:
My wife and I spent 4 wonderful days at the Phoenician for our Spring Break.  The staff was all so friendly and helpful, the hotel, pool and restaurants were all terrific.  When we checked in, we were were told we had been upgraded to a nicer room with a view of the mountains.  We loved the coffee being available early as we usually rise by 5:30 or 6:00.  

The proximity to restaurants and shopping was a bonus.  

All in all, it was wonderful.

reviews.author: ChappaquaUSA
reviews.title: Fantastic!
reviews.text: We just spent 5 nuts at The Phoenician and had a wonderful stay!  The pools were wonderful and our  suite was well appointed, extremely spacious, and very comfortable.  Service was also great and our concierge was extremely helpful with everything from hiking tips and trail maps to Sedona day trip tips to dining recommendations.  Wonderful trip and we'd highly recommend The Phoenician!

reviews.author: Jiggy
reviews.title: Attention to Detail
reviews.text:
A wonderful place to stay with friends especially if someone in your group has food allergies. This property boasts a dedicated allergen-free kitchen where dishes from all food service outlets can be made and then served. The options for gluten-free are plentiful and pretty much limitless. If it's not on the menu, just ask. 

The servers throughout the food outlets are knwoledgeable and attentive. Sometimes to a fault, they tend to enjoy your company a little too much and don't want to bring you the check to leave, but alas, there could be worse things. 

The rooms are spacious and feature a his & hers closet as well as double sinks in the bathroom. If at anytime your remote control stops functioning, simply drop it on the floor and it will resume operations (not sure why this method is so effective). The beds are also extremely comfortable. However, there are few poweroutlets by the nightstands making it rather challenging to charge anything than an iPhone for which the alarm clock has an adapter for. 

They claim to have 9 pools, but I'd say it was closer to 7 as 3 of them are actually just one pool with some land bridges. Just saying. The hot tub tends to be really hot during the day, but I'm sure its more than enjoyable at night. I was slightly disappointed with the lack of swim-up bar, but the lounge chairs service more than made up for it. 

Also if you plan on outdoor dining off of the lobby at the firepits, claim your spot early as they fill up and folks are reluctant to leave. Moreover, the hotel does NOT provide s'more kits, so bring your own. It's not condoned, but allowed. 

There are also 27 holes of golf as well as putting green and a driving range. The driving range prices are extremely affordable considering everything else on property. Sadly, I did not make it to the gym, but the cactus walk was a nice touch. 

Finally, don't get roped into the $29/day valet parking when the self-parking option is free and easily accessible from the elevators in the lobby.

reviews.author: withvalidity
reviews.title: Almost more staff than guests
reviews.text: I was here for a business gathering. It is a place I would normally not stay at because of the costs but I must say you get what you pay for. The staff, food and facility were all excellent. One nights buffet dinner that included filet, shrimp, crab, etc. was exceptional.

reviews.author: El-orence
reviews.title: Comfortable room, great pool area, relaxing spa area, and excellent service
reviews.text: Stayed 3 nights for a corporate retreat and enjoyed every minute. Bed was probably the best of any hotel I've slept in and the service was excellent. The sauna, and steam room in the spa area were completely empty and allowed for uninterrupted relaxation. Food was prepared with great skill for each meal of the day.  Fire pit area was perfect for late night drinks

reviews.author: JakeandJosiesMom
reviews.title: Great visit!
reviews.text: Great luxury hotel with beautiful grounds, pools and restaurants. Visit the cactus garden and make sure you try the pool slide too! Visited during a company outing, all food provided was good. The final night our two kids joined us and they were awed by the resort. Both my husband and I went to the spa on site and had a Swedish Massage. They did a great job! My kids did go to " Relish" which is the restaurant above the golf club, son had a burger and he did not feel well after, but not sure if that was the cause. Altogether a great visit and glad we stayed re before heading to Sedona for a few days.

reviews.author: pinkbootpootle
reviews.title: Elegant relaxation
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at the Phoenician for 9 nights with my husband and my parents and would go back there in a heartbeat.  We were in Scottsdale for a golfing holiday.  My parents have stayed at the hotel before and it came highly recommended.  We booked the hotel as part of a package which included our golf but not flights through SuperTravel Golf so we got a great rate in our deal.

Upon arrival I was immediately impressed by the hotel drive and landscaping - it was stunning and very manicured.  I dropped my husband and parents off to check in while I went to self park.  We were checked in very efficiently and went off to our rooms.  Within 2 minutes our bags arrived and our porter brought them in.  Due to our room facing the mountain I felt I would miss the sun shining in so reception very quickly arranged for a different room with a more sunny outlook in one of the Casitas at no extra cost.  The receptionist was very helpful and also arranged for one of the bellboys to take me and our cases to the new room which overlooked the golf course.

During our stay we had great service at the bar, both inside and out by the fire pit (highly recommended).  We had breakfast occasionally on the patio although we preferred to try the local breakfast places in Scottsdale town.  Service was excellent each time.

The housekeeping team were excellent and our room was kept spotlessly clean with plenty of fresh towels.  We did not use room service but did request ice and this was brought promptly each time.

Our favourite place to hang out was Relish, the burger place in the Golf Clubhouse.  The team there were excellent and after only one visit knew our drinks order.  We would often pop in for a quick slider and Prickly Pear margarita after a long day at golf. 

I cannot find fault with the Phoenician, every person we interacted with was friendly and courteous, the public areas very clean and well kept and our room was just perfect.

We did end up travelling quite a bit towards Kierlands and that area due to the restaurants but we liked the Phoenician for it's proximity to the main mall and also to the airport.

Great hotel, great service, great stay!

reviews.author: texandra j
reviews.title: Spring Break - Last Minute
reviews.text: Due to inclement weather in another location, at the last minute we changed our plans to stay at the Phoenician.  We were not disappointed!  We had an amazing time. The rooms are large as well as the bathrooms.  The hotel staff is very well trained, polished and professional.  Within 30 minutes of our arrival at the pool on day 1, my son was stung by a wasp.  The pool attendants quickly came to his aid and called security to the pool in the event of an allergic reaction.  They were so professional, concerned and attentive.  The next day, they sought us out at the pool and checked on him again.  They were really amazing.  The property is beautiful.  The Cactus Garden is a must see.  My kids loved the Kids Club!  Everything about this hotel is beautiful.  We even extended our stay one day because we were having such a great time.  It was very hard to leave.

reviews.author: Itchyfeet024
reviews.title: Great Resort!
reviews.text:
With brevity in mind, here's the good & the bad
Good
-service: great service received from room, front desk & pool attendants.  I asked for extra bottles of water & within a couple of minutes, the room attendant comes back with four.
-property: (probably it’s biggest strength) expansive, beautiful walking trail in the cactus garden & other areas of the property & easy hiking on Camelback Mountain.  Less than a 5-minute drive to Scottsdale Mall.
-golf course: great layout – 27 holes; both traditional & desert style courses
-gym: not bad for a resort course; all the equipment that I worked out with were relatively new; adequate selection of cardio equipment
-rooms: beautifully appointed especially the bathrooms

Bad
-pool area:  the hotel had a high occupancy & it was tough to get a free spot if you come in after 10AM.  Some guests were playing the “towel” game i.e. putting towels & other personal items to “reserve” the spot.  There is a policy against this but it didn’t appear to be strictly enforced.
-room location: we were on the 4th floor facing the driveway & the balcony was covered with hedges, hence no view & all we heard were sounds.

reviews.author: 7Ramsfan7
reviews.title: Anniversary Trip - Spectacular
reviews.text:
We just returned from an Anniversary Trip.  We really struggled with selecting a place to stay, and find the right place for value, but still be nice for our trip.

I was hesitant at first to stay at Phoenecian.  Although I had heard many good things, the cost was something to consider.  However, we are really glad we paid a bit more and stayed here.  The reservation manager, Tim Canosa, was very helpful.  He helped us with a snag in our reservation, and was VERY professional and customer focused.  He also welcomed us to our room with a wonderful bottle of Champagne for our anniversary - what a nice surprise.

Some things that jump out at me.

ALL the employees were very friendly, super helpful, and very cheerful.  This is the sign of a well run resort.
Also, the pools are wonderful.  My wife and I spent the most time at the lower pool, which was a bit more secluded.  The Service at this pool was Amazing.  Jeremy was awesome, and a wonderful young lady named Mandi (I think) was the same.
Drinks, food, water came out super fast.
Hiking Camelback Mountain was very convenient and awesome.
The patio restaurant was really a great place to hang out at night.  Great views, fire pits, very relaxing.
The grounds were spectacular, and added to the experience.
Also, the resort is five minutes from Old Scottsdale, which was convenient to great restaurants, shopping, etc...
Spa - fantastic.
Service - any time someplace go busy with customers, whether at pool, front desk, restaurant, etc... it wasn't a minute before extra staff showed up and helped.  This management of this hotel seems to have an awesome system for preventing any bad experience from surfacing for guests.  This was very impressive, and made the experience awesome.

The other thing that was interesting is that there seemed to be a ton of kids at the resort during our stay, however, the resort is laid out so well, that you don't really feel like the kids were there, in the way, etc... Never noticed excessive noise, crowds, or anything like that, and there were hundreds of small children staying there at the time (Chicago schools were on Spring Break).

My wife and I are very frugal, so it was hard to justify spending more to stay at a high end resort, but Phoenician was WELL WORTH ever penny, we will stay there again without hesitation, and recommend it to anyone who asks.

reviews.author: Avondaletraveler
reviews.title: This is the place to stay!
reviews.text:
A warning, my spelling stinks but it's a very knowledge review, I promise, so read on!

My husband and I were just there this past weekend to celebrate our 11th anniversary. All cards on the table, we did meet at the Phoenician and then got married there as well so it will always have a soft spot for us. 

But here is why you cannot go wrong staying here:
The resort is beyond incredible looking. Make sure to bring your camera, you'll want to take a LOT of photos.

The rooms have anything you could ever need. Check that, they could use some black tea, all it had was decaf but I'm nitpicking. They even provide complimentary slippers and turndown service. And they sent a lovely champagne split for our anniversary, so sweet. 

Our room overlooked the pool and were three balconies to the right from the thirsty camel lounge so in the evening we sat outside with a glass of wine and listed to the entertainment (a wonderful singer) without having to go to the bar. 

There are sooooo many options for dining. We ate lunch at RELISH and I had the amazing Blu Burger. The tater tots are excellent as well. 
We stopped at the Ice Cream Parlor for some of their signature Phoenician Crunch ice cream. It's some of the best ice cream I've ever had, don't miss it!

We had dinner at II Terazzo. We had the appitizer special, a mushroom rosotto filled fried balls (looked like meatballs) in a WONDERFUL red sauce. I then had the petite filet with a perfect bernaise and a side of sweet potoatoes, all excellent. 
HOWEVER, my husband had the other steak and found it was not trimmed properly which dampened his enjoyment. The staff quickly offered us complimentary desserts to make up for it but we didn't have the room.

Breakfast was the buffet back at II Terazzo. It was excellent, highly recommended. Don't miss the crossanuts (sp) both regular and chocolate and you can build your own bagel and lox complete with red onion and capers, yum! 

Re entertainment we played tennis twice. The courts were in excellent condition, and they provide towels and water, and if you need, raquetts and balls. The kids club is also right there, hummmm, maybe drop off the kiddos and play a couple of sets?

We also tourned the catus garden which is at the base of Camelback mountain, lovely.

The pool was quite crowded. We sat at the upper pool and were lucky to get two chairs together. Admittedly, we didn't arrive at the pool till about 1 in the afternoon. I'd recommend going earlier to stake out a good spot. It also did take awhile for the attendent to come by to take our drink order (I had a very potent rum and ginger based drink listed in their menu that was well worth the $9 price). But the pools are fantastic, perfect tempature and so beautiful.

There are many other things to do but as this was just a one night stay we didn't get to the spa, gym or golf.

Will we go back again? Just try to stop us!

reviews.author: MesaK
reviews.title: Breath Taking Views,  Wonderful Rooms
reviews.text:
Plan ahead for this destination, it is very popular for spring Break.'
This location is perfectly located for enjoying what Scottsdale , AZ 
has to offer. Great shopping, great restaurants and wonderful views during a hike.
Ask about room location when you book, some rooms may seem more
romantic because there are at the base of the moutain, other rooms provide
breath taking views both are special but you may want to select your experience.
The free tea and coffee service is nice. Overall this place provides a taste of luxury
desert vacation. I would recommend off season to get both a great deal and a relaxing
pace with unbelieveable service.

reviews.author: texasgirl020
reviews.title: FABULOUS SERVICE, BEAUTIFUL PROPERTY
reviews.text:
This was a girls trip.  I've had the great fortune to travel with the same 4 women for the last 20 years.  We have been a lot of different places but had never been to Scottsdale.  What a treat it is to stay at a place that understands what customer service is all about.  This is a large property, that can sometimes mean that the people who work there are on "auto pilot"  Not the case at the Phoenician.  From the moment we arrived at the main desk, to the wait staff at Relish to our friends Steve and Sam at the Oasis we were treated like queens.  (We actually think we are queens)  The room service was spectacular...one evening we decided to have dinner on our balcony and asked them for candles...they found some and rushed them right over.  Its that kind of customer service that doesnt show up as often as it should in these 5 star hotels.  

We ate one night at the J & G Steakhouse which is on the property.  What a great experience.  Make reservations before you travel to be sure that you can get in and then request a table outside.  The view is stunning and the food fantastic.  

We stayed in the casitas which was very nice as that allowed us to be near the pool area.  We found the pool at the bottom to be a little quieter (less kids) and we had chairs that looked out on to the pond that is there...very nice! Another great little extra is that they brought around pitchers of water for each group so that you always had water.  Our water pitchers were replaced 5 or 6 times in a day so you always had ice water which is just another example of the above and beyond this place turned out to be. 

We travel to a lot of 5 star hotels and Starwood should really take a close look at the GM and staff for this hotel and make sure that all properties strive to be as excellent as the Phoenician.  Thanks to the entire staff for making our trip memorable!

reviews.author: sds1966
reviews.title: 2nd year back
reviews.text: We came back because we enjoyed our trip so much last year.  Nothing has really changed except they now offer free coffee/tea outside Il Terrazzo in the AM which is great.  The pool service was a bit slower this year but the pool was packed everyday.  I heard people complaining about not being able to hold chairs but I have always found this irritating when on vacation so I commend the Phoenician for their policy.  We will probably be back next year!

reviews.author: JessieC16
reviews.title: Waste of a lot of money
reviews.text:
I am a starwood Good member and usually stay at an SPG property.  We along with three other families came here for spring break. We have grown up kids so typically rent two rooms. we paid 1500 per room for a total of three nights ( so a total of 3000 for the two rooms). One of the rooms bathroom stinks, after a shower, like sewage.

Second, while we rented the two rooms, we found that  you could rent a large (1400 sq ft)  1 bedroom suite for approx $2100 for the same duration. Save urself the money!!

Additionally, the service is not all that great...for breakfast, they bring you a tea cup without a teaspoon, do not deliver the newspapers, etc. do not come hear for spring break and just check out the room and suite prices....the vacation, so far, has been a real disappointment.

reviews.author: suburbanmom7813
reviews.title: Lovely but not special
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is a lovely and the service is great, from the waitstaff at Relish Burger to the staff in the fitness center.  The problem is that during spring break the pools are absolutely packed.  

There are days we would be at the pool by 9:15 and there were no available pool chairs.  The pool staff will try to locate chairs (old vinyl lounge chairs) and set them up for you but that might be in the lawn area, outside of the pool, with not a bit of shade.  The days that we were able to get pool chairs, the chairs were literally lined up in 4 rows, with about an inch of space between them.  This was a major negative for us, as we were looking to go do some sightseeing in the morning, before the heat of the day, and come back to the hotel to enjoy the pool.  It was so stressful to think that we wouldn't be able to sit at the pool if we didn't get there immediately after breakfast.  The space around one pool is taken primarily by cabanas ($275 per weekday, $375 per weekend day).  

There are ducks on property that hang out in the pool.  On top of that, guests were tossing chips into the pool to feed the ducks and no one who worked at the hotel was asking them to stop.  This seemed kind of gross and not what we expected at this level of hotel. 

There was not much to do at night with kids, even during spring break.  They had movies at the pool two nights.  We tried to take them to the ice cream parlor that has been mentioned in previous reviews.  It was closed by 8:00 on a Friday night, which seemed unusually early. 

Our room was not ready until 5:30 on the day of check-in.  Maybe this is the norm but we hadn't experienced this in many years of traveling. 

The good: 
No complaints about service.  Staff worked hard to keep pool area clean and bring water pitchers around.  The concierge was extremely helpful in giving restaurant recommendations/reservations, hike suggestions, etc.  She encouraged us to stop back before we left for a hike to pick up cold bottled water.  She also told us that Il Terrazzo provides a complimentary coffee station in the mornings which would have been nice to know when we checked in, since we had been purchasing coffee elsewhere.  

A yoga class was very enjoyable - nice bright fitness room and the instructor was helpful.  

Our room (deluxe room in casitas) was spacious, with a large patio and very quiet.  We didn't really hear anyone from within our room.  

All in all, there were no major complaints.  It might be better to be there during off-peak season.  But there was nothing about the grounds or facility that really "wowed" us.  We would not be interested in returning.

reviews.author: JBCol
reviews.title: Magnificent property
reviews.text:
Traveled to AZ for business so the hotel was chosen for me. However, the hotel is beautiful, from the lobby to the pool, the spa, the restaurants and the hotel shops, we were impressed at every turn. The rooms themselves are very spacious, huge bathroom with Jacuzzi tubs with every amenity you can think of (lip balm, nail file, cotton pads for makeup remover, slippers, robe, ipod dock/radio,small in-room safe) with turn down service nightly. I was very happy this is where I was booked to stay!

Staff was wonderful across the board. Helpful and pleasant. 
Ate in all of the restaurants, food was good, no complaints. (try the tater tots at Relish!)

Spa was enormous, very clean, with many treatment rooms and a meditation room to relax before/after treatments. A bit tricky to find the spa (its down a flight of stairs beneath the hair salon) but well worth the walk across the grounds. I had a massage with Cher, one of the best I've had, I highly recommend! 

Pools were very crowded so be sure to head out early to secure a prime spot (and plan to stay there) The hotel discourages "saving" lounge chairs and has several signs posted stating they will remove unattended property after 9am, which I think is a great idea. 

Overall we had a great stay and I would return to this property if I'm ever in the area again.

reviews.author: happy2travel2marco
reviews.title: Worst vacation in 10 years!
reviews.text: I really wanted to like it here.  Our room so far away we felt like we had to pack up for the day to go anywhere.  Horrible spa experience-service, the worst ever!  Restaurants were ok.  Nothing to write home about.  Other guests were obnoxious.  They must have run a special discount to get some of the other guests to come that week.  Hotel service never followed through on anything.  I felt I was back in my office monitoring employees and keeping up on everyone.  It just wasn't a vacation at all.  I have more specifics and could go on for days.  What was horrible about this hotel?  The pool staff, pool, the rooms, cleanliness, front desk staff, spa personnel, spa itself highly disappointing, restaurants wait service very slow.  The hotel was packed.  You would think they would have not had it so crowded that week.  Perhaps everything would have been better.  That is a chance I'm not willing to take.  From now on I'll head back to the Biltmore.  I'm not suggesting this hotel I just don't remember any, not anything like this, happening there.  What a horrible experience.  I vacation about 5-6 weeks a year and this was my worst vacation in 10 years including a carnival cruise I took 5 years ago!

reviews.author: MaureenA99
reviews.title: Disappointing Pool Experience
reviews.text: We were looking forward to spending our day at the beautiful pools pictured on the website. We had a day of relaxing, swimming, sipping drinks and eating lunch poolside in mind.  When we arrived in the pool area about half the chairs were occupied, but few chairs were available although there were signs indicating that personal belongings would be removed from empty chairs because of high occupancy.  Very few people were in the pool.  We finally joyfully located chairs and were setting our things down, when an employee came over to say he was just going to set up those chairs other guests.  He pointed to another area and said there were chairs over there and he would help us later.  Disappointed we set out in that direction, but found no available chairs.  As we stood around looking in all directions for an open chair, a lovely guest offered two chairs in the very back section, saying her children could share since they would likely be in the water much of the day.  She indicated that an employee would bring us towels.  We gratefully settled in, but the employee indicated she would not bring us towels.  We had to go to another area and check-in.  The guest was surprised by that, but off we went to check in and get our towels.  As we sat at the pool, we observed the same employee who would not bring us towels, offer to bring towels to other guests arriving in the area.  We did not hear her tell a single other guest to go get their own towels.  About 45 minutes later, the employee who took the chairs we originally located, walked by and said something like...I see you found chairs.  We are pretty normal looking folks, have been fortunate to visit a number of lovely resorts/hotels and have never been treated so shabbily. Very disappointing experience.

reviews.author: CalGirl86
reviews.title: Gorgeous Grounds
reviews.text: This was our third stay and we can't wait to come back.  Ground are beautiful, full of interesting plants and art.  Restaurants are all good and I particularly like the sushi on the back patio Thursdays- Saturdays.  Spa is lovely and so is the golf.  This makes a great getaway spot!  My only complaint is that the valet service is not efficient.  Even calling down in advance, our car was never ready for us.  However, the overall experience is still very good.  Great for spring training, girls week-ends shopping or a romantic holiday.

reviews.author: Craig M
reviews.title: High expectations
reviews.text:
This is a world class hotel and one expects it to be for the price it charges.  So, while my comments are of a nit-picky type it is because one expects perfection at a hotel of this ilk.  Item one, we checked in and were given a room with a delightful view of a concrete retaining wall - it is hard to image that a hotel that charges over $600 per night would have a room like that, let alone use it for a paying customer but they did.  Obviously, I asked for another room and they were oh so nice about it but we were given one on the lower level so far to the end of the hotel that the walking was substantial.  One wonders?

We had dinner at one of the restaurants and the service was excellent, the food superb but small portions and very expensive.  The value equation was severely tested, one expects just a bit more for $50 per head.

Third, when you arrive the valet parks your car, if you don't ask, it is $39 per night or if you have them return it to you and you park it yourself before 11:00 PM in the same covered lot, it is no charge.  Glad I asked.

So net, net - it is a great hotel but not perfect, it is expensive for everything but the rooms are spacious and the grounds spectacular.

reviews.author: TexasMod76
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort.. Lush Property..We LOVED it!
reviews.text: It is an amazing resort and im not sure were to start.. The property is stunning and beautiful. The service is second to none. We stayed in a "Casita" overlooking Camelback mountain and the pool area with a great private patio for breakfast! (also parking spots at no charge) It's expensive but without a doubt worth the money! They have a beautiful golf course and give you free bikes if you want to see the area on two wheels! If you book at Phoenician you wont get the boutique feel but you will be amazed every aspect of the resort!

reviews.author: Barbara R
reviews.title: Awesome experience
reviews.text: It was an amazing experience.  Great value also considering what you are getting. Gorgeous grounds.  It was an enchanting stay for the Christmas holiday that we spent in Phoenix with our kids and grandkids.

reviews.author: Sue C
reviews.title: Every year for a month.
reviews.text: Rooms with a view are the best. Have come the last 4 years and stayed for a month each time. Pools are beautiful if you can get a seat. Restaurants are quite good. We come for three reasons. James, greeting in the lobby makes you feel at home. Kelly, in ice cream parlor always has a smile and is super! Christine, in the Il Terrazzo is an absolute gem. Always smiling and what a personality! Rooms need updating and cleaning staff need to speak a little English and clean better! We stay a month, no one thanks us or gives us upgrades.

reviews.author: Gary G
reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.text: This hotel and resort was amazing. The grounds were impeccable. Food was great. Staff were fantastic. Really enjoyed my stay here! Would highly recommend Relish the Burger Bar. Would live to stay here again.

reviews.author: HangLTX
reviews.title: Great views and great conference space
reviews.text: Our meetings went very well at the Phoenician.  Wonderful views and the service has been excellent.  The rooms are large and very clean.  They go above and beyond to provide great food, even when you have (gluten) allergies.

reviews.author: hkouman
reviews.title: amazing facilities.....poor food and beverage
reviews.text:
A business trip for en exhibition inside the hotel!! rooms are very big and clean!! maid service is very good! Exhibition was very well organised and staff were very friendly!!! they only bad experience was some of f&b dept.....it looks liked that if you wanted to have a late dinner the only place was the bar downstairs that one night staff told us not to try ordering because we d have to wait for an hr + !Also room service would take 45 mins...which is acceptable for the roomservice!! but dining option felt quite limited....!!!

the first day of the buffet...they forgot to offer bread where the specific main courses ''was asking'' for it....!! the next day the put bread....the second day of the buffey they had a wide range of past....even if the theme was italian (which i dont know) the recipies were very similar

its a beautiful place! i d go back of course!

reviews.author: Baumer121
reviews.title: Ideal resort that have everything!
reviews.text: The resort has everything for the ultimate vacation; great golf courses, tennis complex, swimming pools, fitness and spa and great weather.  We just returned from 5 nights at the resort.  We stayed in a 2 bedroom Casitas suite; the suite was fantastic with 3 full bathrooms, each with a shower, jacuzzi tub, toilet room, and double sink.  The suite had a great stereo system, 3 TVs , dining room table, living room, full kitchenette, and 3 private decks.  The pool service was great everyday; ice water in pitchers constantly refilled, great food service, and even cracker jacks in celebration of spring training.  The tennis center and golf courses are what would be expected of a 5 star resort. The restaurants are also excellent.  The breakfast is amazing, Tim, the manager makes sure the service is top notch and they cater ro individual needs (my daughter is gluten free and they were very accomodating).  We also ate at the J&G Seakhouse and the food was very good and the service was also very good.  One quick story to show how amazing the srvice is; I left my wallet in my room safe and realized it when already at the airport.  It was only an hour or so before my flight and they managed to get the wallet deliver it to me at the airport so I wouldn't miss my slight.  In summary, the Phoenician is truly an amazing five star plus resort.

reviews.author: the1015club
reviews.title: Desert oasis with mountain views.  Relax and refresh.
reviews.text: My spouse had a business trip, but it was all relaxing for me.  We stayed in a casita, down the hill from the lobby and main hotel buildings. Very quiet and close to the golf clubhouse and spa.  The pools were beautiful and the adults only pool kept the splashing and noise to the kiddies at the waterslide and other pools. This is a beautifully manicured property about 30 minutes drive from the Phoenix airport.  It is a bit on the older side, but the main evidence of that was some dated wallpaper.  A few of the standout features of our room were a true walk-in closet with a separate overhead light, a dimmer switch for the bathroom lights, and great furniture on the deep balcony with thick cushions on the chairs and chaise. The view of Camelback Mountain from our balcony was the icing on the cake.  The walking paths throughout the property and cactus garden are a unexpected addition to the usual resort hotel experience.

reviews.author: arubadive
reviews.title: a true 5 star
reviews.text: This is a fabulous resort! We had no complaints during our 4 night stay...The food is so fresh and the services are second to none. Grounds are amazing and quite tropical. We just love this place! Another fun thing to do is to climb camel back mountain located right behind the resort! well worth the effort. And don't forget to get their signature ice cream " Phoenician Crunch"

reviews.author: Sojourns In Truth
reviews.title: Convention Hotel and Spa
reviews.text:
I'd always wanted to try the Phoenician - as a spa destination. I was surprised when my company named it as our incentive trip. The grounds are beautiful and perfectly manicured. I didn't golf but those who did said it was wonderful. Our room was in the casita. Easily accessible and had a lovely view of the fountains in the lake. Food was decent. (We were eating in mass scale, not the restaurants). Service was good from front desk, lounge and lobby bar. Housekeeping didn't show until after 2:30 one day and we'd already been out and come back. There was a layer of dust in several areas of the bathroom. Everything in the room was in good working order except the vanity makeup mirror in the bathroom, which should have lit up but wouldn't. I guess the bulb was blown. It remained that way so I guess housekeeping never checked it. The pools are delightful. The staff is extremely attentive - if you ask where something is, they don't tell you, they take you....Signature 5 star service. If I was a spa guest, seeking a retreat, I'd not have been happy with the corporate crowd overtaking the lobby bar. But there were other lounge areas in more quiet places and my little group managed to escape to the steakhouse lounge, which was incredibly beautiful and on the top floor with a deck with firepits overlooking the pools and gold course.  Very tranquil. It's a stunning place and I'd consider it a "must see" for any true traveler. I'd stay in the casitas again. There are parking spaces just outside the doors to the rear of the casitas - perfect if you have a vehicle.  On another note, when we checked in, we were told that in order to have our reserved room (a king) we'd need to take a an accessible room (handicapped, For the politically incorrect) or a double in the casitas. The casitas sounded better and people in the main hotel said they though the casitas were the superior option, but when I reserve a king at a 5 star resort, I expect to get what I reserved.....Not a compromise that I need to negotiate at check in. I get sick of hotels making me negotiate my room at check in. The double was a mistake. When you are used to a king, you need to sleep in a king, IMO. . At minimum, I'd like what I reserved. 
Also, don't go without a fat wallet ( not that you would anyway). Cocktails were $20 each. Each time the two of us sat at the bar, it was $100 with tip. Be ready for that. The drinks are well made and they are generous with pours. I was drinking French Martinis - very well done. Overall, is return, stay in the casitas (in a king!) and spend more time in the spa. I also thought the spa was small and I would have expected more quiet areas/hydro retreat...maybe a plunge pool and some aromatherapy....a place to escape and relax before or after a treatment.

reviews.author: Nancy P
reviews.title: Please, 5-star? Who are you kidding?
reviews.text: The Phoenician is a lovely property, but take a bundle of cash for ANY extra charge you can imagine and be prepared for surprises. A regular cup of carry-out coffee is more than $4.00, oatmeal is $9, you are charged for "porterage" even if you never see a porter and wheel in your own bag, and despite the high-end rack rate, you are charged on top of that for housekeeping, which, for us, one day did not happen at all and another day we had to request it since past 2 PM, it did not look like it was going to happen for the second day in a row.
