Location: Like most resorts, u need a car, there are always limo service available for 14$ to take to 5 mile radius which basically ocvers the mall, downtown area  and restaurants.
Amenities: many swimming pools, Water slide (for the families with children). Very good renovated gym, Gold club and tennis court.
Lobby had live music band at every night I was there. 
At times you may feel it is a not brand new hotel but you will feel at all time you are in a luxurious hotel.

reviews.author: Sunbound
reviews.title: Well done Phoenician staff
reviews.text: Great hotel with impeccable service. Outstanding facilities all around and well maintained grounds. The pool, tennis, golf course and gym facilities were amazing. The staff throughout were excellent and the suite we stayed in felt like home.

reviews.author: RMG66
reviews.title: Far exceeded our expectations
reviews.text: We recently stayed in a casita suite at the Phoenician and were blown away by the experience. The resort is quite grand in scale and has an elegance one imagines from a bygone era. The staff we encountered was very friendly and utra professional.  We rented a cabana by the Mother of Pearl Pool, which for our family with teens was a good fit.  The Mother of Pearl Pool had some small children playing about, but was not over run with tots like the upper pools appeared to be.  The service poolside was exceptional.  However, in comparison to some of the cabanas we have rented in Las Vegas, I have to say this one at the Phoenician was a bit small and not as well equipped, for example, no television or a/c.  We enjoyed snacks and drinks poolside which all arrived in a timely fashion and were of excellent quality.  The highlight of our stay though was the suite.  The decor of the casita suite we stayed in was lovely.  We felt as though we were guests in an elegant home rather than in a hotel.  We had a pool-view suite which had a fabulous view of the mountains as well.  Ours was a ground floor suite, which normally is not my thing for safety concerns, but in this case the suite flowed so perfectly out onto the 3 patios (yes, 3 patios) and the manicured lawn it literally felt like we were in a luxurious home.  The living room had a large sofa, a few occassional chairs and a desk equipped with a fax machine. There was a large flat screen tv in the living room placed above a grand fireplace.  Also in the living area was a stunning dining room table which seated 6 and a buffet.  We were able to enjoy room service as a family around that table and were amazed by the level of service, such as toast made table side to our liking.  The bedrooms were both very large and comfortable. All in all we had a king bedroom with large luxurious bath, a second bedroom with two queens and another luxury bath and the living room in the center which had a pull out sofa bed and another full bath.  Our family of 6 was more than comfortable, and the pampering at the Phoenician makes you never want to leave.

reviews.author: DeAunderia
reviews.title: Oasis in Scottsdale
reviews.text: The Phoenician was a small respite from the toll of completing my PhD and despite visiting during the rainy season, we truly enjoyed the lush amenities provided us there.  We ate really tasty burgers at RELISH BURGER BISTRO... $16 is a bit steep,... so we only went once, but we enjoyed the little extras - cute basket of tater tot fries, buttery, grilled bun and homemade root beer.  Well, I actually didn't like how sweet the root beer was, so I just exchanged for water, but it was still a nice touch.  The breakfast brunch on Sunday at Il Terrazzo is not to be missed with fluffy, blueberry pancakes with the addition of lemon infused ricotta... just lovely!  The grounds are well-maintained and our room was whisper quiet despite the many guests on our floor.

reviews.author: Ritchie S
reviews.title: Consistent excellence
reviews.text: This must be my 10th stay here and it never disappoints. Quality abounds. My main hotel located Room was excellently furnished and equipped. Throughout the service is seamless and unobtrusive. The whole complex really is immaculate. A great place for a short break.

reviews.author: V H
reviews.title: Poor Billing Practices
reviews.text:
The staff in the restaurant and in the bar are outstanding. 

However, be advised that the accounting system will begin placing credit card charges in the amount that they feel necessary to secure their charges. They bill in advance (you are not trustworthy to pay your bill), and are impossible to get hold of to reconcile the account, if your stay is on a weekend.

I had to call my credit card company to refute the charges which popped up before I even finished my stay or charged anything. They also billed it in excess of the charges incurred by a large amount. 

I will not stay at the Phoenician again. Since it is a Starwood property I include this in all future travel as an organization which I will avoid as much as alternatives exist.

reviews.author: chadchicago
reviews.title: Top Notch for Business
reviews.text: I was here for a business conference, and couldn't be more impressed with the facilities, food, and service.  The rooms were large and truly different that the typical chain offering.  The hotel maintains a collection of cactus plants immediately next to the property, and it is a delight to walk through.  The pool area is pristine.  Most of the meals I had were banquet service, but this was the kind of place where the banquet offerings are truly like a great restaurant meal.  I was not able to bring the family, but surely will the next time.  The setting, next to a dramatic and massive rock formation, is memorable.

reviews.author: VivianinNYC
reviews.title: Magnificent
reviews.text: What a beautiful resort. I had absolutely no complaints. A true 5 star resort. The pools are great. The service is unbelievable. The staff is very friendly and helpful I would definately recommend and return!

reviews.author: OnTheGo9961
reviews.title: Business Conference-no internet??
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, room was top notch, and hotel staff was extremely nice.  I attended a national business conference at the Phoenician in Scottsdale.  The internet service was almost non-existent.  I understand that the resort is built against Camelback mountain, but it seems to me that any location designed so well for multiple conferences would certainly have looked into the internet problem.  The only spot I could get access was the cyber cafe - very inconvenient.  If you are looking for a great get-away to play some golf and relax, this would be the place!

reviews.author: niquee2
reviews.title: June stay
reviews.text:
Pro's:
-Great location, mountainview- able to go hiking within walking distance.
-Beautiful hotel- nice pools, nice scenery.
-Staff was very friendly  & helpful.

Cons:
-Internet service was not good- it kept going in and out, and we would have to keep signing in again. Had to have a tech come up and look at it, and it still was not much better.
-A bit expensive
-Not much night life in the area, you would have to travel off the hotel about 15 minutes.
-Be careful what room you are in.  We had a mountain view, and read reviews so we tried to get an upgrade to a different section.  When we were moved, the room we originally had was actually much better, so we ended up moving back.

Overall a really good experience if you are looking to get away & relax somewhere nice, but still want to have some time doing activities (ie: hiking, bike riding, tennis, etc.)  We also took a tour bus to see the Grand Canyon for the day which was a great experience, though it may depend on who your driver is.  Our guy was funny, so it was much better than renting a car to go out there in my opinion.

reviews.author: MysteryShopper27
reviews.title: Over Billing and Dated Room
reviews.text: Very disappointing. Could not get a call back from the hotel's Sales Department about whether they had a conference room available for my group. I was double billed for not one, but two different stays at this hotel (one in August and one in September). The accounting/billing group doesn't not answer their phones and has not returned my phone messages. I've called over 20 times to get the refunds that I'm owed, but somehow after 20 calls the matter is not yet resolved. I'm also awaiting a return call from the GM, Mark V. Interestingly, the accounting group cites a known problem (CAUSING CUSTOMERS TO BE DOUBLE BILLED) that is related to a new software system. Apparently they have had this "known problem" for at least a month now. My advice to future guests...beware and check your credit card statements for double billings. Also, although this resort is generally beautiful, I paid extra for an upgraded room Starwood calls a Casita Room....don't go for this upgrade as these rooms are away from the main hotel building (inconvenient) and are dated.

reviews.author: Mdennis28
reviews.title: 5 Star... really!!!
reviews.text: Recently stayed at the Phoenician and many of the positive comments are accurate.  However, for a supposedly five star resort their is just some things that are off.  The internet connectivity throughout the resort is awful, and in the conference center it is non-existent without paying for it.  It even seems that they block the cell reception in the conference center to force you to use their wi-fi.   I also have an issue with my bill that I have been trying to resolve.  I have left 4 messages and have yet to have one call returned.  All in all, I doubt that I will ever return to this resort. There is just too much competition in Scottsdale to deal with these issues.

reviews.author: Mike3412
reviews.title: This poor is for one reason only and it's a big one in my opinion
reviews.text:
All the superlatives are right.  It's a beautiful place with over-the-top customer service.  Our one-bedroom casita is great.  The pool is fantastic.  

The reason for the poor rating?  The wired internet is only in the living room, not in the bedroom.  So what, right?  The problem is the wireless internet is so bad it is non-useable.  The computer desk in the living room (where the only wired internet outlet is) is small and faces a wall.  The computer desk in the bedroom (where the wired internet isn't and the wireless internet does not work)  is huge, and faces huge sliding doors with a great view of the grounds.

I called customer service to complain about the wireless internet signal being too weak to work and was told they would send someone out to look at it.  I told them that wouldn't do any good because the problem is a weak signal, not a malfunction.  Then they told me that the good news is that they are working on an upgrade that would be available later this year and would increase coverage greatly.  That doesn't help me much.

I could use my laptop in the living room but couldn't use my ipad.  I have a sling box set up at home to watch Tivo recordings from on my ipad which didn't work at all because of no wireless.  I also missed the Sunday hometeam football game.

Would I come back?  Not if the wireless internet did not work.

reviews.author: Beautiful37
reviews.title: Amazing location and staff
reviews.text: I had an amazing stay at this location for a weekend with the family.  Can I say that this place has everything covered, from the playground for my toddler, to the beautiful swimming pools and beautiful views.  I will definitely make a note to visit again, whether it be with family or couples getaway this place does it all.

reviews.author: OhioAnimallover3
reviews.title: Beautiful resort with outstanding staff!!
reviews.text: Our experience at the Phoenician was amazing! Check in was a breeze, there was a small line but it moved very quickly and there was a manager walking around passing out cool bottled water to everyone, very nice on that 95 degree day!! Our room and view were both wonderful. The room was very clean, plenty of linen. The bed was heavenly!! No trouble falling asleep, it was very cozy. We had a lovely balcony on the 4th floor overlooking the pool. Perfect view!! Getting up every morning seeing the pool and the mountains in the background was awesome.  Self parking was very easy, we used the underground parking and it was just a short walk to the elevators up to the room, not bad at all. The pool is open 24 hours which we took advantage of! The weather is great around 9-10pm, so we went for a swim and used the whirlpool. Enjoyed that very much!! During the day when you are poolside they bring you a pitcher of ice water with glasses.... Very nice! We loved our stay at the Phoenician!! If you are looking for a gorgeous resort in Scottsdale look no further than The Phoenician.

reviews.author: WellTraveled14725
reviews.title: There are not enough superlatives!
reviews.text: Just returned from a 4 day business conference at the Phoenician.  It is easily the best hotel I've ever stayed in, and I've stayed in many.  I'm not a golfer and didn't have time to visit the spa or the pools,  so I can't comment on those amenities.  The staff, everyone from the front desk to the bell desk to the maintenance staff are uniformly polite, welcoming, and competent.  The conference center is well laid out, with excellent A/V facilities, and even food well above the typical "hotel food".  The room was clean, large, and comfy, with a usable desk and plenty of power outlets.  The high speed internet is genuinely high speed and not the typical sluggish DSL of many hotels.

reviews.author: MrsO707
reviews.title: Made our trip worth it!
reviews.text: Me and my husband went to a wedding last weekend in flagstaff and we decided to make the most of the trip visit scottsdale, Sedona and flagstaff. Well when we arrived to Scottsdale it was kind of a yucky day which I was bummed about so instead of sitting out by the Phoenician's beautiful 9 pools like planned to do wasn't going to happen!!!!!! we ended up wandered around the resort. (which btw is beautiful and the staff is BEYOND friendly) We went to there wine tasting room inside the resort we got the best treatment the guys in the wine shop told us where to eat, drink and things to see so we got the most out of our short trip..they were SO friendly the sommelier even came over to the bar from the wine bar and let us try some top of the line tequila and suggested some drinks he was great! We also had a lot of fun at the thirsty Camel...bomb mai tai's at the bar! Overall they made our trip! It was definitely hard to leave and its going to be hard to just stay at a standard hotel..now! Thanks Phoenician ...we cant wait to come back just to stay here!

reviews.author: Jordan J
reviews.title: Really fantastic! Very impressed!
reviews.text:
I am a very hard guest to please, We take 1-2 weekend trips a month in the south west and like to stay at the very best resorts and I am a real stickler for the details.

The Phoenician really hit top marks on nearly everything. Yes the rooms are a bit dated, but honestly I didn't care. The grounds, the staff, the food - everything was fantastic.

The food was a bit overpriced - but the drinks were actually very fair so it balanced it out. We did managed to spend nearly $400 in on food and drinks in 1 night, but we had a really fantastic time.

One more thing - the bed - amazing! Super soft sheets, great pillows!

reviews.author: spchiro
reviews.title: Quite frankly, it doesn't get better than this
reviews.text: My wife and I took a long overdue extended weekend during the Labor Day holiday to do nothing but relax.  We decided to spend our time at the Phoenician, which neither of us had been to, but had been aware of, having spent previous years vacations in Phoenix at other properties.  I'm always interested in how I am treated as a customer, whether at a restaurant or staying at a hotel, and I am someone who goes in with the glass half full, and not with the glass half empty.  I've left my cynicism behind years ago, and understand that my experience is mine to make or break.  I go in positively expecting the best, yet reserve what I consider to be a healthy dose of critical thinking that is willing to spot inconsistency, and then share it in a positive way.   Bottom line, the Phoenician now can count on me as one of their fans.  I was impressed with the attentive customer service that I received from each and every individual staff member whom I encountered, no matter what position they were in.  Our days were spent by the lower pool, going from lounge chair to water and back and forth from 9am to 5pm.  We were told that for this holiday weekend, there would be no exclusive adult pool and, gracefully, there were no particularly rowdy kids.  It all worked.  The chairs were comfortable, the towels were huge, and the water was the perfect temperature for floating around on a styrofoam noodle, which there were plenty of.  This is a high end resort, and you will pay for it.  I would say that it was well worth the price.  We had a package that gave us the 4th night free, as well as a $65 breakfast credit.  We stayed in a superior deluxe casita, which has the larger bathrooms and a beautiful view of the lagoon, the casita grounds, and the lower pool and cabana area.  The resort is so well appointed, inside and out, the Il Terrazzo restaurant (the only one we went to) so excellent, that we would have been satisfied not to leave the grounds, even though we did leave to seek out other restaurants.  There is obviously a very good customer service training program going on, and I would say that it is working.  I appreciated the attention paid to the guest children, with activites planned around the pool for them and, at night, an outdoor movie by the pool.  Even though the place was quite crowded over this past weekend, I never felt crowded and I always was attended to as if there were far fewer people  around.  So as not to write the kind of glowing review that looks like I work for the place, I will say that I noticed little bits of wear and tear, such as the bussing station in Il Terrazzo that should be refinished or replaced, some chips and gouges in the concrete around the pool area, and less than perfect clean up of various areas (such as finding a half eaten french fry on our balcony when we checked in - it was gone the next morning).  These to me are minor and did not detract from the comfortable ambience of this resort.  My impression is that if I had called about the french fry they would have come running.  Attention to customer service is always number one in my book, and, I gather, in the Phoenician management's book, also.  I would stay here again and again, and am planning to so next year.  I would say that if this place does not meet someone's high standards, perhaps nothing ever will.  Excellent job, Phoenician!

reviews.author: Mplsdtgirl
reviews.title: A place of yes!!!
reviews.text:
I am going to start with my only disappointment.  I only considered staying at hotels with an adult pool.  The Phoenian actively marketed and promoted their adult only pool so I was very upset when they removed the restriction on no children and allowed them in the adult only pool.  I was told it was because it was a busy holiday weekend which in my mind was all the more reason to not allow kids.
This hotel is first class.  The service was amazing and I am a service snob.  I have never been any where that called me by name so much.  No matter what I asked for the answer was always yes.  I never left the hotel there was no need.  
If the staff waited on you once they remembered your name and how you like things when you return.  I can't say enough good things about the staff.  Kudos to their training program and management.  
My room was clean and beautiful.
The pool chairs were nice and they had extra long towels that covered the entire chair which was really nice.  The bar at the pool had great staff.  Friendly and efficient.  I can't wait to come back.

reviews.author: SSPP73
reviews.title: Oh Phoenician, I love you but you need a makeover.
reviews.text:
I'm a huge fan of the Phoenician Tea. My friend & I do tea here at least 4x a year. We decided to mark our 35 year friendship by going to the tea & staying the night at the Phoenician. We booked massages, planned to do brunch, and have a great time.

The first thing we noticed when we opened our room was the smell. It smelled old, like a faded cigar masked by an air freshener. As an asthmatic, I'm very sensitive to smells. My friend had trouble with the smells too. We noticed cob webs on the walls and the carpet seemed a bit worn too. Our beds were comfortable enough.

During our tea, I noticed little details like the bathroom door's finish was chipping and wall corners were chipped. Papers were strewn on the bathroom floor and attendants weren't visible like the past. 

I hope the Phoenician takes care to maintain their property and address these cosmetic issues. She's a beautiful resort in need of a bit of TLC.

reviews.author: greekannoula69
reviews.title: desert oasis
reviews.text:
The overall resort was amazing, first class all the way, with amazing views from every corner !
My sons and I traveled in August , but it was sweltering hot.  There werent many people visiting at the time and scottsdale was a ghost town.  We still had a wonderful time because of our accomodations. Our room was large and comfy, very clean and the grounds were OUTSTANDING !  I would stay again for sure, BUT not in August !

reviews.author: jdmrosa
reviews.title: Very pleasant stay!
reviews.text: We stayed here on a combination business/pleasure trip, as I was attending a conference at the resort. Our room was clean and comfortable. The housekeeping staff came twice a day (morning and then evening for a turndown service), and they never once came while we were in the room, which was impressive. There were two things about the bathroom that were a little disappointing: no air vent or fan to help dissipate heat/humidity, and the stand up shower is a bit small especially compared to the very large size of the bathroom. For the resort as a whole, the property is very beautiful and sits at the edge of Camelback Mountain. We did take advantage of the pools a couple nights. However, we were disappointed to find out that on weeknights, the pool bar and grill close at 5 pm! Hoping to have a relaxing dinner by the pool, we instead were able to get some dishes and drinks "to go" from the Italian restaurant, with help from the friendly bartender at the adjacent lounge. The couple meals we did eat at the hotel were very good, but quite expensive. We often drove into nearby Scottsdale to eat and enjoy the many delicious restaurants there.

reviews.author: els217
reviews.title: This resort never disappoints!
reviews.text: Stayed here for six nights. As always the service is exceptional. They never say no at this resort. The grounds are beautiful and well maintained. The pool area is fantastic. Breakfast here is good but it is pricey. Love sitting at the Thirsty Camel lounge for drinks. The fitness facility is great for a resort. Headphones for the machines are provided as well as plenty of bottled water. Overall I love staying here! My only negative review is the carpet in the Casita rooms are a disgrace to this resort.  For what you pay these rooms really need a make over. I wore socks because the carpet was so dirty.  Please do not misunderstand.  I would go back here without question.  I hope this problem is resolved soon!

reviews.author: eliz933
reviews.title: Total and complete bliss!!!
reviews.text: My husband and I recently stayed at The Phoenician with my parents. The only bad thing about our trip was that we did not stay long enough!  From the arrival experience with Brandon and Chris to the great poolside service from Rich and his team, to the incredible gourmet dinner we had in Il Terrazzo it was all over the top!  We have stayed before and each time the experience gets better. Our rooms were beautiful. I love the new carpet in the hallways and really the rooms are the best in town. Al and Greg assisted us with dinner and it was one of the most incredible meals we have ever had. The new chef is great and he has made some nice tweaks to the menu, but they still the best bread ever. I wish I'd had time for some Phoenician Crunch ice cream in the Cafe, time to shop and time for the spa, but not this trip.  We did make it down the waterslide 3 times and got to enjoy the sunset before dinner. Thank you for such a memorable night. And a special thank you to Al and Greg in Il Terrazzo for one of the best dinners my parents and I have ever had!  They were so thrilled especially since it was my dad's birthday and my husband and I were paying.  The pastry team even made a special pie I ordered in advance- best weekend ever!!

reviews.author: IslandGirl721
reviews.title: Five Star Conference
reviews.text: If you are looking for a location to hold your next conference - look no further - the Phoenician is your place!!  My company held our conference here in June and it was just amazing.  We actually had three conferences over the course of a week for about 800 attendees in the travel industry - not an easy crowd to please!  But I have to say that  the staff at the Phoenician completely exceeded our expectations.  We have held our meetings at other luxury properties, and we all agreed that the Phoenician is the one to beat!  The level of service we received in the planning process was incredible.  Our conference manager, Andrew, and reservations manger, Mindie, were the best I've ever dealt with.  Once on site, everything went so smoothly I still can't believe it.  There isn't one thing I can think of that wasn't absolutely perfect.  The property is amazing, the rooms were all beautiful, meals were gourmet (hats off to Chef!), conference space incredible, but I think the best thing about the Phoenician is their staff. They were always right there thinking of what we needed before we even asked!  They were truly top-notch meeting professionals like no others!  After the conference, we received rave reviews from travel agents, and top travel industry executives!  Thank you to everyone at the Phoenician!

reviews.author: Ann B
reviews.title: Very Special Night
reviews.text: While we always enjoy our stay at the Phoenician, our one night "birthday" visit was over the top.  We enjoyed a beautiful room and our dinner at El Terrazo could not have been better.  It was hard to choose from the great menu described so well by Al, the best waiter ever.  Overwhelmed by the amazing wine list Greg was able to discern our preferences from a few weak descriptions on our part and brought us the perfect choice.  The food was perfectly prepared and presented with perfection.  The "special order" of the birthday dessert our daughter had requested exceeded all our expectations.  It's a birthday we will never forget at the most beautiful and friendly resort in Arizona.

reviews.author: Jaysolo
reviews.title: Total Luxury
reviews.text: I truly enjoyed my stay at the Phoenician. Me and my wife were treated like royalty by all the staff! The resorts 9 pools are a thing of beauty. I have never seen a more luxurious grounds! The food was awesome as well from breakfast to lunch and dinner even the pool side food was incredible! Our room was cleaned thoroughly twice a day! I would highly recommend this property to anyone! We can't wait to go back! If u stay at this resort I promise you will love it, make sure you say hi to our favorite pool side waiter Jarred!

reviews.author: Sylvain P
reviews.title: Oasis in the desert
reviews.text:
This was day 3 of a roundtrip from L.A. to San Francisco. We spent one night at the resort, stayed at the Phoenician on our wayfrom L.A. to the Grand Canyon.
The resort is remarkable, in its size as in its quality. Very inexpensive (at least in August) and of top quality (service and rooms).
Some drawbacks: 
The pool area was fine, the pool being almost unusable to swim or to cool off as it was hot like a bath and rather shallow (1.15 m). Temperature around Phoenix was about 43C.
If you want to eat at J&G Steakhouse, be prepared to let some money there. While my Angus steak was delicious, the so-called handcut fries were no thrill - don't take them, they are no better than those at some fastfood restaurants. We found this restaurant to be highly overpriced - if price matters.
Breakfast at "The Terrazzo" was excellent (to coffee fans:U.S. Standard i.e. Easy refills of brewed coffee, no Italian style coffee machine with delicious crema)

reviews.author: FrankP62
reviews.title: Another great visit
reviews.text:
Great visit once again to The Phoenician. This time we stayed at the Canyon in a suite. As usual the  staff are brilliant right across the Hotel. Nothing is too much and any requests were dealt with swiftly and professionally. Julian in the Canyon was the total professional. Bar staff are first class, particularly Andrew in the Relish Bar and Beradine and Debs in Il Terrazzo. Cleaning is first class and food in Il Terrazzo was top notch, again superb service by Christine. The guys who run you around Dillon and Damian were once again first class. If it seems there's a lot of names in this review then that's how much an impression they made on us. Great Hotel , brilliant staff.
Frank Price

reviews.author: Evan K
reviews.title: Luxury that doesn't disappoint - this is where you go to spoil yourself!
reviews.text:
The phoenician is impressive from the moment you turn off Camelback Road. We stayed, as a family, in the low season (August) and it was a fantastic experience. 9 pools to explore and a water slide that was great for the kids, but fun enough for the supervising adults as well. Lounging by the pool is fantastic as well with such good food/drink service. 

Overall the property is stunning and provided us with a great family 'getaway' where we could easily spend all day lounging around. If you can, get a pool-view room - the view is fantastic and the balcony is a great place to have coffee/read the paper. Rooms are very spacious but unfortunately all we could get was two over-sized doubles (we were told they don't have two queens) which for two adults is kind of tight. One big downside was that there wasn't a small fridge to keep our own drinks, and to get ice you have to call for room service. Great cactus garden to explore, and the gym is one of the best I've ever visited within a hotel/resort. We also enjoyed the option of the complementary self parking lot which was underground and nice for avoiding the summer sun.

Lots of food choices within the resort, though none are inexpensive, but the locations are perfect, especially at The Thirsty Camel - a great spot for snacks and drinks in the evening.

Close to really good shopping and a great choice of restaurants and only 2.5 hours away from Sedona. It's expensive for a family vacation, but if you choose your food carefully, you can definitely make it work!

reviews.author: LA_Girl
reviews.title: Excellent Time, Excellent Resort
reviews.text:
We stayed in March during spring training.  We were upgraded to a casita.  

This resort is amazing and the staff wonderful.  They bend over backwards to make you happy.  Wish we had been able to stay more than three nights.  

Spent lots of time in the gorgeous hot tub at night gazing at the stars.

reviews.author: Franziska R
reviews.title: 5 Star - we would give 7 Stars!
reviews.text: We stayed in The Phoenician with our 3 children and enjoyed every minute! The friendly staff helped wherever they could. Fresh good water served as soon the previous bottle was empty, the clean pools, waterside - just great! Little rabbits to come for a morning greet next to our patio made us having a great start of the day. High tea was on highest level, the staff just as friendly as we always dream of! The cactus Garden locaded on the resort ist beautiful, so are our rooms. Big, clean, wonderful! We agree with all previous rates with 5 Stars!

reviews.author: TableOf5
reviews.title: Pretty good!
reviews.text:
We LOVE traveling and admittedly, tend to choose the nicest hotels available.  We've always heard great thing about Phoenician so on our Scottsdale/Phoenix leg of trip we had to check it out!
So as not to be to wordy I'll give my bullet points:
PROS:
-great service
-good location
-family loved cactus garden
-good food
-liked coffee/ice cream shop
-fun pool{s}

CONS:
-felt seriously outdated
-not so great service in lobby area bar
-never once were told or heard about a possible kids' club?

It was really good! Not amazing, but not even remotely bad or anything.  I think we just had very high expectations and I taken aback slightly by the outdated decor and design.
I will say that we found the staff inside and out to be very hospitable.
I am sad to have left something behind in the room and the hotel did not come across it.
It was not a small item so it's not easily lost, it was definitely left behind, so that was disappointing :(

reviews.author: Alex L
reviews.title: Casita Bliss
reviews.text: Wonderful and spectacular resort. We were upgraded into a Casita and had Town Car service to the main building. Property is emmaculate and beautiful. Paticularily enjoyed the gardens behind the main building and the large outdoor swimming pool.

reviews.author: tcty
reviews.title: 5 Star hotel with great amenities
reviews.text:
We stayed in The Phoenician with our two children and it was a great experience.  Spacious rooms, friendly staff and good restaurants.  The best part for our kids is the pool.  It was a pleasant surprise to find a water slide feature in the pool, our younger one spent hours on the slide while we relaxed by the main pool.  

Rooms are quite large, however top floor (4th) one side faces a roof like structure, so it possible ask if there is a room facing the other side.  Otherwise it was a great stay and we will be back.

reviews.author: Lolaco6
reviews.title: Hotel de grand standing, luxe, grande chambre, SDB luxe, grand et beau parc, plusieurs piscines, fitness, ideal pour passer une
reviews.text:
Oasis de luxe et confort. Chambre spacieuse, grande Salle de bain. Plusieurs restaurants. Plusieurs piscines. Très beau parc. Salle de Fitness . 
Clime trop forte.
Bonne étape avant Grand Canyon.
Qualité de service.

reviews.author: vicky s
reviews.title: The best ever!
reviews.text:
We were immediately given an upgrade to a fantastic suite! You could have fit our house in one of the bathrooms and we had 3 amazing  balconies.
Staff were SO attentive, food matched everything else and was beautifully prepared. Lovely pools area, spa etc. usual fab but expensive shops within the hotel.
Best hotel I have ever stayed in!

reviews.author: 3Canons
reviews.title: Not as nice as I expected
reviews.text:
My husband, seven year old and I stopped at the Phoenician on our way to the Grand Canyon.  We were looking forward to a couple days of R&R.  The property itself is beautiful, but we were greatly disappointed in the rooms, which are in great need of updating.  The service was just ok, I never felt that any of the staff went above and beyond to make us comfortable.  As far as value for your money, the food and drinks were obscenely expensive.  We had a simple breakfast at their coffee shop and it was over $40.  During the summer months the pool closes early, so be prepared to hunt down towels and make a long walk to the main restauarant to get a poolside cocktail.  
The hotel's fine dining restaurant Il Terrazo was fine, the waitstaff was friendly, but a little slow and forgetful.  
The aspects that we liked about The Phoenician was the huge pool (aside from the non-existent service), the Concierge was extremely knowledgeable and Relish restaurant was a good casual option.  Our son particularly enjoyed the tabletop S'mores.

reviews.author: gitch69
reviews.title: Wonderful Staff
reviews.text: From the moment I entered the lobby, the service was wonderful! I did not seen a frowning face anywhere in the hotel. My room was large, clean and comfortable. Loved having a choice of different restaurants within the hotel!

reviews.author: ChicagoGirl017
reviews.title: Very Good, but not a 5 Star Experience
reviews.text:
I would rank our stay at The Phoenician between 3.5 and 4 Stars...

Let me start by saying that I had every intention of staying at the Hyatt Gainey Ranch for this trip, because I am a Gold member and had points to spend. However, this summer, the Hyatt was renovating their entire pool complex and that was not just not an option for my family. I thought that The Phoenician would be a similar stay in that both properties had the same kinds of amenities and the Casita option. 

Thus, my family reserved two Grand Deluxe Casitas on the first floor. I really enjoyed the patio and since we had our dog, the ground floor was very convenient for potty breaks. The grounds of this resort are extremely vast and beautiful. Between the Koi ponds and the Orchid gardens, and the backdrop of Camelback mountain, you are literally looking at beautiful views all day long. 

What I really liked about my stay:

- The check-in process was easy
- Excellent grounds and fitness facility
- Casita parking right outside the building
- Thirsty Camel Lounge and Patio
- Relish Burger Bistro
- Complimentary pitchers of ice water at the pools
- The Cactus Garden
- Turn-down service (but housekeeping sometimes arrived too early in the a.m.)
- Complimentary late check out

Why I was disappointed:

And, let me just say, that when I stay at a 5 star property, I expect near perfection-

- The Food was ridiculously expensive. We were lucky because we had a car and could go off the property. The resort will not let you deliver ANY food in. I am also sick of 5 star properties saying that they are in line with other 5 star properties in regards to their food cost!  Instead of following along, Be innovative and offer a more economical option. It should not cost $7 for a bagel!

-  I really disliked the location of our casitas. We were traveling as a family, but not with young children. Our back patios were literally at the base of the children's waterslide. This was not peaceful or relaxing and with our dog, it was very stressful at times. It was not the kind of trip we were anticipating. When I expressed my concerns about the location, I ran into an employee at the front desk who was not helpful and seemed to care less. I was not offered a change of location or venue.

- Finally, my family was visiting partly to reunite with some family in the Phoenix are and partly to celebrate my parents 37th wedding anniversary. Reservations was aware of this fact. Sadly, during our entire stay, nobody wished them a "Happy Anniversay", offered a complimentary drink, or meal or a even a special gesture...at all. I was VERY surprised that we were not offered a complimentary upgrade at check-in, considering that the property was only at 1/3 capacity ( we learned this from an employee). It saddened me to read a recent review concerning a family's stay at the Four Seasons Troon North and ALL of the complimentary, special things the resort did for this man's wife's birthday. We were not acknowledged at all. We didn't feel special at all, and honestly the stay was just not that memorable.

I know what that feeling is like, when you feel like you are the only guest because of how well you are treated and taken care of. I have stayed at these resorts before. However, I did not feel this way at The Phoenician. 

For those visiting, I would suggest at some point staying in Sedona, because it is so unique and the shopping, spas and tours (to me) are way more special than plain-old Scottsdale. 

Then, I would suggest, that if you are looking for that 5 star treatment, either splurge and stay at The Canyon Suites, or stay at The Four Seasons Troon North. This is what I plan on doing next time. There must be reasons why a 5 star property like The Phoenician is only #12 on Trip Advisor, and I think those extra above and beyond moments that were lacking during my trip are the reasons why.

reviews.author: Joeysdoll
reviews.title: Taste of Luxury
reviews.text:
My husband took me to the resort for my birthday weekend. We found the service exceptionally attentive from the Front Desk check-in to checkout. Standouts were the well-appointed room (large bath with marbled double sinks, huge shower and spa tub) evening turn down service. We came in from dinner to find the bath tidied, radio playing KBAQ softly, and chocolate on the pillows.  The carpeting in the room unfortunately was showing its age and badly needed shampooing. 
One thing stood out as unacceptable for a luxury resort. The lanai was filthy. Bird droppings coated the lounge and chair cushions while dirt encrusted the table. Leaves and dirt strewed the patio. We didn't use it the entire stay. Disappointing. 
The resort itself has stunning views of Camelback Mountain, especially from the pools. We spent part of the afternoon lounging by the hot tub which was lovely. The myraid lounges strewn around could have used a good cleaning, however. 
All in all, we greatly enjoyed our stay.

reviews.author: amesaur
reviews.title: Gorgeous Hotel
reviews.text: The property was very well maintained and immaculate. The rooms were beautiful and very clean. Turn down service as well. The burger restaurant was really good and service throughout the resort was very good. The pools were all very nice and there was plenty of room. The small tents that you could rent for a day by the pool were really nice and if you were with the family or a larger group it would be nice to do for a day. We really enjoyed our stay here, would go back again and definitely recommend it, Great spa as well!

reviews.author: Amadroid
reviews.title: Nice, but not great.
reviews.text: My wife were eargerly anticipating staying at the Phoenician, our first time, to celebrate our anniversary. The amenities were excellent. Dinner was wonderful at the steakhouse, over the top. The room was not as clean as it should have been. Food pieces in the corners and stains on a rug that should be replaced. Bed was comfortable, barhroom was spacious and clean. Patio furniture was very dusty, could not enjoy it. Rented a cabana, it was like day in paradise. Sam attended to our needs and was excellent. My wife and enjoyed the spa and meditation room very much. Be forewarned if you use a debit card for incedentals. Holds will be placed on the card making the funds unavailable, and they will make you wait up to a week for the funds to be available again even though they were paid in full. They could of fixed this, but chose not to. Because of this we will not return.

reviews.author: Will M
reviews.title: Amazing place to stay
reviews.text:
Yep, she's been around a while and some might argue that the decor is dated but this is one classy resort and customer service is top notch. I was here on business for a convention being held at the resort and everything was excellent - food, beverage, staff, etc. I don't have one thing to complain about. This is definitely a 5-star resort and if you ever have the opportunity to stay here you'll appreciate it.

By the way, staff gratuity was included as part of my conference fees and not once was I asked for extra money. I tipped a little a couple of times for hauling my heavy suitcase up a flight of stairs but it was nice to know that all of the staff had been briefed to not expect tips from conference attendees.

Bottom line - this is an amazing place to stay!

reviews.author: Molliebclyde
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: First impressions were not good. Took more than one hour to get checked in due to the understaffed front desk, the lock on one of our rooms was malfunctioning and the front desk clerk was woefully undertrained to correct the problem.  Lots of apologies, but nothing else. And that was my feeling with other problems with the stay: people falling all over themselves to apologize, but problems at an alleged five-star resort shouldn't happen to begin with. Honestly, the operation felt like amateur hour.  Inadequate staffing persisted in the restaurants and pool.  And when staff did appear they were more often than not indifferent. This, combined with the torn and stained carpets, damaged furniture, non-functioning telephones, room service trays left in the hall for entire days, dated furnishings ... no, this is not a five-star resort.  The J&G Steakhouse onsite is adequate, but not spectacular.

reviews.author: spartanchick1
reviews.title: Scottsdale for Business
reviews.text:
I stayed at The Phoenician for almost a week recently for a large conference. What really impressed me (and it takes a lot...i work in the industry) was the level of service from staff. No matter what I asked for, they delivered...and with a smile no less. I didn't have an opportunity to eat in the restaurants - all meals were within the conference area facilities - but i wasn't impressed with the food i did have. I had a standard guestroom, which was nice but nothing out of the ordinary for a luxury hotel. Spotless though, and had a very large balcony. 

It wasn't until the last day that I actually got to see the property unfortunately. The grounds are gorgeous. This must be an incredible vacation destination. I did have a spa treatment before going home though and it was to die for.

reviews.author: Lisa Y
reviews.title: Beautiful location, highly-cared for property and accommodating staff.
reviews.text:
This is definitely a top-notch resort.  Most of the staff are wonderful (see exception below), the accommodations are luxurious, and the grounds are well-maintained.   

Because the hotel was relatively empty (afterall it was summer in Arizona), the front desk upgraded us to a beautiful suite -- with three terraces, a living room and a large bedroom.  (I must add that we are Starwood Gold members.)  

The gym was super nice.  I am a high-maintenance exercise nut.  Not only were the lifecycles, treadmills and ellipticals in good shape but the gym had wonderful supplementary equipment like a bosu ball, weights, weighted bars and so on.  And, of course, there were plenty of headphones, bottled water and a beautiful view of Camelback Mountain. 

The pool area was also quite nice and very, very large.  In fact, there were five pools, including one for adults only, a basketball  and volleyball area, and a slide.  Chairs were plentiful, and fountains and foot bridges were situated on the way from one pool to the next.  Also, there was a dedicated pool person who organized games for kids, young adults and older adults with lots of energy each day.  The only negative in our whole experience was that the pool attendants did no attending.  Given that there were only a handful of guests on the property, it was difficult for us to get poolside meal service or towel service.   Go figure.  Hence, I gave the hotel a 4 instead of a 5.

Next, we only ate lunch on the property.  There are too many good restaurants in Scottsdale to stay on the premises.  Our son has severe food allergies and the lunch staff was very good about preparing safe food.  In fact, the hotel's main kitchen has a dedicated space for preparing food for guests with allergies.  We really appreciated the establishment's sensitivity to the food allergy issue.

Finally, I developed an eye condition on the trip that required the constant application of heat compresses.  Housekeeping looked in storage for a new machine, couldn't find one and brought me up one they had meticulously cleaned so I could use it to heat up washcloths for my eye.  The hotel did not charge us for the microwave -- nice touch.

I would not hesitate to stay here again.

reviews.author: Suzy_Shopper
reviews.title: Great place to relax!  Just what we needed!
reviews.text:
I booked two days at the Phoenician and we all really enjoyed ourselves.  We stayed at the Casitas and had a lovely room with a patio outside.  The bathroom was ginormous, we all could have camped out in there it was so big!  Two sinks, a lovely shower, big walk in closet, a bathroom and a huge tub!  

The pools were OK -- a little dated.  Staff was nice and friendly and overall we had a very nice time.  The golf course restaurant was very good and they have amazing burgers and scrumptious margaritas.  I think that was the best part of the whole stay!

reviews.author: Aurora
reviews.title: Will stay again
reviews.text:
My sister and i were here in July of 2011 for a conference, we didn't stay here, we had to stay down the road at the Camelback but we spent the majority of our time here. We loved the grounds, we loved the employees, and we wished we could have stayed here. We were welcomed as guests even though technically we were visitors. We were allowed to use the pool and all amenities. We are going to the same conference next summer and will make sure we book here early enough so we can stay. I think it's one of the most beautiful places I've stayed and the backdrop of the mountains sure does help!

We did NOT eat here though, we were lucky enough to have a car which is a luxury nobody else had so we heard that everyone at the conference paid through their nose for food and drinks. We did order one drink and it was pricey! Just so you know if you eat there you will be paying alot for it!

reviews.author: pieLansing
reviews.title: All around five star resort.
reviews.text:
This resort is wonderful. I was so relaxed staying there.  The rooms are very spacious, bathroom are large, safe in the closet. The beds are very comfortable. I love the Keurig coffee machine, and to enjoy it relaxing on the patio looking at Camelback Mountain is great.  The pool area is huge, we didn't have trouble getting chairs.  They bring you nice thick towels and pitchers of ice cold water.  The food at the pool was good and not over priced.   The staff was very friendly and helpful.  The evening turn down was nice.  To go into our room and have the lights dimmed, music on and Belgium chocolates on our pillows was a nice touch.  I highly recommend the 
Phoenician.

reviews.author: jen1555
reviews.title: Beautiful resort
reviews.text:
A group of us stayed in casitas at this beautiful resort. The rooms were lovely and the bathrooms were spacious. There was a large walk-in closet. Unfortunately, in my room, it was in the corner by one of the very comfortable beds and it was difficult to get into it. In other rooms, the closet is inside the bathroom.

The bathroom had 2 sinks, a large  walk-in shower with a ledge for sitting, a beautiful separate tub, and a separate room with the toilet and a bidet. There were plenty of towels and amenities.

The patio was a great place to sit in the morning with a cup of coffee from the in-room Keurig coffee maker. I enjoyed the privacy of my patio versus the patios on the other side which have a view of the pool.

The amenities in the room are first class. There was even an umbrella for those few days when it rains in Phoenix. Valet parking is pricey at $29/night but there was free parking at the casitas.
The food was excellent but the menus didn't include enough lighter fare such as salads. The drinks are very pricey. $16 for margaritas/cosmos and $11 for Bombay/tonic.

We rented a cabana by the pool. The staff was very attentive and we had our own mini-fridge stocked with water, Red Bull, and vitamin water as well as fresh fruit in the morning and yummy brownies in the afternoon. There was even live music because of the holiday weekend.

The grounds are gorgeous and the way the hotel is situated against Camelback Mountain is impressive. I was even able to do some birding from my patio. 

The staff was very friendly and accommodating for the most part. The front desk seemed a little confused at times but it was a holiday weekend. Some of our rooms were not ready until very late but once we were all situated in our rooms, everything was lovely.

reviews.author: nthirion
reviews.title: Old grand lady
reviews.text:
We stayed a few nights for business.

The service was ok but the rooms are old. Everything was very clean but it caters for a statesmen  of the 80's type person. The place is very big and does not have personal feel.

I didn't play golf during the visit and perhaps that would have made me more favorable. If the hotel had no golf course it would have suffered for it.

reviews.author: Tony155019
reviews.title: Ultimate comfort and service!
reviews.text: Attended a corporate sponsored event. From the moment I arrived I was treated with the utmost courtesy and professionalism. Every staff member I engaged with was friendly and extremely helpful. The room was spotless. The bed and pillows were beyond comfortable. I would come back in the evenings to a turned down bed with chocolates, curtains drawn, lights dimmed and music playing. The entire resort is a paradise. The three tiered pool with its waterslide and poolside bar will satisfy young and old. The Spa has a well-equipped gym and a fantastic eucalyptus steam room, among other amenities. The golf course is scenic, challenging and a real treat to play. The Phoenician definitely lives up to its’ Five Star, Triple A rating! I would come back in a heartbeat.

reviews.author: COSharps
reviews.title: Oasis in the desert
reviews.text: I was lucky enough to stay at the Phoenician for a conference two weeks ago. It's a beautiful and classy resort that is also family-friendly. The cost of drinks, snacks, and meals on site was prohibitive for many attendees, but with a rental car or cab there are literally dozens of great places to eat within a five-minute drive. The adults-only pool (tiled in mother of pearl) was beautiful and relaxing, and the water slide seemed to be a big hit with the kids. I spent a lot of time laying out on the huge shaded balcony enjoying the peace, quiet, and beautiful scenery. The beds are comfortable and my bathroom included a sunken bathtub as well as a walk-in shower. It was a treat to stay there and should I find myself back in the area, you can bet I'll be booking The Phoenician again!

reviews.author: Onesweetlife
reviews.title: Underwhelming and pricey
reviews.text: We booked a weekend here with some friends and planned to be poolside soaking up the sun.  Upon check in the front desk advised they upgraded our view which was nice.  Well, the view was of the roof.  So much for an upgrade.  On the way to the room there was a lot of construction going on in the hallway, with electrical cords that we almost tripped over and ladders we had to manuever around.  The room was clean, however, needs to be updated, it is no longer 1985.  The following morning we exited our room to be greeted by more construction and freshly painted walls.  It seemed as if with a resort this size they could have closed this hallway down for the work to be done and placed us in a wing where there was no work going on.  In spite of this, we did have a great time at the Mother of Pearl pool where we rented a cabana for two days.  The service was impeccable.  The menu was a disappointment, however.  Everything was very expensive...our cabana bill including food and beverage for two days was $1,500.00 - there were four of us.  There are several restaurants on the property - we loved Relish - the burger bistro.  Great food, reasonable prices and good service.  Would we return?  Probably...but only because we had such a great time pool side, not for the rooms.

reviews.author: tracyh2437
reviews.title: The Phoenician
reviews.text: My family of four, with two young children, stayed at the Phoenician for 3 nights in May 2011.  The Hotel was everything we saw on the website.  There were many lovely restaurants, great pools, the staff was friendly and professional.  We thought the rooms were excellent, with large spaces and big bathrooms.  The balconies were a nice extra space.  There were multiple pools with a minor waterslide for the kids.  Everywhere we went in this hotel, it was just stunning.   The hotel backs onto cambelback mountain which is amazing to see the raw scenery so close.  We would go back anytime...

reviews.author: Pickyman
reviews.title: Easy going, luxurious resort nestled against Camelback Mountain
reviews.text: This neutral-toned, 'un-stuffy' resort is 5 star all the way.  Spacious grounds, fronted by 27 fabulous golf holes and backed by a superb Cactus garden to stroll along right up against  Camelback Mountain. Pools are great, and towels are brought before you can even ask for them.  For family stays, choose either the luxurious suites in a private wing (2 bedroom suites link for large groups) or stay in the charming, 8 unit casitas if you have a car because you park it right outside your door, yet you share all amenities and the pools are right out from your patio or balcony.  Throughout the resort there are tasteful works of art, sculptures and genuine fossil artifacts with tastefully stocked shops offering beautiful southwestern items.  Restaurants are excellent and there are tons more within a short drive.  You're 20 minutes from the airport and 5 minutes from the huge Scottsdale shopping mall. My first time in Arizona.  I was impressed.

reviews.author: Mr_and_Mrs_K_TN
reviews.title: Great stay!
reviews.text: The Phoenician hosted a work-related conference, but the environment is excellent for a vacation. In fact, many attendees brought the family as the environment is so peaceful it felt more like a vacation than work!  From the moment of checking in, we were surrounded by travel and leisure professionals.  Food items are expensive, but there is a Safeway down the street and they do not mind guests bringing in bottled water to stash in the mini fridge.  Your stay comes with daily clean up and turn down services, and we were surprised to find wonderful Replenish amenities.  When the airlines lost luggage, the hotel made up for it in complementary supplies.  Views are great even if located over the roof.  Do ask NOT to be placed on the first level as those views are non-existent.  I cannot wait to visit again!

reviews.author: ccmac
reviews.title: Fabulous time!
reviews.text:
My husband, 16-year-old son, and I just returned from our 10 day Southwest adventure, and chose to spend our last two nights at The Phoenician.  We had such a wonderful time there!  The property is gorgeous, and the service first-class.  We began relaxing the moment we entered the beautiful marble lobby.  The colors were soothing and the artwork complimented the space.  Their front desk staff was pleasant and accommodating.  

Our room was a "two double" in the main building overlooking the pool.  It was quite large, decorated nicely, with a large, lovely bathroom!  We did feel the beds were small, especially for my 6'6" husband & myself in one bed, but the mattress and bedding was quite comfortable.  I enjoyed sitting in the lounge chair on the large balcony overlooking the pool, and strolling the property.  (Yes, it was hot, but mornings and evenings were pleasant, and our balcony was mostly shaded, so very nice to sit out there and gaze at the beautiful surroundings.)

The grounds and pools are just beautiful and manicured so nicely.  As we explored on our first afternoon, we discovered the pool bar.  Special "thanks" to Steve, the bartender, who quickly got us in "vacation" mode with conversation and a couple of delicious drinks.  

We had dinner at Relish, the more casual restaurant by the golf course, and the burgers were so yummy!  Our full-day there was spent at the pool, mostly the mother-of-pearl pool, then venturing to the pool on the next level up.  The pool loungers were very comfortable, with deep cushions.  Towels (in-room and at the pool) were thick and large. 

Overall, our stay was wonderful, and we would definitely stay again if visiting the Phoenix area.

reviews.author: aglama
reviews.title: What a Resort!
reviews.text: Would love to spend a long weekend as a couple at this resort. Has it all, ambience, amenities, golf spa, and a great pool area.

reviews.author: Rhoda07
reviews.title: Luxury hotel with your well-being experience satisfied
reviews.text: Just returned from a 5 night wonderful tradeshow/conference at the Phoenician in Scottsdale, AZ. We had a very nice room on the end that was large and spread out with a huge patio. It was a little walk to our room but didn't mind it after eating all of the wonderful food. Prices a little high with wine 10.00, drinks 12.00 and food starting at 16.00-but everything was great!  Enjoyed the spa and fitness center and they flowed nicely together in the buildings.  I also enjoyed a meditation session with Cindy-she was awesome!  The conference rooms were a bit cooler than need be even with my layered shirts and blazer-I was chilled.  The birds at the outside restaurant were enjoying the cream left on tables from other guests, that was not the most appetizing-but what you do-we were outside. Thank you for a top notch AZ Starwood hotel

reviews.author: Michelle-OdysseyTrvl
reviews.title: Perfect in Phoenix
reviews.text:
I had the opportunity to stay at the Phoenician for 6 nights this past June and it truly took my breath away.  

Talk about a 5 star without feeling pretentious!  Upon check in, I had the pleasure of meeting Kelly.  She made the check in process totally seemless! In addition, during our brief chat, I mentioned that whatever room I was being assigned to, I'd appreciate a nice view if at all possible.  Let me tell you, she did not disappoint and actually shocked me. Take a peek at picture and you'll know why. Thoughout my stay, and anytime I walked by the main registration desk, she always had a smile on her face and asked how everything was.  

Then at the Bell Desk, we encountered Charles, who was kind enough to take us to our room via golf cart. Again, another very approachable person willing to tell you anything you wanted to know about the area and resort. Then once to the room, promptly brought the luggage in, got everything setup, showed us key room features and make sure we had fresh ice.  As he left, he mentioned if we ever just wanted a ride back up to the main entrance (instead of the 3 minute walk), to just give them a call.  

The only item in the room that I would like changed would be the shutters in the bathroom.  Being on first floor, would have preferred something with a little more privacy. Other than that, cannot complain about anything.  BTW, I stayed in Casita 7182 w/ two oversize double beds, walk in closet, full bathrooms, with sitting area in shower, separate soaking tub, double vanity, private toilet and bidet.  

Pool area is an oasis within itself, guess that is why the bar/restaurant area is called the oasis.  The staff at the pool are extremely attentive as well.  Lunch and drinks served pool size are large portions, nice value for the money.  The best part the pool is open 24 hours, so a late night swim isn't out of the question and is very relaxing before heading to bed.

I didn't have a chance to golf on this trip, but those that did said they enjoyed the course very much.  I'm personally going to make a point of visiting this property again for a true vacation, as it made it's mark on me!

reviews.author: Brian T
reviews.title: A first-rate resort conveniently located in Scottsdale
reviews.text: We stayed here for a week with my two teenage kids and loved it.  We were here in June which made it triple-digit hot for an east coast person, but it was manageable (a dry heat…LOL).  The amenities and personal service are as-described in the literature, but beyond what’s published I would add that the Phoenician’s is ideally located in Scottsdale on the northeast side of town.  There are many great restaurants, shopping, and theaters within a few minutes’ drive.  Furthermore, it was convenient to slip out to the Superstition Mountains, Canyon Lake, and Camelback Mountain.  The Mediterranean wrap at the Oasis (pool side) was great for lunch.  We did dinner at Relish’s Burger Bistro which is also a great value…in a place where you can really drop some coin.

reviews.author: John E
reviews.title: great day for pampering
reviews.text: bought a spa facial for myself and my wife, which included unrestricted access to all spa facilities and pool.   The attention to detail is always welcome (I had been an employee in the early 90's).  We experienced the work out center,  received the facial (it says something when most employees have been there for 20+ years!), loved the included Tarot reading, jumped into the jacuzzi, sauna, and steam rooms,  coupled with my wife for a meditation class, then headed to poolside for totally wonderful get away day here in town.   The views of Camelback Mountain, the sculpted landscaping,  delicious sandwich off the pooside menu- quite a day which we plan to take advantage of soon again.

reviews.author: Faulkner8251
reviews.title: A WOnderful Resort
reviews.text: First and foremost.. the service was amazing. We had a room in the Canyon Suites which was spacious, beautiful and very well appointed. But most of all the Service was the best that I have seen. Lora at the Suites area was one of the most gracious, informed and professional hotel employees in the industry.  This hotel is posh, but comfortable, quiet but moving. The brunch was also amazing. Food again was great but the service was spectacular.Christine our server went out of her way to pamper my 83 year old dad. I also noticed other server operating in the same matter. Overall this was a wonderful experience.

reviews.author: emrtravel
reviews.title: Stunning resort with the highest standard of service
reviews.text:
I have been visiting the Phoenician for more than a decade, whenever I visited the area. This is one of the most stunning resorts in the world. The grounds are immaculately landscaped and cared for. There is not a weed in sight. The resort sits at the base of Camelback Mountain in Scottsdale, Arizona, a resort city adjoining Phoenix, Arizona, that has more than 30 four and five star resorts. Anyone can build a luxury hotel, but the thing that makes this resort stand out is that the impeccable service is consistent. No matter when you visit, whether high season or low, whether you arrive draped in fur or in shorts and sneakers, the staff will treat you as if you are a VIP. 

On one occasion, my husband and I brought my mother and father and on the second day my mother was not feeling well. She had caught the flu or a cold on the flight in. When my father showed up in the dining room for breakfast alone, the waiter asked if his wife would be joining him. He explained that she wasn't feeling well. A short while later, while he was still eating breakfast, room service arrived with complimentary home made chicken soup, a pot of tea and biscuits, and bottled water (with a rose in a vase) for my mother. 

Rooms: In the main building, rooms are quite large (around 600 s.f.) and look out over the expansive grounds, including world famous golf course and a huge pool area. Standard rooms look at the mountain, but are otherwise the same. The mountain views can also be stunning. Camelback mountain is covered with saguaro cacti and at night spotlights illuminate the mountain and the scenery is breathtaking.  Bathrooms are large with oversized tubs (some have jacuzzis), showers, marble floors and vanities, and are stocked with more than the usual amount of amenties. Towels are large and fluffy. Rooms include luxurious bathrobes. There are flat screen televisions and a sitting area alongside the bed and on the patio/balconies. 

The Canyon Suites are a separate all suite resort within a resort area east of the main building. They have their own drive up area, concierge, and pool area similar to the signature swan pool on the main grounds. 

The Phoenician Residences are two and three bedroom villas, some with their own swimming pools, garages and golf carts. 

Dining: Food is outstanding but expensive. Il Terrazo serves Italian American fare. World famous chef Jean George Vongerichten's J & G Steakhouse sits at the top of the resorts' main building overlooking the grounds. Room service food appears to be the same as what can be ordered at Il Terrazo, but note that there is an automatic delivery fee that is more than 20%. Relish Burger Bistro is available at the clubhouse and food can be ordered while in the spa and served in their juice bar area. 

Perhaps the best traditional afternoon tea in the area is served in the afternoons until 3pm. Reservations are highly recommended as this sells out. It is a very formal affair though most people dining wear resort casual dress (dress code applies in the building so no bathing suits).  

Private dining is available in the Praying Monk, an area that looks like a medieval wine cellar. I've never eaten there but the atmosphere is amazing. Limited seating (its a very tiny space). 

There is also an old fashioned ice cream parlor with indoor and outdoor seating on the grounds. 

Pools: Multiple pool areas including large upper area pools, lower area childrens pools include a 165 foot waterslide and the resort's signature pool, crafted of mother of pearl tile (an adult only area) surrounded by luxurious cabanas like you've never seen before: ceiling fans, tables, chairs, television, computer hook ups and wifi access, robes, fruit basket, and poolside dining. 

Sports: Championship golf course, tennis, hiking, tours, 20,000 s.f. spa (The Center for Well Being). 

Other activities: Cactus Garden, nearby dining and shopping at Fashion Square (a five minute drive east of the resort), and a world famous art collection worth more than $25 million dollars. Shops on the grounds include gift shops, jewelry store, women's clothing, and resort wear for both men and women. 

Note: There is a fee for valet parking and currently a resort fee of $29 per night that includes access to the fitness facilities and a number of other amenities. There is a kids club on the grounds with many activities and I can attest to the fact that this place is special. When my daughter was given a choice between going to an amusement park or the Funicians kids club for her birthday, she chose Funicians. Half days are around $45 and full days with lunch $75.

The experience at the Phoenician is outstanding but their peak season room pricing is extremely high. If possible try to come in the off season, when temperatures rise beginning in May and the prices drop from 50-75%.

reviews.author: xavi8
reviews.title: A proper luxury resort hotel
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is a full service luxury resort, that really looks like its brochures. It is a very efficient and slick operation, with exceptional customer service, and super friendly staff. From the point of arriving, you know you are somewhere special and far from the run-of-the-mill generic 'luxury' hotel. 

Stunning location and views over Camelback. Restaurants serve an eclectic range of tasty foods, and Sunday brunch is something only the American's can do properly, especially here. Plenty of sightseeing and shopping opportunities near by.

reviews.author: RUSSELL GUAJARDO
reviews.title: 5 star
reviews.text: This truly is the best of the best...every part of this stay was on point.. check in was fast and easy ..rooms were perfect size and upscale ...for me the best part was the pool , amazing...... You really get what you pay for ....

reviews.author: George9
reviews.title: Trail End
reviews.text:
We stayed on the taill end of our south western trip.
Besides the pool, not much you can do in the heat, as the temp outside was 111. 
Our 6 year old loved the water slide.
Food Very expensive.

reviews.author: DanaS213
reviews.title: Classy place
reviews.text:
I was there in mid June for a 5 day conference held at this hotel and conference centre. First impressions are very positive, and the Camelback Mountain backdrop is a unique aspect of the Phoenician. The lobby area really takes full advantage of the view, and the restaurants are beautifully designed. Room was large and nicely appointed. The free shoeshine service was a pleasant surprise. The pool areas were very well laid out, but the weather was too hot to spend much time there. Wonderful fitness centre.

The conference facilities are excellent and well designed for outdoor and indoor activities. I was somewhat disappointed with the food in the conference centre. Also the steak restaurant was not as great as I would have expected.

reviews.author: Ian M
reviews.title: Unaldulterated Luxury in the Arizona Sunshine
reviews.text: We spent a marvellous ten days in this luxurious resort and can't recommend it too highly. A spectacular setting immediately below Camel Back Mountain reveals a substantial property with large, comfortable rooms, good wines, beers and good food. Nine swimming pools to laze in, and as many sunbeds as you could possibly want.  You'll get first class service in the restaurants and by the pool(s).  The hotel and the grounds are immaculate and the rooms are spotlessly clean - good facilities and powerful showers. Scottsdale Old Town is only five minutes drive from the resort and there are plenty of shops and eateries all around.  If you can't be bothered leaving the hotel, spend a couple of hours in J G's Steakhouse on Thursday evenings for excellent Jazz and tasty bites, or - seven days a week - call in at the the Golf Clubhouse for burgers and beers with Happy Hour prices from until 6.00 pm.  Or simply laze on the terrace with a glass of chilled Pinot Grigio or a Pacifico beer to hand in the warmth of the setting sun and watch as a myriad of planes land into Phoenix Sky Harbor. Don't miss out on this amazing resort - this is our fourth visit and we'll be back next year.

reviews.author: Morgan621
reviews.title: Incredible Stay
reviews.text: To date, this is probably the best stay of my life anywhere.  My wife and I came for our honeymoon, and it met all of our expectations.  The property and rooms are beautiful, and customer service is fantastic.  The bellman who walked our luggage to the room was fantastic (late 20's, glasses), ate in all restaurants during our stay, never disappointing.  We met the Director of Operations at one point (his name escapes me) and he was very welcoming - as a guest I really appreciate when someone of that high level takes time to speak with guests, it says a lot about the property.  If I am in Phoenix again, I am staying here, no questions asked.

reviews.author: shnlewis
reviews.title: The Phoenician Does Not Live Up To Its 5 Stars
reviews.text:
We were recommended to The Phoenician by our travel agent as well as my sister-in-law who had stayed here a decade back.  

The Good:  Service is impeccable.  The staff knows and remembers you by name.  The hotel rooms are really quiet and sound proof.  The grounds of the hotel are absolutely stunning.  The spa, fitness center, etc are also really nice.  The beds are SUPER comfortable.  Great pool, great golf and great tennis.  Also, the fitness center offers Pilates:  YAY.

The Bad:  When youd rive up to the hotel, it is gorgeous.  Then you see the "standard rooms" which look nothing better than a Holiday Inn.  We paid for an upgraded Casita room and the hotel did upgrade us to a deluxe Casita room.  However, the room was nothing special.  Our room was outdated and no larger than a standard room.  We had a patched area in the ceiling that was never painted.  Their food was just OK, but extremely overpriced.  Their spa is beautiful until you look at their menu.  They wanted $300 for a 50 minute massage.  Absolutely overpriced so we went to a spa off the property, Spa Lamar, totally worth it.

All in all, I gave the hotel 4 stars b/c the grounds are gorgeous, the service is impeccable, but the food, drinks and spa are completely overpriced.  Don't waste your money on paying for an upgraded room because there is nothing "upgraded" about it.  Definitely worth trying this hotel out, just don't plan on this being an all-inclusive hotel once you arrive.

reviews.author: merwest
reviews.title: Honeymoon Stay and it was beyond expectations!
reviews.text: We are on a 18 day cross country honeymoon road trip and this was our first stop. Got a great AAA rate that included a resort credit.  Self park is free and valet is $29 and the self park is accessible by room elevator-very convenient so skip the cost.  There are 3 main levels of pools, great golf and tennis. Ate at all the restaurants-top notch. Loved the coffee bar by the shops (kind of hidden but was great for a grab and go). Il Terrazo was nice but over priced. The room was great-double upgraded with my starwood status and over looked the pool. Got a massage cert on Travelzoo.com for $220 worth of services for $99, so worth checking out. The rooms were spotless, comfortable and the bathroom was huge.  Was a great splurge!  They even treated us to complementary champagne upon arrival since they knew it was our honeymoon.

reviews.author: IslandGirl7373
reviews.title: Great place for families
reviews.text: We had a great stay but unfortuately for us, only one night.  We were headed to Sedona, the Grand Canyon and Monument Valley so we stayed here on our way out of Phoenix.  Our room was beautiful.  My 10 year old daughter said the bathroom was her favorite of any hotels she has stayed at.  The pool area was huge.  Pools, a water slide, a good sized hot tub...  And the night we were there, they had an outdoor movie for the kids and the "electric slide" with the slide lit up and open late.  Staff was incredibly pleasant.  Would love to go back for a longer stay.

reviews.author: katie2275
reviews.title: Not up to 5 stars
reviews.text:
The Bad: 
 - The room just felt out dated.  The wall paper was starting to peel.  The carpet was frayed.  The fake laminate from the dresser was pulled on the edge of the drawers.
 - The hallways and rooms smelled of very old wool.
 - Food at Il Terrazzo was terrible.  My husband's filet ($40+) was drenched in salt and way over cooked for medium (almost zero pink).  My monkfill picatta was also overcooked.
 - One day we had amazing service at the pool, the next day was awful.
 - The golf course is not in good shape.  My husband has played at the Phoenician two to three times a year for the past 5 years.  It is his favorite course of all time.  However, this is the worst shape he has ever seen it.
 -  Just not what you expect when paying for 5 stars. 

The Good:
 - Gorgeous manicured grounds
 - The pools were lovely.  With varying temperatures, which was nice.
 - There valet / bell boy / check in service was amazing.
 - The bed was very comfortable.
 - The bathroom was updated.  I would give it 4 stars, because for some reason there is an air conditioning vent in the shower.  Nothing like a cold breeze when damp.
 - The fitness center is very well appointed.  They have yoga classes, all the equipment you could need, water bottles, towels, and fresh fruit.  And a beauitful view.

The irritating:
 - I let my son pick out candy at the Ice cream shop.  The clerk has a nasty comment about letting my child eat too much candy. a.) it was not that much, and b.) he was sharing it with his dad.
 - Our female server at the pool would disappear and we couldn't get food / bill...
 - You cannot get your own ice.  You have to order through room service.  This means you are constantly tipping.

reviews.author: dmas6
reviews.title: Beautiful location and very close to Camelback Mountain!
reviews.text:
