I had an opportunity to stay at this location and absolutely loved this hotel. It has a very impressive pool with areas to practice your free throws or jump shots in the pool. The workout facility was very nice with modern machines and of course the massage was outstanding.I also enjoyed all meals that were served during my stay. I enjoyed the location as it is within walking distance of Camelback Mountain which is a local favorite for mountain climbing. (Well, mountain climbing for this city dude.) I would recommend that you climb with a friend just in case. 

I did not play golf at the time of my visit, but the golf course looked great. I would check other reviews on the golf course as I am not able to give you a perspective on how difficult it is from where I viewed the course.

Enjoy your trip and make sure you climb to the top of the mountain so you can say you were on top of the world!

reviews.author: Ben
reviews.title: A Grand Honeymoon
reviews.text: We spent the beginning of our honeymoon here at the Phoenician! We were pleasantly delighted to have been upgraded to a top floor suite with fresh chocolate strawberries in our room complimentary of the resort staff! I wish my wife and I could have stayed longer and will for sure be back shortly to enjoy more of the amenities that this beautiful resort has to offer. Thank you to everyone at the Phoenician for the kind words upon our arrival, from the gate keeper to the gardening staff waving at my fully decorated car on the way out. It was truly a grand experience!

reviews.author: AFisher926
reviews.title: Best nights sleep ever!!
reviews.text:
I have traveled extensively around the world and on occasion have stayed in some 5 star Michelin rated properties, but none has afforded me the most restful nights sleep I had  the last two nights while at your lovely Phoenician Resort.
The grounds were spectacular, my husband and I enjoyed walking them both mornings.  I could go on and on about your property, It truly was an all around classy resort, I can't wait to come back.

Afisher

reviews.author: angie54
reviews.title: you can't get better than this!
reviews.text:
Visited The Phoenician with my husband and two college aged sons.  It doesnt get better than this!  From the moment you enter the hotel with James as your "greeter" it is 5 star all the way.  I have never met a more pleasant staff where every answer to any question you ask is yes....There is nothing they will not do for you.
The grounds are magnificent and the rooms incredibly maintained.  Theres something for everyone.  Tennis, golf, beautiful pools and great restaurants in Phoenix and Scottsdale at night.
Yes, we went to two Major League Baseball Games and had phenomenal seats which we are not used to as Yankee fans!
Jacque and Michelle are top-notch concierges!
The only problem writing this rave review is that I want to go back next year and don't want to have a problem getting a room!!

reviews.author: acdhuber
reviews.title: Four, not five stars (maybe even three and a half)
reviews.text: I was excited to stay at the Phoenician because I had heard so many nice things about the resort. The grounds are very well manicured, and the lobby is very lovely, in an old-Phoenix kind of way. This is the type of resort that tries to block the desert, covering it with green lawn, as opposed to embracing the beauty of the desert. The grounds are gorgeous, but our room was really very dingy and quite dirty. The carpet was filthy, and the room could have used a fresh coat of paint. The room was a decent size, and the view of the pool with Camelback Mountain in the rear, was very nice. However, the bathroom was gross. The shower did not drain, leaving a pool of several inches of water every time we showered. Also, the ceiling of the shower was covered in mold -- just not a very nice experience at any star level of resort. The pool experience was a disaster. We often stay at area resorts over holiday weekends, so the crowds are not a problem. However, we had been assured that there would be an adults-only pool, free of children. Over the holiday weekend, that was not the case. At all. Every other five-star resort in the area manages to carve out a small section for those who seek an adults-only experience at the pool, even on busy holiday weekends. Not so the Phoenician. Despite the assurances of the reservation agent, there was absolutely no pool space reserved for adults. Very disappointing, especially given our experience at other local resorts of this caliber. Honestly, there are other resorts in the area that offer an experience much closer to five stars.

reviews.author: cynbyn
reviews.title: A four star
reviews.text: The Phoenician was not a five star, okay maybe it was ten - fifteen years ago but not anymore. Upon arrival the lobby had that old glamour feel to it, but I also couldn't tell if the carper had dirty scuffs or if that was just the color of it. The bedroom location was a trek - down a lobby, up an escalator, through an outside area back through another lobby. The room was standard for a four star. There was a spider on the headboard (Im not one for spiders but I can forgive them for this since the outdoor terrace was practically built into camelback mountain). However the carpet wasn't vaccumed or it was superficially. Down beside the bedside locker there was a lot of lint and fluff and general dirt. The outside bar was vey badly lit, we had to use the light from our phones to read the menu. On the first proper day here, we went down to the pool but it was full to capacity! There was staff on hand, helping people to set up sunlounger but they didnt come near us. They were pretenting to be busy. We had to lift our own sunloungers off a stack of extras that they had set up, We could see everyone had towels but again that was another trek back in through the pool area to get these. Once this was completed we got to relax. I think the staff could have had the surpluss sunloungers already set up for people. We did have dinner in the steakhouse restaurant, we ordered the Tasting Menu and it was DEVINE! The next day I saw the fitness center which is super modern and has everything you could wish for. We went for a walk around the grounds which are pretty extensive and maintained to a high standard. Overall the resort is lovely, service is hit and miss and the rooms are not five star.

reviews.author: JesseHenry
reviews.title: Great Resort
reviews.text:
We loved the Phoenician. The resort was lovely and the staff was superb.  The concierge desk helped us make some great dinner reservations. Excellent suggestions and so very friendly. Matt, the manager of the lounge off the lobby was so friendly and also had an excellent and friendly staff. The ice cream shoppe (which was so much more.  A great place for lunch or to pick up some muffins and coffee to bring back to your room for breakfast) also had such a warm and friendly staff.  The pool staff was also great and very accomodating. The rooms were very spacious with a nice patio area.  The place was spotless and the grounds were lovely.  The resort is looking a little tired in spots (i.e. our rug was a little old and worn) but everything else was so wonderful that you just overlooked that.  It was a great place to be...centrally located and just a lovely spot. We can't wait to return!  Oh, and my husband enjoyed the golf as well which was great as this was one of the main points of the trip.  He liked the golf course at the Phoenician and also enjoyed the other golf courses he played in the area (suggestions by the concierge). Only minor complaint was that we had to pay for internet which seemed a bit much given the cost of the resort!

We also loved the tours suggested by the staff. The Pink Jeep Tour and the Grand Canyon Tour was really fun.

All in all, it was a great trip.

reviews.author: docnroll
reviews.title: Always a Relaxing Luxurious place to stay
reviews.text: I have traveled three times to the Phoenician and always enjoy the beautifully displayed sculptures encorporated into their landscaping. Easy walk to to take a wonderful hike at Camelback and beautiful cactus garden on property. Will definitely return.,

reviews.author: MSlayton1013
reviews.title: Excellent service, great room
reviews.text:
My husband and I chose The Phoenician based on a great online deal and weren't disappointed. The hotel is very elegant throughout with the best service we have ever experienced. We had quick, early check-in with a room upgrade. The rooms are spacious with huge double vanity bathrooms and separate tub and showers. Each day you also get normal maid service and then turn down service in the evening where bottled water and chocolates are delivered to your room. 
The food at the Oasis pool grill is very good .... The mahi mahi and guacamole tray were our favorites. Service at the pool is also excellent. There is more than enough staff and they continually deliver pitchers of ice water thoughout the day to your chair.
We loved Relish Burger Bar....best burgers we have ever had and a great happy hour (the only happy hour in the hotel that we could find, so take advantage). Set on the golf course with tvs to watch the game....very attentive staff too. 
The hotel is also about one mile away from a great mall and restaurant area. We recommend taking a cab to the mall rather than the courtesy cars staffed by the hotel. A cab is about $8 while the courtesy car is a minimum of $13. We did use the courtesy car to return to the airport and prices were pretty equal to a cab. 
Overall, we had a great stay and vacation. The hotel was built in the 80s, so it is a bit dated but is in great condition and is kept up well.  It won't be as new as other resorts but still very nice and the rooms are updated it apeared  The only issues we ran into were spotty Internet service in the room and an issue with some of our tv stations not working. After our second complaint about the tv, they came and replaced the entire tv. We couldn't help but laugh at that but it fixed the issue! In addition, they compensated us with a free in room movie for the hassle.

reviews.author: Pat L
reviews.title: It Doesn't Get Any Better Than This!
reviews.text: This was my husband’s and my 4th stay at the Phoenician  Resort, Scottsdale, AZ and this time we brought 3 friends with us.  Each time we visit, it is more amazing than the last.  Staff is incredibly friendly and knowledgeable.  Just about the entire staff remembers and calls you by name. Sometimes, I have a hard time remembering my own!  To be greeted at breakfast with “Good Morning, Mr.& Mrs.____“ before we even reach the hostess station makes us feel so special.  It is  like they really appreciate our business and want us there.  Our room was more than lovely.  Large, and immaculate.  The huge bathroom was spotless.  Night service would remove any used towels, turn down your bed, put soft music on, fill the ice bucket, leave chocolates and the luxury of all, place a white  cloth on the floor on the sides of the bed so that when you got up in the middle of the night your feet were not on the rug but on the foot cloth. That, I had never experienced at any other hotel.  The grounds did not have a blade of grass out of place and the landscaping was beautifully done with waterfalls, pools, flowers, trees and ponds.  One day while pointing out the Desert Walk on the property, a bell boy, Manuel, saw us and asked us to get into the golf cart and took us on a tour of the entire grounds.  He had worked there for 16 years and was a wealth of information. The concierge staff was more than helpful, knowledgeable and very accommodating.  Would arrange any activity you desired. House keeping would come back after they cleaned the room and ask if everything was Ok.  If not, they would fix it.  The pools were warm and clean and the pool staff very attentive.  This time we witnessed the pool staff in action.....  9 baby ducks followed Mommy Duck into the pool.  Unfortunately, the babies did not know how to swim yet.  Babies were stuck in the pool when Mom flew out.  4 or 5 pool staff worked about 45 minutes to get the ducks out.  Mommy would not let them near the babies.  Finally, after getting them into a box, the staff said they would bring the ducks to the pond, just a few feet away.  Mommy would know where to find them.  Well, Mommy didn’t know  and was quite upset.  We finally had to leave and go back to our room, however, shortly after returning there, we received a call from the pool staff saying the ducks were united with their mother.  The staff knew how concerned we were and wanted to put our mind at ease that all was well.  I cannot imagine any other resort having as much concern for the ducks or their guests.  They certainly went above and beyond.  The Phoenician has a great location with lots to do in the Phoenix, Scottsdale and Tempe area. Sedona less than 2 hours away.   This is truly a First Class, 5 Star Resort, one you have to experience just once, but you’ll go back!

reviews.author: natalia64
reviews.title: Super relaxing atmosphere, great location
reviews.text: We stayed overnight at the Phoenician and loved it.  The beds are so comfortable, you don't want to get up in the morning!  The grounds are impeccable, it is so beautiful.  We are looking forward to a longer stay soon.  The location is great, too.  We saw a very friendly little jackrabbit taking a rest from the heat, which made a perfect welcome to our casita!

reviews.author: marcia A
reviews.title: A beautiful resort in Phoenix
reviews.text: Our room and the facility were beautiful.  The bed was extremely comfortable, amenities first-rate and the staff excellent. We had a mountain view king room with a huge bathroom.  We used the fitness center which was extremely well outfitted.  The 8 pools were arranged in a descending fashion and were beautiful and well-staffed.  Food in the restaurants is quite expensive, but that is to be expected in a 5 star resort.  Off season rates are extremely reasonable.

reviews.author: FirstClassFedora
reviews.title: Classically Extravigant
reviews.text:
There are a lot of excellent options for full service resorts in the Phoenix area.  But The Phoenician stands out for its central location, lavish appointments and excellent service.  The property is a symbol of 1980's excess with an amazing, world-class build.  If you want to feel like a million bucks and want a property a little more formal than other comparable options then the Phoenician may be a good choice for you.  Great for couples, golfers and jet setters...  not as ideal for families or younger travelers seeking nightlife or a 'scene'.  Also consider Royal Palms and Arizona Biltmore.

Location:  The Phoenician is located on the Phoenix-Scottsdale border near downtown Scottsdale and minutes from the Biltmore area and PHX.  The property is set on the SE side of Camelback Mountain, affording excellent views of the city.  (Something most competing properties cannot offer.)  While you are close to many things you can walk to nothing.  If you want to get off property then either rent a car or be prepared to use the resort's town car service.  (Taxi cabs are NOT allowed to pick up guests on property.)

Dining/Amenities:  We did not try the full service restaurant but did enjoy excellent room service at breakfast.  The food quality was superb and the service was unusually outstanding.  The new-ish J&G Steakhouse has best on property views of the city, very good craft cocktails and good (but perhaps not notably so) cuisine.  Try the cocktail lounge before dinner.  The Phoenician offers a full spa, golf and tennis.  The pools look especially nice.

Rooms:  We stayed in the casitas below the main building.  The room was spacious and offered an incredible view of Camelback Mountain.  Everything about the appointments was first class from the linens to the technology.  Marble, gold plate and berber everywhere.  While a refresh has updated the color palate the rooms retain their 1980's opulence.  It's a better thing than you might expect.  On the down side the room was not as clean as you might expect for the price range and the patios are less than private.  Overall my wife and I quickly felt at home and in love with the place.

Service:  People are helpful and usually crisp.  Something about our interactions (other than room service) left something to be desired.  I'm nitpicking but at this price point you deserve to know that service is arguably more intuitive at the smaller, boutique Royal Palms but it still top notch here.  Perhaps just not world class.

Other:  Self-Park is available and convenient.  This is a Starwood Property that participates in SPG.  Very good wi-fi.  The $29 resort fee is pushing it and is higher than some competing properties.  

Bottom Line:  The Phoenician is incredibly unique and perhaps unexpected in Phoenix.  You will pay 5 star prices.  Value will be there if the property fits your traveling needs and you will have a memorable experience.

reviews.author: ColumbusTravelers87
reviews.title: Best customer service I've ever
reviews.text:
I've stayed in Ritz Carlton's and Four Seasons.  I have to say that the service at this hotel was better than some of those.  Every person I came in contact with went overboard to be friendly and helpful.  I was there for 4 days for a work convention.  So often the food/staff in hotel catering/convention areas are mediocre.  Not the Phoenician...it was fantastic!!  

EVERY employee would say hello.  I called the front desk to ask where I could buy a rajor and then sent a complimentary one to my room immediately and then called 3 minutes later to make sure I received it and asked what else they could do.

I lost my diamond earrings in the spa and the locker room attendant spent 2 hours trying to find them.  When she finally did, she cried with me.....real tears!  Everyone is the spa was fantastic.

The food (serving 500+ people) was delicious.  

They have a wine shop in the hotel where you can do tastings and we had so much fun there one afternoon.

The rooms were very nice.  The pools looked fantastic, but I wasn't able to enjoy them.

I would love to go again for a personal vacation.

reviews.author: hikingrealblue
reviews.title: Great Business Conference Location
reviews.text: The resort was very nice with plenty of ammenities for everyone.  The Cactus Garden was beautiful, the pools were refreshing, and the health center was excellent for a workout while traveling.  The conference center had comfortable seating with good views from all angles. I enjoyed a walk to the top of the Camelback Ridge behind the resort.  I recommend the hike for those looking for a little more excercise.

reviews.author: ozmadmax
reviews.title: Luxury, quality and service
reviews.text: Stayed here for a 2 day conference. Check-in was excellent (although a little too strained to be a balance between friendly and formal). Room was ready and well equiped. Good night sleep. Breakfast excellent. Good internet connection. Friendly staff. Professional, clean and well run establishment.

reviews.author: Lynn M
reviews.title: Desert Vacation
reviews.text:
We planned a week-long  vacation on at the end of April 2012 at this wonderful hotel. It is a luxury hotel, with all the amenities, but not stuffy . We hated to leave our deluxe casita guest room, which was across from the golf club  and with a beautiful view of the Oasis Pool.  The resort is large and accommodated 2-3 major business meetings during our visit. However, the resort is so large, beautifully maintained, and the rooms soundproof, that you do not notice any "influx"  of guests. Plenty of pools, cabanas, chairs and wait staff to provide you with anything you might need. Room service was not more than 20 minutes from a phone call. 
The MOST IMPORTANT RESORT ASSET  is the staff..smiling, helpful, gracious... just plain  "NICE."  Each reflected excellent training. Elizabeth at the front desk was a wonderful  Starwoods' Representative, she answered many of our questions during the week. All of the staff , even our maid Rada, were wonderful...we will  return again soon, except the next time we will stay longer!

reviews.author: BMWtravel
reviews.title: Overpriced
reviews.text: Overall impression was beautiful when driving in. Main entrance was very nice as well with a beautiful terrace. Room was average and the floor we stayed on was undergoing a remodel which was very apparent when stepping off the elevator - unacceptable  for a $450 /night room. Italian Restaraunt was good. Golf course was also good (greens always break to the city).

reviews.author: K Pastore
reviews.title: Always a pleasure
reviews.text: We have stayed here a couple of times for business and have not been disappointed.  The spa is excellent and many people that have gone profess the best message they ever received.  They were out of Kings when we arrived, but the double was a great location with access to everything.  I hiked the Camelback mountain each morning (go early before the heat and crowds) which is only a one mile walk from the property.  I really enjoyed their daily fitness schedule including the yoga and daily medication.

reviews.author: Gaurav M
reviews.title: Great Hotel - With lots of activities
reviews.text:
Great place. Here were a few highlights:
1) There is a killer yoga class on Sunday at 10:00. The instructor is part life-coach / part-dancer and part-yoga instruction during the one-hour class. I wasn't in the class - but she hosts it on one of the lawns adjacent to the pool. 
2) The hotel service is exceptional - and the staff went out of their way to make my stay comfortable. 
3) The pools / lawns are amazing and can provide days of amusement for those looking for  a relaxed trip
4) There is plenty to do: Hiking Camelback, chilling by the pools, playing golf, sampling high-tea. Something for everyone. 

Cons:
1) Crowds are a little older. 
2) The hotel "feels" a little old when you first walk-in. It is, however, well maintained.
3) Can be pretty expensive - but I was able to snag a discounted rate!

reviews.author: didr
reviews.title: expensive but well worth the price
reviews.text: This is a true luxury hotel/resort. Extensive and very impressive art collection (with an audio self-tour), beautiful cactus garden. Restaurants leave something to be desired (separate reviews). Rooms are perfect, service is excellent. Location is very convenient to other Scottsdale/Phoenix attractions, but you need a car for that. Highly recomment self-parking; it's easy and convenient; less expensive.

reviews.author: RPH3
reviews.title: Still Excellent
reviews.text: I've stayed here 5 times over the past 10-12 years , all for corporate events. The quality of the staff is outstanding and the grounds are immaculate. This time I unfortunately had a lousey room location and in spite of Starwoods Preferred staus was told "we have no other rooms". I made it clear I was unhappy. Quietly I was hoping I would get a call back the next day suggesting another room, but that call did not come. In fairness, my expectaion came because of past excellent experiences. If you a re corporate travel professional you probably already know that this and the Biltmore are consistently as good as it gets for large groups. Food was superb at all buffets and sit down meals.

reviews.author: Andy08London
reviews.title: Fabulous hotel in a lovely location
reviews.text:
A fabulous hotel in a lovely location. Great if you like golf as it has its own beautiful golf course. Even better if you like swimming - are eleven pools enough for you? 

Our hotel room was very spacious and had a fabulous bathroom.  Be careful about your view though. Don't ask - as we did - for a view of the mountain. You end up being almost on the mountain - with no view at all! And a dim room into the bargain! I also found that all the corridors smelt a little damp and musty - although the rooms didn't.  

Aside from breakfast, we didn't eat in the hotel. We tried the buffet breakfast one day but found that the little cafe near the lobby was just as nice, less expensive and had much better service!

All in all a very relaxing and enjoyable experience.

reviews.author: Cudiva
reviews.title: Nice resort worth trying
reviews.text: Went to the Phoenician for a girl get a way trip in April.  The property is beautiful but maybe a little too big.  We were in the main building and I didn't like going through almost a maze to find the gym, luckily the landscapers were helpful in navigating us through.  The gym was nice and clean, had plenty of equipment and a studio as well.  I did not care for the bathroom set up personally the tub would be great for a small child but definitely not a soaking tub.  I dislike when the vanity is in the bathroom, when you have more than one traveler it makes it hard to get ready.  I did eat breakfast and found our waitress to be indifferent when I ask her to take back the burnt toast she served.  For the cost of breakfast (6 dollars for mediocre coffee) I would expect the waitress to look at what they are serving.  All of the other employees that I encountered were wonderful.  I do think they need more attendants at the pool, we did have to hunt down help with an umbrella.  Don't know if I will stay again on our next trip but it was definitely worth trying once.   Thought the spa services were overpriced so we booked at the Gainy Ranch instead and had a fabulous experience.  Definitely a good location for shopping and eating at some great restaurants.

reviews.author: sslanier
reviews.title: Guests were kind of stuffy!
reviews.text: Not a great pool vibe. Guests were boring and rude. The resort and staff were amazing!

reviews.author: gfdeb
reviews.title: Lovely property in need of an upgrade
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is an absolutely beautiful property with immaculately landscaped grounds and flower beds.  It is truely stunning.  So are the room prices for what is provided.  This was my 3rd stay in one of the apparently regular rooms.  There is absolutely nothing in these rooms to justify these prices and I believe every one of our group of about 14 conference attendees felt that same.  The carpet looks spotted and dirty, the deck furniture needs cleaning as it is stained-table and one lounge chair.  The very large bathroom had a bathroom scale with the top peeling off of it.  Yech.  The free internet access was difficult to log on to and you had to do it multiple times per day.  I have never seen a set up as cumbersome anywhere and I travel alot.

On the plus side, the service was almost impeccable- from arrival, the bell desk, check in, the daily staff, room service, pool attendants, lounge, restaurant,  etc.  I did have one interaction with a front desk person who was slightly less helpful then almost anyone else but still nearly perfect overall.  They are true professionals.

reviews.author: Ralph D
reviews.title: Outstanding in every way!
reviews.text:
This resort was built by the most famous S & L baron in the last great real estate meltdown in the late 1980s. At that time, The Phoenician was considered to be the height of excess and symbolic of the era. Stay at The Phoenician and you will know why.

This is an outstanding resort in a beautiful setting at the base of Camelback Mountain. Its campus like grounds make you feel like you are in an oasis in the middle of the desert, but, in reality, you are smack in the middle of wonderful Scottsdale, Arizona. This resort is close to everything, mere minutes to the airport, downtown Phoenix, and downtown Scottsdale.

It is 1st class all the way...27 holes of golf, deluxe spa, pools galore, and premium dining. The rooms are spacious and super comfortable. The service is friendly and non-stop.

I recommend a casita room.

The only downside...everything on property is expensive...it is easy to spend money. However, for a 5-Star resort, this is not unique.

Enjoy!

reviews.author: Jessica J
reviews.title: We enjoyed our quick trip to Scottsdale
reviews.text:
The Phoenician Resort is beautiful and we enjoyed every moment of our stay there.  The rooms were nice and the grounds were immaculate with flowers and cactus.  We requested an early arrival and they were ready for us when we got there which was very nice.  We rented a pool cabana the first day and the service there (Rich) was fantastic.  The weather was beautiful and the pools were the perfect temperature.  

We had the help of Gary the concierge helped us plan our trip and we followed all of his suggestions and recommendations.  Dinner our first night was at Roku Akor a Japanese restaurant outside of the resort. The food was unique and excellent and our service was great.

The second night we ate at the J&G steakhouse on the property.  Unfortunately, we did not enjoy our meal there quite as much. The atmosphere was fantastic and the view was beautiful.  The have a very expansive wine list and the service was excellent.  However, my husbands Prime Ribeye was not up to par.  There was a lot of gristle and my husband had to keep spitting out his bites.  It was not fun to watch.  :)

We ate breakfast each day at the buffet on the resort and the food and service there were fantastic. 

Overall  - we enjoyed our stay.  We wish we had stayed longer so we could enjoy the golf course and spa.  Maybe next time!

reviews.author: seashelley
reviews.title: Amazing property and beyond excellent service!!
reviews.text: Our family just returned from 5 nights at the Phoenician. Our stay there was perfect. This is truly one of the most beautiful resorts I have ever seen. The grounds are maintained to perfection. The pools are expansive and set up very nicely. The pool staff was wonderful. They set our chairs up and brought fresh water throughout the day. Someone was always available. The service at the Phoenician was excellent from check in to check out. We encountered many  employees during our stay and we were blown away that we were greeted by each and every one. I have never experienced such genuine warmth at any resort in the past. While the food on property is a little on the high side you will not be disappointed in the quality. The rooms are very roomy, bathrooms great and we loved the over sized balconies. We had a pool view room which I highly recommend. We can't wait to return and I know we will never stay anywhere other than the Phoenician.

reviews.author: Pat D
reviews.title: Beautiful Setting
reviews.text: Our family stayed 6 nights for Spring Break. The Phoenician is one of the nicest resorts that I have stayed at. The setting is beautiful. It is at the base of Camelback Mountain so you have an up close view of the mountain. There is a cactus garden path that is an attraction in itself. My 8 year old loved learning the names of the different desert plants. My only problem with this resort was paying the extremely high prices for food at the restaurants but we were on vacation so I did not worry. It is a huge resort so be prepared to walk!  Very well kept and luxurious!

reviews.author: Ryan
reviews.title: The Phoenician makes me proud to be an Arizonan.
reviews.text: Growing up I drove by the Phoenician every single day. I always admired the entrance, and even snuck into the pool area a few times back in high school ;o) My fiance and I were lucky enough to travel back to AZ last week, and stayed (finally) at this absolutely gorgeous resort for 4 nights. I can not say enough about the Phoenician. The grounds are breathtaking! Truly the heart of the Arizona desert. Beautiful walking paths throughout the resort, and along the base of Camleback Mountain. We hiked the mountain right from the walking trail at the resort. The 8 pools are amazing! And the drink menu has  delicious. Everyone works very hard at maintaining the grounds. It shows how much pride everyone has to work there. Smiles all around. I highly recomend staying at this one of a kind beauty in the heart of my hometown.

reviews.author: lamagid
reviews.title: One of the nicest hotels I've been to!
reviews.text: This is my family's 3rd time back at the Phoenician, and we rarely return to the same locations.  It is one of the most beautiful hotels we've been to. Yes, it is pricey. A cheeseburger at the pool is $16.  But it is one great cheeseburger. And the service is amazing.  People just seem to be waiting to help you. Towels, chairs, turn down service, ice water, etc.  The rooms and bathroom are luxurious and roomy.  Only issue: water pressure not great in the shower.  But each bathroom also has a tub for two.  The food at the pool is much better than your average resort lunch. My kids have always loved the pools and water slide, but now they're teenagers and we went on some great day trips to balance out days at the resort.  The weather is guaranteed unlike Florida or Caribbean.  If you leave the resort for dinner, the concierge has lists and lists of great restaurants at good value.  It's only 15 minutes to the airport.  It's the one vacation spot all 6 people in my family agree upon!

reviews.author: RSBoston
reviews.title: Beautiful but pricey
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is an absolutely gorgeous resort. From the view of Camelback mountain to the pool to the cactus garden to the little hidden gems of green space and garden, everything about this resort is beautiful. I travelled on a few different reservations (business trip, Starwood awards nights, Starwood points) and the people at check-in and check-out were very helpful and competent in handling the multiple reservations. I even got upgraded to a room on the end of the hotel with a huge lanai and view of both the pool and the mountain.

I had lots of fun hanging by the pool, going into Scottsdale to shop, and climbing Camelback (challenging but rewarding!) I also enjoyed the fitness center and spa services.

One word of warning - be prepared to spend money. The restaurants were expensive ($80 for two glasses of wine and two small salads at the Italian restaurant, $25 for two hot teas and granola parfaits for breakfast at the ice cream shop). You will also pay a resort fee, porterage fee for bags (I handled my own bags and was still charged), housekeeping fee, etc. Towards the end of the trip I was paying to go into downtown Scottsdale to eat lunch and dinner.

In summary, it was a wonderful and relaxing trip. I would gladly go back, but I will be more prepared for the prices next time!

reviews.author: hawksnut
reviews.title: The Phoenician, fit for a king, but not on spring break.
reviews.text: I was quite excited to experience The Phoenician.  It is a visual paradise - the grounds are beautiful.  We visited during spring break in March and it was a bit of a madhouse.  The pool chairs were quickly taken and reserved, even though there are signs that state that there is no "saving" the chairs.  The main pool water was not clean.  I cannot speak for the other pools because our children only wanted to use this particular pool with the volleyball and basketball nets.   Because the pool was so crowded, the bar/kitchen service was a bit slow.  Our room was not ready upon check-in and we had to wait almost two hours (received an apology) and we did not get the mountain view that we originally requested.  Again, an apology for that, too.  Our room was quite comfortable and pleasant and we loved the roomy balcony (housekeeping was lacking/not that great).  Golfing at the resort was very nice as were the spa and fitness center.  We dined at J & G Steakhouse (excellent) and the concierge services were outstanding (assited us with baseball tickets, restaurant recommendations and directions).  Bottowm line:  The Phoenician is a beautiful, opulent place.  Perhaps plan to stay away during spring break.

reviews.author: sds1966
reviews.title: Wonderful week!
reviews.text:
I was torn between booking this place or the Westin Kierland.  I chose The Phoenician because the Westin seemed like too much of a conference resort. I do not regret our decision.  We had a wonderful time and the service was top notch!
We had a grand deluxe room facing the pool. Some may worry the noise level may be high with a pool view but this is not the case.  The room was very clean and housekeeping did a great job.  The beds were very comfortable which is a plus for people with bad backs!
One thing I can't stand about most resorts is you have to get out at the crack of dawn to "reserve" chairs at the pool. We were there last week (week before Easter) and never had a problem finding chairs which made things a bit more relaxing.  The service at the pool was fantastic.  They were always quick to bring you drinks, food, etc.
We ate the buffet breakfast every morning (included in our package). The food was good but the selection was not very large in comparison to other places. Beware, kids pay the same price for the buffet! ($25)
We had the pleasure of dining at both Il Terrazzo and J & G Steakhouse and thoroughly enjoyed our meals. Service at the Cafe was also to be commended!
We always enjoy trying different places every year, but I must say, we are thinking of returning here next year!!

reviews.author: Gopakumar G
reviews.title: great place!
reviews.text:
Pretty much everything about this place was top notch. I was there for a conference with few hundred visitors. The hotel did not seem to have any problem accommodating so many guests. The room was great with a very nice view. 
My favorite part of the stay was the morning hike to the nearby Camelback mountain. Make sure to check it out if you have the time.

reviews.author: PHCHS
reviews.title: usine a groupes.....
reviews.text:
Au pretexte de spendide environement de verdure,et d entree majestueuse.....histoire de justifier des prix indecents eu une reputation tout a fait surfaite ,vous trouverez en fait :
-un hotel qui a tres mal vieilli ,et ne s est pas renouvelle,
-des chambres evidemment convenables,mais absolument pas a la hauteur de ce que vous pouriez attendre,pour plus de.....700 $ la nuit.....sans petit dejeuner...,et le tout ,sans vue pour la mienne...
-mais ,surtout ,cerise surle gateau ,un hotel archi complet ,ne permetant pas l acces normal a la 
piscine et a ses instalations ,..autrement que dans d epouvantables conditions d exode,rappelant un tres mauvais 2 etoiles des baleares au mois d aout.....
Bref ,des conditions epouvantables pour un excecrable rapport qualite prix......et absolument indigne de figurer dans la "luxury collection "de starwood....

reviews.author: Michele Y
reviews.title: LOVE IT!!!
reviews.text: This is our 5th trip to The Phoenician and we just LOVE IT!! The customer service has been FANTASTIC! The staff has always treated us like we are royalty, we got upgraded to a casita because of how frequently we've visited. The grounds are always so well kept and they are constantly working on them to make sure they are at their best. The fitness center that has been redone since our last visit 2 years ago, it is GREAT!! All new equipment, and now open 24/7!! And our dining experiences have been wonderful. We have enjoyed the Il Terrazzo every time we're here, it's a tradition to celebrate either a birthday or anniversary. I definitely  would recommend this is you are looking for some great relaxation, you could spend hours just by their fantastic pools alone. That's where we are headed!

reviews.author: Charles V
reviews.title: Phoenician back on track?
reviews.text:
A year ago we wrote that quality seemed to have slipped at the Phoenician. We just returned from another visit and had a very different and very good experience. For starters, the guard at the gate welcomed us by name (from a check in list he had) and recognized our guest status with Starwood hotels, as the Phoenician is a member of their Luxury Collection. That had never happened before in 10 prior visits. The front desk receptionist did the same and also noted how many times we had visited the resort, and thanked us for returning. That had never happened before either. For this stay we had requested one of the casitas by the lower pool, by specific room number. The front desk honored it and had the room for us, which is impressive since March is one of their busiest months. They were an hour late delivering the room because the prior guest failed to check out on time.  They gave us a gift for the wait, and even offered to upgrade us to 1200ft suite in the Canyon Suites if we didn't want to wait. We decided to wait because we like the casitas so much.  The bellmen and valets were very courteous.  Room service delivered within the the timeframe they told us, albeit at the very end of the time frame, and the food was very good. The house keeping staff and the turn-down person were very good and very personable. The room was in excellent condition and the linens and furniture all looked good.  They had added a new Keurig coffee maker since our last stay. 

The hotel grounds were in magnificent condition. 

We were very pleased overall, especially with the courtesy of the front desk staff (even during a very busy check in period).

reviews.author: Bijal
reviews.title: Fantastic Spa, Beautiful Views, and Amazing Service!
reviews.text:
We were visiting over Valentine's day since my husband had a conference in Scottsdale. My review is for the spa, which is called "The Center for Well-Being" and hotel "The Phoenician". 

The Center for Well-being was EXACTLY what I needed after being in need of a serious facial, wax, and full-body massage, wrap, and scrub!

All of the front reception staff was SUPER friendly and helpful in booking an experience and giving opinions on exactly what I'm looking for.

I got an AMAZING Clarifying Infusion facial with MaryAnn. She was absolutely fantastic and after getting dozens of facial, she literally was the most scientific in her explanation of exactly what product she was using and what it does. The facial was a bit pricier than what I normally spend ($200), but it was TOTALLY worth it with the hyperbaric oxygen they use, which is basically a really cool stream of concentrated oxygen that she gently used all of your face (for roughly 15 minutes of the session...so it's really effective) and it's supposed to reduce bacteria. The description claims you will see results in ONE DAY and I REALLY did! My husband literally saw me and said my skin looked like it did on the wedding day! I actually saw MaryAnn the next day for a wax and she was stunned to see how impressive the results were. I cannot recommend this treatment enough if you are somebody that has adult acne and needs help. I bought all the products she recommended and have been using them at home and literally BARELY break out now after wax treatments because of the products I'm using! It's been a life changer for me.

I also really loved my Desert Serenity Scrub, Wrap and Massage with Amy. It's their signature treatment - and I can see why. I LOVED the fact that the shower is within the treatment room so between the scrub and after the wrap you get to take a quick shower. It was uber relaxing and my skin felt super smooth and rejuvenated and the massage was fabulous.

I also wanted to comment on the facilities based on the some of the reviews I had read on Yelp. I'm a professional commercial interior designer, and I think they have done some real renovating and what I saw was really fresh design in most of the areas and in other areas may need some further updating, but nothing that AT ALL would deter from you going there!

Our stay at the hotel was really nice. The rooms are a bit dated, but the views and public areas are absolutely fantastic. Our FAVORITE place to eat was at RELISH. They had the best fried pickles, queso fundido, and burgers! We also loved hiking up Camelback mountain, which is only a 15 minute walk from the hotel. I'm NO hiker by any means, and it took us roughly 2.5 hours roundtrip (we didn't get all the way to the peak because it was a bit scary for a non-hiker like me), but loved the experience. Those Arizona blue skies are absolutely fantastic.

reviews.author: denisetreacy
reviews.title: absolutley fantastic
reviews.text: the best hotel i have ever stayed in, pure luxery , could not fault a thing.

reviews.author: AHSteinberg
reviews.title: Very Nice location, Great Restaurant, Dissapointing Service
reviews.text:
I was visiting the Scottsdale area on a business trip and stayed for 3 nights at The Phoenecian.  The facilities are nice and new.  There are numerous places to eat there and either catch a quick meal or sit for a nice dinner.  The J&G steakhouse is actually fantastic and I'm a NY'er so I'm hard to please in that realm.  The pool area is also quite nice and expansive.  

My main issue with this hotel was the service.  When I checked in the gentleman behind the counter was not as helpful as he could have been.  I asked what restaurants in the hotel were opened and he did not mention J&G.  I had to go back and ask him about it at which point he called for a reservation for me.  I'm not sure why he didn't suggest that the first time around.  

I also had a package delivered to the hotel.  I waited on hold over 10 minutes before someone at the front desk spoke with me.  The front desk told me the business area had the package so I went to pick it up.  The business area told me it was at the front desk.  I wasted over 25 minutes on this exercise.  

Every time I called for room service or the front desk I was placed on a significant hold.  I would much rather stay the next time at the Westin Kierland.  

In summation, it's a nice hotel with nice facilities.  If service is of little consequence to you then you should have no reservations about staying here.  Otherwise, you will be dissapointed.

reviews.author: HealthDiva
reviews.title: Gorgeous View
reviews.text:
As a resident of the Phoenix/Scottsdale area, I make it a point to visit the beautiful attractions we have here. I don't want to leave it up to the visitors to enjoy this gorgeous area.

I recently went to one of my favorite places...The Phoenician...to enjoy a sunny, Saturday afternoon with friends. Although I did not stay at the Phoenician, I have been there many times for the same reason: To simply have a glass of wine, sit on the upstairts patio, and relish the Scottsdale skyline, the two gorgeous pools below, and the beautiful foliage that surrounds the entire complex. I could get lost in this place. It is impossible to bring your troubles to this patio. The background piano music brings peaceful melodies and sometimes, even a memory or two.

If you just want to escape the world for an hour or two, this is the place to go. Again, I cannot speak to the hotel accommodations. But, even if the glass of wine is a little "pricey" than the other restaurants -- it's worth the "escape"!

reviews.author: terere2
reviews.title: Earns its diamonds!
reviews.text:
Service and facilities define a property at this level and The Phoenician delivered.  Check in was smooth and Robert provided the newspapers that I wanted.  The room was very comfortable and offered a great view of the pools from the terrace as well as a large tub and a separate glass shower.  Ben at Il Terrazo made my breakfast enjoyable with impeccable service and Belinda gave me ride suggestions when I picked up a bicycle (included in the resort fee).  The fitness center was fantastic and I used the spa for a sauna and shower.  In fact, there was no late check out (I'm a Platinum) but Caroline at the front desk allowed use of the facilities through the afternoon.  
Oh, take a hike up Camelback Mountain.  I don't play tennis but they even offer a grass court and the grounds were gorgeous.  My only regret is that I couldn't stay more than a day.  This is a world-class property.

reviews.author: Champagnejen
reviews.title: Oh so Overpriced and disappointing
reviews.text:
My parents took me, my husband, my Nanna, and my brother and sister to stay here over Christmas. We had just come form the most amazing hotel in Vegas (The Wynn Encore) and were ready for our next adventure!
Just to give you a bit of perspective, the suite my parents stayed in in Vegas had a grand piano, a private spa room for in room massages, a massive bathroom with a large jacuzzi tub, a wonderful view, and living room. It was basically the size of a good penthouse apartment. 
My father spent the same amount of money in each hotel.
So, you can imagine our dismay when we arrive at the Phoenician to find our rooms are rather small, dated, with tiny bathrooms! However, we were willing to accept this, after all, it was an older hotel.
but the experience here just got worse and worse. We went from missing Vegas to generally being quite annoyed. Here are some examples of the dreadful service at this hotel.
1. I ordered room service breakfast , and when they offered a bagel with my salmon I said no, I really wanted to stay away from carbs. Alas, they turn up with 4 bagels.
2. Checking in was so slow, and whereas the hotel in vegas upgraded our suites (as Amex customers), the phoenician did nothing.
The concierge at this hotel is pathetically useless. I'll make you a bet that 9 times out of ten, whatever you call up and ask about they either will not know the answer or b) Say it's not their job and will pass you off to another section of the hotel (who by coincidence, also doesn't know and can't help you).
3. My husband ordered Champagne and chocolates to be delivered to our room as a surprise when we got home form dinner. That was delivered to my parents........
4. For new years eve they were not able to book any tables for us in the hotel lobby. Not because they were full, but because they didn't want to do it. Going the extra mile for customers paying quite a lot of money is obviously not their style!
5. me and my husband would often order cigarettes from the 24 hour room service. They often never came. We later found out that room service doesn't bring cigarettes, house keeping does. So, why didn't they ever tell us this when we ordered them?
6. I would leave  laundry bags with notes on clearly indicating that i would like the laundry service. They would never be picked up.
The rooms were hardly cleaned. Cleaners would come in every day but I started noticing that they never cleared glasses or plates. So I started cleaning up. That's not what you want on vacation! Come on!
I must mention that the swimming pool staff are very good. They were the highlight of our trip. They saved the same cabana for my family every day, always made sure we were happy and had everything we needed, and even laid towels down on the side of the pool in case I wanted to read. My favourite day was when they gave me a champagne cocktail in a plastic champagne flute so that I could sip it in the pool. Lovely.
Having said that, I did encounter one pool guy who informed me that they would be closing the cabanas soon as "the hotel doesn't want to pay them to work any longer". ooooh!
I did visit the spa and it's incredibly dated and small. It reminds me of an average gym locker room. And it's not that clean either.
The salon was another highlight. Well, for me anyway! My Mum and my Nanna got blow-drys  that were so hilarious! I've never seen so much volume! I'm told that is the style in Arizona.
I got a mani/pedi, and facial threading from these two lovely ladies. I can't remember where they were from. Romania? They did a wonderful job, and brought me out of my denial by making me get an upper lip thread!

So, to sum up, this  hotel frankly needs to be ripped down and built again. They also need to be selective in the staff they hire (no more teens with absolutely no experience). They really need to teach a different attitude there. They need more enthusiasm, and can do. All the staff appeared so jaded!

My poor parents, who had many romantic memories of this hotel in the 80's, were sorely disappointed in what it had become, and I know that they will never go again. They were so looking forward to showing us this place and now they wish they hadn't.

reviews.author: TravelFeedback7
reviews.title: Too many billing errors
reviews.text: The mutitude of billing errors everyone in our group has experienced is unacceptable from a resort of this caliber.  I have been trying to get assistance since yesterday morning and have yet to get a call back from someone who cares. The resort itself is beautiful.

reviews.author: simonjjb
reviews.title: Wonderful five star service, property and dining
reviews.text: We stayed for 5 nights at the Phoenician over President's Day week.  My husband had a conference at the hotel, and my 12 year old son and I tagged along.  Although we arrived before check-in time, our room was ready.  We were not pleased with the location of our room, so we asked for a different room.  We had to wait a few hours, but they did accommodate our request for a room closer to the pool.  The rooms are beautiful- spacious, clean, and comfortable and the bathroom is also quite large with two vanities.  Although the hotel was quite busy during our stay, we never had an issue with dining.  In fact, we did not have reservations for dinner one evening, and walked into JG Steakhouse and they immediately sat us without hesitation.  The food there was delicious, as were all the breakfasts and lunches we enjoyed at the resort.  We lucked out with beautiful, warm weather that week and the pool is lovely.  Many of the pool staff were very helpful in getting extra umbrellas when needed.  Unfortunately, my son got a sudden stomach bug one afternoon and on the way back to our room, he got sick on the carpet right outside our room door, before we had the chance to get the room key.  A woman staff person immediately came over to us and told us not to worry, she would get someone to clean it up, and asked if we needed anything.  A few minutes later, after we were settled in our room, we received a call from a hotel staff person asking how my son was feeling, and they offered to get a doctor.  They also offered to send us some ginger ale.  At that point, he was feeling better, and they did send some ginger ale.  The next day we received a note in our room saying "we certainly hope your little boy is feeling better soon".  So thoughtful and considerate.  All in all, we had a wonderful trip, and we have been to many 5 star luxury hotels and resorts.  The Phoenician is quite simply one of the best resorts we have ever visited.  We will definitely return.

reviews.author: stefhef
reviews.title: Nice Place
reviews.text: We stayed at the Phoenician for a week over President's Day week.  It is a very nice hotel.  The rooms are quite spacious and the bathrooms are very nice.  The beds are extremely comfortable.  We ate at JG Steakhouse one night which was also very nice.  We went there as well on Thursday night during which they have happy hour specials and a jazz trio (only on Thurs.).  I definitely recommend this.  We have stayed several times at the Camelback; although it is a bit more casual and the rooms, while still very nice, are not as nice as the Phoenician's, I like the Camelback better because it has character.  The Phoenician seems like just another large, luxurious hotel but lacks any character.  I also found the service to be so-so.  We had a fine stay there, nothing wrong at all; just not as authentic a stay as I have found at the Camelback.

reviews.author: Michelle C
reviews.title: Great service & beautiful property
reviews.text: The Phoenician was a beautiful property and the service was amazing.  I left my key in my room after going to the fitness center (which had a very large selection of great equipment), and there was a very long line at the front desk of people waiting to check in.  The executive manager noticed that I was standing in line and came to see what he could do to help me.  While I was waiting for my key the staff in the lobby brought me bottled water as well.  Every time I went through the property the staff asked if they could help.  The grounds of the hotel are incredibly beautiful and the golf course was wonderful too.

reviews.author: Rosejules
reviews.title: Best stay/hotel/service ever!
reviews.text:
I can't say enough good things about the Phoenician! I was completely amazed by the kindness and hospitality by every person working at the hotel. I just couldn't believe how lovely everyone was. 

The views are amazing, the hotel is gorgeous, and the activities are fun and adventurous! 

On our way to hike Camelback mountain,  we flagged down a gentleman driving a golf cart for some directions. It was the executive manager of the hotel, Mr. Bauman. This man is obviously busy and has a hotel to run, but he stopped and chatted with us, offered to take us to the start of the trail, and was our own personal tour guide for the few minutes we drove through the Phonecian property. He gave us his card and let us know about the pickup service back to the hotel from the mountain. We got picked up in record time in a luxurious Mercedes Benz. Mike, our driver, was personable and such a nice person. 

Every driver, every door man, each and every one of the staff we encountered, was so warm and accommodating. If they sensed even the slightest discomfort in our stay, they immediately asked what they could do to help. But obviously there was absolutely nothing wrong so there was nothing to fix. 

Luanne, at the wellness center, gave me a relaxing and wonderful facial. My therapeutic massage from Gene, also at the wellness center, was 50 minutes of heaven. I absolutely loved it! 

This was the best stay I've ever had at a hotel and would definitely come back to vacation again.

reviews.author: AMMJK
reviews.title: Paradise.
reviews.text: Perfect choice for an idyllic vacation.  Great restaurants, superior staff, gorgeous grounds and facilities.  A wonderful escape designed to help you relax and feel special.  Suggested to them that music at the pool is unnecessary--the natural sounds of the grounds are otherwise perfect.

reviews.author: Jumbuck06
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, good service but overpriced if not using the facilities.
reviews.text: Considering the rates they charge for a room, I do not think one should pay extra for internet access. I thought paper cups and plastic stirrers at the in room coffee station was a little tacky.

reviews.author: Tuturista
reviews.title: Gracious and spacious
reviews.text: Despite its checkered past, The Phoenician is a gracious grand dame of resorts, and unusually conveniently-located for a resort of this type: you can walk into downtown, or up to Camelback Mountain - both are that close. I was here for a convention, which the staff handled very well. The savvy front desk clerk offered me a choice of rooms: either the main building, or in one of the outer buildings, closer to the spa & fitness center. I chose the latter, and enjoyed a garden view and free convenient parking. The rooms are quite big and almost identical in both locations. Nothing is done particularly imaginatively here - the usual posh hotel decor & typical resort shops - but the staff do smile at you, the grounds are well-cared-for, and the food was quite good. I used my scarce free time to enjoy a reasonably-good (not great) massage at the spa, and to go for an outing to Taliesin West (well worth it!).

reviews.author: letti001
reviews.title: 24 hour Vacation
reviews.text: Got the chance to spend a wonderful relaxing night at the resort.  It was beautiful, relaxing, well maintained with excellent service.  Special recognition to Nathan at the Front Desk who checked me in, answered my many questions, and was wonderful at making my stay even more perfect than I could have imagined.  Had a great service at the spa and time to hike Camelback, so easy to get to from the resort.  Enjoyed every minute of my stay, thank you!

reviews.author: CtJennifer
reviews.title: Our family loved it
reviews.text: Our family of 5 (2 adults and 3 girls ages 8, 10 & 13) stayed for 4 nights during Winter Break after visiting Sedona and the Grand Canyon.  The weather cooperated with high 70s and we used the pools each day, the tennis courts and hiked Camelback Mt.  Although it's quiet for families, it's not stuffy and kids feel welcome.  I appreciated that it wasn't crazy and there weren't a thousand choices to worry about missing something or getting to the next thing.  The service was spectacular, our room big and comfortable and Relish was a great hotel restaurant with kids.  We had friends come by for a swim and dinner and they were welcomed by the hotel.  As a bonus, we used Starwoods points and we thought the #  of points were a deal.

reviews.author: E H
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: I was accompanying my husband, who was there for 5 days of business. Glorious pools, grounds, dry air, architecture, desert calm. I walked the grounds and had such a great time with the sculpture gardens and cacti, and butterflies. We managed to escape and climb Camelback Mountain, and that was the high point. Beautiful tennis area, and many different surfaces (including grass) to play on. Food was great, staff was mixed, I hate waiting to be seated for something like a coffee, when there are 15 open tables. The buildings are sprawling and the layout is a little confusing. Pool tile areas can be slippery, I saw a few spills. There are gardens, koi and flowers at every turn. Wish we had time to golf. Nice and close from airport.

reviews.author: fozzetti
reviews.title: Wish I could have stayed longer
reviews.text: Got to spend a night here recently. I was only in for a short time so I didn't get to enjoy the property, as I have in the past. But the resort is still well appointed and well taken care of. The rooms are very nice, if closing in on the time for a remodel. The bed may be the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in. Nice bath and bath amenities... Worth the trip.

reviews.author: DonK
reviews.title: Top quality resort!
reviews.text: What a wonderful way to get away from the snow!  Beautiful grounds with several pools and waterfalls everywhere.  Super massage at the spa and lots of dining choices.  It's expensive so be prepared.

reviews.author: Nicole B
reviews.title: Mixed feelings about this place
reviews.text:
The positive:
The backdrop is camelback and the views were stunning from the public areas.  Restaurant staff and service was excellent.  The food was spectacular - especially at J&G restaurant. The rooms were nice - and the patio area was refreshing to lounge on. 

The negative:
We checked in and left our luggage with the bellboy.  We made it to our room after a 20 minute wait in line....no luggage.  I called the front desk and inquired about it since I needed to change my clothes and attend a meeting.  I was told the luggage would arrive promptly.  10 more minutes and my husband went looking for it.  It was still on the curb completely unattended.    Then we received a knock on our door several minutes later asking to check our minibar since it had not been checked after the prior guests checked out.  Tacky. Not what I would expect of a hotel of this caliber.   One other negative item for us is that our room overlooked the croquette court. This is just a luck of the draw and no ones fault.  For the price, I was expecting nicer views. 

I would not visit this hotel again - maybe my expectations were too high.

reviews.author: tripadvizor2012
reviews.title: Good rooms, poor service, overall not worth the premium
reviews.text:
The positives:
-- Good rooms, spacious, and comfortable
-- Plenty of amenities in the hotel, and beautiful setting, particularly if you like golf

The negatives:
-- Mediocre service. It feels at times like the staff are resting on their laurels (i.e. they "know they are the best hotel in AZ"). I found some staff (but certainly not all) to be inconsiderate at times. 
-- A good example came when I asked for a one-hour checkout extension. The automated "Sorry sir, we cannot accommodate your request" didn't feel like the friendly kind of effort you would expect for this premium hotel.
-- Don't order room service!!! Mediocre would be a compliment..... the food is stale, has been laid out a long time, and is generally low quality.

The Bottom Line: the mistake I made here was thinking that a $400+ per night price tag would ensure a weekend of relaxation and luxury. This is definitely a good hotel hotel, but you will be really disappointed that you didn't pay half the price for an excellent alternative (the Biltmore, Royal Palms, etc.) with friendlier service.

reviews.author: John V
reviews.title: Wonderful Staff - Great Hotel
reviews.text:
We stayed for three nights and as much traveling as I have done may I 
say that the quality of service was as great as I have seen anywhere in the
world. Not a single staff member failed to always greet my wife and I and
everyone had a smile on their face! From doormen to servers to room attendants
the service was AAA. 

Beyond the service, even after some 20 years the hotel is immaculate and 
the lawns and gardens spectacular.

The only fault I might have would be the memory of the double bogie on the 
first hole I played on the golf courses - but it is hard to blame it on the hotel!

reviews.author: travelingurl
reviews.title: The Service, It's About the Service
reviews.text:
We moved from a different Phoenix area property to the Phoenician because we didn't feel the other property was delivering as we had hoped.

Our last minute reservation was for a casita room, overlooking the pool and waterslide.  In fact, I'm not sure it would be possible to be any closer to the hot tub.

Our room, at first glance, wasn't particularly generous or special.  But then we went into the bathroom which rivals the sleeping space in square footage.  A six-piece bath with a shower we probably could have fit 5 people in and a walk-in closet.

Also in the sneaky-big category, was the outdoor/balcony area.  Chaise lounge and table with chairs, and plenty of room to walk around.  All covered and shaded, which is probably very desirable in the hot summer months.

All this was great, but what really set the Phoenician apart was the service.  Jennifer in the Terrazzo waited on us 2 mornings.  I had inquired about almond milk for lattes on day one and she ordered it in so it was available on day 2.  Marcel was the "pool boy" (I'm sure there is a better term for this) and besides being adorable, was attentive and professional.  

All in all, the Phoenician provided a lovely vacation experience.  We really enjoyed it and wouldn't hesitate to return.

reviews.author: le-metro
reviews.title: Fantastic time at The Phoenician
reviews.text:
We attended a 4 day Corporate event at The Phoenician.   All aspects of service were top notch.   We were greeted professionally and escorted to our room.   It was a bit of a hike as we were situated in the far eastern portion of the resort.   However, the room was expansive, with a King bed, large living room area, and very large washroom.   Washroom had a separate shower, soaker tub, private toilet and bidet.   As per some other reviewers, the hallways were a bit dated and dark, but in good repair.  The room's wallpaper and washroom did look older, but were clean and very well kept.

The service, in both the dining areas and on the grounds, was superb.   From the small restaurants around the facility to the main catered dining rooms, everyone provided excellent service.   As an example, we were at the "Mother of Pearl" pool, and a staff member came by and offered to bring us a pitcher of water, bucket of ice and glasses for our party.   A nice gesture while sunbathing by the pool.   Everyone went over and above to make sure our stay was pleasant.   In most cases, the staff had no idea we were part of a Corporate function and treated each of us well.

On site were some small store, including the popular ice cream parlour.   This was a hit with many.    There are many breakfast options, including the ice cream parlour which serves a nice variety of eat in or take out fare.

The grounds are well kept, with a variety of pools and water falls.  All pools are nicely heated, as well as a couple of children's pools.   The grounds also include the historic Jokake Inn, where we were invited to an outdoor Bar-B-Que as part of one event.

All in all, a very nice Resort with great staff and beautiful grounds.    An excellent choice.

reviews.author: Buddha86
reviews.title: Great surrounding atmosphere
reviews.text:
I have stayed in the Phoenician multiple times. What I enjoyed the most is the view or the location. The food is was pretty good. From the lobby the downstairs restaurant have some great dessert. The couple of bar tenders, I think in their late 30s to early 40's by the pool side near the restaurant are really nice people, always pleasure to see them (I'm trying to think about their name.) Some of the employee's in the lobby area could use a bit more smiling so they come across as warm and less reserved(that will probably be my only complain!)

I would recommend your stay in the Phoenician but if you like to step it up a level notch check out the Canyon Suites, it just gets better;)

reviews.author: phoebeparker
reviews.title: big was better
reviews.text: we didn't think  we'd enjoy this large a resort but booked a casita on the beautiful grounds of the Phoenician hotel. the service was amoung the best we'd ever encountered. the restaurants were delicious and well priced and our breakfasts from AMEX platinum were included. the rooms were spacious, views of the pools (5) were relaxing and the art work on the property amazing. vice president Beiden was there over the same  weekend and secutiry was very tight but manageable. we look forward to returning soon.

reviews.author: dtgdallas
reviews.title: Mixed Comments
reviews.text:
Visited The Phoenician last week for a combo business/pleasure trip.  Overall thoughts are positive, but not without some reservations.

Checked in late afternoon after a brief wait.  Our room was way, way on the far end of the resort property, about as far away as it could be.  Someone’s got to have the room that’s farthest away, and my wife and I are both able-bodied, so it wasn’t a huge deal.  The employee that checked us in did mention how long the walk was, but said it was an oversized room and hoped we would find it comfortable.  As it turns out, the room’s size was very generous, very spacious.  And we had a nice deck with two chaise lounges, two regular chairs and a little table – all facing the setting sun.

The hallway to our room was dark (not W Hotel-like “chic dark”, but just dark and depressing) and in need of refurbishment.  The carpeted areas leading up to the internal doors that separated the inside hallway to the outside hallway were a bit soiled and frayed, probably from years of roller bags and luggage carts banging across the threshold.  The room itself was okay.  The furniture was decent, the flat screen TV was decent, the bed and bedding was excellent (one of the best hotel beds I’ve slept on in a while), the bathroom was okay.  The only significant issue with the room was the shower.  If my wife and I took back to back showers, the water would begin to back up.  This was particularly noticeable to me, because I was almost always the second person to shower, and my wife takes long showers.  By the end of my relatively short shower, I would have water at about ankle height.  I thought about reporting it to the front desk, but didn’t because I knew that the shower had to run for 15 minutes or more before it happened, so the maintenance guy would probably show up, turn on the water, see it drain okay and then think we were crazy.  I probably should’ve reported it anyway, but didn’t.  The other comment on the room was about the little wet bar area, where the coffee maker was, etc.  The caulk between the counter and backsplash around the three sides of the wet bar area was very old – a bit discolored with some gaping holes where the caulk had cracked.  I commented to my wife “you know, it wouldn’t cost anything to have someone take the old caulk out and put fresh caulk in and this would look so much better….”.  

Service throughout the resort was spotty.  Spotty might not be the right word, because it was more typically good/great than disappointing, but, as is typically the case, the disappointments stand out more than the good interactions.  On the good/great side, we were looking for the sundry shop one evening after dinner, probably around 9 p.m.  We inquired at the front desk, and the young man said “The Pinata Shop is already closed, but I can find someone to open it up for you”.  We said “that’s not necessary”, but he insisted.  And he then personally escorted us from the front desk to the sundry shop, opened it up, let us shop for our soda and snack and then charged it to our room.  That was excellent service.  The concierges were excellent in our few brief encounters.  The bellmen were excellent.  The business center staff was very helpful.  On to the disappointing….the service at the pool, while polite, was inconsistent.  Example:  we sit down next to a colleague/friend and a waitress swings by and asks if we would like menus.  My wife and I say yes, our friend says yes, so two menus are handed out.  45 minutes later (and I’m not exaggerating) we hadn’t seen hide nor hair of the waitress. One would think that if you ask if someone wants a menu and they readily say yes, it’s because they’re hungry and want to order some food.  I finally had to flag a towel boy and ask him to find the waitress so we could order lunch.  She comes over, takes our order and then begins to walk away, and we say “miss, I think our friend here wants to place an order, too!”.  The next day we waited forever to get the check at the pool, and when we finally flagged down our server (a man, this time), he kept flipping through the checks and couldn’t find our check.  He was a good guy, but he finally, said “I’m sorry, I can’t find it, I’m going to have to go print it out again”.  Which could happen, I know, but since we had already waited so long, we said “just add the automatic gratuity, we’re going to head to our room”.

The biggest service lapse related to housekeeping.  I was in my room on Saturday morning watching my alma mater play a bball game on ESPN.  The doorbell rings about 10:30 a.m. (the game started at 10 a.m. local time) and it’s housekeeping.  The first words out of her mouth were “Do you want your room serviced today?”  I was really, really surprised that she would ask that question at a place like The Phoenician.  It’s not as if it was 5 p.m. and we had had the Do Not Disturb sign on the door all day.  I said “yes, we would but would you mind coming back in about an hour and a half”.  The lady says ok.  An hour and a half later (I’m being generous, it might have been a little less than 90 minutes, but let’s say 90 minutes), the game is still on and the doorbell rings again.  It’s the same lady, and I say “I’m sorry!  Would you mind coming back in 30 minutes?”   She hesitated, paused, and had this look of irritation on her face that really threw me for a loop.  She hemmed and hawed a bit, before finally saying “yes, okay”.  Maybe I was really screwing their schedule up, but it was only noon, on a Saturday (when I’ve got to think that people are, generally, leaving their rooms later than they are during the week).  Her irritated look irritated me, so I said, trying to make a point, “are you sure that’s okay?”, to which she replied “yes, that’s fine”.  I don’t know, maybe I’m at fault and readers of this review will tell me that I am.  

One final comment regarding housekeeping.  At some point on Saturday, between the time we left for the pool and returned from the pool, someone dropped off a tray of candies, with a postcard from the resort manager thanking us for our stay (we were leaving the next day).  We left the tray, uneaten, on the wet bar counter and headed off to dinner.  When we returned, the housekeeping staff had been in the room for the turndown service, and we noticed that one of the candies had been eaten!  It was completely not a big deal, because we weren’t going to eat them all anyway, but it was still a bit weird.  Knowing I was probably going to post a review on Trip Advisor, I asked my wife twice “are you sure you didn’t eat one of these??”  She let me know, in no uncertain terms, that she hadn’t.  

Let me close with a couple of positives.  The food was great.  We had lunch at Il Terrazzo on day of arrival – great (and great service, too).  We had a group dinner at Il Terrazzo on evening two and the food was outstanding.  The lunches we had poolside were very good.  

We will definitely return (partly due to business commitments, but for pleasure, too), but the service lapses are, at best, interesting.

reviews.author: TheFrasiers
reviews.title: Business meeting
reviews.text:
In January I was there for a meeting. The rooms were spacious. The only negative aspect about the room was that the bathtub was a little outdated. The carpet in the hallways needed to be replaced.

Overall the grounds were nice. The pool looked inviting, and I was disappointed I wasn't able to enjoy this more.  

Relish, one of the restaurants on the property, overlooked the golf course and was amazing.

reviews.author: oliver m
reviews.title: classic
reviews.text:
I stayed the in Jan2012 for a three nights as we had a company event.

The biggest plus for the phoenician is it's amazing area which includes:

- Restaurants
- Bars
- Pools
- awesome golf course
- and something like an private Mountain where you have an amzing view

You basically have the impression that you are stranded in a luxury oasis. So alone the whole setup is worth a visit, if not for the night then for you hanging out at the pool or the terrace witha an amazing view over the valley or just a round golf.

The Service is on a very good standard, there is nothing to complain but also nothing to highlight.

The Food is als very good standard with the same lack of low- or highlights.

Housekeeping was very good, the rooms are perfectly clean.

The rooms are the weak spot. As the Hotel has already a couple of year in his records, the rooms could you a renovation or at least a minor modernisation. i.e The instruments to control the air condition seemed to me to be like 30 yers old. The biggest issue was the mini bar which was really noisy.

I am always wondering why hotels wait that long to make a modernization. Is it because they earn enough money due to a lack of competition or is it that they don't earn enough to invest and try to milk the cow to it's leats extent. Regardless of what it really might be, if they would spend this minor effort they would have gotten an excellent rating.

reviews.author: Singerred
reviews.title: Great rooms and excellent service.
reviews.text: I stayed her for two nights for a conference. The banquet food was really good, and for each meal, I was asked if I had any dietary issues. Our room was spacious and well-appointed. The bed was amazingly comfortable and the sheets were nice. Our room was very quiet as well. The bar had signature Mimosas with fresh fruit, which were wonderful. The fitness room had nice equipment. It is a large property, so it can be a walk to get from place to place.

reviews.author: John W
reviews.title: This Place Rocks
