reviews.text: Stayed here awhile ago now but wow what a Hotel. Loved the place because it has a romance about it. Nothing fake and Great Service in all Departments. Can't wait to go back again and try some golf too.

reviews.author: Norbert1951
reviews.title: It's getting a bit tired
reviews.text: There Wifi is a joke not only is it bad, it should be free.

reviews.author: intrepidtravelerfla
reviews.title: THE choice in Scottsdale
reviews.text:
I am often on the west coast for business and stay here on my way back. I have stayed here many times over the past 10+ years and each time am impressed. 

The hotel itself is nearly an icon; the rooms spacious. I have never eaten in the restaurants so I can't speak about them.

When in Scottsdale, stay here.

reviews.author: MoniqueVG
reviews.title: Great hotel at Camelback Mountain.
reviews.text:
My husband and I spent Saturday night , January 21st, at that nice hotel with great views. The service is very good.  The room was nice and well appointed.  (We suggest they change the carpet (also in the halls) since it is (or looks..) outdated.
We toured the Cactus Garden, on the property,  which was  very interesting, and beautiful.
We really enjoyed JG Steak House, which is a lot more than a Steak House.  We took the 'tasting menu' which was delicious! And..this young chef, who worked before in a very good restaurant in Manhattan, is sure on his way to his first Michelin * .  Good luck to him.

reviews.author: eig_04
reviews.title: Nice place but big hotel feel
reviews.text: My boyfriend and I stayed here during the BCS bowl game this year. It was a great hotel: the rooms were large, clean, and attractive; the patio of the room was great; the restaurant was pretty good; and the pool area was absolutely beautiful. However, it is a really big place and has a "big hotel" feel to it (complete with conference rooms, underground parking, shopping center, multiple restaurants...). While some might like this, it's not nearly as romantic as some of the other, more private and individualized properties in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: Twintime1
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: I stayed here awhile ago but would like to stay again. Even the standard rooms are amazing and that mother of pearl pool.....beyond my expectations.  I think women are big on bathrooms and this one was head to toe marble!  I also had services at the spa that I loved.  I would highly recommend this oasis!

reviews.author: The_Traveling_Tom
reviews.title: OASIS!
reviews.text:
We stayed here in both April '11 and Thanksgiving '11 and had a great time...my advice would be NOT to pay attention to the nay-sayers. The Phoenician continues to be one of our favorite American Starwood properties. The grounds, the rooms, the pools, the service and the restaurants are all way above average IMHO!

The many "events" planned at holiday time were fun for all, and there are wonderful things to do in the area...FLLW's Taliesn West tour is remarkable, and a special shout out to Frank & Lupe's courtyard restaurant (in the back!) for great food and local color...

I guess my one piece of advice would be to be certain to try to get a Grand Deluxe room overlooking the valley/pool. I don't think you will enjoy the mountainside/parking court/roofscape rooms anywhere near as much, and I suspect that many of the less-than-stellar reviews arise from this reason.

Special thanks to Ellyn Gluskin for helping make this (and our previous) stays such amazing family celebrations! 

We have not stayed in the Canyon Suites, and while they look nice, they are quite separate from the main property FWIW.

Enjoy!

reviews.author: Lauren S
reviews.title: Awesome hotel
reviews.text: This hotel was amazing.  I had a beautiful room with a beautiful view.  and the staff were unbelievable and extremely accomodating.

reviews.author: MolokoMan
reviews.title: Beautiful Hotel!
reviews.text: We went here on our honeymoon and this hotel was great! You can get massages, play in the huge pool, hike camelback mountain. There are also lots of restaurants nearby. I would not eat at the restaurants inside the hotel. We didn't like them very much but there are lots of restaurants within a couple miles that you can choose from.

reviews.author: Vanh33
reviews.title: New Year's 2012
reviews.text: Very nice property. Great views, great pools, and top notch service. Did need some updating of carpet and few other things. Overall it is worth it's rating. Stayed new year's eve 2011.

reviews.author: 20TravelJunkie
reviews.title: Impresses me every time
reviews.text:
Where do I start here? well lets start with the rooms. The beds are great...so comfy! the room is cleaned like i would clean it...spotless. the standing shower...love it! the balcony...beautiful at sunrise/sunset. I stayed in the main part of the hotel both times i went and its nice. the second you pull up to the door youre greeted by a cheerful staff member. the lobby is gorgeous. they really know how to start your stay off right. 
the many pools they have...awesome! i tried all of them! 
il terrazo is my favorite resteraunt and they have the best breakfast although its a tad pricey. the wait staff is wonderful. i also like relish they have awesome burgers and a wide range of tequilas. i dont drink but i found the tequila to be very pricey. 
theres plenty to do on the property. one thing i recommend is hiking camelback mountain in the morning. its incredible. 
i really dont have enough good to say about this place. its sure is wonderful and its worth the price.
downsides: the first time we went they asked us if we wanted to valet our car and we did however we were unaware of the 29 dollar charge. unless youre willing to pay 29 dollars every day to valet, use the free parking garage.

reviews.author: Dave-from-Boston-USA
reviews.title: My new favorite hotel
reviews.text:
Leveraging our points, we stayed at the Phoenician for 5 nights in mid-January.   Overall we were extremely pleased with the experience.  It may be one of my favorite hotels in the world. 

Pros: all the stuff that comes with the resort fee such as the bikes, lounge at the spa, great fitness center, etc.; huge rooms; tons of little amenities and great yoga classes taught by Meta.

Cons: expensive if you don't have points, a bit of a walk (but very doable) at night (they will loan you a bike during the day) to get anywhere "off-campus" if you choose not to rent a car.

Mini-gripe: They charge $20 ($10 if you pay the resort fee) for a "120 min" guided hike that is "an intense cardio workout".  Obviously these are very subjective terms, and from my perspective, a huge exaggeration.   They really should change the description to read: "a hike up to Post 18 on Camelback mountain which is less than half way to the summit, but still an athletic experience for those who aren't well conditioned.  Note that most of the allocated time will be on the road getting to and from the trailhead."  Though they did refund my $10 after I alerted the front desk to this minor grievance.  

I wrote an extensive blog article about the Phoenician, Camelback Mountain and nearby parts of Scottsdale with tons of pictures and tricks such as where to get a free healthy breakfast.  Check it out at: http://freetravelgenius.com/phoenician/

Do note that we were there from Jan 12 to Jan 18th.  The place pretty much looked like a ghost town during this period.  I think it may have had to do with being a less busy time of year, or maybe the place is just so big, you can't see anyone else.  Anyway, it worked out great for us, but it is possible my thoughts would be different if there were big crowds.

reviews.author: meanchat
reviews.title: Management went above and beyond
reviews.text:
My wife and I recently stayed at the resort to celebrate our anniversary.  We were last there about 12 years ago when our son was 9 months old and decided to go back without the kids to have some adult time.  Although there were some minor kinks during our first day, management went out of their way to ensure that the remainder of our stay was excellent.  Although the weather was not as sunny as we had hoped for, we were able to make use of the on-site ExecuCar service to visit the Old Scottsdale area as well as the Desert Botanical Garden, both of which were close to the property.  Although we have a timeshare at the Four Seasons Troon North, which we like very much, it was nice to be more centrally located.  The hotel is only 15 minutes from the airport and with an early check-in and late check out, we were able to maximize our time at the resort.

We had a fantastic dinner at Il Terrazzo restaurant with a special dessert tray at the end of our meal.  My wife enjoyed her salmon and my filet mignon was also great as was the service by Sara.  As we made a room switch during our stay, we saw various views of the property, but the one that I most enjoy is the one from the rooms facing Camelback Mountain with all of the cacti as a backdrop to the beautiful pools and landscaping of the property.  

We wish we could have stayed longer and look forward to returning with our children in the near future so they can enjoy the pool with the slide, the on-site ice cream parlor and the Funician Kids Club.  

I would recommend both this property and the Canyon Suites within the resort, which is a bit more upscale.  For me, the short trip was about reconnecting with my wife in a beautiful atmosphere and the small details made the stay all the more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Nicky
reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: This is certainly not a hotel I would have gone to if it wasn't paid for on my behalf.  Just too expensive.  However, the rooms were fantastic!  The casitas are well built and very quiet with great balconies.  The staff were very pleasant and I really appreciated how speedy they were at getting my passport to me at the airport when I forgot it behind in my room safe.  You are very well taken care of whether you are in a business meeting, conference or lounging at the fire pits.  I gave a three to value only because I think it's ridiculous to pay $43.50 for bacon and eggs.  The grounds are beautiful, the views are better, overall, a fantastic luxury experience.

reviews.author: arts1994
reviews.title: Lovely but not perfect!
reviews.text: Our recent stay at The Phoenician in the first week of 2012 was lovely, but not perfect. The setting is great, the rooms wonderful and quiet. The in-room breakfast delicious and on time!! The restaurant food menus were limited in terms of healethy choices, especially the small selection in the salads was bothersome. Overall the staff was helpful, with as major exception the difficulty we encountered at check-out when we discovered a mistaken charge to our account. The clerk was at best unhelpful in the situation and if anything accusatory suggesting that we were "changing story" to him. In the end he failed to bill the stay to two different credit cards, as we had requested. And even the phone call today to get this rectified was handled rather poor and chaotic and not apologetic at all. It left us with a bad taste after a lovely week.

reviews.author: Kyle B
reviews.title: Luxury in the desert
reviews.text:
An exceptional Starwood property, I wouldn't hesitate to return.  It is not cheap, but the experience is top notch.  Excellent pool area with multiple swimming pools, hot tubs, water slide, full-service bar.  Kids and adults will enjoy the traditional and boozy versions of sno-cones while baking in the sun.  The gym is well-equipped, and attached to the spa area.  Prices for services are high to match the room rates, but it is a nice facility.
 
Two of my favorite things about the property are the bike rentals and the proximity to Camelback for hiking.  While I could easily have enjoyed lounging by the poolside all day, I'm glad I borrowed the bike and rode south along the canal system.  The hike up the mountain the next day was also better than expected - well worth the the time and sweat involved.

The food served at the casual / to-go cafes on site were just OK, and didn't merit the high prices.  However, an exception to this were the delicious breads that you could order at the bakery in the small shopping arcade.  Delicious and quite reasonably priced.  I was also told by my Mom that the tea service offered at the Phoenician is top notch.

reviews.author: SteveNYCity
reviews.title: Our family loved our stay
reviews.text: Our family stayed in a suite at the Phoenician while we were there for the Fiesta Bowl and had a wonderful stay.  I'm sure part of it was the gorgeous weather since it was 80 degrees for our 3 days.  My young children had a blast at the pools (which were heated), whether going down the long slide 100 times or shooting at the basketball hoop.  The suite was spacious and the bathrooms were clean and large.  The shower was fantastic!  The beds were very comfortable, although the pillows were really mushy, but maybe that was just ours.  We ate at the burger bistro one evening and the terrace restaurant another and found the food at both to be excellent.  Breakfast on the outdoor patio at the terrace was a nice way to start the day!  The burger place also has a nice list of craft beers to try.  The concierge was very helpful the couple of times we sought her out.  We were a bit bothered by the $13 wifi, but in the end, decided to stay off the grid for a few nights, which was just fine!  Getting to the airport was fast and simple.  My wife informed me that will come back again this or next winter, so I'm sure that will happen.

reviews.author: Pistol Pete
reviews.title: Excellent...  One of the best places we've stayed.
reviews.text:
We came out and stayed for the fiesta bowl.  The service was outstanding for all the amenities we used.  Top notch!!  Gentlemen, while you are here, you need to see Sam at the salon...  Old school barber that gave me the best haircut and shave I've ever had.  

I would recommend this establishment without hesitation.

reviews.author: Scott B
reviews.title: Scottsdale Splendor
reviews.text: The grounds are impeccable for pool, dining, or explore the cactus garden along the side of Camelback Mountain. As a Starwood Platinum member the upgrade to a casita suite made a big difference for our young family, and in particular the large balcony and massive bathroom were great!

reviews.author: Thermodynamix
reviews.title: Excellent for a nice laidback vacation
reviews.text: Stayed there for 4 days in late December. The rooms were very comfortable and well maintained. Got an upgrade to a suite as well. Concierge and staff was very helpful too. Very pretty grounds, golf course and tennis courts, running trails and cactus garden

reviews.author: NorcalTraveler_9
reviews.title: NIce resort...., but please offer free wifi
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed at the Phoenician over Christmas weekend (12/23-12/27) to visit with family.  We were upgraded from a Deluxe King room to a Casita with no additional cost.  It was obvious the resort was virtually empty.

In a nutshell:

The grounds are immaculate and the resort is beautiful and very well-located.  Great for walking, jogging, and access to Camelback.

You have to pay for wifi and for the gym which are two big negatives for me.

No turn down service the first night we were there (not a big deal to me, but this is a "5 star" resort). Also noticed an ice bucket with champagne glasses sitting outside a service area for 3 days before they were picked up.

No complementary paper or breakfast card left in the room until the Monday after Christmas.  We did get a plate of Christmas cookies on Christmas Eve - yum!

Casita was spacious with a ground floor patio overlooking the central courtyard.  Large bathroom with two separate vanities.  Carpet needed replacement or cleaning.

All in all, a very nice resort with friendly staff.  However, in this day and age, not having free wifi is a sore spot. I also feel that it "nickels and dimes" people to pay $10/day for gym access.

reviews.author: Astroph
reviews.title: Relaxing stay
reviews.text: Stayed in a Grand Deluxe Room for one night. The size of the room was very comfortable and the balcony view was great. I appreciated the free car service to get to distant locations on the resort. The tennis club stayed open late so that I could pick up a basketball and allowed me to play as long as I wanted to on their court. They even came out with a few pitchers of waters so we could play. Very friendly staff and decent SPG Platinum recognition.

reviews.author: rubyred75
reviews.title: Beautiful and Amazing
reviews.text: Suites are amazing and beautiful , t.v. in bathroom mirrors was fun. Staff and service wonderful . Grounds lovely , to cold to swim but pool looked beautiful. Location is perfect. Restaurants were fantastic . I would stay again and recommend to a friend.

reviews.author: got2go
reviews.title: Very nice but not great
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is certainly an amazing piece of property.  The location is wonderful, the property is lovely, with large grounds to walk around.  This is a nice way to get in a walk without having to go out on the busy Scottsdale road. 
It is the rooms however that don't seem to live up to the rating and cost of this hotel.  We were given the option to upgrade our room for $10, which we did.  Had we not done this, the room would certainly have been overpriced..  In addition there is another $29 for the resort fee, $30 for parking, and a very high tax rate.  By the time I was done the rate was nearly $450 a night.  It is a nice place, but after travelling to many parts of the world, I expect much more for this price.
I have to say however, the service and people are top shelf at the Phoenician.

reviews.author: Mplsguy_7
reviews.title: Special event found a home
reviews.text:
For our 40th wedding anniversary, I wanted to plan a special experience for my special wife of so many years. She had never been to Scottsdale--or anywhere in the SouthWest--and I only for business. While I had no previous exposure to the Phoenician, other than reading here about it's reputation, and after conducting pretty thorough research--we placed our reservations. 

If you too, are looking for a special location, this one deserves the title 'resort'. The service level from all employees you'll encounter really places your interests and need in the fore-front. Concierge service was on target with every recommendation. Rooms are very comfortable and the beds and bedding luxurious. Everything in the room and bath underscore the devotion to your satisfaction.

Highly recommended. Enjoy yourself...

reviews.author: Travelgirl60745
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort
reviews.text: We stayed here for 2 nights, very quick trip to Phoenix , but the hotel is fabulous.  We were not able to enjoy many of the facilities, but the grounds are gorgeous, the location is perfect for Phoenix and Scottsdale, and the service is very good.  Beautiful landscaping, the rooms were very large as was the bathroom.  Beds were cery comfortable and we were on the 4th floor which meant no one was above us.  Bathroom had plenty of amenities.  Everyone we encountered was extremely helpful at the hotel.  I will stay there again on my next trip.

reviews.author: InNYfromGA
reviews.title: Nice property, slightly dated, lacking excitement
reviews.text:
If I had to guess I'd say The Phoenician was constructed in the 70s.  Maybe older.  The property is beautiful.  Everything is well manicured.  Everything was clean.  The property is luxurious but very boring.  Not the place for young people, unless you want to act like you're in your late 60s.  I wanted to take a nap the whole time I was there.  The oxygen tanks and walkers in the lobby/restaurants epitomize the mood.  

I was cashing in free resort nights with SPG so i didn't have to pay the outrageous rate for my room.  I saw that it was about $400 a night.  I personally feel like you can get more bang for your buck.  Having stayed previously at Westin Kierland, I suggest it over The Phoenician.  I was upgraded to a "casita" which didn't seem to be that much bigger than what I would think the normal hotel rooms would be.  The casitas are essentially a condo style setup, sharing outdoor stairs with another room or two.  Our casita was located in the "A" building.  Our balcony had a beautiful view of the pools and common area where they were having a yoga class on Saturday morning.  There were probably at least 100 people with their mats.  I guess that was kind of cool.  

The room itself wasn't anything special.  Normal sized room with a king sized bed.  Flatscreen tv and mini bar area.  The bathroom was nice.  It had a garden tub, two sinks, and a closet style shower.  The toilet was in a separate room with a door.

We didn't really do much at the property.  There are several shops with souvernirs, overpriced clothing, etc in the same building as the lobby.  There was a cool ice cream shop.  Pleasant Armenian fellow named "Shant," I think, was quick to offer samples.  

During the holiday season, The Phoenician offers a free shuttle to Scottsdale Fashion Square--a very nice mall about a mile east of The Phoenician.  We killed a few hours there...definitely no signs of a recession there.  
 
The entrance to The Phoenician has a manned guard station.  This keeps the rough crowd out but also prevents your food delivery driver to bring food to your room.  The food has to be given to a resort employee who then delivers the food to your room.  Slightly irritating.  Casitas have free parking directly in front of your building.  Anything free at this resort is a plus.  The concierge was very helpful.  I think her name was Jacque.

I prefer Westin Kierland over The Phoenician.  The Phoenician is nice, though very tired.  I guess I need a little more excitement in my life.

reviews.author: Robokrugie
reviews.title: Truly first class!
reviews.text:
This was our third time at the Phoenician, spend there 3 glorious nights and wish we could have spent more.. The grounds , the pools,the cactus garden all spotless and beautifully kept.
The food everywhere was delicious , the afternoon tea is a must - with little sandwiches, light scones and decedant deserts..Our room was spacious with a balcony overlooking the golfcourse - was very comfortable.We also visited their spa and had a couple of massages-was very impressed with how knowledgable the staff was and gladly personalized the treatments to my needs,also participated in a meditation class that they offer- wish I have done a couple more,I was very impressed with Cindy she is a gem - with a totaly different kind of meditation technique ,I loved it! I very highly recomend the Phoenician -it's truly a first class  place for a relaxing vacation!!! We will  be back next time for a longer stay...

reviews.author: Cisco96
reviews.title: Staff Took Great Care of Me With My Broken Foot
reviews.text:
OVERVIEW OF BRAND
Starwood Hotels & Resorts established the Luxury Collection after it acquired Sheraton (Sheraton had bought the properties from an Italian group and branded these unique hotels as Sheraton Luxury Hotels).  These hotels are intended to reflect each area’s unique culture or the historic building it is in (e.g., if it used to be a royal palace) as opposed to mirroring the look of other hotels within the brand.  Luxury Collection Hotels used to have a uniform logo (with four horses) but each hotel was allowed to design it’s own logo beginning in 2009, which may confuse some customers.

THE PHOENICIAN
This hotel opened in 1988, and it is located approximately 12 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX).  An affordable way to get here is to take SuperShuttle for about $16.00 each way (if reserved online) plus tax. The grounds consist of a massive golf course, tennis courts, a cactus garden, a spa and fitness center (in the Centre for Well-Being), a salon, and a barbershop.  There is a mini-mall called “the Shops at the Phoenician,” which includes a coffee shop, ice cream parlor, cyber café, wine and spirits shop, a fashion store, small art gallery, and a gift shop.  Self-parking is free while valet costs $29.00 per day. 

The in-room guest services guide states that there is a resort dress code with jeans only allowed during the day: “Appropriate evening wear is resort casual. Slacks, button-down or polo shirts, skirts, pants and dresses are acceptable.” I’d only brought jeans so I hid in my room the first night.  However, when I asked the front desk about this on my second day, the staff informed me that the rules have become more relaxed except for the J&G Steakhouse. 

Several staff members stated that the slow periods at the resort (i.e., when you may get better deals and more attention) is in-between Thanksgiving and Christmas and during the hot summer months.  

THE ROOM
This is my first stay at the Phoenician (over Thanksgiving Weekend), and I was assigned a “Deluxe Room” on the first floor of the Main Building (B Wing); my view consisted of a green lawn (on which people played badminton) and a large concrete slab.  In this type of room, you should find a 42” LG flat-screen (720p) LCD TV; a “mini bar” and fridge with soft drinks, wine, beer, and spirits (price range = $1.50 [small bag of chips] to $55.00 [champagne]); a pull-out couch; coffee table; desk; an iron and ironing board; a wall safe; and a Sony CD clock radio (ICF–CD–7000) with an iPod jack.  There is no coffee maker in the room.  The bathroom has a hairdryer, dual sinks, a cushion seat, and Remede bath products.  There is a patio with a round table, two chairs, and a lounge chair (for sun tanning).  There is WiFi and Ethernet; prices are about $13.00–20.00 depending on the amount of bandwidth that you want.

FOOD
There are 11 restaurants and eateries on the grounds.  I only ate food from two of them: The Thirsty Camel and Il Terrazzo, which both seemed to have the same menu.  Room service is available 24-hours with breakfast items ranging $7.00 (cereals) to $22.00 (Crab Benedict Plate); lunch/dinner ranging $8.00 (soups and salads) to $34.00 (steak and fries); and a limited after-hours menu ranging from $7.00 (desserts) to $17.00 (pizza).  There is an afternoon teatime (2:00–3:00PM) in the main lobby.  The resort does have the Kids Pass Program, which is an “all-inclusive dining program” for children 12 and younger.  Visit the SPG site for more details (www.spgpromos.com/kidspass/).

GYM AND POOL
The fitness center is located at the Centre for Well-Being, and it looked like a well-equipped hotel gym.  There are numerous pools and cabanas on the property, including one pool designated for adults only. There are exercise classes that you can sign up for (for a fee) and a daily guided-hike up the mountain.  

SPG SPECIFIC
There is no Club Lounge for the regular hotel; however, I think there is one at the Canyon Suites (an exclusive area of the resort).  Otherwise, there are no free food/drink perks for Gold/Platinum-Preferred Guests.  Platinum members do get 500 Starpoints, free Internet (regardless of what bandwidth you choose), and the resort fee ($29.00) is waived.  There is no “Green Choice” Program (where you waive housekeeping for points or credit) at this hotel.

I requested late checkout and was given 2:00PM (versus the 4:00PM typical for Platinum).  I’m not sure why as there was a mass exodus in the morning given it was the Sunday of a holiday weekend…and the beginning of their “slow season” in between Thanksgiving and Christmas.  Nevertheless, I know that SPG resorts don’t have to give late checkout (Sheraton–Carlsbad being the absolute worst about this), and I appreciated the 2:00PM offer.

OVERALL RATING
The Phoenician is a beautiful desert resort, though it may be uncomfortable for people not wanting a very upscale place with a rather homogenous crowd.  Yet, the staff is extremely friendly (esp., Bernie, a bartender; and Connie, a housekeeper) and they offer many interesting activities if you don’t care to golf, play tennis, or hangout by the pool.  For instance, I signed up for the “Adult Cocktail Making Class,” in which Kira taught us to make a pumpkin martini for the holidays, gave us generous samples of an Amaretto-infused warm-cider, and samples of wine—a nice free treat given the lack of free drinks for Platinum guests typical of most other properties.  I am also very appreciative of the chef who prepared me a special Thanksgiving meal for my room (which was not on the room-service menu) given that I was somewhat immobile because I recently broke my foot.  Overall, the Phoenician is a very nice retreat to come to, even as a “staycation” for the locals.

reviews.author: Geekontherun
reviews.title: Excellent service and they go the extra mile *****
reviews.text: I love this resort.  I had free nights that I needed to use and was able to convince anyone to take them so I ended up using them on a business trip.  I was stunned with the level of service at this resort.  They me at the door and knew who I was.  They walked me to my room where there was a delightful assortment of cheeses and snacks waiting for me.  They do have a fully stocked honor bar in the room with amazing choices including fabulous wine!  The room was spacious and beautiful with fresh flowers.  The bed was VERY comfortable and the bathroom was huge!  They had aromatherapy bath salts and amazing shampoos (I wish they sold them at the resort!).  The spa is amazing.  I did get a foot massage that I loved but made the mistake of letting her use the cups on my back (painful).  Monday through Friday the sommelier  has wine in the lobby of the suites hotel with tasty appetizers and home made breads (olive).  You must eat at the italian restaurant is is amazing as well.  I enjoyed every morsel and service was amazing!  The ice cream shop I also ate at in the morning and the food was equally as good as the food at the italian restaurant.  Stay away for D & G the food was not good and the service was terrible!

reviews.author: Matthew G
reviews.title: Great Resort, But Losing Its 5-Star Touch A Bit
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Phoenician for 2 nights in August with my family, and although we had a great stay and enjoyed the hotel, I think it may be resting on its laurels a bit.  I had heard of the Phoenician many times before coming to Scottsdale.  It had really been hyped up as the most gorgeous 5-star resort one could want.  However, I noticed some areas that could use improvement, just in terms of renovations and service.  I think one contributing factor to being less ‘wowed’ than I expected was the fact that we had just finished 2 nights at the beautiful Ritz-Carlton outside of Tucson.  Having that as a comparator, I still loved the Phoenician, but didn’t see it as quite the same level of service.  

The Phoenician is a large, beautiful resort, nestled right at the foot of Camelback Mountain.  Considering that it’s in the desert, it’s really great how lush and green everything is.  It’s like a beautiful island oasis, so they definitely put a ton of effort and money into creating this feel in the desert.  That impressed me.  The grounds are large, with lots of waterfalls, koi ponds, and palm trees.  It’s nice to walk around the resort, and in keeping with its desert location, there is a cactus garden on the Camelback side of the hotel. I guess it would also be really easy to do some hiking on Camelback from the resort.

The location was really great for touring the area.  It’s only a 5-10 minute drive from Old Town Scottsdale and all of its shopping, art galleries, and many restaurants.  We took advantage of that area for dinner each night.  It was also convenient to some of the attractions we wanted to see in Phoenix  (the hotel is essentially right on the border of greater Phoenix and Scottsdale).  It was also a very easy 20-minute drive back to the airport at the end of our stay. I loved being right in the middle of things, yet have the secluded resort feel when we were there.

We chose a grand deluxe room in the casitas.  I definitely recommend both this room type and the casitas in general.  I was very confused when booking a room online before the trip, so it was good to figure out what the different room types are.  Essentially, you have a choice between 2 locations and 3 views. The price only seems to differ by view, not location.  The 2 locations are the main building and the casitas (there are many more rooms available in the main buildings).  The main building rooms are in the 2 large horseshoe-shaped buildings on the side of the resort by Camelback.  This is where the lobby, restaurants, and conference facilities are located.  The other option is the casitas.  These are also arranged in a horseshoe shape, but they are a grouping of several small two-story buildings across the resort by the golf club.  The rooms here all have exterior entrances and parking right by the buildings.  We chose a casita room just to try something different, plus it sounded very convenient for parking and access to the pool, which it was! Even if you’re in the casitas, it’s only about a 5-minute walk up to the main buildings, which requires walking up past the 3 levels of pools. I actually thought it was a really pleasant walk at night.  I looked at the aerial view of the resort on Google Maps to get a good feel for how it’s set up before we arrived. 

In terms of the views, superior is the most basic view.   In the main buildings, this means looking across at other rooms and the hotel driveway. The way these buildings are built, one is built directly behind the other, so that rooms on one side of each look right into those in the other building.  In the casitas, a superior view would get you a view of parking lots.  Deluxe is the next view upgrade.  Deluxe is a view of Camelback Mountain and the cactus garden in the main buildings, but a view of the golf course and gardens in the casitas.  The best view is Grand Deluxe.  We went for this view and loved it.  Regardless of which building you choose, this is a view of the pools and beautiful grounds/gardens in the middle of the resort.  You’ll just be looking at different pools depending on which building you select.  

Our room itself was great, and very spacious.  We were on the second floor of the casita and loved the view.  The casitas do not have elevators if you’re on the second floor, but that wasn’t a problem at all.  It was so convenient to be able to park our car in the small lot right outside our casita, and just walk up the stairs and into our room.  Our room had windows on 3 sides, which is unusual for a basic hotel room.  The balcony was huge, and so nice to sit out on.  The balcony was completely covered, which was perfect in the August heat, and had a chaise lounge, as well as a table with 2 chairs.  We had a great view of the mother-of-pearl pool from our balcony.  The room itself was a great size, and decorated just as the pictures show.  The rooms are pretty neutral with a botanical sort of style.  It definitely wasn’t just redone, but it was still nice.  I think the rooms will need to be renovated soon to look fresher.  However, everything was in great condition and perfectly clean.  The bathroom was great.  We had a huge bathroom, much larger than what I’ve seen in other pictures posted.  It had a tub, 2 separate vanities, a walk-in-closet, and huge shower that could easily hold several people. The toilet is in a separate room with a bidet.  The bathroom definitely shows the age of the rooms.  The bathroom is very nice with marble everywhere, just doesn’t look like it’s ever been updated. 

We really enjoyed time at the pool.  There are several pools on different levels, each with lounge chairs and lots of noodles in the pools (some of which definitely needed to be replaced-they're cheap enough!).  The top level has multiple pools closest to the main buildings.  The middle level is the adults-only pool with a swim-up pool bar.  The lowest level is the signature mother-of-pearl pool, which is the one we chose to use, since it was closest to our room.  There is also a very fun pool slide by the lowest level pool. I recommend guests of all ages try the slide. It wasn’t too crowded at the resort when we were there on a weekend in August, so we didn’t have trouble getting lounge chairs ever, but I can see that it might be an issue other times of year.  A lot of the chairs are reserved for those who purchase cabanas for the day.  

Maybe it was because we were in a casita, and would come and go from there, but we didn’t encounter much of the staff.  The only staff I interacted with was the pool attendants, who actually left a bad taste in my mouth.  They essentially keep all of the towels in their cabana, and are responsible for bringing each guest a towel when they arrive at the pool, along with a complimentary pitcher of ice water.  They also serve drinks and food.  The first day I was at the pool, the staff must have looked at me and decided that I wasn’t going to be purchasing any food or drinks, and basically ignored me.  It took almost half an hour for someone to even come over with a towel and water pitcher.  In the meantime, the same few guests were being waited on over and over again.  Once someone finally did come over to me, there was no apology.  The attendant acted as if I had refused a towel previously and was bringing it over “just in case you need one”.  I don’t have a problem getting my own towel, and I honestly wish towels would just be out to pick up yourself.  However, if a resort sets up the pool like this, with attendants guarding the towels, I expect that everyone will at least be given a towel promptly.  I will say, the second and third days at the pool, the service was better. 

All in all though, we really did enjoy our stay here.  The grounds are lovely, and the room was really comfortable and nice. Time at the pool was so relaxing.  Looking at the lobby and some things about the rooms, though, I will say that the hotel seems like it’s seen better days.  It’s a bit over the top with marble for my taste.  It looks like it was built to be really flashy in the 1990s, but that’s just not the style that new resorts have today.  My parents were really impressed by the marble and crystal chandeliers everywhere in the lobby, but my brother and I thought it was a little over-the-top and outdated.  The rooms, while nice, were also not recently redone, and the bathroom definitely showed its age. Is it beautiful? Yes.  Is it a great resort? Yes.  Does it live up to its hype? Not quite as much as I expected.  I think it’s seen slightly better days, and service needs to get better (at least at the pool) to stay a truly 5-star property.  There is stiff competition for resorts in this area.  I recommend the resort highly, but I wasn’t quite impressed enough to say it’s the only place to go in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: azgirls2011
reviews.title: Fabulous
reviews.text: As a very special holiday treat we took our young teenage daughters to The Phoenician for afternoon tea.  There were ten of us (5 mothers and 5 daughers) and the experience was absolutely fabulous.  Wanda was our server and she was lovely, very warm and engaging and provided superior service with a sense of fun and genuine joy....truly a credit to your team.   The food was simply incredible, delcious sandwiches, light fluffy scones with real devonshire cream and lemon curd and decadent deserts.  The atmsophere was charming, we have lovely memories of our special afternoon together.

reviews.author: ellie411
reviews.title: Beautiful property - a very relaxing stay.
reviews.text: Stayed at the property with my husband and 3 teenagers the week of Thanksgiving. Overall, a very enjoyable experience. The grounds are absolutely beautiful, and the pools were fabulous.The service was, for the most part, excellent. All of the staff I encountered was very helpful and courteous. I, like many other people after reading these reviews, mistakenly wandered onto the golf course during my morning walk. The man who drove up on the golf cart was very friendly - even though he told me I had to leave as it was dangerous. They really should mark that better for us non-golfers! The rooms were comfortable, but I have to say the king sized bed that I shared with my husband definitely had a depression in the middle, which made it hard to sleep well. Not what you expect to find at a resort of this caliber. We had very nice breakfasts every morning dining at the outdoor restaurant and a really wonderful meal our last night at J&G's. The meal did last 3 1/2 hours, not sure why, but they should definitely pick up the pace of the serving. It was hard on my elderly mother and young niece to sit at the table that long. The spa was ok, nothing special, and like everything else, very pricy. Not sure if I'd go back to the spa next time. We already decided we'll come back to the resort next year, but will try to get a room closer to the elevators or maybe try one of the casitas. Overall, it was a very enjoyable experience.

reviews.author: PETER M
reviews.title: Wall to wall class.
reviews.text: From the moment you drive in off Camelback road you realise you are entering somewhere special. The long driveway that takes you past the Phoenician golf course up to the hotel is in itself spectacular. When you get to the hotel main entrance you are greeted by bell boys who take care of your luggage and valet park your car for you. Walking in the hotel it is then you know you have made the right choice of hotel, it is nothing short of spectacular. From that moment on it is first class all the way. The Grand Delux rooms on the first floor are the best in my opinion they are spacious with the most comfortable bed and spacious bathroom with a closet shower, these rooms make for easy access to the pools and the breakfast restaurant. There are 4 pools to choose from some with cabanas (for an extra charge). Each pool is exceptional with attendants to match, they will bring you a jug of iced water whenever you need it, drink and food can be served at your sunbed or there is a restaurant for lunch which sits beside the swim up pool bar. Your every need is taken care of at all times. We have stayed at most of the 5 star hotels in Scottsdale and none of them come close to the Phoenician. Trust me as I am a hotel snob and this is the best by far, all be it expensive, but why "slum it" when on vacation is the way I view it and with the Phoenician you get what you pay for and more. Try it once and you will go back I promise you that.

reviews.author: Sarah K
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Service not so much
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is beautiful. I stayed there with my husband and his business partners and their wives in mid November. I'll go through a list of pros and cons:
Pros: The views are amazing. The rooms are nice and pretty large. I love that the room we stayed in had a patio area and a view of Camelback. The pool area was a large and well kept. Breakfast at Terrazo was very good. 
Cons: Service was next to awful, unfortunately. We went to J&G steakhouse and dinner took almost 3 hours!! They did comp us two desserts because of this, but when your spending $700 on dinner, that doesn't do much. The food was okay, we went to Mastro's City Hall Steakhouse the next night and it was much better as was the service. We stayed 4 nights and had drinks each night in the lobby bar area. Getting a drink was like pulling teeth. I don't know if they were understaffed or what, but it was difficult to ever find a waitress. We ate breakfast at the Terazzo. The service again was lacking and they ended up comping our whole breakfast because of the wait (which was nice but we had "waited" our whole vacation so we were kind of fed up. The last complaint was the things you have to pay for. We expected to pay a lot for our stay, we knew this was an expensive place, but a few things were just really big turn offs. My husband had a business meeting. They rented a small room for one day, it was $500. No problem. Then they wanted an internet hook up for one IPad, they were told that would be another $500!! There was a marker board in the room, assumed it was included in the rental fee. But when they asked where the markers were, you had to BUY them!! It was a little crazy. I think the employee could see the distaste in my husbands eyes and comped him the internet connection. So they are good at comps, but not without irritating their guests first. 

We probably won't stay here again. It was a beautiful place for sure, but the little things, poor service, nickle and diming small things, just were too distasteful for us.

reviews.author: TNElvis
reviews.title: Storied property is run down--needs major interior renovation
reviews.text:
The Desert Southwest was arguably hit as hard as any region of the United States as a result of the Great Financial Crisis of 2007-2008. The ensuing economic downturn has led to cascading real-estate prices and diminished economic activity throughout the Valley of the Sun. This is all too apparent at the Phoenician, the once famous luxury resort located in Scottsdale, AZ. 

We traveled and met a group of friends in the spring of 2011 for a long weekend. It should be noted that the grounds and landscaping at the Phoenician are still immaculate... We went with the three day tennis package and stayed in a standard king room. The room itself was large enough to be comfortable and had a small patio overlooking the main entrance to the resort. The interior of the room was worn and looked about five years overdue for an upgrade. The same story was true with the bathroom--everything was worn and needed to be redone. This is not the trait of a five star resort.

The pool was nice and we rented a cabana for one of the days of our stay. The same theme prevailed with the cabana as it wasn't that clean and seemed rather worn. The service at the pool and cabana was average but friendly. 

The tennis facility was first class but the service there was a little behind the quality of the facility itself. It is highly recommended otherwise.

This resort has seemingly unlimited potential and it's a bit surprising that it's in the shape it is in considering it is a Starwood property. In the meantime the best options remain the Royal Palms or Four Seasons?

reviews.author: Gill H
reviews.title: First Rate
reviews.text: Not only is the Phoenician a beautiful setting it is blessed with having a first rate, well-trained and caring staff.  Beautiful pools, extensive cactus garden, and minutes to downtown Scottsdale restaurants and Old Towne.  Been there there three times and looking forward to our next visit.

reviews.author: Konrad D
reviews.title: Spectacular staff and facility
reviews.text:
This is one of the most memorable resorst I have ever stayed at.  The staff is fantastic on attending to your needs and wants.  They continually asked my wife and I if we needed anything, or what they could do to make our stay better.

I am quite a foodie and all of the meals were above my expectation.

The room is spacious and well appointed.

It is not cheap, but well worth the expense if you are looking for a beautiful facility and exquisite staff.

A great central location in the Scottsdale area.

Thank you Phoenician for a fantastic conference.

BG

reviews.author: amys839
reviews.title: Relaxation at its best!
reviews.text: This resort had it all-great service, beautiful and spacious rooms, excellent food, gorgeous facilities and the golf course is second to none. We enjoyed every second we were there and would only go back there!

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: The Phoenician
reviews.text: Excellent resort hotel . Great location , views are outstanding . great size rooms , excellent service and magnificent public areas . Food at all outlets was great . Wonderful sporting facilities .

reviews.author: 1travelerof6
reviews.title: Our favorite Scottsdale property
reviews.text: We just love this hotel and return over and over. Last time we stayed at the new Canyon Suites- loved the private pool and attentive service. Many restaurants on property provide different dining opportunities on longer stays, and the food in all of the establishment is delicious. We always rent a cabana and enjoy the attentive service, Evian water misters, towels, and sunscreen provided. The location is perfect, and the scenery is the best in Scottsdale. We just can't get enough of Camelback mountain, and we love hiking up the mountain in the early morning. Breakfast outdoors can't be beat- the views from the patio are gorgeous. Drinks on the patio are always fun, with the torches lit.

reviews.author: babara s
reviews.title: Wonderful food
reviews.text: I went to sunday brunch for an employee party it was absolutely fabulous. we had mamosa and played croquet the grounds were absolutely beautiful. I would love to go there again im trying to plan a vacation soon

reviews.author: CarlesseC
reviews.title: It doesn't get any better than this!!
reviews.text: The grounds are breathtaking, the service beyond belief, the accomodations are first class with the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in and the shower in the room is awesome.  I love the spa, the pools, the hottub, the restaurants.....EVERYTHING.  This was my 10th time at the Phoenician and God willing, I'll have 10 more!!!

reviews.author: Aunt M
reviews.title: a wonderful time of year - another wonderful visit
reviews.text: This is our 8th year that we've met up with friends to enjoy a long weekend retreat at this beautiful resort. We were there the end of OCT and left NOV 1st ... the weather was perfect! the resort and all the services were as they always are - outstanding :)  Highly recommend!

reviews.author: pemard
reviews.title: No one called us "guys" for 8 days!  For the most part, service was superior
reviews.text: The service personnel, from the busboys to the front desk staff to the golf pro shop folks, were obviously very well trained.  (Ironically, the only one I would say was not personable was the concierge.)  The grounds are lovely.  Golf course is pleasant to play even for a duffer, and has some lovely views.  Everything at the restaurants is high quality (yes, expensive).  Take advantage of the free morning coffee outside the Italian restaurant in the mornings.  Though you might end up having to walk a good distance depending on where your room is.  Someone else's review remarked about the hall carpets seeming to smell funny - I agree.  The only real complaint I have is the clock radio in the room.  The first night the opera CD started to play at 12:50 AM - could not figure out how to turn the darn thing off - had to pull the plug.  Then couldn't get the darn thing reset - too bloody complicated.  Bring a travel alarm or use your cell phone.  I asked some other guests about this at breakfast and they said they couldn't figure the thing out either.  We wanted to rent a car at the on site Hertz desk our last day, but they were sold out - so make your arrangements well in advance.  The food at the burger bar "Relish" is really tasty - but don't think you'll grab lunch there at the turn.  Wait until you're done with your round.  The service is good, but the food takes a long time to come out - prepare to relax.

reviews.author: mpkp
reviews.title: Resort Hotel
reviews.text:
Stayed here in Nov 2011 on Company weekend.

All that you would expect of large company driven hotel. Make sure to ask for a room that has a view over the front and not over the barren Camelback mountain or near the loading bay!

reviews.author: Ron M
reviews.title: Great conference location
reviews.text: Recently stayed here for a conference.  The hotel staff were friendly and helpful, and the property was beautiful.  The patio area adjacent to the bar, with its lounge seating and firepits, is the perfect way to spend a cool November evening.

reviews.author: Sandra P
reviews.title: Great Hotel
reviews.text:
This was our second stay at the Phoenician, lovely pools, great restaurants on the property, spacious room, great views, the staff overall just lovely. 
Unfortunatly the cleaning staff did not do a great job keeping our room clean during our 8 day stay (they don't vacuum and never windex the coffee table or desk top).  
J&G steak house located within the Phoenician is a must visit, the food, staff and views just amazing! Oh, also don't miss going to "Relish" the burger bistro on the property, yummmy burgers!!!

reviews.author: SavorSluthTraveler
reviews.title: Good hotel
reviews.text: Good hotel , but given options in this resort market, it was better then good but not FS or Ritz level of service.

reviews.author: Megan D
reviews.title: Not terribly impressed.
reviews.text:
My husband was speaking at a conference, so my 4 year old and I tagged along for some warm weather and sunshine.  The first day my daughter and I explored the grounds and had fun at the playground and pool.  She must have gone down the water slide 100 times, however the second day it was cloudy and we decided to explore the cactus garden.  Immediately above the cactus garden is the golf cart path, however we didn't know this was the golf cart path as there are no signs saying that you shouldn't be walking on this path.  We just thought it was part of the cactus garden.  As we were walking an employee (he was wearing a Phoenician vest and nametag, but i didnt get his name) on a cart comes tearing around the corner, we step off the path, but he must have been in a bad mood, because he felt the need to pull over and snap at us about not walking on the cart path and that it's not a safe place to walk.  

The room was pretty nice if in need of some new carpet.  Beds were comfortable.  The hallway was dark and dirty and smelled.  Everything was very expensive (including the little cafe), but I understand that when coming to a resort like this.  Most of the employees were nice, but I just couldn't help feeling like this is not a great place to bring a child even with the water slide, the pools, the playground and the kids club.

reviews.author: Bob B
reviews.title: You Get What You Pay For
reviews.text: I stayed at The Phoenician from October 26, 2011 to October 29, 2011.  The grounds are beautifully landscaped and occupy over 200 acres.  You have the choice to valet park ($$$) or self-park ($0) if you drive. The self parking is very convenient and is located beneath the main hotel building. Baggage was quickly and efficiently delivered to our room.  Check in was efficient, pleasant and informative.  The room was large, clean, very comfortable and had a nice view although we did not specify any view.  The beds were very comfortable.  The bathroom was huge and could reasonably accomodate The Village People simultaneously.  Although pricey, the food was delicious and the drinks were well mixed.  There are better selections for dinning off the premise if you have children or are on a budget.  The golf course while rather short was in excellent condition even though this is the overseeding season.  All in all, a wonderful place to stay.

reviews.author: Austin M
reviews.title: Engagement... Best time ever
reviews.text: I worked with the concierge to assist me with my engagement plans..  The hotel worked with me on every detail making this a trip of a lifetime.  We enjoyed a day at the spa as well as hitting the tennis courts in the evening.  I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking to be pampered by the staff and looking for a place to relax.  Thanks again for a great stay

reviews.author: jollyman45
reviews.title: Awesome Stay
reviews.text:
I just spent the weekend at The Phoneician in Scottsdale, Az and I could not have had a better stay.  The staff was friendly and knowledgeable and the complex was beautiful.  I got engaged here and the staff was exceptional in making sure that everything was perfect for the whole stay.

If you head to the Wellness Center, ask for Stacey (massage therapist) and Trish (facial).  Both were exceptional.

reviews.author: FSquared
reviews.title: Great weekend experience
reviews.text:
We spent 4 nights at the Phoenician in October of this year and had the most amazing time.
We were upgraded to a deluxe room with a spectacular view of the grounds facing south. We did not want to leave the room or balcony view. The bathroom products are incredible! However the pools are so tempting we had to experience all of them (There are 7) - and they were incredible! The pool staff is professional and the pool side menu is very reasonable for a property of this caliber. We did our best to experience all of the restaurants on site. The Relish Burger Bar has excellent burgers for all tastes and are very creative - you need to sample all of the special relishes! We dined at the Il Terrazzo restaurant for our anniversary dinner and for breakfast. The service and atmosphere was outstanding! We highly recommend dining there - the food is delicious and very well presented. They have an extensive wine list for all tastes and budgets. Coffee at the Ice Cream Parlour / cafe was a bit pricey @ $5 a cup but not unexpected at a property like this. If you so choose, the tennis facility is immaculate and the golf course looks great - lots to do without ever leaving the property! We can hardly wait to bring our family back in the spring to enjoy this property again! As a SPG Platinum member, we have experienced many great Starwood Properties and the Phoenician has become a new favorite!

reviews.author: travelingmomhhsc
reviews.title: What a treat!
reviews.text: We recently stayed at the Phoenician for a night when returning from Sedona/ Grand Canyon to await our flight home early the next morning. We had a large room with a huge balcony overlooking part of the golf course.  First time that my husband has ever readily agreed to having breakfast in the room, as we could eat on the balcony!  Had a great dinner in their restaurant. We were only there for such a short time, we really wished we could have stayed longer to experience all of their amenities. Can't wait till we can return to really enjoy it!  Concierge staff was great.

reviews.author: klf94
reviews.title: Another wonderful trip at the Phoenician
reviews.text: This is approximately our 10th trip to the Phoenician.  We usually go in October with several other couples and have never been disappointed.  The property is beautiful and very well manicured.  The service was wonderful everywhere from the pool to the golf shop, and the turn down service.  We enjoyed a fabulous meal at J&G Steakhouse, a great relaxing meal at Relish over the golf shop, and relaxing by the pool.  The rooms were in great shape.

reviews.author: Ryan G
reviews.title: Great place, we chilled by the pool. My mom had issue with the spa.
reviews.text:
we had a great time here during our fall getaway. We chilled by the pool and played  alittle golf and tennis. The food and service are great.

Even though the hotel itself is a little old, it still first class. We even had a celebrity sighting there.

My mom and wife went tho the spa one day to get their nails done and they totally over paid. My mom was furious. I think she said it was $90 each for a simple manicure only. She talked with the staff and they really didn't do much to make her feel better about it. 

So if you go, you will have great time as long as you go off site for some girly pampering at a reasonable price.

reviews.author: drdave60
reviews.title: Beautiful location, awesome service
reviews.text: My wife and I spent a long weekend in the desert at the Phoenician. It was my third visit, although the first where I wasn't on a business trip. I was a little concerned being at a big resort that has many conferences going on - I didn't want to get ignored while there. Upon arrival we were met by a friendly face at the front gate and the smiles from the staff never stopped coming for the entire weekend. The resort has top notch facilities but what sets it apart is the staff - each and every one seemed sincerely interested in taking care of our needs. Our room was typical of a resort set up, and the housekeeping staff was excellent.  All in all, a great stay. Small tip - don't be afraid to self park as valet runs a steep $39 a night.

reviews.author: letitsnow1
reviews.title: Needs Renovating, but Service is Excellent
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is gorgeous.  The lobby, the cactus garden, the restaurants, the pool.  However the INSIDE of this hotel needs desperately to be renovated.  Hallway carpets were FULL of stains.  Doors were battered as if they'd been rammed with luggage or housekeeping carts too many times.  Air Conditioner in room was noisy and inconsistent.They put a nice flat screen television inside an old TV armoire, and left all the dvd, stereo spots empty.  It was clear they updated the tv, just didn't want to through out the big tv furniture?    It was just.....old.  Having stayed at other luxury properties in the Scottsdale area I expected more from a AAA 5 Diamond Resort.  
As for room service, we ordered 3 times, each time was within 30 minutes, but when I ordered toast, they actually brought me cold bread and a toaster to make my own.  That was a bit surprising.  I've NEVER had room service bring me a toaster before.  Not sure what that was all about. 
Went for a polish change at the salon, where my esthetician, neney or something like that, proceeded to jab me in my nail bed with a metal cuticle pusher and then gleefully laughed when I yelled out in pain.  They then were audacious enough to add an automatic 20% tip.  My toe literally hurt for days, and she giggled more than once.  She was Russian I was told, and clearly found it funny.  That was the only thing she did with the metal pusher, and I'm curious if it was done intentionally. 
There were lots of GOOD things, though.  Amazing Staff.  I cannot praise the staff enough. Beverly Skripsy in Concierge was amazing.   Every single employee on the property went out of there way to greet you.  Housekeeping staff were friendly, extremely thorough, and spoke English when you passed in the hallways.  Loved that.  
Our server at J&G Steakhouse, Jason, was just perfect for us! From the maitre d to the busboys, everyone at the restaurant was friendly as can be.  
Our breakfast server at Il Terrazo, who's name I have forgotten, was also just a peach.

reviews.author: Rose48162
reviews.title: First trip to Phoenix
reviews.text: We were fortunate enough to book a room at the Phoenician on our first trip to Phoenix. It was a wonderful experience! The room was lovely, the pools were the perfect temperature, the breakfast delicious. My husband sent quite a bit of time in your cactus garden and I walked the paths at sunrise. Both beautiful. The High Tea with our daughter was the perfect way to end a delightful visit.

reviews.author: Pat G
reviews.title: Grand style and luxury
reviews.text: I attended a conference a few years ago at The Phoenician. Because I registered late, I wasn't able to book my accommodations at The Phoenician during the conference, but I extended my stay a day so I could spend the night here. The conference facilities were fabulous and the service was great. The room was very beautiful and luxurious -- one of the nicest hotels I've ever stayed in, including some of the great hotels in Vegas. When I checked in, there was a dish of fruit and cheese waiting for me. I had never had that before and I thought it was a very nice, welcoming touch. I don't know if they do this for all guests, or just because I was a conference attendee, but I liked it. I spent a large portion of the late evening floating in the pools -- I think that have about 17 pools at this property. Because it was late, and because there are so many pools, I had the pool to myself most of the time. I'm thinking they must have been salt water pools, because I just lay on my back watching the night sky for a couple of hours and didn't need an inflatable to stay afloat. It was a very beautiful, relaxing way to unwind. I guess the service was okay because I didn't have any bad experiences, but I don't remember anything outstanding about the service, either. However, I transferred to The Phoenician from The Royal Palms where I had the most outstanding customer service I've ever experienced anywhere, so maybe I was just comparing The Phoenician to that. Overall, a lovely place with a lot of amenities. I would definitely recommend it.

reviews.author: pfbird
reviews.title: Elegant but not Perfect
reviews.text:
I just returned from three days at the Phoenician. The rate of nearly $350 a night with taxes was lower than usual ($400-plus) because I got a conference rate. For that much money, my expectations were high, and rest assured, the Phoenician did a lot of things right. But it falls short in some key areas.

First, the strong points. The resort is in a spectacular setting at the foot of Camelback Mountain. The rooms are expansive, with balconies, bidets, top-quality linens, and marble bathrooms that feature oval soaking tubs, glass-enclosed showers and elegant toiletries. There are many thoughtful touches. As a nod to the dry climate, lip balm is included with the bathroom supplies, and a bottle of water is left on the nightstand as part of the turndown service each evening. The staff is uniformly friendly and helpful.

Most of the public areas and restaurants are impressive, offering fountains, art, and lovely views of Scottsdale and the mountains. The menu prices are high, though, and I was hard-pressed to find a bottle of wine under $50 in the signature Italian restaurant. Wines by the glass ran from $12 to $20.

The grounds are equally attractive, landscaped with flowers and cactus plants throughout, and including several swimming areas on two levels. There's a spa, a golf course, and even an on-site cactus garden.

But there were some disturbing shortcomings. Unlike many fine hotels, there was no coffee service in the rooms or in the lobby. Guests are directed to the expensive restaurant, or they can pay $9 for a four-cup pot delivered from room service (before fees, taxes, and gratuities). The Phoenician also has poor wireless service, for which it charges $12.95 a day, something provided free at Red Roof Inns across America.

In stark contrast to the beautiful lobby areas, the carpeting in the guest hallways appears stained and threadbare in places. And within the lovely gardens and grounds, the ponds looked dirty, not a great environment for the many koi fish swimming through the waters. A dead fish floated in one of the ponds.

By and large, the convention areas work well, and the food service is competently executed. Here again, though, there were shortcomings. At one evening panel presentation, the sound system failed entirely at one point, and was hard to listen to the rest of the time.

But all in all, it was a delightful experience. My advice, though, it to shop around if you’re going to Scottsdale or Phoenix. There are many lovely resorts at less than $200 a day, and the savings could pay for a lot of fun.

reviews.author: Traci S
reviews.title: Lost and then Found
reviews.text: I was recently asked for a recommendation for a hotel in the Phoenix area.  My friend requires great service when she travels.  I had only one hotel on my mind when she asked for my recommendation.  I told her that the best service in the valley comes from the Phoenician.  This jogged a memory of recent trip in August.  One thing to know about the Phoenician is that the grounds are quite large and there are so many beautiful parts of the hotel.  Unfortunately, I am one of those women that breathes life into the stereotype that women have no sense of direction.  And so, I found myself quite lost on the grounds of the Phoenician with 2 young tired children, lots of bags and high temperatures.  I must have looked dazed and confused because an employee of the Phoenician approached me and asked if she could help.  She had already figured I was lost.  Her name was Carolyn and she introduced herself to me and my children (which really impressed me).  She quickly took my bags and asked me my room number.  And rather than pointing me in the right direction she escorted me to my room.  We had a few a minutes to chat (like I said the grounds are really sprawling and I was on the wrong side of the hotel).  She was so kind to my children.   I had the chance to ask her what her job was at the hotel.  I truly expected her to say that she was a concierge with her welcoming service.  She told me she worked in the banquet department.  This just showed me that the service at this hotel runs deep and that its not just the folks at the front desk putting on a good show.  And the service continued at the Ice cream Parlor and the pool.  We had a great time and will back again.

reviews.author: DBC925
reviews.title: Friendliest staff anywhere
reviews.text:
We were here for 4.5 days in October, to see Jimmy Buffett on Thursday night and the Steelers on Sunday.  Despite the fact that Scottsdale is on the other side of Phoenix from these venues, we picked the Phoenician.

Much has been written thus far about the opulence of this resort, and most of it is true. 

Golf, biking, hiking, tennis, swimming are all available without leaving the resort.  The equipment is all new-ish and up to date, and the rec area featuring the clubhouse and tennis garden are an easy walk from the main building.

There are several bars/lounges in the resort, but as a warning, they are all very low-key.  If you're looking for nightlife, you're going to have to leave the Phoenician.  In fact, the only live entertainment while we were there was a guitarist that can only be described as "coma-inducing" playing in the main lobby off of the Thirsty Camel bar.  This was really the only drawback to the entire resort.

The staff though, is what makes this place.  From the valet to the front desk to housekeeping to the bartenders, tennis staff, pool staff and grounds crew, everyone was on top of their game.  You never passed a staff member in a hallway without being greeted, and on more than one occasion, they even asked out of the blue how our stay was and if there was anything that they could do for us. 

There are several pools, including one that is "adult-only".  Getting chairs was not a problem, as the pool staff continuously monitored unused chairs and replaced old towels with new, and moved belongings to a common area where they could be picked up by their owners.  Great idea to keep people from "reserving" chairs at 9:00 AM only to not return until 2:00 PM.  We've all seen that at every resort.

If you're looking for a relaxing place to get away from it all, The Phoenician in Scottsdale is an excellent choice.

reviews.author: Jayson G
reviews.title: Best Group Services Staff
reviews.text: We completed a very complicated program with 3 separate but overlapping back-to-back conferences very successfully. We couldn't have done this without the dedication of a very skilled and talented team of hotel professionals. For my responsibilities in housing and attendee services, we partnered seamlessly from the start with our counterparts in Convention Services and Group Reservations as well as the Front Desk staff. We especially would like to acknowledge the efforts of Ms.Tori Paul and Ms. Mallory Willson, for endlessly going above and beyond to make the impossible happen for our challenging and demanding annual group. They've continued a standard of excellence against which to benchmark for future years programs.

reviews.author: RJDUK
reviews.title: Great trip
reviews.text: This is a beautiful hotel with plenty of staff all eager to make us feel at home. We enjoyed hanging out by the pool with our kids and watching a football game in the Relish Burger Bistro. Looking at the majestic Camelback Mountains in all thier ruggedness while relaxing in luxury is great!

reviews.author: gellybeanlovescake
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Absolutely fabulous! We got a great deal that brought the room price down several hundred dollars. Not sure what the deal was, but keep an eye out in early December. Perfect time of year! Everything was just fabulous - service, rooms, food, the grounds. I wish we could have stayed longer. We talked about coming back again with the kids (we felt bad seeing the three different pools and slides, knowing how much they would enjoy). The wonderful soaking tub helped to ease the guilt away. We did some easy hikes on the grounds and enjoyed the desert landscape and wild life. We even went on a walking art tour. Since it was December they had a huge gingerbread house display. I'm missing it already ...

reviews.author: K L
reviews.title: Wonderful Property!!
reviews.text: We stayed at the Phoenician in September and what an absolutely PERFECT time for a visit! The guest rooms are fantastic, large, clean and the beds are awesome! The large property is fantastic and the pools were terrific. At the times we swam no one was ever in them so we had them nearly all to ourselves most of the time. The food was fabulous and the customer service was remarkable. The staff really new how to cater to us and we had wonderful experiences with the concerige as well. We will definately stay at The Phoenician again!

reviews.author: CanadaFamily
reviews.title: Very...nice
reviews.text: I stayed here in the July heat with teenage daughter. The hotel was very spread out. We were quite a ways away from the main hotel. Arriving in the dark, late late at night, it was very difficult to find out way to our block of rooms and no escort was offered or provided. The pools are very nice, although brutally difficult to find chairs. The resort pools seem to be open (for fee, I assume) to locals who use it as a personal backyard pool-- over half of the kids my daughter hung with were locals. The dining was expensive, but the quality was very high. Room was spacious and well attended to.

reviews.author: Paula H
reviews.title: Couldn't have been better
reviews.text: This place is amazing - far and above CUSTOMER SERVICE!  They truly know that the customer is what makes the business successful and respectfully go out of their way to exceed expectations.  I spend over half the year in hotels and this one is at the top of my list!

reviews.author: fasiVirginia
reviews.title: Loved It!
reviews.text:
My husband and I recently stayed at the hotel.  Loved everything about hotel.  We stayed in a one bedroom at the Phoenician Canyon Suites.  The room was beautiful and the service everywhere on the property was spectular.  The food at the resort was absolutely delicious.  The location was perfect, easy to get to anywhere off the property.  I am going  back again in November and I am  trying the main resort instead of the Phoenician Canyon Suites - no particular reason, just to see what the rooms are like in the other part of the property.

The Phoenician Canyone Suites were a 2 minute walk to the main facility.  

Loved the resort - loved the service.

reviews.author: Derek H
reviews.title: First Class Service
reviews.text: My wife, 9 month old son, and I just went down to the Phoenician for the weekend.  The most notable thing was the outstanding service.  The property itself is spectacular, and being from Seattle, the weather was refreshing.  Il Teratzo on site was very delicious. Relish was a great spot with good food too.  My only dislike of the whole experience was that everything was overpriced; but what else would you expect really? It was a bit challenging to navigate the property with a stroller, but rolling through the Cacti garden was great and probably an underrated asset to the property.  Free coffee in the morning at Il Terazo, and news paper were nice.  Awesome pools with a slide.  Overall a fantastic resort and I would highly recommend it.

reviews.author: Diane G
reviews.title: Great hotel, spa prices ridiculous
reviews.text: The Phoenician is a five star hotel....no doubt about it.  Everything is first class however the spa pedicure price is just ridiculous !!  The price is $90 and it is no better than pedicures I get at spas in and around Los Angeles.  At $90 maybe throw in a manicure with buffing at least.  The facility was very nice and the girls who worked on us were great but the whole experience was not $90 worth.  If you want to get a manicure or pedicure while there I would look into going into Scottsdale.  I complained to the hotel and they did not offer to reduce the charge.  Bet five years ago they would have but with the economic downturn they listened politely and left it at that.

reviews.author: embqk3
reviews.title: Wonderful place if you can find a good deal on the room
reviews.text: We were able to get a great deal on the room for our stay, which was nice because everything else at the hotel (food, drinks, spa, etc...) is very expensive. Other than than being pricey the hotel was wonderful and I would highly recommend it.

reviews.author: Carolstapenhorst
reviews.title: Wonderfull hotel!
reviews.text: A Very big Room, a wonderfull pool, Nice place To walk around, lot of options of entertainment inside hotel area. Be carefull cause a lot of things have an extra charge, even the gym room.

reviews.author: Denise C
reviews.title: Users Conference
reviews.text: Attended a users conference at this resort.  I found the accomodations to be excellent.  The staff were superior and always helpful.  It was obvious they specialize in meeting and often exceeding the needs of large groups.  There were about 1,200 participants in our group and meeting rooms, meals, and comfort was exceptional.  I would look forward to having another conference at this resort.  I am not a golfer, but those that were had all positive comments about the golfing.  The conference rates for rooms were affordable.

reviews.author: a c
reviews.title: I am planning a return trip very soon!!!
reviews.text: My stay at this hotel was amazing!  The best customer service:  everyone really went out of their way to take care of me...incredibly nice and gracious.  Awesome, huge room...facilities and grounds that have something for everyone:  excellent fitness room, incredible pool, stunning golf course..it was the best.  Every moment of my stay could not have been better.  This is a hotel I will return to often.

reviews.author: BingoBubbaMommy
reviews.title: Excellent room
reviews.text: We absolutely loved The Phoenician. Gorgeous sprawling property, rooms are huge. The pool was great. We loved the Spa and had one of the best facials ever, The bunnies running around were a joyful bonus.

reviews.author: thetravelingspears
reviews.title: Relaxing time with Husband and our new baby.
reviews.text:
My husband and I decided to stay here for two nights over Memorial Day Weekend 2011.  Our baby was about a 3 weeks old at we were given the okay by our Dr to travel with him.  

My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed ourselves here.  We stayed in a standard room that overlooked the front of the hotel.  We loved it!  We managed to have a mini-romantic evening, relaxing on the balcony (the outdoor furniture is very nice) while our son slept peacefully on the bed.

We at the Thirsty Camel, Il Terrazzo, and The Relish.  Thirsty Camel's didn't have many options.  I enjoyed my roasted chicken with potatoes from Il Terrazzo, and my Turkey Burger from The Relish was delicious...I highly recommend trying this place.

We plan to visit this place soon recommend this hotel for both couples and families.
