What, like there are no other staff that could substitute in a hotel that size? If I were manager I'd be on reception in such circumstances, as it's the first thing a customer experiences. I generally don't go back to hotels where I have to wait to check in.

Prior to our visit we'd been offered the chance to upgrade to Grande Deluxe rooms for an extra $10 per night, and the rooms we were given (3139 & 3141 on the main floor at one end) were a very good size. Our double room had a king-sized bed, desk and coffee table with sofa and two armchairs; our kids' twin room was similarly generous in its proportions. Both had nice, large & well-appointed bathrooms. Everything looked pretty new, although the corridors outside the rooms were rather dark.

All the rooms in the main building appear to look out onto the 'Oasis' - a group of pools circling around a bar, cafe and waterslide. Our kids (11 & 13) really liked the pool area since in addition to the basic attraction of water to swim in, there was a volleyball net and a basketball hoop - both of which provided excellent excuses for making friends with other kids staying at the resort. Backing onto the pool area are two large lawns which were laid out for croquet which was also a nice thought.

Bell service throughout both stays was very good - valet parking, luggage and so forth were all handled efficiently and politely. Sadly, this was about the extent of the good service we experienced. What went on at the restaurants was pretty much at the other end of the spectrum.

Firstly, we were somewhat surprised on arrival at breakfast the first morning to be asked if we'd made a reservation. For breakfast? You have to be kidding, right? Not all the tables inside or out were occupied, but even to sit inside we had to wait a few minutes before being seated (had we wanted to sit outside, I think we were told the wait would have been 15 minutes). When you're on vacation at a top-class resort do you really want to have to figure out the night before what time you're going to get up and have breakfast? I think not. Once seated, things didn't really improve. We had breakfast three times in total during our stays at the Phoenician, and on each occasion we had to wait a long time (in one instance, nearly 15 minutes) before being offered any drinks or menus. That's just unacceptable. The breakfast buffet - something our kids love about resort vacations - was also rather limited: it seemed as though the hotel was much more geared to a la carte breakfast. The other thing that struck us was that the staff didn't appear to be at all efficient - tables were left for a long time after guests had departed before being cleared, something we would not expect to see at a quality resort, especially outside as it attracts birds scavenging for leftovers which is not hygienic. 

Poor service was not unique to Il Terazzo, either. We had lunch one day at the poolside Oasis restaurant, which had a very pleasant ambience, but had to wait a spectacularly long time for very straightforward fare. And when we chased our order, the waitress said something like "I'm sure it's coming as fast as the kitchen can go". Errrm, well maybe you could check it's not already waiting for us on the pass perhaps or find out how long it's going to be? 

Our second stay we again opted for upgrade to Grande Deluxe but this time things went a bit pear-shaped. Our kids are 11 & 13 and while they're perfectly capable of taking care of themselves, it's kind of nice if you're on holiday as a family to be located in the same part of the hotel. So we were a bit surprised to be allocated 3108 and 3014, which are at least 100 yards apart, separated by the hotel lobby. Unfortunately, because we were out to dinner and had only taken one set of room keys when we originally checked in (because the other room wasn't ready), we didn't realise this until 10pm by which time it which was too late to do anything about it. To their credit, when I raised the matter the following day with the reservations department, they recognized their error and credited us the $10 upgrade premium.

One more thing - when are hotels going to realize that they should include internet for free, not charge for it? If Starbucks can do it, so can Starwood!

So - to summarize - lovely hotel, shame about the patchy service. But a decent manager could put that right in a heartbeat.

reviews.author: dlc66
reviews.title: Wonderful experience
reviews.text: I went with my 17 year old granddaugher for a quick 3 day trip over her spring break - this is our second trip to the Phoenician.  We absolutely loved it.  The service aand hospitality are without question the best I have had anywhere in a long time.  All our requests were promptly attended to and even things we didnt ask for were thought of by some member of the staff and taken care of like delivering forgotten items to our room. Leah in the gift shop went out of her way to find something we had wanted and wasnt availabe in the shop and without asking found it and had it delivered to our room.  The food in both restaurants was excellent and we were comped for a glass of wine and dessert for no reason other than a little wait for the entre.  I must say that I do have a certain preference for room type and location athe resort and there are some rooms that are not located in best part  and are too dark and without a view so avoid those.  All grounds and recreation areas are beautiful - spa very good also.  We cant wait to go again.

reviews.author: Neep
reviews.title: Luxury!
reviews.text: Awesome room, fabulous surroundings, wonderful pool area.  Friendly staff.... and it was near to wonderful Scottsdale.  I just hope to return one day.

reviews.author: Rk1972
reviews.title: Beautiful, Hot & Fun
reviews.text:
Stayed with our children and another family the grounds are beautiful, pools are great, food was wonderful and service was excellent. Would go back in a heart beat.

Food at il terrazzo was great service from Nick and Jennifer outstanding. Pool service was wonderful lots of chairs in the sun and plenty of umbrellas, Jared provided great service with food and drinks.

Rooms were good able to sleep 2 adults & 2 young children easily. Housekeeping did great job.

Tennis center was fantastic. Lessons with Jonathan or playing singles or doubles worked. If you want early times book before you go. 

Kids activity center was great for kids, wii, movies, air hockey. Perfect to get kids out of sun for part of the day.

reviews.author: TravelerFromColo99
reviews.title: Food Service is not real good
reviews.text:
The first words out of the bartendar's mouth today were 'It's going to be awhile before I can get to you.'  Hmmm  it's 11am on Saturday and all I wanted was a soda for the kids.  There were only 3 people at the pool bar when I walked up (nobody wanted to take the order at the pool).  I was here 1 month ago and found the same  level of food service.  

We're staying in a casita suite and the showers have mold and mildew. It's not the cleanest hotel I've stayed in!

reviews.author: Sheicor
reviews.title: Birthday Getaway
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at the Phoenician in Scottsdale for the first time a week ago. We went to relax and celebrate my birthday and couldn't have had a more pleasant experience. The service was exceptional and the grounds and guestroom were just beautiful. There is really a well run machine....but the most memorable moment was when one of the pool attendants recoginized my husband at the pool, where he had forgotten his sunglasses a day before (not that he remembered WHERE he had forgotten them), and told him he had found them he then brought them to him. I wish I could rememeber the attendants name :-( I would recommend this property to anyone that wants to experience luxury, exceptional customer service and comfort. Kudos to the Management Team and staff!!!

reviews.author: 3TULALIP
reviews.title: WORST SERVICE AT A NICE PROPERTY
reviews.text:
We live in Shanghai, and travel the world frequently for work and leisure.  This was supposed to be a very relaxing vacation at a nice resort.  I can only say that the only good service here is at the pool.  The Italian restaurant on property (Il Terrazzo) has really bad service, which forced us to meet our friend from Phoenix at a different restaurant when they could not seat us.  We were at the reservation desk when a woman came up and canceled her reservation, and they had 11 tables at 8:30 PM that were not full.  Surprising they could not fit 3 for dinner.

The next night we had a great meal at Cowboy Caio, in Scottsdale, away from the hotel.  Well worth the cab ride.  But don't think about using the Phoenician car--it is twice a cab ride, and they don't allow cabs to wait here at the hotel.  The goal of this hotel is not customer service, rather it appears to be "once we have the suckers here, how can we suck the most out of them".

Dinner tonight was the the final insult.  Over 30 minutes for a cold appetizer of antipasta.  And the duty manager thought 30 minutes was fine.  He tried to explain that 30 minutes was perfectly acceptable because they had many European clients who did not want to be rushed.  However, the Europeans at the table next to us, were complaining loudly about the terrible serive as well.  So, if you want to have a really, really slow drink, appetizer, and meal experience, you can come to Phoenician (thanks Daniel, Duty Manager).  Everything is about 50% overpriced, and they don't care.

Finally, the additional complaints include the transportation.  $50 a day to rent a bicycle, and if you want a cab other than their cars, they delay calling one, and it takes about 20 minutes (town is about 5 minutes away) to get a cab to take you.  It appears that the bellman's job is to suck as much cash out of each guest as possible.  I would avoid this resort at all costs--bad management, bad policies, but workers that appear to be trying hard.

reviews.author: timbotravel50
reviews.title: Work in Work Out didn't Work Out
reviews.text:
I purchased the Work In Work Out package where you pay in advance to use the gym with internet included. Was thinking to be able to work hard at the hotel then be able to work out and enjoy some of the resort on my off hours.  Lets just say I wish I went to the many other resorts in Scottsdale. First thing, there was no wi-fi in my room.  While they claimed it's available anywhere in the resort, my room had no signal and when calling every single day of the seven days that I stayed, they gave me the same lame excuse that they're putting it on the priority list. But nothing happened.  They have a two foot wire that you could plug into your laptop at the desk- but I could stay anywhere if I wanted to be cramped in the corner to surf online. Plus in the modern day of ipads and iphones there's no ethernet plugin.  So you're SOL.  

Secondly, the gym closes at 7:30pm (6pm weekends).  So you work hard all day and can't wait to go for a run or have a steam in the sauna only to find you've got :30min to pack it in.  

I'm sure there's lots of other things that are good about this place but the poor customer service in dealing with the main reason I came here stained the experience.  Never again. Lets just say if you're coming to Scottsdale for business and you rely on certain things that you can get from a three star hotel but you expect to happen in a 5 star, take your money somewhere else. You'd probably get a better deal.  I'd recommend Sanctuary as I've stayed there before and they're amazing.

reviews.author: SurLeNil
reviews.title: Excellent Location, Average Rooms
reviews.text:
The pros:  The hotel is centrally located to many attractions in the Phoenix and Scottsdale area to include Fashion Swuare, museums, nightlife, and restaurants.  The hotel grounds are impressive with the art work, golf courses, tennis courts, swimming pools and the cabanas.  In fact, the pool cabanas and the service provided were outstanding -- you pay for it but we were not disappointed with the level of attention.  The breakfast offered at the Il Terrazo was very good but not great.  We also had dinner one night and were very pleased with the food, service and wine recommendation.

Cons.  The rooms are a little dated and could use an update.  We were in the Casitas and found the bed to be good but below what we would expect from a top tier resort.  Additionally, little things like no I-Pod chargers are annoying when so many of us travel with these devices.  In the children's activity area, the WII did not work and the activity area is in a fairly isolated part of the hotel by the tennis complex.

In closing, we had a really good visit and will probably come back again.  However, there are definintely areas that the hotel could improve upon.

reviews.author: peytonisrad
reviews.title: Such an amazing resort!
reviews.text:
The hotel itself is breathtaking. It has a giant driveway up to the main lobby which shows the expansiveness of the property really well, including a full golf course. The lobby is completely gorgeous with a big fountain out front & marble flooring throughout.
The room wasn't super amazing decor wise but we had a room with 2 beds in it & it still felt very large & every room comes with a balcony. The bed were SO comfy with great comforters & pillows.
Also, the bathroom was giant too! It had a big tub, double sinks, & at least a 3 person glass shower with amazing shampoo & conditioner. The staff really goes above & beyond by leaving a personalized note from the housekeeper that is cleaning your room outlining the hours she'll be coming by, etc. Even though we never saw her or needed anything, it was a nice touch having a name to put with our thank you tip.
We had breakfast at the Il Terrazzo restaurant outside & had the cutest waiter, Tom! He was so nice & absolutely hilarious, joking around with us & just all around super friendly. The buffet was delicious too. I would highly recommend it with the omelet bar, SO GOOD! The drinks at the pool bar were a little watered down & waaayyyy high priced but it is a resort so it's to be expected.
Overall our experience was amazing. From the 9 pools [with a waterslide!!], to the comfy bed & giant shower. Just be prepared to shell out some serious cash if you want to eat or drink anything at the hotel but again, it is a resort so most already expect that.

reviews.author: Mojodyno
reviews.title: I can't imagine visiting Phoenix without staying at the Phoenician!
reviews.text: Great service throughout the entire hotel, unbelievable golf, great amenities, well managed, nice bar atmosphere and close to shopping. Just do it!

reviews.author: penntf
reviews.title: Fantastic AZ Destination
reviews.text:
I was fortunate enough to stay at the Phoenician in Scottsdale for a work function and was there for 4 days.  The property was fantastic and the service was great.  Although the choice to stay at the Phoenician was made for me by my company, I walked around everyday wondering if I would want to come back.  The answer is yes.

The resort is very beautiful with the desert mountains in the backdrop.  The resort offers so many activites from golf, volleyball, pool, spa, etc.  It's really a great resort if you plan on spending multiple days in one location.  It's certainly perfect for a family getaway as there are a lot of activities to keep many people with different interests busy.  

I chose to take some time at the spa.  My massage was wonderful and I'd recommend the spa to anyone who visits the Phoenician.  

The only thing that disappointed me was the value of the experience.  Great venue, but very pricey.  For example, I ordered coffee, oatmeal, fruit plate, and orange juice for room service for breakfast and the total came to $52.00.  I order room service often and that's about $25+ more than I usually get the same order for.  This is really my only complaint.  

That said, the service was great and accomodating.  Rooms and resort was clean.  Pool looked great, although I didn't have time to lounge.  My colleagues thought the golf course was incredible.

Although the value was missing, I'll be back.

reviews.author: Angela N
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
We have stayed at the Phoenician probably 5or 6 times. It has been one of our favorite hotels. But this stay we have noticed a great decline in some of the services and cleanliness of the rooms. We were told we could get an early check if we came early to be in line for the first available rooms. We had to wait and it was only an hour before regular check in instead of the noon time we had hoped for. A server spilled my daughter-in-laws drink poolside and gave her the sticky glass with minus about an inch of her drink and just laughed. We returned one evening and the valet staff were standing around chit chatting and just left the car there running. We waited until finally we had to ask them to go park the car. We had two rooms which we paid $10 extra a night per room for a view. I wondered what the room without a view was like. One of the rooms was okay but the other was looking right into a tree top not seeing much else. I asked for an adjustment and they said they would check into it. Still have not heard back. The shower could have been cleaner. Very expensive to eat on the property. No coffee maker in the room. We like to make coffee while getting ready in the morning but you have to get dressed and go to the restaurant to get your complimentary coffee. Quite pricey to have a car on property also. But if you are coming and going throughout the day it is worth it but just to park it very expensive. A bottle of water was $6.50 and there was a charge for 15 minute increments for internet use. 
On the positive side it is still a beautiful location and there were many very helpful and pleasant employees but we did scope out some alternatives while there for 8 days for our next visit to Scottsdale.

reviews.author: IndyTravelGal
reviews.title: Impeccable Service!
reviews.text:
I spent four nights at this wonderful place with an intent to enjoy some sun, spa treatments and a three day conference.  The service was impeccable.  I arrived late am to the hotel and was allowed to check in early to a very nice grand deluxe room.  The receptionist was so nice and throughout my stay I was always greeted with a smile and a hello.  Twice when I was walking the grounds (which were beautiful) the front gatesman offered and gave me bottles of water.   The staff also brought pitchers of ice water to the lounge chairs at the pool  (it just would appear as I had my eyes closed just relaxing in the wonderful sun).  As you can tell I live where we haven't seen the sun since October.  
 I ordered room service twice and it was in my room within 30 minutes and the food was fantastic.  I also ate at the Il Terrazzo for breakfast and the Oasis for lunch (3X).  I found the food to be very good (loved the strawberry and spinach salad and again the staff/service was great.  
I did two signature spa services at the Centre for Wellbeing.  I was a relaxed "noodle" after my hot stone massage and the facilities had a wonderful sauna and steam room.  Service was again extremely good. 
It was great getaway but way too short.

reviews.author: Charles V
reviews.title: Quality has slipped at the Phoenician
reviews.text: This was my 5th or 6th stay here.  In the past it's been a luxury experience. Not so much this time. The casita rooms we had should be remodeled. Screen doors didn't work properly, carpets looked old, bathroom door didn't close, telephone message light wouldn't go off (even after reporting). Dimmer switch in bathroom was shorting out (we reported it).  Pool bar closed at 5pm  (2 hrs before sunset) and there were still customers at the bar when it closed. That was really annoying--why not call a supervisor and ask for backup bartender coverage?!  That should be expected at a Luxury Collection property.  Pool bar looked shabby. Glass waterfall features at pool were covered with calcium deposits and possibly mold in the corners--they need serious cleaning. Croquet hoops on big lawn above pool were rusty and bent looking, game equipment in disrepair and tossed about lawn.  However, brunch at restaurant was good. Housekeeping staff and turn down staff were very good. Front desk staff pleasant.

reviews.author: haleyalex101
reviews.title: BEAUTIFUL! but they charged a lot for some items
reviews.text: Overall the hotel was great! Room was clean and tidy, and so was the hotel. The only problem was that they tried to charge you extra. For example, a bottle of water in your room is $6.50, and to use a computer was $5.99 for 15 minutes. another example is one day we did the dune buggy tour(which was GREAT!) and we wanted to clean our clothes, $8.50 to clean ONE SHIRT! But besides that minor problem, it was GREAT!

reviews.author: sisaac
reviews.title: Beautiful spot, but does not have its act together on service, or dining
reviews.text:
Staff are friendly and smile, but vary widely in experience and service orientation. Examples: I called room service for dinner on a Monday evening (Monday mind you) and was told it would be an hour wait. It was suggested that I go to the Lobby Bar ara for quick alternative. Did so, but had the same hour wait, as the kitchen was the sam kitchen for room service.

Upon check in told staff I was a Platinum Starwood. They could not find my record. They finally did, but  Ihad to tell them what I was entitled to as a Platinumn.

They charged a portege fee for luggage transport in and out, but when I call edn thjem at check out time they never showed up. IO called back in 20 minutes and was toile that the bell desk had not been informed. As I was in a hurry I took my own bags down.

The fiorst room they gave me was dingy and overlooked the roof of the pool. As a Platinume I should be automatically offered an up grade if available, not a downgrade. I had to change rooms.

When I checked out there was a restaurant charge on by bill that wasn't mine. I called it to the attention of the person who was checking me out, and she went inot the back, came out with a mountain of paper reciepts, and began to look through manually. As I had a flight to catch, had a driver waiting, and lost a half an hour due to the bell service I left. It was subsequently cleared up the next day.

I could go on, but you get the picture. Everyone was very nice; few were very good.

reviews.author: NBfromArlington
reviews.title: Beautiful setting, uneven service.
reviews.text: The hotel is set right up against the mountains, with a beautiful cactus garden for morning or evening strolls.  Service was spotty, however.  The staff were wonderful when not busy, asking whether there was anything they could do for you.  But room service had an hour wait for a simple bowl of soup, and the operators did not answer the phone for over 7 minutes when a colleague called.  Phone and internet reception were spotty also.

reviews.author: Alyjoy133
reviews.title: Beautiful charming resort
reviews.text: The things I liked about this resort is it isnt as huge as some of the other properties in the desert. The service and cleanliness is amazing. Rooms are large and very classy. Pool area is very nice with attentive staff refreshing your water constantly. The spa was amazing too.

reviews.author: MinnesotaMom651
reviews.title: disappointed
reviews.text: This was our second stay at the Phoenician, and unfortunately it did not meet the high standards set by our first visit. The room was dusty, mildew in the shower, had to call for housekeeping service one day, very slow restaurant service and not enough chairs by the pool. Overall, an incredibly beautiful place that is showing a lot of wear and seems to have lost the friendly staff we encountered four years ago.  For the money, I think there are better values in the area.

reviews.author: santhony
reviews.title: Very Nice, Obscenely Expensive Resort
reviews.text:
First of all, everyone knows that The Phoenician is hideously expensive.  If you go to a resort like this and agonize over the price and the hundreds of ways they scheme to separate you from your money, you're going to ruin your vacation.  If you can afford to stay at a resort like The Phoenician, just enjoy yourself and pay the bill when it comes due.  That said, it should be recognized that this resort is not just hideously expensive, it is obscenely expensive (example, three soft drinks from the on-course bevarge cart will run you $18.  A hamburger at Relish, the clubhouse grill is $16).

We traveled with a couple who were attending a medical convention, so received a favorable room rate.  We stayed in the casitas and I can highly recommend them.  While they are removed from the hotel itself (a short walk), they are immediately adjacent to the golf clubhouse and spa.  The rooms were very nice and surprisingly quiet.  The beds were very comfortable and the shower pressure was amazing.  I don't understand how they can get away with that kind of water usage in the desert, but I promise you, you could fill a swimming pool with the water that shower put out in five minutes.  No complaints whatsoever concerning the accomodations.  In addition, the surrounding grounds are beautiful and impeccably maintained.

My wife utilized the spa and was very happy with the treatments and the service she received there.  We did not experience the pools, but they were lovely and I'm sure very servicable.

The golf course sports three nine hole tracts and we played the Desert/Canyon nines.  Simply put, this is not an impressive golf experience.  First, it was VERY crowded and pace of play was a problem.  The length of the round exceeded five hours and that is unacceptable.  The course is also VERY short, measuring only 6,000 yards from the tips.  While it is only a par 70, most championship courses measure closer to 7,000 yards.  As a result of its lack of length, many of the holes are "tricked up" and poorly designed.  For example, a 303 yard par 4 with a pond in front of the green, requiring a mid iron off the tee and a sand wedge approach; a 97 yard, sharply downhill par 3 that you could throw a ball to; and numerous par 5s reachable with short iron second shots.  It could be fun under some circumstances, and the conditioning of the course was not bad, but there are dozens of better golf options within a 30 minute drive.  The practice area is marginal at best and the range was actually out of golf balls.

We did have one particularly bad experience upon completing our round.  As we finished very near dark, one of our travel companions neglected to remove his $400 range finder from the cart.  The cart was taken directly to the cart barn to be serviced for the next day's play.  Without question, the range finder was discovered in the process of cleaning the cart, but was not turned in to lost and found.  This has happened to a group of mine on two other occasions (once involving a watch).  In those two instances, after being initially told that the property had not been located, the head pro ultimately went to the service area, read the Riot Act, and returned with the property.  For two days, Phoenician staff showed little or no interest in recovering my friend's range finder.  Finally, they offered him a cheaper model that someone else had lost and never recovered.  I suspect if he keeps his eye on e-Bay, he may recognize his rangefinder for sale by someone with a Phoenix/Scottsdale address.

We had lunch at Relish and the pricey burgers were very tasty.  We dined at J&G Steakhouse with a fantastic view of the valley and the food there was excellent as well.  The Sunday brunch was only average at best, with not nearly enough food available at the buffet, sending long lines snaking through the restaurant.

Bottom line, this is a sumptious, beautiful, full service resort that has fantastic accomodations, a very nice spa and an average golf course.  It is convenient to the airport and sports very nice restaurants and service.  It is also obscenely expensive, so don't sweat the small stuff or you'll ruin your vacation.

reviews.author: boylanmichael
reviews.title: Not acceptable for 5 diamond resort
reviews.text: Our reservations were made at the last minute and we were givin a room overlooking the rooftop, marginal, but acceptable, the room was nice, clean and comfortalbe.  The pool area was very nice and the attendants very courteous and accomodating.  We made reservations for the fine dining resturant (J&G, I believe) for 8:15 PM, our table was not ready so they asked if we would wait in the bar area and wait we did for at least 5 minutes before we were acknowledged. (there were very few people in the bar at the time)  We had a drink and were seated about 8:45 PM.  I had asked for seating near and overlooking the city, as it was are anniversery, we were ushered to a table  in the back of the resturant behind a piller with no view.  When we asked for different seating they assured us that there was none available.  Our waiter was hurried and very annoied with us, we waited unusually long for menus, water and felt like the wait staff was not properly trained or had too much service area to maintain.  We elected to leave the resturant after only having appitisers.   I would not give you a good recommendation for a top quality resort.    Respectfully,  Michael Boylan

reviews.author: Bmercouple
reviews.title: Beautiful Property - Unresolved Billing Issues
reviews.text:
I attended a conference at the hotel last week, and my wife travelled with me so we arrived a few days early.  This is a beautiful hotel, kept up very nicely, and there are no complaints about our stay.

Unfortunately, there were a couple billing issues that I have yet to resolve.  Since my wife checked out of the room while I was at meetings, I did not see the hotel bill until yesterday.  On our arrival day, we were charged $28 for "Porterage", but we did not use any bell staff, ask for bag assistance, and we used self-park (not valet) the whole time we were there.  Additionally, there was a $5 per day (PLUS $0.47 in state tax) on our bill.  I really get tired of getting nit-picked to death with all of these fees and charges, and this charge was not disclosed at check-in.  We had tipped the housekeeping staff each day, so we essentially paid twice for what used to be part of the room price.

The worst part is I called the hotel's "Guest Billing" department yesterday morning, and as of nearly 30 hours later I have yet to receive a response from them.  Additionally, I sent them an e-mail late yesterday with all of the details and have not heard anything back from that method of communication either.  I understand billing errors occur, but there is NO excuse for such a "luxury" hotel to not respond to my questions/concerns.

reviews.author: RoxieMoxie
reviews.title: Superb hotel experience on every level
reviews.text:
Gorgeous room with balcony overlooking lawn and pool. Bend over backwards service--down to the smallest detail.  I hurt my foot and asked for ice one night. The next day fresh ice was in my bucket--though I never asked. Exquisite grounds. Restaurant meal was extremely memorable for all 6 in our party. 6 pools!  Hotel overbilled me on Internet service and when I mentioned it they immediately removed the whole charge,no questions asked. One of the best properties I've ever stayed and I was there 4 days on business.

2 improvement area:  Our lunches (that corp., client ordered) were not top drawer. Hotdogs, salads, tuna wraps. No imaginative dishes.

Had to pay for Internet.  $12.95 a day and  bill incorrectly said $25 and $30. a day. But they removed charge when I asked.

reviews.author: AMMJK
reviews.title: Superb vacation
reviews.text: If you are looking for a resort that offers gorgeous views, gracious service and one of the quietest rooms you will ever find in a complex, consider booking into the Phoenician. Our week long stay in the 3rd week of February was memorable--breakfast on the patio of our room (in the 200s area) with a view of the lovely grounds and distant Scottsdale, a stunning mother -of-pearl pool, wonderful walking through extensive facilities, and very fine food.   You can take a long day trip to the Grand Canyon, made particularly special by lingering winter snow.  The management and staff are to be complimented for their friendly, polite manner and effort to make your stay very enjoyable.

reviews.author: dado4007
reviews.title: Just OK
reviews.text: Let me just say this is the first time I've ever written a review so for me to actually write something takes alot.  This is my 4th trip to the Phoenician and while the views are great and the grounds look nice, the actual inside of the hotel is showing its age.  The bathrooms have always been awesome - especially the showers, but I had mold in my shower this time and the showerhead was just a trickle of water.  The carpet is worn and it just looks old.  In the meeting room which is the newest addition, you could tell the difference and it was first class.  However, when we had the dinner and we couldn't tell if we were having fish or chicken, that's pretty bad.  (It was fish that was terribly over cooked.)  It's overall still a nice place, especially the pool area, just not worth the price they change.  I would still come back, just don't expect 1st class.  Hope this helps.

reviews.author: Frank49022
reviews.title: We thought it was not worth the money.
reviews.text:
This was our third stay at the resort and we felt that the rooms are looking worn (carpeting and wall coverings).
We were part of large group and were assigned double beds.  They did not have a king available but said they would contact us the next day if one became available.  We never heard one way or the other. A call would have made a diference.l

reviews.author: martythegreat
reviews.title: Looking shabby in places, "nickel and dime you to death"
reviews.text: They should charge an extra $50 per night and stop charging $6 for a cup of coffee, $7 for a bottle of water, $13 to use the workout facilities and $14 for internet access! The property was overgrown and confusing, the hallways show the hotels age. They are trying but need to get with the program. There are better places to stay!

reviews.author: Deb94939
reviews.title: Dirty Sheets, Shower Light Fixture Falling Our of Ceiling
reviews.text:
We did our research and cross-referenced gold lists, web sites and even tripadvisor. We decided to splurge and book a casita. This choice was a disaster.

In a nutshell:  Dirty sheets in one bed.  Holes in the sheets in the other bed.  45 minutes to get a key that worked so that we could even get into the remaining rooms of our suite.  The light fixture was falling out of the ceiling in the shower.  Gum stuck on the pull out couch bed.  45 more minutes to get a roll away (after waiting the first 45 minutes for functuning keys) because extra sheets and blankets were nowhere to be found.  

If you think you're going to a relaxing, luxurious vacation at the Phonecian, you're not.

reviews.author: amieli
reviews.title: This was a great stay the hotel is bigger than expected, but staff was friendly!
reviews.text: I enjoyed my stay at The Phoenician, the beds were very comfortable and the pool was beautiful.

reviews.author: elpsusi
reviews.title: der Knaller
reviews.text:
Was soll man zu diesem Hotel sagen? Das ist einfach nur der Knaller. Das fängt an bie der Tiefgarage in der man sehr angenehm seinen Wagen parken kann und hört bei tollen Restaurantes auf. Die Zimmer sind einfach ein Traum. Riesig groß und mit den feinsten Möbeln ausgestatte. Unser Bad alleine hatte bestimmt 15 qm. Die Poolanlage ist tip top sauber und von einem Botanischen Garten umgeben. Diese Hotel ist einfach der Traum auf Socken, wenngleich wenn man ein wenig auf sein Geld schauen muss, so gibt es auch schöne Hotels in der Nähe welche ein wenig preiswerter sind.
Aber einmal sollte man dort Urlaub gemacht haben.

reviews.author: taaroa1
reviews.title: Looks nicer than it is
reviews.text: First off, beautiful grounds, views etc. I disagree with most of the complaints as far as the bars, restaurants go. I thought they were generally fine. The food and atmosphere was very good. My problem was with the service and the value. First day there we had to wait almost 30 minutes to get menus at pool bar. Lunch (salad and fish tacos w 2 drinks) was $68, ouch. Second day the concierge seemed annoyed we were asking for some recommendations. Add that to the fact that they wanted $19.95 a day for WiFi and $10 day for the fitness center!! Transportation to town (2 miles) was $13, would have expected a complementary shuttle from such a high end property. I wasn't in a cheap room either, I was paying for an Executive Suite!! For the money I spent, all of those things should have been included. Seems like the 5 Diamond award was from some time ago.

reviews.title: OK
reviews.text:
The negatives first. J and G Steakhouse was a big disappointment. Service was mediocre at best and so was food. When I got my final bill e-mailed to me there was a charge for the spa for which I never went to. Called the hotel after I got home and they said that they couldn't do anything until acounting was in on Tuesday after Presidne't's Day. Where was the manager?

Room was good. Carpet outside or elevator was dirty and old and various walls need to be painted. Attention to detail is lacking for such a hogh end hotel.

reviews.author: flashg709
reviews.title: Beautiful hotel, great service
reviews.text: I went with several friends for a golf outing and had a wonderful experience.  our first hotel room (one of the suites) had an ant problem so we were moved to a new room.  the front desk offered 10K starwood points, which certainly made up for it.  the hotel is massive and has scenic views.  staff was extremely friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: debmanj
reviews.title: Beautiful setting, beautiful room but it is not up to its previous level of service in the bars or restaurants.
reviews.text: The hotel staff themselves are gracious and helpful. The room was beautiful, large, and extremely clean.  My complaint is with the restaurants and bar.  I dined with friends at J&G steakhouse, and at the Il Terrazzo.  Service was slow and inattentive at J&G.  Food was mediocre, with extremely small portions for a steakhouse, especially vegetable sides.  Il Terrazzo was definitely better, with an enjoyable meal, but again rather slow service.  The Patio Bar was atrocious.  Patrons had to get up to request food and drink. Servers seemed to disappear.  It seems like the slow down in  tourism over the last 3 seasons has led to a slowdown in (restaurant) responsiveness.

reviews.author: Cartman1968
reviews.title: Beautiful rooms and beautiful property.
reviews.text:
I always start with the negative reviews and after reading them I will be extra careful with my valuables here.  I do not like their policy of having to pay for the room upfront when making the reservation either.  But that said, this is a really beautiful resort and I would reccomend it as a romantic getaway or for a family visit.  

The rooms are beautiful.  The beds are luxurious and comfortable.  The bathrooms are huge with a nice big jacuzzi.  The cacus garden and nature trail is OUSTANDING!  You will see all kinds of birds, cactus, lizards, small mamals- it's beautiful.  There are bunnies hopping around all over the resort!

The pools are just incredible too.  There are like 3 or 4 of them that plateau down hill.  I saw Jennifer Love Hewitt in one of the cabanas here one time!

The food here is excellent too.  I would try and get a deal on your rooms as the resort is kind of expensive.  The golf course is nice too but not so nice for the environment.

I am hesitant to reccomend anywhere is Arizona since it has become a cesspool of racists but if you have to go here this is a great place to stay.

reviews.author: jimludwig18
reviews.title: Absolutely outstanding
reviews.text: Upon arrival we were told by the clerk that we were being upgraded to a suite.  We figured a living room/ bedroom combination.  When we entered the room it was unbelieveable.  It was over 2000 square feet with 3 balconies and every possible feature.We can't thank the hotel enough for this experience.  We are Starwood customers for life.

reviews.author: Sybarite_11
reviews.title: Excellent Service
reviews.text:
The place is very nice and the service is truly excellent.   From the moment you step out onto the hotel driveway until the moment you check out, all the hotel staff is there to greet you with a smile.  Furthermore, they are quite accommodating.

1.  We were a little late to our dinner at Il Terrazo, so our friends went to the restaurant bar for a few drinks.  The hostess gladly moved our dinner reservation a little later, and we did not feel rushed at all.  For breakfast, they offered to prepare us a fresh meal after the buffet closed since we were only there for a half hour.

2.  We went to the hot tub at 11PM.  The pool service was already closed.  Room service gladly delivered some wine, not to our room, but out to the hot tub area itself.

My thanks to the valet, front desk, restaurant and bar staff, pool service, and spa staff for your professional and hospitable service.  We will definitely return.

reviews.author: minaroya
reviews.title: Good Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel is truly beautiful.  There hotel grounds are immaculate.  We tried the Il Terrazo restaurant the first day for breakfast.  We had to enter the patio through the formal dining area because the entrance was not open.  We asked the waiter to sit us and he did that immediately but after we were sitted the manager came and told us that we had to go through the hostess and all the table in the section we were sittiing was taken.  We got up and went through the hostess and were sent to the same area for sitting.  There was lots of empty tables.  Also, there were lots of birds feeding off of customers tables.  This kind of offended us and we chose not to eat in the hotel restaurants.  This was a shame because we really wanted to try their other restaurants.  The only one we tried was the ice cream parlor which had light breakfast and the people were extremely polite and service was fantastic.  Also, they have travel desk that can  help you with your sightseeing and they really gave us great tips and saved us lots of time.  The hotel rooms feel very private in the way that they are designed.  The cactus garden is absolutely beautiful.

reviews.author: mmmmm1998
reviews.title: Beautiful hotel
reviews.text: Went to AZ with my husband'sand his family! The hotel was beautifully decorated the grounds were breathtaking. Our room was ok, there was paper that had fallen between the bed and night stand and upon checking in it was there on the floor. I guess they don't vacuum in between the furniture. Our view was of camelback mountain which we were litterally looking straight into the side of the mountain it was werid. Not sure it's worth how expensive it is.

reviews.author: sadoski
reviews.title: Renew your body and mind for a low nightly rate in the summer!
reviews.text: Check out their summer rates!  You can book rooms at more than half off their normal rates when you book during July - August!  I had first visited this hotel on my honeymoon 10 years ago.  My husband and I had visited ever summer for the following four years (then children came along)!  I returned recently as a "girls getaway".  It was just as amazing as I remembered.  Luxurious, spotlessly clean, spacious rooms.  Complimentary fluffy robes for the length of your stay. Scheduled turn downs, soft mat placed at your bedside for comfy tootsies from the moment you wake up!  I love the multiple pools option.  Feeling like a good splash or a just want a relaxing moment poolside?  The option is yours.  Dining facilities are worth the visit.  A little expensive, but the food, atmosphere, view and service is well worth it.  The Wellness Centre is just that, a place to make you feel good.  Meditate or have a spa treatment.  There are many to choose from.  (The Bindi Treatment is my favorite).  Complimentary robes, flip flops and lockers are offered to you at sign in at the Wellness Centre.  I am not a golfer, however, my husband is.  I volunteer to drive the golf cart so that I can enjoy the beautiful scenery and read a book for a relaxing morning.  Scottsdale has a lot to offer people traveling alone and with families.  Upscale neighborhoods, shopping, dining, etc.

reviews.author: dugald b
reviews.title: Splendid hotel ... no complaints.
reviews.text: This is a fine hotel! The room was big, the bathroom fittings deluxe, the bedding and towels luxurious. The public spaces, indoors and out, are grand and well kept. The staff are well trained and courteous. We will return.

reviews.author: Njenk58
reviews.title: Great Hotel !
reviews.text: Wonderful property - would go back again in a second!  Excellent food and staff.  The rooms are absolutely luxurious.  They feature fine linen bedding, beautiful views and newly renovated bathrooms.  This is a gem and has great golf too.  The pools are huge and the fitness center was excellent as well as the spa.  Had a terrific massage and great meals.

reviews.author: travelbugged4
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: Stayed with my 2 kids under 10 and in-laws.  Very disappointed in the service of the resort...especially the restaurant at breakfast.  Beautiful resort and lots to do.  Kids loved the pool.  Probably would not stay again because it is a lot to pay for not getting quality service.

reviews.author: gseb10
reviews.title: nice but chintzy hotel
reviews.text:
Great place but $10/person to use fitness center is ridiculous. Charge a little extra for the room if you need to. I felt the same about the pro shop. They would not let me return balls I had just bought even though I had not opened the package. 
Obviously I am being picky but I do not like to be "nickled and dimed" when I am staying at an exclusive resort. Internet access was not free either.

reviews.author: goferris
reviews.title: Service is Worth the Money
reviews.text: Stayed here recently on a leisure trip to enjoy the sun and warm weather. The hotel is very clean and elegant, but it is a bit dated and could use some modernization. The service is, by far, the best service I've received. The front desk handled a small issue immediately and surpassed my expectations. The concierge (Jacque) made wonderful recommendations and I thought it was great that the concierge desk was open later into the evening than most other hotels I've stayed. The grounds are impeccably kept and manicured and the pool wait staff was very attentive. My first of two small gripes is the high cost of internet access ($12.95/day). Why are hotels still charging for this option in 2011?!? My second gripe is the shower head. For this caliber hotel, I expected a better shower head than something at a 2 or 3 star hotel. It was very loud, unadjustable and pounded quite hard on my skin. Overall, I will definitely stay here again--even if just for the service!

reviews.author: Kelly B
reviews.title: Best Place I've ever stayed in the USA
reviews.text: This hotel was fabulous from the moment you step on property. I've stayed at Ritz-Carlton's and at Four Seasons and for Scottsdale Arizona you can't beat this property. The service is wonderful meeting your every need, the rooms are spacious, comfortable and have beautiful views... I would suggest going for a view room because all have balconies. You really can't beat this place. I would also suggest you rent a car because you will need to drive here and there to a few places. Old Scottsdale is great as well. The other thing I should mention is that we stayed at this property and they were sold out, however when you went to play tennis, use the fitness center or walk around it seemed as though you were the only one in the property! That was great and something I loved.

reviews.author: DanyL32
reviews.title: A bit disappointing for the price !
reviews.text:
Often, I feel that if the price is high, it's nice and clean, but beware the price for this hotel is not representative of the quality of the rooms. The rooms are clean but a bit old, due to be refreshed. For the rest of the hotel, everything is beautiful and luxurious. Many swimming pools, walking areas are beautiful on, and quite private.   Prices for a la carte restaurant are extremely expensive

The Fairmont Scottsdale Princess is truly superior, even luxurious and the prices are more affordable.

reviews.author: Katia P
reviews.title: Absolutely gorgeous resort!
reviews.text:
We loved this resort!  But be sure to get a Casita as they are stunning and the location is convenient to everything.  Even the one bedroom casita's are huge, and plenty of room for 4 people.

In our opinion this is not a casual resort.  Being Aussies, we quite like walking around in bathers, flip flops etc., however we felt we had to dress up around the resort.  It is very upmarket.  But in saying that, such a beautiful place.

The pool and waterslide are fantastic and our kids (ages 11 & 13) loved it and spent hours there.  We had lunch by the pool every day and whilst the food was expensive, it was really good. 

We also ate a lot of room service and it was quite good - not fantastic, but quite good.  Once again, very expensive.  Everything about this resort is expensive, but you get what you pay for.

reviews.author: Jadrija
reviews.title: Luxury
reviews.text:
Everything is as they say: luxurious, grande, clean, excellent, top of the line service, you feel welcome at every moment and everywhere.
We weren't able to enjoy all of the amenities (i.e. I don't golf), but they are obvious end extraordinary. Like heated swimming pools for example. Outside was -2C (28F), but kids were playing in the heated open pool. 
Service was extraordinary. We even got the Mercedes R350 with a driver to take us to the other side of the resort (some 300 meters away) for the New Year's party (and back, of course, when the party finished). Also, we didn't like the first room we got - it was changed in a minute with the much better one - no questions asked!
All in all - great 3  nights stay.
The only drawback might be the price, but - you get what you pay for!
P.S. Don't miss to visit Frank Lloyd Wright's Taliesin West and a desert botanic garden!!!

reviews.author: Lucky12345042
reviews.title: Wonderful
reviews.text: Wonderful stay at this resort.  Highly recommend, and I am very particular.  Only drawback was paying for WiFi and would like tea and hot chocolate offered with morning coffee.

reviews.author: saipantraveler
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, wonderful service
reviews.text: The staff was extremely friendly and helpful.  The hotel grounds were immaculate.

reviews.author: dishmktg
reviews.title: What happened to the Beautiful Meditation Atrium?
reviews.text:
I have been bringing my family to the Phoenician for the Holidays nearly every year for the past decade. One of the highlights of our stay has been to enjoy the peace and tranquility of the meditation atrium. We loved the light colors and many beautiful plants. We also participate in the wonderful meditation classes and enjoy the unique meditation music that is played.

We were extremelly disappointed to see the atrium has been altered and no longer looks inviting nor relaxing. The floor is cold and hard, and the walls have been destroyed by horrible, depressing colors that do not inspire meditation nor relaxation.  The addition of a carpet in a very deep color with a pattern that represents "union skins" creates a dizzy effect against the grout pattern of the flooring. We were wondering who would decorate in such a way, and if that person was educated as to the use of the room, and colors that are more appropriate for the intended purpose. 

We hope this will inspire the hotel to take a serious look at this room and consider making the appropriate changes. The room just depressed us.

reviews.author: forrest73
reviews.title: beautiful facilities and great service
reviews.text:
the phoenician is one of the nicer resorts i've stayed at in a while.  the facilities were very nice and up-to-date.  the service was also impeccable.

we had some out of the ordinary requests and they were able to accommodate us which was a plus.

we also scheduled a spa appointment / massage which was also great.

bottom line: great place to stay if you're looking to relax.  a bit on the pricey side but still a good value.

reviews.author: Giovanni Jose
reviews.title: Impeccable service
reviews.text: The staff were so friendly, it almost seemed surreal how genuine their smile and hospitality were. From the moment we checked in, the front desk staff did their best to put us in a nice room. I highly recommend the privacy of the casitas, where we chose to stay. We had lunch outside at Il Terrazzo and inside for dinner. The Sunday buffet was well worth the food, service and ambiance overlooking all of the pools, yes, all (there are 9). The dinner inside was delicious, from the fresh olive bread, arugula salad, the shrimp/lobster bisque and the salmon with clams, leeks and potatoes, took us out of our element. Although there is a $10 charge for the Fitness center, it didn't matter because the service they offered was high quality which included a meditation room, steam, sauna, jacuzzi and access to all locker amenities. In addition, the grounds were kept in its highest form, with a trail on the camelback mountains as well as numerous gardens and Southwest Artwork. There is much to do here and you won't be disappointed in whatever you choose to take part on.

reviews.author: unique78
reviews.title: AMAZING
reviews.text: This was my first trip to Arizona. The location of this resort is perfect. Everything you could possibly need is all within a 5 minute drive. This includes a great nightlife (every type of club desired from dance to hip-hop to posh); a mall with every store (from Gap to Gucci); restaurants galore (although I recommend the laid back restaurants like the TeePee.. more bang for your buck and the food is honestly better). But back to the resort... The pools are perfect. The weather was only in the high 70s but the pools are heated so feel free to take a dip. There's a gorgeous mountain just behind the resort which I climbed (for a city girl I'm proud :)). the rooms are spacious and clean.... huge flat screen tv... soaking tub... I could go on and on. i will definitely be back!!!!!

reviews.author: edandmer
reviews.title: Made our trip an amazing experience!!!!!
reviews.text:
My family and I switched to The Phoenician late one night after our other hotel refused to help us after we found a snake in our room. We called The Phoenician and they were more than happy to help us. 

I explained to the hotel front desk at The  Phoenician what happened at the other hotel and how upset my two children and myself were. I guess they could hear the fear in my voice and they quickly helped to make me feel at ease. They took all my information while asking information about my trip, my family, whether we had eaten dinner, and anything else that popped up.

When we got to the hotel, about 10 PM, we were quickly unpacked and escorted to the front desk where they were waiting for us to check in. One of the ladies took into account how upset my kids were with their terrifying experience and had a stuffed animal for each of them waiting at the check in. The front desk even took the time to make sure that room service allowed us to order food and have it delivered ASAP for the children. We were given a beautiful room and taken care of like family. We loved the room, the pool, the water slide, the hotels, the amenities,( great products and lip balm) and the restaurants are awesome!!!

There is not one thing I would change about The Phoenician! We are traveling cross country again this sumer and we are going out of our way to spend some time at The Phoenician! We will be back this summer!

reviews.author: PleasantlyRachelle
reviews.title: Beautiful resort that Sparkles with great views for day and night!!
reviews.text:
I was blessed to stay at this resort and meet the wonderful Staff and tasted some pretty amazing food. My room was facing the east/ south so the sunrises were amazing! I had views facing Phoenix sparkling at night from my huge terrace. I think December is a great time to visit because the weather was perfect too . Crisp and a a little breeze. Perfect for golfing or hiking some trails. 
A super special place for an amazing 5 course meal with perfect pairings is the Praying Monk - a working wine cellar where you and ur closest 9 friends can be enlightened through food n drink. 
Elizabeth Anderson is so wonderful. For being such a high end resort she is super personable and friendly to the guests and ( what I thought was most noteable is she was friendly to her staff too!) 
I have been telling everyone about my stay at the Phoenician! Loved it! 

PS The pool glows at night lush trees providing shade during the day and privacy from the view of the rooms at night. Opened 24 hours!! Great for night owls like myself!

reviews.author: mommybaker
reviews.title: Best Hotel experience in the US
reviews.text: High level of service, attention to detail, Had dinner at the Praying Monk  multi course meal every morsel and accompaning wine, fantastic! gorgeous pools, spa. i really love this resort. Al Glover @ the Praying Monk was phenomenal  . Great meeting spaces or just relax... i heard the golf was great also.

reviews.author: SDG13
reviews.title: Usually Great...
reviews.text: This Phoenician has been a destination of mine for 21 years. It is a gracious lovely property and a well run hotel through all the changes it's been through over time. One of the highlights is usually the spa/gym called The Center for Well Being. Unfortunately, during this visit, there were renovations being done and there was no access to the spa or locker rooms. We were told to use the facilities at the Golf locker rooms and found their facilities also being worked on. Not sure if we would have stayed somewhere else but there should have been some forewarning of this prior to our stay. One other thing, the room we stayed in needed freshening. There were stains on the carpeting and on the couch.

reviews.author: SadieDog03
reviews.title: Great venue for a wedding weekend
reviews.text:
Stayed at The Phoenician recently for a destination wedding.  100+ people had traveled to Scottsdale for this wedding.  Most of us stayed in the Casitas at a very attractive rate (well under $200 per night).  We were in building B which was very convenient to the hot tub and not too far from the main building.  Outside the back of our casita was a nice lawn, gazebo and waterfall (where the wedding photos were taken). For those staying in a second level of the casitas, they had stairs to climb with luggage if they didn't use the bellman to help. Didn't have the opportunity to dine in any of the restaurants but from looking at the menus and talking to others, the prices seemed high......but it is a resort.  Didn't come across anyone that was too impressed with the burger venue. As many reviewers have commented, the Internet charges are pretty ridiculous.  The room & bed was extremely comfortable.  I give this hotel 5 stars due to the fact we paid so little for our room.  If we paid regular rates, I would probably only give it 4.
The wedding aspect of the trip was very nice. After the church ceremony, we came back to the hotel for lawn bowling on the East lawn, then a cocktail reception in the garden. Very pretty, though the weather was a bit unseasonably cool.  I was a bit surprised that the reception was in a permanent "tent" structure, but it was still very nice, though you did have to walk outside and into the main building to use the restrooms.  If traveling to Scottsdale again, I would definitely consider staying here again, or one of the other fine boutique resorts in the area.

reviews.author: apacherodeo
reviews.title: Best luxury resort, best staff in the U.S.
reviews.text: I travel throughout the U.S. and am reminded time and time again that the Phoenician is one of the most luxurious hotel in the U.S. It a beautiful property but it's the Staff that makes it world class.  Elizabeth Anderson and Sarah Schmutz in the sales department  have gone out of their way time and again to set up my reservations and to make my stay perfect.  Phil Mitchell, one of the hotel managers,  has helped me on numerous occasions when I needed assistance.  Similarly, Chris at the front desk has gone out of his way as well for me time and again, even arranging for the gift shop to open after hours because I needed some over the counter medicines..  Beverly at the Concierge desk is always so helpful and pleasant.  She even gave me a Phoenician t-shirt one trip when she saw I was wearing a Four Seasons t-shirt.  Adam and Anthony at the Bell desk always have a warm and pleasant greeting.  I know it sounds like I have stock in the hotel.  I don't but I wish I did!  Giv eth ePhoenician staff an opportunity and you'll see what I mean.  Gary Agron

reviews.author: Deanna9
reviews.title: Perfect...great service, beautiful grounds and great beds!
reviews.text: We stayed here for one night with our 2 children (9&13).  From check-in to check-out the service was exceptional...check-in quick and friendly, concierge was extremely helpful with a dinner restaurant to suit us and the kids tastes, bell service/car service to Camelback mtn were all fabulous!  And, the beds were very comfortable, view over the pool was relaxing, rooms were immaculate and bathroom was spacious.  I would highly recommend this hotel for business or pleasure...There was absolutely nothing to complain about!

reviews.author: MooreHouston
reviews.title: Nothing compares to The Phoenician
reviews.text: Everything about the Phoenician is on such a different level than most hotels.  Everywhere I travel, I compare it to the Phoenician and so far haven't found anything in this category that even compares.  The Front Desk employees are the best!

reviews.author: FlyDC
reviews.title: Very Nice Hotel
reviews.text:
This was our second trip to the Phoenician. Very nice hotel. Great service. Everywhere you went someone was there to help.
The spa was just ok. Very expensive for the treatments and the ambiance was anything to write home about. 
I am gold in Starwood Preferred Guest. I would have thought that the $10 gym fee would be waived for gold - but not a chance. I would understand if the workout room was something special or if you got access to the steam, sauna, etc. (I sent an email to Starwood while I was at the hotel and the hotel called me and comp'd the $10 per guest, per day. I was very appreciative but still think they should change the policy versus just waiving the fee if you take the time to complain to corporate.)
Rooms were very nice. Luxury linens and amenities. 
Grounds were nice. Pool was very crowded one day. The 'pool boy' helped to move some chairs around for us. He was shocked when I offered a tip. He went above and beyond in my mind and really deserved it.
Anyway - would recommend it. 
We had Sunday Brunch at the Biltmore. Fantastic! Property is dated and wouldn't want to stay there - but a walkaround before/after brunch is required as the architecture is really cool. Brunch was a deal at about $40 a person which included a very nice buffet plus a plated entree. (In Palm Beach it would have ben $85....)
Great restaurants in Scottsdale - so ensure you get a rental car!

reviews.author: Jim O
reviews.title: As always - a fantistic experience
reviews.text: We've gone to the Phoenician for many years and will continue to do so...the accomodations are first rate, the service is superior and the availability of things to do are second to none...highly recommended

reviews.author: Aunt M
reviews.title: A beautiful desert oasis, staffed by true hospitality professionals, who make sure you have an amazing stay.
reviews.text: This was our 8th time visiting the Phoenician and October is the perfect time to visit this beautiful desert oasis, staffed by true hospitality professionals, who make sure you have an amazing stay.

reviews.author: LeisureErik
reviews.title: Great service; Over the top luxury
reviews.text:
I attended a conference in Scottsdale and (long story) ended up staying at the Phoenician.  It wasn't my first choice of hotels, as it was an inconvenient location.  But I was very pleased with the room and the property and the service which (partially) made up for the inconvenient location.

I was upgraded to the Canyon Suites, which are relatively new.  The room and the lobby are stunningly beautiful.  It isn't necessarily my type of decor in that it is a bit stodgy, but everything is new and in perfect order and extremely luxurious.  The best part was the service.  The "ambassadors" were prompt and thoughtful with room service and helping make transit arrangements.  I was very impressed.

The only downside to the hotel is that it is a bit formal and (as noted above) quite fancy.  I don't think that I would take my young children here but would consider it for a romantic getaway.

reviews.author: mforward
reviews.title: Grossly overpriced and beware of room ratings
reviews.text:
I booked two deluxe rooms at this resort and was expecting to be more than satisfied with our accomodations. However, we were forced to upgrade to the highest ranked room type (grand deluxe) when our "deluxe" rooms had each looked over the convention centre roof into the windows of the rooms in the building across the rooftop.  We have travelled all over North America and Europe and we have never before encountered such poor value for the price. Apparently, the rooms at the Phoenician are ranked according to the views, starting with unappealing.  Only the highest of three room grades gives you a view that is acceptable.  When I asked why our original rooms were not considered superior (lowest ranking) instead of deluxe, I was told that the rooms had a view of the city overtop of the building across the convention centre roof. Give me a break!  Our new rooms had a nice view of the fountains adjacent to the lower pool but I resented having to pay top dollar just to be satisfied. 

Another major complaint I have about this resort, is that everything is grossly overpriced ($9 for a mini bottle of San Pellegrino at the pool) and has a hidden 20% gratuity attached. I was livid to discover after I tipped 20% at the spa that my bill already had a 20% gratuity attached.  The gratuity is added in every single restaurant even with room service yet every single bill has a line entitled "gratuity" with a blank line. You have to read the fine print to see that the gratuity is included. Very deceiving. They also nickel and dime you to death even charging for internet.  I would really expect in this day and age to have free internet at a five star hotel. 

Finally, the service at each of the three restaurants we ate at was unacceptably slow.  I can't argue about the beautiful setting and grounds, but, the lower 
pool, despite being beautiful, is next to a duck pond and I often saw ducks and their excrement in the swimming pool.  Disgusting. When I asked one of the poolside servers about it he just shrugged and said they try to scare them off but that they just come right back. Anyway, I am sorry to conclude that there must certainly be other beautiful resorts in Phoenix that give better value and service for your money.

reviews.author: jdub88
reviews.title: Great food, location, amenities, but poor beds
reviews.text:
Some things are great and better than anywhere else....food is really good, proximity to airport, camelback mountain (hiking), and good shopping (within walking distance), golf course and tennis courts are very good and literally right there. No need to get in car.

Things needing improvement:  bed was way too soft. My back was not happy. Service was mixed...most times very good, but a few times understaffed and poor. Fitness center:  good but way too small for the size of this place. There were people fighting for cardio equipment at the peak times. Need to double the amount of cardio stuff and it would be fine.

LOVED the ability to hike camelback mountain straight from our room. This alone is a huge plus. LOVED that golf and tennis are RIGHT THERE. LOVED that it is barely 15min from the airport and taxis are right there on the property to take you there. LOVED that we could walk to a mall with high end shops (Barney's, Gucci, etc...).

If they would just get firmer beds I'd be back in a heartbeat.

reviews.author: LJMJonthemove
reviews.title: Not worth the price!
reviews.text:
This hotel is part of a "luxury" collection and touts that brand.  The grounds are nice and the bell staff were very friendly and welcoming, a good sign. But, after that, we were mostly disappointed.  The hotel room was roomy but not fabulous -- Hampton or Hilton Garden Inn do almost as well for far less. The room carpet was wet from a recent cleaning, and we got no real response to our call to complain about the wet.  Air conditioning was an old thermostat; this meant a choice to freeze or roast, nothing in between.  Bath towels -- only 3 sets provided, 4 should be standard.  Towels were large, but much-laundered, rough and non-absorbent.  Tiny shower stall.  

Adding to the perception this hotel talks luxury but then skimps and goes solely for dollars was the total lack of free internet.  For almost $400 a night, this is disconcerting.  

Overall, disappointing.  Nice staff and grounds well kept, but wildly overpriced and lots of high charges for mini-bar, water, internet, parking, etc.  Does not feel like luxury at all, despite their pretensions.

Asked for a comment card to share this set of comments with management.  Was given a postcard w/o postage or envelope, to turn in at the front desk.  (Like it's ever going to be read that way.)  Any business that doesn't want customer feedback on their product doesn't deserve further business.

reviews.author: doras01
reviews.title: Simply Fabulous from A to Z
reviews.text: I can't say enough good things about this beautiful and pristine resort.  The service was excellent.  We always felt that the staff wanted and would do anything for the gusts to be happy.  From the pool staff to the front desk to the concierge to the cleaning staff to the bell boy etc....all were so helpful and friendly.  The location is also a plus, it is a very short drive to downtown ScottsdaleI.  The Cactus Garden, gold course and pool area's are all well taken care of.  One of the most important thing is where ever the eye looked was beautiful and that is key to me on vacation.

reviews.author: SunsetBlvd23
reviews.title: Gut und teuer
reviews.text: Das Phoenician liegt in Scottsdale und damit einerseits zentrumsnah, zugleich ist es aber auch abgeschieden auf einem riesigen Areal am Camelback Mountain, und somit ein richtiges Resort, das man nicht verlassen muss. Die riesigen Ausmaße erstreckt sich auch auf die Poollandschaft mit unzähligen Wasser-Bade-Rutschmöglichkeiten. Die Zimmer sind gut und haben meist einen Blick zur Poollandaschaft. Leider sind die Preise einer der teuersten in der Phoenix-Gegend, sodass sich Alternativen anbieten, die fast den gleichen Standart erreichen aber doch deutlich günstiger sind.

reviews.author: erwinhw
reviews.title: ein Traum
reviews.text:
seit 10 Jahren besuche ich immer im Februar einen Kongress in Phoenix. Auch hatte ich einmal den Phoenician mit der Familie besucht. Während es im Sommer zu heiß ist, sind die Temperaturen im Frühjahr perfekt.
In den Casidas sind die Zimmer sehr geräumig und luxuriös, zum Canyon hin eher dunkel.
Restaurants und Service sind perfekt - und teuer. Ein Paradies für Golfer.

reviews.author: Linda Work
reviews.title: Elegant hotel, beautiful pools, just "okay" spa
reviews.text: The hotel is grande, service is polite but not over-the-top.  The room was beautiful and the bathroom, I'd go back just for the bathroom with its large tub and feel-at-home luxury.  There are several shops which are always nice to peruse.  The pools are wonderful and the attendants are there with a pitcher of water even before you lay down, which is a good thing in the Phoenix heat you'll need that water asap!  Mostly I was disappointed with their spa.  It was small, they had very little product for sale and I thought the salespeople were less-than-helpful rather preferring to unpack their new shipment of rejuvenators than attend to a client.  Aside from that, my stay was quite nice and the resort itself is lovely.

reviews.author: OldB0ldPil0t
reviews.title: Five Star -- With a Few Caveats
reviews.text:
All the praise that others have written in their reviews is well-deserved. The property is beautiful, the rooms are spacious and clean, and the staff we encountered were without exception friendly, courteous and helpful.

But a couple of caveats. The room, while a good size, was a little "tired". The right-hand screen door was off its track and hard to move; some of the bath towels were thin enough to be considered Motel 6 quality; and in a place as hot as Phoenix there were no ice machines to be found anywhere. Also, it would have been nice if someone had posted a notice that when the sliding glass doors are not firmly closed the room a/c shuts off.

But those are niggling comments about an overall beautiful property. What was more serious, to us, was the feeling that the hotel nickel-and-dimed us to death in terms of prices. For example, there are no coffee-makers in the rooms. If you get up early and want a cup of coffee, forget it until the lobby-area coffee shop opens at 7 a.m. Then you have the privilege of paying $4.50 for a small cup of very average coffee, and $12 for a croissant.

As stated earlier, there are no ice machines on the floors so if it's a cold drink you want you have to call room service, which involves both a wait and a tip. For a few ice cubes. Local phone service (does anyone not have a cell phone?) is reasonable for calls up to an hour. After that, though, it's $10 a minute (you read that right) PLUS a 130% hotel surcharge. Hello? And where in-room wireless is almost universally free, here you pay by the hour. Oh, and if you choose to wait for the aforementioned coffee shop to open in the "business center" across the hallway and want to use the internet, that will be $5.95 for 15 minutes. I won't even go into the price of food at the poolside cafe. Overnight valet parking, $29? True, people have the option of self-parking for free. However, we recently stayed at the Grand Hyatt at Lake Tahoe, an equally upscale resort hotel, where valet parking was included in the room price, making for an all-smiles experience.

All in all we found these sorts of charges and such things as not having a coffee maker in each room to be not very customer-friendly. While we understand that resort hotels tend to be pricey and accept that, it appeared in this case that the hotel was really gouging its customers, which left a somewhat sour taste. I suggest that this property do a thorough review of its customer service philosophy, for while its staff is exemplary, they are held prisoner by 20th-century pricing and customer service practices.

reviews.author: thegoodsongs
reviews.title: Truly a 5-star Resort!
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is truly a magnificent, breathtaking 5-star resort that , in comparison to many other fine resorts Scottsdale has to offer, will stand out above the rest.

 First, the property is so large and the accommodations quite far from the main entrance that one will never hear any kind of street noise or even see the street (or any other resorts) to mar the view of the gorgeous, lush setting of the Phoenician for that matter.

Our party had 2 connecting rooms - one with a king bed and large sitting area with sofa, the other room included 2 queen beds, comfy chair, desk, etc. The bathrooms in each were large with Roman tubs, large showers with the best waterfall-like showerheads I've ever experienced, double sinks and a privately enclosed toilet or bidet (whichever you prefer.) Both rooms had huge balconies which overlooked the main property, views of close-up and distant mountains and in our corner room - views of the beautiful cactus gardens. The only downside to our magnificent rooms was the long walk to get to them. In the annex where we stayed, it didn't matter if we used the self-parking garage or had valet parking - we still had to walk a considerable distance to our rooms after having taken 2 separate elevators. If you're in reasonably good health, you shouldn't have too much problem with the walk (good exercise!)

Just remember, once you're on the grounds of the Phoenician, you'll never want to venture out to see or do anything else! From the golfing, hiking trails, tennis courts (including a grass court), swimming pools too numerous to count (and even find!), shopping and first-rate restaurants, plan to stay for an extended time at the Phoenician whenever you're in the Phoenix/Scottsdale area. 

A truly, truly great find!!!

reviews.author: looking4sun09
reviews.title: Gorgeous!
reviews.text:
What a beauty!  Gorgeous pools, grounds and hotel!!
Perfect location. We went during the slower part of summer so the pools were
pretty empty. It was paradise in the desert.

reviews.author: OS68
reviews.title: Ganz nett, aber mehr leider auch nicht
reviews.text:
Typisch amerikanisches Resort-Hotel. Es fehlt an nichts, aber es hat auch keinen besonderen Charme. Das Steakrestaurant ist bestenfalls durchschnittlich. Positiv hervorzuheben ist die Lage in der Nähe von Downtown Scottsdale und einer sehr großen Shopping-Mall. Geradezu unverschämt sind dagegen die Parkgebühren ($30/Tag).
Fazit: Gerade in und um Scottsdale geht das deutlich besser für weniger Geld.

reviews.author: fcbenni
reviews.title: Great hotel, great rooms, nice atmosphere
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is located 20min by cab from the airport PHX and close to the city Scottsdale with many bars and restaurants.

The hotel itself is built on a very large areal with multiple leisure time activities like golf, swimming or the fitness center. It also offers multiple bars and restaurants.

The rooms are large, clean and comfortable and the staff is very friendly..

reviews.author: MariaD0104
reviews.title: Beautiful setting.  Courteous staff.
reviews.text: The Phoenician is beautiful.  It is set against the mountains with a cactus garden in the back and the wonderful pool area in the front.  Many fantastic restaurants on property.  Our room was gorgeous, and it was only a standard room.  Very spacious.  It had the most comfortable bed with luxurious bed coverings and linens.  Great shower too.  Everything was beautifully decorated.  Staff was also very courteous, helpful, cheerful.

reviews.author: gigilum
reviews.title: A Desert Oasis
reviews.text: Our stay at The Phoenician was everything you would expect from a luxury hotel.  Everything went smoothly from check-in to check-out.  The hotel sits at the base of the Camelback Mountains - a sight to behold and the hotel itself is beautiful.  Our room was spacious, functional and had a great view.  The staff at this place is incredible, they live to make you smile.  We will definitely be back.

reviews.author: JillYGAZ
