reviews.title: Beautiful Get Away
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed at the Phoenician over Father's Day weekend. We were offered a room in the main building or a Casita. We chose the Casita because it was near the pool and we planned on spending alot of time there. We chose wisely! The room was beautiful and was very close to the pools. We had a very comfortable patio on a grassy area with a waterfall and stream. The grounds were immaculate and the service was great.

We enjoyed the pool 2 days. They had good poolside service and a good menu for poolside food. The only complaint about the pool area was there were two tile walkways separating different portions of the pools and those tiles were slippery. We saw several people slip (without falling fortunately). Many people would take off their shoes / flip flops to make the walk because they obviously knew from prior walks!

We dined at Il Terrazzo and had a wonderful meal. My husband enjoyed the Mac N Cheese that was made with white cheddar and broccoli and I enjoyed the Kobe Flat Iron, we shared with each other and couldn't have been happier with our meals.

All in all, the Phoenician was a great couple's retreat - not overrun with kids, upscale, beautiful and very relaxing.

reviews.author: Diana Andrade
reviews.title: Gorgeous property in the desert but no refrigerated AC!
reviews.text:
We checked in at The Phoenician on July 30-Aug 2, 2010 for a weekend of golf. Booked  two rooms - One King and one Double.  Originally booked a superior room but was "supposedly" upgraded to a King Casita (7153 connecting).  I would have preferably remained in the superior room as I will describe.  The property is gorgeous and well-manicured at all times.  Several pools around the property - considering the size, it is very quiet.  Room service is prompt but expensive.  Ordered 2 onion soups to our "casita" for $42 which included all the extra fees they added.  The price on the menu was $9.00 each.  Our room was conveniently located right across the golf clubhouse which allowed easy access without driving around.  The golf course was under some sort of maintenance therefore my husband did not enjoy it as much.  He considers the Biltmore and Gainey Ranch to be the best so far.  Each room has a plasma screen tv, two phones, large bathroom with tubs ,safe, iron and table, robes and slippers.  Minibar - expensive. Our room had a Dream Machine CD/Radio, the other room had a Bose.  Don't know why.  Internet for a fee is available in the rooms.  Each room had a private balcony with lounge chairs and a table.  Our room balconies faced Camelback Mountain for a nice view.  Had breakfast at the Il Terrazo - good but pricey.  A-la-carte - The Steal-Cut oatmeal is to die for!  Buffet is about $25pp.  Excellent service.  Later discovered the cafe in the hotel shoppes which serves the same items but at a much lower price.  Dined on July 31 at Il Terrazo - excellent food and service but again very very pricey.  I ordered the Filet Mignon with 6 shrimp that was excellent - better that Ruth Chris!  The Pina Colada arrived quite watered down.  The server quickly replaced it with a Lemon Drop Martini.  The restaurant had only about 6 tables occupied (two were ours) on a Saturday night.  Overall the staff is very courteous and professional at all times.  

PROBLEMS: 1.)  Room had a leak by the sliding glass door.  Water leaked in during a rainstorm.  Maintenance came to evaluate problem but blamed it on the rain. They said it was coming from the balcony on top.  Did nothing else but offered to vacuum up the water from the carpet.  That was never done    2.) None of the rooms on this property have refrigerated A/C but a water coil cooling system that dumps 100% humidity into the rooms.  It was the most uncomfortable condition.  Sheets were moist; carpet is icky; cannot do your hair with humidity and the awful humid smell.  Contacted maintenance again when on the second day we realized that something was wrong with the temperature of the room.  We felt ill with the dampness.  The tech came and explained that this was a cooling system and that in the summer the humidity was felt higher.  Living in New Mexico, we are very familiar with evaporative cooling systems, aka "Swamp Coolers," and are not very fond of.  In our home, we have refrigerated air (we are original Floridians - so we know what we are talking about.)  They offered to move us to another room that may be a little cooler without as much humidity but we declined as it was our last night and did not want to move.  We were completely disappointed with the tempertature condition of this property.  A 5 star property with a mediocre cooling system!  As my husband prefers Arizona to play golf, we frequently visit Scottsdale and Phoenix but have never experienced this problem in any of the many hotels 3-5 stars tht we have stayed. Tthe front desk staff was made aware of the discomfort we experienced and compensated us however, The Phoenician is definitely not on our return list until the cooling systems is upgraded.

reviews.author: sjc0009
reviews.title: So disaappointing this time around!!!
reviews.text:
After three long flights, I arrived once more at the entrance to the Phoenician, which always impresses me,the grounds /ameninities are wonderful.
I had reserved a Grand Deluxe room. To my surpirse I was allocated a Casita Grand Deluxe Room and not one in the main building. After retrieving my car and luggage from the valet i had to load up the car and go locate my room (7522). I arrived at the small car park at my casita , the lot was full, I later found out why, the burger restaurant is oposite so non resident guests take the liberty to park here. There is no assistance at these rooms or I wasnt offered. I had to take my own luggage to my second floor casita in the 100 degree afternoon. Compared to the other accomodations I have stayed in Grand deluxe and Canyon Suites, this room was very small. I was staying there for 6 nights on a business trip. On closer inspection the floor carper was all stained and was in need of a good deep clean. I wore my shoes at all times. I called reception and spoke to Amanda  as I had aired my concern with her upon check in that I was in a casita room and it probably was not as nice a room as the main building, She told me there were no GD rooms available to change, although the hotel was at 22% occupancy. I called again and spoke to Sara and she told me they would change me next day. The call or the alternative room was never offered. Hence I never ate breakfast or dinner in the main hotel as I didnt want to have to drive and park underneath or walk in the heat across the pool areas, which are very nice. It's a inconvenience, one that I was not prepared for. I used the room telephone to leave a voice message at our AZ office 4 times on several days, 22 seconds, 34 seconds etc. I found  telephone charges of $41.70 four times, its there standard connection charge,obsurd!

reviews.author: BGosivetti
reviews.title: Great family resort
reviews.text: Beautiful property, nice rooms. Excellent pool facilities. Good access to Camelback Mountain.  The front desk area can be a bit chaotic, and service responsiveness can be slow given size of resort (maybe somewhat understaffed?), but staff has great attitude and works hard to be responsive.

reviews.author: AZretiree
reviews.title: Disappointed in a 5 Diamond Resort
reviews.text: Good Suite. When we arrived, the bathroom had a loud noise and we could  not find out from where it was coming from. We called Engineering - the man discovered the Jacuzzi was on even though there was no water in the tub. Someone just left it running and we do not know how long it had been going on. There was dust bunnies (dust balls) on the bathroom floor which had been there for a long time so we guess the room had not been cleaned for a very long time. The toilet room door was very difficult to open and close. Because of my small stature, once the valet guys had seen me inside, they had to tell each other and one even came inside acting as if he was looking for someone. How immature they acted. If they are working at a 5 Diamond resort, they ought to act more mature. Unacceptable behavior. The best staff member was the one who did the evening turndown, supplied fresh towels, etc.

reviews.author: SalsaPicante78
reviews.title: Stunning Property Earns Its Reputation
reviews.text:
I was lucky to catch a great rate on this hotel and stayed here for two nights for business.  My father lives in Paradise Valley and had often talked about the hotel's reputation.  I was not disappointed.  
The room I had looked at the back of Camelback Mountain, amazing!  I could step out on my patio in the morning and see lots of wildlife.  There is a walking path and a golf path but they are just out of view and the traffic never disturbed me.
The hotel is a massive complex, but all beautifully tended to with a gracious and helpful staff.  I don't like to ask for much but when a bell man offered up a cold water after a long day of meetings in the Phoenix heat, it was like he read my mind.  I didn't even have to ask!
The pools are another amazing feature.  I really want to come back on a vacation where I could spend more time floating around them.  
The restaurants are overpriced but the Jean George steakhouse was a very good (but not great) meal.
If you have the option of staying here, take it.  First time I have given a property 5 stars.

reviews.author: newyorker020
reviews.title: Great hotel and resort.. they have it all
reviews.text:
I have stayed at the Phoenician many times.  They have everything there.  My only disappointment in this latest trip was that my room was not ready at 9am after I arrived from ny - and I left on a 6am flight.. a room immediately would have really made this visit better, but I must say the rates were incredibly reasonable and the place was full.  

I have a sister with kids in the area so I know the hotel is super kid friendly and also a great spot for relaxation sans kids.  I usually have the kids visit for a day or two and they always find other kids to play with in the pool and enjoy the restaurants and the ice cream shop!  The kids did tennis and golf activities this year and really enjoyed them.. Without the kids you have all the time in the world to enjoy the quiet pool and the amazing spa.. maybe even guided meditation.   
I like the starwood brand and you do get the sense that people spend their business earned points on personal trips here. Tennis facilities are great.

reviews.author: SaksiaofManhattan
reviews.title: A wonderful experience in the Arizona desert
reviews.text:
From the entrance to the resort, the drive up to the lobby, we thought WOW, and we were not disapponted.
The Phoenician is in a wonderful location, set within the backdrop of Camelback Mountain.
The Lobby and lobby bar, The Thirsty Camel give you an idea of what is to be a perfect relaxing location.
Upon check in, we were allocated a stunning deluxe room overlooking the lawns and pool areas. One slight negative here, was the check in clerk seemed more keen on me signing up to a Starwood loyalty card.
I will summarise the different facilities on the resort site to give an overview of each;
Pool area - nice ambience with first class facilities. Usually very attentive poolhosts and hostesses, plus waitress facilities at pool side.
Pool Bar - Centre of lunchtime activity. Good drinks menu, and basic but fair snack menu. Great service from Steve and Juliane. New TV installed allowing a drink with the days sport on.
Il Terrazzo - Breakfast menu was fair. Had eveining meal (Italian fare) which was very good. The terrace area was lovely (watch for the friendly but hungry birds).
J&G Steakhouse _ Located on the 6th floor, very good food, ate there twice, 1st time was better, as waiter on 2nd visit seemed slightly uninterested, but nice place with stunning views of Scottsdale and Phoenix in the distance.

Returned for 2nd visit after 4 day trip in San Diego. Arrived 3rd July, so for a day or two the occupancy was near 100% for Indepedence Day.
Given a deluxe room with extended balcony with views of golf course, Cactus garden and the grounds. Beautiful balcony to watch the Arizona sun go down over Camelback.

In summary a great place to stay, yes some things are quite expensive.
$6.50 for large Latte
$6.00 for bottle of beer.
$120.00 for meal and drinks for two.

However the overall impression was a great big PLUS, and we will deifnately return.

reviews.author: BlueTiger28
reviews.title: Feeling super-relaxed after a weekend stay.
reviews.text:
I just returned from a weekend at the Phoenician and it was great!  Because it was 112 degrees the rates were very reasonable.  The a/c kept the indoors cool but not too cold and the pool was glorious!  

Pros:
1. The room was clean, spacious, with a nice view of the cactus garden out back.  The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was great!  We were upgraded when we checked in so I'm not sure what style room we had.  Given some negative reviews on the quality of the rooms, perhaps they've remodeled/updated recently?
2. The service was consistently helpful and friendly.
3. Fiesta Fridays at Relish (the Golf Club burger bar):  The margaritas were tasty and only $5.  They had a good band and there was dancing.
4.The pools are amazing! We swam laps, shot some hoops and went down the water slide.  Because it was offseason, it was not at all crowded.  There was plenty of lounge chairs in the shade and they supply oversized, thick beach towels.  
5. The spa was expensive but very nice.  We took advantage of the summer time discount of a 2nd service for 50% off.
6. Free, underground parking. 
7. Generally beautiful views from every part of the property.

Cons:
1. The food is very expensive.  Breakfast costs about $50 for two people.  That's not too bad for the Sunday buffet but otherwise it feels like extortion. $10 for oatmeal... really?
2. No coffee maker in the room.  We like to bring our own tea and instant oatmeal along when we travel.  It just makes for a healthier way to travel.  You can get a coffee machine delivered to your room but it costs $38 for the duration of your stay.  
3. No recycling or evidence of water conservation.
4. No free wifi.  It costs $6 for 15 minutes online in their 'internet cafe'.  

I don't think I would go here during the 'high season' but I would definitely go back in the off season to take advantage of the discounts and combine a little bit of luxury and a visit with friends who live in Phoenix.

reviews.author: Stormygirl
reviews.title: Absolutely the best.
reviews.text: Fabulous accommodations, what a value in the summer!

reviews.author: windiecarreras
reviews.title: Magnificent
reviews.text: What a wonderful hotel We arrived at the hotel and I asked if our suite had a lovely view, Well the young woman at the front desk said, not really. Our suite was overlooking the temporary ballroom tent and it would be on the side where there was construction going on. The front desk immediately solved the situation and we were given a great suite at the top of the building overlooking the golf course. Maybe our stay would have not been as good had we stayed in the other room. The grounds are beautiful (even with the constuction) there are several pools that interconnect, there is a mother of pearl pool, quiet and for adults, a koi pond. We ate at the restaurant by the pool, had breakfast and lunch it was pricey but delicious. One thing I will say is do not stay there if you are on a budget, you can not be worried about  the cost as you should go in knowing that everything will be pricey. Michelle is the best concierge around. Valet parked the first day then did self-parking, save that money for a drink by the pool. Grounds and room were always pristine, service was excellent and loved the cactus garden. Did not use the Spa. My husband and son went golfing and we did use the tennis courts.

reviews.author: andreadurf
reviews.title: Can't Wait To Return!!
reviews.text: My husband and I just returned from our 4th of July weekend at the Phoenician and we can't wait until our next trip to Scottsdale.   I can't say enough about the staff and how accomodating they all were. Their main goal seemed to be to make us comfortable and make sure we were happy even on such a busy weekend.  The resort is spectacular and our room was spacious with a beautiful view.  The pool area and the grounds were well maintained and kept clean even with such a large group of people.  The only negative we experienced was our cabana rental.  The cabana's are a little pricey but we decided it would be worth it to rent one for the 4th of July.  The hotel had over sold the cabana's at the Mother of Pearl pool which made it not at all relaxing since the majority of the locals that showed up as part of a large group were mostly children and teenagers.  The hotel did comp us for our food and drink at the pool without us asking them to, but I still felt a little ripped off.  We returned to the same pool the following day to the "free seats" and got to see the cabana renters actually relax in a quiet setting.  I learned to not rent a cabana during a holiday. :)   I do have to say that our attendant at the cabana's, Rich, was the most awesome of all the staff we encountered that weekend.  Even with the large crowd he kept a smile on his face and was extremely attentive.  Thanks so much Rich for a great 4th.   Dinner at the italian restaurant was soooo good and again the service was above and beyond.  Even the maintenance and housekeeping employees took the time to stop what they were doing to say hello as we passed.  We stay at quite a few different hotels each year and never see this kind of service. My new saying is "What do you think this is?  The Phoenician"

reviews.author: Mblaca
reviews.title: A splendid resort hotel
reviews.text:
I was in Phoenix overnight for a business meeting.  Yes it is summertime and the temperature was north of 110 degrees f.  Even so, the Phoenician, at $186 per night, was a great value.  My room was spacious.  It had a patio overlooking Camelback Mountain that was delightful in the evening and morning.  The air conditioning worked beautifully day and night.

I didn't have time to brave the golf course or visit the pool - but the facilities looked great.  My dinner at the Italian restaurant was good, not outrageously expensive and came with attentive service.

I can't wait to go back.

reviews.author: MPKeller
reviews.title: Beautiful place, terrible staff and service
reviews.text:
I had my wedding here in April.  There is plenty of staff here that try to make your stay as comfortable as possible, but maybe it's because the staff is so large that some of them feel like they can get by on treating you poorly because they work for such a big hotel and they'll just fall into the mix.

Grounds:  

The hotel is beautiful.  It's the most beautiful hotel/resort I have ever been to.  Everything was in bloom in April and our wedding pictures are exploding with Arizona spring colors.  It was gorgeous.  Some of the staff was awesome as well- Megan at Oasis is an angel, and the guy who made sure everything went smoothly at the reception was amazing (so sorry I can't remember his name).  The food at the reception was wonderful and surpassed my expectations.  Everything was prepared beautifully and exceptionally well.

Golf:  

My husband arranged a golf day for himself and 5 others in his group.  I was not there, but from what my husband told me, the golf guys did not prepare the guests' golf cart, the guests loaded it themselves.  Also, the guests were only given one small bottle of water each.  Hello- this is Arizona, it's a desert.  When the guests asked for ice (the ice machine nearest to the golf area was being cleaned), the golf guys told them to go get it at the cafe.  That's not 5 star service, and the Phoenician is supposed to be a 5 diamond resort.  This was very disappointing.  There are so many golf resorts in Arizona, this is the last time my husband and his guests will golf here.

The Valet:

There is a lack of organization and communication with the valet staff. There is no system here- you get someone when you get someone.

Oasis Cabana Grill:  

Megan who works as a server here is so gracious and friendly.   She was amazing.  My husband's family hung out here the whole week they were here.  Great pool area for kids, quiet pool for adults.  

Oasis Grill and Phoenician Management:

I have, however, a HUGE complaint about the Oasis/Phoenician management.  My husband and I were married on a Saturday.  We were NOT at the pool at any point during this day.  For some reason, our room was charged for over $500 from the Oasis Grill.   At no point did anyone from the Grill call my room to get authorization to charge my credit card this amount- they just did it without my knowledge or consent.

Weeks after the wedding when I went through our credit card bills, I noticed this large, strange amount.  I called the Phoenician and they told me it was for a cabana and miscellaneous food and drinks for the day my husband and I were married.  "That's strange", I thought- we weren't even at the Oasis Grill that day.  I asked for receipts and the guy I talked to was very responsive and sent them to me immediately.  The receipt he sent, however, did NOT include a signature page.  I know I didn't sign anything and neither did my husband.  I called back to ask if they had this signature page.  

After 2 days, I received an email from the assistant manager of the resort who asked me to call her back.  She stated that there was an error, I shouldn't have been charged.  She also asked if I know who Mr. X was.  I told her I did, and she responded that the charge should have went to him, she doesn't know why it didn't.  She then told me TO CALL Mr. X and ask him to pay his bill.   Nowhere in this conversation did she apologize for the UNAUTHORIZED use of my credit card for over $500, instead, she wanted ME to fix the Phoenician's mistake- and she didn't ASK me to do it, she basically told me to do it.   Is common courtesy a thing of the past?  Is it completely outdated to be communicative in a professional manner?  I responded by telling her calmly that I don't feel like it is my responsibility to call Mr. X on the Phoenician's behalf.  This woman said okay and got off the phone, not a word of apology, not a "have a nice day", nothing.  I should also comment that I had not in the two conversations I had with her raised my voice or acted unprofessionally (it was a business transaction, after all).  I've learned a long time ago that you don't get what you want by acting like a brat.  And I wasn't a brat, so I don't think I deserved the kind of treatment she gave me, especially when I spent so much money at the Phoenician for my wedding, had my guests book rooms there for several days, and especially when it was their error.  

The Short Story:

I'm very disappointed and since the Phoenician probably doesn't really care if I'm happy with them or not, the best I could do is review the resort with the added warning:  watch your credit card statements after you stay here because your credit card on file at the hotel IS NOT SAFE.  I repeat at the risk of sounding obnoxious, but $500 is a lot of money:  YOUR CREDIT CARD IS NOT SAFE HERE.  

I wish I had LOVED the Phoenician, but ultimately, the resort is only as good as its staff and management.

reviews.author: Baluzo
reviews.title: Hotel magnifique
reviews.text:
j'ai fais une halte de 2 jours dans cet établissment, trés reposant, magnifiquement décoré pas trop chargé.
Bref un vrai havre de paix arrivant de Chicago et de Las Vegas.

reviews.author: ElPasoLalo
reviews.title: outstanding!
reviews.text:
After a not so pleasant stay at the W Times Square, i was reluctant to book the stay since it was the same corporation.
i will do this quick so i dont bore, if the facility is not brand new, the up keep is great and the grounds are amazing, however, after traveling the United States, Central America and Europe, and beeing lucky enough to stay at Meridian, Four seasons, Mandarin Oriental and many more, the people at The Phoenician made all the difference.
This is the first stay ever in which i NEVER, saw less than the most polite and accomodating staff, i am talking reception, restaurant, bar, pool, everywhere!
Lets face it, almost everywhere you may encounter a polite person but with less than a full tank of fuel in pleasing. Not at The Phoenician, not one instance where we felt less than 100% effort!

reviews.author: cessnajockey
reviews.title: Best Hotel Experience EVER!
reviews.text:
This has to be one of the best hotel stays that I've EVER had - from check in to check out, these people are flawless.  Even when the toilet overflowed and flooded the bathroom, the staff responded immediately and had it fixed and cleaned up in no time.  

We were assigned a Casita in a building next to the pool slide - this made my 6 year old VERY happy.   And even though we had self parking outside our door, the bell staff drove us and our luggage to our room in a cart and the valet drove and parked our car outside our room and delivered our keys to us.

George, the pool attendent, was the best - he remembered our names and greeted us name each day.  He took care of making sure we had everything we desired - water, food, etc.  When a waiter couldn't be found, he'd go get one.   His performance couldn't of been better!  And the slide area was the best I've come across - NICE shaded area around the bottom of the pool slide for parents to relax so no sunscreen even needed.

When I wanted a fish sandwich in my room, which I had tried earlier at the poolside restaurant, room service figured out what I wanted and went and got it for me even though it was not on their menu or served by their restaurant.  Now that's SERVICE!

At the spa, the massage was decent and my six year old was welcomed in the massage room with me since the club for the kids was closed.

Overall, this was the best hotel experience  I've ever had!  This is what staying in a 5 star hotel SHOULD be.

reviews.author: Katy K
reviews.title: Relaxing Stay Overlooking the Mountains
reviews.text: I just returned from my stay in Scottsdale at The Phoenician.  I have to say, my travel agent couldn't have made a better recommendation.  My friends and I took a much needed girls getaway to relax, and relax we did!  The weather was beautiful and the pool area was awesome.  My favorite part was the fact that the staff brought us pitchers of ice water and it was never empty.  Drinks and food were very good... a little pricey, but that's what you'd expect at a AAA-Diamond resort, so we knew what we were in for.  I thought our deluxe room would have been a bit bigger, but all in all it was very nice and we had a great view.  One thing most would like, but being an independent person I really didn't was the fact that we had to call for ice whenever we needed it (yes I know... the torture :).  I recommend the Mac and Cheese at the Terrazo restaurant.  Very yummy.  I'd also recommend taking the opportunity to climb Camelback Mountain.  It's right behind the resort, and about a 20 minute walk to get to the trail.  I'd at least climb halfway up to see the great views of the city and a view of The Phoenician from above. We had an amazing trip and we'd book this resort with our friend (and travel agent) at Fox World Travel again and again for a nice little vaca.

reviews.author: jperk1819
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text:
Spent four nights at the hotel recently.  The first two nights were for business and the second two for fun.  As far as providing an excellent place for a business conference the Phoenician did a perfect job. Not to far from the airport, easy check in check out.  Lunch out under a tent, meetings in a room that was large but not so large as to loose any sense of intimacy, dinner back out under the stars, a great venue. I have included pictures of the grounds and my really spacious suite and from them you will see its a very pretty setting, lots to do or not to do.  A great setting.
But that is not why I titled this review "excellent".  
It is the people that make this resort great.  
During the second day of our stay we got word that our daughter had been in a car accident. Nothing horrible but she was shaken up.  As were we being so far from home.  The next day the General Manger went out of his way to find us and ask how she was doing.  When we asked how he knew, his response was perfect, and I believe is the mantra for all the staff...it was 'his job to know'.  For the next 72 hours many staff greeted us by name and asked of our daughter's well being.  
In a short review I can say that staff can make a nice facility pretty crummy or staff can make an 'ok' facility seem great.   In this case the Phoenician offers both great facilities and a really great staff.  They have earned our respect and we will return.

reviews.author: FloridaMember
reviews.title: Great business trip
reviews.text:
My husband and I were at the Phoenician for a business meeting. We loved the grounds, the rooms and the service. The planned dinner was wonderful. I had a great massage by Stacy at the spa. The resort was all we expected. 

We found some time to hike the Camalback Mountain which is walking distance from the hotel. It's a straight up hike with great views. 

We ordered room service the morning we were leaving. We had 2 bagels and lox, a pot of coffee and 1 orange juice. The server brought a toaster and toasted the bagels in our room! He set a nice table with cloth on our patio, which was lovely. We were pretty shocked when it was time to pay the bill.... $70! Luckily it was a business expense.

reviews.author: SusieJue
reviews.title: Relaxing stay with excellent service
reviews.text:
I booked a long weekend Sat- Mon, at the Phoenician using 12,000 Starwood points per night in April when the weather is absolutely perfect! It was just after the Spring Break crowds had left and it was pure heaven. You can valet park or self park for free.

Check-In
The check-in was speedy and I love Daniela Ilieva at the Front Desk. As a Platinum member I was upgraded to a very large Grand Deluxe room (4196) with a huge balcony. The Main Building has 6 floors and the rooms at the far end are bigger have the large balconies.

The Platinum Thank You amenity (chips, salsa and bottle water) was quickly brought to my room, as was the luggage.  The mini refrigerator was already in the room, as I had requested it ahead of time. The service at this resort is excellent. Complimentary shoe shine, if you want.

Note: bottle water is not provided free in the room, but you can get it, no charge, from the concierge or down in the Fitness Center ( they have fruit there too).  I love, James, the resort ambassador who greets you at the door.  There is also free coffee in the morning until 9 am at  Il Terrazzo Di Luce. I was surprised and disappointed that the water and coffee was not in the room as it is in most domestic Starwood hotels (one reason it did not get Excellent rating from me).

Room
The room was huge with king bed, gigantic flat panel TV, sofa + 2 chairs, desk and balcony with lounge and table + 2 chairs. I was told the bed was a Westin Heavenly bed ( very comfy) and the bath towels were so plush!  Two closets, mini bar and large bathroom with Remede toiletries...really in heaven now ( valued at $40.)! I love that the room had a bathroom scale, but unfortunately, this one wasn't working. Magazines in the room to read or take to the pool. Turn down service between 6-9 pm with chocolates.

I asked for a DVD player and at first they said it was for a fee, then the next thing I know, they brought one up and installed for free! Also, since there was no coffee maker, I asked for some hot water to make tea and they delivered with a nice cup/saucer, cloth napkin and spoon at no charge. Everyone is so friendly and wanting to help make your stay enjoyable.

Amenities
There is a Business Center/Cyber Cafe with one free computer near the lobby and fax/copier.  There are other shops here, (florist, women's fashion, general store, wine/beer, souvenir) but were all closed when I walked by.

Disappointing was the Centre for Well Being spa...it looked dated and in need of remodel (also why it didn't get Excellent rating). The free Fitness Center appeared to be well equipped (has a scale) and there was a room for classes.

Two acre Cactus Garden is along the north edge of resort grounds and is very interesting to stroll through.

Restaurants
I did not eat at any of the restaurants, but the Il Terrazzo patio is beautiful this time of year and they have a Sunday Brunch from 10 - 2:30 pm at three courses for $35. and $10 more for traditional American breakfast buffet. Afternoon tea in the lobby appears to be very popular, open daily at 2 pm. The highlight of the resort is world renown Jean-George Vongerichten's J & G Steakhouse.

Pool
The Oasis pool is the main pool with a children's pool and whirlpool.  There is a 165 foot water slide for kids and young at heart. Mother of Peal pool for adults overlook the Necklace Lake filled with beautiful koi, ducks and one turtle. Cabanas are available for rent. The one turnoff was there was alot of bird dropping on the lounge chairs and weren't cleaned off daily. I got home and bird dropping on my clothes, etc...gross. Needs to be some improvement in this area (definitely not getting an Excellent rating for this)!

Activities
Funician Kids Club is supervised program for ages 5-12. Family Activity Center with movie theater, video game room, air hockey, foosball and board games. 27 hole golf course and 11 court tennis complex.

Nearby is the Fashion Square mall with many of my favorite stores, such as Antropologie, Macy's and upscale designer store, such as, Jimmy Choo, Louis Vuitton, Gucci and Barneys New York. There are many restaurants and my favorite Paradise Bakery, love the spicy Southwest Chicken Caesar salad! Also a movie complex.

Overall, this resort is very nice with excellent service and good location ( love Fashion Square). It is very relaxing and I would return again, but there are alot of other great places in Scottsdale, like the Westin Kierland (I like the Kierland Commons next door) and Fairmont Scottsdale Princess (best spa experience yet).

Check out the photos from my stay:
http://www.facebook.com/album.php?aid=120446&id=1539673139&l=07b2ad012e

reviews.author: Becca_C
reviews.title: Beautiful Oasis in the footprint of Camelback Mountain
reviews.text:
I'll say up front that it is not my usual style to stay in 5 star resorts when I vacation.  For business trips, I like 4star, and abroad I'm a fan of bed and breakfasts or even hip hostels.

However, there's a very good reason to stay at a resort in a desert climate:  you want a fun pool environment.  The Phoenician was absolutely excellent in this aspect, as well as pretty much everything else.  The staff was very friendly and professional, willing to go that extra mile.

We got a double upgrade to a casita.  These are the units to stay in....not only did we have a pool view, but rising just above it was Camelback mountain.  I chose to get the ground floor so we could just walk right out onto the grounds for an easy stroll to the pool complex.

Food:
Poolside service is great during the week, as there are much less patrons.  You'll wait longer on the weekends, but nothing to complain about.  The kobe burger was EXCELLENT.  The ice cream parlor was perfect for a low-key breakfast and other snacks.  I didn't eat dinner at the restaurants, as I wanted to check out the Scottsdale scene.

Pool:
Multi-level pool complex.  The upper decks are active, and even have a basketball hoop.  Mid-level has a beautiful Mediterranean tiled spa with pools and waterfalls.  Lower level is the mother of pearl star pool, meant for serenity and quietness.  I really loved this setup.

Grounds:
The grounds are immaculate.  Since this is the desert and there are numerous water features here, naturally you will hear a lot of animals.  Countless birds sing at the pools, and there are many bunnies hopping around.

Room:
Spacious and beautiful.  Had a large bathroom with a vanity and separate closet with a walk-in shower.  The soaking tub was a bit shallow for my taste.  The linens are top quality and the room is decorated in very neutral tones.  As this is a top resort, of course everything is an add-on:  no coffee maker, no mini-frig (well there is, but it's full and sensored).  You even are supposed to call room service for ice!  This isn't necessary though, because a portion of the service closets aren't locked where you can get your ice.

Spa:
This will be a separate Yelp review.  But I was very happy.

Value:
Our special rate for the room definitly makes me feel the value was very high for what we paid.  The casitas I say again are the place to stay in this resort.  You are steps away from your car (private parking), have a view of the mountain and pools, and you don't have to walk through lots of hallways to reach other parts of the resort.  This was a fantastic experience, much better than my stay at JW Marriott at Desert Ridge.  Phoenician is still a large property, but the service sets it apart....and the casita...oh the casita...

reviews.author: lovecapecod2
reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: Our stay at the Phoenician was nothng but average.  The hotel was nice enough and the grounds were beautiful.  However, I felt for a luxury hotel it was a little off.  While the room we stayed in was spacious and very comfortable, the rug was a little worn and there was garbage left on our balcony.  We also sat outside for drinks and appetizers at night.  Unfortunately, we weren't able to sit by one of the fire pits as the cushions on the chairs left alot to be desired.   Definitely not something I would expect for the money you are paying.  We were unable to take advantage of the pools but they looked amazing and their cactus garden in the back was beautiful.   All in all, in was just average, definitely not the worst but not the best either.

reviews.author: ridgebackgirl
reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.text: My husband and I had been wanting to go to Arizona for some time now. We had a great experience all around. Our room was clean and the staff was very friendly. The concierge staff was very nice and helpful. When we found out it was snowing in the  Grand Canyon and weren't sure if we should go, the concierge was very helpful in helping us to decide and when we decided against it, she suggested many other things for us to do instead. The only thing we could have done without was the J&G Steakhouse. I just don't think it was our "thing." The place was extremely expensive (which was expected by the way) but the overall atmosphere to be frank gave us the "creeps." But like I said before, just wasn't our style. We much enjoyed the atmosphere at Il Terrazo (spelling) better! The ice cream shop was great too. We had breakfast there every morning and Amy our server was very friendly and helpful. I wanted a smoothie with no dairy and she made one that was great!!! Our experience was very good and we really enjoyed that Hertz car rental was right there on the premises. Made life a lot easier! Overall, our experience was very good and we would definitely stay here again!

reviews.author: SacramentoDella
reviews.title: Not up to par
reviews.text: Something was wrong at the Phoenician.  While parts of the hotel were spotless, others were in a state of woe.  We walked past the same spill on a walkway for two days.  The furniture at the pool was dirty and worn.  The pool area was overcrowded, and understaffed.  It took 20 minutes to get an order from a server (while we sat at a dirty, sticky pool bar) and then another 10 to get the check.  In contrast, the front desk staff was efficient and helpful.  Food was OK but pricey.  We had the distinct impression that the Phoenician was running some type of "sale" and was not properly staffed for the influx.   The hotel also charges a hefty sum for internet access, on top of steep room prices.  Why do high end hotels do this?

reviews.author: greatday1031
reviews.title: A sad experience
reviews.text:
The Phoenician is an absolutely beautiful property. Sadly that's where the quality ends.
Our arrival was marred by an inept bell staff who first was lackadasical in getting us to the right place. (a casita room) and then delivered our luggage to the wrong room and then told us that they couldn't find it. We got it 3 hours later and the bellman gave us a dirty look when we didn't tip him. (Fouad)
The pool was gorgeous and the staff there were nice. The restaurants are quite exspensive , even for a luxery resort. Our server at the bar (Bernadine) was wonderful and friendly. The rooms need some serious updates and the staff was overworked, yet attentive. They need to hire more staff and dump the bellmen. Will not return.

reviews.author: K M
reviews.title: WILL Come back!
reviews.text: We loved the Phoenician, booked a room at another hotel and hated it...stopped at the Pheonician and had to stay! They took $20 off our room because of our experience! CLEAN, has room service 2X a day! We only hung out at the pool 2X in a week and they helped us get chairs once and we asked once! But had a great time! Yes, overpriced but what hotel isnt! Minutes away from ALL restaurants and stores! We booked r room early and came back hrs later and noone helped us get our luggage out of our car or bring it to our room. They need to be more attentive in front of the lobby! We didnt have a view in our room, 1st floor but...lots of privacy and close to the 1st floor bar where the bartender is the BEST! Breakfast is good at the hotel but pricey, the ice cream shop has a cheaper breakfast! Did not eat at the hotel  for lunch or dinner....too many great places to go, and great golfing! WILL be back!!!!! Cutest Easter parade ever!

reviews.author: Jill F
reviews.title: everything was perfect, again
reviews.text: We just got back from the Phoenician Hotel in Scottsdale AZ. .  It was our second visit to the Phoenician.  We stayed here last year same time of year and liked it so much we decided to return again this year from 3/25-3/31.  I have to say everything was just as wonderful as the first time. The hotel was beautiful and the staff is very friendly and helpful.  Our room was on  the fourth floor of the main building facing the pool. Beautiful view!  It is very large for a hotel room and really comfortable.  The decor could probably use an update but everything is still very elegant and clean.  Huge bathroom with marble and shower and large tub. Balconies are large and private and very clean with nice porch furniture.  The grounds are very lush and the pool area is beautiful too.  The only negative I would mention is trying to get a chair by the pool if you arrive any later than 8:00 am.  Last year when you arrived at the pool an attendant was at your side immediately  asking you if you needed a chair.  This year there was far less attendants if any at all and all the chairs were taken by people who sent someone down at like 7 am to save chairs for people who didn't even arrive until later in the afternoon.  This was mildly irritating.  Other than that it's a great place.  Just a hint.  Everything is expensive at the Phoenician.  If you are looking for a bargain don't stay here.  The restaurants were delicious and the pool lunches were great too.  The waitresses at the pool are really nice  and very attentive. We did not use the gym or the spa  So in closing we had another GREAT vacation at The Phoenician.

reviews.author: lmiela
reviews.title: A marvelous resort
reviews.text: This is a 5 Star resort in all aspects, we stayed in a Casita  Room overlooking the pools with a great view of Camelback Mountain.. Our room was located in Casita A on the second floor and was perfect in every way. Our balcony patio was so enjoyable we had several meals delivered, staff set up our balcony patio with linens wonderful tableware, and the food was fresh and delicious. We truly enjoyed this resort and can't wait to go back again. The staff was very helpful and polite, and always ended any and every conversation by asking us if there was anything else they could do for us.  It was a very special experience, and this resort is one we hope you will try as well.

reviews.author: ibbunee
reviews.title: disappointing
reviews.text:
My hubby and I were really disappointed with our stay at the Phoenician. The grounds are nice and the service was pretty good, but the rooms are very dated and 3-star at best. It didn't help that our stay coincided with some rainy weather so we didn't get to enjoy the pools or gardens, but even considering this misfortune, we didn't feel that we got our money's worth from this hotel. For the price we paid and the 5-star rating, I was expecting more luxury.

I also utilized the spa for a facial and the salon for a pedicure. Talk about WAY OVERPRICED! I know hotel spas are known from being pricey but these prices were ridiculous. Again, not worth the money.

Overall, we were quite disappointed with our stay at The Phoenician. So much that we left after 1 night even though we had already paid for 2.

reviews.author: shootingstarbeauty
reviews.title: It was raining outside, but it was still beautiful inside.
reviews.text:
We went to Scottsdale during one of the rainiest weeks of the year.  However, even though we were barely able to sit out and enjoy the beautiful pools at the resort, we still had a wonderful visit.  The service at the hotel is impeccable, as is the food at both the bar and the restaurants.  Everything here is pricey, but the service you will receive is second to none.

Our room had soothing, neutral colors.  The bathroom was large and well-appointed.

We loved, and took great advantage of, the gym.  All of the equipment is state-of-the-art and is well-maintained.  While we managed to get comped for the gym, it is well worth the price of $10 to get in there for a good workout.

One note of caution: valet parking, while fast, is pricey ($25/day).  Self-parking is free.  You can self-park and be right underneath the main building of the hotel.  There's really no need to valet park if you'd rather put your money towards something else.

reviews.author: CharlotteKreuzberg
reviews.title: Like to be on Honeymoon again... made me felt like
reviews.text:
What an awesome hotel - what an awesome stay we had...
no other place like this for golf, honeymoon or just to relax - everything we could experience had been fantastic... it had been 3 days full of magic

reviews.author: Carol M
reviews.title: Beautiful Hotel
reviews.text: My husband and daughter joined me on a business trip to Phoenix and we stayed at the Phoenician.  We were in a private suite which overlooked the tennis courts and had mountain views right outside our veranda (which was huge).  The weather was quite hot since it was July, so we would spend a great amount of time on the veranda after the sun went down.  The grounds are breathtakingly beautiful, with many pools to choose from. The nightly turn down service was a plus, and the room  was gorgeous, with a full living room for entertaining.  The staff was friendly and accomodating (with one exception), but overall the staff was great. The only negative was the nightly visitor we had in our room, a huge blackish brown beetle that is indigenous to the area and comes from the mountains that surrounded our room.  This thing was massive, about 3 inches long. I've since discovered that they can reach up to 6 inches long!! Thank God the one in our room wasn't that big, I think I would have had to check out.  My husband would gently escort this beetle out off the veranda every night and every night he would return.  We called the front desk and they said it was quite common but that they were harmless (not exactly true, they do bite if provoked).  These bugs were also at the pool area after dark, one flew onto my head while we sat by the pool, yuck! The hotel of course, has no control over this so I'm not blaming them just thought I'd mention it for those travelers that freak out over bugs.  We had afternoon English tea in their tearoom and it was Phenomenal (see review).

reviews.author: Alister
reviews.title: OVERRATED
reviews.text: I read the reviews on this hotel and expected a top class hotel. Sadly I was dissappointed. Poor service, average facilities and overall more of a big complex feel rather than the standard expected and recieved at other top worldwide golfing hotels.

reviews.author: CageFreeWill
reviews.title: Worth a Stay
reviews.text: I really liked this hotel.  I stayed here for a business function and had the misfortune of missing my flight out on the Sunday that I was to leave.  The hotel offerd to extend my stay at the dicounted rate that my company had secured.  The property is beautiful if sprawling (be prepared to do a lot of walking).  The rooms were comfortable and clean and they allow pets in certain areas.

reviews.author: Compasspersonnel
reviews.title: Fabulous...
reviews.text:
My partner and I have just returned from 9 days at the Phenician, and other than perhaps our room being ever so slightly tired in terms of decor, we loved it.
Great view from the rooms, they all appear to overlook the pools and gardens, ours certainly did, allowing us also to view the sun coming up as we lay in our 6ft bed!
Breakfast overpriced but the ambience of the restaurant at breakfast more than compensated for it.
Chose to breakfast in the room a couple of times, then out at the breakfast club just 5 mins away in a car.
Valet parking was swift and trouble free, and whilst we had a cabana by the pool all week ( big bonus) we only found the service at the pool lacking one of the days and on expressing our disapointment at the lack of service  we were given a free day by way of an apology.
Afternoon tea is available mid afternoon, so if you miss the UK ,one can, and wee were., tempted by china teacups and cucumber sandwiches just like they serve at the Ritz and about the same exhorbatant price, but again, worth it in my view.

The sun shone, the services we required proved to be on par with other 5 star hotels and we found the concierge staff particularly helpful and a mind of information in terms of restaurant and shopping choices.
Fashion mall just 5 mins in the car and lived up to iour expectations.
Spa and gym disappointing and ludicrous prices in the hair salon and no we most definately shouldnt have been charged $10 for use of the gym!
Other than all that..Cant wait to get back.

reviews.author: Rob S
reviews.title: Seen Former Glories, But Still A Good Property
reviews.text:
I think 5 years ago this would have been the best place to stay in the area. The setting is peaceful, near the airport and has a great golf course. I feel that the hotel could do with a lick of paint here and there and a nudge in the direction of an upgrade in some areas. 

Overall, good service level, good food and good sized rooms. Not a bad price.

reviews.author: JBelf
reviews.title: Beautiful Property, Terrible service
reviews.text:
This hotel has no idea of the meaning of 5-star service.  No warmth in their manner, but more of a "what do you want" attitude from the bellmen, the front desk, the golf starter, and the bartenders.  Our group had 700+ rooms and I heard similar comments from my colleagues.  I will give high marks to the service staff that served our conference area.  The food for our luncheons and breakfasts was very well done.  Not what I expected for these rates.  I wouldn't tolerate this level of service at a best western.  I checked out and moved to the Fairmont Princess; MUCH nicer spa also

Dr James

reviews.author: HollyHop_9
reviews.title: A 5 star experience
reviews.text:
We only stayed at the Phoenician for two nights but had a wonderful time and were impressed by the hotel, it's a true 5 star. The location is great with wonderful views and easy access to Scottsdale, the service was flawless, the property is beautiful and the rooms are large and well equipped. Our room had a sofa and full size desk as well as the King size bed. The bathrooms are particularly good: a large bathroom with two sinks, a large bathtub, and separate shower. Our room looked out onto a courtyard with a fountain and the pool beyond. It was lovely to sit out on the balcony and have a morning coffee. There isn't a coffee maker in the rooms but tea and coffee are available complimentary at the terrace restaurant each morning and afternoon. The pools are lovely and when we visited there were plenty of loungers available. Valet parking is available but the self parking is so easy in the garage under the hotel that we didn't bother with the valet.

If I got a chance to return to the Phoenix/Scottsdale area I'd choose to return to the Phoenician

reviews.author: Amosuk
reviews.title: Canyon Suites are the way forward......
reviews.text:
We stayed for 3 nights in September 2009. The hotel itself is very nice, if a little sprawling, but the Canyon Suites are another level. 
We were shown around the room thoroughly by the excellent "Ambassador". It really was a huge room with every amenity.
The restaurants were all excellent and teh bars well serviced and with great mixologists.
The pools however were a small let down. The main hotel pool was packed and had a very large resort feel, so we opted for the smaller Canyon suites pool.
Much nicer and very quiet although because of this the service was extremely slow.
Overall a great hotel and we would definately return...

reviews.author: UKLizzie
reviews.title: A lot depends on the room you get .....
reviews.text: I like The Phoenician.  I stay in Scottsdale fairly regularly and I rank it my No.2 hotel there, beaten only by the Royal Palms, the quiet intimacy of which I really love.  The Phoenician is much larger and hosts a lot of conventions which inevitably changes the atmosphere somewhat (noisy groups roaming the premises, no room in any of the bars etc.)  But the service is still pretty good and the rooms, bathrooms and common areas are all elegantly decorated so if the rates are reasonable, I'll very happily stay there.  The numerous, large pools make it  particularly attractive if pool time or sunbathing is high on your agenda.  I recommend the Grand Deluxe rooms which are a bit larger than the basic ones and some of which have a beautiful view of the pool area and valley beyond.  But some have better views than others, and for me, a lot of the wow factor depends on that view, so I've been disappointed by my room in the past.  And if there's a big convention on, and you've just booked the one room, your requests for a better one probably won't work.  But this time I got a great room, close to the centre of the building and with a great view.  Food and drink prices are very high, but probably no higher than other local hotels. I wish the bathtubs were deeper, but that's really my only complaint.

reviews.author: CaliforniaYolanda
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: I reserved a weekend golf getaway for my husband and after looking into, it is adverstised as an 18 hole course when in reality it is not.  It is 3 - 9 hole courses and when I made the reservation they did not disclose the fact that one of the nine holes was closed which makes a difference when you're booking a package that includes unlimited golf.  Therefore, we cancelled the reservation within the appropriate time and reserved at the Fairmont.  The reservation was cancelled on 11/19/09 and now 18 days later still don't have the deposit credited.  When verified, they credited to supposedly an unknown account.  Will never reserve at Phoenician-and would not recommend.

reviews.author: Travelerx001
reviews.title: EH - Nice but not stellar
reviews.text:
We are stayed at the hotel in December and had an okay experience.  The facilities and grounds are well kept and the rooms were updated.  However, for a hotel of this class I expected stellar service and I didn't feel that the hotel fully delivered.  I needed a car to pick me up and take me back to the hotel.  I called and was told that the concierge wasn't available and that the bellhop wasn't answering.  I expected that the person on the other end of the line would be able to walk over and request a car, but instead I heard a tepid, "I will try".  What does that mean?  In the end, I had a cab, but not without unwanted stress.  

Here are a few other things people may want to know: 
- High resort prices, $6 for coffee, $14 for a tuna sandwich at the ice cream shop
- There is 1 small playground for kids, but other than that, I didn't see a whole lot for kids to do, especially for kids under 5
- Rooms are spacious and well appointed, but beds and pillows are very soft
- You can't order pizza delivery or other types of food delivery to your room, you have to meet them at the outer gate (due to hotel security rules)
- Food is unremarkable and overpriced

reviews.author: David S
reviews.title: The Phoenician...service and style in the desert
reviews.text:
I just recently completed a golf trip to Scottsdale and we could have not been more pleased with our stay at the Phoenician.  We have an annual trip usually at Kiawah Island but we wanted to do something differnt this year.  My last trip to Scottsdale was seven years ago and I will not wait that long again to return.

The staff( front desk, concierge, bellstand, and housekeeping) at the Phoenician were excellent and very friendly.  The rooms were large and well appointed.  The common areas were beautiful and oriented towards the lovely grounds and the desert in the distance.  This hotel is fairly large but it is also perfect for smaller leisure groups or couples wanting to be pampered.

We played both Troon North courses and We Ko Pa and we were truly impressed with their condition and the professionalism of the pro shops.  Our golf performance was average but the courses were spectacular.  We managed to also find the Arizona casino following two of our golf outings.

I highly suggest that guests frequent Old Town Scottsdale.  Breakfast Club has the best innovative  breakfast fare I have had.  We also ate at the Roaring Fork, Cowboy Ciao, Chelsea's Kitchen.  There seemed to be alot going on in this area at night.

Hopefully, we will return to Scottsdale next year for the warm weather, beautiful golf courses and the hospitality of the Phoenician.

reviews.author: nmycka
reviews.title: Excellent from beginning to end!
reviews.text: We just returned from the Phoenician for a convention and it was fabulous.  The service was excellent and every amenity was provided.  Granted, it was expensive, however, it was worth it.  I'd highly recommend the spa and pool area.  Heaven on earth!

reviews.author: love2travel79
reviews.title: Good Family Friendly Resort.
reviews.text:
My husband and son stayed here on a weekend trip. We found this property very nicely kept, grand, beautiful decor and comfortable.  The grounds are expansive and well maintained. The pool area was big enough that it nevefer felt crowded. It was easy to get lounge chairs in the sun or shade. However, there was poor pool side service. The rooms are decent size with his and her's of closet space, large bathrooms but a little outdated. Room services was timely and good was well prepared. The property is about a 5 minute drive from Downtown Scottsdale and Fashion Square Mall. Overall, we were satisfied with our choice to stay here.  

 Wheather in October was perfect, warm but not hot with a cool breeze in the afternoon. 

The resort has free self parking that they will not advertise. Entrance is through a driveway on the left prior to reaching the Valet stop.

reviews.author: roadwarrior30
reviews.title: Classic dated, some issues
reviews.text: As a reviewer, I need to answer your question -- namely, is it OK to stay here? Our group of 600 descended upon this hotel for several days. The property is certainly beautiful and well maintained and the staff accommodating to every request.  The rooms are a bit dated, not the current theme of newer chic hotels to offer clean modern lines, but it's well maintained. Part of our staff stayed at the newer W hotel (1 mile away) which had is 'the' hotel to stay at. The only real negative I encountered was inconsistent hot water in the room, I attribute this to too few guests at the property. This hotel is a fine choice for your visit to the Phoenix/Scottsdale area.

reviews.author: Matilde75
reviews.title: 砂漠のエキゾチックなリゾート。
reviews.text:
日本語の口コミがなかったので、かなり前の滞在ですが、書きます。家族とゴルフリゾートで行きました。アリゾナの夏は太陽がものすごくきついですが、乾燥した空気でアジアの夏より過ごしやすいです。冬のほうが、避寒地なので価格は高いです。
ゴルフ場はかなりロングコースで崖超え当たり前、と厳しいですが、よいコースで、サボテンの砂漠の中、プレイリードックや野兎も見つつプレイできるのは、なかなかない光景で感動します。
ほぼ毎日スコールがあるのですが、ホテルの部屋から遠くの砂漠とサボテンと町に落ちる遠雷を見ながら過ごす、という経験は人生でも初めてでした。ぜひ、お勧めします。
部屋もホテル館内も、都内の新しい外資系ホテルに慣れた日本人が高級ホテルとして認識してよろしいレベルだと思います。
近くのショッピングモールは穴場ですが、少々柄の悪い人はいます。
ただ、私には愛想のよろしいスタッフ。（私は英語が苦手）。親が激怒したのは「こんな高級リゾートに日本人が来るようになったのか」とつぶやいたスタッフの一言だそうで。（かなり侮蔑的な言い方だったらしいです。おそらくスタッフは大学生のアルバイトだったのかと思います。）。日本人も来るんだよ、日本人にもお勧めするから、目の前では軽蔑の言葉は言わず、裏で言ってくれたらよろしいかな。と思いました。
よって。侮蔑の英語すらわからない私には、エキゾチックな砂漠の天国でした。
アリゾナがとても好きになりました。

reviews.author: JetSetLifeUS
reviews.title: Definitely worth to be part of The Luxury Collection!
reviews.text:
Wow. This is how I have to start this review. The Phoenician is one of those hotels that you plan on returning to the next time you are in town. Several room amenities that we experienced include: turn down service with chocolates, the wait staff offered to get us fresh ice with our room service meal, and soothing music playing in your room with fresh ice each night. These little bits are small, but quickly add up as you realize that importance of knowing that the hotel cares for your business by providing these little things that you will remember and makes The Phoenician different than other hotels.

The room was clean and very nice. I thought the room reminded me of a room in a french mansion with nice white walls, white moulding, and golden carpet in our room. The patio was definitely a nice way to relax and sunbathe. We opted for a entry level executive suite and were moved to a larger suite when I pointed out that the square footage of the suite we reserved was more than the suite we received. I did not know that there are suite categories so technically they were the same class. Nonetheless the manager on duty moved us to a larger suite as the check in person did not explain this. I was wowed with the hotel making sure I was happy. The location is pretty close to anything you wanted like the Kierland Commons and Old Scottsdale, both for shopping. 

The grounds are breath taking with the Camelback Mountain on one side and lush green golf courses on the other side. With a gated in fence we felt safe 100% of the way during our stay. 

Would I return, yes. The Centre for Well Being Spa and golf courses are top notch and I enjoyed these portions of our stay. What is nice is a full cactus garden you can walk through on the resort grounds. Very informative and fun at the same time.

More pictures and information is available at my personal travel experience site: http://www.jetsetlife.us/resorts/luxurycollection/phoenician/phoenician.html

reviews.author: travelernovice
reviews.title: Relaxing Resort
reviews.text: While everything is very expensive, the resort is beautiful and has excellent customer service. Room service comes in a timely manner (but is very pricey). The pool staff is very gracious. The pool bar has an excellent selection of drinks. The lower level dining option has great food and prices are reasonable for a resort. The steak house restaurant has excellent steak, but the rest of the food was mediocre.  You can sit on the patio to the wee hours of the night, with a great view, on your own private sofa, next the fire place and order drinks and dessert from the attentive wait staff. This was one of the best times of my trip! PS- The 7 tiered swimming pools were beautiful and uncrowded.

reviews.author: sunshinelovers
reviews.title: Would not want to pay top dollar for this place
reviews.text:
We stayed for ten nights at the beginning of September, it was very hot but we got a great rate :) 

Negatives

The hotel rooms were a dissapointment - we booked a deluxe room which is one up from the entry level room. They are old and lacking any character. We were moved after a few nights due to an ant problem to a room that was a grand deluxe and although it was HUGE it was no better. They need to give the rooms a refurb asap as I notice that a lot of people on trip advisor have commented on this. On the upside the beds were amazingly comfortable!

The breakfast was limited and over priced. They have a buffet on weekends which is tiny and then a limited menu in the week, this is always a pain to us as we dont want to wait 15mins for a bowl of cereal in the morning. So we took to eating in the little cafe which was expensive but did the trick. We also ate dinner at the Italian one night, food was average.

Positives

The pool areas are spacious and they bring round pitchers of ice water - service is great. In fact service throughout the resort is excellent. There is a great programme of activities for kids and for sporty types such as yoga and tennis circuits, which was a nice touch.  The golf course is excellent and prices are reasonable.

The location of the hotel is wonderful, stunning Camelback Mountain towers over the resort and there are lots of shops and restauranats nearby - including a big mall.

Overall its a great property but I would not want to return until a refurb has been completed.

reviews.author: John H
reviews.title: Excellent!
reviews.text: Everything about the Phoenician was brilliant - OK the ice cream was a bit OOT but well worth the indulgence! The grounds are extremely well kept with plenty of room around them and the pools to relax. The conference rooms were discrete so if you were on holiday you wouldn't really have noticed the business activity that may be going on. Good location for day trips out to Grand Canon, golf, shopping in the old town etc.

reviews.author: TrevorNYC1111
reviews.title: Never disappointed - the Phoenician is the Tops
reviews.text: Sixth time and second for personal....top notch stay and not a complaint in mind. The grounds are impeccably kept and the rooms are fantastic. This is a very unique and special place! Get a Grand Deluxe King room - well worth it!

reviews.author: ReignTraveler
reviews.title: Food costs are out of hand
reviews.text: I have stayed all over the world and this hotel by far has the most expensive food. $6.50 for a tall drip coffee or $5 for a bagel? My family(8 & 3 year old kids) and my wife stayed here for 5 nights end of August. I am used to spending a lot for hotel foods as I travel for work but this hotel has taken the prices to another level. In the future, we will stay at the Westin Kierland where you can walk to nearby restraunts and shops.

reviews.author: aark
reviews.title: beautiful hotel a little dated
reviews.text: We stayed at the Phoenician and all in all had a great time with a few hiccups . I agree with the other reviewers that the hotel is a little dated but the grounds a beautiful with little meandering pathways with waterfalls and fountains. We stayed in a casita room over looking the grounds, pool, and camelback mountain the room was spacious and very clean with a huge bathroom with tub seperate shower and toilet room with bidet it also had a walk in closet with a wall safe. The service was outstanding in all the areas except the pool which seemed to be understaffed the wife asked for an ice tea and the server took almost a half an hour to bring it.Ate at J&G Steakhouse the most beautiful view in the city be prepared to spend some money but well worth it I had the NY with three different sauces and the wife had the Dover Sole which she said was the best she ever had. Hike Camelback Mountain behind the hotel but be warned it is a 2 mile walk before you even get to the traihead but you will have a great view if you make it to the top. My only other concern was at the pool with the kids there seemed to be alot of college kids drinking and saying some innapropiate things in front of the kids I am not sure if they were guests of the hotel there seem to be no one checking.

reviews.author: Jerseygrl68
reviews.title: Just ok
reviews.text: I was in Sedona on my way to Scottsdale, I called them and asked for directions,  no one & I mean no one could tell me the exit number I was to look for off of the hwy. They just kept saying look for Camelback Rd. But I would have liked some markers or exit numbers to look for, being I am from Jersey. I booked my room directly with the hotel and was assured by the reservationist that upgrading to a Grand Deluxe would give me an incredible view. I requested an upper flr and late check out on Sunday. After arriving @ 8;30pm on a Friday evening, the clerk told me I was on the bottom floor and had no other room, she also said their were no requests on my file. As I saw in other  reviews I was not offered an upgrade of any means, in fact she offered me a downgrade. My room overlooked a bush and cement patio that housed a fountain, not the sweeping pool views  I was prosmised on the phone. I went to m y room and called the 1-800 number who looked up my reservation and told me that indeed those requests were on my file. Now I am fuming. I waited till the morning and spoke with Rebecca the manager, who was sweet & apologized and switched my room to the fourth floor. I was only staying 2 nights so it was a pain to worry about that when I wanted to be at the pool. I was also never offered anything for my inconvience. After moving I was looking forward to my cabana by the pool. it was the first time I ever rented one. Ben our server was all over us till about 12 noon. As soon as the pool got busy we never saw him. The ppl sitting by the pool paying nothing extra was getting better service than us. We never got the free fruit tray because when we wanted to go up to the room he was once again MIA. When I checked out he had the nerve to tack on a $50 tip for bringing us 2 rounds of drinks and lunch I waited an hour for cause we couldn't find him. Once again Rebecca was kind &  adjusted the bill ,but I would have preferred great service from the beginning and not taking money off the bill. The pools are great and the cactus garden is not to be missed, but if I went back I would try somewhere else.

reviews.author: kelleyt
reviews.title: Phoenician Is A Little Piece of Desert Heaven
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at the Phoenician and can't understand who could possibly review this hotel poorly.  They must just be hard to please! This is an outstanding hotel, with fabulous ammenties, and over the top customer service.  From check in to check out, everyone at the hotel was friendly, nice, helpful, and just generally happy to be working there.  I would rather be treated well than have perfectly clean carpet anyday!  I see many people on these reviews that mention stains on the carpet.  I would imagine it is very hard to keep a hotel of that size pristine without any marks on the carpet.  Those people should stay somewhere where shoes are not allowed!  Those minor little details could not deter me from loving every little detail of the Phoenician.  The only complaint I would venture to even remark would be the prices of food and beverage.  But, I am in Scottsdale with tons of stores, restaurants, shops, Starbucks, etc.  I didn't need to stay there for the food!
The pools were awesome for both kids and adults.  It was 114 degrees so you had to stay in the water.  The staff kept your pitchers filled with ice water, and were easy to find if you needed a beverage.  
The grounds were beautiful, well kept, and amazingly green.  On the backside of the resort, if you stay facing the mountain is also terrific.  Our room was a corner suite so the walk was far to the resort.  But, we walked along side the mountain and took advantage of the trails and desert gardens.

reviews.author: ncinaz
reviews.title: Faded but still a nice hotel
reviews.text:
We just stayed at the Phoenician for the first time in about a decade and I daresay they haven't changed a thing in that time. OK, there are new TVs in the rooms and the restaurants look like they have been upgraded, but everything else is surprisingly run-down. Carpets are tattered and stained. Furniture is attractive but aged. Breakfast at Il Terrazzo was mediocre at best. An outdoor hallway was littered with dead bees throughout our stay. 

Despite all that, it's still a nice hotel, although how they are able to command just about the highest rates in the area is a mystery to me. Service was generally outstanding and the pools and grounds are still knockouts. It's hard not to like the place but it is long overdue for renovations.

reviews.author: Wiley12
reviews.title: The Phoenician is Where It's At
reviews.text:
Recently stayed at the Phoenician over a July weekend and really do not have a bad word to say about it.  Many good ones though.  Let's see:

Rooms: Upon check-in we were upgraded to a Casita Suite probably b/c the hotel was at 40% occupancy.  I mean, who trips to Phoenix in July?  The Living Room of the Casita Suite was a bit outdated with the furniture but very spacious and had a very large patio that looked out onto the golf course.  The bedroom was nicely updated with all the amenities that one would expect to find at a resort of this caliber.  The bed was large and very comfortable and the TV was updated and large as well.  The patio of the bedroom was again a good size and provided many seating options.  

Bathroom:  Very nice sized bathroom with separate tub and glass shower.  The shower was very large and provided a bench and an amazing shower head that provided a very nice flow of water.

Pool:  The pool(s) are the best thing about the resort.  We spent both days on the top level at the activities pool and enjoyed basketball and volleyball and music, both live and radio, all while being waited on by very attentive pool attendants providing complimentary water and beverage service (not complimentary).  The water slide was great and the kids that were out at the resort seemed to really enjoy that as well.  There is a pool for everyone depending on what you are in the mood for.  If you would like to hang out at the pool without all the activities then the serenity pool on the lower level is probably for you. 

Grounds:  The grounds around the hotel are simply beautiful.  It's a good walk from the Casita Suites to the main hotel but the grounds are so beautiful that it's not a big deal at all.  If, not for the heat you would forget that you are in Scottsdale.

Food:  Did not eat at the resort so I have no comment.

Service:  In addition to the upgrade of the room and the service at the pool the overall hospitality and striving to make our stay perfect was definitely noticed.  We called the front desk around 12:30am the first night that we were there b/c a glass of wine had been spilled on the bed.  Housekeeping was at the room and had the bed lines all changed withing 5-10 minutes (they got a nice tip for that one).  I made several requests upon check-in, none of them unreasonable, and they were all taken care of in a very timely manner without the hint of a complaint.

$: Yes, it's expensive but you get what you pay for.  Parking charges were avoided because of staying in the Casitas but there is free self parking that is not too far away from the main lobby.  Drinks are a bit on the high side but you should know what to expect going into a experience like this.  Do your research and then you are not surprised.

Overall, I would definitely recommend the Phoenician to friends and family and to people looking for a great getaway in the middle of the dessert.

reviews.author: SpongeBobCH
reviews.title: Very nice and relaxing stay
reviews.text:
Very nice luxury resort and nice views.
Really professional staff , as you would expect at this level (but do not always get).  We only stayed one night on a round trip through Arizona and Nevada but we enjoyed every minute. Very nice pool area - open 24 h   ! - (bar service stops at 6 pm). 
Beautiful gardens, pools and nice restaurants. Everything is a bit pricy, though not outrageous - but thats kind of expected in a 5* resort (a draft beer at the pool is around 6 dollars + tax, a pitcher of lemonade for the whole family is 10 dollars)
It  can be seen that the resort is not brand new, but it is kept in very good shape.
Overall very much recommended if you get a decent price (or can afford paying the regular rate). 
Note : Valet parking (no other choice available to my knowledge)  is some 20 dollars + tips extra

reviews.author: njenkinson
reviews.title: I will definitely be back - a fantastic resort!
reviews.text:
Amazing guest rooms, restaurants, pools, golf, shops, spectacular views, a gym, salon, fabulous conference facilities...all on-site at The Phoenician!

A must-do is a hike up Camelback Mountain (within walking distance).

reviews.author: Paul R
reviews.title: AAA+  Excellent hotel. Very luxurious.
reviews.text:
I have been here twice, both times on business.  Summer rates, while hot in Phoenix, are reasonable and the hotel is extremely luxurious.  

Rooms are large and the views spectacular.  I like this for business but hightly recommend it for vacations.  It is a real gem in the Scottsdale area.  

The staff treats you like royalty!

reviews.author: vanessa83
reviews.title: I Love This Place
reviews.text:
Self-admittedly a travel snob. Luxury Collection makes me swoon. This place does not fail to impress, even on my third visit. 

The Phoenician is a calming luxury retreat, overlooking the wondrous hues of Camelback Mountain contrasting a sky so vivid blue, you'd think you were dreaming. The resort itself is what you would expect - sprawling multilevel pools, service staff that seem to read your mind, great spa, amazing tennis courts, and spectacular golf course.

Driving up to the lobby, after the initial wow factor, you'll wonder whether you should have worn something a little nicer. Check-in staff was friendly as can be, we asked for a suite in the casitas and they kindly gave it to us after a little persuasion. A huge 1300 sq. ft. suite for $135/night?!?! Twilight Zone. Another great reason to go in the off-season. Also asked for a complimentary fitness pass that was offered last time, so no $20 fee every time, and we attended many yoga and meditation classes. 

The rooms are on the borderline of dated, I believe they will be addressing this soon. They're still quite luxurious, spacious, equipped with oversized bath products etc etc. More than pleasant.

We played tennis - the pro played in Wimbledon and actually offered constructive advice. 

There's a free Games Room in the tennis club for kids with a Wii, mini movie theatre, air hockey, ping pong etc. And although we are not kids, this was our guilty pleasure.

The café was great for gelato, breakfast items. The smoothies were very tasty, as were many other menu items (also a food snob) - and not outrageously expensive. The restaurant was expensive (but really, what do you expect?), but very good.
