We went for a getaway and we truly felt relaxed and pampered the entire time. This place is great if you crave luxury on a budget. The great part is you're still a stone's throw away from many shopping options and fab restaurants in Scottsdale. Definitely recommend Lon's at the Hermosa Inn - romance and delectable menu.

Re: 'Thieves' review - Whether you’re at the Ritz or Motel 6, don’t leave your valuables around and they won’t get stolen. I have surprised on many occasion at how many individuals have access to your room and do access your room throughout the day.

reviews.author: julias
reviews.title: Enjoyed the Phoenician
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at the Phoenician for 3 nights over Father's Day weekend.   The hotel is very relaxing and the staff very friendly.   The rooms are contemporary and pretty large with a desk and seperate sitting area.   There are several pools, including a waterslide pool, as well as a serenity-style pool.  The steak house J & G was really very good with great ambience and a creative menu.  If you have a car, you can self-park for free and forego the $26/day valet charge.  Overall, the Phoenician was a good solid choice.

reviews.author: Meemer1
reviews.title: Flawless
reviews.text:
Arrived for a 4 day, 3 night stay in the Canyon Suites over 4th of July weekend.  Only $275 a night as July is off season for this resort - an incredible value for the experience.

We were greeted by name by our 'ambassador' and were already checked in somehow, he took us straight to our suite at 11 am.  The room was gorgeous, stylish and well appointed.  The bed and pillows are dream inducing and wonderful.  

Morning brings complimentary coffee and tea in the lobby, afternoon is freshly made fruited tea and iced lemon water, along with fruit.  You can also request in-room 'silver coffee service' in the old style heavy silver serving pieces.  However the lobby service and silver service begin at 6am; tough as we were visiting from the east coast and up by 4 or 5 am (not their fault!)

Canyon suites have a private pool, and while children are permitted, the mood is clearly adult.  Servers bring pitchers of ice water - complimentary - and keep the pool immaculate and area clean and stocked with towels.

Resort was not crowded due to the time of year, which made the visit very quiet and relaxing.   No problems getting into the restaurants, both major eateries were wonderful - sommelier at Il Terrazo was gracious and informative.

Staff at the resort...without a single exception...were 4-star.  Everyone pleasant, greeting you with a hello, have a nice day.  And seeming very sincere.  The grounds are immaculate - constant grooming.  The resort and rooms were lovely without being overly-fancy.  Sophisticated and elegant.

We left dinner early one night (birthday dinner for both of us) because I was not feeling well, and the waitress packed a box of cookies for me to enjoy later.  Top notch.  Afternoon tea is a must.

Without a doubt, one of the finest vacations we have experienced.  The staff anticipated every need, always offered cold bottled water (again complimentary!), offered to take pictures, etc. and truly seemed concerned that their guests enjoy every aspect of the Phoenician.  Every detail attended to here!

Useless note: Arizona hot in July....like, Africa hot.

reviews.author: rufit21
reviews.title: THIEVES!!!!
reviews.text:
My wife and I were looking forward to traveling to Arizona and spending sometime in the sun, since the weather on the east coast has been dismal.  We chose The Phoenician Resort after careful research, and stayed from June 21-26.  Let's start by saying that everything was perfect, and that we did not have one complaint about the resort.  Actually, we raved to our friends and family members about how great of a time we had, and had planned to return next year with our two children.
 
The problem started on June 28.  My wife, who is a bank manager called me and asked if I used my credit card to purchase over $300.00 dollars worth of items from a undisclosed website (a well known book store), and I told her, "No".  Furthermore, I advised my wife that I haven’t even used my credit card in over a week, and that we had used her card while on vacation.  Nonetheless, she informed me that someone had stolen my credit card information and was purchasing products online.  How could this be?  I have never had my credit card stolen.  After sitting down with my wife and thinking how this could have happened, I told her I left my wallet in the bedroom while visiting the pool and working out while at the Phoenician.  I told her that I remember coming back to the room and noticed that my wallet was slightly disturbed from where I had left.  I remember opening the wallet and noticed that everything was accounted for, and left it at that.  My wife also informed me that she was missing a diamond charm from her bracelet, which she later informed that it was of no value (the person who stole it must have thought it was real).

We didn’t call to inform the manager of the resort because we really didn’t have any proof.  If they read this, “You have a thief/thieves amongst your staff”.

Nonetheless, you use your own judgment.  I've been in law enforcement for several years and have investigated crimes like this before.  In actuality, I did subpoena the records to the company where the perp attempted use my credit card.  However, the company recognized the purchase as being fraudulent and reimbursed me, so I suspended the investigation.

Just be careful when visiting this resort with your valuables.  There is a safe in the room and it should be used.  In my line of work I should have known better, but would have never thought that a 5 star resort would have staff that would go through guests personal items for their own personal gain.

Furthermore, I loved Arizona and won’t let this individual deter us from returning.  If anyone reads this could you please give me another “trustful” resort to visit?  I would like to return next year with wife and kids.

reviews.author: Deakins
reviews.title: Relaxing stay
reviews.text: As soon as we checked into the Hotel we got undressed and into our swimsuits and headed down to the pool, and enjoyed all the pools!  I LOVED it I was SOOO relaxed!

reviews.author: Enchantress71
reviews.title: The bloom has fallen off the rose....
reviews.text:
I really should have listened to the negative comments on this site about The Phoenician.  The grounds of the hotel are amazingly well cared for, standing in stark contrast to the guest rooms.  The guest rooms were spacious, however, they were in need of a serious renovation.  The carpets had stains on them and were generally on the thread bare side.  The bed was large and nice, however, the sheets had a few small holes in them.  The crown modeling and the walls looked slightly worn.  The bathroom was large, but needed an overhaul.  Everything needed updating/replacing.  You could tell that perhaps ten or fifteen years ago this resort was beautiful, but they had done very little, if anything, to upgrade and modernize the facility.  

The first room I was assigned was at the end of a hallway in the main building that smelled like feet.  There was a large pile of trash in front of the door of an adjacent room that sat there for hours before it was removed.  The room itself was dark and the patio doors opened to a patio that was almost completely blocked by a wall and shrubbery.  Only a sliver of light reached the inside of the room, making it feel cave like (or jail like) and confining.  I promptly asked for another room and was assigned a casita near the spa.  This room was equally as worn, however, it had a lovely view of the koi fish pond and the pool.

The pools are plentiful (nine of them, to be exact) and nice, however, they seem to have a duck problem.  Flocks of ducks swim in both the koi pond and the pools themselves, leaving duck poop around the entrances to the pool.  On one occasion, a duck had left a gift right at the entryway to the pool, and when one of the cabana boys was alerted to its presence by one of the guests, he said he would "tell his manager" and did absolutely nothing about it.  Neither he or manager did anything about that poop pile or any of other poop piles left by the duck during my four day stay.

Safety might be an issue at this hotel as well.  While I was sitting in my room, a gentleman opened my door with a keycard that the front desk had given him.  I think we scared the living daylights out of one another.  He told me that he had been assigned the room I was in, and I told him there must be some mistake.  After he left, someone from the front desk called, not to apologize, but to ask me what I was doing in the room because according to the hotel's records, I was supposed to transfer rooms again on that very day.  I informed her that I had no desire to move and if I had to move again it would be to another room at another hotel.  

The resort food is expensive, however, that wasn't my biggest problem with it.  The resort has a problem with ever aggressive birds that swoop down and grab the very expensive food straight from the plates of the patrons.  As people would leave their tables to retrieve food from the breakfast buffet ($25 + tip), the birds would swoop in and take a nip from people's water and juice glasses.  If someone left the table with food on it,  forget about it.  The crow-like birds would carry everything off in an instant.  The operated in packs.  At one point during breakfast on Saturday, a bird flew down and pecked a woman eating breakfast.  She wasn't hurt, and the restaurant staff was extremely apologetic, but they could do nothing to abate the chronic bird situation.  

The resort was particularly boring as well.  No real activities to speak of and the pool bars, which were hopping during the day, closed at 6pm sharp, leaving most folks looking for things to do off of the resort property during the evening.  Good thing self-parking was plentiful, because you could come and go as you pleased in order to find entertainment off property. 

The spa is sufficient, however, it's ridiculous that the only way you can use the only gym in the resort without paying an additional daily fee, is to purchase a spa treatment.  If you purchase a spa treatment, access to the smallish gym is complimentary for the day of your spa treatment, however, if you don't, you have to pay $20 a day to use the gym.

Final note:  If you go to this resort, make sure you have mapquest directions or a GPS before you come to Phoenix.  On three different occasions, I called the resort for directions and got different and wrong directions every single time.  What should have taken about twenty minutes to get to the resort from the airport, ended up taking me more than an hour.  I eventually just ran across it with absolutely no help from the resort staff.

p.s. -- On my last morning at the resort, I made my way to one of the pools and guess what saw on the lawn?  I pair of dirty mens underwear.  Lovely.

reviews.author: Family of Seven
reviews.title: Favorite Starwood Resort in Phoenix/Scottsdale Area
reviews.text:
Despite the busy Memorial Day holiday weekend, this resort is so spread out, we didn't even notice it. I'm a Platinum SPG member and was greatfully upgraded to two rooms in the Casitas (nearby kid's pool) by Aaron at the front desk. Don't need to valet, just park next to room. This resort is great for every leisure experience. I have five young children and they all love this resort. The Canyon rooms and pool are also nice (also don't need valet w/basement parking).
They have four or more pools here, kid's water slide, golf, tennis, etc. On Camelback Rd so great location. Great indoor and outdoor malls in either direction on Camelback. 
Favorite Restaurant is Mastros in North Scottsdale on Pima Rd (take the 101 Loop from McDonald Rd). Mastros has many other nearby locations. Best bone-in ribeye steak, sea bass, mac & cheese, chocolate pudding cake, etc.
My children loved the nighttime watersliding and movie (at pool).  We have a vacation home on the Indian Wells Golf Coarse (3.5hrs away in CA) and still come here once a year. The Phoenician is always a fun experience (as long as you get the right room).

reviews.author: GoneAgainNashua_NH
reviews.title: Be careful of the Reservation system at the Phoenician which is part of the The Luxury Collection.
reviews.text:
Be careful of the Reservation system at the Phoenician which is part of the The Luxury Collection. 

If you stay at this resort or make a reservation with the luxury collection, be aware that the rooms are paid for in advance and are Non Changeable And Non Refundable. 

After making the reservation, we found the rates had been discounted by 1/3. We contacted the hotel and this is there response.

“Hotels calculate how busy they will be and offer the rates that are available for each day of the year. Because new reservations are made every day, this situation changes frequently. Though rates usually increase, the opposite can happen; if there are cancellations of large conferences or groups for example, the hotel will have more rooms available and may be able to offer a lower rate to attract more bookings. 
Your reservation at The Phoenician, was made on one of our Starwood branded websites under the 'Internet Only' rate plan as a fully prepaid, non refundable, non changeable reservation. 
The Internet Only rate plan was created to allow guests to book on our Starwood branded websites while still enjoying the benefits of the Starwood Preferred Guest program. As this rate tends to be much lower than any other rate plan, it has very strong restrictions associated with it. For this reason, the cancellation policy clearly appears throughout the reservation process to allow the guest to change to a different rate before confirming their reservation and their acceptance of these restrictions. 
We do offer other rate plans which have more flexibility for guests who require more flexibility in their travel plans. We must uphold the cancellation policies for each of our different rate plans. 
We appreciate your patronage of Starwood Hotels & Resorts Worldwide and I do apologize for any inconvenience that this has caused you but hope that you will understand the need for these policies. We are unable to modify this reservation or rate.”

We also stayed in the rear of the hotel with a "Mountain view".  The only problem is the Mountain is only 50’ away.  

Stay somewhere else

reviews.author: Sarah
reviews.title: Great Stay at the Canyon Suites
reviews.text: Fantastic stay! Rooms were awesome, clean and staff bent over backwards for our every need. SPA was AMAZING!! I highly recommend this resort for groups, couples and outings!

reviews.author: PSPman222
reviews.title: Best Luxury Resort - better than expected
reviews.text:
We were going to Scottsdate for a wedding.  We decided on the Phoenician for 3 nights even after reading some poor reviews on tripadvisor.  I was there for 2 weeks!  I have stayed at some of the top resorts in the US and this was right up there with all of them.   This includes 4-season (Maui) and Ritz Carlton (Lake Las Vegas).  I do not understand some the past poor reviews.  Everything at the resort was near perfect.  

I am a SPG Platinum member and did get an upgraded room to a much larger room.  I noticed they were doing construction right outside my room and requested a room change.  They said they were out of the larger rooms and could only put me in the mountian view basic room.  Room was very nice (bit small) but very impressive. 

Food was amazing here.  We loved breakfast and the italian restaurant at night.  I will upload a pic of the meal but both were 5 star meals.  

Pool was amazing.  Waiters were everywhere looking to charge $20 for a cheeseburger.  I accidently paid $18 for sun tan loation.  O-well.  Not too worried since I was on vacation. 

Tennis courts were amazing with a small play area with the Wii setup.  Enjoyed that.  I have an 18 month old daughter and we cannot wait to take her here next Spring.

Self park was SOOO easy and FREE!  Did I mention it was free?  I was amazed how close it was and that it was free!  You basically park underground right under the lobby for free. 

Overall, if you can take the $200-$400 per night in Scottsdale then there is nowhere else to stay.  Lots to do with incredible grounds and service.  A must stay if you are in Scottsdale.

reviews.author: andy4pr
reviews.title: Exceptional Service and BEAUTIFUL grounds
reviews.text:
I am a very discriminating traveler and it takes a lot to impress me.  I've visited this resort twice and it is probably the best place I've ever stayed.  The service is absolutely, positively exceptional - you cannot beat it.  The grounds are beautiful.  I'm not a huge fan of Scottsdale, as there aren't a whole lot of things do "see" in the area, but you can spend several days at this resort and not miss the outside world.

I wholeheartedly recommend this resort to anyone visiting the Phoenix area.  It is a great place to stay.  If possible, and if you can afford it, I recommend staying in the Canyon Suites (a resort inside a resort), but all of their rooms are great.  

Awesome service.  Awesome food.  Really cool afternoon tea.  You really need to stay here!

reviews.author: chicagonurse
reviews.title: Nice resort, but pricey...
reviews.text: I was at The Phoenician for a business meeting for several days. It is a very nice resort that is conveniently located. I opted to extend my stay by one night which set me back $199 (1/2 of the regular price). The restaurants and bars are EXTREMELY expensive as were the Spa services. They also charge $12.95 a day for internet access, which, for such an expensive resort, should be included in the cost of the room.  I did enjoy the Cactus Garden, which features over 300 types of cactus and desert plants. The pools were very nice as well.  I probably would not seek this out as a place to stay if I were traveling at my own expense, but it was a nice experience on the company's dollar.

reviews.author: bostonskigal
reviews.title: Great weekend getaway-but 5 star it is most definately not
reviews.text: We are SPG members and my 4 girlfriends and I go away every year on mostly points.  We like to stay in a suite so we can all be together.  We were upgraded to a Casita suite from two rooms-which was really nice of the manager.  We also like to have a kitchenette for wine/cheese and some breakfast foods.  We arrived to find the kitchen like the "grinch who stole Christmas."  There wasn't even a knife in the drawer, no dishes, no papertowels, no coffee maker-zero.  Why have a fridge and dishwasher if it's not a real kitchen.  We did love the pool, we hiked Camelback (amazing), the yoga teacher was awesome, the food at La Terrazza was great although waitress in the bar was terrible, she tried to sell us on the 50% off any wine at least 5 times and was constantly interrupting us for no real reason, and when it was time to pay she stranded us)  Rooms were tired and furniture dated, however bed was super comfortable, bathrooms gorgeous/all marble, flat screen TV's. The grounds were amazing,  but overall they just don't have their act together enough to be 5 star.

reviews.author: Angie55
reviews.title: Nice and relaxing
reviews.text: Great hotel!  The best parts were definitely the bed (extremely comfortable), the bathroom (absolutely huge), the balcony (had a lounge chair as well as a table and chairs), and the pools - I think there are 8 or 9.  Free self parking in the garage was an added bonus.  Very good location - easy to get around.  Very quiet - I never heard anyone in the halls, etc.  Beautiful hotel!  I truly cannot think of anything negative to say... Well, I never did figure out how to work the alarm clock!

reviews.author: Rob D
reviews.title: Very good Experience at the Phoenician
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed at the Phoenician in May.  The weather was perfect and the experience at the resort was the same.  We booked on points so were a little more free with our spending.  The only negative thing I could possibly say about the property is the food and beverage are steep.  However, when you stay at a Starwood Luxury property this is usually par for the course.  

Overall the pool area is perfect.  Plenty of space to spread out and relax.  They have a bar that juts out into the pool area and they have misters that allow you to enjoy a drink or lunch even when it is 100+ outside.  

The Spa was very good.  We booked an early massage and a class at teh workout center.  We were the only ones who showed for the class so we were able to enjoy a private fitness session.  The spa was great and the ammenities didn't dissapoint.  A very relaxing morning.

We visited the Thirsty Camel on 2 of the nights and enjoyed a drink with a great veiw of the area.  

The service was near perfect everywhere on the property.  

I would definitely go back and stay again.

reviews.title: Iffy
reviews.text: If this was a three or four star hotel I would rate it higher, but for the price, I think I'd pass next time and find another place.  Our room was a little on the dated side and a lobby makeover is certainly in order.  We travel alot and comparing it to other hotels with this rank, there's no comparison. The outdoor facilities (pools and courts and grounds) were far nicer than the interior.  The service was five star and even the restaurant meals we had were below par.

reviews.author: bridgetn
reviews.title: Beautiful, Peacefull, $ Spendy
reviews.text:
Stayed at the Phoenician in April.   

I found the Resort beautiful.  The landscaping, gardens, flowers, trees and all were lush and refreshing from the brown dead WI scenery i came from.   

The front desk, housekeepers, bartenders, pool boys, etc... were very pleasant & go out of there way for whatever request you may have.   I thought they were all very friendly and cannot think of one bad thing to say about any of the employees at the Phoenician. 

The rooms were clean and very spacious.  And the beds were more comfy than mine.  Bathrooms were great too.  

The pool area is what you wanted it to be.   if you wanted quiet  - you could have peace and quiet.  they did have music playing during the day but that was near the pool bar.   you could not even hear it on the other side.     You can make whatever you want it to be during  your stay.  if you someone you wants to find fault and complain about the music being too loud then your the person who puts yourself right next to the drums.  The pool area is very large and there are many pools to choose from so just choose the area that suits you.

Oh and they have a huge hot tub down in the pool area that is open 24-7.   went down there later at night for a few cocktails.    our little group of 6-8 people were usually the only ones in it.  It was very relaxing after a long day.  

OK the only thing i have bad to say is the prices for food & drink.   The are outrageous!  my friend order a grilled cheese sandwich.  nothing special.  bread and cheddar cheese.  $18.00.    How good can you make a grilled cheese for 18.00 ?  another friend and i split a burger and fries,  had 2 beers a piece and some tortilla chips and salsa for  $68.00.  so if you need a drink, besides water - that is complimentry, plan on spending some cash.   

hope this helps any questions feel free to contact me.

reviews.author: charlie15
reviews.title: Nice, comfortable and modern.
reviews.text:
The Phoenician would not be my typical vacation choice, since I don't play golf and it is a very expensive hotel. However, since I was there for a business meeting I enjoyed my stay.
The Hotel is well located, 15 minutes from the airport. The grounds and golf courses are superbly kept and spectacular. The room was large and luxurious and the bed very comfortable. Service in general is excellent as well. For those who need their work out the fitness center is top notch!

reviews.author: Mark-LosAngeles-CA
reviews.title: Weird 80s Concept Hotel
reviews.text:
Yes, it's 5 star.  Yes, it's in Scottsdale.  But who really wants to stay in a kitsch 80s boutique whose main building looks suspiciously like a GEICO regional office and with an interior straight from The Donald's tower in NYC.

Worst of all though is the acres of lawn and water features.  Here in the desert.  It just all seems so out-of-step and inappropriate now.  Maybe creating these "oases" was all the range 25 years ago but today it just seems wasteful in terms of water resources.  The trouble is that management probably hasn't realised how amusing this place is - or rather would be if the issue of water conservation in the south-west were not so serious.  Slopping millions of gallons of water on manicured lawns and sub-tropical plants while the Colorado River dries up to a trickle is not just non-PC, it's downright unethical.  There are plenty of great hotels around that make the most of the gorgeous desert landscape and vegetation (like the Hyatt in Palm Springs).  They really should take a look around at the competition across AZ, CA and NM.

Be warned too that this is firmly a 'family hotel', at least it was a Easter Spring Break.  Zillions of kids everywhere - especially in the 'Relaxation Pool' (what's that about?).  Between the ever present, over-loud poolside rock music from the speakers and the little angels you won't find much peace unless you sneak off to the golf club house and eat and drink there (the main restaurant was closed for a refurb when we were there).

The Spa was dated too.  Cheap tile on the floors and walls rather than natural materials.  And maybe i'm out of touch but $150 for a 50 min Swedish massage?  I can't vouch for how good it might have been as I swallowed my tongue when I saw the price list and had to be escorted to the relaxation area for a long lie down and a cold flannel.

Value-wise we paid little for our room (which was very good - large and with a generous terrace).  But they'll nail you on the food and drinks.  We're used to Four Seasons prices but given the kitschness of the hotel we were expecting to pay 80s food prices too.  Well, not really but we didn't expect a $19 burger at the pool.  My girl and I are small eaters but even the simplest lunch (appetizer, small salad, 2 glasses of wine) worked out somewhere noth of $60.

Finally, before choosing this hotel you have to ask yourself if you want to stay in a sort of ersatz palace styled on a 5,000 year old civilisation from the eastern Meditteranean but stuck in a suburb of Pheonix.  I wish I had.  We'd have stayed at the Marriott or Four Seasons instead.

Oh yeah - and as for paying $15 or $20 a day for wifi when the rest of the world gives it for free these days - get real!  The business centre was helpful though and I (and a few other starry-eyed men) filed our tax returns from there. 

I suppose apart from the horrendous extras bill and the lack of peacefulness it was quite an amusing choice for Easter!

reviews.author: golflady4
reviews.title: Phoenician-not what it is cracked up to be!
reviews.text: The hole experience was a nightmare.  The bathrooms had mold in the showers.  The rooms were right next to the dryers that kept us up all night.  The room keys never worked.   They claim they are kid-friendly but the park is completely on the other end of the hotel that takes 10 minutes to walk to.   The Fairmount in Scottsdale is a better location for young children.   The golf course was very expensive and not at all challenging.  The doorman gave us wrong directions for a trip to the Apache Trail that got us lost for an hour.  The concierges disagreed on each other's recommendations.  Great location--near shopping and hiking.  The food was OK--I've had better at the Four Seasons and Ritz Carlton.  I commented to the manager of the hotel and have not heard a thing.  I will never go back or recommend this hotel to anyone.  It is too much money for what it is.

reviews.author: William28London
reviews.title: Fabulous rooms with stunning views
reviews.text:
My partner and I stayed here for a couple of nights on our US trip back in August. The hotel looks at bit 1970s with the OTT chandalier in the lobby, and for two Brits in Phoenix in August, it was so hot we almost melted. 

However, the room was fantatsic. Among the best I have ever stayed in. A beautiful terrace with gorgeous views of the mountains. The food was very good, if a little expensive.  The pool was great and the lawns were immaculately maintained given the heat should have destroyed everything.

It was a great hotel on our way up to Vegas.

reviews.author: PrairieWoman
reviews.title: A very nice...but very tired...property
reviews.text:
This review is tough to write, as there were both highs and lows in my stay at the Phoenician.  On the positive side, the property is simply amazing.  My room had a large patio and had an amazing view of Camelback Mountain.  Having time in my room was actually a pleasure, as I could push back the patio doors and enjoy the outdoors.  The bathrooms were very spacious with great soap/shower products.  The beds and bedding were very comfortable.  

The rooms themselves were pretty spacious, but very worn and tired, with stains on the carpet and furniture.  The wallpaper was peeling in a couple of spots.  This is such a shame...it's easy to see how this was once a 5-star property, but it's just not quite "there" anymore.

I would have to add that the staff was a mixed bag.  Some of them (restaurant and housekeeping) were terrific.  I found that the front desk staff was a bit snobby and pretentious.  

While I didn't get to eat in the steakhouse, I did visit their onsite Italian restaurant twice.  Very good service and food on both occasions.  The breakfast buffet was good...but pricey.

reviews.author: WindyCity
reviews.title: Family Spring Break - Great Choice
reviews.text: My family just spent 9 great days at this property for spring break. We can into the trip a bit hesitant due to the fact that Scottsdale doesn't have a body of water for the kids to play at.  What we found was a very upscale resort with tremendous grounds. The property is quite beautiful and the very well maintained.  Our rooms were quite spacious, and had a nice rear exit into a really cool cactus garden that my kids spent hours in.  The hotel staff was extremely helpful.  We leveraged them for everything - bell desk, rides to and from Camelback Mtn, tennis, pool service, milk for the baby - everyone had a positive attitude and was very willing to help us at every turn.  We spent most of our time at the pools, which are very well kept, have plenty of seating, and has a great slide for the kids.  They even have a nice little pool for infants. The property has one primary restaurant - Il Terrazzo - we ate breakfast there a few times -- buffet is just ok and not the very plentiful or efficient. (We went t the breakfast club in old town a few times - great food) I would recommend you go off property for most of your meals as the food at the hotel is just mediocre.  We did eat at J&G Steakhouse - great views, but not the best service.  The manager was very engaged in our meal, yet the waiter was a bit stuck on himself and impatient.  Not the type of service you expect when spending $500 for a meal.  In old town our kids loved - Sugar Bowl for ice cream and Oregano's Pizza. We also really enjoyed Chelsea's Kitchen and Los Sombreros.  As a day trip we took our kids to the Zoo.  It's 10 minutes away and made for a nice trip. Being from Chicago we are a bit spoiled with our Zoo's, but we actually found the Phx Zoo to be a fun experience.  In closing on the hotel, it is in a great location right near old town and very nice shopping. Its a 15 min walk from great hiking, and it really is a beautiful setting.  With an improved restaurant, they would be a true 5 star property.

reviews.author: minaminou
reviews.title: "Beware of positive reviews"
reviews.text:
Was there last week and I hate to have to spend 5 minutes of my time writing a review for a hotel, however I believe others travelers deserve to know how bad this resort is.  The staffs are rude and dismissive,  additional charge for everything,  from bandages, internet, aspirins gym,  very noisy, due to 24 hrs pool/ hot tub,  restaurant food very average and overpriced,  cleanliness is below average for 5 stars rating.  
 I do wonder how can anyone possibly rate this hotel as 5 diamonds ?  Ratings of anything above 2 are probably written by the employees.

reviews.author: clm1855
reviews.title: Beautiful Setting, Great Rooms, just a few hiccups but I'd stay again in a hearbeat
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Phoenician and rented a casita.  The casitas are the townhouse style units. I called the hotel directly to inquire about the units. The reservations clerk was top notch and was able to ensure we received a one-story unit as I have problems with stairs.  The location was great and being a first floor unit my kids could run outside to an open grassy area to play and watch the fish at the KOI pond. One perk of the first floor rooms is room service will bring your in-suite meals to the patio if requested. The room itself was beautiful and HUGE. I only have two complaints about the room. 1. I was told the living room had a full size sofa bed but it was only twin size. We called housekeeping and they provided the nicest rollaway I'd ever seen without charge. However, we had to wait 45 minutes to get it.  The only other drawback was noise in the morning. The casitas were built with two housekeeping staff closets per building and the staff is up early and working and the doors slam LOUDLY. If you want the luxury of sleeping in late and you are a light sleeper you may want to stay in the main resort.
There are several pools and you can rent a cabana for $150/day. It includes a dedicated server, fruit plate, waters, red bulls, and other sodas, sunscreens, afternoon dessert tray.  We have a 2 year old who naps and he could sleep in the privacy of the casita.  The casita has a ceiling fan and masonry walls so it is considerably cooler than outside. Also, renting a casita means you don't have to get to the pool super early to get the primo deck chairs. Just tell them how many you need and they make sure they are all placed and reserved right in front of your casita.  
The resort is beautiful, much of having been renovated as of late. The staff was professional and kind.  The swimming pools and room service are open 24 hours.
Being at the base of Camelback Mountain allowed by husband and 8-year old daughter to go hiking. There is also bicycle rental. 
Mary Elaine's the french restaurant has been replaced with the J&G Steakhouse which was outstanding. The restaurant design is LA cool and has to have one of the best views in all of the Phoenix/Scottsdale area. The food was exceptional. We also really enjoyed our breakfast at Il Terrazzo. We had dinner here one night as well and while the food was good, the service was super slow which was odd since we dine early due to our young kids and we were one of only five customers in the entire restaurant at the time.  Slow dinner service at Il Terrazo and noisy mornings due to housekeeping are my only complaints. I would happily return here again. Our stay was more than pleasant and it's a great place for everybody. Parents with kids don't miss the 9:30am feeding at the KOI pond.  The kids are given huge cups of food to feed the fish and they loved it.

reviews.author: momtrip
reviews.title: Recent Negative Reviews Right on the Money
reviews.text:
I'm here right now. And if the suite I'm in is any indication of the rest of the hotel, this isn't even a a 4-star property--barely a 3. Carpet with stains, nails poking up at the doors. Broken slats on window coverings. Waterstains on the wallpaper. Yes, the decor is quite hard-worn and aged.

Cleanliness? That's a joke. Aside from crumbs on the floor and dustballs the size of rabbits, my daughter, who was barefoot, discovered a pile of broken glass in the corner of the room. Their "immediate" response took 20 minutes. Old lightbulbs had been left behind on the bathroom counters by the staff. I had to dispose of 8 old lightbulbs that, for some reason, were left behind as a welcome gift?

This is a SUITE, mind you, a 1,200 foot high-end space. With a view of: Construction scaffolding, construction debris, rooftops. Unbelievable.

The moment I walked in, my dismay was obvious to the bellhop, who seemed rather shocked too. I called the front desk to ask to be moved. Long story short: I called around 6 times until I was told I'd be moved--to the satellite building, far away from the main action. But not now. In the morning. Who knows what I'll find there. I would much rather move to another hotel entirely and will try to do that tomorrow morning. Sigh.

Room service food: Adequate. But for these prices, adequate is highway robbery. And let's not forget that I'm paying $12.95 for the wireless connection that is allowing me to type this response. I hate nickel-and-diming high-end resorts.

I KNEW I should've booked at the Four Seasons Troon North, which is a gem of a property. Oh well. You win some, you lose some.

reviews.author: bodyforlife
reviews.title: Nice resort but service is lacking
reviews.text: Just got back from a stay at the Phoenician.  Although the resort was beautiful, I was thoroughly disappointed in their service and won't return.  I don't take a lot of vacations but do like to stay at a top notch place when I do go.  For me, the service is by far the most important aspect on my trips and I found the staff at the Phoenician lacking in that respect.  We were given a mountain view room.  Typically, when I hear a hotel advertise mountain versus pool view rooms, it's not a big deal to me (in fact, I'd prefer the mountain except in I'm in a coastal hotel with a view of the ocean).  In this case though, what they mean by mountain is opening your shade and being right next to a mountain (so close you can tell the bugs on the bushes).  So essentially, you don't really have a view.  That wasn't the greatest, but the bigger problem was I had no phone reception on half of the room and the other half I was only able to get one bar (clearly a result of being right next to a mountain).  We went to the NCAA basketball game on our first day in town so we weren't in the room much.  The next morning, I went down to use the fitness facility and found it to be sub-par for a hotel of the level of the Phoenician (needed a serious refresh...they have a bunch of antiquated machines and spin bikes).  I asked the concierge is she knew of a track nearby (figured I'd just go for a jog instead since I didn't like the fitness center).  She had some maps laid out for jogs on the complex but I informed her that running on asphalt takes its toll on my knees and that I really needed a track.  I asked if there was a college nearby and she directed me to ASU, but gave me bad directions (had me turn right on Camelback and it should have been left).  I drove for about 35 minutes and never came across the first street that I was supposed to turn on (Scottsdale Blvd).  So that waste over an hour of my time for nothing.  As I kept having calls drop off on my phone, I became more annoyed with the situation and by Saturday morning complained to the front desk.  The snooty clerk replied.."well sir, we can't do anything about the way the hotel is constructed".   I thought to myself, so what are you saying?...your customers have to suck it up and deal with it?  I would think a more professional clerk would have apologized for the inconvenience and immediately look to switch my room (instead of me telling the clerk that this wouldn't do).  So I had the room switched but it wasn't available yet (it was 7am).  He said I would receive a call informing me when the room was ready.  By 12:30, we hadn't received a call and had to leave for the game so I called the front desk.  The clerk said to leave our package luggage on the bed and it would be moved for us to the new room by the time we got back.  We arrived back at the hotel at 5.  The new room was ready but the luggage hadn't been moved (they said they would take care of it right away).  So we went to the bar for a little over an hour.  We got back to the room...still no luggage.  I called back to the desk and the clerk apologized and said it would be done right way).  After another hour and still no luggage, I went to the desk and complained (we had 8 o'clock dinner reservations at a restaurant away from the hotel).  We finally received our luggage just before 7:30 and needless to say didn't really have time to freshen up a bit before dinner (actually just got to the restaurant at 8).  Although the front desk manager apologized the next day, it really didn't matter to me at that point.  She asked what she could do to make me happy and offer a massage or a free meal.  I just asked if it was possible to get an "uneventful" day from her staff (which was really all I wanted all along).  She had a look on her face like she didn't even know how to respond to that request (as though that was might be asking the impossible).   I mentioned that I really didn't think I was asking too much to have our luggage delivered and perhaps her staff could have at least made sure we had some ice (they don't have ice machines so we had to call room service for ice).  She was surprised by the ice comment and questioned whether we had had turn down service (apparently the maids are supposed to deliver ice every night).  I informed her we never received ice in the 3 nights we had been there and I had to call for it (and of course, tip their room service which I thought was bogus).  She did end up comping our lunch but honestly it just didn't matter.  I can't stand it when a 5 star hotel provides shoddy service like this.  There are plenty of deals out there especially with the economy being in the shape it's in (even for 5 star hotels).  My wife actually chose the hotel (I was pushing for the Four Seasons).   The last day at the hotel was our 25th wedding anniversary, but I was just too annoyed to really enjoy it.  Too bad the staff doesn't realize they ruin people's stays when they can't deliver a quality experience.

reviews.author: Kimandkids
reviews.title: No more 'fun' at the 'fun'icians kids club !
reviews.text:
Our final trip to this former 5 star resort (now 4 stars)....
we've been coming here  for awhile...but, 
alas, we'll have to go elsewhere...
Kids'  were bored with new regime at club not to mention TOO much
walking now...
too un-interesting crafts...and
no more lunches my kids love.
So, we had to cancel the club and have them hang at the pool w/us...just
so they could walk less, swim more....and eat what they love !
Plus dog poop on the lawn ....tsk tsk....
we're outta here !

reviews.author: Lenore P
reviews.title: No complaints
reviews.text: Fifth time back to the Phoenician.  Clean and luxurious. Had  our teenage children with us and they loved the pool and the overall serenity of the hotel.  Travel nearby to hike and take advantage of Scottsdale's restaurants.  Great vacation and high recommended.

reviews.author: mlizBoston
reviews.title: Spacious room, great amenities
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here for a long weekend in January at the end of a conference he attended at the resort.  We booked massages at the spa, dined at Windows on the Green, sat by the pool.  Our favorite activity was sitting outdoors with drinks by the fire pit at the Thirsty Camel Lounge.  Very special accommodations in the one bedroom (King) casita that we stayed in.  This is a fantastic getaway spot and you can't beat the sunshine.

reviews.author: nyflanctraveler
reviews.title: Beautiful hotel, incredible grounds, real luxury
reviews.text:
This hotel was extremely nice and real luxurious right from the time you drive through the entrance.  The grounds are immaculate and the rooms are very nice.  We had a room with a waterfall in our backyard that was super relaxing at night.  The rooms itself are top notch.  Very comfortable bed, big flat screen tv, great shower and really nice bathroom. They have about 8 pools and they are all nice and a bit different.  The service is good but the staff is very unsociable. They almost act like robots and just do their jobs but have very little interaction with the guests.  The food was great and the drinks were real expensive.  Overall very nice stay and would definitely like to go back again.

Me and my fiancee actually liked going in the summer when it was super hot because you can sit in the pools all day long and drink and never have to get out. They also have plenty of areas to sit in the shade all throughout the resort.

reviews.author: innkeepa
reviews.title: Great Christmas at the Phoenician
reviews.text: A top notch experience at this wonderful resort. Staff could not be more helpful. As Innkeepers ourselves, we notice the little things, well done Phoenician!

reviews.author: travelsalot_7
reviews.title: Proceed with Caution!
reviews.text: We stayed at The Phoenician in Scottsdale, Az. from 1/15/09 thru 1/18/09.  The hotel and grounds were beautiful, but we encountered a number of problems with the service and staff.  The big problem was, I had a diabetic medical emergency and went to the mini bar to quickly grab some juice only to find I either a) didn't have a key or b) couldn't find one after searching for it.  I dialed "0" and was put on hold for a while and then was connected to the front desk.  I clearly stated "I am having a diabetic medical emergency and don't have a key to the mini bar.  I need sugar."  The reply was:  "We'll send somebody right away".  I waited for about 10  minutes, the need growing more urgent and finally I called our friend who was staying a floor below us and told her that I needed help.  She came right up with juice and M & M's.  (My blood sugar reading was 61 when this all started).  My friend called the desk and got the same person I had called to ask why nobody had responded to my urgent medical call.  He said he had "called the bell captain and informed him" because he himself could not leave the desk or he would have been fired.  She demanded to speak to the manager and was told that he was not there but would be told to call her.  Instead, he called our line while we were out and apologized that we "had not received a key to the mini bar and it would not happen again".  No mention of the fact that they had ignored a medical emergency  call.  In addition, we found the service on the outdoor dining to be terrible - it took almost 3 hours to get a dinner completely served and the staff to be dismissive in most venues.

reviews.author: SeychellesDream
reviews.title: Lovely Hotel
reviews.text:
Lovely hotel with very courteous and helpful staff. I stayed at a spacious casita and although I had to walk to the main hotel, it was a lovely walk though the grounds. At departure I called for a staff member to pick me up for check-out and he was there immediately with the golf cart.  

We also rented a car which was promptly delivered to us. When the young man inspected it and noticed the trunk was full of dry grass he took it away immediately and cleaned it up for us.

reviews.author: WendyEliz
reviews.title: Spend your money elsewhere
reviews.text:
We booked a package deal through Liberty Travel for a Christmas stay.
I arrived a few hours before my parents and was greeted by Aaron at the front desk and by Robert, who helped me with my bags. Robert was wonderful, it was obvious Aaron wanted to be elsewhere.
My mother purchased a package deal and requested mountain views. Aaron confirmed that we faced the mountain. Our rooms faced the parking lot. Since they were at 17% capacity I asked to change rooms. Robert was gracious and immediately went to the hotel manager to see what he could do. Aaron, need i say it? not friendly. 
I changed rooms to a garden level, no real view, but better than a parking lot.
In general, the rooms were nice, a bit dated, but nice. the grounds were beautiful and the pools (although under repair) were lovely. too cold to swin anyway I suppose. The waitstaff were wonderful, the food delicious.
Our only problems were centered around Aaron, who was asked to make dinner reservations at the Windows on the Green, he never did since when we arrived, the placed was closed.
He was also very rude to my parents at check out when they were working out the bill. Again, it was a package deal. Breakfast was included. Aaron was infomred at check in and he confirmed that it would be taken care of. 
He must have forgotten, because at check out all breakfasts were charged and Aaron stated that they do not honeor third party coupons. are you kidding? My mother called Liberty Travel, who immediately recified the situation, love them. 
Rather than admitting his mistake, Aaron told my mother that she should have brought this to his attendtion at check in. She reminded him that she had.
All in all, the place was nice, but the front desk was terrible and caused all sorts of problems, plus they nickel and dime you for everything. For their room rates, it's insulting. Gym access $25/pp, internet $12/day
Go to the Ritz, or the Four Seasons, there is a reason they are well known and established.

reviews.author: kemac2016
reviews.title: All out luxury and pampering at The Phoenician
reviews.text:
Our family of four just returned from a 3 night getaway at The Phoenician Hotel in Scottsdale. The first impression of the hotel is stunning with beautiful architecture and  landscaping. The rooms at the Phoenician are the most comfortable I have stayed in. Every need has been premeditated to make sure you are as comfortable as can be and the beds and linnens were the best.
The hotel has 9 pools and beautiful pool side Cabana's which we took advantage of. There was no need to eat off premises either. We breakfasted on our own patio with fresh made pastries and coffee from the Ice cream cafe and dined at both the Italian restuarant and the Windows on the green which were both superb. We really enjoyed the terrace for our after dinner drinks where seating is arranged around giant outisde fireplace pits for total luxury. Our 6 year old even got to roast marshmallows! I would recommend the Phoenician for famalies looking for a great family getaway and total relaxation.

reviews.author: Jane D
reviews.title: Beautiful Views In a Peaceful Setting
reviews.text: My girlfriends and I chose the Phoenician for our annual weekend getaway based on location and spa services.  We were not disappointed!  We arrived and were warmly greeted and shown to our room on the ground floor (leads straight out to the numerous pools and luscious grounds).  We booked two rooms and had asked for them to be adjoining -- no problem, our request was honored. We happen to stay during a non-busy weekend (September 19-22), and it was wonderful -- no crowds at the pools, got our spa treatments when we wanted, and enjoyed poolside and golfside dining in a peaceful surrounding. The grounds were well tended, the staff were friendly and accommodating, and the amenities in the bathrooms were well stocked/replenished. The concierge was very helpful when we asked about a walking/hiking route -- we were directed towards Camelback Mountain and sent off with complimentary bottles of water. What a view! The plus side: Very friendly staff, clean rooms and well appointed/stocked with fresh towels and bath needs, well manicured grounds, top-notch spa. The minus side: hotel uses a private car to take you where you want to go, but does not offer taxis to come onto the property unless you request one. If you do use the private car, be aware the price range can be anywhere from $10-14, at the discretion of the driver (even if the destination is less than 3 miles away). Also, the hotel restaurant, Il Terrazo, we felt was way overpriced for the (non) quality of service (limited staff) and food (had better fine dining away from the resort).

reviews.author: alexzandra h
reviews.title: Resort is Fab, but staff need some customer service training
reviews.text:
I stayed here for a week on business. The grounds and hotel are phenomenal, the pools are spectacular. I had no problems with cleanliness or the aesthetics of the facilities. 

There was an issue with the internet, their high speed cut in and out and prevented any filed from downloading properly. However, I understand the resort is not meant for business, so I'm not holding the intermittent internet against them. 

I was very surprised with the general attitude from the employees. They were very snobby and acted like I was bothering them if I asked any question, ie how do I get to this part of the hotel, etc. The bar tender in the lobby bar acted like i was incompetent when I asked where i could get a lite salad, other then a Ceaser. ( the bar menu is very limited, hence why I asked) I thought this was an isolated instance, but the lack of customer service continued. The waiter at the restaurant was rude, the room service operator acted like he was doing me a favor by taking my order, and the room service deliveryman acted appalled when I asked to charge the bill to card rather then my room, even though i mentioned this when I was giving my order, and apologized for any inconvenience.  

Maybe, my experience was isolated, but regardless I doubt I will be staying here again. I

reviews.author: lambertbunch
reviews.title: Fabulous Phoenician!
reviews.text: Top-notch resort at the foot of Camelback Mountain. No complaints! Clean resort. The pool area is inviting and relaxing. Friendly and attentive staff. Plenty to do: golf, tennis, hiking, on-site cactus garden and art displays.

reviews.author: kenpo1980
reviews.title: One of the Best
reviews.text: Me and a buddy of mine did a "guys weekend" at this hotel last December and I have to say it was easily one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in. I have stayed in many five star hotels but what set this hotel apart was the unbelievable service and courtesy of  the staff. It felt as though almost no request was unreasonable and they did their best to make sure a couple of rough guy like us in their mid-thirties were happy. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

reviews.author: TRET
reviews.title: Business
reviews.text:
Excellent Ressort in comparism to other US ones. Great check inn, great staff. Very helpful and very accurate. 

It is expensive (incl. costs at restaurants and bars/pools) - but you are in one of the leading ressorts in Scottsdale and food and drinks a worth the money. Seen much more terrible ones in California - absolutely value for your money .

Room services was great and in time (you will not find it in most of the five stars ressorts in the US).

Only one remark: Business Center - keep on further trying: When you want to send something to overseas - they are not capable to do.

All in all a great place to spend vacation instead of business - would definteley return again.

Did not play golf and may not judge it. Did some running to the near Camel Back Mountain - great.

reviews.author: dynamo
reviews.title: Luxury at its finest
reviews.text:
Awesome experience - the room was huge and so were the bathrooms. The pools were awesome, though the fitness center required a fee even if you are a hotel guest.

Everything was first class!

reviews.author: snoopy933
reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised
reviews.text:
Stayed 3 nights here.  Had heard that it was slightly "stuffy" but we didn't find this at all.  

The room was lovely - tranquil colours - and the marble bathroom was beautiful.  One of my bugbears is always the lack of clothes hangers in hotels - not in this case!  

The mother-of-pearl pool was a peaceful place to relax and the water was warm.  

Staff were attentive and friendly, particularly in the bakery, where they insisted that we take a free cookie or brownie for our journey home.  

Lots of activities, great location and best of all, following disappointing experiences at a couple of other Scottsdale hotels, where we were unceremoniously displaced without notice from hotel bars and pool areas to make way for conference functions, the conferences & functions at The Phoenician seem to be contained in their own areas of the hotel.  There were several taking place while we were there and not once did we feel like we were at a hotel which gave preference to conference guests.  (The conference areas looked very nice, so don't be put off if you are going there for a conference!).

The bad points: it isn't made particularly clear when you arrive that you will be charged $26 per night for valet parking  - this is just printed faintly on the valet receipt.  We retrieved our car after we checked in and parked it in the closest self parking area - there is a lift up to the lobby from there.

Disappointed that there is a $20 charge if you want to use the gym before 3pm and $10 for after 3pm.  

Inconvenient that the only printer in the cyberspace area was out of order when we wanted to check in for our flight online.  Also, there is an hourly charge for using the internet in the cyberspace room.  

The restaurants were empty while we were there, which was a shame, but the bar area was nice and the food from the bar was delicious, particularly the cioccolato dessert!

It takes a little while to find your way around the resort, even with the map you are given, but once you have the hang of it, its a beautiful place.

We would definitely go back, as we left feeling refreshed and relaxed, and feel that this resort compared favourably in terms of character and customer service with eg. the Fairmont & the Hyatt Regency, where we have stayed previously.

reviews.author: IAS-KC
reviews.title: Amazing resort and spa!
reviews.text:
This was for a business retreat for my husband, so everything was taken care of for us. We were upgraded to a casita, which was lovely and very large, but unfortunately it had a view of the parking structure and we could hear cars and see headlights if we kept the door or curtains open.  It was also a handicapped room and the shower was in the same room as the toilet.  Whenever we took a shower, it flooded the entire floor. This initially upset me, I even called to change rooms, but they were full.  It's hard to complain when someone is picking up the tab and it was very clear that other rooms had amazing views and non-handicapped bathrooms so we let it go.

My upsets were quickly offset by the amazing resort and spa. I thoroughly took advantage of the fitness programs, walks, yoga, stretching - even belly dancing! The spa treatments were amazing and the daily meditation was wonderful! 

The many pools were great to relax in.  Our favorite were the ones at the Canyon Suites.

Also, be sure not to miss the cactus garden. We toured it twice!

The food and service at the resort were first class. They truly earn their luxury status.

reviews.author: sonnie512
reviews.title: Heaven on Earth @ The Phoenician
reviews.text:
This was our 4th visit to the Phoenix/Scottsdale area and our 3rd stay at the Phoenician.  As always, our expectations were met and we were not disappointed with our investment.  Everything and everyone from the moment we drove up to the property to our last goodbye to the staff at the Ice Cream Parlor/Cafe was beautiful.  The rooms are fantastic, clean, comfortable and abundant with luxury.  This year we were upgraded to a Casita - which was so much fun and a thrill for us...we would have been satisfied with a regular room but how nice to be welcomed for our anniversary and our third stay with such a nice upgrade.  A bottle of champagne and chocolate covered strawberries awaited us with a nice handwritten note by the Manager welcoming us back and wishing us well on our anniversary. 

We travel the same week each year - Labor Day weekend to the Saturday that follows.  It isn't in season for Arizona, so we already get a break on the cost - I suppose people think we're crazy for sitting in the sun at 112 degrees BUT it's a dry heat.  The staff at the Phoenician always treat us like we're special no matter what time of year it is.  We started this year in Tucson and spent Labor Day weekend counting down the days until we returned to Scottsdale.

The restaurants on property are all fabulous.  Diverse menus and terrific staff - everyone wants to be sure you're comfortable and it doesn't seem fake.  It's as if we were family.  What my husband and I have grown to realise is that the Phoenician hires happy people who generally seem really happy to be working on the property.  What we really like is that we see the same faces year after year.  Even the housekeeping staff greet you with smiles and do such a nice job of keeping your room neat.  I love what they do with all of our mess of travel brochures, magazines and all of our toilettries!  We always feel safe and secure.

On our 2nd visit, we stayed at the Fairmount Princess and we were so disappointed.  We kept going back to the Phoenician to hang out!

reviews.author: terrylowen
reviews.title: Wedding Rings and Chanel Rng Stolen on First Day.
reviews.text:
I had the worst experience possible at the Phoenician in Scottsdale, Arizona.

First of all, the room seemed dirty and not what you would expect at ALL from a FIVE-STAR DIAMOND RESORT hotel... I would have rather stayed in my home city at the Drake in Chicago, but I wanted some sun.

Missing Wedding Ring and Chanel Ring:
The second morning of our stay, when we woke-up, the maid was standing outside the door waiting to come in and entered the room while we were in it. Note: she did not swipe her card. I accidently left my wedding rings on the night table. Well, I walked five to ten feet down the hallway and realized--in fright--that the rings were not on my fingers! We turned around and ran back to the room to the night table. In horror, we realized the rings were GONE. For some reason, the maid, even though she did not know what we lost, started looking for the rings!!!!

During the entire vacation we are talking to our insurance company and the police. We were talking to the management at the hotel, etc. Plus, I am on an emotional rollercoaster the entire vacation. 

Well, to make a long story short, we finally get a call from the hotel while we are boarding our plane and they say "WE RETRIEVED THE RINGS FROM THE ROOM." This is six days later, after my husband and I moved furniture, looked between matresses and in closets, took off sheets and went through every piece of that room starting from one corner to the next every single day. Even the deck that we did not sit on. I will mention that the same maid was waiting for us to leave on the last day.

Final Note: After six days of a completely ruined vacation with police, the insurance company and hotel executive staff, the hotel offered NO COMPENSATION ON ANYTHING!!!!

We have asked for compensation from this hotel, and I was nice enough to not make a scene when we were leaving. However, we have not heard anything back from them. 

Can you imagine if something happened to you while you were staying there and you did not receive any compensation? Pretty pathetic.

A Very Unhappy Guest
Chicago, IL

reviews.author: Msk6261
reviews.title: Luxury Collection it is
reviews.text:
Beautiful, well maintained property and professional, attentive staff. I really don't know what more you could want.

We came with a large group that pretty much took the whole place over. The service in this circumstance was outstanding. From our   perspective, everything went very smoothly.  Even the banquet food (which I don't have high expectations for) was surprisingly excellent.

Loved the water slide!

We had  a wonderful, relaxing long weekend.

reviews.author: cheatedbyoutrigger
reviews.title: Fantastic Staff and restaraunts!
reviews.text:
The most pleasurable getaway we have had.  The Canyon Suires accomadations are marvelous.  The suite was bigger than my wifes home!  The staff is always attentive to your needs, and go out of their way to show it.  They remember your name and appear to be interested in you as a patron.  The management is to be commended for their training and oversight.   

By the way, unlike many other hotels we have stayed at, Valet Parking was at NO additional  charge.

reviews.author: johnicho19
reviews.title: Nice Resort, but.....
reviews.text:
This was our third trip to Scottsdale and decided to try a new resort so we decided to book 4 nights at the Phoenician.  Upon arrival our check in was quick and the staff was attentive. The resort grounds are beautiful, and the location at the base of Camelback mountain is breathtaking.  Our room was in good condition and spacious.  

Now you are probably wondering why is this only rated at 2 stars.  Well to make a long story short, I took a star off for every cockroach me or my wife had to kill in our nicely appointed room.  Yes that is right, 3 cockroaches in 4 nights at a supposed 5 star resort????  Unbelievable.  I  have stayed at other resorts and had no such issues.  I've even stayed at many economy chain hotels without this lack of pest control.  Thankfully they left an umbrella in the room which we used to kill them.  I'm hoping that this wasn't the intended purpose of leaving an umbrella in the suite.   I voiced my concern at check out and all I got was a "well I'll write that down, but besides that did you have a good stay"??.  So in case they didn't write it down and didn't take any further pest control action, and you are about to check in, just say no to Suite 7121.

reviews.author: adamunc
reviews.title: Everything It Should Be...
reviews.text:
…at summer rates, anyway. Stayed here three nights over Labor Day Weekend on a AAA deal at $167 per night, with a Camelback view. Everything at the resort is on a grand scale, yet not overwhelming, with the exception of it being a bit of a maze to get to some rooms. The lobby has a real wow factor, from the large fountain to the high-ceilinged sitting area with a terrace opening off it… spectacular. I’m something of a hotel bar junkie, so that lobby lounge terrace overlooking the entire Valley of the Sun really impressed me. 

Rooms are large and supremely comfortable and soothing. Lots of tans and sage greens, with some additional color provided by striking desert botanical prints on the walls. There’s plenty of storage/closet/shelf space and a very large-screen TV. Balconies are also very sizeable with a full-length chaise, plus table and chairs. The only complaint I could think of in the rooms is that the nice oval soaking tubs are quite shallow. I would think you would want to carefully consider view at this resort, as there wasn’t a great deal of difference in price for room categories, but there was a great deal of difference in view quality. I had the Camelback/cactus garden view on the rear of the hotel, which was quite nice and panoramic. There’s also the view of the Valley, same as the lobby terrace—these rooms also overlook the pool complex. But there would be some rooms with views of the entranceway or a rooftop, so if view is important to you, specify what you want. 

The pool area is spectacular, with waterfalls and lots of angles and cubbyholes, as well as large open swimming areas. Set off to one side was a small courtyard fountain pool with beautiful tiling. It was usually not at all crowded, so if all you wanted to do was lounge in the water, you might try there if there was too much activity at the main pool. I have to give a special nod to the service at the Oasis pool bar—some really good sandwiches and wonderful servers. If the drinks “come out a little big,” then you get the extra. The Centre for Well-Being spa, despite the pretentious name, offers great massages and an impressive relaxation area with sleep-inducing zero-gravity chairs. 

I’m not much on golf or tennis, but I did hear lots of guests praising those facilities. I do enjoy hiking, and it’s about a fifteen minute walk on surface streets to get to the trailhead for Camelback Mountain. This hike is moderately difficult, but definitely worth the effort for the views. You get spectacular panoramas of the valley, including the resort. The best views are the first forty-five minutes or so of the trail, so you can make a round trip from your room in about two hours.

The only thing The Phoenician is lacking at the moment is a true signature restaurant. There’s a Jean-Georges Vongerichten steakhouse scheduled to open this fall in place of Mary Elaine’s, so that will probably correct the deficiency. The two primary restaurants now are Windows on the Green, at the golf clubhouse; and Il Terrazzo, in the main building. Both are solid, if not spectacular, and offer a wide variety of dishes. I can recommend the gnocchi with wild boar ragout at Il Terrazzo and the quail at Windows. There are a few more casual, cheaper places sprinkled around. Room service serves the Il Terrazzo menu and was very speedy both times I used it. 

There wasn’t a single service mis-step in my three days. Everyone was unfailing pleasant, efficient, and knowledgeable. Housekeeping came and went without ever interrupting, so there seems to be a real effort to be inconspicuous about servicing the rooms. 
 
Some other quick notes:
•	The ExecuCar service is handy and costs no more than a cab, so should you need to leave the property it’s there.
•	Ice is delivered by room service, but there are also ice machines in the housekeeping closets, which aren’t locked. 
•	Lon’s at the Hermosa is worth the trip for dinner outside the resort

I’m already planning my trip for next 4th of July so I can see the fireworks around the Valley from the lounge terrace.

reviews.author: travelguyto
reviews.title: A First Class Resort
reviews.text:
My family and I spent 10 days at this resort in mid August.
We were not sure after reading several not so flattering reviews 
however the resort,staff and facilities were first class.After a not so smooth check in the rest of the stay was perfect.Front desk staff acted as they started that day and it took 3 different people to
arrange our room which was lovely.Do not valet park for $26 a day as the self park is fine.Will definitely return.

reviews.author: ricardoi
reviews.title: Great hotel!!!
reviews.text: This is an impressive hotel. The suites are just marvellous and the staff is first rate. One of the best hotels I have stayed.

reviews.author: wordub
reviews.title: Wonderful resort, food prices hurt
reviews.text:
I made my reservations very early the day of my stay through Starwood Perfered Guest program. I took the best rate available with the AAA rate. Under $200.00 per night. I checked in early (about 12:45pm) and I was greeted warmly by a front desk staff memeber with no waiting. Check-in took about 2 mins. and I was off to my room on the sixth level. My room was spacious, well appointed, clean, comfortable and was stocked with Gilchrist and Sommes 4oz size ammenities.  The balcony had a cushioned lounge chair, tables and chairs. The view was nice. I actually sat out in the sun for about 45mins on my deck and worked on my tan. Quite comfortable if you like hot 102F
sun, which I am used to. Not all patios/balconies face the sun. 
The pool was pretty cool. Not too many people and plenty of lounge chairs. The lobby is spectacular. The lounges and restaurants are all open to the view of the valley below. 
There was an LG 32"" Flat screen TV that seems a bit grainy if the signal isn't HD, but it added a nice touch. There was a CD player alarm clock with a Classical Collection CD there for relaxing music. Anyway, I was starving, so I called down for some room service. I thought I'd go with the Phoenician Burger, Tuscan Bean Soup and a Bloody Mary(19.50 , 9.50 and 9,00 resectivley) A bit pricey, but what the heck...It is a luxury hotel. They said it would take about 30 mins. After 45mins I called down and they said there had been a mix-up in the kitchen and the food was on it's way. I looked
at the menu and I saw that they add 22% plus $4.00 plus tax to the bill. Anyway, after all of the redicuious surcharges and tip that meal cost me  over $65.00! The food and cocktail were Ok, not nearly worth what I paid for them though. With the wait and the price, I figured they shave some off my bill. Don't get me wrong, I'm not cheap skate, but fair price is one thing...highway robbery is another.
  The foor was quiet. Very little hallway noise. The oversized oval tub was nice to relax in after a serious pinch to my wallet. The bed was confortable and I slept pretty well. In the morning I had a WSJ and a USA Today at my door. I called at 6:00a and ordered a two cup pot of coffee. After all of the surcharges and tip I was out another $19.00 for coffee!  It was possible they thought I said 4 cup pot . The coffee was ok. For me, it is a necessity to have coffee in the morning. In-room coffee makers would be much better than paying enormous surcharge for a morning cup of Joe.
Beware of valet parking...it costs $26.00 per night plus tip. Self park is complimentary. When checking-out I mentioned the outrageous in-room service prices and the staff member said he was sorry, but that is the resort set price. I was not happy. I did fill-out the guest survey with my likes and dislikes. 
 Overall, the hotel is very high-end. It is part of the Starwood Hotel's Luxury Collection. In order of luxury and price it goes: Four Points, Sheraton, Westin, The Luxury Collecton.  The room price was a bargin, but the huge surcharges on in-dinning made me feel I was taken.
I usually stay in Starwood Hotel Properties and this one may want to re-think the extra charges. This fact makes me give the resort a lower rated review. Not one of my best stays. It is possible that Starwood properties have lost their way a bit.

reviews.author: getcrunk
reviews.title: Everything you would want from an upscale resort.
reviews.text:
I had read so much on here about the hotel (good and bad), it was hard to know what I expected. But let me tell you, this resort lived up to its pristine reputation. From the moment you drive onto the property and see the palatial golf courses and hotel grounds, you are in heaven.

We self-parked, which took some luster out of our luxury experience, but at nearly $30 a day to valet the car, we figured self-parking wasn't so bad.

Check-in was a breeze, and we were given the caliber of room we requested. We were booked in a Deluxe Double room with a city view--and that's exactly what we got. And it was definitely up to par. The room was large, with plenty of closet space, drawers, a large armoir, AND a shiny new flat-screen HDTV. The bedding was luxurious, and the pillows not too overwhelming. There was also a desk and chair, as well as a chaise lounge. A lot of other hotels have all these things in the rooms, but it wasn't as cramped as other hotels. There was no crunch of space, and even quite a lot of walking space between the bed and the TV. But the best part was that the bathroom was practically half the size of the hotel room itself! Large sunken tub, separate glass shower, toilet room, and two sinks. The bathroom was the best part.

The staff everywhere we turned was helpful, attentive, and friendly. The check-in desk clerk was great, and he directed us to the room with no confusion. The concierge was on point. I asked for her recommendation for a good Asian restaurant, and within minutes she had booked us a reservation at a local favorite that happened to be extremely busy. And after we came back from dinner, the housekeeping had done the turn-down service, which was to be expected. As it was hot, it was nice to have a bucket full of ice waiting, towels and etc replaced, and the beds readied for us. A very personal touch was that my sister brings this little pillow with her everywhere since she was a baby. And when we had returned to the room, the beds were turned-down, and they had also arranged my sister's raggedy little pillow right in the middle of all the bed pillows. It was a personal touch that was appreciated. Other than that, the pool service was good, could have been speedier, but was good nonetheless.

Since the hotel was really near Old Town Scottsdale and the Fashion Square, there was no need to eat at the over-priced on-site restaurants. There was plenty to choose from, I mean like dozens of restaurants within about a couple miles. Anything from mall fast-food to PF Chang's to more upscale fine-dining. They even had a Sprinkles cupcakes near the mall, which was a treat for us Southern Californians! The location of the resort was very good.

The only downside was that we needed to run to a drug store or grocery store to grab some personal toiletries one night, and there was not one in sight for a good couple of miles from the hotel. You would think with the mall and Old-Town nearby there would be easy to find stores, but we drove for a good while trying to find one. We ended up finding one in a less-desirable part of town. But this was not a deal breaker.

The resort is top-notch, and we will be back again!

reviews.author: dragoncoach
reviews.title: Fabulous if you know what is offered
reviews.text:
We had a wonderful trip. People warned us that August was miserable in AZ but we figured in exchange for this kind of deal on a 5 star hotel we would handle the heat. 

Facility- 
This beauty is set back from Camelback Rd up against the hill. You don't get quite the spectacular entrance when you enter via the self parking area but it is still beautiful. 
Our room was a good 5 minute walk from the car. We were on the far end of the 6th floor in room 6188. We had a great view from there and it was incredibly quiet so it was worth the walk. We had a lovely balcony with chairs, a table and a lounge chair. We could not see the pools from our room but we couldn't hear them either. Our last night we stayed out late on the balcony (even in the heat) and watched a lightening storm on the horizon while we sipped champagne. 
The pools were beautiful. I can't think of anything more I could have wanted except perhaps a pool that was for adults only. That would have been nice. My husband and I even went down the big water slide!
There was some broken concrete here and there and some water damage on a wall or two. On a property this large there are bound to be little things here and there. 
The bathroom was bigger than my kitchen at home. A big sunken tub, big shower with a glass door and a separate toilet. 

Services - 
The staff was helpful. Unfortunately we did go on a drive they suggested only to find (after nearly an hour of driving) that the last 22 miles to the dam and lake was dirt. Most insurance companies don't cover rentals off the pavement so we couldn't take the drive. The hotel should have known that when they sent us.
They were helpful in setting up tables at restaurants and answering questions. 
What bothered me about the hotel was that I never knew what was offered until I went looking. While walking by the pool I saw people doing aqua aerobics. When I asked the staff was able to produce a whole schedule of free "wellness" activities. There were meditations, walks, aqua aerobics and many others. I found out the day before we left. I wished I had known before.
The same thing happened with the turn down service. We didn't know they were delivering ice until the last night.
