During the entire duration of my meal the potatoes were never replenished. The bacon was sitting in the warmer on a piece of toast and seems to get staler as time passed. If you want to eat “fresh” scrambled eggs, get them through the omelet station. A bottle of wine (small one, mind you) at the mini-bar costs $49. There were other dining establishments on site but I didn’t check them out. The restaurants generally closed after lunch to set up for dinner, so if you need an in between meal, your dining options are very limited. If you want to order something through in-room dining, there is an automatic 22% service charge, plus taxes, and a $4 delivery fee slapped on the entire order which is obscenely expensive but should be expected at a place like this. 

I didn’t utilize much of the resorts facilities; however, there are “nine” pools at this resort and there is a water slide. I personally wouldn’t pay money to use the cabanas I saw; however, it does offer a shred of privacy. I didn’t see a lot of pool attendants out at 9AM as I would have expected to cater to the needs of the guests. But then again, there were an abundance of chairs, etc; thereby illustrating the resort was not running at capacity; hence, less pool staff were needed. Spa/Fitness facilities—didn’t see them, so I can’t comment. 

As this is a AAA Five-Diamond rate property, you should, keyword: expect superlative service which is sometimes not on par with other five-diamond properties. It took two hours to deliver a welcome note after speaking to someone from the front-desk. There are only two concierge desks with two people supposedly serving at capacity 600+ rooms. Concierge was unable to get information about cost of a taxi to the airport as opposed to taking the sedans at the hotel ($37 to the airport). While the resorted noted we were celebrating an anniversary, nothing came to us, no amenity. If you are there for a special occasion and nothing comes, call and ASK for it because you deserve it. We called and ½ a bottle of champagne and cookies were sent to our room. Having things sent to your room takes a LONG time. Housekeeping kept knocking at our door despite a DNB sign. As we were departing our room, housekeeping came in and asked us how long we were going to be until we left, we said ten minutes, and ten minutes later as we left the room, the housekeeper was waiting outside and jumped right in to clean our room—it was a really rushed feeling. Check-out was very smooth and efficient. 

All in all, if you could secure a very good deal during low season, the location is excellent because you are in closer proximity of select attractions. This resort is big so I am sure one could keep themselves occupied if they choose not to leave the resort. The resort is definitely due for a renovation if they want to charge anything in excess of $400+. I didn’t mind paying $230ish but if I paid anything close to $700+ for the room I was staying in, I would be absolutely livid. If the property did an absolute makeover of guest rooms, tasteful at that, then it may warrant paying such rates—which I don’t mind paying if it is consistent with its offerings.

reviews.author: wantingonlythebest
reviews.title: The Best Stay to date!
reviews.text: This was without doubt the best stay at any hotel I have ever stayed in.  The service was unbelieveable - they could not do enough to help.  A real personal and friendly service.  They gave us a free upgrade, produced anything we required within minutes. I unfortunately had to visit a doctor whilst there, and they without hesitation organised an appointment and gave us a courtesy limo too!  The resort is beautiful, stunning and spotless.  We really could not fault it, and are actually thinking of getting married there!

reviews.author: PhoenicianGirl
reviews.title: Best Resort Ever!
reviews.text:
This was my fourth stay at The Phoenician, and it has never disappointed!  I live in Phoenix, so can book a stay pretty much any time I want.

I come to The Phoenician in the summertime, when rates are low.  Well, everything's pricey, but let me tell you, worth every penny!  I truly believe The Phoenician is the best resort in the State of Arizona, if not the entire Southwest.

I have never had a negative experience here.  The hotel staff are the most attentive and nice I've ever come across.  I was a solo guest, and was always made to feel welcome and comfortable.

I was a "Spa Girl" most days... The Centre for Well-Being is a fantastic spa!  I had services everyday... a facial, the 80-Minute Swedish Massage, a pedicure, and the Barefoot In the Lemongrass treatment.  The price for the 80-minute massage gave me pause, but hell, you can't take it with you, and there's more to life than working and paying bills!  Treat yourself as I did!  Every treatment was amazing!  The massage was unforgettable!

The Terrace Dining Room has always been wonderful to me.  Most nights, I ate in the bar.  The staff was so kind and attentive, without being intrusive.

I simply don't think you can do any better than The Phoenician.  I've already planned another visit for early December!  I shall return again and again!

reviews.author: neelleyclan
reviews.title: Awesome Resort
reviews.text: My girlfriends and I stayed at the Phoenician in June 2006. Our room was very cozy, the grounds beautiful  and the food delicious.  You paid for this in cost but if you enjoy luxury it is well worth every penny.  For about $150 a day you can rent a private cabana by the pool.  I highly recommend this.  Not only do you get shade and comfort poolside, you have your own bathroom and shower.  We did have a problem with the pool on our last day.  The chemicals were out of sync and all of our bathing suits and hair were destroyed (we all were green).  It was horrible and we all were shocked this would happen at a resort such as The Phoenician. Thankfully management was very understanding and they  reimbursed us for our suits and hair care.  The service was exceptional and caring. We did not visit the spa but I hear it is wonderful too.  I highly recommend this resort to anyone who likes to be pampered.

reviews.author: congeo
reviews.title: Incredible service and accommodations
reviews.text:
If you want the ultimate in service, accommodations, and just
an overall fantastic experience, visit the Phoenician Hotel
and Resort in Scottsdale, AZ
It deserves every 5 Star rating it has earned, and as a travel
industry guest ie: Airline Employee, this must rate in my
personal Top 5!
From check in to check out, every employee treats you as a
welcomed friend, not a hotel guest. The concierge staff is especially
wonderful, and helped us plan our car trip to the Grand Canyon
during the Sedona fires.  They monitored the internet
every day, assuring us a safe and enjoyable trip.
The pools are incredible, and the restaurants are also
first rate. I am already planning a return trip.

reviews.author: PittsburghCori
reviews.title: Relaxation and Utter Indulgence at the Phoenician
reviews.text:
My husband and I spent six relaxing days at the Phoenician this June.  He was there for business, I for pleasure, and both of us to celebrate our wedding anniversary.  I emailed the resort to tell them it was our anniversary, ask for a room upgrade, and make dinner reservations.  When we arrived at the resort we had been upgraded to a Junior Suite in the Canyon Building. 

The Canyon Building is above the center of the resort and very private.  We never ventured to any of the other pools or buildings, other than for dinner at Windows on the Green.  Staying there was the way to go for a couple looking for relaxation and quiet. Our suite was spacious, bright, and airy.  There is an honor bar and fridge which we promptly filled with our own beer, water, and snacks from a local Safeway.  The price of the food and drink in the honor bar was outrageous.  We’re talking a $14 bottle of airplane sized vodka.  Really.  The bathroom was beautiful and the bed was like a dream.   I can see where the dated comments regarding the furnishings come from.  It wasn’t obvious until you looked a little closer, but there were some nicks in the wood and scratches on the glass.  It wasn’t a big concern to me, but if I had paid the peak season price of $2500 a night for one of these suites I would have wanted absolute perfection.  It wouldn’t take much to update and I’m sure it’s in the future of the resort.   

The Canyon pool was the absolute best.  No kids.  On weekdays, at its most crowded, there were maybe 10 of us there.  It was wonderfully relaxing and the pitchers of ice water were a very necessary nice touch.  I was hot like I’ve never been hot before in my life!  Spending the days on the padded loungers reading the USA Today delivered to my room each morning was as close to perfection as it gets.  I ate lunch by the pool most days.  Everything was overpriced, but fine.  Nothing spectacular, but it required no effort on my part, so it worked for me.  Being tucked down in the valley of Camelback Mountain provided absolutely amazing scenery.  The pools are all open 24 hours a day and a night swim was the ideal way to unwind before bed.   Unfortunately, we were unaware there was a spa just a few steps away from the Canyon pool.  It’s in a pretty little spot nestled in the desert.  

The room was replenished each day and the turn down service was lovely to come home in the evening to.  Every employee we came in contact with greeted us with a smile and a kind word.   A great majority of them seemed to be college kids.  The food and service at Windows on the Green was top notch.  We received a complimentary toast and dessert for our anniversary.  We ordered room service at 2:00 a.m. and they were the most expensive and delicious cheese burgers I’ve ever had!  We had the Canyon building’s concierge call us cars any time we needed to get somewhere and rides ranged from $12 - $40.  Into Old Town was $12, out to the airport was $40, and the in between.   
We had an amazing time.  It was about nothing more than relaxation and indulgence.  I would lay by the pool all day, go to the room and take a bubble bath in the marble Jacuzzi tub, and nap in a giant fluffy bed…I was so spoiled.  It’s tough to be back in the real world again.  I would stay at the Phoenician again in the off-season.  The lower rates make it well worth it.  I’d think twice about in-season rates because it costs money just to breathe there.  If you’re in the mood to treat yourself, I’m sure you’ll be spoiled by the Phoenician, too!

reviews.author: Otto
reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.text:
Just returned from business trip to Scottsdale and stayed at the Phoenician.   The facilities are older yet in good repair overall.  The entrance, lobby, bar & dinning areas are very nice.  The large complex of pools & waterslide are laid out so are you visually separated and don’t feel your crowded.  Some tiles were missing but general repair and pool bathrooms were in good order.  

The “Center for Well Being” more commonly known as a spa, is beginning to show its age.  The men’s locker room, sauna and steam bath was worn.  The locker area was in poor condition.  Old lockers were marred and had stained surfaces, broken hinge on my locker #130.  The showers took approximately 1.5-2 minutes to get hot water and the hardware was worn.  Looking up in the shower you will notice they replaced the “rain-fall” large water head with a smaller unit found in the standard room shower yet did not repair the larger entry hole left by the old shower head leaving a larger hole.  The attendant had nothing to do but follow me around.  I bumped into him going into the shower, coming out of the steam shower and whirlpool, felt stalked.

The rooms were nice size with comfortable beds and excellent linen.  The bathroom has an ageless soft quality with plenty of natural stone everywhere.

Overall service is great. Food was very good.  Setting was excellent with views of Camelback Mountain and meticulously maintained grounds.  Negatives:  that attendant in the spa, all wallpaper in the rooms and halls needs to be replaced (stained, torn, etc…) carpets very worn.

reviews.author: KatieLouWho
reviews.title: Perfect Place to relax!
reviews.text:
We recently decided to take a relaxing vacation (instead of a hurried sight seeing vacation) and set our sights on Scottsdale, Arizona. A little leery at first that we would be the youngest people in the retirement town, we decided to stay at The Phoenician Resort for some much needed R&R. And we loved it! The room was very comfortable and spacious, not to mention the view of Camelback Mountain from our balcony! The bathroom was also very nice with a shower, a tub and lots of counter space - and full size complimentary toiletries. (These toiletries were top notch too - wonderfully aromatic Grapefruit Eucalyptus designed specifically for the Spa at The Phoenician).

While we were there my husband took in a round of golf at the resort's course. The views were spectacular he noted - although he said the course was just alright. I took in the spa while he played. I enjoyed the Tranquility Scrub, Wrap and Massage. It was heavenly! After my spa treatment, I indulged in the Meditation Atrium provided for spa guests. It was nice to let everything soak in and continue my relaxation without having to rush to get dressed and get out of the facility. 

When we weren't golfing or enjoying the spa, we spent most afternoons by one of the 9 pools the resort offers. Each day as we were "setting up camp", we were greeted by someone from the wait staff. They would deliver a pitcher of ice water and help you put up your umbrella (if desired). The drinks by the pool (although a tad expensive) were worth every penny. I don't know what it is about sitting by the water with a fruity beverage in hand but it really makes you feel like you are on vacation.

Overall this resort was the best experience I have had on vacation. The staff was very attentive and catered to any need. The overall price was more than we normally spend but we returned home relaxed and refreshed and knew we had made a great choice! I would definitely return to Scottsdale - and will stay at the Phoenician!

reviews.author: Mojo8
reviews.title: Nice resort
reviews.text:
Our first impression of the hotel was that our room was huge. I think it must have been oversized, because it was closer to 800 sq feet and then a 300 ft patio/balcony with a retractable awning!  We were quite impressed. The rooms were definitely in need of updating, but overall pretty nice. The service was always attentive.  

The food was pretty good. If we had had to pay for breakfast, it might have  been a little expensive for the breakfast buffet.  The selection is a little limited given the price, but the quality was good.  The other restaurants that we tried were all pretty good.  We travelled with a couple who had a baby.  When the father had to run back to the room for something for the baby and our main courses arrived, the waiter actually took away the first one and replaced his dish with a fresh one, so that it would not be cold.  It  was very considerate. 

The spa was very nice.  It is not as new as some resort spas, a but still clean and nice.  The spa offerings are very diverse and and spa bar/atrium is really nice. I was very impressed by the service at this spa.  The golf course is amazing. It's just beautiful, as it winds around the mt.  

The only complaint I had was about the pool decks. There was simply not enough room to accomodate the guests poolside. With the 3 pool decks, we should not have had to walk around 3 times at 2pm to find two chairs.  It was a holiday weekend, but still, that's what we were there for.  The little extras at the pool in the afternoon were a very nice touch though. 

The resort was really attempting to cater to families, so they offered alot of extra activities for the weekend, including dive-in movies, marshmellow roasts, etc.  Those were fun to take advantage of, even without kids.  This seems like a very family friendly resort.

reviews.author: jaymemm
reviews.title: Good Experience
reviews.text: The grounds are beautiful and impressive.  The staff is generally very nice and helpful.  Service was very good.  The rooms are dated and are in need of renovation in several areas.  I enjoyed my stay, but would definitely not pay the rates again for this hotel -- this is not quite a $500 or more/night hotel -- a great place to stay if you have points to use.  The hotel nickles and dimes you more than any comparable hotel I have stayed at.  Overall, a very nice experience.

reviews.author: FrequentFlier7297
reviews.title: Hated It!
reviews.text: It was the worst service I have ever experienced at a hotel. The restaurant service was poor, the staff was rude. I cannot believe this is a 5 star resort. Someone needs to stay there that is multicultural and see how they treat you. Once our company complained to the management the service turned around completely. How unfortunate. Don't go!

reviews.author: Firsttimers10
reviews.title: Beautiful, but not welcoming for children
reviews.text:
We were fortunate to be able to stay at the Phoenician for four nights over spring break this year.  It was all that we expected - exquisite grounds, interior decor, and good location to Old Scottsdale.  The staff was extremely accomodating, though did not seem too thrilled to have a young family in presence (save for the pool staff).  It was difficult to get a recommendation for a restaurant that is acceptable for children - the concierge sent us to one obviously not accomodating to children, and did not tell us a reservation was needed on that Friday night.  Disappointing.  The rooms are fine, beds comfortable, though our carpeting had stains on it.  

I would definitely return, but with just my husband, or for a ladies' weekend.  I do not feel this is an appropriate place for children under the age of 10, and I didn't feel any of the other guests believe it to be either.

reviews.author: SDSteve
reviews.title: Catch a Falling Star!
reviews.text:
Here's the summary in a nutshell.  If you are from the Phoenix area, and you want to spend time at a hotel that will completely make you forget you are in Arizona, the Phoenician is your dream come true.  Landscaped gardens, massive swimming pools, soaring palm trees and more green grass than you can shake a stick it.  Just don't shake a rain stick, because anything else remotely native Arizonan is relegated to a minor role at this property that is more suited to the beaches of Maui than to the Arizona desert.  If you're coming to Arizona on vacation, and want to actually feel like you're in the desert, and enjoy some desert culture, run like the wind to another property.  

Don't get me wrong.  Many folks will probably love the Phoenician.  It has a commanding location at the base of Camelback Mountain.  It has a spa, golf courses and fine restaurants (more on that later).  If you like shopping, Scottsdale is just down the street.  If you like to see and be seen, look no further.  Cash in your Starpoints now.  

Want some peace and quiet?  Steer clear of the lobby.  The fountains are so loud you'll have a tough time hearing the cover band, much less getting the attention of a cocktail waitress.  Want to take a quiet, peaceful late night stroll on the grounds?  Hope you like the Rippingtons.  Want to sleep in on easter sunday morning?  The Phoenician has a very unique wakeup call.  It's called gardeners with leaf-blowers.  Yes, on easter sunday morning at 9 am.  It took three calls to the service desk to get them to leave 90-minutes later, and not before they had blown dust over every car parked near the casitas.  I guess having clean grounds is more important than having the guests have clean cars.  (see photo).  

That's probably the part that really eats me about the Phoenician.  It has so many things going for it, but to truly be a first-class five-star resort, the can-do, guest-first attitude has to permeate to every employee on the property.  It means nothing to have a doorman great every guest in the lobby when you have irresponsible gardeners and stuffy cocktail waitresses.  And then there is the front desk staff.

If you take the room you are assigned, they will be the most pleasant folks you've ever met.  Just don't try to make any changes.  Since we were staying at the hotel for five nights, and we were Starwood Platinum Members, we wanted to ensure a comfortable room for five days.  Being our 10th anniversary, I requested a room with a king bed.  Instead I got a casita with two double beds.  When I requested to change to a king bed, I was relegated to a ground level casita with a breathtaking view of a brick wall.  The dark stuffy room wasn't going to work for five days, so I returned to the front desk and requested to see a room that actually had a view and perhaps was in sight of a cactus.   The room was a major downgrade, and I would've taken it if it wasn't for the fact that someone had smoked in it.  When I asked if they could ionize the room, I was told it would take 90 minutes (fair enough), and so I inquired about if they could transfer my luggage from my original room to the new one when it was ready.  You would've thought I asked the front desk staff to club a baby seal on the head with a big mallet.  After a minute of blank stares and raised eyebrows, they finally demured and graciously, well, not so graciously, offered to have someone deliver my bags to the new room.  If this is how they treat the hotel chain's best guests, I shutter at how they would sneer at a someone with mere mortal hotel status.  

The casitas are a slight improvement over your typical apartment complex.  If you can overlook the fact that the rooms are pushing 30 years old, they are, as other reviewers have written, tired.  The carpeting is worn and stained in areas.  There is not a single comfortable chair in the room.  No sofa, no leather chair or ottoman.  Just two desk chairs and your beds.  The beds are extremely comfortable, the best part of the stay.  The marble bathrooms are nice.  Marble never gets worn and tired.  There are no in-room coffee makers, but room service will gladly set one up for you for a daily fee.  If you want a room with a cactus view, you'll have to settle for the main tower facing the back side of the hotel, where there is a cactus garden at the base of Camelback Mountain.  

The Easter Brunch was delicious and the presentation was masterful.  The chefs should be applauded on their creativity and culinary skills.  The food was superb, as was my bill.  Easter Brunch for two was a world-record $217 including tax and mandatory tip.  It wasn't the food that dissapointed, it was the service.  Twice I had to ask the wait staff to clear my plate when I returned from the buffet, and more than twice I had to ask for my beverage to be refilled.  Once again, the wait staff seemed more interested in checking out how much of a tip the table behind us left, then they were in making sure our coffee was warm.  For $217 you'd think that they would brew the coffee right there at the table.  In fact, for $217, I'd expect Juan Valdez himself to walk by with his donkey and pour my coffee personally.  I don't eat much, and frankly I didn't expect much, but I figure each strawberry I ate cost about $4, so the least they could do is pick up my plate on their way to deposit their tips at the bank.  

I'm being a little tongue in cheek here but only slightly.  Honestly I was hoping to rave about the Phoenician.  I talked about it for weeks before I left.  I was heading to Arizona to unwind on a spa vacation.  Now I'm still talking about it.  Maybe if you went with low expectations you'd be more pleased.  I remember Starwood telling me that the Phoenician is their best resort in Arizona.  I'd really beg to differ.  On so many different levels, the other properties are executing world-class service while many at the Phoenician seems content to rest on their laurels.  

Speaking of resting on laurels, watch where you step at the spa.  After our leaf-blowing wake up call and $5 raspberries, we decided to check out the spa, the other reason that we came to the legendary Phoenician.  I thought for sure the spa would blow my mind and make all the other experiences uneventful.  

The spa did blow my mind, but not in the way you might expect.  I was expecting world class.  We walked into the main spa lobby to inquire about using the facilities for the day and booking some appointments.  There were four people in line in front of us, and the desk was being run by a young lady probably twenty years old.  She was stressed out because the kind people at the front of the line were taking quite a while to decide what type of services to book, while the line was growing longer and longer behind them.  Her stress level was so high that it just permeated the room.  Not the way you want to kick off your $200 Reiki Chakra Balancing.  Undeterred, we waited.  She eventually summonsed some help, and the line started moving, but the entrance had the peaceful mystique of a bus station.  The facilities were underwhelming to say the least.  The spa is truly tired.  The tile floors were dingy, if not dirty.  The jacuzzi in the men's lounge was directly between the locker area and the toilets, right in the main thoroughfare.  It was so crowded, with lots of little kids too, I can't imagine how anyone could find the spa and steam room facilities relaxing.  There is a decent meditation room and the fitness center is modern.  For the prices they charge, you think they could invest a fraction of it into keeping the facilities clean, peaceful and up to date.  Nearly every review I googled on the spa mentions that it is tired, and it truly is.  If they are not willing to invest in improving the spa while charging top dollar for services, I suggest you invest elsewhere as well.  They may have the best spa staff in the world, but it'd be like getting a world-class massage at a 24-Hour Fitness.  I've seen YMCA's with nicer locker room facilities honestly.  Now again I know, some folks will find the spa inviting.  This review isn't for you.  This is for the Starwood people who have been around the world and seen truly world-class spas at the St Regis in Dana Point, at the former Orchid on the Big Island, even at the Sheraton Wild Horse Pass in nearby Chandler who's spa makes the Phoenician's look like a condo-complex recreation room.  

I must credit the hotel on a few items.  First, they did offer to have a bellman come to our room and take our car for a complimentary carwash.  Granted that was after three calls and more than a few other rooms complaining about the blowing dirt, and at the end of the day, I didn't want to trust my new sedan to a hotel that didn't have enough respect for me not to blow dirt on my car in the first place.  And second, they were kind enough to let us check out early without a fee for doing so, probably because they realized that this review would've been twice as long had we stayed!  

Obviously from the reviews, there are many people who loved this resort.  There are some tremendous things about it.  It's just that if you don't get the basics right, if you don't excel at the little things, than the bigger things become less meaningful.  You're only as good as your weakest links, and if you brag about your 5-Diamond Service on your website, you need to back it up.  

As we drove down the long boulevard from the hotel, with the sun setting on Camelback Mountain and the dirt billowing off our windshield as we passed the beautiful fountains, we made tracks for the brand new Sheraton Wild Horse Pass instead.   And how did we, the cynical, difficult, frustrated hotel guests fare down there?  You'll just have to click over there to find out.  But I'll give you a hint.  If there is any justice in the world, the Sheraton Wild Horse Pass will pick up one of the Phoenician's famous five stars in the coming year.

reviews.author: penredj
reviews.title: Poor service & employee issues at the Phoenician
reviews.text:
I spent only a couple hours at the Phoenician, but wanted to share my experience with their outdoor patio restaurant.  Please note that I did not stay at the hotel.

I experienced truly lackadaisical service by our wait staff.  We had to request repeatedly what should be items included with a set table - bread plates, cutlery, creamer for our coffee, etc.  It was a warm day and butter was served in liquid form, which is not appetizing.  Dessert was served smeared across the plate, with our waiter explaining "oh, it slid across the plate!" with a smirk.

Lunch for two was $92, and for that price I expected better quality.

The hotel itself is beautiful and everything seemed to be fully up to date.

While waiting for our car, we witnessed not one but two altercations between valet staff and a member of the management team, including pointed fingers being pressed into the chest.  They stopped briefly and then continued their argument.  Thankfully this occurred at "low volume," but really this should never occur in public view.

An overall disappointing afternoon.

reviews.author: Jim M
reviews.title: One of the Best
reviews.text: One of the best, if not the best, hotels I have stayed at.  Spent a week with my family and have nothing but positives to say.  Beautiful grounds, great staff and great rooms.  Truly a 5 star resort and worth the money.

reviews.author: Zonidetroit
reviews.title: "The Phoenician Baby!
reviews.text: My family and I have been coming to The Phoencian for eleven straight years. Having been to alot of great five star resorts around the country including, The Broadmoor, Ritz Carlton Orlando, and Amelia Island, The Breakers, to name a few I have to say that The Phoencian is the best all around resort we have ever been to. Beautiful setting, backs up to camelback mountain, stunning lobbey area, great rooms (despite some of the comments in this forum about being outdated)awesome marble baths, beautiful grounds, best pool complex of any hotel I have ever stayed at(one of the comments in this forum said the pool was average at best, not any better than your normal country club. Where was this guy staying at?) Great service, golf is way over priced, and ok at best. Sunday Brunch is not to be missed, treat yourself, its worth every penny ( Chefs are grilling beef tenderloin outside) while they are pouring you champagne inside, what a scene. If you go please dress up, the last time we were there I could not believe all the underdressed people showing up. Guys in jeans and golf shorts, one slob even showed up in a bathing suit. Its elegant, dress up! Book a room in the Canyon Building, its like being in your own private mansion. All in all, when my family and I return from a new place for vacation, we always ask to each other the same question, how did it compare to The Phoencian, and its always the same answer, it didnt! The place to see and be seen in Scottsdale AZ.

reviews.author: Billiebob
reviews.title: Nice Time
reviews.text: We had a nice experience at The Phoenician.  We stayed in a suite and it was very nice. The pool and jacuzzi were also very nice along with a beautiful view of Phoenix.  We enjoyed delicious food at The Terrace Restaurant and the Windows restaurant at the golf club.   We enjoyed playing the 27 hole golf course and thought the grounds were immaculate.   We also had a very good sandwich at the 19th hole after golf.  We found all the help to be well trained and pleasant and the concierge also helped us quite a bit.  We had a five star experience.

reviews.author: Curious25657
reviews.title: Nickeled and dimed!
reviews.text:
I was slightly taken aback by the $4.00 daily housekeeping charge on the bill (Oh! Was housekeeping optional? Was it for the two chocolates left on the pillow?) Not to mention the $20.00 daily internet connection fee. 

The $5.95 fresh-squeezed orange juice was really fresh-squeezed because "it says so on the bottle" according to our waiter at "The Terrace", one of the hotel restaurants. I can assure you that fresh-squeezed orange juice, in my experience, comes from pressing oranges in a restaurant kitchen, and not from a bottle!

Waiting 10 to 15 minutes at the pool for your $10 Pina Colada is common, not the exception.

On the whole, considering the price, one would expect a much classier hotel.

Reedeeming factors: the concierges, all extremely courteous, and helpful, the very friendly waitstaff, and the bar on the lobby level with its tables with burning coals at night. Beautiful settings.

reviews.author: Josette H
reviews.title: Horrible Spa Experience
reviews.text: My mother in law loves the Phoenician and gave me a  b'day gift certificate to the Spa.  Having recently moved to AZ from California I was excited to try a decadent treatment but proceeded to get lost on the drive over.  The Map quest directions were wrong and about 20 minutes before the appt. I called for directions and found out that I was on the right track and 10 minutes away. I checked in over the phone to save time and was told that I would receive the full treatment time of 90 minutes. I was understandbly rushed into the changing area. However no one did a client in-take in regard to contraindications, medications or health concerns etc. I received a frown when I asked to use the bathroom.  Then I was led to my spa room and as the esthetician began the treatment. She chided me for having on makeup (I hadn't come from home.) After removing it and begining the treatment she tells me that she will have to take 20 minutes off of my treatment time and  that I would be charged for the full amount.  Which I didn't understand as I wasn't 20 minutes late. Cleansing is included in any treatment time and there should be two cleansings one to remove makeup and one to clean your skin.  She then said that perhaps I should just reschedule and got me off the table and led me in my bathrobe to the front desk where other clothed guests were checking in.  There I was told that I would be accessed a charge for not giving a 24 hour cancellation notice!  I think that it was 20%.  The surly upfront girl of about 17 then offered me appointments that were in the evening during the weekday and the soonest was more than a week away.  Finally it was determined that I should just choose a 60 minute spa service and I was trotted back to the spa room where I received a decent but not fabulous  facial treatment. Afterward I used jacuzzi and the Scotchhose in the shower room and found the shower tiles cracked and fallen out. I thought the spa looked old and rather dated but somewhat charming.  Not $200 treatment charming however. I filled out the customer service card and never heard from anyone.  I will never go back to the spa at the Phoenician again. I have however gone there for lunch. The hostess was friendly and talkative and commented to us that management made many demands of them.  The waitress looked a bit harried and over-worked and brought the wrong food over.  She intimated that it wasn't the best place to work for.  However there were wild rabbits hopping about the landscape and the atmosphere was very serene. I would dine there again only.

reviews.author: Compass31522
reviews.title: Fabulous Phonician
reviews.text:
We stayed here and loved it.  Incredibly relaxing - beautiful grounds - friendly staff - great golf - great pools and waterslide.  We have 3 kids who loved it and were very welcomed.

The rooms are a bit musty and the decor is slightly dated but you have a huge patio and the shower was great.  The upscale French restaurant was not quite what we were in the mood for but very nice.  People dress to the nines (black tie, sequined gowns, etc.) so be ready for that if you go.  

Here's the thing - we used Starwood points to stay here, otherwise, this review would have a different perspective.  You have to have a credit line at the Federal Reserve to stay here - everything is expensive.  From the tipping of the bellmen to the drinks and the golf - it all costs money and a lot of it.

BUT - if you want to truly relax and can afford to splurge a bit, this is the place.  They treated us like royalty - it was Halloween and the kids trick-or-treated within the hotel.  The kids got butterfingers and reese's from the hotel staff who were delighted to see little ones in their costumes.  We will definitely return.

reviews.author: JohnMD
reviews.title: Loved the cacti... not the golfers
reviews.text: We needed a couple days to relax and decided to go to Phoenix.   As I have Starwood points I was able to get a reduced rate... had I paid the going rate of $600+ a night, my comments would be more critical.  Initially they put us over the driveway... then eventually we settled on a room overlooking the beautiful cactus garden between the rooms and the mountain.   The grounds were beautiful... the rooms and the common areas a bit dated and a bit musky smelling.   We enjoyed the restaurants... Windows on the Green had very good Southwestern fare, and The Terrace had a great seafood risotto  (and a nice ambience on the patio.)   It turns out that our room overlooked the tee of the 8th hole... and in the evening, our view was disturbed by golfers climbing to the top, cursing as they hit their balls somewhere other than near the green, and thankfully not into us sitting on our balcony.   We are pretty seasoned travelers....and have stayed at the finest places... but for the money... this one does not quite make it.   I would suggest staying for one night... then head up to Sedona.  Or better yet... try the Biltmore or JW.

reviews.author: Gene_Claude
reviews.title: good but not great
reviews.text:
Stayed at the Phoenician for a couple days for a conference with my wife.

The good:

The setting (literally right next to Camelback Mountain) and the views were great.

The bed was uber-comfortable.

The staff and service were top notch and incredibly responsive.

The outdoor bar/restaurant had a great setting (did not eat there).

The "just OK":

The pool area was fine, but nothing great.  The pools aren't any nicer than a run of the mill country club.

The grounds are very nice, but not any more so than several Scottsdale resorts.

The bad:

My wife and I agreed that the common areas and rooms feel dated.  The rooms (or at least ours, looking out at the haunches of Camelback) were dark, not particularly large and somewhat dingy.  These are not the rooms of a 4 or 5 star resort, they are the rooms of an airport Mariott.  I'm sure the casitas are much nicer.

The ridiculous charges for things that should be complimentary.  Internet access was $20/day.  The mini bar was, of course, insanely overpriced.  Poolside food was overpriced.

My wife reports that the spa is very mediocre.

Overall, I doubt I would ever stay here on my own dollar, but it was a fine place for a conference.

reviews.author: ConnieS
reviews.title: Best hotel in the area
reviews.text:
Went to Phoenix and Scottsdale for a 4 day quick trip. Stayed at a private home, but spent two days touring all the hotels in both Phoenix and Scottsdale.

Result:
#1 place to stay - Phoenician - beautiful resort hotel. Had lunch here and service was exactly like Four Seasons.  Asked our name when we arrived and then addressed us by our name throughout the meal even after knowing we weren't staying at the resort.  This may be important to some people, but this is the only resort that has grass and flowers.  Phoenix and Scottsdale (other than golf courses) are flat, dusty, and the color brown.  If you like shades of brown with no color than Arizona is your kind of place.  So it was nice to enter a resort that actually had color in both grass and flowers.  Pool area luxurious.  

#2 place to stay - Hyatt Regency at Gainey Ranch - for a large hotel, felt "homey".  Pool area had double cushion lounge chairs for couples.  Grounds very pretty - not as nice as the Phoenician, but still very nice.

Would not recommend The Boulders.  Too far from anything and frankly - just blah. Small pool.  Liked the big boulders to look at, but after an hour we'd had enough.  Spa at the entrance of a gated area - not with the hotel.  

Would not recommend JW Marriott Camelback Inn.  Outdated and just bland.  

JW Marriott Desert Ridge is definitely a corporate hotel.  Large, plain, lobby nice, that is about it..nothing special...but for a free stay on the company dime...not too shabby.  If your not with a business group, you will be disappointed.

Overall, unless you golf or love art, I'd skip Phoenix/Scottsdale all together. Nothing to do, will be bored. For the money, go to Cabo, Santa Barbara, Las Vegas, etc.

reviews.author: Stay23176
reviews.title: I expected better....
reviews.text: For the incredible room price, I expected an incredible experience and hotel. Over all, I was very disappointed. While the rooms (including the bathrooms) are very large, the quality of the amenities and services do not match the hype--or my expectations. My stay was for three nights, including a weekend. Some of my issues: dirty room service trays were left in the halls; room service attendants are not friendly; room service carts blocked the hallways; inconsistent cleaning of my room each day; long waits for drinks and food at the pool (hello, anyone work here??); $20/day internet service (most hotels now offer for free or $10/day); no quality control on the limos that service the hotel; low quality towels (yes, I expect large and plush towels for $400+/night); $23 charge for a muffin, juice bottle and banana in the lobby shop. However, I must say that the majority of the staff is extremely friendly and helpful. The only thing I found satisfying was the terrific food and service available in the restaurants. Quite frankly, I didn't find the Phoenician to be any better than a nice Hyatt Regency. The next time I visit Scottsdale I'll spend my time and money at the Four Seasons.

reviews.author: Patricia H
reviews.title: Great spot for hiking and pool lounging.
reviews.text:
Just back from a weekend at the phoenician. We stayed in a suite near the 'sunset spa' and had the hot tub and the pool to ourselves all weekend. I am not a resort person but this is a great place to relax by the pool and have rum drinks and good food delivered to your chaise lounge. We enjoyed hiking to the top of Camelback mountain (map is in your room). My husband thought it would be some sort of paved trail for old folks but it was indeed a really challenging climb. At the end we were basically rock climbing. The views were fantastic. About 3 hours round-trip.

I enjoyed a massage at the spa, too, though I am not a spa person, either. There are all sorts of tubs and showers to relax in after a massage or hike, too. Worth every penny.

Also: the staff was over-the-top professional, down to the lawn crew. The employees are really first-rate. We ordered room service for breakfast and dinner and found it to be fairly tasty. The prices were about the same as at the restaurant, which I found stuffy and boring.

Enjoyed the coyotes howling every night, too.

reviews.author: starwood6589
reviews.title: Loved the Phoenician!
reviews.text: As a Starwood Gold Member, I redeemed points to stay at the Phoenician for 2 nights/ 3 days in March 2005 with my family of five (kids 15,14,10).  We had previously stayed at the Wigwam Resort also owned by Starwood before we arrived at the Phoenician.  Checkin went smoothly and our room was very close to the cactus garden which was very cool to walk around.  Our family enjoyed the numerous pools and it was never a problem finding chairs. Water pitchers were replaced very quickly and poolside lunches was very delicious and arrived quickly.  The Phoenician was very accomadating with every request and the children loved the resort.  The best thing about the resort was the tennis garden where we received playing time on the center stadium court with complementary refreshments and cold towels.  We played $40 for the court and were able to play the whole day.  We even went to play tennis at 10 pm and were chauffered  by golf cart  from the lobby to the tennis courts and back at 11:30 pm.  Also, the ice cream shoppe was very nice even if it was a bit pricey.  Over all, our stay at the Phoenician was excellent and I wouldn't hesitate to reccommend it to anyone and would love to return as soon as possible.

reviews.author: jcm1101
reviews.title: beautiful!!
reviews.text:
My family and I just returned from The Phoenician.  It was a beautiful hotel.  Our room was beautifully decorated and the pool view and mountains from our balcony were picture perfect.  The bathrooms are beautiful to.  The service there is great, the people can't do enough for you.  The hotel is spotless, never saw a finger print on anything. The bedding is to die for so comfortable. The restaurants are terrific! Especially the Sunday buffet.  It was the Thanksgiving Holiday and there were families there but not many.  I would have to say this Hotel is not really family oriented.  Our boys are 4 and 8 and they were really sweet to them. I'm sorry to say some of the people that stay there were a tiny bit stuffy.  But that does not bother me I'm stuffy right back.  My husband and I like to stay in nice places and we are not stuffy at all. They have 9 beautiful pools and they even have pools for the little ones.  All the pools are heated.  Went to the spa it was nice been to nicer ones.  We went on the Detours, Inc. tour to Apache Trail  the views were magnificient.  We also went to Sedona it's beautiful there.  We went on "A Day in the West" tour, it cost us over $200 did not think it was worth the money. Also, the Rolling Stones were doing a concert and they were also staying at the hotel the same time we were there.  I also saw some athletes and my mom told me she heard on the news Jennifer Aniston was at the spa.  So don't be surprised if you see someone famous there.  Being in Arizona you are surrounded by beautiful Mountains, we saw such beautful views. 
Also, there are lots of Casinos in Arizona, no crap tables though.  The Sea of Cortez is 3 hours away and LA is a 6 hour drive.  We also went to the Pheonix Zoo and the Science Center with the kids.  They have great malls too. The flight was 5 hrs going and 4 hours back to New York (smooth flights) If you got the money to spare and want to stay in luxury go for it. You'll be treated like a King and Queen.

reviews.author: COJOWisconsin
reviews.title: What a wonderfully relaxing resort
reviews.text: We visited the Phoenician over the Halloween weekend from Thurs.10/27 to Mon. 10/31 and had a great time.  With 7 pools how can you not!  We took our 7 and 10 year olds with us and they couldn't complain.  It was a bit pricey ordering poolside but that is what vacation is for.  We also had trouble getting as good a service on the weekends by pool as during the week.  The concierge, Jessica (born and raised in Wisconsin), was extremely helpful and unpretentious.  Our room was kept very clean  and up to my high expectations (although the bidet was not working much to my children's disappointment because they had never seen one before!).  The Sunday Brunch was to die for but so was the price-$230 for the four of us-Ouch!  This was the perfect weekend weatherwise.  It was mid 80's every day we were there.  I would recommend staying at the hotel anytime!  I returned home relaxed and rejuvenated:)

reviews.author: 213KellyP
reviews.title: The over priced Phoenician
reviews.text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Phoenician in Scottsdale, AZ.  This hotel is over priced and the rooms are mediocre.  The layout of the resort is difficult to navigate and there are dead ends everywhere you turn.  There are extra charges for everything you do, even though, the room prices are outrages for the accomodations.  Beware the valet parking charge.  It was over $25 dollars.  There is a self park garage which is free.  The fitness center is even an extra $20.  This hotel is definately for those who are advanced in age, as the decor is outdated and drab, with a lot of brass and glass. The grounds are well manicured, the pool is lovely, and the service was great.  This was not enough to make up for the average accomodations. I have stayed in many nicer resorts for half the price.  Overall this resort was disappointing.

reviews.author: Sammyc
reviews.title: Great resort to relax in
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed there for my birthday. We used our starwood points to get 50% off rack rate so it was a good deal.
Service was wonderful. Everyone was very attentive and accomodating. We spent an afternoon by the pool. They give you a pitcher of ice water and refills it often. The pool side food was yummy too. There are many small pools so if you like a little peace & quietness you can go to the 'quiet' pool where all the adults go.
The thirsty camel restaurant by the lobby is a good place to see the sunset. They have live music at nights & we can basically hang out at the resort and never have to leave!
The room was spacious. Huge bathrooms & good citrus shampoo/conditioner/lotion.
I'd stay there again. It's a good place to relax & unwind. It's only about 20-30 min from the airport too. Easy to find.

reviews.author: Climber33641
reviews.title: Our Honeymoon at the Phoenician....
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed at the Phoenician for our honeymoon Nov. 5th - 9th.  Originally, we were supposed to be in the Riviera Maya for the week, but due to the hurricane we had to quickly change our plans.  We decided to go to Arizona since I am a spa-aholic and my husband enjoys golfing.  We chose the Phoenician.  Check in was very smooth.  We were upgraded to a Casita overlooking the pools and Camelback mountain.  It was fairly large and the decor was elegant.  Our room had a strange smell and wet spots on the carpet-not what I would expect from this type of place.  Our bathroom was gorgeous and oversized, which was nice.  A large bathtub and stand alone shower.

The staff was very courteous and would go out of their way to make you feel special.  Our first night in we dined at the very elegan Mary Elaines on the top floor of the resort.  Pricey, but very excellent food.  We told them it was our honeymoon and they gave us complimentary champagne.  And ladies-your purse gets its very own stool to rest on!  The poolside staff is great too.  Sam, our cabana girl knew it was our honeymoon and brought us complimentary chocolate covered strawberries with a plate decorated for a king and queen.  The prickly pear margarittas are great!  Also, Sunday brunch will beat your hightest expectations, a must if you are there on a Sunday.

We really only had a few downsides to the resort-it is outdated and needs some renovation.  Don't even waste your time at their spa--NEEDS DESPERATE HELP.  Being a spa hopper-the best spas in the area- Sanctuary, and Golden Door at the Boulders.  We had treatments at all three resorts, and the Phoenicians amenities are below average.  I guess they want to expand their spa and blast into the mountain to build a new one, but the city won't allow it because of the noise and blowing into the mountain.  And another negative is that you have to pay extra to play tennis-$20/person.  I think that is nuts since you are already paing $400-$500 a night just to stay there.

All in all a great place with immaculate grounds, very courteous staff, great food, and a nice setting.

Katie

reviews.author: Bayturtle
reviews.title: A Ten.
reviews.text: I had four perfect days at the Phoenician.  This hotel replenished my love of the Scottsdale area.  Service was exceptional with every staff member I encountered attuned to my needs.  While not quite as well maintained as a Ritz Carlton, I liked the quiet, relaxed elegance better.  My standard room was huge with large lanai, couch, comfortable chairs, desk and two large dressers.  The bed perfectly comfortable with soft sheets and great pillows.  Food at the special events I attended was memorable.   Can't wait to get back.  Also, the hotel is usually jammed all winter, but late October and early November offers a great climate and fewer people.

reviews.author: OnAir33855
reviews.title: Great escape from Florida's hurricane
reviews.text:
My husband and I had an upgrade from a standard no view room to a quiet casita overlooking mountain, pool, and laguna.  We did not have a car and so stayed on the resort for our entire 3days stay.  We played tennis, laid by the pool, and hiked up Camel Back mountain.  With the resort being so large, you can always find something new to see or do.  The mountain hike is within walking distance from the hotel and it was a beautiful but yet challenging hike to the top. 

Though dining is 30-40% more than what we would pay at off-site restaurants, the food was great.  No complaints about the food quality at the Terrace, the pool Oasis, or the Windows on the Green.  The tortilla soup at the Windows on the Green was so good that I got their recipe.  One night, we ordered a delicious oven-roasted pizza to share and the room service guy set up a romantic table-clothed dinner for us on our patio (including a red rose).  We had packed along our own wine bottle and had a romantic dinner with an incredible sunset view.  In the late evenings, we had hot tea at the lounges and the main terrace by the pit-fires.

Really, my only complaint would be that they should make the pool drinks stronger.  Overall, the Phoenician was a great stay for us.

reviews.author: GoPlaces10647
reviews.title: Fantastic!
reviews.text: I loved the Phoenician!  I was very impressed from the very minute I entered the grounds.  They were very beautiful and well tended.  The valet staff were always very helpful and willing to assist in any way.  I was then greeted by a very nice gentleman who really made me feel welcomed.  I was then guided to registration by other staff who made sure I was well taken care of.  My room was fantastic!  It was spotless, tastefully decorated and very comfortable.  The bathroom was just perfect, marble, plush towels and robes and again spotless.  The pool staff were very attentive but not intrusive.  As soon as I arrived at the pool I was brought a pitcher full of ice water which was refilled as needed (without my having to ask).  I cannot say enough about the service here.  It was top notch and I highly recommend this hotel.  I will definitely be back!

reviews.author: bswatson51
reviews.title: Phoenician was phenomenal
reviews.text:
My girfriend and I (23 and 24) visited the Phoenician and the Four Seasons Scottsdale in late August for a short vacation.  Both hotels were very good, but hard to compare.  We spent 3 days at the Phoenician:

Rooms
Large rooms with nice bathrooms.  Standard 4-5* amenities.

Food
We had the breakfast buffet at the Terrace every morning, it was very good.  We ate light lunches at the poolside cafe and at the deli/ice cream parlor by the Phoenician stores.  We went off-site for dinner every evening so I cannot comment on that.

Spa/Gym
Very nice, expensive but worth it.

Pools
Nice layout.  They were not that crowded when we went, about 50% occupied.  I liked the oval mother of pearl pool the best.  We rented a cabana for $85 one day for the internet and privacy; it worked out well for us.  Good drink service.  Guys-note that the prickly pear margarita is pink.

Location
Really good location, at the base of a mountain pretty close (5-10 minutes) to downtown Scottsdale/shopping.

Service
Really good.  No major issues, but the Concierge was hit or miss depending on who you spoke with.

Other
You can help them feed the ducks/fish/turtles by the "lake" at 9:00-9:30. It can turn into quite the feeding frenzy.
The ice cream parlor has some delicious desserts, I liked the Prickly Pear sorbet.
The crowd was older mostly 40s or 50s and a bit pretentious, but not too bad.  Some families and some younger couples, no one really loud or rowdy.
Use your Amex Platinum to book the hotel if you have one, we saved a couple of hundred dollars by using ours.

reviews.author: Canada78
reviews.title: Worth almost every penny!
reviews.text:
My husband and I were forced to make an emergency stopover in Phoenix due to unexpected illness after a trip to Mexico. I asked the cabbie to take us to the closest 5 star. He recommended the Four Seasons above the Phoenician but it was too far away. As we pulled into the Phoenician’s grounds after a 15 minute ride, even my husband who was extremely ill commented that he was happy with the choice. 
 The Lobby doubles as a restaurant with view and has a large lit fountain at night with a sole pianist which lends great ambiance to the place. Check-in was effortless and quick, and we were presented with a number of room choices. I chose the golf view with King bed, which was the priciest. It was on the second of four floors, and was actually more of a croquet/pool view. We were pleasantly surprised with the room quality as we entered.  Two adequate closets flank a more than adequate mini bar, which contained a multitude of drinks and snacks, tanning essentials and a souvenir or two. They do not have ice machines in plain view so you have to call concierge for that, but they are relatively prompt.
The marble bathrooms are quite spectacular- very spacious with two sinks and a large soaker tub, larger than average toiletries from the spa, and enough towels. My husband commented that he liked the shower gels and shampoo and he normally couldn’t care less about that stuff. There is also a marble shower with excellent water pressure for a very relaxing shower. The toilet is separate, and the entire bathroom was immaculately clean.
 The bed and pillows were extremely soft and comfortable and there were a variety of pillows available. The adjacent couch, coffee table and desk were well appointed. There were four great magazines for us- Travel and Leisure was among them. There was above average quality stationary along with an internet connection for laptops. We paid 19.99 for 24 hours of internet usage and it was well worth it, since my husband was laid up in bed- we could book our plane tickets home without having to leave our room.
The TV was a newer and larger version than what we you’d normally see at a hotel. The dresser could have held more clothing than anyone could bring.
The patio was large and had a table and chairs and a lawn chair for tanning. 
The room was great. It wasn’t the best we’ve been in but it wasn’t far behind.
 The best part of this hotel is the service. The concierge did everything they could to make our stay enjoyable and comfortable, and the front desk graciously extended our check out till 5 pm for a hundred dollar charge- it should have been 250.00, as it’s normally 50 dollars per hour after 12 pm.
The staff were all extremely accommodating (at about midnight we were able to have someone from housekeeping come and change our bedding because my husband had finished sweating out his fever.) The following day I went to the salon with a special request and they were great about meeting it. We prearranged our bell service and airport transportation and it was carried off with zero glitches.
 The pools are on a series of different levels, they’re all great, but a little overcrowded- there are enough padded chaise lounges and to accommodate the crowds however, and enough umbrellas that each couple can share one. There are about 3 large hot tubs and lots of cabanas. Attendants lay out towels for the guests, and menus for the poolside café are on about every third chair. There are a lot of little kids, but they’re not half as bothersome as the many college kids. The clientele had to be the one of the cons to this hotel. Lots of pretentious women walking around the poolside in high heels.
The food wasn’t notable either. We paid 40 bucks for room service to bring us pancakes and a bowl of cereal, and they got the order wrong.
The hotel has a little shopping corridor near the lobby that is quite impressive. From souvenirs, books and cards to sundries, men’s and women’s casual and more formal wear, sleepwear and swimwear, floral and gifts, they’ve got it all in one of about ten shops. There is even a little café there where you can have coffee and lighter fare, although the service there is mediocre compared to the rest of the hotel. We didn’t get a chance to use the spa or golf centre since we were only there for about 24 hours. We are definitely planning to go back though…unless we go to the Four Seasons instead!

reviews.author: Adventure35772
reviews.title: Great Family Trip
reviews.text: My family of 4 love this hotel, this was our second visit. We had a great casita very close to the pool where we could watch the kids from our own patio. The bathrooms are the best i've been in. We also rented a cabana for a day and the service is unsurpassed. The cabana "boy" is very friendly and attentive as well as some nice eye candy. We will be back next year. I think this hotel is well worth the price. We use all the admenties including the Wellness Center and the golf course which my husband loves. Best of all the friendly staff who speak when they see you on the grounds even if they don't speak english they still greet you.

reviews.author: Lindyloo1
reviews.title: Dissapointed
reviews.text:
We had booked a room at the Phoenician before commencing our tour of Arizona and Utah. We were looking forward to a night there as we had just travelled from the U.K. and needed a good rest at a good hotel before driving around Arizona and Utah. This hotel is one of Starwoods luxury collection and we were upgraded as we are Platinum card holders.
The guy at the check in wasn't very pleasant, however, that can be overlooked as we all have our off days. The room, although one of their best, quite honestly was not up to much at all - it felt very stark and the bed was the hardest bed we have ever slept on.
The dining room was pleasant enough (as a room) but we recommend you don't eat there, the food wasn't great at all. There are plenty of other very good restaurants in Scottsdale that you would be able to get a super meal from. We had just come off the plane after a 16 hour journey and did not venture out for that reason.
We slept well enough, probably because we were exhaused from the day before, and when we drew the curtains in the morning we had a pleasant view of a very nice pool.
Unfortunately, we made the mistake of having breakfast there and this was a huge mistake. First of all, we were the only ones in the restaurant (as per the night before) and when we sat down the girl told us that their chef hadn't turned up but they were sure they could give us a good breakfast - they couldn't - my husband's omelette looked like a flying saucer with grated cheese on top to cover their bad cooking, mine was not too bad as they had managed toast.
On checking out watch your bill, we found two meals on our bill instead of one which clearly wasn't right. The surly guy that checked us in the night before rang through to the dining room for the chit only to be told they couldn't find it (very convenient) especially as we were the only people in the restaurant). Anyway, he credited the amount they had overcharged us and we went off.
I don't like writing a bad review but we were so taken aback I felt I had to. This is a very expensive hotel and rooms are $350+. We have had extremely good service from other lodges and hotels we stayed at in Arizona and Utah that would be considered reasonably inexpensive in comparison.

reviews.author: Coastal785
reviews.title: Nice Experience
reviews.text:
As locals, we wanted to play golf and get away from home for a night. We stayed a Saturday night on their "Masters Golf Package". A great deal at $280 (that includes tax) and it included the biggest, best view room, unlimited golf for one day and $50 credit towards breakfast.  I had not heard of this package but their ace reservationist, Hal, told me about it when I called. Upside: everything 5 star. Very clean and first rate.  Best hotel bathroom I have ever seen, turndown, delicious food, most beautiful golf course and awesome golf staff.  Downside: Lots of rude guests (to the staff)  around very crowded pool on Saturday (Sunday was heaven as half the guests) the pool staff was overworked and under staffed, $26 a day parking (you can use the self park for free and hop the elevator up to the lobby), very expensive food: 
Breakfast - Roomservice  - eggs, bacon, coffee and fruit for two $75.  The waiter did set it up beautifully on our gorgeous patio.  
LUNCH: At the pool, fish tacos for 3 adults and kiddy food for 2 plus one drink each $120+ tip.  I would go back but I would try the Boulders or the Four Seasons packages first.

reviews.author: Phillip Y
reviews.title: I LOVE THIS HOTEL
reviews.text:
I highly recommend the Phoenician to anyone staying in the Phoenix/Scottsdale area.  It is a phenomenal resort from the breathtaking views to the relaxing lobby patio to the plush rooms.  The room was top knotch with a a comfortable bed, cool marble bathrooms, and beautiful views of the city and golf course.  I love this hotel and will return to Phoenix just to stay at this resort.  

If you can deal with the heat (it was 110 degrees when I visited), the summer rates are a great value ($190 per night).

My only complaint was the concierge service could use improvement as the concierge rep took a while to acknowledge me while I was waiting with questions about golf.

reviews.author: dutchcouple
reviews.title: Phenomenal Phoenician
reviews.text:
This is absolutely the best hotel we have been to in a long time.
In short, i have not found a better hotel looking at the value for money you get from The Phoenician.

We stayed in a Casita room for 4 nights, from august 7 till august 11. We were so happy when we arrived at this hotel after our terrible stay at The Hotel at Mandalay Bay in Vegas. Check out my review on that hotel !

The Phoenician does everything right. Valet parking was great. The front desk was super accomodating and thats nice if you just before stayed at The Hotel at Mandalay Bay. The Phoenician has a really professional and courteous front desk ! At the last minute i requested a casita room instead of a normal hotel room. Front desk checked, found one and had it cleaned within 30 minutes. While waiting for our room the hotel picked up our bar bill. What more can i say. The casita room was lovely, about 30 feet from one of the 9 pools this resort has. Good bathroom and lots of space. Turndown and cleaning were perfect. When you go to the pool you get lots of towels and water with ice. All the loungers are hardwood, not the cheap metal ones you find in most hotels.
We had dinner in a couple of the restaurants, and it was very good indeed. The different bars were nice as well, you can sit outside and watch the stars or the Phoenix city lights.

It may seem a little boring, but everything was so perfect we actually were sorry we had to leave. For a little over $200 a night there is no better hotel in my humble opinion !!!

We will surely return and stay longer next time !!!

If you want a perfect stay, go to the Phoenician !!!

reviews.author: one_of_seven
reviews.title: Hot but heavenly
reviews.text:
Though the temp was over 110 each day, the stay was the best combination of style and hospitality that I have ever experienced.  The concierge, Gary, was very helpful in recommending outside lunch diner and actually scheduling our dinner at Drinkwater's, a fabulous experience in itself.  The heat really wasn't as bad as it sounds and the time spent around the pool was perfectly comfortable.  (The "dry heat" was very comparable to our routinely hot humid summers of NC and I did not find it uncomfortable to the extreme)

Every employee called me by name and treated me like royalty.  Yes, it is expensive, but when compared to the hotel we stayed at in Sedona and later at the Canyon rim, the Phoenician was the best value overall.  I will return.

reviews.author: dennis h
reviews.title: good and the ugly
reviews.text: good service thru out the hotel,food was above average,valet pking too costly,botanical garden very nice, pool area too noisy and too crowded,the carpet in my rm was dirty and the carpet in the hallway was very dirty!,the hallway was very warm,food trays from rm service left too long in the hallways, no coffee pot in rm,very nice bathroom and amenities.

reviews.author: RallyMonkey
reviews.title: Lived up to expectations
reviews.text:
We spent a week at the Phonecian and left without any major complaints. The hotel is expensive if you pay rack rate but who pays rack rate when good deals are so easy to get. The setting is excellent - we loved the cactus garden. It is not the ideal hotel for those who want to sit by the pool all day and order a cheap pizza in the evening. The extra do add up  (no more than in any other five star hotel), but with a bit of thought you can keep them to a reasonable level. For instance  valet parking is expensive ($25?) but why not self park in the underground car park for free ? The hotel lacks an every-day dining option,  on the other hand the food in the Terrace restaurant was very good, both for evening meal and breakfast. Not cheap, but good quality - and there are plenty of good restaurants in Scottsdale.

The room was in excellent decorative order, and everything worked as it should. Housekeeping was polite, efficient and attentive. The rooms are large, and suitable for comfortable long stays.

The pools can  fill up a little , especially when the hotel is full, and, yes, they do allow children to swim in them ! The pool staff do not clear towels away, and on busy days all the loungers were 'reserved' before 9am. Don't come here just for the pool, but do come if you want an excellent hotel with a good pool.

I suspect some of the negative reviews come from conference goers who need to keep the extras down and would not have chosen this type of hotel for their own holiday. If you are paying your own way the good news is that the hotel is big enough to absorb conferences without making any facilities in to no-go areas for regular guests.

We would return, and rank it in our top 10.

reviews.author: PatWV
reviews.title: High Prices and Over-rated
reviews.text: I stayed at The Phoneician in June for a conference.  My room was large but had some differed maintenance issues such as a large, ugly piece of plaster hanging from the balcony ceiling, a nasty spot by the front door, broken piece of furniture, and tired carpeting. The bathrooms were large and all marble. Hallway carpets looked worn and tired.  Received an unexplained call from housekeeping on my 2nd day that they were terminating housekeeping at my request. Front desk graciously comped me a breakfast on complaining.  Conference food was excellent while the Terrace restaurant was terrible.  I ordered a simple spaghetti and baby tomatoes which arrived gummy, soaked in oil and tasting awful.  The waiter's comment was, "Everyone else that night loved it." Breakfasts were good but expensive.  I ate in the lobby lounge for my dinners and paid $14 for a hamburger. Glasses of wine are in the $12-$22 range.  Wireless Internet is free in the lobby but $22 a night for use in your room via an ethernet cable.  The 7 pools are lovely but full of kids.  Beautiful place but requires lots of extra cash.

reviews.author: Texasnark
reviews.title: Highly Recommend the Phoenician
reviews.text: Did a long weekend in Scottsdale during April, 2005 and stayed at the Phoenician.  We have stayed at the Fairmont Princess before and the Phoenician is much better.  Some have said the rooms are a little tired and I would not disagree, but other than that, it is a great place to stay.  Very comparable to staying at a Four Seasons.  Service is extremely friendly and good.  We finished every night out on the veranda overlooking Phoenix which was really nice.  One night an amatuer astronomer brought his 6 ft telescope for everyone to see Mars...really neat.  Anyway, I recommend this hotel to those who want great service and employees who constantly speak to you with a smile.  It is expensive, so try to find a special rate...but remember, most everything is expensive in Scottsdale.  (Our rate no worse than most of the other high end resorts).  We will be back next year.

reviews.author: cotraveler411
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort
reviews.text:
Absolutely loved this hotel! The grounds are emmaculate and the staff nice, friendly, and accomodating. Our room was in the Canyon building, overlooking the golf course. The room was spacious, very nice, and clean. I would highly recommend this building. It was so nice to sit on the patio and enjoy the peace and quiet and beauty of the area. The building also has its own pool if you prefer quiet, but the walk to the main pool and lobby was really not far at all. 
As others state, it was expensive. However, we did not pay for the stay, and many meals were covered, so it wasn't too bad to splurge. I'm not sure I would pay the high amount to stay there otherwise, but if you don't mind spending LOTS of money, then I'd definitely pick this hotel.

reviews.author: J7349QArichardk
reviews.title: not worth the price
reviews.text: Stayed 3 nights from April 22-25; we spent $600 on a room facing the pool. Way, way, way overpriced for the type of room. We had to change rooms after the first night since we were 2 adults,2 children sharing a room with 2 double beds, totally inadequate for 2 adults to share a double bed. They were able to get us a room with king and pullout sofa bed but still way overpriced. Nice bathrooms but no way was this a great room for the money. Pool area overcrowded on weekends so have to get there early for a lounge chair. We paid $85.00 for a cabana so we didn't have to hassle and this was worth the extra money. Nothing was included in room rate. Valet parking was $26.00, use of fitness center/spa locker area was $18.00. Excellent service and nice grounds but would not go back. True, I am not a golfer so can't comment on golf facilities. Maybe worthwhile in off season just be prepared to spend much money on all extras.  Must say, service was excellent but it better be for $600.00/night.

reviews.author: Dream15870
reviews.title: very nice - very over-priced
reviews.text: This is a very nice hotel, but it is not a good value at all. The rooms are about on a par with a high-end business hotel, but at more than double the cost. The extra charges are nearly inescapable, frequent and consistently outrageous. The food is a mixed bag - some dishes are good some are not so good. The food prices are, however, dependably astronomical. If you have enough money to stay here good for you, but you'll get a lot more for your cash elsewhere.

reviews.author: GoPlaces30451
reviews.title: 4 times a charm!
reviews.text: Have stayed at The Phoenician 4 times in the last year and  a half, and have never been disappointed.It is a goergeous, top- notch property, offering luxurious,spotless rooms, and impeccable service. Although pricey, it is well worth tab, and we would never think of staying anywhere else while in Scottsdale!

reviews.author: tabasco1230
reviews.title: A True Review
reviews.text:
I went to the Phoenician on a business trip that left alot of free time to enjoy the Scottsdale area.  I did not have to pay for the lodgings so I feel I can give you an unbiased opinion.  The hotel and grounds were immaculate and the pool was great.  The only negative was that the bed and room decor appeared a bit dated but it did appear to be spotless.  The property sits at the base of Camelback Mountain which serves as a stunning backdrop both in the day and at sunset.  The staff were for the most part very friendly and went out of there way to make sure your visit was a good one.  I did not utilize the spa nor the gym so I cannot comment on it.  However the charge for both seemed to be in line with many other high class hotels.  The golf course was stunning!  The course is broken into three nine's with different characteristics. The Canyon course is a must.  Other members of my group utilized the Phoenician's concierge service and went on a great hot air balloon excursion, which they all raved about.  Apparently, there were even better vistas to be seen than that of Camelback on the golf course.  I also ate at the poolside "Oasis" and at the Terrace for brunch and both were fantastic.

All in all, this is a great hotel with beautiful grounds.  The main complaint from most users seems to be that of price and if you are a money conscious traveller, this definitely is not the place for you.  Personally, out-of-pocket I would never pay the rack rates for hotels in this range but I have stayed at comparable hotels and the Phoenician is a good option.

reviews.author: Wander5249
reviews.title: Nice to see lovely flowers and green grass!
reviews.text:
We spent seven nights at this beautiful, well run resort.  Coming from cold, rainy, bleak Philadelphia, seeing the vibrant colors and emerald green grass was incredibly inspiring and an added bonus to our vacation.  Our room was impeccably clean, and the room service was excellent.  We ate dinner at The Terrace and Windows on the Green and at The Thirsty Camel. And yes, the prices were outrageous.  One cannot beat sitting outside by the fire pits and looking at the vista. 

We also breakasted each morning at The Terrace. Service at all three places was excellent. The other nights we ventured "off campus" to some extraordinarily superior restaurants, as recommended to us by the concierge and the manager of The Terrace. However, $10.00 for a two minute cab ride was a bit pricey. In hindsight, I would rent a car. We were on the golf package which turned out to be a fairly decent value: unlimited golf, cart, range, and $50.00 towards breakfast. I know you may be saying,"WOW! Who eats $50.00 worth of breakfast?!?!" Believe me, with those prices, it is easy to do.  

The golf courses were spectaculary beautiful and fun to play.  I like the Oasis course the best. We were there peak season and had to wait on the teebox for quite some time on several days.  However, due to the time of year, that is not a surprise. The staff at the golf shop were attentive and interested in hearing feedback about our rounds.  One suggestion I had was to stagger the start times to ten minutes apart, rather than seven.  I disagree with having children be able to play all day, afternoon hours (after 2:00-3:00) would be sufficient. 
We did not sit at the pool much at all. Too many people, especially kids, and we are teachers so we have our fill every day! However, the pools were beautiful and so clean.  The staff were friendly, helpful and genuinely interested in making our stay the best possible.  Would I go back? YES!

reviews.author: Taz_maniac70
reviews.title: I admit it.  I loved it here.
reviews.text:
After reading the mixed reviews of the Phoenician on this site, I have to say I approached my vacation here with a lot of trepidation.  There seemed to potentially be a lot to not like about this place.  There is no getting around the fact that it's overpriced.  It's a place for people with money to show off how much money they have by spending lots of money.  I was there on a family member's tab, but I have to wonder why even monied people would want to throw so much money at this hotel.
