Then of course the place is a tropical garden in the middle of *desert*, which is wrong on so many levels.  If you can get past these things, you can have a great vacation.

The minute I got there I checked in quickly and a bellhop drove my husband and me to our casita in a cart so we wouldn't have to walk the whole way with our luggage.  Our casita room was a bit small, but  had everything we needed and was scrupulously clean.  Our bellhop actually gave us a tour of our own room!  We had a great balcony that was very large and partially overlooked the golf course, a garden, and the mountain depending on where you stood.

Other reviewers are right about hte decor.  It is a bit tired and bland.  Everything is brown and beige and the furniture in the main building looks a bit worn.  This is the Southwest folks!  How about adding some appropriate decor?

The competition for pool chairs is fierce.  You do have to come early for the best seats.  However, if you come late, the pool attendants will try their hardest to find you seats.  If you come early, you can hold onto your seat as long as you can prove that you're really there and not just "reserving" a seat two hours before you sit there (Easter morning I grabbed a chair at 7:30 AM and sat there for two and a half hours.  I left my book and other stuff on the chair and went to brunch and my chair was still waiting for me an hour later).  Pool attendants not only don't expect tips, they refuse them!  The pools tend to get very filled with kids.  If you're a lap swimmer, I suggest the Oasis Pool, which is irregularly shaped, but is so large that it gives you the most space to move around.  While the water slide is meant for kids, no one tells adults not to go on it and it's lots of fun.  

Food is overpriced, but excellent.  I ate at both The Terrace and Windows on the Green.  The former is Italian, the latter Southwestern.  Both were tasty and creative.  The latter could use some Southwestern decor.  Service was great at the restaurants.

I had a wonderful treatment at the beautiful spa.  This is one place where the price seems consistent with most spas of this type.  I highly recommend the Desert Serenity Scrub, Wrap, and Massage.  They were very professional, the locker room was well-equipped, and they have a wonderful meditation room and lots of complimentary teas and coffe and fresh fruit.

All in all I would say Great Service, Beautiful Location, Good food.  A very worthwhile vacation.

reviews.author: kcwkcw
reviews.title: family oriented hotel
reviews.text:
I just got back from the Phoenician.  It is a lovely hotel but its for families with kids.  I am 32 and went with my boyfriend.  We felt a little out a place.  We are from NYC.  We were hoping for a little more action - every restaurant - except Mary Elaines - had children.  The pool is very nice but the children took over the pool.  They we everywhere.  The spa is not that nice.  The treatments were nice but the place was outdated.  How can people say its sooo nice?  The gym had a good amount of machines but dark and depressing.  The meditation room was comfortable but not great.  (i recently went to the Boca Raton Hotel spa - now that is a nice spa!)  The grounds at the Phoenician were perfect - flowers of all colors, bunnies hopping around the landscape, fountains and big lawns,.  

The food is pricely but pretty good.  Rooms are a nice size.  Bathrooms are very big - but the "two person soaking tub" is not for 2 people!  Maybe 2 children.  Oh the "9" pools at the Phoenician - that includes a few small kiddie pools.  All pools had more kids than adults in them.  THey were heated though!  The big jacuzzi had so many children in it that we couldnt get into it.  We went during teh Easter holiday so maybe that is why there were so many children.  Got to the pool on Sat at 11.30 am and could not get a lounge chair.  The hotel started to put chairs in the lawn away form the pool, so i was lucky enough to get one.  On thur and Fri - the pool was quieter and much more appealing.  Service by the pool was great, except for Sat.  People waited an hour for their food.  

Ask for a room facing the pool area for the best views.  We faced the mountain - so close to the mountain, that the room was dark.  Housekeeping was very good.  Our refrigerator was broken but it was stocked with many many things. Restaurant at the golf course was good.  The main dining room - Terrace - wasnt as good.  But everyone who worked at the hotel was soooooo extremely friendly.  

I will go back - one day when i have a family.  If you go with kids, bring balls, frisbees, etc, b/c there are many big lawns to run around in.  The hotel provideds balls too. There is a volleyball court and bball net in the pool.

reviews.author: LuvGolfTravel
reviews.title: A One Time Experience
reviews.text: I used most of my remaining Starwood points to stay here 3 nights last week with my wife.  I knew from its reputation that the resort might be a little stiff for my liking, but I figured we had to try this once.  The experience was quite a paradox.  The resort is enormous and, unless you secure a Casita, you will end up walking a long distance from your room to the pool, tennis courts, golf club and parking.  To avoid this, we packed two back-packs and used the beautiful Mother of Pearl pool as a staging area all day.  I usually enjoy spending time in a hotel's great room and lobby areas, and this was a bit disappointing.  The carpets are tired and the furniture a little stiff.   HOWEVER, despite these first impressions, the resort really grew on us after a few days.   The service we received was first class at every turn:  in the room, at the pool, on the driving range, and at the tennis garden.  Although the resort is stiff, the staff was not, and we were impressed by the friendly professionalism.  The mult-tiered pool area is stunning whether you're laying poolside or viewing it from the balcony or the mountain above; but it's a little too crowded and noisy.   The deluxe room we stayed in was beautiful with an impressive marble bathroom.   Although the food suffered from the usual resort-price-gouging -- it was surprisingly worth it.   We ran the gamut from a big dinner at Mary Elaine's, burgers and wings at the pool and a caesar salad in room service, and were never disappointed by the portions or the quality.  The tennis garden, containing 12 courts surrounded by flower arrangements is also impressive.  The Cactus Garden is also something not to be missed.  We also liked being at the foot of Cambelback Mountain to hike the Cholla trail, and the views from the pool.  Ultimately, we are happy to have experienced "the Phoenician" ... once.

reviews.author: Guide6711
reviews.title: what  more  could you ask for
reviews.text:
Family of five stayed the week after the "big rains".  Heated pool, luxurious service, clean wonderful rooms with a large terrace with an amazing view.  Worth every penny.  I don't agree with one negative comment written.  
This was our third return trip (also have stayed at the Boulders, Four Seasons Troon) and will return again.

reviews.author: gvaguy
reviews.title: Overpriced
reviews.text: Gorgeous location, but this hotel has seen better days and is charging waaay too much, living off a reputation.  The whole place reminded me of my grandmother's place (with the exception of some sitting areas, the decor is very late 20th century desert retirement community).  Some areas are a bit shabby, the carpeting in particular, and they charge you extra fees for everything (even if you don't take advantage of it).  For a luxury hotel they are amazingly cheap, right down to no complimentary newspaper, unless we hit it on an off week...

reviews.author: Road10143
reviews.title: No Value
reviews.text:
This is a beautiful location - and the room is ok (not worth $400-500 though) - but the fees are outrageous.  A $26 per day valet charge, a $14 Bell Gratuity, a $4 Housekeeping Gratuity and get this - a $29 fee for a two minute domestic call.  
    
    Also there was a mysterious mini bar charge that they tried to sneak through.  I felt like my pocket was getting picked every time I turned around.
    
    The service is average and nowhere near levels of other top of the line hotels I've visited:  Four Season Maui, Ritz San Fran, Sofitel London, etc...
    
    This is the second disappointing overpriced stay with Starwood - the other being the Princeville in Kauai.
    
    I think there are better values in the area - check them out.

reviews.author: Zella
reviews.title: Cant believe people moan about this place!
reviews.text: My lord! just read some of the reviews about this hotel,and cannot beleive the things people moan about!! UNless you are the Queen or Bill Gates, then i cannot imagine what could possibly dissapoint you about this hotel!   Could it be that the amazing desert panorama was no good? or the splarkling mother of pearl pool was not pearly enough?  Maybe the live singing in the spactacular Mary elaines( where your handbag gets its own stool!!)was not to your liking? Come on people this place is AMAZING and im not easily impressed. Its beautiful, elegant, and the food is spectacular! The sunday brunch is the best event i have ever eaten at.  The setting is incredible, the staff lovely and the works of art very impressive.  If the only thing people can moan about is the price of the parking, then you probably couldnt afford to go here in the first place. the guy who moaned about the mini bar>>come on you were probably too drunk to know youd drunk it!.  This place is all about luxury and oppulance, if you mind about the money, give it a miss there will be a holiday inn nearby. If however you like the high life go for it its great!

reviews.author: Gitano
reviews.title: Way too expensive
reviews.text: OK place but WAY too expensive - stay in Embassy Suites or something for alot less and almost as good.

reviews.author: Robert S
reviews.title: A Fine Resort
reviews.text: I enjoyed a long weekend at the Phoenician Resort and was most impressed with the lovely surroundings and fine service.  I was situated in the Canyon Building-- a hotel within the hotel with its own spererate lobby and concierge staff.  The pool was quiet and relaxing, with classical music playing in the background.  Unlike the rest of the resort which can feel crowded and noisy, this wing was a most welcomed escape of tranquility.  Service at the resort was superb with good name recognition and the valet would have my car brought to the drive faster than I could get from my room to the lobby.  Be prepared to pay extra for everything--from the gym to parking--but the experience was excellent and I would gladly return.

reviews.author: CaryandCindy
reviews.title: Just O.K.
reviews.text:
Well, after wanting to stay here for the last couple of years, my wife and I were dissapointed in The Phoenician. 
 Upgraded to a "Deluxe" room and it overlooked the back of the resort and at a giant dirt hill. A golf package in the off season made it worth it but if I had paid the $400-600 a night + 10 % tax, valet, tips etc. I would have been VERY dissapointed.
 The room was just average, and the building style is dated( white washed oak, brass etc.)
 I will say the service for the most part is very good, Mary Elaine's in particular, but for $325 for two it better be.
 The golf course is nice and everyone is friendly there, but my wife was not thrilled with the spa and felt it was so-so. 
If you can get a package that seems reasonable great, otherwise there are other places that are better spent.

reviews.author: Bearis123
reviews.title: Good but not great
reviews.text:
We stayed for 7 days at the Phoenician during the last week of August.

Positives:
-Rooms are big, well appointed and clean. Ask for a 1 bedroom casita type room. They are over 600 sqft and include huge bathrooms and terraces as well as dsl, 32" tvs and other great features.
-Staff is very professional, friendly and for the most part go out of their way to please. Everyone from the pool crew to the cleaning crew were superb. 
- Parking was free when you stay in a casita type room as you can park right under it.
-Offseason rates (july-aug) are hard to beat.
-Location is very convenient to the best shopping and dining in Phoenix.

Negatives:
-Resort is very big. It either feels empty and depressing or crowded and hectic depending on whether its empty of pretty booked.
-Tel calls from room (which we never make except for this once) include an initial $24 charge!
-Gym has a $20 per day fee though most of the time we got in for free.
-The restaurants serve decent food though none have any local cuisine or uniqueness to them.
-The resort feels very tired and very 80s which might not be of your liking.
-Lobby and main building areas feel like you are in Las Vegas.
-Pools are not salt water.
-Can get very noisey at times between the kids, the music which is constantly blaring out from pool-side speakers (you can turn the music down/off by turning button) and the constant grounds crew sawing and cutting.

Conclusion:
If you are less than 40 stay at the Four Seasons in Troon North. If you are over 40 or have more than one child, stay here.

reviews.author: Camper2119
reviews.title: Disappointing...
reviews.text:
Staying at American hotels is always a pleasure. However I find when something goes wrong you tend to notice that everything else is going wrong for everyone. I believe this to primarly be bad management, low exployee morale etc.

I stay at many Starwood Luxury & St. Regis Collection hotels all over Europe and the USA (my favorite being St. Regis, Rome) and I was incredibly disappointed with the over all quality of the hotel, service, employees, managers.

If you decide to book at the hotel be prepared for many unknown costs. From valet parking being $27 (the highest in the area I found out - and is not the highest rated hotel). Service quality based upon the gratuity you leave. In my opinion I believe poor/rude service should not be merited by any gratuity. 

Also check your minibar! make sure that if you havent taken anything you tell them and that there is nothing missing. Although this is a service the hotel normally provides daily, we found out after arriving back in the UK my credit card was charged an addtional $88.00! Called them up and found out it was minibar! Then they would refund the wrong charge stating we should have made sure the mini bar was not used.

This is just a list of a few issues, I would not recommend staying there. We will not be returning to Starwood hotels in the USA again as they are obviously inferior and in a different class to their European counterparts.

Regards, 

Dissatisfied customer.

reviews.author: Bjaygee
reviews.title: Very Nice But...
reviews.text:
Spent four days at the Phoenician with our 19 and 16 year olds...it's nice enough, if showing a little of its age...the staff was cordial and competent, and probably the highlight of the resort...the spa was decent but not overwhelming and the food was so so...my wife and I had been to the Mandarin Oriental in Miami the month before, and by that yardstick the Phoenician was good but not great...it's more like a very exclusive country club than a Ritz or Mandarin, both of which I have to admit I prefer...although having a mountain right behind the resort makes for a stunning visual...

If you have to be in Scottsdale, the Phoenician is probably the best there is.  But given a choice, I'd rather go to the Mandarin in Miami any day...

reviews.author: everson420
reviews.title: Awesome hotel
reviews.text: We spent 1 night at The Phoenician, and wished we stayed more.  The hotel is beautiful, everything from the marbel fountains to the cactus gardens.  The suite we had was marvelous, and had three full bathrooms.  The pools were lovely, except for the three drunk guys who spent the afternoon drinking in the children's pool.  The pool had an excellent waterslide, and all of the attendants were friendly and helpful.  The staff was by far the best I've seen.  From the moment of arrival you are treated like royalty.  We would never consider staying anywhere else in the Phoenix-Scottsdale area.

reviews.author: milhouse
reviews.title: Wonderful Resort
reviews.text:
Right on par with the Four Seasons Scottsdale - just depends on what you are looking for (intimate and quiet like the Four Seasons or active and elegant like The Phoenician).

The grounds are layed out exceptionally well and the staff works hard to please. Everything is manicured perfectly. Booked a deluxe view room - upon arrival they bumped us up to a grand deluxe view room with a 600 square foot terrace with 180 degree views (the room was also about 600 square feet). The room was perfectly appointed with nice frette linens and soft warm colors. Gilchrist and Soames bath products were featured in a marble bathroom that also had a jacuzzi tub and a large shower.  Room service, we only had breakfast, was excellent. The work out room also has new equipment and has great views of the pool area. 

One bit of advice would be for them to increase the number of people staffing the concierge desk (only one person on a Sunday morning - had to wait quite awhile just to get to talk to her). Other than that, however, the resort was great and should definitely be the choice of those looking to stay in the heart of Scottsdale (and willing to pay a little extra for it).

reviews.author: lyntom
reviews.title: Absolutely fabulous!!
reviews.text: Stayed at the Phoenician on June 24 and 25.  An absolutely fabulous experience.  Great room with a large balcony and a huge bathroom with sunken tub and a separate, glassed in shower.  The beauty of the grounds and buildings and the level of service is amazing.  Rented a cabana for the day and it was well worth the expense as the service they provide to you is unmatched.  Ate dinner in the Terrace Dining Room, which is very expensive but worth the splurge.   I would live there!!!

reviews.author: Dream25157
reviews.title: Perfect, Perfect, Perfect!
reviews.text:
For me, it was 4 nights of complete paradise!  We arrived and was greeted by the most welcoming staff.  The Phoenician is a very big resort, but not to worry though – anytime we needed a ride to a building, there was always a staff member there to take us to any part of the resort.  The Phoenician has a great fitness center with a wide array of free weights as well as cardiovascular equipment, great pools, which were never crowded, a wonderful cactus garden, beautiful surroundings and so much more.  The most appealing aspect of the Phoenician is its staff – customer service is obviously very essential: we were always greeted with smiles, everyone was helpful and the concierge sat with us for 30 minutes to discuss where we should go, what we should do and to just describe Arizona and what it had to offer.  Thanks Gary!

I do agree with most who say that the restaurants are very expensive. However, we didn’t worry about this because we simply did not go to them.  We did eat at the Ice Cream Parlor for lunch everyday, which has very reasonable prices and a very delicious chicken panini!  For other meals we simply drove to either downtown Scottsdale or Tempe.  Don’t worry about the prices if you have access to a car - the Phoenician resides in a beautiful city that is flourishing and there are plenty of restaurants around.  

For those looking to go to Scottsdale for pure bliss and relaxation, I highly recommend the Phoenician.  It is truly a delightful experience.  We will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Experience11280
reviews.title: My best stay, ever
reviews.text: Absolute opulence.  Amazing room with outstanding amenities.  I had torn my pants.  At the concierge's urging, I left them on the bed, and ran to my meeting.  When I returned two hours later, the pair of pants was on a hanger in my room, pressed and mended.  No charge.  MaryElaine's is a very classy atmosphere.  5* experience throughout.  Great golf as well.

reviews.author: Jet30468
reviews.title: Best Hotel in Phoenix/Scottsdale
reviews.text: The "boys" and I go to this hotel every year in June, and for good reason, have been coming back for 5+ years!  This hotel is the best in the greater Phoenix/Scottsdale area and I would never stay anywhere else.  The pool area is never crowded and the spa is excellent.  The entire staff throughout the hotel are always friendly and knowledgable.  The rooms are all in great shape, kept clean and up to date (the bathrooms are huge!).  Their golf course is also one of my favorite in AZ (friendly to all skill levels).  I highly recommend The Phoenician.  Enjoy!

reviews.author: Companion3827
reviews.title: lovely and relaxing
reviews.text:
We stayed 3 nights at the Phoenician.  It was indeed a lovely and gracious resort.  Very relaxing in every way.  Our family, including 9 and 10 year old, loved it.

The only drawback was the view from the room.  The room itself was great, large and thoughtfully furnished (especially all those toiletries).  But we booked a deluxe room (with city, mountain, or garden view) and were give a room overlooking the main road.  After speaking with the front desk and then a supervisor, we were told there were no better rooms available that night and we could be moved the next day.  The next day, we were moved to a huge room with a huge terrace, overlooking the golf course and city.  Very nice.  But we also overlooked a large white shed-like building and the truck parking area.  Due to a large convention, there were constantly trucks moving in and out, or just parked with their loud A/C units humming.  When checking in to this room, we called to ask about this and were told that the trucks would be gone in an hour or 2.  But it continued for the next 2 days.  Even with the terrace door shut, we were awakened at 7:30 am by the beep-beep-beep of trucks backing up.

Other than that, we found the Phoenician to be very nice.  We took a poolside package, including cabana and breakfast and lunch.  Great service at the cabana.  Poolside could not have been more idyllic.  Loved the spa, even though our massages were fairly clinical.  Meditation class was fun.  Overall, service was friendly and earnest, though not always on-the-mark.  I'd come back any time.

reviews.author: Happy_on_the_road
reviews.title: Wake up early to get a place to sit at the pool
reviews.text:
Spent Easter weekend here (4 nights) in Room 3123, the cheapest level room at US$395 per night. It overlooked the entry garden which was fine but was near an exhaust that nearly knocked me out with a gas smell each time I used the terrace. I was honestly nervous to spend much time outside on the terrace. Good room in size and furnishings, staff did well, a bit stressed at the restaurant, great concierge, outrageous US$26 per day to park and the only place I paid to park in all of the trip. Nice pool grounds but very poor system. Signage says the pool service is open at 9 a.m. I believed them and relaxed my first morning and had breakfast and headed to the pool just prior to 9 a.m. Too late, no chairs left - it looked like a factory with rows and rows of chairs at all pools, even extending on the lawn outside of the pool fence. Not very nice for the price. System is first come, first served and I suggest you get there by 7:15 a.m. when I found the pickings acceptable the next day (amazing - no one sleeps late at this hotel but newspaper comes late). You must return before 10 a.m. or you lose your chair but I noted hotel staff were shy to do this when people left personal items (paperback book, suntan lotion) on the chair and ignored the rule and wandering guests in search of chairs. It is quite amusing to watch the high paying guests who return after 10 a.m. find their chairs are taken by other high paying guests. Pool staff feign ignorance and the guests argue and nearly get into fist fights. A bit of action at a seemingly tranquil spot. There is a Tranquility pool where no music, sports or cell phones are allowed, but the hotel hired a cheesy wedding band to play above the pool and I could not hear the conversation of my partner in the next chair without shouting. Another kind guests gave the band US$300 to stop playing for a couple of hours. Hotel is close to shopping. I liked it, food good and staff try but for their prices, there are no excuses. I would consider returning but would likely prefer to try someplace else that may pay more attention to service and details. Lovely grounds, great spa, service that tries hard but cannot always win due to understaffing, tacky pool chair procedure, need to tip everyone everywhere to get any service. Good to consider, worth visiting the grounds, but think two and three times before booking. 
Also, I wondered how the people whose terraces overlooked the always busy motor entry felt - no privacy and noise, lights and busy activities at all hours - I felt lucky that I could close my terrace door and ignore the gas fumes.

reviews.author: FellowTraveler36205
reviews.title: The Phoenician
reviews.text: Had a great stay at the Phoenician Resort in Scottsdale, AZ. Got upgraded to a suite. Fantastic food at all the hotel's restaurants -- esp. higher end Mary Elaine's. Great service throughout.Golf courses were in superb shape, they were being groomed all days we golfed. Took 4 hours to golf 18 holes -- no backups.Great spa service (according to my wife).Front desk took care of limo issues and made me feel very satisfied.You can enjoy the luxury and never leave the site.Visit it soon. I'm going back in October.

reviews.author: OnAir11012
reviews.title: 117 degrees but wonderful
reviews.text:
Went to the phoenician 6/03 after being in los vegas with four teenagers. As soon as we arrived my stress level mellowed out totally. 
Wonderful pools that were uncrowed this time of year and open 24/7. 
Most of the time we had a pool to ourselves. Wonderful pool attendents to take care of you. Played alittle croquet with the kids. Tennis was hot but fun. Nice clay court but ya gotta pay for it. Rooms were nice, baths even better great toiletries. We had garden level with a nice patio ( slept outside one night) Prices that time of year were great 169.00a room paid 270.oo in vegas. Mary Elaines is a wonderful resturant but 380.00 (tip included) was a bit much. I'm sure room prices are much higher in season but still probably worth it. If you have to ask the price, well you know. At that price I don't know if I'd take the kids. How ever they had a great time and were never board even with nothing much for them to do. ( ages 13-19) They lived in the pool the whole time. Over all one of the nicer places we have stayed, and we generally do high end resorts. Liked it much more than the biltmore. 
Will stay there again when in Pheonix or maybe The Boulders, I here thats wonderful

reviews.author: signothetimes53
reviews.title: Phoenician: Not as good as it thinks it is
reviews.text:
This is a beautiful resort, but this is not as good as it is advertised to be. Service in particular, especially at these very high prices, should be impeccable, but it was not. Overall, the Phoenician did not represent exceptional value for the exceptional price tag everything here commanded. It had the feel of a very high-priced resort that did not pay its help well, and understaffed in several key areas.On the plus side, the food was excellent, the wine lists superb, and the pools, spa, golf and tennis were wonderful.But, the hotel doesn't offer an all-purposes Guest Services line to resolve problems that occur. 
Instead, we found that you had to call the Front Desk, which was perpetually understaffed and overwhelmed by calls and dealing with check-ins and check-outs. Consequently, we were always put on hold for several minutes waiting for a live human being to talk to.The highspeed internet service was barely functioning for most of our stay, and at $20 a day for such service, should have been constant.Second, be forewarned if you visit: if it's raining or overcast here (which admittedly isn't often in the desert), you'd better have a car and leave the property to find something to do, because absolutely EVERYTHING at the Phoenician is keyed around sunny weather. There's nothing here for recreation on a bad weather day other than eating/drinking, and spa services. No game room, no theater, nothing.Finally, the rooms are not as spectacular as I had been led to believe. Ours was a top of the line room overlooking the front of the property and the spectacular swimming pools. But the carpeting was tired, some of the furniture wobbly...and when the banquet crew set up for an outdoor event just below our balcony, they noisily dragged tables and equipment along the concrete in a half-hour cacophony that ended only when I reached banquet services and asked them to tell the work crew to work as a team and carry the equipment together to avoid the noise.We've traveled to great resorts around the world. This one maintains a pretense it is one of the great resorts, and it does some things very well. Other things are not done as well as your run-of-the-mill Sheraton hotel. Perhaps it will be your cup of tea, but it certainly was not ours.

reviews.author: nicolas617
reviews.title: A Wonderful Oasis
reviews.text: A wonderful place with accomdating staff. The rooms are beautiful and very tastefully decorated. The whole experience was a pleasure.

reviews.author: Traveler38536
reviews.title: Terrific place to relax!
reviews.text:
Just returned from a 4 day holiday weekend at the Phoenician. We stayed 
in the Canyon Building in suite 8221..the ground floor. This is our 
favorite buidling to stay in at this resort since we love the lobby 
with its fireplace and view of the magnificient waterfall outside the 
doors. The Canyon building has its own pool area with a wonderful 
large, scenic and private hot tub and the best cabannas on the 
property. 
 The staff was unceasingly friendly and helpful whereever we went on the resort grounds. 
The Center For Well Being was used extensively by us and we enjoyed the 
massages, facials and time to relax in the meditation room with the 
wonderful waterful and lounge chairs. The only spa service not up to 
par was the spa pedicure which had me sitting in a chair with my feet 
in a bowl of water. A massage chair with bubbling foot area is the more 
luxurious and usual setup for an $80 treatment of this sort. Other than 
that, we loved the workout room...the grounds were glorious with all 
the flowering plants and cactus gardens...the food both at the pools 
and the restaurants was outstanding. The most relaxing aspect of 
walking around and enjoying the resort were the many waterfalls they 
had everywhere... For children, they have a childrens program 7 days a 
week, several kiddie pools and a slide that all would enjoy. All in 
all...a wonderful vacation.

reviews.author: FrequentFlier5368
reviews.title: Phoenix Native Says: 'Best Hotel in Phoenix Area'
reviews.text: I have stayed at the Phoenician no less than a dozen times over the years and it is by far my favorite hotel in Phoenix. Better than the Biltmore, Scottsdale Princess, Camelback Inn, and the J.W. Marriot. The Phoenician is like an oasis in the desert. The grounds are plush green with Palm trees and beautiful grass. The hotel is set at the base of Camelback Mountain which makes for incredible views from rooms or if you are lucky enough to eat the best restaurant in Phoenix "Mary Elaine's." Mary Elaine s is by far the finest dining in Arizona. If you enjoy golf the Phoenician's course is breathtaking. One time I was escorted to my room and when the employee found a dead bug that startled my girlfriend the manager gave us our last night for free ($600 a night room). I was born in Phoenix and love this hotel. If you are looking into ultra-luxurious Phoenix accommodations close to the best shopping and night life in the state (Fashion Square Mall and Old Town Scottsdale) the Phoenician is ABSOLUTELY the place to stay.

reviews.author: travelchica
reviews.title: Beautiful, but service needs help
reviews.text: We stayed at the Phoenician for 2 days over the New Years. We have seen some of the other resorts in Scottsdale and felt that the scenery and layout is much more appealing than the others. However, service was not, in our opinion, up to par for a luxury resort. The front desk staff seemed clueless. They struggled with check in, never did call us, as promised, once our room was ready, never let baggage valet know to have our luggage brought up, struggled with check out, etc. We had to constantly call for requests that we shouldn't have had to make. On the other hand, The Oasis restaurant staff was very friendly, we loved the Thirsty Camel lounge with its indoor and outdoor setting and enjoyed the Center for Wellness spa.

reviews.author: sunshone
reviews.title: Excellent trip
reviews.text:
We just returned from a 3 night/4 day stay at the Phoenician. It was a fabulous trip. We were so impressed with the customer service. All of the staff were very helpful and went out of their way to meet our requests. Akwasi at the front desk, along with Leanne and Twila (in the spa) were on top of what it means to make the customer feel pampered. 
Our only suggestions are: have a small coffeepot in the room to be able to enjoy the sunrise and sunset from your room balcony with a cup of coffee/tea and do something about the noise from the helicopter traffic in the a.m. Would we go back - in a heartbeat!

reviews.author: GrandTour35038
reviews.title: What an awful stay...!
reviews.text:
On arrival at the hotel... greeted with the $27 per night valet parking charge (needless to say that we declined, and walked the 2 metres to the car park, to park ourselves!)

First impressions were generally very good. Although check-in was an incredibly tedious process. Booked a Grand Deluxe room with spectacular views. After a VERY long walk, arrived at the nice large room, to find it overlooked the main road into the hotel, and straight into other peoples bedrooms... not particularly spectacular. Asked to move to the room we booked, was kept on the phone for 10 minutes or so whilst the receptionist chewed her gum. She could not give us an answer as to why we were given that room with no views. So, they put us in a room below that, with worse views. Eventually moved to another room, which had everything we booked. One problem... cockroaches in the wc!

In the end we went back to reception, with cockroach... it was laughed about by the staff. WE were not laughing!

After a rather long wait at reception, a Supervisor spared us a couple of minutes of her very busy evening (and it felt that way too) to look into this. No real apology for the problems, and expected us to feel grateful for getting a room in the Canyon Building. A very large, but blandly decorated room. Although the views were good from the very small balcony (compared to the 3rd room we had... with the roaches).

Needless to say... we ended up with bugs in that wc too! It seems that the vents are not shielded from incoming, uninvited guests. There were also cockroaches inside the building, in the recption area and scorpions in the car park lift lobby.

On returning home, I found that my credit card had been overcharged by $300. Didn't respond to my fax after 2 days. Had to call, put on hold for 5 minutes, again, no real apology... it was treated more like a fact of life.

All in all... and INCREDIBLY disappointing stay. Rooms were way overpriced, staff attitude was appauling... This hotel has no idea about good Customer Service, and quality accomodation. Maybe a trip to Europe to see what a quality 5 star hotel is like is in order!

I would NEVER recommend this hotel to anyone.

reviews.author: Destination14767
reviews.title: Wonderful Stay!
reviews.text:
Just returned from a 4 night stay at The Phoenician. Wonderful experience. The rooms and baths are spacious and beautiful. Wonderful resort, with plenty to do right on the grounds. Pools are beautiful. 
Cactus garden is pretty as well. Service is the best we've ever experienced at any hotel or resort. Staff is attentive, pleasant, and works diligently to exceed expectations. Can't say enough good things about the resort, the service and the on site restaurants. Can't wait to go back.

reviews.author: mexidona
reviews.title: Over the Top!
reviews.text:
This place is over the top! Some girlfriends (5) and I met at the Phoenician from all over the nation for my birthday. They originally had us booked for two connecting rooms but upgraded us to a two bedroom villa with it's own private pool and jacuzzi. The villa was amazing. 
The service was top notch and the staff went out of their way to accomodate. Definitely will be back!!

reviews.author: DayTrip33282
reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: We stayed at The Phoenician for 3 nights, and had the time of our lives.  The rates were high, but the staff made you feel like royalty!  The grounds are perfectly manicured, the staff was incredible, the restaurants were fabulous, the spa was unbelievable!  We had an "out of this world" experience!  If you can afford the rates, you owe it to yourself to have this experience!

reviews.author: FellowTraveler2701
reviews.title: One of the world's finest!
reviews.text: This has to be one of the finest hotels in the world.  I travel extensively and have stayed in many luxury hotels, but few compare to this one.  From the moment you turn into the resort and drive past the waterfall and through the lush grounds, you know this will be a great experience.  It doesnt disappoint.  The lobby is beautiful with its Italian marble and there are fresh flowers everywhere.  The whole resort is gorgeous.  My room was very spacious and had all the amenities, not to mention a great view.  The hotel staff was superb.  Everyone was warm and friendly, extremely knowledgeable and without exception went out of their way to make sure everything was just right.  The restaurant on the top floor of the hotel, Mary Elaines, offers exquisite views, the finest service and one of the most impressive wine lists youll ever see, not to mention the extraordinary cuisine.  This is definitely a world class restaurant.  The spa was also world class.  I cant say enough good things about this place.  It was expensive, but worth every penny!
